object.name: books
object.sql: CREATE TABLE books ( book_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, osis TEXT NOT NULL, eng_name TEXT NOT NULL, name TEXT NOT NULL, testament TEXT NOT NULL, chapters INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 )

object.name: verses
object.sql: CREATE TABLE verses ( book_id INTEGER NOT NULL, chapter INTEGER NOT NULL, verse INTEGER NOT NULL, text TEXT NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY (book_id, chapter, verse) )

object.name: version
object.sql: CREATE TABLE version ( slug TEXT NOT NULL, label TEXT NOT NULL )

object.name: idx_v_bc
object.sql: CREATE INDEX idx_v_bc ON verses(book_id, chapter)

object.name: indexing
object.sql: CREATE VIEW indexing AS SELECT b.book_id, b.osis, b.eng_name, b.name, b.testament, b.chapters, v.slug, v.label FROM books b, version v

column.name: text
column.value: This is the written account of Adam's line. When God created man, he made him in the likeness of God.

column.name: text
column.value: He created them male and female and blessed them. And when they were created, he called them "man."

column.name: text
column.value: When Adam had lived 130 years, he had a son in his own likeness, in his own image; and he named him Seth.

column.name: text
column.value: After Seth was born, Adam lived 800 years and had other sons and daughters.

column.name: text
column.value: Altogether, Adam lived 930 years, and then he died.

column.name: text
column.value: When Seth had lived 105 years, he became the father of Enosh.

column.name: text
column.value: And after he became the father of Enosh, Seth lived 807 years and had other sons and daughters.

column.name: text
column.value: Altogether, Seth lived 912 years, and then he died.

column.name: text
column.value: When Enosh had lived 90 years, he became the father of Kenan.

column.name: text
column.value: And after he became the father of Kenan, Enosh lived 815 years and had other sons and daughters.

column.name: text
column.value: Altogether, Enosh lived 905 years, and then he died.

column.name: text
column.value: When Kenan had lived 70 years, he became the father of Mahalalel.

column.name: text
column.value: And after he became the father of Mahalalel, Kenan lived 840 years and had other sons and daughters.

column.name: text
column.value: Altogether, Kenan lived 910 years, and then he died.

column.name: text
column.value: When Mahalalel had lived 65 years, he became the father of Jared.

column.name: text
column.value: And after he became the father of Jared, Mahalalel lived 830 years and had other sons and daughters.

column.name: text
column.value: Altogether, Mahalalel lived 895 years, and then he died.

column.name: text
column.value: When Jared had lived 162 years, he became the father of Enoch.

column.name: text
column.value: And after he became the father of Enoch, Jared lived 800 years and had other sons and daughters.

column.name: text
column.value: Altogether, Jared lived 962 years, and then he died.

column.name: text
column.value: When Enoch had lived 65 years, he became the father of Methuselah.

column.name: text
column.value: And after he became the father of Methuselah, Enoch walked with God 300 years and had other sons and daughters.

column.name: text
column.value: Altogether, Enoch lived 365 years.

column.name: text
column.value: Enoch walked with God; then he was no more, because God took him away.

column.name: text
column.value: When Methuselah had lived 187 years, he became the father of Lamech.

column.name: text
column.value: And after he became the father of Lamech, Methuselah lived 782 years and had other sons and daughters.

column.name: text
column.value: Altogether, Methuselah lived 969 years, and then he died.

column.name: text
column.value: When Lamech had lived 182 years, he had a son.

column.name: text
column.value: He named him Noah and said, "He will comfort us in the labor and painful toil of our hands caused by the ground the LORD has cursed."

column.name: text
column.value: After Noah was born, Lamech lived 595 years and had other sons and daughters.

column.name: text
column.value: Altogether, Lamech lived 777 years, and then he died.

column.name: text
column.value: After Noah was 500 years old, he became the father of Shem, Ham and Japheth.

column.name: text
column.value: In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth.

column.name: text
column.value: Now the earth was formless and empty, darkness was over the surface of the deep, and the Spirit of God was hovering over the waters.

column.name: text
column.value: And God said, "Let there be light," and there was light.

column.name: text
column.value: God saw that the light was good, and he separated the light from the darkness.

column.name: text
column.value: God called the light "day," and the darkness he called "night." And there was evening, and there was morning--the first day.

column.name: text
column.value: And God said, "Let there be an expanse between the waters to separate water from water."

column.name: text
column.value: So God made the expanse and separated the water under the expanse from the water above it. And it was so.

column.name: text
column.value: God called the expanse "sky." And there was evening, and there was morning--the second day.

column.name: text
column.value: And God said, "Let the water under the sky be gathered to one place, and let dry ground appear." And it was so.

column.name: text
column.value: God called the dry ground "land," and the gathered waters he called "seas." And God saw that it was good.

column.name: text
column.value: Then God said, "Let the land produce vegetation: seed-bearing plants and trees on the land that bear fruit with seed in it, according to their various kinds." And it was so.

column.name: text
column.value: The land produced vegetation: plants bearing seed according to their kinds and trees bearing fruit with seed in it according to their kinds. And God saw that it was good.

column.name: text
column.value: And there was evening, and there was morning--the third day.

column.name: text
column.value: And God said, "Let there be lights in the expanse of the sky to separate the day from the night, and let them serve as signs to mark seasons and days and years,

column.name: text
column.value: and let them be lights in the expanse of the sky to give light on the earth." And it was so.

column.name: text
column.value: God made two great lights--the greater light to govern the day and the lesser light to govern the night. He also made the stars.

column.name: text
column.value: God set them in the expanse of the sky to give light on the earth,

column.name: text
column.value: to govern the day and the night, and to separate light from darkness. And God saw that it was good.

column.name: text
column.value: And there was evening, and there was morning--the fourth day.

column.name: text
column.value: And God said, "Let the water teem with living creatures, and let birds fly above the earth across the expanse of the sky."

column.name: text
column.value: So God created the great creatures of the sea and every living and moving thing with which the water teems, according to their kinds, and every winged bird according to its kind. And God saw that it was good.

column.name: text
column.value: God blessed them and said, "Be fruitful and increase in number and fill the water in the seas, and let the birds increase on the earth."

column.name: text
column.value: And there was evening, and there was morning--the fifth day.

column.name: text
column.value: And God said, "Let the land produce living creatures according to their kinds: livestock, creatures that move along the ground, and wild animals, each according to its kind." And it was so.

column.name: text
column.value: God made the wild animals according to their kinds, the livestock according to their kinds, and all the creatures that move along the ground according to their kinds. And God saw that it was good.

column.name: text
column.value: Then God said, "Let us make man in our image, in our likeness, and let them rule over the fish of the sea and the birds of the air, over the livestock, over all the earth, and over all the creatures that move along the ground."

column.name: text
column.value: So God created man in his own image, in the image of God he created him; male and female he created them.

column.name: text
column.value: God blessed them and said to them, "Be fruitful and increase in number; fill the earth and subdue it. Rule over the fish of the sea and the birds of the air and over every living creature that moves on the ground."

column.name: text
column.value: Then God said, "I give you every seed-bearing plant on the face of the whole earth and every tree that has fruit with seed in it. They will be yours for food.

column.name: text
column.value: And to all the beasts of the earth and all the birds of the air and all the creatures that move on the ground--everything that has the breath of life in it--I give every green plant for food." And it was so.

column.name: text
column.value: God saw all that he had made, and it was very good. And there was evening, and there was morning--the sixth day.

column.name: text
column.value: When men began to increase in number on the earth and daughters were born to them,

column.name: text
column.value: the sons of God saw that the daughters of men were beautiful, and they married any of them they chose.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD said, "My Spirit will not contend with man forever, for he is mortal; his days will be a hundred and twenty years."

column.name: text
column.value: The Nephilim were on the earth in those days--and also afterward--when the sons of God went to the daughters of men and had children by them. They were the heroes of old, men of renown.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD saw how great man's wickedness on the earth had become, and that every inclination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil all the time.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD was grieved that he had made man on the earth, and his heart was filled with pain.

column.name: text
column.value: So the LORD said, "I will wipe mankind, whom I have created, from the face of the earth--men and animals, and creatures that move along the ground, and birds of the air--for I am grieved that I have made them."

column.name: text
column.value: But Noah found favor in the eyes of the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: This is the account of Noah. Noah was a righteous man, blameless among the people of his time, and he walked with God.

column.name: text
column.value: Noah had three sons: Shem, Ham and Japheth.

column.name: text
column.value: Now the earth was corrupt in God's sight and was full of violence.

column.name: text
column.value: God saw how corrupt the earth had become, for all the people on earth had corrupted their ways.

column.name: text
column.value: So God said to Noah, "I am going to put an end to all people, for the earth is filled with violence because of them. I am surely going to destroy both them and the earth.

column.name: text
column.value: So make yourself an ark of cypress wood; make rooms in it and coat it with pitch inside and out.

column.name: text
column.value: This is how you are to build it: The ark is to be 450 feet long, 75 feet wide and 45 feet high.

column.name: text
column.value: Make a roof for it and finish the ark to within 18 inches of the top. Put a door in the side of the ark and make lower, middle and upper decks.

column.name: text
column.value: I am going to bring floodwaters on the earth to destroy all life under the heavens, every creature that has the breath of life in it. Everything on earth will perish.

column.name: text
column.value: But I will establish my covenant with you, and you will enter the ark--you and your sons and your wife and your sons' wives with you.

column.name: text
column.value: You are to bring into the ark two of all living creatures, male and female, to keep them alive with you.

column.name: text
column.value: Two of every kind of bird, of every kind of animal and of every kind of creature that moves along the ground will come to you to be kept alive.

column.name: text
column.value: You are to take every kind of food that is to be eaten and store it away as food for you and for them."

column.name: text
column.value: Noah did everything just as God commanded him.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD then said to Noah, "Go into the ark, you and your whole family, because I have found you righteous in this generation.

column.name: text
column.value: Take with you seven of every kind of clean animal, a male and its mate, and two of every kind of unclean animal, a male and its mate,

column.name: text
column.value: and also seven of every kind of bird, male and female, to keep their various kinds alive throughout the earth.

column.name: text
column.value: Seven days from now I will send rain on the earth for forty days and forty nights, and I will wipe from the face of the earth every living creature I have made."

column.name: text
column.value: And Noah did all that the LORD commanded him.

column.name: text
column.value: Noah was six hundred years old when the floodwaters came on the earth.

column.name: text
column.value: And Noah and his sons and his wife and his sons' wives entered the ark to escape the waters of the flood.

column.name: text
column.value: Pairs of clean and unclean animals, of birds and of all creatures that move along the ground,

column.name: text
column.value: male and female, came to Noah and entered the ark, as God had commanded Noah.

column.name: text
column.value: And after the seven days the floodwaters came on the earth.

column.name: text
column.value: In the six hundredth year of Noah's life, on the seventeenth day of the second month--on that day all the springs of the great deep burst forth, and the floodgates of the heavens were opened.

column.name: text
column.value: And rain fell on the earth forty days and forty nights.

column.name: text
column.value: On that very day Noah and his sons, Shem, Ham and Japheth, together with his wife and the wives of his three sons, entered the ark.

column.name: text
column.value: They had with them every wild animal according to its kind, all livestock according to their kinds, every creature that moves along the ground according to its kind and every bird according to its kind, everything with wings.

column.name: text
column.value: Pairs of all creatures that have the breath of life in them came to Noah and entered the ark.

column.name: text
column.value: The animals going in were male and female of every living thing, as God had commanded Noah. Then the LORD shut him in.

column.name: text
column.value: For forty days the flood kept coming on the earth, and as the waters increased they lifted the ark high above the earth.

column.name: text
column.value: The waters rose and increased greatly on the earth, and the ark floated on the surface of the water.

column.name: text
column.value: They rose greatly on the earth, and all the high mountains under the entire heavens were covered.

column.name: text
column.value: The waters rose and covered the mountains to a depth of more than twenty feet.

column.name: text
column.value: Every living thing that moved on the earth perished--birds, livestock, wild animals, all the creatures that swarm over the earth, and all mankind.

column.name: text
column.value: Everything on dry land that had the breath of life in its nostrils died.

column.name: text
column.value: Every living thing on the face of the earth was wiped out; men and animals and the creatures that move along the ground and the birds of the air were wiped from the earth. Only Noah was left, and those with him in the ark.

column.name: text
column.value: The waters flooded the earth for a hundred and fifty days.

column.name: text
column.value: Now the whole world had one language and a common speech.

column.name: text
column.value: As men moved eastward, they found a plain in Shinar and settled there.

column.name: text
column.value: They said to each other, "Come, let's make bricks and bake them thoroughly." They used brick instead of stone, and tar for mortar.

column.name: text
column.value: Then they said, "Come, let us build ourselves a city, with a tower that reaches to the heavens, so that we may make a name for ourselves and not be scattered over the face of the whole earth."

column.name: text
column.value: But the LORD came down to see the city and the tower that the men were building.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD said, "If as one people speaking the same language they have begun to do this, then nothing they plan to do will be impossible for them.

column.name: text
column.value: Come, let us go down and confuse their language so they will not understand each other."

column.name: text
column.value: So the LORD scattered them from there over all the earth, and they stopped building the city.

column.name: text
column.value: That is why it was called Babel--because there the LORD confused the language of the whole world. From there the LORD scattered them over the face of the whole earth.

column.name: text
column.value: This is the account of Shem. Two years after the flood, when Shem was 100 years old, he became the father of Arphaxad.

column.name: text
column.value: And after he became the father of Arphaxad, Shem lived 500 years and had other sons and daughters.

column.name: text
column.value: When Arphaxad had lived 35 years, he became the father of Shelah.

column.name: text
column.value: And after he became the father of Shelah, Arphaxad lived 403 years and had other sons and daughters.

column.name: text
column.value: When Shelah had lived 30 years, he became the father of Eber.

column.name: text
column.value: And after he became the father of Eber, Shelah lived 403 years and had other sons and daughters.

column.name: text
column.value: When Eber had lived 34 years, he became the father of Peleg.

column.name: text
column.value: And after he became the father of Peleg, Eber lived 430 years and had other sons and daughters.

column.name: text
column.value: When Peleg had lived 30 years, he became the father of Reu.

column.name: text
column.value: And after he became the father of Reu, Peleg lived 209 years and had other sons and daughters.

column.name: text
column.value: When Reu had lived 32 years, he became the father of Serug.

column.name: text
column.value: And after he became the father of Serug, Reu lived 207 years and had other sons and daughters.

column.name: text
column.value: When Serug had lived 30 years, he became the father of Nahor.

column.name: text
column.value: And after he became the father of Nahor, Serug lived 200 years and had other sons and daughters.

column.name: text
column.value: When Nahor had lived 29 years, he became the father of Terah.

column.name: text
column.value: And after he became the father of Terah, Nahor lived 119 years and had other sons and daughters.

column.name: text
column.value: After Terah had lived 70 years, he became the father of Abram, Nahor and Haran.

column.name: text
column.value: This is the account of Terah. Terah became the father of Abram, Nahor and Haran. And Haran became the father of Lot.

column.name: text
column.value: While his father Terah was still alive, Haran died in Ur of the Chaldeans, in the land of his birth.

column.name: text
column.value: Abram and Nahor both married. The name of Abram's wife was Sarai, and the name of Nahor's wife was Milcah; she was the daughter of Haran, the father of both Milcah and Iscah.

column.name: text
column.value: Now Sarai was barren; she had no children.

column.name: text
column.value: Terah took his son Abram, his grandson Lot son of Haran, and his daughter-in-law Sarai, the wife of his son Abram, and together they set out from Ur of the Chaldeans to go to Canaan. But when they came to Haran, they settled there.

column.name: text
column.value: Terah lived 205 years, and he died in Haran.

column.name: text
column.value: But God remembered Noah and all the wild animals and the livestock that were with him in the ark, and he sent a wind over the earth, and the waters receded.

column.name: text
column.value: Now the springs of the deep and the floodgates of the heavens had been closed, and the rain had stopped falling from the sky.

column.name: text
column.value: The water receded steadily from the earth. At the end of the hundred and fifty days the water had gone down,

column.name: text
column.value: and on the seventeenth day of the seventh month the ark came to rest on the mountains of Ararat.

column.name: text
column.value: The waters continued to recede until the tenth month, and on the first day of the tenth month the tops of the mountains became visible.

column.name: text
column.value: After forty days Noah opened the window he had made in the ark

column.name: text
column.value: and sent out a raven, and it kept flying back and forth until the water had dried up from the earth.

column.name: text
column.value: Then he sent out a dove to see if the water had receded from the surface of the ground.

column.name: text
column.value: But the dove could find no place to set its feet because there was water over all the surface of the earth; so it returned to Noah in the ark. He reached out his hand and took the dove and brought it back to himself in the ark.

column.name: text
column.value: He waited seven more days and again sent out the dove from the ark.

column.name: text
column.value: When the dove returned to him in the evening, there in its beak was a freshly plucked olive leaf! Then Noah knew that the water had receded from the earth.

column.name: text
column.value: He waited seven more days and sent the dove out again, but this time it did not return to him.

column.name: text
column.value: By the first day of the first month of Noah's six hundred and first year, the water had dried up from the earth. Noah then removed the covering from the ark and saw that the surface of the ground was dry.

column.name: text
column.value: By the twenty-seventh day of the second month the earth was completely dry.

column.name: text
column.value: Then God said to Noah,

column.name: text
column.value: "Come out of the ark, you and your wife and your sons and their wives.

column.name: text
column.value: Bring out every kind of living creature that is with you--the birds, the animals, and all the creatures that move along the ground--so they can multiply on the earth and be fruitful and increase in number upon it."

column.name: text
column.value: So Noah came out, together with his sons and his wife and his sons' wives.

column.name: text
column.value: All the animals and all the creatures that move along the ground and all the birds--everything that moves on the earth--came out of the ark, one kind after another.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Noah built an altar to the LORD and, taking some of all the clean animals and clean birds, he sacrificed burnt offerings on it.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD smelled the pleasing aroma and said in his heart: "Never again will I curse the ground because of man, even though every inclination of his heart is evil from childhood. And never again will I destroy all living creatures, as I have done.

column.name: text
column.value: "As long as the earth endures, seedtime and harvest, cold and heat, summer and winter, day and night will never cease."

column.name: text
column.value: Now the serpent was more crafty than any of the wild animals the LORD God had made. He said to the woman, "Did God really say, 'You must not eat from any tree in the garden'?"

column.name: text
column.value: The woman said to the serpent, "We may eat fruit from the trees in the garden,

column.name: text
column.value: but God did say, 'You must not eat fruit from the tree that is in the middle of the garden, and you must not touch it, or you will die.'"

column.name: text
column.value: "You will not surely die," the serpent said to the woman.

column.name: text
column.value: "For God knows that when you eat of it your eyes will be opened, and you will be like God, knowing good and evil."

column.name: text
column.value: When the woman saw that the fruit of the tree was good for food and pleasing to the eye, and also desirable for gaining wisdom, she took some and ate it. She also gave some to her husband, who was with her, and he ate it.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the eyes of both of them were opened, and they realized they were naked; so they sewed fig leaves together and made coverings for themselves.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the man and his wife heard the sound of the LORD God as he was walking in the garden in the cool of the day, and they hid from the LORD God among the trees of the garden.

column.name: text
column.value: But the LORD God called to the man, "Where are you?"

column.name: text
column.value: He answered, "I heard you in the garden, and I was afraid because I was naked; so I hid."

column.name: text
column.value: And he said, "Who told you that you were naked? Have you eaten from the tree that I commanded you not to eat from?"

column.name: text
column.value: The man said, "The woman you put here with me--she gave me some fruit from the tree, and I ate it."

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD God said to the woman, "What is this you have done?" The woman said, "The serpent deceived me, and I ate."

column.name: text
column.value: So the LORD God said to the serpent, "Because you have done this, "Cursed are you above all the livestock and all the wild animals! You will crawl on your belly and you will eat dust all the days of your life.

column.name: text
column.value: And I will put enmity between you and the woman, and between your offspring and hers; he will crush your head, and you will strike his heel."

column.name: text
column.value: To the woman he said, "I will greatly increase your pains in childbearing; with pain you will give birth to children. Your desire will be for your husband, and he will rule over you."

column.name: text
column.value: To Adam he said, "Because you listened to your wife and ate from the tree about which I commanded you, 'You must not eat of it,' "Cursed is the ground because of you; through painful toil you will eat of it all the days of your life.

column.name: text
column.value: It will produce thorns and thistles for you, and you will eat the plants of the field.

column.name: text
column.value: By the sweat of your brow you will eat your food until you return to the ground, since from it you were taken; for dust you are and to dust you will return."

column.name: text
column.value: Adam named his wife Eve, because she would become the mother of all the living.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD God made garments of skin for Adam and his wife and clothed them.

column.name: text
column.value: And the LORD God said, "The man has now become like one of us, knowing good and evil. He must not be allowed to reach out his hand and take also from the tree of life and eat, and live forever."

column.name: text
column.value: So the LORD God banished him from the Garden of Eden to work the ground from which he had been taken.

column.name: text
column.value: After he drove the man out, he placed on the east side of the Garden of Eden cherubim and a flaming sword flashing back and forth to guard the way to the tree of life.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD had said to Abram, "Leave your country, your people and your father's household and go to the land I will show you.

column.name: text
column.value: "I will make you into a great nation and I will bless you; I will make your name great, and you will be a blessing.

column.name: text
column.value: I will bless those who bless you, and whoever curses you I will curse; and all peoples on earth will be blessed through you."

column.name: text
column.value: So Abram left, as the LORD had told him; and Lot went with him. Abram was seventy-five years old when he set out from Haran.

column.name: text
column.value: He took his wife Sarai, his nephew Lot, all the possessions they had accumulated and the people they had acquired in Haran, and they set out for the land of Canaan, and they arrived there.

column.name: text
column.value: Abram traveled through the land as far as the site of the great tree of Moreh at Shechem. At that time the Canaanites were in the land.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD appeared to Abram and said, "To your offspring I will give this land." So he built an altar there to the LORD, who had appeared to him.

column.name: text
column.value: From there he went on toward the hills east of Bethel and pitched his tent, with Bethel on the west and Ai on the east. There he built an altar to the LORD and called on the name of the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Abram set out and continued toward the Negev.

column.name: text
column.value: Now there was a famine in the land, and Abram went down to Egypt to live there for a while because the famine was severe.

column.name: text
column.value: As he was about to enter Egypt, he said to his wife Sarai, "I know what a beautiful woman you are.

column.name: text
column.value: When the Egyptians see you, they will say, 'This is his wife.' Then they will kill me but will let you live.

column.name: text
column.value: Say you are my sister, so that I will be treated well for your sake and my life will be spared because of you."

column.name: text
column.value: When Abram came to Egypt, the Egyptians saw that she was a very beautiful woman.

column.name: text
column.value: And when Pharaoh's officials saw her, they praised her to Pharaoh, and she was taken into his palace.

column.name: text
column.value: He treated Abram well for her sake, and Abram acquired sheep and cattle, male and female donkeys, menservants and maidservants, and camels.

column.name: text
column.value: But the LORD inflicted serious diseases on Pharaoh and his household because of Abram's wife Sarai.

column.name: text
column.value: So Pharaoh summoned Abram. "What have you done to me?" he said. "Why didn't you tell me she was your wife?

column.name: text
column.value: Why did you say, 'She is my sister,' so that I took her to be my wife? Now then, here is your wife. Take her and go!"

column.name: text
column.value: Then Pharaoh gave orders about Abram to his men, and they sent him on his way, with his wife and everything he had.

column.name: text
column.value: Then God blessed Noah and his sons, saying to them, "Be fruitful and increase in number and fill the earth.

column.name: text
column.value: The fear and dread of you will fall upon all the beasts of the earth and all the birds of the air, upon every creature that moves along the ground, and upon all the fish of the sea; they are given into your hands.

column.name: text
column.value: Everything that lives and moves will be food for you. Just as I gave you the green plants, I now give you everything.

column.name: text
column.value: "But you must not eat meat that has its lifeblood still in it.

column.name: text
column.value: And for your lifeblood I will surely demand an accounting. I will demand an accounting from every animal. And from each man, too, I will demand an accounting for the life of his fellow man.

column.name: text
column.value: "Whoever sheds the blood of man, by man shall his blood be shed; for in the image of God has God made man.

column.name: text
column.value: As for you, be fruitful and increase in number; multiply on the earth and increase upon it."

column.name: text
column.value: Then God said to Noah and to his sons with him:

column.name: text
column.value: "I now establish my covenant with you and with your descendants after you

column.name: text
column.value: and with every living creature that was with you--the birds, the livestock and all the wild animals, all those that came out of the ark with you--every living creature on earth.

column.name: text
column.value: I establish my covenant with you: Never again will all life be cut off by the waters of a flood; never again will there be a flood to destroy the earth."

column.name: text
column.value: And God said, "This is the sign of the covenant I am making between me and you and every living creature with you, a covenant for all generations to come:

column.name: text
column.value: I have set my rainbow in the clouds, and it will be the sign of the covenant between me and the earth.

column.name: text
column.value: Whenever I bring clouds over the earth and the rainbow appears in the clouds,

column.name: text
column.value: I will remember my covenant between me and you and all living creatures of every kind. Never again will the waters become a flood to destroy all life.

column.name: text
column.value: Whenever the rainbow appears in the clouds, I will see it and remember the everlasting covenant between God and all living creatures of every kind on the earth."

column.name: text
column.value: So God said to Noah, "This is the sign of the covenant I have established between me and all life on the earth."

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Noah who came out of the ark were Shem, Ham and Japheth. (Ham was the father of Canaan.)

column.name: text
column.value: These were the three sons of Noah, and from them came the people who were scattered over the earth.

column.name: text
column.value: Noah, a man of the soil, proceeded to plant a vineyard.

column.name: text
column.value: When he drank some of its wine, he became drunk and lay uncovered inside his tent.

column.name: text
column.value: Ham, the father of Canaan, saw his father's nakedness and told his two brothers outside.

column.name: text
column.value: But Shem and Japheth took a garment and laid it across their shoulders; then they walked in backward and covered their father's nakedness. Their faces were turned the other way so that they would not see their father's nakedness.

column.name: text
column.value: When Noah awoke from his wine and found out what his youngest son had done to him,

column.name: text
column.value: he said, "Cursed be Canaan! The lowest of slaves will he be to his brothers."

column.name: text
column.value: He also said, "Blessed be the LORD, the God of Shem! May Canaan be the slave of Shem.

column.name: text
column.value: May God extend the territory of Japheth; may Japheth live in the tents of Shem, and may Canaan be his slave."

column.name: text
column.value: After the flood Noah lived 350 years.

column.name: text
column.value: Altogether, Noah lived 950 years, and then he died.

column.name: text
column.value: Adam lay with his wife Eve, and she became pregnant and gave birth to Cain. She said, "With the help of the LORD I have brought forth a man."

column.name: text
column.value: Later she gave birth to his brother Abel. Now Abel kept flocks, and Cain worked the soil.

column.name: text
column.value: In the course of time Cain brought some of the fruits of the soil as an offering to the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: But Abel brought fat portions from some of the firstborn of his flock. The LORD looked with favor on Abel and his offering,

column.name: text
column.value: but on Cain and his offering he did not look with favor. So Cain was very angry, and his face was downcast.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD said to Cain, "Why are you angry? Why is your face downcast?

column.name: text
column.value: If you do what is right, will you not be accepted? But if you do not do what is right, sin is crouching at your door; it desires to have you, but you must master it."

column.name: text
column.value: Now Cain said to his brother Abel, "Let's go out to the field." And while they were in the field, Cain attacked his brother Abel and killed him.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD said to Cain, "Where is your brother Abel?" "I don't know," he replied. "Am I my brother's keeper?"

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD said, "What have you done? Listen! Your brother's blood cries out to me from the ground.

column.name: text
column.value: Now you are under a curse and driven from the ground, which opened its mouth to receive your brother's blood from your hand.

column.name: text
column.value: When you work the ground, it will no longer yield its crops for you. You will be a restless wanderer on the earth."

column.name: text
column.value: Cain said to the LORD, "My punishment is more than I can bear.

column.name: text
column.value: Today you are driving me from the land, and I will be hidden from your presence; I will be a restless wanderer on the earth, and whoever finds me will kill me."

column.name: text
column.value: But the LORD said to him, "Not so; if anyone kills Cain, he will suffer vengeance seven times over." Then the LORD put a mark on Cain so that no one who found him would kill him.

column.name: text
column.value: So Cain went out from the LORD'S presence and lived in the land of Nod, east of Eden.

column.name: text
column.value: Cain lay with his wife, and she became pregnant and gave birth to Enoch. Cain was then building a city, and he named it after his son Enoch.

column.name: text
column.value: To Enoch was born Irad, and Irad was the father of Mehujael, and Mehujael was the father of Methushael, and Methushael was the father of Lamech.

column.name: text
column.value: Lamech married two women, one named Adah and the other Zillah.

column.name: text
column.value: Adah gave birth to Jabal; he was the father of those who live in tents and raise livestock.

column.name: text
column.value: His brother's name was Jubal; he was the father of all who play the harp and flute.

column.name: text
column.value: Zillah also had a son, Tubal-Cain, who forged all kinds of tools out of bronze and iron. Tubal-Cain's sister was Naamah.

column.name: text
column.value: Lamech said to his wives, "Adah and Zillah, listen to me; wives of Lamech, hear my words. I have killed a man for wounding me, a young man for injuring me.

column.name: text
column.value: If Cain is avenged seven times, then Lamech seventy-seven times."

column.name: text
column.value: Adam lay with his wife again, and she gave birth to a son and named him Seth, saying, "God has granted me another child in place of Abel, since Cain killed him."

column.name: text
column.value: Seth also had a son, and he named him Enosh. At that time men began to call on the name of the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: Thus the heavens and the earth were completed in all their vast array.

column.name: text
column.value: By the seventh day God had finished the work he had been doing; so on the seventh day he rested from all his work.

column.name: text
column.value: And God blessed the seventh day and made it holy, because on it he rested from all the work of creating that he had done.

column.name: text
column.value: This is the account of the heavens and the earth when they were created. When the LORD God made the earth and the heavens--

column.name: text
column.value: and no shrub of the field had yet appeared on the earth and no plant of the field had yet sprung up, for the LORD God had not sent rain on the earth and there was no man to work the ground,

column.name: text
column.value: but streams came up from the earth and watered the whole surface of the ground--

column.name: text
column.value: the LORD God formed the man from the dust of the ground and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life, and the man became a living being.

column.name: text
column.value: Now the LORD God had planted a garden in the east, in Eden; and there he put the man he had formed.

column.name: text
column.value: And the LORD God made all kinds of trees grow out of the ground--trees that were pleasing to the eye and good for food. In the middle of the garden were the tree of life and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil.

column.name: text
column.value: A river watering the garden flowed from Eden; from there it was separated into four headwaters.

column.name: text
column.value: The name of the first is the Pishon; it winds through the entire land of Havilah, where there is gold.

column.name: text
column.value: (The gold of that land is good; aromatic resin and onyx are also there.)

column.name: text
column.value: The name of the second river is the Gihon; it winds through the entire land of Cush.

column.name: text
column.value: The name of the third river is the Tigris; it runs along the east side of Asshur. And the fourth river is the Euphrates.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD God took the man and put him in the Garden of Eden to work it and take care of it.

column.name: text
column.value: And the LORD God commanded the man, "You are free to eat from any tree in the garden;

column.name: text
column.value: but you must not eat from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, for when you eat of it you will surely die."

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD God said, "It is not good for the man to be alone. I will make a helper suitable for him."

column.name: text
column.value: Now the LORD God had formed out of the ground all the beasts of the field and all the birds of the air. He brought them to the man to see what he would name them; and whatever the man called each living creature, that was its name.

column.name: text
column.value: So the man gave names to all the livestock, the birds of the air and all the beasts of the field. But for Adam no suitable helper was found.

column.name: text
column.value: So the LORD God caused the man to fall into a deep sleep; and while he was sleeping, he took one of the man's ribs and closed up the place with flesh.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD God made a woman from the rib he had taken out of the man, and he brought her to the man.

column.name: text
column.value: The man said, "This is now bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh; she shall be called 'woman,' for she was taken out of man."

column.name: text
column.value: For this reason a man will leave his father and mother and be united to his wife, and they will become one flesh.

column.name: text
column.value: The man and his wife were both naked, and they felt no shame.

column.name: text
column.value: This is the account of Shem, Ham and Japheth, Noah's sons, who themselves had sons after the flood.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Japheth: Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech and Tiras.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Gomer: Ashkenaz, Riphath and Togarmah.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Javan: Elishah, Tarshish, the Kittim and the Rodanim.

column.name: text
column.value: (From these the maritime peoples spread out into their territories by their clans within their nations, each with its own language.)

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Ham: Cush, Mizraim, Put and Canaan.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Cush: Seba, Havilah, Sabtah, Raamah and Sabteca. The sons of Raamah: Sheba and Dedan.

column.name: text
column.value: Cush was the father of Nimrod, who grew to be a mighty warrior on the earth.

column.name: text
column.value: He was a mighty hunter before the LORD; that is why it is said, "Like Nimrod, a mighty hunter before the LORD."

column.name: text
column.value: The first centers of his kingdom were Babylon, Erech, Akkad and Calneh, in Shinar.

column.name: text
column.value: From that land he went to Assyria, where he built Nineveh, Rehoboth Ir, Calah

column.name: text
column.value: and Resen, which is between Nineveh and Calah; that is the great city.

column.name: text
column.value: Mizraim was the father of the Ludites, Anamites, Lehabites, Naphtuhites,

column.name: text
column.value: Pathrusites, Casluhites (from whom the Philistines came) and Caphtorites.

column.name: text
column.value: Canaan was the father of Sidon his firstborn, and of the Hittites,

column.name: text
column.value: Jebusites, Amorites, Girgashites,

column.name: text
column.value: Hivites, Arkites, Sinites,

column.name: text
column.value: Arvadites, Zemarites and Hamathites. Later the Canaanite clans scattered

column.name: text
column.value: and the borders of Canaan reached from Sidon toward Gerar as far as Gaza, and then toward Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah and Zeboiim, as far as Lasha.

column.name: text
column.value: These are the sons of Ham by their clans and languages, in their territories and nations.

column.name: text
column.value: Sons were also born to Shem, whose older brother was Japheth; Shem was the ancestor of all the sons of Eber.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Shem: Elam, Asshur, Arphaxad, Lud and Aram.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Aram: Uz, Hul, Gether and Meshech.

column.name: text
column.value: Arphaxad was the father of Shelah, and Shelah the father of Eber.

column.name: text
column.value: Two sons were born to Eber: One was named Peleg, because in his time the earth was divided; his brother was named Joktan.

column.name: text
column.value: Joktan was the father of Almodad, Sheleph, Hazarmaveth, Jerah,

column.name: text
column.value: Hadoram, Uzal, Diklah,

column.name: text
column.value: Obal, Abimael, Sheba,

column.name: text
column.value: Ophir, Havilah and Jobab. All these were sons of Joktan.

column.name: text
column.value: The region where they lived stretched from Mesha toward Sephar, in the eastern hill country.

column.name: text
column.value: These are the sons of Shem by their clans and languages, in their territories and nations.

column.name: text
column.value: These are the clans of Noah's sons, according to their lines of descent, within their nations. From these the nations spread out over the earth after the flood.

column.name: text
column.value: So Abram went up from Egypt to the Negev, with his wife and everything he had, and Lot went with him.

column.name: text
column.value: Abram had become very wealthy in livestock and in silver and gold.

column.name: text
column.value: From the Negev he went from place to place until he came to Bethel, to the place between Bethel and Ai where his tent had been earlier

column.name: text
column.value: and where he had first built an altar. There Abram called on the name of the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: Now Lot, who was moving about with Abram, also had flocks and herds and tents.

column.name: text
column.value: But the land could not support them while they stayed together, for their possessions were so great that they were not able to stay together.

column.name: text
column.value: And quarreling arose between Abram's herdsmen and the herdsmen of Lot. The Canaanites and Perizzites were also living in the land at that time.

column.name: text
column.value: So Abram said to Lot, "Let's not have any quarreling between you and me, or between your herdsmen and mine, for we are brothers.

column.name: text
column.value: Is not the whole land before you? Let's part company. If you go to the left, I'll go to the right; if you go to the right, I'll go to the left."

column.name: text
column.value: Lot looked up and saw that the whole plain of the Jordan was well watered, like the garden of the LORD, like the land of Egypt, toward Zoar. (This was before the LORD destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah.)

column.name: text
column.value: So Lot chose for himself the whole plain of the Jordan and set out toward the east. The two men parted company:

column.name: text
column.value: Abram lived in the land of Canaan, while Lot lived among the cities of the plain and pitched his tents near Sodom.

column.name: text
column.value: Now the men of Sodom were wicked and were sinning greatly against the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD said to Abram after Lot had parted from him, "Lift up your eyes from where you are and look north and south, east and west.

column.name: text
column.value: All the land that you see I will give to you and your offspring forever.

column.name: text
column.value: I will make your offspring like the dust of the earth, so that if anyone could count the dust, then your offspring could be counted.

column.name: text
column.value: Go, walk through the length and breadth of the land, for I am giving it to you."

column.name: text
column.value: So Abram moved his tents and went to live near the great trees of Mamre at Hebron, where he built an altar to the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: At this time Amraphel king of Shinar, Arioch king of Ellasar, Kedorlaomer king of Elam and Tidal king of Goiim

column.name: text
column.value: went to war against Bera king of Sodom, Birsha king of Gomorrah, Shinab king of Admah, Shemeber king of Zeboiim, and the king of Bela (that is, Zoar).

column.name: text
column.value: All these latter kings joined forces in the Valley of Siddim (the Salt Sea).

column.name: text
column.value: For twelve years they had been subject to Kedorlaomer, but in the thirteenth year they rebelled.

column.name: text
column.value: In the fourteenth year, Kedorlaomer and the kings allied with him went out and defeated the Rephaites in Ashteroth Karnaim, the Zuzites in Ham, the Emites in Shaveh Kiriathaim

column.name: text
column.value: and the Horites in the hill country of Seir, as far as El Paran near the desert.

column.name: text
column.value: Then they turned back and went to En Mishpat (that is, Kadesh), and they conquered the whole territory of the Amalekites, as well as the Amorites who were living in Hazazon Tamar.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the king of Sodom, the king of Gomorrah, the king of Admah, the king of Zeboiim and the king of Bela (that is, Zoar) marched out and drew up their battle lines in the Valley of Siddim

column.name: text
column.value: against Kedorlaomer king of Elam, Tidal king of Goiim, Amraphel king of Shinar and Arioch king of Ellasar--four kings against five.

column.name: text
column.value: Now the Valley of Siddim was full of tar pits, and when the kings of Sodom and Gomorrah fled, some of the men fell into them and the rest fled to the hills.

column.name: text
column.value: The four kings seized all the goods of Sodom and Gomorrah and all their food; then they went away.

column.name: text
column.value: They also carried off Abram's nephew Lot and his possessions, since he was living in Sodom.

column.name: text
column.value: One who had escaped came and reported this to Abram the Hebrew. Now Abram was living near the great trees of Mamre the Amorite, a brother of Eshcol and Aner, all of whom were allied with Abram.

column.name: text
column.value: When Abram heard that his relative had been taken captive, he called out the 318 trained men born in his household and went in pursuit as far as Dan.

column.name: text
column.value: During the night Abram divided his men to attack them and he routed them, pursuing them as far as Hobah, north of Damascus.

column.name: text
column.value: He recovered all the goods and brought back his relative Lot and his possessions, together with the women and the other people.

column.name: text
column.value: After Abram returned from defeating Kedorlaomer and the kings allied with him, the king of Sodom came out to meet him in the Valley of Shaveh (that is, the King's Valley).

column.name: text
column.value: Then Melchizedek king of Salem brought out bread and wine. He was priest of God Most High,

column.name: text
column.value: and he blessed Abram, saying, "Blessed be Abram by God Most High, Creator of heaven and earth.

column.name: text
column.value: And blessed be God Most High, who delivered your enemies into your hand." Then Abram gave him a tenth of everything.

column.name: text
column.value: The king of Sodom said to Abram, "Give me the people and keep the goods for yourself."

column.name: text
column.value: But Abram said to the king of Sodom, "I have raised my hand to the LORD, God Most High, Creator of heaven and earth, and have taken an oath

column.name: text
column.value: that I will accept nothing belonging to you, not even a thread or the thong of a sandal, so that you will never be able to say, 'I made Abram rich.'

column.name: text
column.value: I will accept nothing but what my men have eaten and the share that belongs to the men who went with me--to Aner, Eshcol and Mamre. Let them have their share."

column.name: text
column.value: After this, the word of the LORD came to Abram in a vision: "Do not be afraid, Abram. I am your shield, your very great reward."

column.name: text
column.value: But Abram said, "O Sovereign LORD, what can you give me since I remain childless and the one who will inherit my estate is Eliezer of Damascus?"

column.name: text
column.value: And Abram said, "You have given me no children; so a servant in my household will be my heir."

column.name: text
column.value: Then the word of the LORD came to him: "This man will not be your heir, but a son coming from your own body will be your heir."

column.name: text
column.value: He took him outside and said, "Look up at the heavens and count the stars--if indeed you can count them." Then he said to him, "So shall your offspring be."

column.name: text
column.value: Abram believed the LORD, and he credited it to him as righteousness.

column.name: text
column.value: He also said to him, "I am the LORD, who brought you out of Ur of the Chaldeans to give you this land to take possession of it."

column.name: text
column.value: But Abram said, "O Sovereign LORD, how can I know that I will gain possession of it?"

column.name: text
column.value: So the LORD said to him, "Bring me a heifer, a goat and a ram, each three years old, along with a dove and a young pigeon."

column.name: text
column.value: Abram brought all these to him, cut them in two and arranged the halves opposite each other; the birds, however, he did not cut in half.

column.name: text
column.value: Then birds of prey came down on the carcasses, but Abram drove them away.

column.name: text
column.value: As the sun was setting, Abram fell into a deep sleep, and a thick and dreadful darkness came over him.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD said to him, "Know for certain that your descendants will be strangers in a country not their own, and they will be enslaved and mistreated four hundred years.

column.name: text
column.value: But I will punish the nation they serve as slaves, and afterward they will come out with great possessions.

column.name: text
column.value: You, however, will go to your fathers in peace and be buried at a good old age.

column.name: text
column.value: In the fourth generation your descendants will come back here, for the sin of the Amorites has not yet reached its full measure."

column.name: text
column.value: When the sun had set and darkness had fallen, a smoking firepot with a blazing torch appeared and passed between the pieces.

column.name: text
column.value: On that day the LORD made a covenant with Abram and said, "To your descendants I give this land, from the river of Egypt to the great river, the Euphrates--

column.name: text
column.value: the land of the Kenites, Kenizzites, Kadmonites,

column.name: text
column.value: Hittites, Perizzites, Rephaites,

column.name: text
column.value: Amorites, Canaanites, Girgashites and Jebusites."

column.name: text
column.value: When Abram was ninety-nine years old, the LORD appeared to him and said, "I am God Almighty; walk before me and be blameless.

column.name: text
column.value: I will confirm my covenant between me and you and will greatly increase your numbers."

column.name: text
column.value: Abram fell facedown, and God said to him,

column.name: text
column.value: "As for me, this is my covenant with you: You will be the father of many nations.

column.name: text
column.value: No longer will you be called Abram; your name will be Abraham, for I have made you a father of many nations.

column.name: text
column.value: I will make you very fruitful; I will make nations of you, and kings will come from you.

column.name: text
column.value: I will establish my covenant as an everlasting covenant between me and you and your descendants after you for the generations to come, to be your God and the God of your descendants after you.

column.name: text
column.value: The whole land of Canaan, where you are now an alien, I will give as an everlasting possession to you and your descendants after you; and I will be their God."

column.name: text
column.value: Then God said to Abraham, "As for you, you must keep my covenant, you and your descendants after you for the generations to come.

column.name: text
column.value: This is my covenant with you and your descendants after you, the covenant you are to keep: Every male among you shall be circumcised.

column.name: text
column.value: You are to undergo circumcision, and it will be the sign of the covenant between me and you.

column.name: text
column.value: For the generations to come every male among you who is eight days old must be circumcised, including those born in your household or bought with money from a foreigner--those who are not your offspring.

column.name: text
column.value: Whether born in your household or bought with your money, they must be circumcised. My covenant in your flesh is to be an everlasting covenant.

column.name: text
column.value: Any uncircumcised male, who has not been circumcised in the flesh, will be cut off from his people; he has broken my covenant."

column.name: text
column.value: God also said to Abraham, "As for Sarai your wife, you are no longer to call her Sarai; her name will be Sarah.

column.name: text
column.value: I will bless her and will surely give you a son by her. I will bless her so that she will be the mother of nations; kings of peoples will come from her."

column.name: text
column.value: Abraham fell facedown; he laughed and said to himself, "Will a son be born to a man a hundred years old? Will Sarah bear a child at the age of ninety?"

column.name: text
column.value: And Abraham said to God, "If only Ishmael might live under your blessing!"

column.name: text
column.value: Then God said, "Yes, but your wife Sarah will bear you a son, and you will call him Isaac. I will establish my covenant with him as an everlasting covenant for his descendants after him.

column.name: text
column.value: And as for Ishmael, I have heard you: I will surely bless him; I will make him fruitful and will greatly increase his numbers. He will be the father of twelve rulers, and I will make him into a great nation.

column.name: text
column.value: But my covenant I will establish with Isaac, whom Sarah will bear to you by this time next year."

column.name: text
column.value: When he had finished speaking with Abraham, God went up from him.

column.name: text
column.value: On that very day Abraham took his son Ishmael and all those born in his household or bought with his money, every male in his household, and circumcised them, as God told him.

column.name: text
column.value: Abraham was ninety-nine years old when he was circumcised,

column.name: text
column.value: and his son Ishmael was thirteen;

column.name: text
column.value: Abraham and his son Ishmael were both circumcised on that same day.

column.name: text
column.value: And every male in Abraham's household, including those born in his household or bought from a foreigner, was circumcised with him.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD appeared to Abraham near the great trees of Mamre while he was sitting at the entrance to his tent in the heat of the day.

column.name: text
column.value: Abraham looked up and saw three men standing nearby. When he saw them, he hurried from the entrance of his tent to meet them and bowed low to the ground.

column.name: text
column.value: He said, "If I have found favor in your eyes, my lord, do not pass your servant by.

column.name: text
column.value: Let a little water be brought, and then you may all wash your feet and rest under this tree.

column.name: text
column.value: Let me get you something to eat, so you can be refreshed and then go on your way--now that you have come to your servant." "Very well," they answered, "do as you say."

column.name: text
column.value: So Abraham hurried into the tent to Sarah. "Quick," he said, "get three seahs of fine flour and knead it and bake some bread."

column.name: text
column.value: Then he ran to the herd and selected a choice, tender calf and gave it to a servant, who hurried to prepare it.

column.name: text
column.value: He then brought some curds and milk and the calf that had been prepared, and set these before them. While they ate, he stood near them under a tree.

column.name: text
column.value: "Where is your wife Sarah?" they asked him. "There, in the tent," he said.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD said, "I will surely return to you about this time next year, and Sarah your wife will have a son." Now Sarah was listening at the entrance to the tent, which was behind him.

column.name: text
column.value: Abraham and Sarah were already old and well advanced in years, and Sarah was past the age of childbearing.

column.name: text
column.value: So Sarah laughed to herself as she thought, "After I am worn out and my master is old, will I now have this pleasure?"

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD said to Abraham, "Why did Sarah laugh and say, 'Will I really have a child, now that I am old?'

column.name: text
column.value: Is anything too hard for the LORD? I will return to you at the appointed time next year and Sarah will have a son."

column.name: text
column.value: Sarah was afraid, so she lied and said, "I did not laugh." But he said, "Yes, you did laugh."

column.name: text
column.value: When the men got up to leave, they looked down toward Sodom, and Abraham walked along with them to see them on their way.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD said, "Shall I hide from Abraham what I am about to do?

column.name: text
column.value: Abraham will surely become a great and powerful nation, and all nations on earth will be blessed through him.

column.name: text
column.value: For I have chosen him, so that he will direct his children and his household after him to keep the way of the LORD by doing what is right and just, so that the LORD will bring about for Abraham what he has promised him."

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD said, "The outcry against Sodom and Gomorrah is so great and their sin so grievous

column.name: text
column.value: that I will go down and see if what they have done is as bad as the outcry that has reached me. If not, I will know."

column.name: text
column.value: The men turned away and went toward Sodom, but Abraham remained standing before the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Abraham approached him and said: "Will you sweep away the righteous with the wicked?

column.name: text
column.value: What if there are fifty righteous people in the city? Will you really sweep it away and not spare the place for the sake of the fifty righteous people in it?

column.name: text
column.value: Far be it from you to do such a thing--to kill the righteous with the wicked, treating the righteous and the wicked alike. Far be it from you! Will not the Judge of all the earth do right?"

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD said, "If I find fifty righteous people in the city of Sodom, I will spare the whole place for their sake."

column.name: text
column.value: Then Abraham spoke up again: "Now that I have been so bold as to speak to the Lord, though I am nothing but dust and ashes,

column.name: text
column.value: what if the number of the righteous is five less than fifty? Will you destroy the whole city because of five people?" "If I find forty-five there," he said, "I will not destroy it."

column.name: text
column.value: Once again he spoke to him, "What if only forty are found there?" He said, "For the sake of forty, I will not do it."

column.name: text
column.value: Then he said, "May the Lord not be angry, but let me speak. What if only thirty can be found there?" He answered, "I will not do it if I find thirty there."

column.name: text
column.value: Abraham said, "Now that I have been so bold as to speak to the Lord, what if only twenty can be found there?" He said, "For the sake of twenty, I will not destroy it."

column.name: text
column.value: Then he said, "May the Lord not be angry, but let me speak just once more. What if only ten can be found there?" He answered, "For the sake of ten, I will not destroy it."

column.name: text
column.value: When the LORD had finished speaking with Abraham, he left, and Abraham returned home.

column.name: text
column.value: Now Abraham moved on from there into the region of the Negev and lived between Kadesh and Shur. For a while he stayed in Gerar,

column.name: text
column.value: and there Abraham said of his wife Sarah, "She is my sister." Then Abimelech king of Gerar sent for Sarah and took her.

column.name: text
column.value: But God came to Abimelech in a dream one night and said to him, "You are as good as dead because of the woman you have taken; she is a married woman."

column.name: text
column.value: Now Abimelech had not gone near her, so he said, "Lord, will you destroy an innocent nation?

column.name: text
column.value: Did he not say to me, 'She is my sister,' and didn't she also say, 'He is my brother'? I have done this with a clear conscience and clean hands."

column.name: text
column.value: Then God said to him in the dream, "Yes, I know you did this with a clear conscience, and so I have kept you from sinning against me. That is why I did not let you touch her.

column.name: text
column.value: Now return the man's wife, for he is a prophet, and he will pray for you and you will live. But if you do not return her, you may be sure that you and all yours will die."

column.name: text
column.value: Early the next morning Abimelech summoned all his officials, and when he told them all that had happened, they were very much afraid.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Abimelech called Abraham in and said, "What have you done to us? How have I wronged you that you have brought such great guilt upon me and my kingdom? You have done things to me that should not be done."

column.name: text
column.value: And Abimelech asked Abraham, "What was your reason for doing this?"

column.name: text
column.value: Abraham replied, "I said to myself, 'There is surely no fear of God in this place, and they will kill me because of my wife.'

column.name: text
column.value: Besides, she really is my sister, the daughter of my father though not of my mother; and she became my wife.

column.name: text
column.value: And when God had me wander from my father's household, I said to her, 'This is how you can show your love to me: Everywhere we go, say of me, "He is my brother." '"

column.name: text
column.value: Then Abimelech brought sheep and cattle and male and female slaves and gave them to Abraham, and he returned Sarah his wife to him.

column.name: text
column.value: And Abimelech said, "My land is before you; live wherever you like."

column.name: text
column.value: To Sarah he said, "I am giving your brother a thousand shekels of silver. This is to cover the offense against you before all who are with you; you are completely vindicated."

column.name: text
column.value: Then Abraham prayed to God, and God healed Abimelech, his wife and his slave girls so they could have children again,

column.name: text
column.value: for the LORD had closed up every womb in Abimelech's household because of Abraham's wife Sarah.

column.name: text
column.value: Some time later God tested Abraham. He said to him, "Abraham!" "Here I am," he replied.

column.name: text
column.value: Then God said, "Take your son, your only son, Isaac, whom you love, and go to the region of Moriah. Sacrifice him there as a burnt offering on one of the mountains I will tell you about."

column.name: text
column.value: Early the next morning Abraham got up and saddled his donkey. He took with him two of his servants and his son Isaac. When he had cut enough wood for the burnt offering, he set out for the place God had told him about.

column.name: text
column.value: On the third day Abraham looked up and saw the place in the distance.

column.name: text
column.value: He said to his servants, "Stay here with the donkey while I and the boy go over there. We will worship and then we will come back to you."

column.name: text
column.value: Abraham took the wood for the burnt offering and placed it on his son Isaac, and he himself carried the fire and the knife. As the two of them went on together,

column.name: text
column.value: Isaac spoke up and said to his father Abraham, "Father?" "Yes, my son?" Abraham replied. "The fire and wood are here," Isaac said, "but where is the lamb for the burnt offering?"

column.name: text
column.value: Abraham answered, "God himself will provide the lamb for the burnt offering, my son." And the two of them went on together.

column.name: text
column.value: When they reached the place God had told him about, Abraham built an altar there and arranged the wood on it. He bound his son Isaac and laid him on the altar, on top of the wood.

column.name: text
column.value: Then he reached out his hand and took the knife to slay his son.

column.name: text
column.value: But the angel of the LORD called out to him from heaven, "Abraham! Abraham!" "Here I am," he replied.

column.name: text
column.value: "Do not lay a hand on the boy," he said. "Do not do anything to him. Now I know that you fear God, because you have not withheld from me your son, your only son."

column.name: text
column.value: Abraham looked up and there in a thicket he saw a ram caught by its horns. He went over and took the ram and sacrificed it as a burnt offering instead of his son.

column.name: text
column.value: So Abraham called that place The LORD Will Provide. And to this day it is said, "On the mountain of the LORD it will be provided."

column.name: text
column.value: The angel of the LORD called to Abraham from heaven a second time

column.name: text
column.value: and said, "I swear by myself, declares the LORD, that because you have done this and have not withheld your son, your only son,

column.name: text
column.value: I will surely bless you and make your descendants as numerous as the stars in the sky and as the sand on the seashore. Your descendants will take possession of the cities of their enemies,

column.name: text
column.value: and through your offspring all nations on earth will be blessed, because you have obeyed me."

column.name: text
column.value: Then Abraham returned to his servants, and they set off together for Beersheba. And Abraham stayed in Beersheba.

column.name: text
column.value: Some time later Abraham was told, "Milcah is also a mother; she has borne sons to your brother Nahor:

column.name: text
column.value: Uz the firstborn, Buz his brother, Kemuel (the father of Aram),

column.name: text
column.value: Kesed, Hazo, Pildash, Jidlaph and Bethuel."

column.name: text
column.value: Bethuel became the father of Rebekah. Milcah bore these eight sons to Abraham's brother Nahor.

column.name: text
column.value: His concubine, whose name was Reumah, also had sons: Tebah, Gaham, Tahash and Maacah.

column.name: text
column.value: Now the LORD was gracious to Sarah as he had said, and the LORD did for Sarah what he had promised.

column.name: text
column.value: Sarah became pregnant and bore a son to Abraham in his old age, at the very time God had promised him.

column.name: text
column.value: Abraham gave the name Isaac to the son Sarah bore him.

column.name: text
column.value: When his son Isaac was eight days old, Abraham circumcised him, as God commanded him.

column.name: text
column.value: Abraham was a hundred years old when his son Isaac was born to him.

column.name: text
column.value: Sarah said, "God has brought me laughter, and everyone who hears about this will laugh with me."

column.name: text
column.value: And she added, "Who would have said to Abraham that Sarah would nurse children? Yet I have borne him a son in his old age."

column.name: text
column.value: The child grew and was weaned, and on the day Isaac was weaned Abraham held a great feast.

column.name: text
column.value: But Sarah saw that the son whom Hagar the Egyptian had borne to Abraham was mocking,

column.name: text
column.value: and she said to Abraham, "Get rid of that slave woman and her son, for that slave woman's son will never share in the inheritance with my son Isaac."

column.name: text
column.value: The matter distressed Abraham greatly because it concerned his son.

column.name: text
column.value: But God said to him, "Do not be so distressed about the boy and your maidservant. Listen to whatever Sarah tells you, because it is through Isaac that your offspring will be reckoned.

column.name: text
column.value: I will make the son of the maidservant into a nation also, because he is your offspring."

column.name: text
column.value: Early the next morning Abraham took some food and a skin of water and gave them to Hagar. He set them on her shoulders and then sent her off with the boy. She went on her way and wandered in the desert of Beersheba.

column.name: text
column.value: When the water in the skin was gone, she put the boy under one of the bushes.

column.name: text
column.value: Then she went off and sat down nearby, about a bowshot away, for she thought, "I cannot watch the boy die." And as she sat there nearby, she began to sob.

column.name: text
column.value: God heard the boy crying, and the angel of God called to Hagar from heaven and said to her, "What is the matter, Hagar? Do not be afraid; God has heard the boy crying as he lies there.

column.name: text
column.value: Lift the boy up and take him by the hand, for I will make him into a great nation."

column.name: text
column.value: Then God opened her eyes and she saw a well of water. So she went and filled the skin with water and gave the boy a drink.

column.name: text
column.value: God was with the boy as he grew up. He lived in the desert and became an archer.

column.name: text
column.value: While he was living in the Desert of Paran, his mother got a wife for him from Egypt.

column.name: text
column.value: At that time Abimelech and Phicol the commander of his forces said to Abraham, "God is with you in everything you do.

column.name: text
column.value: Now swear to me here before God that you will not deal falsely with me or my children or my descendants. Show to me and the country where you are living as an alien the same kindness I have shown to you."

column.name: text
column.value: Abraham said, "I swear it."

column.name: text
column.value: Then Abraham complained to Abimelech about a well of water that Abimelech's servants had seized.

column.name: text
column.value: But Abimelech said, "I don't know who has done this. You did not tell me, and I heard about it only today."

column.name: text
column.value: So Abraham brought sheep and cattle and gave them to Abimelech, and the two men made a treaty.

column.name: text
column.value: Abraham set apart seven ewe lambs from the flock,

column.name: text
column.value: and Abimelech asked Abraham, "What is the meaning of these seven ewe lambs you have set apart by themselves?"

column.name: text
column.value: He replied, "Accept these seven lambs from my hand as a witness that I dug this well."

column.name: text
column.value: So that place was called Beersheba, because the two men swore an oath there.

column.name: text
column.value: After the treaty had been made at Beersheba, Abimelech and Phicol the commander of his forces returned to the land of the Philistines.

column.name: text
column.value: Abraham planted a tamarisk tree in Beersheba, and there he called upon the name of the LORD, the Eternal God.

column.name: text
column.value: And Abraham stayed in the land of the Philistines for a long time.

column.name: text
column.value: Now Sarai, Abram's wife, had borne him no children. But she had an Egyptian maidservant named Hagar;

column.name: text
column.value: so she said to Abram, "The LORD has kept me from having children. Go, sleep with my maidservant; perhaps I can build a family through her." Abram agreed to what Sarai said.

column.name: text
column.value: So after Abram had been living in Canaan ten years, Sarai his wife took her Egyptian maidservant Hagar and gave her to her husband to be his wife.

column.name: text
column.value: He slept with Hagar, and she conceived. When she knew she was pregnant, she began to despise her mistress.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Sarai said to Abram, "You are responsible for the wrong I am suffering. I put my servant in your arms, and now that she knows she is pregnant, she despises me. May the LORD judge between you and me."

column.name: text
column.value: "Your servant is in your hands," Abram said. "Do with her whatever you think best." Then Sarai mistreated Hagar; so she fled from her.

column.name: text
column.value: The angel of the LORD found Hagar near a spring in the desert; it was the spring that is beside the road to Shur.

column.name: text
column.value: And he said, "Hagar, servant of Sarai, where have you come from, and where are you going?" "I'm running away from my mistress Sarai," she answered.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the angel of the LORD told her, "Go back to your mistress and submit to her."

column.name: text
column.value: The angel added, "I will so increase your descendants that they will be too numerous to count."

column.name: text
column.value: The angel of the LORD also said to her: "You are now with child and you will have a son. You shall name him Ishmael, for the LORD has heard of your misery.

column.name: text
column.value: He will be a wild donkey of a man; his hand will be against everyone and everyone's hand against him, and he will live in hostility toward all his brothers."

column.name: text
column.value: She gave this name to the LORD who spoke to her: "You are the God who sees me," for she said, "I have now seen the One who sees me."

column.name: text
column.value: That is why the well was called Beer Lahai Roi; it is still there, between Kadesh and Bered.

column.name: text
column.value: So Hagar bore Abram a son, and Abram gave the name Ishmael to the son she had borne.

column.name: text
column.value: Abram was eighty-six years old when Hagar bore him Ishmael.

column.name: text
column.value: Sarah lived to be a hundred and twenty-seven years old.

column.name: text
column.value: She died at Kiriath Arba (that is, Hebron) in the land of Canaan, and Abraham went to mourn for Sarah and to weep over her.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Abraham rose from beside his dead wife and spoke to the Hittites. He said,

column.name: text
column.value: "I am an alien and a stranger among you. Sell me some property for a burial site here so I can bury my dead."

column.name: text
column.value: The Hittites replied to Abraham,

column.name: text
column.value: "Sir, listen to us. You are a mighty prince among us. Bury your dead in the choicest of our tombs. None of us will refuse you his tomb for burying your dead."

column.name: text
column.value: Then Abraham rose and bowed down before the people of the land, the Hittites.

column.name: text
