column.value: He said to them, "If you are willing to let me bury my dead, then listen to me and intercede with Ephron son of Zohar on my behalf

column.name: text
column.value: so he will sell me the cave of Machpelah, which belongs to him and is at the end of his field. Ask him to sell it to me for the full price as a burial site among you."

column.name: text
column.value: Ephron the Hittite was sitting among his people and he replied to Abraham in the hearing of all the Hittites who had come to the gate of his city.

column.name: text
column.value: "No, my lord," he said. "Listen to me; I give you the field, and I give you the cave that is in it. I give it to you in the presence of my people. Bury your dead."

column.name: text
column.value: Again Abraham bowed down before the people of the land

column.name: text
column.value: and he said to Ephron in their hearing, "Listen to me, if you will. I will pay the price of the field. Accept it from me so I can bury my dead there."

column.name: text
column.value: Ephron answered Abraham,

column.name: text
column.value: "Listen to me, my lord; the land is worth four hundred shekels of silver, but what is that between me and you? Bury your dead."

column.name: text
column.value: Abraham agreed to Ephron's terms and weighed out for him the price he had named in the hearing of the Hittites: four hundred shekels of silver, according to the weight current among the merchants.

column.name: text
column.value: So Ephron's field in Machpelah near Mamre--both the field and the cave in it, and all the trees within the borders of the field--was deeded

column.name: text
column.value: to Abraham as his property in the presence of all the Hittites who had come to the gate of the city.

column.name: text
column.value: Afterward Abraham buried his wife Sarah in the cave in the field of Machpelah near Mamre (which is at Hebron) in the land of Canaan.

column.name: text
column.value: So the field and the cave in it were deeded to Abraham by the Hittites as a burial site.

column.name: text
column.value: The two angels arrived at Sodom in the evening, and Lot was sitting in the gateway of the city. When he saw them, he got up to meet them and bowed down with his face to the ground.

column.name: text
column.value: "My lords," he said, "please turn aside to your servant's house. You can wash your feet and spend the night and then go on your way early in the morning." "No," they answered, "we will spend the night in the square."

column.name: text
column.value: But he insisted so strongly that they did go with him and entered his house. He prepared a meal for them, baking bread without yeast, and they ate.

column.name: text
column.value: Before they had gone to bed, all the men from every part of the city of Sodom--both young and old--surrounded the house.

column.name: text
column.value: They called to Lot, "Where are the men who came to you tonight? Bring them out to us so that we can have sex with them."

column.name: text
column.value: Lot went outside to meet them and shut the door behind him

column.name: text
column.value: and said, "No, my friends. Don't do this wicked thing.

column.name: text
column.value: Look, I have two daughters who have never slept with a man. Let me bring them out to you, and you can do what you like with them. But don't do anything to these men, for they have come under the protection of my roof."

column.name: text
column.value: "Get out of our way," they replied. And they said, "This fellow came here as an alien, and now he wants to play the judge! We'll treat you worse than them." They kept bringing pressure on Lot and moved forward to break down the door.

column.name: text
column.value: But the men inside reached out and pulled Lot back into the house and shut the door.

column.name: text
column.value: Then they struck the men who were at the door of the house, young and old, with blindness so that they could not find the door.

column.name: text
column.value: The two men said to Lot, "Do you have anyone else here--sons-in-law, sons or daughters, or anyone else in the city who belongs to you? Get them out of here,

column.name: text
column.value: because we are going to destroy this place. The outcry to the LORD against its people is so great that he has sent us to destroy it."

column.name: text
column.value: So Lot went out and spoke to his sons-in-law, who were pledged to marry his daughters. He said, "Hurry and get out of this place, because the LORD is about to destroy the city!" But his sons-in-law thought he was joking.

column.name: text
column.value: With the coming of dawn, the angels urged Lot, saying, "Hurry! Take your wife and your two daughters who are here, or you will be swept away when the city is punished."

column.name: text
column.value: When he hesitated, the men grasped his hand and the hands of his wife and of his two daughters and led them safely out of the city, for the LORD was merciful to them.

column.name: text
column.value: As soon as they had brought them out, one of them said, "Flee for your lives! Don't look back, and don't stop anywhere in the plain! Flee to the mountains or you will be swept away!"

column.name: text
column.value: But Lot said to them, "No, my lords, please!

column.name: text
column.value: Your servant has found favor in your eyes, and you have shown great kindness to me in sparing my life. But I can't flee to the mountains; this disaster will overtake me, and I'll die.

column.name: text
column.value: Look, here is a town near enough to run to, and it is small. Let me flee to it--it is very small, isn't it? Then my life will be spared."

column.name: text
column.value: He said to him, "Very well, I will grant this request too; I will not overthrow the town you speak of.

column.name: text
column.value: But flee there quickly, because I cannot do anything until you reach it." (That is why the town was called Zoar.)

column.name: text
column.value: By the time Lot reached Zoar, the sun had risen over the land.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD rained down burning sulfur on Sodom and Gomorrah--from the LORD out of the heavens.

column.name: text
column.value: Thus he overthrew those cities and the entire plain, including all those living in the cities--and also the vegetation in the land.

column.name: text
column.value: But Lot's wife looked back, and she became a pillar of salt.

column.name: text
column.value: Early the next morning Abraham got up and returned to the place where he had stood before the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: He looked down toward Sodom and Gomorrah, toward all the land of the plain, and he saw dense smoke rising from the land, like smoke from a furnace.

column.name: text
column.value: So when God destroyed the cities of the plain, he remembered Abraham, and he brought Lot out of the catastrophe that overthrew the cities where Lot had lived.

column.name: text
column.value: Lot and his two daughters left Zoar and settled in the mountains, for he was afraid to stay in Zoar. He and his two daughters lived in a cave.

column.name: text
column.value: One day the older daughter said to the younger, "Our father is old, and there is no man around here to lie with us, as is the custom all over the earth.

column.name: text
column.value: Let's get our father to drink wine and then lie with him and preserve our family line through our father."

column.name: text
column.value: That night they got their father to drink wine, and the older daughter went in and lay with him. He was not aware of it when she lay down or when she got up.

column.name: text
column.value: The next day the older daughter said to the younger, "Last night I lay with my father. Let's get him to drink wine again tonight, and you go in and lie with him so we can preserve our family line through our father."

column.name: text
column.value: So they got their father to drink wine that night also, and the younger daughter went and lay with him. Again he was not aware of it when she lay down or when she got up.

column.name: text
column.value: So both of Lot's daughters became pregnant by their father.

column.name: text
column.value: The older daughter had a son, and she named him Moab; he is the father of the Moabites of today.

column.name: text
column.value: The younger daughter also had a son, and she named him Ben-Ammi; he is the father of the Ammonites of today.

column.name: text
column.value: Abraham was now old and well advanced in years, and the LORD had blessed him in every way.

column.name: text
column.value: He said to the chief servant in his household, the one in charge of all that he had, "Put your hand under my thigh.

column.name: text
column.value: I want you to swear by the LORD, the God of heaven and the God of earth, that you will not get a wife for my son from the daughters of the Canaanites, among whom I am living,

column.name: text
column.value: but will go to my country and my own relatives and get a wife for my son Isaac."

column.name: text
column.value: The servant asked him, "What if the woman is unwilling to come back with me to this land? Shall I then take your son back to the country you came from?"

column.name: text
column.value: "Make sure that you do not take my son back there," Abraham said.

column.name: text
column.value: "The LORD, the God of heaven, who brought me out of my father's household and my native land and who spoke to me and promised me on oath, saying, 'To your offspring I will give this land'--he will send his angel before you so that you can get a wife for my son from there.

column.name: text
column.value: If the woman is unwilling to come back with you, then you will be released from this oath of mine. Only do not take my son back there."

column.name: text
column.value: So the servant put his hand under the thigh of his master Abraham and swore an oath to him concerning this matter.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the servant took ten of his master's camels and left, taking with him all kinds of good things from his master. He set out for Aram Naharaim and made his way to the town of Nahor.

column.name: text
column.value: He had the camels kneel down near the well outside the town; it was toward evening, the time the women go out to draw water.

column.name: text
column.value: Then he prayed, "O LORD, God of my master Abraham, give me success today, and show kindness to my master Abraham.

column.name: text
column.value: See, I am standing beside this spring, and the daughters of the townspeople are coming out to draw water.

column.name: text
column.value: May it be that when I say to a girl, 'Please let down your jar that I may have a drink,' and she says, 'Drink, and I'll water your camels too'--let her be the one you have chosen for your servant Isaac. By this I will know that you have shown kindness to my master."

column.name: text
column.value: Before he had finished praying, Rebekah came out with her jar on her shoulder. She was the daughter of Bethuel son of Milcah, who was the wife of Abraham's brother Nahor.

column.name: text
column.value: The girl was very beautiful, a virgin; no man had ever lain with her. She went down to the spring, filled her jar and came up again.

column.name: text
column.value: The servant hurried to meet her and said, "Please give me a little water from your jar."

column.name: text
column.value: "Drink, my lord," she said, and quickly lowered the jar to her hands and gave him a drink.

column.name: text
column.value: After she had given him a drink, she said, "I'll draw water for your camels too, until they have finished drinking."

column.name: text
column.value: So she quickly emptied her jar into the trough, ran back to the well to draw more water, and drew enough for all his camels.

column.name: text
column.value: Without saying a word, the man watched her closely to learn whether or not the LORD had made his journey successful.

column.name: text
column.value: When the camels had finished drinking, the man took out a gold nose ring weighing a beka and two gold bracelets weighing ten shekels.

column.name: text
column.value: Then he asked, "Whose daughter are you? Please tell me, is there room in your father's house for us to spend the night?"

column.name: text
column.value: She answered him, "I am the daughter of Bethuel, the son that Milcah bore to Nahor."

column.name: text
column.value: And she added, "We have plenty of straw and fodder, as well as room for you to spend the night."

column.name: text
column.value: Then the man bowed down and worshiped the LORD,

column.name: text
column.value: saying, "Praise be to the LORD, the God of my master Abraham, who has not abandoned his kindness and faithfulness to my master. As for me, the LORD has led me on the journey to the house of my master's relatives."

column.name: text
column.value: The girl ran and told her mother's household about these things.

column.name: text
column.value: Now Rebekah had a brother named Laban, and he hurried out to the man at the spring.

column.name: text
column.value: As soon as he had seen the nose ring, and the bracelets on his sister's arms, and had heard Rebekah tell what the man said to her, he went out to the man and found him standing by the camels near the spring.

column.name: text
column.value: "Come, you who are blessed by the LORD," he said. "Why are you standing out here? I have prepared the house and a place for the camels."

column.name: text
column.value: So the man went to the house, and the camels were unloaded. Straw and fodder were brought for the camels, and water for him and his men to wash their feet.

column.name: text
column.value: Then food was set before him, but he said, "I will not eat until I have told you what I have to say." "Then tell us," Laban said.

column.name: text
column.value: So he said, "I am Abraham's servant.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD has blessed my master abundantly, and he has become wealthy. He has given him sheep and cattle, silver and gold, menservants and maidservants, and camels and donkeys.

column.name: text
column.value: My master's wife Sarah has borne him a son in her old age, and he has given him everything he owns.

column.name: text
column.value: And my master made me swear an oath, and said, 'You must not get a wife for my son from the daughters of the Canaanites, in whose land I live,

column.name: text
column.value: but go to my father's family and to my own clan, and get a wife for my son.'

column.name: text
column.value: "Then I asked my master, 'What if the woman will not come back with me?'

column.name: text
column.value: "He replied, 'The LORD, before whom I have walked, will send his angel with you and make your journey a success, so that you can get a wife for my son from my own clan and from my father's family.

column.name: text
column.value: Then, when you go to my clan, you will be released from my oath even if they refuse to give her to you--you will be released from my oath.'

column.name: text
column.value: "When I came to the spring today, I said, 'O LORD, God of my master Abraham, if you will, please grant success to the journey on which I have come.

column.name: text
column.value: See, I am standing beside this spring; if a maiden comes out to draw water and I say to her, "Please let me drink a little water from your jar,"

column.name: text
column.value: and if she says to me, "Drink, and I'll draw water for your camels too," let her be the one the LORD has chosen for my master's son.'

column.name: text
column.value: "Before I finished praying in my heart, Rebekah came out, with her jar on her shoulder. She went down to the spring and drew water, and I said to her, 'Please give me a drink.'

column.name: text
column.value: "She quickly lowered her jar from her shoulder and said, 'Drink, and I'll water your camels too.' So I drank, and she watered the camels also.

column.name: text
column.value: "I asked her, 'Whose daughter are you?' "She said, 'The daughter of Bethuel son of Nahor, whom Milcah bore to him.' "Then I put the ring in her nose and the bracelets on her arms,

column.name: text
column.value: and I bowed down and worshiped the LORD. I praised the LORD, the God of my master Abraham, who had led me on the right road to get the granddaughter of my master's brother for his son.

column.name: text
column.value: Now if you will show kindness and faithfulness to my master, tell me; and if not, tell me, so I may know which way to turn."

column.name: text
column.value: Laban and Bethuel answered, "This is from the LORD; we can say nothing to you one way or the other.

column.name: text
column.value: Here is Rebekah; take her and go, and let her become the wife of your master's son, as the LORD has directed."

column.name: text
column.value: When Abraham's servant heard what they said, he bowed down to the ground before the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the servant brought out gold and silver jewelry and articles of clothing and gave them to Rebekah; he also gave costly gifts to her brother and to her mother.

column.name: text
column.value: Then he and the men who were with him ate and drank and spent the night there. When they got up the next morning, he said, "Send me on my way to my master."

column.name: text
column.value: But her brother and her mother replied, "Let the girl remain with us ten days or so; then you may go."

column.name: text
column.value: But he said to them, "Do not detain me, now that the LORD has granted success to my journey. Send me on my way so I may go to my master."

column.name: text
column.value: Then they said, "Let's call the girl and ask her about it."

column.name: text
column.value: So they called Rebekah and asked her, "Will you go with this man?" "I will go," she said.

column.name: text
column.value: So they sent their sister Rebekah on her way, along with her nurse and Abraham's servant and his men.

column.name: text
column.value: And they blessed Rebekah and said to her, "Our sister, may you increase to thousands upon thousands; may your offspring possess the gates of their enemies."

column.name: text
column.value: Then Rebekah and her maids got ready and mounted their camels and went back with the man. So the servant took Rebekah and left.

column.name: text
column.value: Now Isaac had come from Beer Lahai Roi, for he was living in the Negev.

column.name: text
column.value: He went out to the field one evening to meditate, and as he looked up, he saw camels approaching.

column.name: text
column.value: Rebekah also looked up and saw Isaac. She got down from her camel

column.name: text
column.value: and asked the servant, "Who is that man in the field coming to meet us?" "He is my master," the servant answered. So she took her veil and covered herself.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the servant told Isaac all he had done.

column.name: text
column.value: Isaac brought her into the tent of his mother Sarah, and he married Rebekah. So she became his wife, and he loved her; and Isaac was comforted after his mother's death.

column.name: text
column.value: Abraham took another wife, whose name was Keturah.

column.name: text
column.value: She bore him Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak and Shuah.

column.name: text
column.value: Jokshan was the father of Sheba and Dedan; the descendants of Dedan were the Asshurites, the Letushites and the Leummites.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Midian were Ephah, Epher, Hanoch, Abida and Eldaah. All these were descendants of Keturah.

column.name: text
column.value: Abraham left everything he owned to Isaac.

column.name: text
column.value: But while he was still living, he gave gifts to the sons of his concubines and sent them away from his son Isaac to the land of the east.

column.name: text
column.value: Altogether, Abraham lived a hundred and seventy-five years.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Abraham breathed his last and died at a good old age, an old man and full of years; and he was gathered to his people.

column.name: text
column.value: His sons Isaac and Ishmael buried him in the cave of Machpelah near Mamre, in the field of Ephron son of Zohar the Hittite,

column.name: text
column.value: the field Abraham had bought from the Hittites. There Abraham was buried with his wife Sarah.

column.name: text
column.value: After Abraham's death, God blessed his son Isaac, who then lived near Beer Lahai Roi.

column.name: text
column.value: This is the account of Abraham's son Ishmael, whom Sarah's maidservant, Hagar the Egyptian, bore to Abraham.

column.name: text
column.value: These are the names of the sons of Ishmael, listed in the order of their birth: Nebaioth the firstborn of Ishmael, Kedar, Adbeel, Mibsam,

column.name: text
column.value: Mishma, Dumah, Massa,

column.name: text
column.value: Hadad, Tema, Jetur, Naphish and Kedemah.

column.name: text
column.value: These were the sons of Ishmael, and these are the names of the twelve tribal rulers according to their settlements and camps.

column.name: text
column.value: Altogether, Ishmael lived a hundred and thirty-seven years. He breathed his last and died, and he was gathered to his people.

column.name: text
column.value: His descendants settled in the area from Havilah to Shur, near the border of Egypt, as you go toward Asshur. And they lived in hostility toward all their brothers.

column.name: text
column.value: This is the account of Abraham's son Isaac. Abraham became the father of Isaac,

column.name: text
column.value: and Isaac was forty years old when he married Rebekah daughter of Bethuel the Aramean from Paddan Aram and sister of Laban the Aramean.

column.name: text
column.value: Isaac prayed to the LORD on behalf of his wife, because she was barren. The LORD answered his prayer, and his wife Rebekah became pregnant.

column.name: text
column.value: The babies jostled each other within her, and she said, "Why is this happening to me?" So she went to inquire of the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD said to her, "Two nations are in your womb, and two peoples from within you will be separated; one people will be stronger than the other, and the older will serve the younger."

column.name: text
column.value: When the time came for her to give birth, there were twin boys in her womb.

column.name: text
column.value: The first to come out was red, and his whole body was like a hairy garment; so they named him Esau.

column.name: text
column.value: After this, his brother came out, with his hand grasping Esau's heel; so he was named Jacob. Isaac was sixty years old when Rebekah gave birth to them.

column.name: text
column.value: The boys grew up, and Esau became a skillful hunter, a man of the open country, while Jacob was a quiet man, staying among the tents.

column.name: text
column.value: Isaac, who had a taste for wild game, loved Esau, but Rebekah loved Jacob.

column.name: text
column.value: Once when Jacob was cooking some stew, Esau came in from the open country, famished.

column.name: text
column.value: He said to Jacob, "Quick, let me have some of that red stew! I'm famished!" (That is why he was also called Edom.)

column.name: text
column.value: Jacob replied, "First sell me your birthright."

column.name: text
column.value: "Look, I am about to die," Esau said. "What good is the birthright to me?"

column.name: text
column.value: But Jacob said, "Swear to me first." So he swore an oath to him, selling his birthright to Jacob.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jacob gave Esau some bread and some lentil stew. He ate and drank, and then got up and left. So Esau despised his birthright.

column.name: text
column.value: Now there was a famine in the land--besides the earlier famine of Abraham's time--and Isaac went to Abimelech king of the Philistines in Gerar.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD appeared to Isaac and said, "Do not go down to Egypt; live in the land where I tell you to live.

column.name: text
column.value: Stay in this land for a while, and I will be with you and will bless you. For to you and your descendants I will give all these lands and will confirm the oath I swore to your father Abraham.

column.name: text
column.value: I will make your descendants as numerous as the stars in the sky and will give them all these lands, and through your offspring all nations on earth will be blessed,

column.name: text
column.value: because Abraham obeyed me and kept my requirements, my commands, my decrees and my laws."

column.name: text
column.value: So Isaac stayed in Gerar.

column.name: text
column.value: When the men of that place asked him about his wife, he said, "She is my sister," because he was afraid to say, "She is my wife." He thought, "The men of this place might kill me on account of Rebekah, because she is beautiful."

column.name: text
column.value: When Isaac had been there a long time, Abimelech king of the Philistines looked down from a window and saw Isaac caressing his wife Rebekah.

column.name: text
column.value: So Abimelech summoned Isaac and said, "She is really your wife! Why did you say, 'She is my sister'?" Isaac answered him, "Because I thought I might lose my life on account of her."

column.name: text
column.value: Then Abimelech said, "What is this you have done to us? One of the men might well have slept with your wife, and you would have brought guilt upon us."

column.name: text
column.value: So Abimelech gave orders to all the people: "Anyone who molests this man or his wife shall surely be put to death."

column.name: text
column.value: Isaac planted crops in that land and the same year reaped a hundredfold, because the LORD blessed him.

column.name: text
column.value: The man became rich, and his wealth continued to grow until he became very wealthy.

column.name: text
column.value: He had so many flocks and herds and servants that the Philistines envied him.

column.name: text
column.value: So all the wells that his father's servants had dug in the time of his father Abraham, the Philistines stopped up, filling them with earth.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Abimelech said to Isaac, "Move away from us; you have become too powerful for us."

column.name: text
column.value: So Isaac moved away from there and encamped in the Valley of Gerar and settled there.

column.name: text
column.value: Isaac reopened the wells that had been dug in the time of his father Abraham, which the Philistines had stopped up after Abraham died, and he gave them the same names his father had given them.

column.name: text
column.value: Isaac's servants dug in the valley and discovered a well of fresh water there.

column.name: text
column.value: But the herdsmen of Gerar quarreled with Isaac's herdsmen and said, "The water is ours!" So he named the well Esek, because they disputed with him.

column.name: text
column.value: Then they dug another well, but they quarreled over that one also; so he named it Sitnah.

column.name: text
column.value: He moved on from there and dug another well, and no one quarreled over it. He named it Rehoboth, saying, "Now the LORD has given us room and we will flourish in the land."

column.name: text
column.value: From there he went up to Beersheba.

column.name: text
column.value: That night the LORD appeared to him and said, "I am the God of your father Abraham. Do not be afraid, for I am with you; I will bless you and will increase the number of your descendants for the sake of my servant Abraham."

column.name: text
column.value: Isaac built an altar there and called on the name of the LORD. There he pitched his tent, and there his servants dug a well.

column.name: text
column.value: Meanwhile, Abimelech had come to him from Gerar, with Ahuzzath his personal adviser and Phicol the commander of his forces.

column.name: text
column.value: Isaac asked them, "Why have you come to me, since you were hostile to me and sent me away?"

column.name: text
column.value: They answered, "We saw clearly that the LORD was with you; so we said, 'There ought to be a sworn agreement between us'--between us and you. Let us make a treaty with you

column.name: text
column.value: that you will do us no harm, just as we did not molest you but always treated you well and sent you away in peace. And now you are blessed by the LORD."

column.name: text
column.value: Isaac then made a feast for them, and they ate and drank.

column.name: text
column.value: Early the next morning the men swore an oath to each other. Then Isaac sent them on their way, and they left him in peace.

column.name: text
column.value: That day Isaac's servants came and told him about the well they had dug. They said, "We've found water!"

column.name: text
column.value: He called it Shibah, and to this day the name of the town has been Beersheba.

column.name: text
column.value: When Esau was forty years old, he married Judith daughter of Beeri the Hittite, and also Basemath daughter of Elon the Hittite.

column.name: text
column.value: They were a source of grief to Isaac and Rebekah.

column.name: text
column.value: So Isaac called for Jacob and blessed him and commanded him: "Do not marry a Canaanite woman.

column.name: text
column.value: Go at once to Paddan Aram, to the house of your mother's father Bethuel. Take a wife for yourself there, from among the daughters of Laban, your mother's brother.

column.name: text
column.value: May God Almighty bless you and make you fruitful and increase your numbers until you become a community of peoples.

column.name: text
column.value: May he give you and your descendants the blessing given to Abraham, so that you may take possession of the land where you now live as an alien, the land God gave to Abraham."

column.name: text
column.value: Then Isaac sent Jacob on his way, and he went to Paddan Aram, to Laban son of Bethuel the Aramean, the brother of Rebekah, who was the mother of Jacob and Esau.

column.name: text
column.value: Now Esau learned that Isaac had blessed Jacob and had sent him to Paddan Aram to take a wife from there, and that when he blessed him he commanded him, "Do not marry a Canaanite woman,"

column.name: text
column.value: and that Jacob had obeyed his father and mother and had gone to Paddan Aram.

column.name: text
column.value: Esau then realized how displeasing the Canaanite women were to his father Isaac;

column.name: text
column.value: so he went to Ishmael and married Mahalath, the sister of Nebaioth and daughter of Ishmael son of Abraham, in addition to the wives he already had.

column.name: text
column.value: Jacob left Beersheba and set out for Haran.

column.name: text
column.value: When he reached a certain place, he stopped for the night because the sun had set. Taking one of the stones there, he put it under his head and lay down to sleep.

column.name: text
column.value: He had a dream in which he saw a stairway resting on the earth, with its top reaching to heaven, and the angels of God were ascending and descending on it.

column.name: text
column.value: There above it stood the LORD, and he said: "I am the LORD, the God of your father Abraham and the God of Isaac. I will give you and your descendants the land on which you are lying.

column.name: text
column.value: Your descendants will be like the dust of the earth, and you will spread out to the west and to the east, to the north and to the south. All peoples on earth will be blessed through you and your offspring.

column.name: text
column.value: I am with you and will watch over you wherever you go, and I will bring you back to this land. I will not leave you until I have done what I have promised you."

column.name: text
column.value: When Jacob awoke from his sleep, he thought, "Surely the LORD is in this place, and I was not aware of it."

column.name: text
column.value: He was afraid and said, "How awesome is this place! This is none other than the house of God; this is the gate of heaven."

column.name: text
column.value: Early the next morning Jacob took the stone he had placed under his head and set it up as a pillar and poured oil on top of it.

column.name: text
column.value: He called that place Bethel, though the city used to be called Luz.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jacob made a vow, saying, "If God will be with me and will watch over me on this journey I am taking and will give me food to eat and clothes to wear

column.name: text
column.value: so that I return safely to my father's house, then the LORD will be my God

column.name: text
column.value: and this stone that I have set up as a pillar will be God's house, and of all that you give me I will give you a tenth."

column.name: text
column.value: When Isaac was old and his eyes were so weak that he could no longer see, he called for Esau his older son and said to him, "My son." "Here I am," he answered.

column.name: text
column.value: Isaac said, "I am now an old man and don't know the day of my death.

column.name: text
column.value: Now then, get your weapons--your quiver and bow--and go out to the open country to hunt some wild game for me.

column.name: text
column.value: Prepare me the kind of tasty food I like and bring it to me to eat, so that I may give you my blessing before I die."

column.name: text
column.value: Now Rebekah was listening as Isaac spoke to his son Esau. When Esau left for the open country to hunt game and bring it back,

column.name: text
column.value: Rebekah said to her son Jacob, "Look, I overheard your father say to your brother Esau,

column.name: text
column.value: 'Bring me some game and prepare me some tasty food to eat, so that I may give you my blessing in the presence of the LORD before I die.'

column.name: text
column.value: Now, my son, listen carefully and do what I tell you:

column.name: text
column.value: Go out to the flock and bring me two choice young goats, so I can prepare some tasty food for your father, just the way he likes it.

column.name: text
column.value: Then take it to your father to eat, so that he may give you his blessing before he dies."

column.name: text
column.value: Jacob said to Rebekah his mother, "But my brother Esau is a hairy man, and I'm a man with smooth skin.

column.name: text
column.value: What if my father touches me? I would appear to be tricking him and would bring down a curse on myself rather than a blessing."

column.name: text
column.value: His mother said to him, "My son, let the curse fall on me. Just do what I say; go and get them for me."

column.name: text
column.value: So he went and got them and brought them to his mother, and she prepared some tasty food, just the way his father liked it.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Rebekah took the best clothes of Esau her older son, which she had in the house, and put them on her younger son Jacob.

column.name: text
column.value: She also covered his hands and the smooth part of his neck with the goatskins.

column.name: text
column.value: Then she handed to her son Jacob the tasty food and the bread she had made.

column.name: text
column.value: He went to his father and said, "My father." "Yes, my son," he answered. "Who is it?"

column.name: text
column.value: Jacob said to his father, "I am Esau your firstborn. I have done as you told me. Please sit up and eat some of my game so that you may give me your blessing."

column.name: text
column.value: Isaac asked his son, "How did you find it so quickly, my son?" "The LORD your God gave me success," he replied.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Isaac said to Jacob, "Come near so I can touch you, my son, to know whether you really are my son Esau or not."

column.name: text
column.value: Jacob went close to his father Isaac, who touched him and said, "The voice is the voice of Jacob, but the hands are the hands of Esau."

column.name: text
column.value: He did not recognize him, for his hands were hairy like those of his brother Esau; so he blessed him.

column.name: text
column.value: "Are you really my son Esau?" he asked. "I am," he replied.

column.name: text
column.value: Then he said, "My son, bring me some of your game to eat, so that I may give you my blessing." Jacob brought it to him and he ate; and he brought some wine and he drank.

column.name: text
column.value: Then his father Isaac said to him, "Come here, my son, and kiss me."

column.name: text
column.value: So he went to him and kissed him. When Isaac caught the smell of his clothes, he blessed him and said, "Ah, the smell of my son is like the smell of a field that the LORD has blessed.

column.name: text
column.value: May God give you of heaven's dew and of earth's richness--an abundance of grain and new wine.

column.name: text
column.value: May nations serve you and peoples bow down to you. Be lord over your brothers, and may the sons of your mother bow down to you. May those who curse you be cursed and those who bless you be blessed."

column.name: text
column.value: After Isaac finished blessing him and Jacob had scarcely left his father's presence, his brother Esau came in from hunting.

column.name: text
column.value: He too prepared some tasty food and brought it to his father. Then he said to him, "My father, sit up and eat some of my game, so that you may give me your blessing."

column.name: text
column.value: His father Isaac asked him, "Who are you?" "I am your son," he answered, "your firstborn, Esau."

column.name: text
column.value: Isaac trembled violently and said, "Who was it, then, that hunted game and brought it to me? I ate it just before you came and I blessed him--and indeed he will be blessed!"

column.name: text
column.value: When Esau heard his father's words, he burst out with a loud and bitter cry and said to his father, "Bless me--me too, my father!"

column.name: text
column.value: But he said, "Your brother came deceitfully and took your blessing."

column.name: text
column.value: Esau said, "Isn't he rightly named Jacob? He has deceived me these two times: He took my birthright, and now he's taken my blessing!" Then he asked, "Haven't you reserved any blessing for me?"

column.name: text
column.value: Isaac answered Esau, "I have made him lord over you and have made all his relatives his servants, and I have sustained him with grain and new wine. So what can I possibly do for you, my son?"

column.name: text
column.value: Esau said to his father, "Do you have only one blessing, my father? Bless me too, my father!" Then Esau wept aloud.

column.name: text
column.value: His father Isaac answered him, "Your dwelling will be away from the earth's richness, away from the dew of heaven above.

column.name: text
column.value: You will live by the sword and you will serve your brother. But when you grow restless, you will throw his yoke from off your neck."

column.name: text
column.value: Esau held a grudge against Jacob because of the blessing his father had given him. He said to himself, "The days of mourning for my father are near; then I will kill my brother Jacob."

column.name: text
column.value: When Rebekah was told what her older son Esau had said, she sent for her younger son Jacob and said to him, "Your brother Esau is consoling himself with the thought of killing you.

column.name: text
column.value: Now then, my son, do what I say: Flee at once to my brother Laban in Haran.

column.name: text
column.value: Stay with him for a while until your brother's fury subsides.

column.name: text
column.value: When your brother is no longer angry with you and forgets what you did to him, I'll send word for you to come back from there. Why should I lose both of you in one day?"

column.name: text
column.value: Then Rebekah said to Isaac, "I'm disgusted with living because of these Hittite women. If Jacob takes a wife from among the women of this land, from Hittite women like these, my life will not be worth living."

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jacob continued on his journey and came to the land of the eastern peoples.

column.name: text
column.value: There he saw a well in the field, with three flocks of sheep lying near it because the flocks were watered from that well. The stone over the mouth of the well was large.

column.name: text
column.value: When all the flocks were gathered there, the shepherds would roll the stone away from the well's mouth and water the sheep. Then they would return the stone to its place over the mouth of the well.

column.name: text
column.value: Jacob asked the shepherds, "My brothers, where are you from?" "We're from Haran," they replied.

column.name: text
column.value: He said to them, "Do you know Laban, Nahor's grandson?" "Yes, we know him," they answered.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jacob asked them, "Is he well?" "Yes, he is," they said, "and here comes his daughter Rachel with the sheep."

column.name: text
column.value: "Look," he said, "the sun is still high; it is not time for the flocks to be gathered. Water the sheep and take them back to pasture."

column.name: text
column.value: "We can't," they replied, "until all the flocks are gathered and the stone has been rolled away from the mouth of the well. Then we will water the sheep."

column.name: text
column.value: While he was still talking with them, Rachel came with her father's sheep, for she was a shepherdess.

column.name: text
column.value: When Jacob saw Rachel daughter of Laban, his mother's brother, and Laban's sheep, he went over and rolled the stone away from the mouth of the well and watered his uncle's sheep.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jacob kissed Rachel and began to weep aloud.

column.name: text
column.value: He had told Rachel that he was a relative of her father and a son of Rebekah. So she ran and told her father.

column.name: text
column.value: As soon as Laban heard the news about Jacob, his sister's son, he hurried to meet him. He embraced him and kissed him and brought him to his home, and there Jacob told him all these things.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Laban said to him, "You are my own flesh and blood." After Jacob had stayed with him for a whole month,

column.name: text
column.value: Laban said to him, "Just because you are a relative of mine, should you work for me for nothing? Tell me what your wages should be."

column.name: text
column.value: Now Laban had two daughters; the name of the older was Leah, and the name of the younger was Rachel.

column.name: text
column.value: Leah had weak eyes, but Rachel was lovely in form, and beautiful.

column.name: text
column.value: Jacob was in love with Rachel and said, "I'll work for you seven years in return for your younger daughter Rachel."

column.name: text
column.value: Laban said, "It's better that I give her to you than to some other man. Stay here with me."

column.name: text
column.value: So Jacob served seven years to get Rachel, but they seemed like only a few days to him because of his love for her.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jacob said to Laban, "Give me my wife. My time is completed, and I want to lie with her."

column.name: text
column.value: So Laban brought together all the people of the place and gave a feast.

column.name: text
column.value: But when evening came, he took his daughter Leah and gave her to Jacob, and Jacob lay with her.

column.name: text
column.value: And Laban gave his servant girl Zilpah to his daughter as her maidservant.

column.name: text
column.value: When morning came, there was Leah! So Jacob said to Laban, "What is this you have done to me? I served you for Rachel, didn't I? Why have you deceived me?"

column.name: text
column.value: Laban replied, "It is not our custom here to give the younger daughter in marriage before the older one.

column.name: text
column.value: Finish this daughter's bridal week; then we will give you the younger one also, in return for another seven years of work."

column.name: text
column.value: And Jacob did so. He finished the week with Leah, and then Laban gave him his daughter Rachel to be his wife.

column.name: text
column.value: Laban gave his servant girl Bilhah to his daughter Rachel as her maidservant.

column.name: text
column.value: Jacob lay with Rachel also, and he loved Rachel more than Leah. And he worked for Laban another seven years.

column.name: text
column.value: When the LORD saw that Leah was not loved, he opened her womb, but Rachel was barren.

column.name: text
column.value: Leah became pregnant and gave birth to a son. She named him Reuben, for she said, "It is because the LORD has seen my misery. Surely my husband will love me now."

column.name: text
column.value: She conceived again, and when she gave birth to a son she said, "Because the LORD heard that I am not loved, he gave me this one too." So she named him Simeon.

column.name: text
column.value: Again she conceived, and when she gave birth to a son she said, "Now at last my husband will become attached to me, because I have borne him three sons." So he was named Levi.

column.name: text
column.value: She conceived again, and when she gave birth to a son she said, "This time I will praise the LORD." So she named him Judah. Then she stopped having children.

column.name: text
column.value: When Rachel saw that she was not bearing Jacob any children, she became jealous of her sister. So she said to Jacob, "Give me children, or I'll die!"

column.name: text
column.value: Jacob became angry with her and said, "Am I in the place of God, who has kept you from having children?"

column.name: text
column.value: Then she said, "Here is Bilhah, my maidservant. Sleep with her so that she can bear children for me and that through her I too can build a family."

column.name: text
column.value: So she gave him her servant Bilhah as a wife. Jacob slept with her,

column.name: text
column.value: and she became pregnant and bore him a son.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Rachel said, "God has vindicated me; he has listened to my plea and given me a son." Because of this she named him Dan.

column.name: text
column.value: Rachel's servant Bilhah conceived again and bore Jacob a second son.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Rachel said, "I have had a great struggle with my sister, and I have won." So she named him Naphtali.

column.name: text
column.value: When Leah saw that she had stopped having children, she took her maidservant Zilpah and gave her to Jacob as a wife.

column.name: text
column.value: Leah's servant Zilpah bore Jacob a son.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Leah said, "What good fortune!" So she named him Gad.

column.name: text
column.value: Leah's servant Zilpah bore Jacob a second son.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Leah said, "How happy I am! The women will call me happy." So she named him Asher.

column.name: text
column.value: During wheat harvest, Reuben went out into the fields and found some mandrake plants, which he brought to his mother Leah. Rachel said to Leah, "Please give me some of your son's mandrakes."

column.name: text
column.value: But she said to her, "Wasn't it enough that you took away my husband? Will you take my son's mandrakes too?" "Very well," Rachel said, "he can sleep with you tonight in return for your son's mandrakes."

column.name: text
column.value: So when Jacob came in from the fields that evening, Leah went out to meet him. "You must sleep with me," she said. "I have hired you with my son's mandrakes." So he slept with her that night.

column.name: text
column.value: God listened to Leah, and she became pregnant and bore Jacob a fifth son.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Leah said, "God has rewarded me for giving my maidservant to my husband." So she named him Issachar.

column.name: text
column.value: Leah conceived again and bore Jacob a sixth son.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Leah said, "God has presented me with a precious gift. This time my husband will treat me with honor, because I have borne him six sons." So she named him Zebulun.

column.name: text
column.value: Some time later she gave birth to a daughter and named her Dinah.

column.name: text
column.value: Then God remembered Rachel; he listened to her and opened her womb.

column.name: text
column.value: She became pregnant and gave birth to a son and said, "God has taken away my disgrace."

column.name: text
column.value: She named him Joseph, and said, "May the LORD add to me another son."

column.name: text
column.value: After Rachel gave birth to Joseph, Jacob said to Laban, "Send me on my way so I can go back to my own homeland.

column.name: text
column.value: Give me my wives and children, for whom I have served you, and I will be on my way. You know how much work I've done for you."

column.name: text
column.value: But Laban said to him, "If I have found favor in your eyes, please stay. I have learned by divination that the LORD has blessed me because of you."

column.name: text
column.value: He added, "Name your wages, and I will pay them."

column.name: text
column.value: Jacob said to him, "You know how I have worked for you and how your livestock has fared under my care.

column.name: text
column.value: The little you had before I came has increased greatly, and the LORD has blessed you wherever I have been. But now, when may I do something for my own household?"

column.name: text
column.value: "What shall I give you?" he asked. "Don't give me anything," Jacob replied. "But if you will do this one thing for me, I will go on tending your flocks and watching over them:

column.name: text
column.value: Let me go through all your flocks today and remove from them every speckled or spotted sheep, every dark-colored lamb and every spotted or speckled goat. They will be my wages.

column.name: text
column.value: And my honesty will testify for me in the future, whenever you check on the wages you have paid me. Any goat in my possession that is not speckled or spotted, or any lamb that is not dark-colored, will be considered stolen."

column.name: text
column.value: "Agreed," said Laban. "Let it be as you have said."

column.name: text
column.value: That same day he removed all the male goats that were streaked or spotted, and all the speckled or spotted female goats (all that had white on them) and all the dark-colored lambs, and he placed them in the care of his sons.

column.name: text
column.value: Then he put a three-day journey between himself and Jacob, while Jacob continued to tend the rest of Laban's flocks.

column.name: text
column.value: Jacob, however, took fresh-cut branches from poplar, almond and plane trees and made white stripes on them by peeling the bark and exposing the white inner wood of the branches.

column.name: text
column.value: Then he placed the peeled branches in all the watering troughs, so that they would be directly in front of the flocks when they came to drink. When the flocks were in heat and came to drink,

column.name: text
column.value: they mated in front of the branches. And they bore young that were streaked or speckled or spotted.

column.name: text
column.value: Jacob set apart the young of the flock by themselves, but made the rest face the streaked and dark-colored animals that belonged to Laban. Thus he made separate flocks for himself and did not put them with Laban's animals.

column.name: text
column.value: Whenever the stronger females were in heat, Jacob would place the branches in the troughs in front of the animals so they would mate near the branches,

column.name: text
column.value: but if the animals were weak, he would not place them there. So the weak animals went to Laban and the strong ones to Jacob.

column.name: text
column.value: In this way the man grew exceedingly prosperous and came to own large flocks, and maidservants and menservants, and camels and donkeys.

column.name: text
column.value: Jacob heard that Laban's sons were saying, "Jacob has taken everything our father owned and has gained all this wealth from what belonged to our father."

column.name: text
column.value: And Jacob noticed that Laban's attitude toward him was not what it had been.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD said to Jacob, "Go back to the land of your fathers and to your relatives, and I will be with you."

column.name: text
column.value: So Jacob sent word to Rachel and Leah to come out to the fields where his flocks were.

column.name: text
column.value: He said to them, "I see that your father's attitude toward me is not what it was before, but the God of my father has been with me.

column.name: text
column.value: You know that I've worked for your father with all my strength,

column.name: text
column.value: yet your father has cheated me by changing my wages ten times. However, God has not allowed him to harm me.

column.name: text
column.value: If he said, 'The speckled ones will be your wages,' then all the flocks gave birth to speckled young; and if he said, 'The streaked ones will be your wages,' then all the flocks bore streaked young.

column.name: text
column.value: So God has taken away your father's livestock and has given them to me.

column.name: text
column.value: "In breeding season I once had a dream in which I looked up and saw that the male goats mating with the flock were streaked, speckled or spotted.

column.name: text
column.value: The angel of God said to me in the dream, 'Jacob.' I answered, 'Here I am.'

column.name: text
column.value: And he said, 'Look up and see that all the male goats mating with the flock are streaked, speckled or spotted, for I have seen all that Laban has been doing to you.

column.name: text
column.value: I am the God of Bethel, where you anointed a pillar and where you made a vow to me. Now leave this land at once and go back to your native land.'"

column.name: text
column.value: Then Rachel and Leah replied, "Do we still have any share in the inheritance of our father's estate?

column.name: text
column.value: Does he not regard us as foreigners? Not only has he sold us, but he has used up what was paid for us.

column.name: text
column.value: Surely all the wealth that God took away from our father belongs to us and our children. So do whatever God has told you."

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jacob put his children and his wives on camels,

column.name: text
column.value: and he drove all his livestock ahead of him, along with all the goods he had accumulated in Paddan Aram, to go to his father Isaac in the land of Canaan.

column.name: text
column.value: When Laban had gone to shear his sheep, Rachel stole her father's household gods.

column.name: text
column.value: Moreover, Jacob deceived Laban the Aramean by not telling him he was running away.

column.name: text
column.value: So he fled with all he had, and crossing the River, he headed for the hill country of Gilead.

column.name: text
column.value: On the third day Laban was told that Jacob had fled.

column.name: text
column.value: Taking his relatives with him, he pursued Jacob for seven days and caught up with him in the hill country of Gilead.

column.name: text
column.value: Then God came to Laban the Aramean in a dream at night and said to him, "Be careful not to say anything to Jacob, either good or bad."

column.name: text
column.value: Jacob had pitched his tent in the hill country of Gilead when Laban overtook him, and Laban and his relatives camped there too.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Laban said to Jacob, "What have you done? You've deceived me, and you've carried off my daughters like captives in war.

column.name: text
column.value: Why did you run off secretly and deceive me? Why didn't you tell me, so I could send you away with joy and singing to the music of tambourines and harps?

column.name: text
column.value: You didn't even let me kiss my grandchildren and my daughters good-by. You have done a foolish thing.

column.name: text
column.value: I have the power to harm you; but last night the God of your father said to me, 'Be careful not to say anything to Jacob, either good or bad.'

column.name: text
column.value: Now you have gone off because you longed to return to your father's house. But why did you steal my gods?"

column.name: text
column.value: Jacob answered Laban, "I was afraid, because I thought you would take your daughters away from me by force.

column.name: text
column.value: But if you find anyone who has your gods, he shall not live. In the presence of our relatives, see for yourself whether there is anything of yours here with me; and if so, take it." Now Jacob did not know that Rachel had stolen the gods.

column.name: text
column.value: So Laban went into Jacob's tent and into Leah's tent and into the tent of the two maidservants, but he found nothing. After he came out of Leah's tent, he entered Rachel's tent.

column.name: text
column.value: Now Rachel had taken the household gods and put them inside her camel's saddle and was sitting on them. Laban searched through everything in the tent but found nothing.

column.name: text
column.value: Rachel said to her father, "Don't be angry, my lord, that I cannot stand up in your presence; I'm having my period." So he searched but could not find the household gods.

column.name: text
column.value: Jacob was angry and took Laban to task. "What is my crime?" he asked Laban. "What sin have I committed that you hunt me down?

column.name: text
column.value: Now that you have searched through all my goods, what have you found that belongs to your household? Put it here in front of your relatives and mine, and let them judge between the two of us.

column.name: text
column.value: "I have been with you for twenty years now. Your sheep and goats have not miscarried, nor have I eaten rams from your flocks.

column.name: text
column.value: I did not bring you animals torn by wild beasts; I bore the loss myself. And you demanded payment from me for whatever was stolen by day or night.

column.name: text
column.value: This was my situation: The heat consumed me in the daytime and the cold at night, and sleep fled from my eyes.

column.name: text
column.value: It was like this for the twenty years I was in your household. I worked for you fourteen years for your two daughters and six years for your flocks, and you changed my wages ten times.

column.name: text
column.value: If the God of my father, the God of Abraham and the Fear of Isaac, had not been with me, you would surely have sent me away empty-handed. But God has seen my hardship and the toil of my hands, and last night he rebuked you."

column.name: text
column.value: Laban answered Jacob, "The women are my daughters, the children are my children, and the flocks are my flocks. All you see is mine. Yet what can I do today about these daughters of mine, or about the children they have borne?

column.name: text
column.value: Come now, let's make a covenant, you and I, and let it serve as a witness between us."

column.name: text
column.value: So Jacob took a stone and set it up as a pillar.

column.name: text
column.value: He said to his relatives, "Gather some stones." So they took stones and piled them in a heap, and they ate there by the heap.

column.name: text
column.value: Laban called it Jegar Sahadutha, and Jacob called it Galeed.

column.name: text
column.value: Laban said, "This heap is a witness between you and me today." That is why it was called Galeed.

column.name: text
column.value: It was also called Mizpah, because he said, "May the LORD keep watch between you and me when we are away from each other.

column.name: text
column.value: If you mistreat my daughters or if you take any wives besides my daughters, even though no one is with us, remember that God is a witness between you and me."

column.name: text
column.value: Laban also said to Jacob, "Here is this heap, and here is this pillar I have set up between you and me.

column.name: text
column.value: This heap is a witness, and this pillar is a witness, that I will not go past this heap to your side to harm you and that you will not go past this heap and pillar to my side to harm me.

column.name: text
column.value: May the God of Abraham and the God of Nahor, the God of their father, judge between us." So Jacob took an oath in the name of the Fear of his father Isaac.

column.name: text
column.value: He offered a sacrifice there in the hill country and invited his relatives to a meal. After they had eaten, they spent the night there.

column.name: text
column.value: Early the next morning Laban kissed his grandchildren and his daughters and blessed them. Then he left and returned home.

column.name: text
column.value: Jacob also went on his way, and the angels of God met him.

column.name: text
column.value: When Jacob saw them, he said, "This is the camp of God!" So he named that place Mahanaim.

column.name: text
column.value: Jacob sent messengers ahead of him to his brother Esau in the land of Seir, the country of Edom.

column.name: text
column.value: He instructed them: "This is what you are to say to my master Esau: 'Your servant Jacob says, I have been staying with Laban and have remained there till now.

column.name: text
column.value: I have cattle and donkeys, sheep and goats, menservants and maidservants. Now I am sending this message to my lord, that I may find favor in your eyes.'"

column.name: text
column.value: When the messengers returned to Jacob, they said, "We went to your brother Esau, and now he is coming to meet you, and four hundred men are with him."

column.name: text
column.value: In great fear and distress Jacob divided the people who were with him into two groups, and the flocks and herds and camels as well.

column.name: text
column.value: He thought, "If Esau comes and attacks one group, the group that is left may escape."

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jacob prayed, "O God of my father Abraham, God of my father Isaac, O LORD, who said to me, 'Go back to your country and your relatives, and I will make you prosper,'

column.name: text
column.value: I am unworthy of all the kindness and faithfulness you have shown your servant. I had only my staff when I crossed this Jordan, but now I have become two groups.

column.name: text
column.value: Save me, I pray, from the hand of my brother Esau, for I am afraid he will come and attack me, and also the mothers with their children.

column.name: text
column.value: But you have said, 'I will surely make you prosper and will make your descendants like the sand of the sea, which cannot be counted.'"

column.name: text
column.value: He spent the night there, and from what he had with him he selected a gift for his brother Esau:

column.name: text
column.value: two hundred female goats and twenty male goats, two hundred ewes and twenty rams,

column.name: text
column.value: thirty female camels with their young, forty cows and ten bulls, and twenty female donkeys and ten male donkeys.

column.name: text
column.value: He put them in the care of his servants, each herd by itself, and said to his servants, "Go ahead of me, and keep some space between the herds."

column.name: text
column.value: He instructed the one in the lead: "When my brother Esau meets you and asks, 'To whom do you belong, and where are you going, and who owns all these animals in front of you?'

column.name: text
column.value: then you are to say, 'They belong to your servant Jacob. They are a gift sent to my lord Esau, and he is coming behind us.'"

column.name: text
column.value: He also instructed the second, the third and all the others who followed the herds: "You are to say the same thing to Esau when you meet him.

column.name: text
column.value: And be sure to say, 'Your servant Jacob is coming behind us.'" For he thought, "I will pacify him with these gifts I am sending on ahead; later, when I see him, perhaps he will receive me."

column.name: text
column.value: So Jacob's gifts went on ahead of him, but he himself spent the night in the camp.

column.name: text
column.value: That night Jacob got up and took his two wives, his two maidservants and his eleven sons and crossed the ford of the Jabbok.

column.name: text
column.value: After he had sent them across the stream, he sent over all his possessions.

column.name: text
column.value: So Jacob was left alone, and a man wrestled with him till daybreak.

column.name: text
column.value: When the man saw that he could not overpower him, he touched the socket of Jacob's hip so that his hip was wrenched as he wrestled with the man.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the man said, "Let me go, for it is daybreak." But Jacob replied, "I will not let you go unless you bless me."

column.name: text
column.value: The man asked him, "What is your name?" "Jacob," he answered.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the man said, "Your name will no longer be Jacob, but Israel, because you have struggled with God and with men and have overcome."

column.name: text
column.value: Jacob said, "Please tell me your name." But he replied, "Why do you ask my name?" Then he blessed him there.

column.name: text
column.value: So Jacob called the place Peniel, saying, "It is because I saw God face to face, and yet my life was spared."

column.name: text
column.value: The sun rose above him as he passed Peniel, and he was limping because of his hip.

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore to this day the Israelites do not eat the tendon attached to the socket of the hip, because the socket of Jacob's hip was touched near the tendon.

column.name: text
column.value: Jacob looked up and there was Esau, coming with his four hundred men; so he divided the children among Leah, Rachel and the two maidservants.

column.name: text
column.value: He put the maidservants and their children in front, Leah and her children next, and Rachel and Joseph in the rear.

column.name: text
column.value: He himself went on ahead and bowed down to the ground seven times as he approached his brother.

column.name: text
column.value: But Esau ran to meet Jacob and embraced him; he threw his arms around his neck and kissed him. And they wept.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Esau looked up and saw the women and children. "Who are these with you?" he asked. Jacob answered, "They are the children God has graciously given your servant."

column.name: text
column.value: Then the maidservants and their children approached and bowed down.

column.name: text
column.value: Next, Leah and her children came and bowed down. Last of all came Joseph and Rachel, and they too bowed down.

column.name: text
column.value: Esau asked, "What do you mean by all these droves I met?" "To find favor in your eyes, my lord," he said.

column.name: text
column.value: But Esau said, "I already have plenty, my brother. Keep what you have for yourself."

column.name: text
column.value: "No, please!" said Jacob. "If I have found favor in your eyes, accept this gift from me. For to see your face is like seeing the face of God, now that you have received me favorably.

column.name: text
column.value: Please accept the present that was brought to you, for God has been gracious to me and I have all I need." And because Jacob insisted, Esau accepted it.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Esau said, "Let us be on our way; I'll accompany you."

column.name: text
column.value: But Jacob said to him, "My lord knows that the children are tender and that I must care for the ewes and cows that are nursing their young. If they are driven hard just one day, all the animals will die.

column.name: text
column.value: So let my lord go on ahead of his servant, while I move along slowly at the pace of the droves before me and that of the children, until I come to my lord in Seir."

column.name: text
column.value: Esau said, "Then let me leave some of my men with you." "But why do that?" Jacob asked. "Just let me find favor in the eyes of my lord."

column.name: text
column.value: So that day Esau started on his way back to Seir.

column.name: text
column.value: Jacob, however, went to Succoth, where he built a place for himself and made shelters for his livestock. That is why the place is called Succoth.

column.name: text
column.value: After Jacob came from Paddan Aram, he arrived safely at the city of Shechem in Canaan and camped within sight of the city.

column.name: text
column.value: For a hundred pieces of silver, he bought from the sons of Hamor, the father of Shechem, the plot of ground where he pitched his tent.

column.name: text
column.value: There he set up an altar and called it El Elohe Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: Now Dinah, the daughter Leah had borne to Jacob, went out to visit the women of the land.

column.name: text
column.value: When Shechem son of Hamor the Hivite, the ruler of that area, saw her, he took her and violated her.

column.name: text
column.value: His heart was drawn to Dinah daughter of Jacob, and he loved the girl and spoke tenderly to her.

column.name: text
column.value: And Shechem said to his father Hamor, "Get me this girl as my wife."

column.name: text
column.value: When Jacob heard that his daughter Dinah had been defiled, his sons were in the fields with his livestock; so he kept quiet about it until they came home.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Shechem's father Hamor went out to talk with Jacob.

column.name: text
column.value: Now Jacob's sons had come in from the fields as soon as they heard what had happened. They were filled with grief and fury, because Shechem had done a disgraceful thing in Israel by lying with Jacob's daughter--a thing that should not be done.

column.name: text
column.value: But Hamor said to them, "My son Shechem has his heart set on your daughter. Please give her to him as his wife.

column.name: text
column.value: Intermarry with us; give us your daughters and take our daughters for yourselves.

column.name: text
column.value: You can settle among us; the land is open to you. Live in it, trade in it, and acquire property in it."

column.name: text
column.value: Then Shechem said to Dinah's father and brothers, "Let me find favor in your eyes, and I will give you whatever you ask.

column.name: text
column.value: Make the price for the bride and the gift I am to bring as great as you like, and I'll pay whatever you ask me. Only give me the girl as my wife."

column.name: text
column.value: Because their sister Dinah had been defiled, Jacob's sons replied deceitfully as they spoke to Shechem and his father Hamor.

column.name: text
column.value: They said to them, "We can't do such a thing; we can't give our sister to a man who is not circumcised. That would be a disgrace to us.

column.name: text
column.value: We will give our consent to you on one condition only: that you become like us by circumcising all your males.

column.name: text
column.value: Then we will give you our daughters and take your daughters for ourselves. We'll settle among you and become one people with you.

column.name: text
column.value: But if you will not agree to be circumcised, we'll take our sister and go."

column.name: text
column.value: Their proposal seemed good to Hamor and his son Shechem.

column.name: text
column.value: The young man, who was the most honored of all his father's household, lost no time in doing what they said, because he was delighted with Jacob's daughter.

column.name: text
column.value: So Hamor and his son Shechem went to the gate of their city to speak to their fellow townsmen.

column.name: text
column.value: "These men are friendly toward us," they said. "Let them live in our land and trade in it; the land has plenty of room for them. We can marry their daughters and they can marry ours.

column.name: text
column.value: But the men will consent to live with us as one people only on the condition that our males be circumcised, as they themselves are.

column.name: text
column.value: Won't their livestock, their property and all their other animals become ours? So let us give our consent to them, and they will settle among us."

column.name: text
column.value: All the men who went out of the city gate agreed with Hamor and his son Shechem, and every male in the city was circumcised.

column.name: text
column.value: Three days later, while all of them were still in pain, two of Jacob's sons, Simeon and Levi, Dinah's brothers, took their swords and attacked the unsuspecting city, killing every male.

column.name: text
column.value: They put Hamor and his son Shechem to the sword and took Dinah from Shechem's house and left.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Jacob came upon the dead bodies and looted the city where their sister had been defiled.

column.name: text
column.value: They seized their flocks and herds and donkeys and everything else of theirs in the city and out in the fields.

column.name: text
column.value: They carried off all their wealth and all their women and children, taking as plunder everything in the houses.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jacob said to Simeon and Levi, "You have brought trouble on me by making me a stench to the Canaanites and Perizzites, the people living in this land. We are few in number, and if they join forces against me and attack me, I and my household will be destroyed."

column.name: text
column.value: But they replied, "Should he have treated our sister like a prostitute?"

column.name: text
column.value: This is the account of Esau (that is, Edom).

column.name: text
column.value: Esau took his wives from the women of Canaan: Adah daughter of Elon the Hittite, and Oholibamah daughter of Anah and granddaughter of Zibeon the Hivite--

column.name: text
column.value: also Basemath daughter of Ishmael and sister of Nebaioth.

column.name: text
column.value: Adah bore Eliphaz to Esau, Basemath bore Reuel,

column.name: text
column.value: and Oholibamah bore Jeush, Jalam and Korah. These were the sons of Esau, who were born to him in Canaan.

column.name: text
column.value: Esau took his wives and sons and daughters and all the members of his household, as well as his livestock and all his other animals and all the goods he had acquired in Canaan, and moved to a land some distance from his brother Jacob.

column.name: text
column.value: Their possessions were too great for them to remain together; the land where they were staying could not support them both because of their livestock.

column.name: text
column.value: So Esau (that is, Edom) settled in the hill country of Seir.

column.name: text
column.value: This is the account of Esau the father of the Edomites in the hill country of Seir.

column.name: text
column.value: These are the names of Esau's sons: Eliphaz, the son of Esau's wife Adah, and Reuel, the son of Esau's wife Basemath.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Eliphaz: Teman, Omar, Zepho, Gatam and Kenaz.

column.name: text
column.value: Esau's son Eliphaz also had a concubine named Timna, who bore him Amalek. These were grandsons of Esau's wife Adah.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Reuel: Nahath, Zerah, Shammah and Mizzah. These were grandsons of Esau's wife Basemath.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Esau's wife Oholibamah daughter of Anah and granddaughter of Zibeon, whom she bore to Esau: Jeush, Jalam and Korah.

column.name: text
column.value: These were the chiefs among Esau's descendants: The sons of Eliphaz the firstborn of Esau: Chiefs Teman, Omar, Zepho, Kenaz,

column.name: text
column.value: Korah, Gatam and Amalek. These were the chiefs descended from Eliphaz in Edom; they were grandsons of Adah.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Esau's son Reuel: Chiefs Nahath, Zerah, Shammah and Mizzah. These were the chiefs descended from Reuel in Edom; they were grandsons of Esau's wife Basemath.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Esau's wife Oholibamah: Chiefs Jeush, Jalam and Korah. These were the chiefs descended from Esau's wife Oholibamah daughter of Anah.

column.name: text
column.value: These were the sons of Esau (that is, Edom), and these were their chiefs.

column.name: text
column.value: These were the sons of Seir the Horite, who were living in the region: Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah,

column.name: text
column.value: Dishon, Ezer and Dishan. These sons of Seir in Edom were Horite chiefs.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Lotan: Hori and Homam. Timna was Lotan's sister.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Shobal: Alvan, Manahath, Ebal, Shepho and Onam.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Zibeon: Aiah and Anah. This is the Anah who discovered the hot springs in the desert while he was grazing the donkeys of his father Zibeon.

column.name: text
column.value: The children of Anah: Dishon and Oholibamah daughter of Anah.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Dishon: Hemdan, Eshban, Ithran and Keran.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Ezer: Bilhan, Zaavan and Akan.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Dishan: Uz and Aran.

column.name: text
column.value: These were the Horite chiefs: Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah,

column.name: text
column.value: Dishon, Ezer and Dishan. These were the Horite chiefs, according to their divisions, in the land of Seir.

column.name: text
column.value: These were the kings who reigned in Edom before any Israelite king reigned:

column.name: text
column.value: Bela son of Beor became king of Edom. His city was named Dinhabah.

column.name: text
column.value: When Bela died, Jobab son of Zerah from Bozrah succeeded him as king.

column.name: text
column.value: When Jobab died, Husham from the land of the Temanites succeeded him as king.

column.name: text
column.value: When Husham died, Hadad son of Bedad, who defeated Midian in the country of Moab, succeeded him as king. His city was named Avith.

column.name: text
column.value: When Hadad died, Samlah from Masrekah succeeded him as king.

column.name: text
column.value: When Samlah died, Shaul from Rehoboth on the river succeeded him as king.

column.name: text
column.value: When Shaul died, Baal-Hanan son of Acbor succeeded him as king.

column.name: text
column.value: When Baal-Hanan son of Acbor died, Hadad succeeded him as king. His city was named Pau, and his wife's name was Mehetabel daughter of Matred, the daughter of Me-Zahab.

column.name: text
column.value: These were the chiefs descended from Esau, by name, according to their clans and regions: Timna, Alvah, Jetheth,

column.name: text
column.value: Oholibamah, Elah, Pinon,

column.name: text
column.value: Kenaz, Teman, Mibzar,

column.name: text
column.value: Magdiel and Iram. These were the chiefs of Edom, according to their settlements in the land they occupied. This was Esau the father of the Edomites.

column.name: text
column.value: Then God said to Jacob, "Go up to Bethel and settle there, and build an altar there to God, who appeared to you when you were fleeing from your brother Esau."

column.name: text
column.value: So Jacob said to his household and to all who were with him, "Get rid of the foreign gods you have with you, and purify yourselves and change your clothes.

column.name: text
column.value: Then come, let us go up to Bethel, where I will build an altar to God, who answered me in the day of my distress and who has been with me wherever I have gone."

column.name: text
column.value: So they gave Jacob all the foreign gods they had and the rings in their ears, and Jacob buried them under the oak at Shechem.

column.name: text
column.value: Then they set out, and the terror of God fell upon the towns all around them so that no one pursued them.

column.name: text
