column.value: The man said, "Who made you ruler and judge over us? Are you thinking of killing me as you killed the Egyptian?" Then Moses was afraid and thought, "What I did must have become known."

column.name: text
column.value: When Pharaoh heard of this, he tried to kill Moses, but Moses fled from Pharaoh and went to live in Midian, where he sat down by a well.

column.name: text
column.value: Now a priest of Midian had seven daughters, and they came to draw water and fill the troughs to water their father's flock.

column.name: text
column.value: Some shepherds came along and drove them away, but Moses got up and came to their rescue and watered their flock.

column.name: text
column.value: When the girls returned to Reuel their father, he asked them, "Why have you returned so early today?"

column.name: text
column.value: They answered, "An Egyptian rescued us from the shepherds. He even drew water for us and watered the flock."

column.name: text
column.value: "And where is he?" he asked his daughters. "Why did you leave him? Invite him to have something to eat."

column.name: text
column.value: Moses agreed to stay with the man, who gave his daughter Zipporah to Moses in marriage.

column.name: text
column.value: Zipporah gave birth to a son, and Moses named him Gershom, saying, "I have become an alien in a foreign land."

column.name: text
column.value: During that long period, the king of Egypt died. The Israelites groaned in their slavery and cried out, and their cry for help because of their slavery went up to God.

column.name: text
column.value: God heard their groaning and he remembered his covenant with Abraham, with Isaac and with Jacob.

column.name: text
column.value: So God looked on the Israelites and was concerned about them.

column.name: text
column.value: Now Moses was tending the flock of Jethro his father-in-law, the priest of Midian, and he led the flock to the far side of the desert and came to Horeb, the mountain of God.

column.name: text
column.value: There the angel of the LORD appeared to him in flames of fire from within a bush. Moses saw that though the bush was on fire it did not burn up.

column.name: text
column.value: So Moses thought, "I will go over and see this strange sight--why the bush does not burn up."

column.name: text
column.value: When the LORD saw that he had gone over to look, God called to him from within the bush, "Moses! Moses!" And Moses said, "Here I am."

column.name: text
column.value: "Do not come any closer," God said. "Take off your sandals, for the place where you are standing is holy ground."

column.name: text
column.value: Then he said, "I am the God of your father, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob." At this, Moses hid his face, because he was afraid to look at God.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD said, "I have indeed seen the misery of my people in Egypt. I have heard them crying out because of their slave drivers, and I am concerned about their suffering.

column.name: text
column.value: So I have come down to rescue them from the hand of the Egyptians and to bring them up out of that land into a good and spacious land, a land flowing with milk and honey--the home of the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites and Jebusites.

column.name: text
column.value: And now the cry of the Israelites has reached me, and I have seen the way the Egyptians are oppressing them.

column.name: text
column.value: So now, go. I am sending you to Pharaoh to bring my people the Israelites out of Egypt."

column.name: text
column.value: But Moses said to God, "Who am I, that I should go to Pharaoh and bring the Israelites out of Egypt?"

column.name: text
column.value: And God said, "I will be with you. And this will be the sign to you that it is I who have sent you: When you have brought the people out of Egypt, you will worship God on this mountain."

column.name: text
column.value: Moses said to God, "Suppose I go to the Israelites and say to them, 'The God of your fathers has sent me to you,' and they ask me, 'What is his name?' Then what shall I tell them?"

column.name: text
column.value: God said to Moses, "I AM WHO I AM. This is what you are to say to the Israelites: 'I AM has sent me to you.'"

column.name: text
column.value: God also said to Moses, "Say to the Israelites, 'The LORD, the God of your fathers--the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob--has sent me to you.' This is my name forever, the name by which I am to be remembered from generation to generation.

column.name: text
column.value: "Go, assemble the elders of Israel and say to them, 'The LORD, the God of your fathers--the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob--appeared to me and said: I have watched over you and have seen what has been done to you in Egypt.

column.name: text
column.value: And I have promised to bring you up out of your misery in Egypt into the land of the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites and Jebusites--a land flowing with milk and honey.'

column.name: text
column.value: "The elders of Israel will listen to you. Then you and the elders are to go to the king of Egypt and say to him, 'The LORD, the God of the Hebrews, has met with us. Let us take a three-day journey into the desert to offer sacrifices to the LORD our God.'

column.name: text
column.value: But I know that the king of Egypt will not let you go unless a mighty hand compels him.

column.name: text
column.value: So I will stretch out my hand and strike the Egyptians with all the wonders that I will perform among them. After that, he will let you go.

column.name: text
column.value: "And I will make the Egyptians favorably disposed toward this people, so that when you leave you will not go empty-handed.

column.name: text
column.value: Every woman is to ask her neighbor and any woman living in her house for articles of silver and gold and for clothing, which you will put on your sons and daughters. And so you will plunder the Egyptians."

column.name: text
column.value: Moses answered, "What if they do not believe me or listen to me and say, 'The LORD did not appear to you'?"

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD said to him, "What is that in your hand?" "A staff," he replied.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD said, "Throw it on the ground." Moses threw it on the ground and it became a snake, and he ran from it.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD said to him, "Reach out your hand and take it by the tail." So Moses reached out and took hold of the snake and it turned back into a staff in his hand.

column.name: text
column.value: "This," said the LORD, "is so that they may believe that the LORD, the God of their fathers--the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob--has appeared to you."

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD said, "Put your hand inside your cloak." So Moses put his hand into his cloak, and when he took it out, it was leprous, like snow.

column.name: text
column.value: "Now put it back into your cloak," he said. So Moses put his hand back into his cloak, and when he took it out, it was restored, like the rest of his flesh.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD said, "If they do not believe you or pay attention to the first miraculous sign, they may believe the second.

column.name: text
column.value: But if they do not believe these two signs or listen to you, take some water from the Nile and pour it on the dry ground. The water you take from the river will become blood on the ground."

column.name: text
column.value: Moses said to the LORD, "O Lord, I have never been eloquent, neither in the past nor since you have spoken to your servant. I am slow of speech and tongue."

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD said to him, "Who gave man his mouth? Who makes him deaf or mute? Who gives him sight or makes him blind? Is it not I, the LORD?

column.name: text
column.value: Now go; I will help you speak and will teach you what to say."

column.name: text
column.value: But Moses said, "O Lord, please send someone else to do it."

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD'S anger burned against Moses and he said, "What about your brother, Aaron the Levite? I know he can speak well. He is already on his way to meet you, and his heart will be glad when he sees you.

column.name: text
column.value: You shall speak to him and put words in his mouth; I will help both of you speak and will teach you what to do.

column.name: text
column.value: He will speak to the people for you, and it will be as if he were your mouth and as if you were God to him.

column.name: text
column.value: But take this staff in your hand so you can perform miraculous signs with it."

column.name: text
column.value: Then Moses went back to Jethro his father-in-law and said to him, "Let me go back to my own people in Egypt to see if any of them are still alive." Jethro said, "Go, and I wish you well."

column.name: text
column.value: Now the LORD had said to Moses in Midian, "Go back to Egypt, for all the men who wanted to kill you are dead."

column.name: text
column.value: So Moses took his wife and sons, put them on a donkey and started back to Egypt. And he took the staff of God in his hand.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD said to Moses, "When you return to Egypt, see that you perform before Pharaoh all the wonders I have given you the power to do. But I will harden his heart so that he will not let the people go.

column.name: text
column.value: Then say to Pharaoh, 'This is what the LORD says: Israel is my firstborn son,

column.name: text
column.value: and I told you, "Let my son go, so he may worship me." But you refused to let him go; so I will kill your firstborn son.'"

column.name: text
column.value: At a lodging place on the way, the LORD met Moses and was about to kill him.

column.name: text
column.value: But Zipporah took a flint knife, cut off her son's foreskin and touched Moses'feet with it. "Surely you are a bridegroom of blood to me," she said.

column.name: text
column.value: So the LORD let him alone. (At that time she said "bridegroom of blood," referring to circumcision.)

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD said to Aaron, "Go into the desert to meet Moses." So he met Moses at the mountain of God and kissed him.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Moses told Aaron everything the LORD had sent him to say, and also about all the miraculous signs he had commanded him to perform.

column.name: text
column.value: Moses and Aaron brought together all the elders of the Israelites,

column.name: text
column.value: and Aaron told them everything the LORD had said to Moses. He also performed the signs before the people,

column.name: text
column.value: and they believed. And when they heard that the LORD was concerned about them and had seen their misery, they bowed down and worshiped.

column.name: text
column.value: Afterward Moses and Aaron went to Pharaoh and said, "This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: 'Let my people go, so that they may hold a festival to me in the desert.'"

column.name: text
column.value: Pharaoh said, "Who is the LORD, that I should obey him and let Israel go? I do not know the LORD and I will not let Israel go."

column.name: text
column.value: Then they said, "The God of the Hebrews has met with us. Now let us take a three-day journey into the desert to offer sacrifices to the LORD our God, or he may strike us with plagues or with the sword."

column.name: text
column.value: But the king of Egypt said, "Moses and Aaron, why are you taking the people away from their labor? Get back to your work!"

column.name: text
column.value: Then Pharaoh said, "Look, the people of the land are now numerous, and you are stopping them from working."

column.name: text
column.value: That same day Pharaoh gave this order to the slave drivers and foremen in charge of the people:

column.name: text
column.value: "You are no longer to supply the people with straw for making bricks; let them go and gather their own straw.

column.name: text
column.value: But require them to make the same number of bricks as before; don't reduce the quota. They are lazy; that is why they are crying out, 'Let us go and sacrifice to our God.'

column.name: text
column.value: Make the work harder for the men so that they keep working and pay no attention to lies."

column.name: text
column.value: Then the slave drivers and the foremen went out and said to the people, "This is what Pharaoh says: 'I will not give you any more straw.

column.name: text
column.value: Go and get your own straw wherever you can find it, but your work will not be reduced at all.'"

column.name: text
column.value: So the people scattered all over Egypt to gather stubble to use for straw.

column.name: text
column.value: The slave drivers kept pressing them, saying, "Complete the work required of you for each day, just as when you had straw."

column.name: text
column.value: The Israelite foremen appointed by Pharaoh's slave drivers were beaten and were asked, "Why didn't you meet your quota of bricks yesterday or today, as before?"

column.name: text
column.value: Then the Israelite foremen went and appealed to Pharaoh: "Why have you treated your servants this way?

column.name: text
column.value: Your servants are given no straw, yet we are told, 'Make bricks!' Your servants are being beaten, but the fault is with your own people."

column.name: text
column.value: Pharaoh said, "Lazy, that's what you are--lazy! That is why you keep saying, 'Let us go and sacrifice to the LORD.'

column.name: text
column.value: Now get to work. You will not be given any straw, yet you must produce your full quota of bricks."

column.name: text
column.value: The Israelite foremen realized they were in trouble when they were told, "You are not to reduce the number of bricks required of you for each day."

column.name: text
column.value: When they left Pharaoh, they found Moses and Aaron waiting to meet them,

column.name: text
column.value: and they said, "May the LORD look upon you and judge you! You have made us a stench to Pharaoh and his officials and have put a sword in their hand to kill us."

column.name: text
column.value: Moses returned to the LORD and said, "O Lord, why have you brought trouble upon this people? Is this why you sent me?

column.name: text
column.value: Ever since I went to Pharaoh to speak in your name, he has brought trouble upon this people, and you have not rescued your people at all."

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD said to Moses, "See, I have made you like God to Pharaoh, and your brother Aaron will be your prophet.

column.name: text
column.value: You are to say everything I command you, and your brother Aaron is to tell Pharaoh to let the Israelites go out of his country.

column.name: text
column.value: But I will harden Pharaoh's heart, and though I multiply my miraculous signs and wonders in Egypt,

column.name: text
column.value: he will not listen to you. Then I will lay my hand on Egypt and with mighty acts of judgment I will bring out my divisions, my people the Israelites.

column.name: text
column.value: And the Egyptians will know that I am the LORD when I stretch out my hand against Egypt and bring the Israelites out of it."

column.name: text
column.value: Moses and Aaron did just as the LORD commanded them.

column.name: text
column.value: Moses was eighty years old and Aaron eighty-three when they spoke to Pharaoh.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD said to Moses and Aaron,

column.name: text
column.value: "When Pharaoh says to you, 'Perform a miracle,' then say to Aaron, 'Take your staff and throw it down before Pharaoh,' and it will become a snake."

column.name: text
column.value: So Moses and Aaron went to Pharaoh and did just as the LORD commanded. Aaron threw his staff down in front of Pharaoh and his officials, and it became a snake.

column.name: text
column.value: Pharaoh then summoned wise men and sorcerers, and the Egyptian magicians also did the same things by their secret arts:

column.name: text
column.value: Each one threw down his staff and it became a snake. But Aaron's staff swallowed up their staffs.

column.name: text
column.value: Yet Pharaoh's heart became hard and he would not listen to them, just as the LORD had said.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD said to Moses, "Pharaoh's heart is unyielding; he refuses to let the people go.

column.name: text
column.value: Go to Pharaoh in the morning as he goes out to the water. Wait on the bank of the Nile to meet him, and take in your hand the staff that was changed into a snake.

column.name: text
column.value: Then say to him, 'The LORD, the God of the Hebrews, has sent me to say to you: Let my people go, so that they may worship me in the desert. But until now you have not listened.

column.name: text
column.value: This is what the LORD says: By this you will know that I am the LORD: With the staff that is in my hand I will strike the water of the Nile, and it will be changed into blood.

column.name: text
column.value: The fish in the Nile will die, and the river will stink; the Egyptians will not be able to drink its water.'"

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD said to Moses, "Tell Aaron, 'Take your staff and stretch out your hand over the waters of Egypt--over the streams and canals, over the ponds and all the reservoirs'--and they will turn to blood. Blood will be everywhere in Egypt, even in the wooden buckets and stone jars."

column.name: text
column.value: Moses and Aaron did just as the LORD had commanded. He raised his staff in the presence of Pharaoh and his officials and struck the water of the Nile, and all the water was changed into blood.

column.name: text
column.value: The fish in the Nile died, and the river smelled so bad that the Egyptians could not drink its water. Blood was everywhere in Egypt.

column.name: text
column.value: But the Egyptian magicians did the same things by their secret arts, and Pharaoh's heart became hard; he would not listen to Moses and Aaron, just as the LORD had said.

column.name: text
column.value: Instead, he turned and went into his palace, and did not take even this to heart.

column.name: text
column.value: And all the Egyptians dug along the Nile to get drinking water, because they could not drink the water of the river.

column.name: text
column.value: Seven days passed after the LORD struck the Nile.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD said to Moses, "Now you will see what I will do to Pharaoh: Because of my mighty hand he will let them go; because of my mighty hand he will drive them out of his country."

column.name: text
column.value: God also said to Moses, "I am the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: I appeared to Abraham, to Isaac and to Jacob as God Almighty, but by my name the LORD I did not make myself known to them.

column.name: text
column.value: I also established my covenant with them to give them the land of Canaan, where they lived as aliens.

column.name: text
column.value: Moreover, I have heard the groaning of the Israelites, whom the Egyptians are enslaving, and I have remembered my covenant.

column.name: text
column.value: "Therefore, say to the Israelites: 'I am the LORD, and I will bring you out from under the yoke of the Egyptians. I will free you from being slaves to them, and I will redeem you with an outstretched arm and with mighty acts of judgment.

column.name: text
column.value: I will take you as my own people, and I will be your God. Then you will know that I am the LORD your God, who brought you out from under the yoke of the Egyptians.

column.name: text
column.value: And I will bring you to the land I swore with uplifted hand to give to Abraham, to Isaac and to Jacob. I will give it to you as a possession. I am the LORD.'"

column.name: text
column.value: Moses reported this to the Israelites, but they did not listen to him because of their discouragement and cruel bondage.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD said to Moses,

column.name: text
column.value: "Go, tell Pharaoh king of Egypt to let the Israelites go out of his country."

column.name: text
column.value: But Moses said to the LORD, "If the Israelites will not listen to me, why would Pharaoh listen to me, since I speak with faltering lips?"

column.name: text
column.value: Now the LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron about the Israelites and Pharaoh king of Egypt, and he commanded them to bring the Israelites out of Egypt.

column.name: text
column.value: These were the heads of their families: The sons of Reuben the firstborn son of Israel were Hanoch and Pallu, Hezron and Carmi. These were the clans of Reuben.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Simeon were Jemuel, Jamin, Ohad, Jakin, Zohar and Shaul the son of a Canaanite woman. These were the clans of Simeon.

column.name: text
column.value: These were the names of the sons of Levi according to their records: Gershon, Kohath and Merari. Levi lived 137 years.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Gershon, by clans, were Libni and Shimei.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Kohath were Amram, Izhar, Hebron and Uzziel. Kohath lived 133 years.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Merari were Mahli and Mushi. These were the clans of Levi according to their records.

column.name: text
column.value: Amram married his father's sister Jochebed, who bore him Aaron and Moses. Amram lived 137 years.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Izhar were Korah, Nepheg and Zicri.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Uzziel were Mishael, Elzaphan and Sithri.

column.name: text
column.value: Aaron married Elisheba, daughter of Amminadab and sister of Nahshon, and she bore him Nadab and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Korah were Assir, Elkanah and Abiasaph. These were the Korahite clans.

column.name: text
column.value: Eleazar son of Aaron married one of the daughters of Putiel, and she bore him Phinehas. These were the heads of the Levite families, clan by clan.

column.name: text
column.value: It was this same Aaron and Moses to whom the LORD said, "Bring the Israelites out of Egypt by their divisions."

column.name: text
column.value: They were the ones who spoke to Pharaoh king of Egypt about bringing the Israelites out of Egypt. It was the same Moses and Aaron.

column.name: text
column.value: Now when the LORD spoke to Moses in Egypt,

column.name: text
column.value: he said to him, "I am the LORD. Tell Pharaoh king of Egypt everything I tell you."

column.name: text
column.value: But Moses said to the LORD, "Since I speak with faltering lips, why would Pharaoh listen to me?"

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD said to Moses, "Go to Pharaoh and say to him, 'This is what the LORD says: Let my people go, so that they may worship me.

column.name: text
column.value: If you refuse to let them go, I will plague your whole country with frogs.

column.name: text
column.value: The Nile will teem with frogs. They will come up into your palace and your bedroom and onto your bed, into the houses of your officials and on your people, and into your ovens and kneading troughs.

column.name: text
column.value: The frogs will go up on you and your people and all your officials.'"

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD said to Moses, "Tell Aaron, 'Stretch out your hand with your staff over the streams and canals and ponds, and make frogs come up on the land of Egypt.'"

column.name: text
column.value: So Aaron stretched out his hand over the waters of Egypt, and the frogs came up and covered the land.

column.name: text
column.value: But the magicians did the same things by their secret arts; they also made frogs come up on the land of Egypt.

column.name: text
column.value: Pharaoh summoned Moses and Aaron and said, "Pray to the LORD to take the frogs away from me and my people, and I will let your people go to offer sacrifices to the LORD."

column.name: text
column.value: Moses said to Pharaoh, "I leave to you the honor of setting the time for me to pray for you and your officials and your people that you and your houses may be rid of the frogs, except for those that remain in the Nile."

column.name: text
column.value: "Tomorrow," Pharaoh said. Moses replied, "It will be as you say, so that you may know there is no one like the LORD our God.

column.name: text
column.value: The frogs will leave you and your houses, your officials and your people; they will remain only in the Nile."

column.name: text
column.value: After Moses and Aaron left Pharaoh, Moses cried out to the LORD about the frogs he had brought on Pharaoh.

column.name: text
column.value: And the LORD did what Moses asked. The frogs died in the houses, in the courtyards and in the fields.

column.name: text
column.value: They were piled into heaps, and the land reeked of them.

column.name: text
column.value: But when Pharaoh saw that there was relief, he hardened his heart and would not listen to Moses and Aaron, just as the LORD had said.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD said to Moses, "Tell Aaron, 'Stretch out your staff and strike the dust of the ground,' and throughout the land of Egypt the dust will become gnats."

column.name: text
column.value: They did this, and when Aaron stretched out his hand with the staff and struck the dust of the ground, gnats came upon men and animals. All the dust throughout the land of Egypt became gnats.

column.name: text
column.value: But when the magicians tried to produce gnats by their secret arts, they could not. And the gnats were on men and animals.

column.name: text
column.value: The magicians said to Pharaoh, "This is the finger of God." But Pharaoh's heart was hard and he would not listen, just as the LORD had said.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD said to Moses, "Get up early in the morning and confront Pharaoh as he goes to the water and say to him, 'This is what the LORD says: Let my people go, so that they may worship me.

column.name: text
column.value: If you do not let my people go, I will send swarms of flies on you and your officials, on your people and into your houses. The houses of the Egyptians will be full of flies, and even the ground where they are.

column.name: text
column.value: "'But on that day I will deal differently with the land of Goshen, where my people live; no swarms of flies will be there, so that you will know that I, the LORD, am in this land.

column.name: text
column.value: I will make a distinction between my people and your people. This miraculous sign will occur tomorrow.'"

column.name: text
column.value: And the LORD did this. Dense swarms of flies poured into Pharaoh's palace and into the houses of his officials, and throughout Egypt the land was ruined by the flies.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Pharaoh summoned Moses and Aaron and said, "Go, sacrifice to your God here in the land."

column.name: text
column.value: But Moses said, "That would not be right. The sacrifices we offer the LORD our God would be detestable to the Egyptians. And if we offer sacrifices that are detestable in their eyes, will they not stone us?

column.name: text
column.value: We must take a three-day journey into the desert to offer sacrifices to the LORD our God, as he commands us."

column.name: text
column.value: Pharaoh said, "I will let you go to offer sacrifices to the LORD your God in the desert, but you must not go very far. Now pray for me."

column.name: text
column.value: Moses answered, "As soon as I leave you, I will pray to the LORD, and tomorrow the flies will leave Pharaoh and his officials and his people. Only be sure that Pharaoh does not act deceitfully again by not letting the people go to offer sacrifices to the LORD."

column.name: text
column.value: Then Moses left Pharaoh and prayed to the LORD,

column.name: text
column.value: and the LORD did what Moses asked: The flies left Pharaoh and his officials and his people; not a fly remained.

column.name: text
column.value: But this time also Pharaoh hardened his heart and would not let the people go.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD said to Moses, "Go to Pharaoh and say to him, 'This is what the LORD, the God of the Hebrews, says: "Let my people go, so that they may worship me."

column.name: text
column.value: If you refuse to let them go and continue to hold them back,

column.name: text
column.value: the hand of the LORD will bring a terrible plague on your livestock in the field--on your horses and donkeys and camels and on your cattle and sheep and goats.

column.name: text
column.value: But the LORD will make a distinction between the livestock of Israel and that of Egypt, so that no animal belonging to the Israelites will die.'"

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD set a time and said, "Tomorrow the LORD will do this in the land."

column.name: text
column.value: And the next day the LORD did it: All the livestock of the Egyptians died, but not one animal belonging to the Israelites died.

column.name: text
column.value: Pharaoh sent men to investigate and found that not even one of the animals of the Israelites had died. Yet his heart was unyielding and he would not let the people go.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD said to Moses and Aaron, "Take handfuls of soot from a furnace and have Moses toss it into the air in the presence of Pharaoh.

column.name: text
column.value: It will become fine dust over the whole land of Egypt, and festering boils will break out on men and animals throughout the land."

column.name: text
column.value: So they took soot from a furnace and stood before Pharaoh. Moses tossed it into the air, and festering boils broke out on men and animals.

column.name: text
column.value: The magicians could not stand before Moses because of the boils that were on them and on all the Egyptians.

column.name: text
column.value: But the LORD hardened Pharaoh's heart and he would not listen to Moses and Aaron, just as the LORD had said to Moses.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD said to Moses, "Get up early in the morning, confront Pharaoh and say to him, 'This is what the LORD, the God of the Hebrews, says: Let my people go, so that they may worship me,

column.name: text
column.value: or this time I will send the full force of my plagues against you and against your officials and your people, so you may know that there is no one like me in all the earth.

column.name: text
column.value: For by now I could have stretched out my hand and struck you and your people with a plague that would have wiped you off the earth.

column.name: text
column.value: But I have raised you up for this very purpose, that I might show you my power and that my name might be proclaimed in all the earth.

column.name: text
column.value: You still set yourself against my people and will not let them go.

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore, at this time tomorrow I will send the worst hailstorm that has ever fallen on Egypt, from the day it was founded till now.

column.name: text
column.value: Give an order now to bring your livestock and everything you have in the field to a place of shelter, because the hail will fall on every man and animal that has not been brought in and is still out in the field, and they will die.'"

column.name: text
column.value: Those officials of Pharaoh who feared the word of the LORD hurried to bring their slaves and their livestock inside.

column.name: text
column.value: But those who ignored the word of the LORD left their slaves and livestock in the field.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD said to Moses, "Stretch out your hand toward the sky so that hail will fall all over Egypt--on men and animals and on everything growing in the fields of Egypt."

column.name: text
column.value: When Moses stretched out his staff toward the sky, the LORD sent thunder and hail, and lightning flashed down to the ground. So the LORD rained hail on the land of Egypt;

column.name: text
column.value: hail fell and lightning flashed back and forth. It was the worst storm in all the land of Egypt since it had become a nation.

column.name: text
column.value: Throughout Egypt hail struck everything in the fields--both men and animals; it beat down everything growing in the fields and stripped every tree.

column.name: text
column.value: The only place it did not hail was the land of Goshen, where the Israelites were.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Pharaoh summoned Moses and Aaron. "This time I have sinned," he said to them. "The LORD is in the right, and I and my people are in the wrong.

column.name: text
column.value: Pray to the LORD, for we have had enough thunder and hail. I will let you go; you don't have to stay any longer."

column.name: text
column.value: Moses replied, "When I have gone out of the city, I will spread out my hands in prayer to the LORD. The thunder will stop and there will be no more hail, so you may know that the earth is the LORD'S.

column.name: text
column.value: But I know that you and your officials still do not fear the LORD God."

column.name: text
column.value: (The flax and barley were destroyed, since the barley had headed and the flax was in bloom.

column.name: text
column.value: The wheat and spelt, however, were not destroyed, because they ripen later.)

column.name: text
column.value: Then Moses left Pharaoh and went out of the city. He spread out his hands toward the LORD; the thunder and hail stopped, and the rain no longer poured down on the land.

column.name: text
column.value: When Pharaoh saw that the rain and hail and thunder had stopped, he sinned again: He and his officials hardened their hearts.

column.name: text
column.value: So Pharaoh's heart was hard and he would not let the Israelites go, just as the LORD had said through Moses.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD said to Moses, "Go to Pharaoh, for I have hardened his heart and the hearts of his officials so that I may perform these miraculous signs of mine among them

column.name: text
column.value: that you may tell your children and grandchildren how I dealt harshly with the Egyptians and how I performed my signs among them, and that you may know that I am the LORD."

column.name: text
column.value: So Moses and Aaron went to Pharaoh and said to him, "This is what the LORD, the God of the Hebrews, says: 'How long will you refuse to humble yourself before me? Let my people go, so that they may worship me.

column.name: text
column.value: If you refuse to let them go, I will bring locusts into your country tomorrow.

column.name: text
column.value: They will cover the face of the ground so that it cannot be seen. They will devour what little you have left after the hail, including every tree that is growing in your fields.

column.name: text
column.value: They will fill your houses and those of all your officials and all the Egyptians--something neither your fathers nor your forefathers have ever seen from the day they settled in this land till now.'" Then Moses turned and left Pharaoh.

column.name: text
column.value: Pharaoh's officials said to him, "How long will this man be a snare to us? Let the people go, so that they may worship the LORD their God. Do you not yet realize that Egypt is ruined?"

column.name: text
column.value: Then Moses and Aaron were brought back to Pharaoh. "Go, worship the LORD your God," he said. "But just who will be going?"

column.name: text
column.value: Moses answered, "We will go with our young and old, with our sons and daughters, and with our flocks and herds, because we are to celebrate a festival to the LORD."

column.name: text
column.value: Pharaoh said, "The LORD be with you--if I let you go, along with your women and children! Clearly you are bent on evil.

column.name: text
column.value: No! Have only the men go; and worship the LORD, since that's what you have been asking for." Then Moses and Aaron were driven out of Pharaoh's presence.

column.name: text
column.value: And the LORD said to Moses, "Stretch out your hand over Egypt so that locusts will swarm over the land and devour everything growing in the fields, everything left by the hail."

column.name: text
column.value: So Moses stretched out his staff over Egypt, and the LORD made an east wind blow across the land all that day and all that night. By morning the wind had brought the locusts;

column.name: text
column.value: they invaded all Egypt and settled down in every area of the country in great numbers. Never before had there been such a plague of locusts, nor will there ever be again.

column.name: text
column.value: They covered all the ground until it was black. They devoured all that was left after the hail--everything growing in the fields and the fruit on the trees. Nothing green remained on tree or plant in all the land of Egypt.

column.name: text
column.value: Pharaoh quickly summoned Moses and Aaron and said, "I have sinned against the LORD your God and against you.

column.name: text
column.value: Now forgive my sin once more and pray to the LORD your God to take this deadly plague away from me."

column.name: text
column.value: Moses then left Pharaoh and prayed to the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: And the LORD changed the wind to a very strong west wind, which caught up the locusts and carried them into the Red Sea. Not a locust was left anywhere in Egypt.

column.name: text
column.value: But the LORD hardened Pharaoh's heart, and he would not let the Israelites go.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD said to Moses, "Stretch out your hand toward the sky so that darkness will spread over Egypt--darkness that can be felt."

column.name: text
column.value: So Moses stretched out his hand toward the sky, and total darkness covered all Egypt for three days.

column.name: text
column.value: No one could see anyone else or leave his place for three days. Yet all the Israelites had light in the places where they lived.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Pharaoh summoned Moses and said, "Go, worship the LORD. Even your women and children may go with you; only leave your flocks and herds behind."

column.name: text
column.value: But Moses said, "You must allow us to have sacrifices and burnt offerings to present to the LORD our God.

column.name: text
column.value: Our livestock too must go with us; not a hoof is to be left behind. We have to use some of them in worshiping the LORD our God, and until we get there we will not know what we are to use to worship the LORD."

column.name: text
column.value: But the LORD hardened Pharaoh's heart, and he was not willing to let them go.

column.name: text
column.value: Pharaoh said to Moses, "Get out of my sight! Make sure you do not appear before me again! The day you see my face you will die."

column.name: text
column.value: "Just as you say," Moses replied, "I will never appear before you again."

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD said to Moses,

column.name: text
column.value: "Tell the Israelites to turn back and encamp near Pi Hahiroth, between Migdol and the sea. They are to encamp by the sea, directly opposite Baal Zephon.

column.name: text
column.value: Pharaoh will think, 'The Israelites are wandering around the land in confusion, hemmed in by the desert.'

column.name: text
column.value: And I will harden Pharaoh's heart, and he will pursue them. But I will gain glory for myself through Pharaoh and all his army, and the Egyptians will know that I am the LORD." So the Israelites did this.

column.name: text
column.value: When the king of Egypt was told that the people had fled, Pharaoh and his officials changed their minds about them and said, "What have we done? We have let the Israelites go and have lost their services!"

column.name: text
column.value: So he had his chariot made ready and took his army with him.

column.name: text
column.value: He took six hundred of the best chariots, along with all the other chariots of Egypt, with officers over all of them.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD hardened the heart of Pharaoh king of Egypt, so that he pursued the Israelites, who were marching out boldly.

column.name: text
column.value: The Egyptians--all Pharaoh's horses and chariots, horsemen and troops--pursued the Israelites and overtook them as they camped by the sea near Pi Hahiroth, opposite Baal Zephon.

column.name: text
column.value: As Pharaoh approached, the Israelites looked up, and there were the Egyptians, marching after them. They were terrified and cried out to the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: They said to Moses, "Was it because there were no graves in Egypt that you brought us to the desert to die? What have you done to us by bringing us out of Egypt?

column.name: text
column.value: Didn't we say to you in Egypt, 'Leave us alone; let us serve the Egyptians'? It would have been better for us to serve the Egyptians than to die in the desert!"

column.name: text
column.value: Moses answered the people, "Do not be afraid. Stand firm and you will see the deliverance the LORD will bring you today. The Egyptians you see today you will never see again.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD will fight for you; you need only to be still."

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD said to Moses, "Why are you crying out to me? Tell the Israelites to move on.

column.name: text
column.value: Raise your staff and stretch out your hand over the sea to divide the water so that the Israelites can go through the sea on dry ground.

column.name: text
column.value: I will harden the hearts of the Egyptians so that they will go in after them. And I will gain glory through Pharaoh and all his army, through his chariots and his horsemen.

column.name: text
column.value: The Egyptians will know that I am the LORD when I gain glory through Pharaoh, his chariots and his horsemen."

column.name: text
column.value: Then the angel of God, who had been traveling in front of Israel's army, withdrew and went behind them. The pillar of cloud also moved from in front and stood behind them,

column.name: text
column.value: coming between the armies of Egypt and Israel. Throughout the night the cloud brought darkness to the one side and light to the other side; so neither went near the other all night long.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Moses stretched out his hand over the sea, and all that night the LORD drove the sea back with a strong east wind and turned it into dry land. The waters were divided,

column.name: text
column.value: and the Israelites went through the sea on dry ground, with a wall of water on their right and on their left.

column.name: text
column.value: The Egyptians pursued them, and all Pharaoh's horses and chariots and horsemen followed them into the sea.

column.name: text
column.value: During the last watch of the night the LORD looked down from the pillar of fire and cloud at the Egyptian army and threw it into confusion.

column.name: text
column.value: He made the wheels of their chariots come off so that they had difficulty driving. And the Egyptians said, "Let's get away from the Israelites! The LORD is fighting for them against Egypt."

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD said to Moses, "Stretch out your hand over the sea so that the waters may flow back over the Egyptians and their chariots and horsemen."

column.name: text
column.value: Moses stretched out his hand over the sea, and at daybreak the sea went back to its place. The Egyptians were fleeing toward it, and the LORD swept them into the sea.

column.name: text
column.value: The water flowed back and covered the chariots and horsemen--the entire army of Pharaoh that had followed the Israelites into the sea. Not one of them survived.

column.name: text
column.value: But the Israelites went through the sea on dry ground, with a wall of water on their right and on their left.

column.name: text
column.value: That day the LORD saved Israel from the hands of the Egyptians, and Israel saw the Egyptians lying dead on the shore.

column.name: text
column.value: And when the Israelites saw the great power the LORD displayed against the Egyptians, the people feared the LORD and put their trust in him and in Moses his servant.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD said to Moses and Aaron in Egypt,

column.name: text
column.value: "This month is to be for you the first month, the first month of your year.

column.name: text
column.value: Tell the whole community of Israel that on the tenth day of this month each man is to take a lamb for his family, one for each household.

column.name: text
column.value: If any household is too small for a whole lamb, they must share one with their nearest neighbor, having taken into account the number of people there are. You are to determine the amount of lamb needed in accordance with what each person will eat.

column.name: text
column.value: The animals you choose must be year-old males without defect, and you may take them from the sheep or the goats.

column.name: text
column.value: Take care of them until the fourteenth day of the month, when all the people of the community of Israel must slaughter them at twilight.

column.name: text
column.value: Then they are to take some of the blood and put it on the sides and tops of the doorframes of the houses where they eat the lambs.

column.name: text
column.value: That same night they are to eat the meat roasted over the fire, along with bitter herbs, and bread made without yeast.

column.name: text
column.value: Do not eat the meat raw or cooked in water, but roast it over the fire--head, legs and inner parts.

column.name: text
column.value: Do not leave any of it till morning; if some is left till morning, you must burn it.

column.name: text
column.value: This is how you are to eat it: with your cloak tucked into your belt, your sandals on your feet and your staff in your hand. Eat it in haste; it is the LORD'S Passover.

column.name: text
column.value: "On that same night I will pass through Egypt and strike down every firstborn--both men and animals--and I will bring judgment on all the gods of Egypt. I am the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: The blood will be a sign for you on the houses where you are; and when I see the blood, I will pass over you. No destructive plague will touch you when I strike Egypt.

column.name: text
column.value: "This is a day you are to commemorate; for the generations to come you shall celebrate it as a festival to the LORD--a lasting ordinance.

column.name: text
column.value: For seven days you are to eat bread made without yeast. On the first day remove the yeast from your houses, for whoever eats anything with yeast in it from the first day through the seventh must be cut off from Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: On the first day hold a sacred assembly, and another one on the seventh day. Do no work at all on these days, except to prepare food for everyone to eat--that is all you may do.

column.name: text
column.value: "Celebrate the Feast of Unleavened Bread, because it was on this very day that I brought your divisions out of Egypt. Celebrate this day as a lasting ordinance for the generations to come.

column.name: text
column.value: In the first month you are to eat bread made without yeast, from the evening of the fourteenth day until the evening of the twenty-first day.

column.name: text
column.value: For seven days no yeast is to be found in your houses. And whoever eats anything with yeast in it must be cut off from the community of Israel, whether he is an alien or native-born.

column.name: text
column.value: Eat nothing made with yeast. Wherever you live, you must eat unleavened bread."

column.name: text
column.value: Then Moses summoned all the elders of Israel and said to them, "Go at once and select the animals for your families and slaughter the Passover lamb.

column.name: text
column.value: Take a bunch of hyssop, dip it into the blood in the basin and put some of the blood on the top and on both sides of the doorframe. Not one of you shall go out the door of his house until morning.

column.name: text
column.value: When the LORD goes through the land to strike down the Egyptians, he will see the blood on the top and sides of the doorframe and will pass over that doorway, and he will not permit the destroyer to enter your houses and strike you down.

column.name: text
column.value: "Obey these instructions as a lasting ordinance for you and your descendants.

column.name: text
column.value: When you enter the land that the LORD will give you as he promised, observe this ceremony.

column.name: text
column.value: And when your children ask you, 'What does this ceremony mean to you?'

column.name: text
column.value: then tell them, 'It is the Passover sacrifice to the LORD, who passed over the houses of the Israelites in Egypt and spared our homes when he struck down the Egyptians.'" Then the people bowed down and worshiped.

column.name: text
column.value: The Israelites did just what the LORD commanded Moses and Aaron.

column.name: text
column.value: At midnight the LORD struck down all the firstborn in Egypt, from the firstborn of Pharaoh, who sat on the throne, to the firstborn of the prisoner, who was in the dungeon, and the firstborn of all the livestock as well.

column.name: text
column.value: Pharaoh and all his officials and all the Egyptians got up during the night, and there was loud wailing in Egypt, for there was not a house without someone dead.

column.name: text
column.value: During the night Pharaoh summoned Moses and Aaron and said, "Up! Leave my people, you and the Israelites! Go, worship the LORD as you have requested.

column.name: text
column.value: Take your flocks and herds, as you have said, and go. And also bless me."

column.name: text
column.value: The Egyptians urged the people to hurry and leave the country. "For otherwise," they said, "we will all die!"

column.name: text
column.value: So the people took their dough before the yeast was added, and carried it on their shoulders in kneading troughs wrapped in clothing.

column.name: text
column.value: The Israelites did as Moses instructed and asked the Egyptians for articles of silver and gold and for clothing.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD had made the Egyptians favorably disposed toward the people, and they gave them what they asked for; so they plundered the Egyptians.

column.name: text
column.value: The Israelites journeyed from Rameses to Succoth. There were about six hundred thousand men on foot, besides women and children.

column.name: text
column.value: Many other people went up with them, as well as large droves of livestock, both flocks and herds.

column.name: text
column.value: With the dough they had brought from Egypt, they baked cakes of unleavened bread. The dough was without yeast because they had been driven out of Egypt and did not have time to prepare food for themselves.

column.name: text
column.value: Now the length of time the Israelite people lived in Egypt was 430 years.

column.name: text
column.value: At the end of the 430 years, to the very day, all the LORD'S divisions left Egypt.

column.name: text
column.value: Because the LORD kept vigil that night to bring them out of Egypt, on this night all the Israelites are to keep vigil to honor the LORD for the generations to come.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD said to Moses and Aaron, "These are the regulations for the Passover: "No foreigner is to eat of it.

column.name: text
column.value: Any slave you have bought may eat of it after you have circumcised him,

column.name: text
column.value: but a temporary resident and a hired worker may not eat of it.

column.name: text
column.value: "It must be eaten inside one house; take none of the meat outside the house. Do not break any of the bones.

column.name: text
column.value: The whole community of Israel must celebrate it.

column.name: text
column.value: "An alien living among you who wants to celebrate the LORD'S Passover must have all the males in his household circumcised; then he may take part like one born in the land. No uncircumcised male may eat of it.

column.name: text
column.value: The same law applies to the native-born and to the alien living among you."

column.name: text
column.value: All the Israelites did just what the LORD had commanded Moses and Aaron.

column.name: text
column.value: And on that very day the LORD brought the Israelites out of Egypt by their divisions.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Moses and the Israelites sang this song to the LORD: "I will sing to the LORD, for he is highly exalted. The horse and its rider he has hurled into the sea.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD is my strength and my song; he has become my salvation. He is my God, and I will praise him, my father's God, and I will exalt him.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD is a warrior; the LORD is his name.

column.name: text
column.value: Pharaoh's chariots and his army he has hurled into the sea. The best of Pharaoh's officers are drowned in the Red Sea.

column.name: text
column.value: The deep waters have covered them; they sank to the depths like a stone.

column.name: text
column.value: "Your right hand, O LORD, was majestic in power. Your right hand, O LORD, shattered the enemy.

column.name: text
column.value: In the greatness of your majesty you threw down those who opposed you. You unleashed your burning anger; it consumed them like stubble.

column.name: text
column.value: By the blast of your nostrils the waters piled up. The surging waters stood firm like a wall; the deep waters congealed in the heart of the sea.

column.name: text
column.value: "The enemy boasted, 'I will pursue, I will overtake them. I will divide the spoils; I will gorge myself on them. I will draw my sword and my hand will destroy them.'

column.name: text
column.value: But you blew with your breath, and the sea covered them. They sank like lead in the mighty waters.

column.name: text
column.value: "Who among the gods is like you, O LORD? Who is like you--majestic in holiness, awesome in glory, working wonders?

column.name: text
column.value: You stretched out your right hand and the earth swallowed them.

column.name: text
column.value: "In your unfailing love you will lead the people you have redeemed. In your strength you will guide them to your holy dwelling.

column.name: text
column.value: The nations will hear and tremble; anguish will grip the people of Philistia.

column.name: text
column.value: The chiefs of Edom will be terrified, the leaders of Moab will be seized with trembling, the people of Canaan will melt away;

column.name: text
column.value: terror and dread will fall upon them. By the power of your arm they will be as still as a stone--until your people pass by, O LORD, until the people you bought pass by.

column.name: text
column.value: You will bring them in and plant them on the mountain of your inheritance--the place, O LORD, you made for your dwelling, the sanctuary, O Lord, your hands established.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD will reign for ever and ever."

column.name: text
column.value: When Pharaoh's horses, chariots and horsemen went into the sea, the LORD brought the waters of the sea back over them, but the Israelites walked through the sea on dry ground.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Miriam the prophetess, Aaron's sister, took a tambourine in her hand, and all the women followed her, with tambourines and dancing.

column.name: text
column.value: Miriam sang to them: "Sing to the LORD, for he is highly exalted. The horse and its rider he has hurled into the sea."

column.name: text
column.value: Then Moses led Israel from the Red Sea and they went into the Desert of Shur. For three days they traveled in the desert without finding water.

column.name: text
column.value: When they came to Marah, they could not drink its water because it was bitter. (That is why the place is called Marah.)

column.name: text
column.value: So the people grumbled against Moses, saying, "What are we to drink?"

column.name: text
column.value: Then Moses cried out to the LORD, and the LORD showed him a piece of wood. He threw it into the water, and the water became sweet. There the LORD made a decree and a law for them, and there he tested them.

column.name: text
column.value: He said, "If you listen carefully to the voice of the LORD your God and do what is right in his eyes, if you pay attention to his commands and keep all his decrees, I will not bring on you any of the diseases I brought on the Egyptians, for I am the LORD, who heals you."

column.name: text
column.value: Then they came to Elim, where there were twelve springs and seventy palm trees, and they camped there near the water.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD said to Moses,

column.name: text
column.value: "Consecrate to me every firstborn male. The first offspring of every womb among the Israelites belongs to me, whether man or animal."

column.name: text
column.value: Then Moses said to the people, "Commemorate this day, the day you came out of Egypt, out of the land of slavery, because the LORD brought you out of it with a mighty hand. Eat nothing containing yeast.

column.name: text
column.value: Today, in the month of Abib, you are leaving.

column.name: text
column.value: When the LORD brings you into the land of the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Hivites and Jebusites--the land he swore to your forefathers to give you, a land flowing with milk and honey--you are to observe this ceremony in this month:

column.name: text
column.value: For seven days eat bread made without yeast and on the seventh day hold a festival to the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: Eat unleavened bread during those seven days; nothing with yeast in it is to be seen among you, nor shall any yeast be seen anywhere within your borders.

column.name: text
column.value: On that day tell your son, 'I do this because of what the LORD did for me when I came out of Egypt.'

column.name: text
column.value: This observance will be for you like a sign on your hand and a reminder on your forehead that the law of the LORD is to be on your lips. For the LORD brought you out of Egypt with his mighty hand.

column.name: text
column.value: You must keep this ordinance at the appointed time year after year.

column.name: text
column.value: "After the LORD brings you into the land of the Canaanites and gives it to you, as he promised on oath to you and your forefathers,

column.name: text
column.value: you are to give over to the LORD the first offspring of every womb. All the firstborn males of your livestock belong to the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: Redeem with a lamb every firstborn donkey, but if you do not redeem it, break its neck. Redeem every firstborn among your sons.

column.name: text
column.value: "In days to come, when your son asks you, 'What does this mean?' say to him, 'With a mighty hand the LORD brought us out of Egypt, out of the land of slavery.

column.name: text
column.value: When Pharaoh stubbornly refused to let us go, the LORD killed every firstborn in Egypt, both man and animal. This is why I sacrifice to the LORD the first male offspring of every womb and redeem each of my firstborn sons.'

column.name: text
column.value: And it will be like a sign on your hand and a symbol on your forehead that the LORD brought us out of Egypt with his mighty hand."

column.name: text
column.value: When Pharaoh let the people go, God did not lead them on the road through the Philistine country, though that was shorter. For God said, "If they face war, they might change their minds and return to Egypt."

column.name: text
column.value: So God led the people around by the desert road toward the Red Sea. The Israelites went up out of Egypt armed for battle.

column.name: text
column.value: Moses took the bones of Joseph with him because Joseph had made the sons of Israel swear an oath. He had said, "God will surely come to your aid, and then you must carry my bones up with you from this place."

column.name: text
column.value: After leaving Succoth they camped at Etham on the edge of the desert.

column.name: text
column.value: By day the LORD went ahead of them in a pillar of cloud to guide them on their way and by night in a pillar of fire to give them light, so that they could travel by day or night.

column.name: text
column.value: Neither the pillar of cloud by day nor the pillar of fire by night left its place in front of the people.

column.name: text
column.value: The whole Israelite community set out from Elim and came to the Desert of Sin, which is between Elim and Sinai, on the fifteenth day of the second month after they had come out of Egypt.

column.name: text
column.value: In the desert the whole community grumbled against Moses and Aaron.

column.name: text
column.value: The Israelites said to them, "If only we had died by the LORD'S hand in Egypt! There we sat around pots of meat and ate all the food we wanted, but you have brought us out into this desert to starve this entire assembly to death."

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD said to Moses, "I will rain down bread from heaven for you. The people are to go out each day and gather enough for that day. In this way I will test them and see whether they will follow my instructions.

column.name: text
column.value: On the sixth day they are to prepare what they bring in, and that is to be twice as much as they gather on the other days."

column.name: text
column.value: So Moses and Aaron said to all the Israelites, "In the evening you will know that it was the LORD who brought you out of Egypt,

column.name: text
column.value: and in the morning you will see the glory of the LORD, because he has heard your grumbling against him. Who are we, that you should grumble against us?"

column.name: text
column.value: Moses also said, "You will know that it was the LORD when he gives you meat to eat in the evening and all the bread you want in the morning, because he has heard your grumbling against him. Who are we? You are not grumbling against us, but against the LORD."

column.name: text
column.value: Then Moses told Aaron, "Say to the entire Israelite community, 'Come before the LORD, for he has heard your grumbling.'"

column.name: text
column.value: While Aaron was speaking to the whole Israelite community, they looked toward the desert, and there was the glory of the LORD appearing in the cloud.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD said to Moses,

column.name: text
column.value: "I have heard the grumbling of the Israelites. Tell them, 'At twilight you will eat meat, and in the morning you will be filled with bread. Then you will know that I am the LORD your God.'"

column.name: text
column.value: That evening quail came and covered the camp, and in the morning there was a layer of dew around the camp.

column.name: text
column.value: When the dew was gone, thin flakes like frost on the ground appeared on the desert floor.

column.name: text
column.value: When the Israelites saw it, they said to each other, "What is it?" For they did not know what it was. Moses said to them, "It is the bread the LORD has given you to eat.

column.name: text
column.value: This is what the LORD has commanded: 'Each one is to gather as much as he needs. Take an omer for each person you have in your tent.'"

column.name: text
column.value: The Israelites did as they were told; some gathered much, some little.

column.name: text
column.value: And when they measured it by the omer, he who gathered much did not have too much, and he who gathered little did not have too little. Each one gathered as much as he needed.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Moses said to them, "No one is to keep any of it until morning."

column.name: text
column.value: However, some of them paid no attention to Moses; they kept part of it until morning, but it was full of maggots and began to smell. So Moses was angry with them.

column.name: text
column.value: Each morning everyone gathered as much as he needed, and when the sun grew hot, it melted away.

column.name: text
column.value: On the sixth day, they gathered twice as much--two omers for each person--and the leaders of the community came and reported this to Moses.

column.name: text
column.value: He said to them, "This is what the LORD commanded: 'Tomorrow is to be a day of rest, a holy Sabbath to the LORD. So bake what you want to bake and boil what you want to boil. Save whatever is left and keep it until morning.'"

column.name: text
column.value: So they saved it until morning, as Moses commanded, and it did not stink or get maggots in it.

column.name: text
column.value: "Eat it today," Moses said, "because today is a Sabbath to the LORD. You will not find any of it on the ground today.

column.name: text
column.value: Six days you are to gather it, but on the seventh day, the Sabbath, there will not be any."

column.name: text
column.value: Nevertheless, some of the people went out on the seventh day to gather it, but they found none.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD said to Moses, "How long will you refuse to keep my commands and my instructions?

column.name: text
column.value: Bear in mind that the LORD has given you the Sabbath; that is why on the sixth day he gives you bread for two days. Everyone is to stay where he is on the seventh day; no one is to go out."

column.name: text
column.value: So the people rested on the seventh day.

column.name: text
column.value: The people of Israel called the bread manna. It was white like coriander seed and tasted like wafers made with honey.

column.name: text
column.value: Moses said, "This is what the LORD has commanded: 'Take an omer of manna and keep it for the generations to come, so they can see the bread I gave you to eat in the desert when I brought you out of Egypt.'"

column.name: text
column.value: So Moses said to Aaron, "Take a jar and put an omer of manna in it. Then place it before the LORD to be kept for the generations to come."

column.name: text
column.value: As the LORD commanded Moses, Aaron put the manna in front of the Testimony, that it might be kept.

column.name: text
column.value: The Israelites ate manna forty years, until they came to a land that was settled; they ate manna until they reached the border of Canaan.

column.name: text
column.value: (An omer is one tenth of an ephah.)

column.name: text
column.value: The whole Israelite community set out from the Desert of Sin, traveling from place to place as the LORD commanded. They camped at Rephidim, but there was no water for the people to drink.

column.name: text
column.value: So they quarreled with Moses and said, "Give us water to drink." Moses replied, "Why do you quarrel with me? Why do you put the LORD to the test?"

column.name: text
column.value: But the people were thirsty for water there, and they grumbled against Moses. They said, "Why did you bring us up out of Egypt to make us and our children and livestock die of thirst?"

column.name: text
column.value: Then Moses cried out to the LORD, "What am I to do with these people? They are almost ready to stone me."

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD answered Moses, "Walk on ahead of the people. Take with you some of the elders of Israel and take in your hand the staff with which you struck the Nile, and go.

column.name: text
column.value: I will stand there before you by the rock at Horeb. Strike the rock, and water will come out of it for the people to drink." So Moses did this in the sight of the elders of Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: And he called the place Massah and Meribah because the Israelites quarreled and because they tested the LORD saying, "Is the LORD among us or not?"

column.name: text
column.value: The Amalekites came and attacked the Israelites at Rephidim.

column.name: text
column.value: Moses said to Joshua, "Choose some of our men and go out to fight the Amalekites. Tomorrow I will stand on top of the hill with the staff of God in my hands."

column.name: text
column.value: So Joshua fought the Amalekites as Moses had ordered, and Moses, Aaron and Hur went to the top of the hill.

column.name: text
column.value: As long as Moses held up his hands, the Israelites were winning, but whenever he lowered his hands, the Amalekites were winning.

column.name: text
column.value: When Moses' hands grew tired, they took a stone and put it under him and he sat on it. Aaron and Hur held his hands up--one on one side, one on the other--so that his hands remained steady till sunset.

column.name: text
column.value: So Joshua overcame the Amalekite army with the sword.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD said to Moses, "Write this on a scroll as something to be remembered and make sure that Joshua hears it, because I will completely blot out the memory of Amalek from under heaven."

column.name: text
column.value: Moses built an altar and called it The LORD is my Banner.

column.name: text
column.value: He said, "For hands were lifted up to the throne of the LORD. The LORD will be at war against the Amalekites from generation to generation."

column.name: text
column.value: Now Jethro, the priest of Midian and father-in-law of Moses, heard of everything God had done for Moses and for his people Israel, and how the LORD had brought Israel out of Egypt.

column.name: text
column.value: After Moses had sent away his wife Zipporah, his father-in-law Jethro received her

column.name: text
column.value: and her two sons. One son was named Gershom, for Moses said, "I have become an alien in a foreign land";

column.name: text
column.value: and the other was named Eliezer, for he said, "My father's God was my helper; he saved me from the sword of Pharaoh."

column.name: text
column.value: Jethro, Moses' father-in-law, together with Moses' sons and wife, came to him in the desert, where he was camped near the mountain of God.

column.name: text
column.value: Jethro had sent word to him, "I, your father-in-law Jethro, am coming to you with your wife and her two sons."

column.name: text
column.value: So Moses went out to meet his father-in-law and bowed down and kissed him. They greeted each other and then went into the tent.

column.name: text
column.value: Moses told his father-in-law about everything the LORD had done to Pharaoh and the Egyptians for Israel's sake and about all the hardships they had met along the way and how the LORD had saved them.

column.name: text
column.value: Jethro was delighted to hear about all the good things the LORD had done for Israel in rescuing them from the hand of the Egyptians.

column.name: text
column.value: He said, "Praise be to the LORD, who rescued you from the hand of the Egyptians and of Pharaoh, and who rescued the people from the hand of the Egyptians.

column.name: text
column.value: Now I know that the LORD is greater than all other gods, for he did this to those who had treated Israel arrogantly."

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jethro, Moses' father-in-law, brought a burnt offering and other sacrifices to God, and Aaron came with all the elders of Israel to eat bread with Moses' father-in-law in the presence of God.

column.name: text
column.value: The next day Moses took his seat to serve as judge for the people, and they stood around him from morning till evening.

column.name: text
column.value: When his father-in-law saw all that Moses was doing for the people, he said, "What is this you are doing for the people? Why do you alone sit as judge, while all these people stand around you from morning till evening?"

column.name: text
column.value: Moses answered him, "Because the people come to me to seek God's will.

column.name: text
column.value: Whenever they have a dispute, it is brought to me, and I decide between the parties and inform them of God's decrees and laws."

column.name: text
column.value: Moses' father-in-law replied, "What you are doing is not good.

column.name: text
column.value: You and these people who come to you will only wear yourselves out. The work is too heavy for you; you cannot handle it alone.

column.name: text
column.value: Listen now to me and I will give you some advice, and may God be with you. You must be the people's representative before God and bring their disputes to him.

column.name: text
column.value: Teach them the decrees and laws, and show them the way to live and the duties they are to perform.

column.name: text
column.value: But select capable men from all the people--men who fear God, trustworthy men who hate dishonest gain--and appoint them as officials over thousands, hundreds, fifties and tens.

column.name: text
column.value: Have them serve as judges for the people at all times, but have them bring every difficult case to you; the simple cases they can decide themselves. That will make your load lighter, because they will share it with you.

column.name: text
column.value: If you do this and God so commands, you will be able to stand the strain, and all these people will go home satisfied."

column.name: text
column.value: Moses listened to his father-in-law and did everything he said.

column.name: text
column.value: He chose capable men from all Israel and made them leaders of the people, officials over thousands, hundreds, fifties and tens.

column.name: text
column.value: They served as judges for the people at all times. The difficult cases they brought to Moses, but the simple ones they decided themselves.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Moses sent his father-in-law on his way, and Jethro returned to his own country.

column.name: text
column.value: In the third month after the Israelites left Egypt--on the very day--they came to the Desert of Sinai.

column.name: text
column.value: After they set out from Rephidim, they entered the Desert of Sinai, and Israel camped there in the desert in front of the mountain.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Moses went up to God, and the LORD called to him from the mountain and said, "This is what you are to say to the house of Jacob and what you are to tell the people of Israel:

column.name: text
column.value: 'You yourselves have seen what I did to Egypt, and how I carried you on eagles' wings and brought you to myself.

column.name: text
column.value: Now if you obey me fully and keep my covenant, then out of all nations you will be my treasured possession. Although the whole earth is mine,

column.name: text
column.value: you will be for me a kingdom of priests and a holy nation.' These are the words you are to speak to the Israelites."

column.name: text
column.value: So Moses went back and summoned the elders of the people and set before them all the words the LORD had commanded him to speak.

column.name: text
column.value: The people all responded together, "We will do everything the LORD has said." So Moses brought their answer back to the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD said to Moses, "I am going to come to you in a dense cloud, so that the people will hear me speaking with you and will always put their trust in you." Then Moses told the LORD what the people had said.

column.name: text
column.value: And the LORD said to Moses, "Go to the people and consecrate them today and tomorrow. Have them wash their clothes

column.name: text
column.value: and be ready by the third day, because on that day the LORD will come down on Mount Sinai in the sight of all the people.

column.name: text
column.value: Put limits for the people around the mountain and tell them, 'Be careful that you do not go up the mountain or touch the foot of it. Whoever touches the mountain shall surely be put to death.

column.name: text
column.value: He shall surely be stoned or shot with arrows; not a hand is to be laid on him. Whether man or animal, he shall not be permitted to live.' Only when the ram's horn sounds a long blast may they go up to the mountain."

column.name: text
column.value: After Moses had gone down the mountain to the people, he consecrated them, and they washed their clothes.

column.name: text
column.value: Then he said to the people, "Prepare yourselves for the third day. Abstain from sexual relations."

column.name: text
column.value: On the morning of the third day there was thunder and lightning, with a thick cloud over the mountain, and a very loud trumpet blast. Everyone in the camp trembled.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Moses led the people out of the camp to meet with God, and they stood at the foot of the mountain.

column.name: text
column.value: Mount Sinai was covered with smoke, because the LORD descended on it in fire. The smoke billowed up from it like smoke from a furnace, the whole mountain trembled violently,

column.name: text
column.value: and the sound of the trumpet grew louder and louder. Then Moses spoke and the voice of God answered him.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD descended to the top of Mount Sinai and called Moses to the top of the mountain. So Moses went up

column.name: text
column.value: and the LORD said to him, "Go down and warn the people so they do not force their way through to see the LORD and many of them perish.

column.name: text
column.value: Even the priests, who approach the LORD, must consecrate themselves, or the LORD will break out against them."

column.name: text
column.value: Moses said to the LORD, "The people cannot come up Mount Sinai, because you yourself warned us, 'Put limits around the mountain and set it apart as holy.'"

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD replied, "Go down and bring Aaron up with you. But the priests and the people must not force their way through to come up to the LORD, or he will break out against them."

column.name: text
column.value: So Moses went down to the people and told them.

column.name: text
column.value: And God spoke all these words:

column.name: text
column.value: "I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of Egypt, out of the land of slavery.

column.name: text
column.value: "You shall have no other gods before me.

column.name: text
column.value: "You shall not make for yourself an idol in the form of anything in heaven above or on the earth beneath or in the waters below.

column.name: text
column.value: You shall not bow down to them or worship them; for I, the LORD your God, am a jealous God, punishing the children for the sin of the fathers to the third and fourth generation of those who hate me,

column.name: text
column.value: but showing love to a thousand generations of those who love me and keep my commandments.

column.name: text
column.value: "You shall not misuse the name of the LORD your God, for the LORD will not hold anyone guiltless who misuses his name.

column.name: text
column.value: "Remember the Sabbath day by keeping it holy.

column.name: text
column.value: Six days you shall labor and do all your work,

column.name: text
column.value: but the seventh day is a Sabbath to the LORD your God. On it you shall not do any work, neither you, nor your son or daughter, nor your manservant or maidservant, nor your animals, nor the alien within your gates.

column.name: text
column.value: For in six days the LORD made the heavens and the earth, the sea, and all that is in them, but he rested on the seventh day. Therefore the LORD blessed the Sabbath day and made it holy.

column.name: text
