column.value: The fruit of your womb will be blessed, and the crops of your land and the young of your livestock--the calves of your herds and the lambs of your flocks.

column.name: text
column.value: Your basket and your kneading trough will be blessed.

column.name: text
column.value: You will be blessed when you come in and blessed when you go out.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD will grant that the enemies who rise up against you will be defeated before you. They will come at you from one direction but flee from you in seven.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD will send a blessing on your barns and on everything you put your hand to. The LORD your God will bless you in the land he is giving you.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD will establish you as his holy people, as he promised you on oath, if you keep the commands of the LORD your God and walk in his ways.

column.name: text
column.value: Then all the peoples on earth will see that you are called by the name of the LORD, and they will fear you.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD will grant you abundant prosperity--in the fruit of your womb, the young of your livestock and the crops of your ground--in the land he swore to your forefathers to give you.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD will open the heavens, the storehouse of his bounty, to send rain on your land in season and to bless all the work of your hands. You will lend to many nations but will borrow from none.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD will make you the head, not the tail. If you pay attention to the commands of the LORD your God that I give you this day and carefully follow them, you will always be at the top, never at the bottom.

column.name: text
column.value: Do not turn aside from any of the commands I give you today, to the right or to the left, following other gods and serving them.

column.name: text
column.value: However, if you do not obey the LORD your God and do not carefully follow all his commands and decrees I am giving you today, all these curses will come upon you and overtake you:

column.name: text
column.value: You will be cursed in the city and cursed in the country.

column.name: text
column.value: Your basket and your kneading trough will be cursed.

column.name: text
column.value: The fruit of your womb will be cursed, and the crops of your land, and the calves of your herds and the lambs of your flocks.

column.name: text
column.value: You will be cursed when you come in and cursed when you go out.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD will send on you curses, confusion and rebuke in everything you put your hand to, until you are destroyed and come to sudden ruin because of the evil you have done in forsaking him.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD will plague you with diseases until he has destroyed you from the land you are entering to possess.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD will strike you with wasting disease, with fever and inflammation, with scorching heat and drought, with blight and mildew, which will plague you until you perish.

column.name: text
column.value: The sky over your head will be bronze, the ground beneath you iron.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD will turn the rain of your country into dust and powder; it will come down from the skies until you are destroyed.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD will cause you to be defeated before your enemies. You will come at them from one direction but flee from them in seven, and you will become a thing of horror to all the kingdoms on earth.

column.name: text
column.value: Your carcasses will be food for all the birds of the air and the beasts of the earth, and there will be no one to frighten them away.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD will afflict you with the boils of Egypt and with tumors, festering sores and the itch, from which you cannot be cured.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD will afflict you with madness, blindness and confusion of mind.

column.name: text
column.value: At midday you will grope about like a blind man in the dark. You will be unsuccessful in everything you do; day after day you will be oppressed and robbed, with no one to rescue you.

column.name: text
column.value: You will be pledged to be married to a woman, but another will take her and ravish her. You will build a house, but you will not live in it. You will plant a vineyard, but you will not even begin to enjoy its fruit.

column.name: text
column.value: Your ox will be slaughtered before your eyes, but you will eat none of it. Your donkey will be forcibly taken from you and will not be returned. Your sheep will be given to your enemies, and no one will rescue them.

column.name: text
column.value: Your sons and daughters will be given to another nation, and you will wear out your eyes watching for them day after day, powerless to lift a hand.

column.name: text
column.value: A people that you do not know will eat what your land and labor produce, and you will have nothing but cruel oppression all your days.

column.name: text
column.value: The sights you see will drive you mad.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD will afflict your knees and legs with painful boils that cannot be cured, spreading from the soles of your feet to the top of your head.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD will drive you and the king you set over you to a nation unknown to you or your fathers. There you will worship other gods, gods of wood and stone.

column.name: text
column.value: You will become a thing of horror and an object of scorn and ridicule to all the nations where the LORD will drive you.

column.name: text
column.value: You will sow much seed in the field but you will harvest little, because locusts will devour it.

column.name: text
column.value: You will plant vineyards and cultivate them but you will not drink the wine or gather the grapes, because worms will eat them.

column.name: text
column.value: You will have olive trees throughout your country but you will not use the oil, because the olives will drop off.

column.name: text
column.value: You will have sons and daughters but you will not keep them, because they will go into captivity.

column.name: text
column.value: Swarms of locusts will take over all your trees and the crops of your land.

column.name: text
column.value: The alien who lives among you will rise above you higher and higher, but you will sink lower and lower.

column.name: text
column.value: He will lend to you, but you will not lend to him. He will be the head, but you will be the tail.

column.name: text
column.value: All these curses will come upon you. They will pursue you and overtake you until you are destroyed, because you did not obey the LORD your God and observe the commands and decrees he gave you.

column.name: text
column.value: They will be a sign and a wonder to you and your descendants forever.

column.name: text
column.value: Because you did not serve the LORD your God joyfully and gladly in the time of prosperity,

column.name: text
column.value: therefore in hunger and thirst, in nakedness and dire poverty, you will serve the enemies the LORD sends against you. He will put an iron yoke on your neck until he has destroyed you.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD will bring a nation against you from far away, from the ends of the earth, like an eagle swooping down, a nation whose language you will not understand,

column.name: text
column.value: a fierce-looking nation without respect for the old or pity for the young.

column.name: text
column.value: They will devour the young of your livestock and the crops of your land until you are destroyed. They will leave you no grain, new wine or oil, nor any calves of your herds or lambs of your flocks until you are ruined.

column.name: text
column.value: They will lay siege to all the cities throughout your land until the high fortified walls in which you trust fall down. They will besiege all the cities throughout the land the LORD your God is giving you.

column.name: text
column.value: Because of the suffering that your enemy will inflict on you during the siege, you will eat the fruit of the womb, the flesh of the sons and daughters the LORD your God has given you.

column.name: text
column.value: Even the most gentle and sensitive man among you will have no compassion on his own brother or the wife he loves or his surviving children,

column.name: text
column.value: and he will not give to one of them any of the flesh of his children that he is eating. It will be all he has left because of the suffering your enemy will inflict on you during the siege of all your cities.

column.name: text
column.value: The most gentle and sensitive woman among you--so sensitive and gentle that she would not venture to touch the ground with the sole of her foot--will begrudge the husband she loves and her own son or daughter

column.name: text
column.value: the afterbirth from her womb and the children she bears. For she intends to eat them secretly during the siege and in the distress that your enemy will inflict on you in your cities.

column.name: text
column.value: If you do not carefully follow all the words of this law, which are written in this book, and do not revere this glorious and awesome name--the LORD your God--

column.name: text
column.value: the LORD will send fearful plagues on you and your descendants, harsh and prolonged disasters, and severe and lingering illnesses.

column.name: text
column.value: He will bring upon you all the diseases of Egypt that you dreaded, and they will cling to you.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD will also bring on you every kind of sickness and disaster not recorded in this Book of the Law, until you are destroyed.

column.name: text
column.value: You who were as numerous as the stars in the sky will be left but few in number, because you did not obey the LORD your God.

column.name: text
column.value: Just as it pleased the LORD to make you prosper and increase in number, so it will please him to ruin and destroy you. You will be uprooted from the land you are entering to possess.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD will scatter you among all nations, from one end of the earth to the other. There you will worship other gods--gods of wood and stone, which neither you nor your fathers have known.

column.name: text
column.value: Among those nations you will find no repose, no resting place for the sole of your foot. There the LORD will give you an anxious mind, eyes weary with longing, and a despairing heart.

column.name: text
column.value: You will live in constant suspense, filled with dread both night and day, never sure of your life.

column.name: text
column.value: In the morning you will say, "If only it were evening!" and in the evening, "If only it were morning!"--because of the terror that will fill your hearts and the sights that your eyes will see.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD will send you back in ships to Egypt on a journey I said you should never make again. There you will offer yourselves for sale to your enemies as male and female slaves, but no one will buy you.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Moses climbed Mount Nebo from the plains of Moab to the top of Pisgah, across from Jericho. There the LORD showed him the whole land--from Gilead to Dan,

column.name: text
column.value: all of Naphtali, the territory of Ephraim and Manasseh, all the land of Judah as far as the western sea,

column.name: text
column.value: the Negev and the whole region from the Valley of Jericho, the City of Palms, as far as Zoar.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD said to him, "This is the land I promised on oath to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob when I said, 'I will give it to your descendants.' I have let you see it with your eyes, but you will not cross over into it."

column.name: text
column.value: And Moses the servant of the LORD died there in Moab, as the LORD had said.

column.name: text
column.value: He buried him in Moab, in the valley opposite Beth Peor, but to this day no one knows where his grave is.

column.name: text
column.value: Moses was a hundred and twenty years old when he died, yet his eyes were not weak nor his strength gone.

column.name: text
column.value: The Israelites grieved for Moses in the plains of Moab thirty days, until the time of weeping and mourning was over.

column.name: text
column.value: Now Joshua son of Nun was filled with the spirit of wisdom because Moses had laid his hands on him. So the Israelites listened to him and did what the LORD had commanded Moses.

column.name: text
column.value: Since then, no prophet has risen in Israel like Moses, whom the LORD knew face to face,

column.name: text
column.value: who did all those miraculous signs and wonders the LORD sent him to do in Egypt--to Pharaoh and to all his officials and to his whole land.

column.name: text
column.value: For no one has ever shown the mighty power or performed the awesome deeds that Moses did in the sight of all Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: This is the blessing that Moses the man of God pronounced on the Israelites before his death.

column.name: text
column.value: He said: "The LORD came from Sinai and dawned over them from Seir; he shone forth from Mount Paran. He came with myriads of holy ones from the south, from his mountain slopes.

column.name: text
column.value: Surely it is you who love the people; all the holy ones are in your hand. At your feet they all bow down, and from you receive instruction,

column.name: text
column.value: the law that Moses gave us, the possession of the assembly of Jacob.

column.name: text
column.value: He was king over Jeshurun when the leaders of the people assembled, along with the tribes of Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: "Let Reuben live and not die, nor his men be few."

column.name: text
column.value: And this he said about Judah: "Hear, O LORD, the cry of Judah; bring him to his people. With his own hands he defends his cause. Oh, be his help against his foes!"

column.name: text
column.value: About Levi he said: "Your Thummim and Urim belong to the man you favored. You tested him at Massah; you contended with him at the waters of Meribah.

column.name: text
column.value: He said of his father and mother, 'I have no regard for them.' He did not recognize his brothers or acknowledge his own children, but he watched over your word and guarded your covenant.

column.name: text
column.value: He teaches your precepts to Jacob and your law to Israel. He offers incense before you and whole burnt offerings on your altar.

column.name: text
column.value: Bless all his skills, O LORD, and be pleased with the work of his hands. Smite the loins of those who rise up against him; strike his foes till they rise no more."

column.name: text
column.value: About Benjamin he said: "Let the beloved of the LORD rest secure in him, for he shields him all day long, and the one the LORD loves rests between his shoulders."

column.name: text
column.value: About Joseph he said: "May the LORD bless his land with the precious dew from heaven above and with the deep waters that lie below;

column.name: text
column.value: with the best the sun brings forth and the finest the moon can yield;

column.name: text
column.value: with the choicest gifts of the ancient mountains and the fruitfulness of the everlasting hills;

column.name: text
column.value: with the best gifts of the earth and its fullness and the favor of him who dwelt in the burning bush. Let all these rest on the head of Joseph, on the brow of the prince among his brothers.

column.name: text
column.value: In majesty he is like a firstborn bull; his horns are the horns of a wild ox. With them he will gore the nations, even those at the ends of the earth. Such are the ten thousands of Ephraim; such are the thousands of Manasseh."

column.name: text
column.value: About Zebulun he said: "Rejoice, Zebulun, in your going out, and you, Issachar, in your tents.

column.name: text
column.value: They will summon peoples to the mountain and there offer sacrifices of righteousness; they will feast on the abundance of the seas, on the treasures hidden in the sand."

column.name: text
column.value: About Gad he said: "Blessed is he who enlarges Gad's domain! Gad lives there like a lion, tearing at arm or head.

column.name: text
column.value: He chose the best land for himself; the leader's portion was kept for him. When the heads of the people assembled, he carried out the LORD'S righteous will, and his judgments concerning Israel."

column.name: text
column.value: About Dan he said: "Dan is a lion's cub, springing out of Bashan."

column.name: text
column.value: About Naphtali he said: "Naphtali is abounding with the favor of the LORD and is full of his blessing; he will inherit southward to the lake."

column.name: text
column.value: About Asher he said: "Most blessed of sons is Asher; let him be favored by his brothers, and let him bathe his feet in oil.

column.name: text
column.value: The bolts of your gates will be iron and bronze, and your strength will equal your days.

column.name: text
column.value: "There is no one like the God of Jeshurun, who rides on the heavens to help you and on the clouds in his majesty.

column.name: text
column.value: The eternal God is your refuge, and underneath are the everlasting arms. He will drive out your enemy before you, saying, 'Destroy him!'

column.name: text
column.value: So Israel will live in safety alone; Jacob's spring is secure in a land of grain and new wine, where the heavens drop dew.

column.name: text
column.value: Blessed are you, O Israel! Who is like you, a people saved by the LORD? He is your shield and helper and your glorious sword. Your enemies will cower before you, and you will trample down their high places."

column.name: text
column.value: Then Moses went out and spoke these words to all Israel:

column.name: text
column.value: "I am now a hundred and twenty years old and I am no longer able to lead you. The LORD has said to me, 'You shall not cross the Jordan.'

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD your God himself will cross over ahead of you. He will destroy these nations before you, and you will take possession of their land. Joshua also will cross over ahead of you, as the LORD said.

column.name: text
column.value: And the LORD will do to them what he did to Sihon and Og, the kings of the Amorites, whom he destroyed along with their land.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD will deliver them to you, and you must do to them all that I have commanded you.

column.name: text
column.value: Be strong and courageous. Do not be afraid or terrified because of them, for the LORD your God goes with you; he will never leave you nor forsake you."

column.name: text
column.value: Then Moses summoned Joshua and said to him in the presence of all Israel, "Be strong and courageous, for you must go with this people into the land that the LORD swore to their forefathers to give them, and you must divide it among them as their inheritance.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD himself goes before you and will be with you; he will never leave you nor forsake you. Do not be afraid; do not be discouraged."

column.name: text
column.value: So Moses wrote down this law and gave it to the priests, the sons of Levi, who carried the ark of the covenant of the LORD, and to all the elders of Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Moses commanded them: "At the end of every seven years, in the year for canceling debts, during the Feast of Tabernacles,

column.name: text
column.value: when all Israel comes to appear before the LORD your God at the place he will choose, you shall read this law before them in their hearing.

column.name: text
column.value: Assemble the people--men, women and children, and the aliens living in your towns--so they can listen and learn to fear the LORD your God and follow carefully all the words of this law.

column.name: text
column.value: Their children, who do not know this law, must hear it and learn to fear the LORD your God as long as you live in the land you are crossing the Jordan to possess."

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD said to Moses, "Now the day of your death is near. Call Joshua and present yourselves at the Tent of Meeting, where I will commission him." So Moses and Joshua came and presented themselves at the Tent of Meeting.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD appeared at the Tent in a pillar of cloud, and the cloud stood over the entrance to the Tent.

column.name: text
column.value: And the LORD said to Moses: "You are going to rest with your fathers, and these people will soon prostitute themselves to the foreign gods of the land they are entering. They will forsake me and break the covenant I made with them.

column.name: text
column.value: On that day I will become angry with them and forsake them; I will hide my face from them, and they will be destroyed. Many disasters and difficulties will come upon them, and on that day they will ask, 'Have not these disasters come upon us because our God is not with us?'

column.name: text
column.value: And I will certainly hide my face on that day because of all their wickedness in turning to other gods.

column.name: text
column.value: "Now write down for yourselves this song and teach it to the Israelites and have them sing it, so that it may be a witness for me against them.

column.name: text
column.value: When I have brought them into the land flowing with milk and honey, the land I promised on oath to their forefathers, and when they eat their fill and thrive, they will turn to other gods and worship them, rejecting me and breaking my covenant.

column.name: text
column.value: And when many disasters and difficulties come upon them, this song will testify against them, because it will not be forgotten by their descendants. I know what they are disposed to do, even before I bring them into the land I promised them on oath."

column.name: text
column.value: So Moses wrote down this song that day and taught it to the Israelites.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD gave this command to Joshua son of Nun: "Be strong and courageous, for you will bring the Israelites into the land I promised them on oath, and I myself will be with you."

column.name: text
column.value: After Moses finished writing in a book the words of this law from beginning to end,

column.name: text
column.value: he gave this command to the Levites who carried the ark of the covenant of the LORD:

column.name: text
column.value: "Take this Book of the Law and place it beside the ark of the covenant of the LORD your God. There it will remain as a witness against you.

column.name: text
column.value: For I know how rebellious and stiff-necked you are. If you have been rebellious against the LORD while I am still alive and with you, how much more will you rebel after I die!

column.name: text
column.value: Assemble before me all the elders of your tribes and all your officials, so that I can speak these words in their hearing and call heaven and earth to testify against them.

column.name: text
column.value: For I know that after my death you are sure to become utterly corrupt and to turn from the way I have commanded you. In days to come, disaster will fall upon you because you will do evil in the sight of the LORD and provoke him to anger by what your hands have made."

column.name: text
column.value: And Moses recited the words of this song from beginning to end in the hearing of the whole assembly of Israel:

column.name: text
column.value: Listen, O heavens, and I will speak; hear, O earth, the words of my mouth.

column.name: text
column.value: Let my teaching fall like rain and my words descend like dew, like showers on new grass, like abundant rain on tender plants.

column.name: text
column.value: I will proclaim the name of the LORD. Oh, praise the greatness of our God!

column.name: text
column.value: He is the Rock, his works are perfect, and all his ways are just. A faithful God who does no wrong, upright and just is he.

column.name: text
column.value: They have acted corruptly toward him; to their shame they are no longer his children, but a warped and crooked generation.

column.name: text
column.value: Is this the way you repay the LORD, O foolish and unwise people? Is he not your Father, your Creator, who made you and formed you?

column.name: text
column.value: Remember the days of old; consider the generations long past. Ask your father and he will tell you, your elders, and they will explain to you.

column.name: text
column.value: When the Most High gave the nations their inheritance, when he divided all mankind, he set up boundaries for the peoples according to the number of the sons of Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: For the LORD'S portion is his people, Jacob his allotted inheritance.

column.name: text
column.value: In a desert land he found him, in a barren and howling waste. He shielded him and cared for him; he guarded him as the apple of his eye,

column.name: text
column.value: like an eagle that stirs up its nest and hovers over its young, that spreads its wings to catch them and carries them on its pinions.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD alone led him; no foreign god was with him.

column.name: text
column.value: He made him ride on the heights of the land and fed him with the fruit of the fields. He nourished him with honey from the rock, and with oil from the flinty crag,

column.name: text
column.value: with curds and milk from herd and flock and with fattened lambs and goats, with choice rams of Bashan and the finest kernels of wheat. You drank the foaming blood of the grape.

column.name: text
column.value: Jeshurun grew fat and kicked; filled with food, he became heavy and sleek. He abandoned the God who made him and rejected the Rock his Savior.

column.name: text
column.value: They made him jealous with their foreign gods and angered him with their detestable idols.

column.name: text
column.value: They sacrificed to demons, which are not God--gods they had not known, gods that recently appeared, gods your fathers did not fear.

column.name: text
column.value: You deserted the Rock, who fathered you; you forgot the God who gave you birth.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD saw this and rejected them because he was angered by his sons and daughters.

column.name: text
column.value: "I will hide my face from them," he said, "and see what their end will be; for they are a perverse generation, children who are unfaithful.

column.name: text
column.value: They made me jealous by what is no god and angered me with their worthless idols. I will make them envious by those who are not a people; I will make them angry by a nation that has no understanding.

column.name: text
column.value: For a fire has been kindled by my wrath, one that burns to the realm of death below. It will devour the earth and its harvests and set afire the foundations of the mountains.

column.name: text
column.value: "I will heap calamities upon them and spend my arrows against them.

column.name: text
column.value: I will send wasting famine against them, consuming pestilence and deadly plague; I will send against them the fangs of wild beasts, the venom of vipers that glide in the dust.

column.name: text
column.value: In the street the sword will make them childless; in their homes terror will reign. Young men and young women will perish, infants and gray-haired men.

column.name: text
column.value: I said I would scatter them and blot out their memory from mankind,

column.name: text
column.value: but I dreaded the taunt of the enemy, lest the adversary misunderstand and say, 'Our hand has triumphed; the LORD has not done all this.'"

column.name: text
column.value: They are a nation without sense, there is no discernment in them.

column.name: text
column.value: If only they were wise and would understand this and discern what their end will be!

column.name: text
column.value: How could one man chase a thousand, or two put ten thousand to flight, unless their Rock had sold them, unless the LORD had given them up?

column.name: text
column.value: For their rock is not like our Rock, as even our enemies concede.

column.name: text
column.value: Their vine comes from the vine of Sodom and from the fields of Gomorrah. Their grapes are filled with poison, and their clusters with bitterness.

column.name: text
column.value: Their wine is the venom of serpents, the deadly poison of cobras.

column.name: text
column.value: "Have I not kept this in reserve and sealed it in my vaults?

column.name: text
column.value: It is mine to avenge; I will repay. In due time their foot will slip; their day of disaster is near and their doom rushes upon them."

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD will judge his people and have compassion on his servants when he sees their strength is gone and no one is left, slave or free.

column.name: text
column.value: He will say: "Now where are their gods, the rock they took refuge in,

column.name: text
column.value: the gods who ate the fat of their sacrifices and drank the wine of their drink offerings? Let them rise up to help you! Let them give you shelter!

column.name: text
column.value: "See now that I myself am He! There is no god besides me. I put to death and I bring to life, I have wounded and I will heal, and no one can deliver out of my hand.

column.name: text
column.value: I lift my hand to heaven and declare: As surely as I live forever,

column.name: text
column.value: when I sharpen my flashing sword and my hand grasps it in judgment, I will take vengeance on my adversaries and repay those who hate me.

column.name: text
column.value: I will make my arrows drunk with blood, while my sword devours flesh: the blood of the slain and the captives, the heads of the enemy leaders."

column.name: text
column.value: Rejoice, O nations, with his people, for he will avenge the blood of his servants; he will take vengeance on his enemies and make atonement for his land and people.

column.name: text
column.value: Moses came with Joshua son of Nun and spoke all the words of this song in the hearing of the people.

column.name: text
column.value: When Moses finished reciting all these words to all Israel,

column.name: text
column.value: he said to them, "Take to heart all the words I have solemnly declared to you this day, so that you may command your children to obey carefully all the words of this law.

column.name: text
column.value: They are not just idle words for you--they are your life. By them you will live long in the land you are crossing the Jordan to possess."

column.name: text
column.value: On that same day the LORD told Moses,

column.name: text
column.value: "Go up into the Abarim Range to Mount Nebo in Moab, across from Jericho, and view Canaan, the land I am giving the Israelites as their own possession.

column.name: text
column.value: There on the mountain that you have climbed you will die and be gathered to your people, just as your brother Aaron died on Mount Hor and was gathered to his people.

column.name: text
column.value: This is because both of you broke faith with me in the presence of the Israelites at the waters of Meribah Kadesh in the Desert of Zin and because you did not uphold my holiness among the Israelites.

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore, you will see the land only from a distance; you will not enter the land I am giving to the people of Israel."

column.name: text
column.value: After the death of Moses the servant of the LORD, the LORD said to Joshua son of Nun, Moses' aide:

column.name: text
column.value: "Moses my servant is dead. Now then, you and all these people, get ready to cross the Jordan River into the land I am about to give to them--to the Israelites.

column.name: text
column.value: I will give you every place where you set your foot, as I promised Moses.

column.name: text
column.value: Your territory will extend from the desert to Lebanon, and from the great river, the Euphrates--all the Hittite country--to the Great Sea on the west.

column.name: text
column.value: No one will be able to stand up against you all the days of your life. As I was with Moses, so I will be with you; I will never leave you nor forsake you.

column.name: text
column.value: "Be strong and courageous, because you will lead these people to inherit the land I swore to their forefathers to give them.

column.name: text
column.value: Be strong and very courageous. Be careful to obey all the law my servant Moses gave you; do not turn from it to the right or to the left, that you may be successful wherever you go.

column.name: text
column.value: Do not let this Book of the Law depart from your mouth; meditate on it day and night, so that you may be careful to do everything written in it. Then you will be prosperous and successful.

column.name: text
column.value: Have I not commanded you? Be strong and courageous. Do not be terrified; do not be discouraged, for the LORD your God will be with you wherever you go."

column.name: text
column.value: So Joshua ordered the officers of the people:

column.name: text
column.value: "Go through the camp and tell the people, 'Get your supplies ready. Three days from now you will cross the Jordan here to go in and take possession of the land the LORD your God is giving you for your own.'"

column.name: text
column.value: But to the Reubenites, the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh, Joshua said,

column.name: text
column.value: "Remember the command that Moses the servant of the LORD gave you: 'The LORD your God is giving you rest and has granted you this land.'

column.name: text
column.value: Your wives, your children and your livestock may stay in the land that Moses gave you east of the Jordan, but all your fighting men, fully armed, must cross over ahead of your brothers. You are to help your brothers

column.name: text
column.value: until the LORD gives them rest, as he has done for you, and until they too have taken possession of the land that the LORD your God is giving them. After that, you may go back and occupy your own land, which Moses the servant of the LORD gave you east of the Jordan toward the sunrise."

column.name: text
column.value: Then they answered Joshua, "Whatever you have commanded us we will do, and wherever you send us we will go.

column.name: text
column.value: Just as we fully obeyed Moses, so we will obey you. Only may the LORD your God be with you as he was with Moses.

column.name: text
column.value: Whoever rebels against your word and does not obey your words, whatever you may command them, will be put to death. Only be strong and courageous!"

column.name: text
column.value: Then Joshua son of Nun secretly sent two spies from Shittim. "Go, look over the land," he said, "especially Jericho." So they went and entered the house of a prostitute named Rahab and stayed there.

column.name: text
column.value: The king of Jericho was told, "Look! Some of the Israelites have come here tonight to spy out the land."

column.name: text
column.value: So the king of Jericho sent this message to Rahab: "Bring out the men who came to you and entered your house, because they have come to spy out the whole land."

column.name: text
column.value: But the woman had taken the two men and hidden them. She said, "Yes, the men came to me, but I did not know where they had come from.

column.name: text
column.value: At dusk, when it was time to close the city gate, the men left. I don't know which way they went. Go after them quickly. You may catch up with them."

column.name: text
column.value: (But she had taken them up to the roof and hidden them under the stalks of flax she had laid out on the roof.)

column.name: text
column.value: So the men set out in pursuit of the spies on the road that leads to the fords of the Jordan, and as soon as the pursuers had gone out, the gate was shut.

column.name: text
column.value: Before the spies lay down for the night, she went up on the roof

column.name: text
column.value: and said to them, "I know that the LORD has given this land to you and that a great fear of you has fallen on us, so that all who live in this country are melting in fear because of you.

column.name: text
column.value: We have heard how the LORD dried up the water of the Red Sea for you when you came out of Egypt, and what you did to Sihon and Og, the two kings of the Amorites east of the Jordan, whom you completely destroyed.

column.name: text
column.value: When we heard of it, our hearts melted and everyone's courage failed because of you, for the LORD your God is God in heaven above and on the earth below.

column.name: text
column.value: Now then, please swear to me by the LORD that you will show kindness to my family, because I have shown kindness to you. Give me a sure sign

column.name: text
column.value: that you will spare the lives of my father and mother, my brothers and sisters, and all who belong to them, and that you will save us from death."

column.name: text
column.value: "Our lives for your lives!" the men assured her. "If you don't tell what we are doing, we will treat you kindly and faithfully when the LORD gives us the land."

column.name: text
column.value: So she let them down by a rope through the window, for the house she lived in was part of the city wall.

column.name: text
column.value: Now she had said to them, "Go to the hills so the pursuers will not find you. Hide yourselves there three days until they return, and then go on your way."

column.name: text
column.value: The men said to her, "This oath you made us swear will not be binding on us

column.name: text
column.value: unless, when we enter the land, you have tied this scarlet cord in the window through which you let us down, and unless you have brought your father and mother, your brothers and all your family into your house.

column.name: text
column.value: If anyone goes outside your house into the street, his blood will be on his own head; we will not be responsible. As for anyone who is in the house with you, his blood will be on our head if a hand is laid on him.

column.name: text
column.value: But if you tell what we are doing, we will be released from the oath you made us swear."

column.name: text
column.value: "Agreed," she replied. "Let it be as you say." So she sent them away and they departed. And she tied the scarlet cord in the window.

column.name: text
column.value: When they left, they went into the hills and stayed there three days, until the pursuers had searched all along the road and returned without finding them.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the two men started back. They went down out of the hills, forded the river and came to Joshua son of Nun and told him everything that had happened to them.

column.name: text
column.value: They said to Joshua, "The LORD has surely given the whole land into our hands; all the people are melting in fear because of us."

column.name: text
column.value: Early in the morning Joshua and all the Israelites set out from Shittim and went to the Jordan, where they camped before crossing over.

column.name: text
column.value: After three days the officers went throughout the camp,

column.name: text
column.value: giving orders to the people: "When you see the ark of the covenant of the LORD your God, and the priests, who are Levites, carrying it, you are to move out from your positions and follow it.

column.name: text
column.value: Then you will know which way to go, since you have never been this way before. But keep a distance of about a thousand yards between you and the ark; do not go near it."

column.name: text
column.value: Joshua told the people, "Consecrate yourselves, for tomorrow the LORD will do amazing things among you."

column.name: text
column.value: Joshua said to the priests, "Take up the ark of the covenant and pass on ahead of the people." So they took it up and went ahead of them.

column.name: text
column.value: And the LORD said to Joshua, "Today I will begin to exalt you in the eyes of all Israel, so they may know that I am with you as I was with Moses.

column.name: text
column.value: Tell the priests who carry the ark of the covenant: 'When you reach the edge of the Jordan's waters, go and stand in the river.'"

column.name: text
column.value: Joshua said to the Israelites, "Come here and listen to the words of the LORD your God.

column.name: text
column.value: This is how you will know that the living God is among you and that he will certainly drive out before you the Canaanites, Hittites, Hivites, Perizzites, Girgashites, Amorites and Jebusites.

column.name: text
column.value: See, the ark of the covenant of the Lord of all the earth will go into the Jordan ahead of you.

column.name: text
column.value: Now then, choose twelve men from the tribes of Israel, one from each tribe.

column.name: text
column.value: And as soon as the priests who carry the ark of the LORD--the Lord of all the earth--set foot in the Jordan, its waters flowing downstream will be cut off and stand up in a heap."

column.name: text
column.value: So when the people broke camp to cross the Jordan, the priests carrying the ark of the covenant went ahead of them.

column.name: text
column.value: Now the Jordan is at flood stage all during harvest. Yet as soon as the priests who carried the ark reached the Jordan and their feet touched the water's edge,

column.name: text
column.value: the water from upstream stopped flowing. It piled up in a heap a great distance away, at a town called Adam in the vicinity of Zarethan, while the water flowing down to the Sea of the Arabah (the Salt Sea) was completely cut off. So the people crossed over opposite Jericho.

column.name: text
column.value: The priests who carried the ark of the covenant of the LORD stood firm on dry ground in the middle of the Jordan, while all Israel passed by until the whole nation had completed the crossing on dry ground.

column.name: text
column.value: When the whole nation had finished crossing the Jordan, the LORD said to Joshua,

column.name: text
column.value: "Choose twelve men from among the people, one from each tribe,

column.name: text
column.value: and tell them to take up twelve stones from the middle of the Jordan from right where the priests stood and to carry them over with you and put them down at the place where you stay tonight."

column.name: text
column.value: So Joshua called together the twelve men he had appointed from the Israelites, one from each tribe,

column.name: text
column.value: and said to them, "Go over before the ark of the LORD your God into the middle of the Jordan. Each of you is to take up a stone on his shoulder, according to the number of the tribes of the Israelites,

column.name: text
column.value: to serve as a sign among you. In the future, when your children ask you, 'What do these stones mean?'

column.name: text
column.value: tell them that the flow of the Jordan was cut off before the ark of the covenant of the LORD. When it crossed the Jordan, the waters of the Jordan were cut off. These stones are to be a memorial to the people of Israel forever."

column.name: text
column.value: So the Israelites did as Joshua commanded them. They took twelve stones from the middle of the Jordan, according to the number of the tribes of the Israelites, as the LORD had told Joshua; and they carried them over with them to their camp, where they put them down.

column.name: text
column.value: Joshua set up the twelve stones that had been in the middle of the Jordan at the spot where the priests who carried the ark of the covenant had stood. And they are there to this day.

column.name: text
column.value: Now the priests who carried the ark remained standing in the middle of the Jordan until everything the LORD had commanded Joshua was done by the people, just as Moses had directed Joshua. The people hurried over,

column.name: text
column.value: and as soon as all of them had crossed, the ark of the LORD and the priests came to the other side while the people watched.

column.name: text
column.value: The men of Reuben, Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh crossed over, armed, in front of the Israelites, as Moses had directed them.

column.name: text
column.value: About forty thousand armed for battle crossed over before the LORD to the plains of Jericho for war.

column.name: text
column.value: That day the LORD exalted Joshua in the sight of all Israel; and they revered him all the days of his life, just as they had revered Moses.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD said to Joshua,

column.name: text
column.value: "Command the priests carrying the ark of the Testimony to come up out of the Jordan."

column.name: text
column.value: So Joshua commanded the priests, "Come up out of the Jordan."

column.name: text
column.value: And the priests came up out of the river carrying the ark of the covenant of the LORD. No sooner had they set their feet on the dry ground than the waters of the Jordan returned to their place and ran at flood stage as before.

column.name: text
column.value: On the tenth day of the first month the people went up from the Jordan and camped at Gilgal on the eastern border of Jericho.

column.name: text
column.value: And Joshua set up at Gilgal the twelve stones they had taken out of the Jordan.

column.name: text
column.value: He said to the Israelites, "In the future when your descendants ask their fathers, 'What do these stones mean?'

column.name: text
column.value: tell them, 'Israel crossed the Jordan on dry ground.'

column.name: text
column.value: For the LORD your God dried up the Jordan before you until you had crossed over. The LORD your God did to the Jordan just what he had done to the Red Sea when he dried it up before us until we had crossed over.

column.name: text
column.value: He did this so that all the peoples of the earth might know that the hand of the LORD is powerful and so that you might always fear the LORD your God."

column.name: text
column.value: Now when all the Amorite kings west of the Jordan and all the Canaanite kings along the coast heard how the LORD had dried up the Jordan before the Israelites until we had crossed over, their hearts melted and they no longer had the courage to face the Israelites.

column.name: text
column.value: At that time the LORD said to Joshua, "Make flint knives and circumcise the Israelites again."

column.name: text
column.value: So Joshua made flint knives and circumcised the Israelites at Gibeath Haaraloth.

column.name: text
column.value: Now this is why he did so: All those who came out of Egypt--all the men of military age--died in the desert on the way after leaving Egypt.

column.name: text
column.value: All the people that came out had been circumcised, but all the people born in the desert during the journey from Egypt had not.

column.name: text
column.value: The Israelites had moved about in the desert forty years until all the men who were of military age when they left Egypt had died, since they had not obeyed the LORD. For the LORD had sworn to them that they would not see the land that he had solemnly promised their fathers to give us, a land flowing with milk and honey.

column.name: text
column.value: So he raised up their sons in their place, and these were the ones Joshua circumcised. They were still uncircumcised because they had not been circumcised on the way.

column.name: text
column.value: And after the whole nation had been circumcised, they remained where they were in camp until they were healed.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD said to Joshua, "Today I have rolled away the reproach of Egypt from you." So the place has been called Gilgal to this day.

column.name: text
column.value: On the evening of the fourteenth day of the month, while camped at Gilgal on the plains of Jericho, the Israelites celebrated the Passover.

column.name: text
column.value: The day after the Passover, that very day, they ate some of the produce of the land: unleavened bread and roasted grain.

column.name: text
column.value: The manna stopped the day after they ate this food from the land; there was no longer any manna for the Israelites, but that year they ate of the produce of Canaan.

column.name: text
column.value: Now when Joshua was near Jericho, he looked up and saw a man standing in front of him with a drawn sword in his hand. Joshua went up to him and asked, "Are you for us or for our enemies?"

column.name: text
column.value: "Neither," he replied, "but as commander of the army of the LORD I have now come." Then Joshua fell facedown to the ground in reverence, and asked him, "What message does my Lord have for his servant?"

column.name: text
column.value: The commander of the LORD'S army replied, "Take off your sandals, for the place where you are standing is holy." And Joshua did so.

column.name: text
column.value: Now Jericho was tightly shut up because of the Israelites. No one went out and no one came in.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD said to Joshua, "See, I have delivered Jericho into your hands, along with its king and its fighting men.

column.name: text
column.value: March around the city once with all the armed men. Do this for six days.

column.name: text
column.value: Have seven priests carry trumpets of rams' horns in front of the ark. On the seventh day, march around the city seven times, with the priests blowing the trumpets.

column.name: text
column.value: When you hear them sound a long blast on the trumpets, have all the people give a loud shout; then the wall of the city will collapse and the people will go up, every man straight in."

column.name: text
column.value: So Joshua son of Nun called the priests and said to them, "Take up the ark of the covenant of the LORD and have seven priests carry trumpets in front of it."

column.name: text
column.value: And he ordered the people, "Advance! March around the city, with the armed guard going ahead of the ark of the LORD."

column.name: text
column.value: When Joshua had spoken to the people, the seven priests carrying the seven trumpets before the LORD went forward, blowing their trumpets, and the ark of the LORD'S covenant followed them.

column.name: text
column.value: The armed guard marched ahead of the priests who blew the trumpets, and the rear guard followed the ark. All this time the trumpets were sounding.

column.name: text
column.value: But Joshua had commanded the people, "Do not give a war cry, do not raise your voices, do not say a word until the day I tell you to shout. Then shout!"

column.name: text
column.value: So he had the ark of the LORD carried around the city, circling it once. Then the people returned to camp and spent the night there.

column.name: text
column.value: Joshua got up early the next morning and the priests took up the ark of the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: The seven priests carrying the seven trumpets went forward, marching before the ark of the LORD and blowing the trumpets. The armed men went ahead of them and the rear guard followed the ark of the LORD, while the trumpets kept sounding.

column.name: text
column.value: So on the second day they marched around the city once and returned to the camp. They did this for six days.

column.name: text
column.value: On the seventh day, they got up at daybreak and marched around the city seven times in the same manner, except that on that day they circled the city seven times.

column.name: text
column.value: The seventh time around, when the priests sounded the trumpet blast, Joshua commanded the people, "Shout! For the LORD has given you the city!

column.name: text
column.value: The city and all that is in it are to be devoted to the LORD. Only Rahab the prostitute and all who are with her in her house shall be spared, because she hid the spies we sent.

column.name: text
column.value: But keep away from the devoted things, so that you will not bring about your own destruction by taking any of them. Otherwise you will make the camp of Israel liable to destruction and bring trouble on it.

column.name: text
column.value: All the silver and gold and the articles of bronze and iron are sacred to the LORD and must go into his treasury."

column.name: text
column.value: When the trumpets sounded, the people shouted, and at the sound of the trumpet, when the people gave a loud shout, the wall collapsed; so every man charged straight in, and they took the city.

column.name: text
column.value: They devoted the city to the LORD and destroyed with the sword every living thing in it--men and women, young and old, cattle, sheep and donkeys.

column.name: text
column.value: Joshua said to the two men who had spied out the land, "Go into the prostitute's house and bring her out and all who belong to her, in accordance with your oath to her."

column.name: text
column.value: So the young men who had done the spying went in and brought out Rahab, her father and mother and brothers and all who belonged to her. They brought out her entire family and put them in a place outside the camp of Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: Then they burned the whole city and everything in it, but they put the silver and gold and the articles of bronze and iron into the treasury of the LORD'S house.

column.name: text
column.value: But Joshua spared Rahab the prostitute, with her family and all who belonged to her, because she hid the men Joshua had sent as spies to Jericho--and she lives among the Israelites to this day.

column.name: text
column.value: At that time Joshua pronounced this solemn oath: "Cursed before the LORD is the man who undertakes to rebuild this city, Jericho: "At the cost of his firstborn son will he lay its foundations; at the cost of his youngest will he set up its gates."

column.name: text
column.value: So the LORD was with Joshua, and his fame spread throughout the land.

column.name: text
column.value: But the Israelites acted unfaithfully in regard to the devoted things; Achan son of Carmi, the son of Zimri, the son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah, took some of them. So the LORD'S anger burned against Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: Now Joshua sent men from Jericho to Ai, which is near Beth Aven to the east of Bethel, and told them, "Go up and spy out the region." So the men went up and spied out Ai.

column.name: text
column.value: When they returned to Joshua, they said, "Not all the people will have to go up against Ai. Send two or three thousand men to take it and do not weary all the people, for only a few men are there."

column.name: text
column.value: So about three thousand men went up; but they were routed by the men of Ai,

column.name: text
column.value: who killed about thirty-six of them. They chased the Israelites from the city gate as far as the stone quarries and struck them down on the slopes. At this the hearts of the people melted and became like water.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Joshua tore his clothes and fell facedown to the ground before the ark of the LORD, remaining there till evening. The elders of Israel did the same, and sprinkled dust on their heads.

column.name: text
column.value: And Joshua said, "Ah, Sovereign LORD, why did you ever bring this people across the Jordan to deliver us into the hands of the Amorites to destroy us? If only we had been content to stay on the other side of the Jordan!

column.name: text
column.value: O Lord, what can I say, now that Israel has been routed by its enemies?

column.name: text
column.value: The Canaanites and the other people of the country will hear about this and they will surround us and wipe out our name from the earth. What then will you do for your own great name?"

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD said to Joshua, "Stand up! What are you doing down on your face?

column.name: text
column.value: Israel has sinned; they have violated my covenant, which I commanded them to keep. They have taken some of the devoted things; they have stolen, they have lied, they have put them with their own possessions.

column.name: text
column.value: That is why the Israelites cannot stand against their enemies; they turn their backs and run because they have been made liable to destruction. I will not be with you anymore unless you destroy whatever among you is devoted to destruction.

column.name: text
column.value: "Go, consecrate the people. Tell them, 'Consecrate yourselves in preparation for tomorrow; for this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: That which is devoted is among you, O Israel. You cannot stand against your enemies until you remove it.

column.name: text
column.value: "'In the morning, present yourselves tribe by tribe. The tribe that the LORD takes shall come forward clan by clan; the clan that the LORD takes shall come forward family by family; and the family that the LORD takes shall come forward man by man.

column.name: text
column.value: He who is caught with the devoted things shall be destroyed by fire, along with all that belongs to him. He has violated the covenant of the LORD and has done a disgraceful thing in Israel!'"

column.name: text
column.value: Early the next morning Joshua had Israel come forward by tribes, and Judah was taken.

column.name: text
column.value: The clans of Judah came forward, and he took the Zerahites. He had the clan of the Zerahites come forward by families, and Zimri was taken.

column.name: text
column.value: Joshua had his family come forward man by man, and Achan son of Carmi, the son of Zimri, the son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah, was taken.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Joshua said to Achan, "My son, give glory to the LORD, the God of Israel, and give him the praise. Tell me what you have done; do not hide it from me."

column.name: text
column.value: Achan replied, "It is true! I have sinned against the LORD, the God of Israel. This is what I have done:

column.name: text
column.value: When I saw in the plunder a beautiful robe from Babylonia, two hundred shekels of silver and a wedge of gold weighing fifty shekels, I coveted them and took them. They are hidden in the ground inside my tent, with the silver underneath."

column.name: text
column.value: So Joshua sent messengers, and they ran to the tent, and there it was, hidden in his tent, with the silver underneath.

column.name: text
column.value: They took the things from the tent, brought them to Joshua and all the Israelites and spread them out before the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Joshua, together with all Israel, took Achan son of Zerah, the silver, the robe, the gold wedge, his sons and daughters, his cattle, donkeys and sheep, his tent and all that he had, to the Valley of Achor.

column.name: text
column.value: Joshua said, "Why have you brought this trouble on us? The LORD will bring trouble on you today." Then all Israel stoned him, and after they had stoned the rest, they burned them.

column.name: text
column.value: Over Achan they heaped up a large pile of rocks, which remains to this day. Then the LORD turned from his fierce anger. Therefore that place has been called the Valley of Achor ever since.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD said to Joshua, "Do not be afraid; do not be discouraged. Take the whole army with you, and go up and attack Ai. For I have delivered into your hands the king of Ai, his people, his city and his land.

column.name: text
column.value: You shall do to Ai and its king as you did to Jericho and its king, except that you may carry off their plunder and livestock for yourselves. Set an ambush behind the city."

column.name: text
column.value: So Joshua and the whole army moved out to attack Ai. He chose thirty thousand of his best fighting men and sent them out at night

column.name: text
column.value: with these orders: "Listen carefully. You are to set an ambush behind the city. Don't go very far from it. All of you be on the alert.

column.name: text
column.value: I and all those with me will advance on the city, and when the men come out against us, as they did before, we will flee from them.

column.name: text
column.value: They will pursue us until we have lured them away from the city, for they will say, 'They are running away from us as they did before.' So when we flee from them,

column.name: text
column.value: you are to rise up from ambush and take the city. The LORD your God will give it into your hand.

column.name: text
column.value: When you have taken the city, set it on fire. Do what the LORD has commanded. See to it; you have my orders."

column.name: text
column.value: Then Joshua sent them off, and they went to the place of ambush and lay in wait between Bethel and Ai, to the west of Ai--but Joshua spent that night with the people.

column.name: text
column.value: Early the next morning Joshua mustered his men, and he and the leaders of Israel marched before them to Ai.

column.name: text
column.value: The entire force that was with him marched up and approached the city and arrived in front of it. They set up camp north of Ai, with the valley between them and the city.

column.name: text
column.value: Joshua had taken about five thousand men and set them in ambush between Bethel and Ai, to the west of the city.

column.name: text
column.value: They had the soldiers take up their positions--all those in the camp to the north of the city and the ambush to the west of it. That night Joshua went into the valley.

column.name: text
column.value: When the king of Ai saw this, he and all the men of the city hurried out early in the morning to meet Israel in battle at a certain place overlooking the Arabah. But he did not know that an ambush had been set against him behind the city.

column.name: text
column.value: Joshua and all Israel let themselves be driven back before them, and they fled toward the desert.

column.name: text
column.value: All the men of Ai were called to pursue them, and they pursued Joshua and were lured away from the city.

column.name: text
column.value: Not a man remained in Ai or Bethel who did not go after Israel. They left the city open and went in pursuit of Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD said to Joshua, "Hold out toward Ai the javelin that is in your hand, for into your hand I will deliver the city." So Joshua held out his javelin toward Ai.

column.name: text
column.value: As soon as he did this, the men in the ambush rose quickly from their position and rushed forward. They entered the city and captured it and quickly set it on fire.

column.name: text
column.value: The men of Ai looked back and saw the smoke of the city rising against the sky, but they had no chance to escape in any direction, for the Israelites who had been fleeing toward the desert had turned back against their pursuers.

column.name: text
column.value: For when Joshua and all Israel saw that the ambush had taken the city and that smoke was going up from the city, they turned around and attacked the men of Ai.

column.name: text
column.value: The men of the ambush also came out of the city against them, so that they were caught in the middle, with Israelites on both sides. Israel cut them down, leaving them neither survivors nor fugitives.

column.name: text
column.value: But they took the king of Ai alive and brought him to Joshua.

column.name: text
column.value: When Israel had finished killing all the men of Ai in the fields and in the desert where they had chased them, and when every one of them had been put to the sword, all the Israelites returned to Ai and killed those who were in it.

column.name: text
column.value: Twelve thousand men and women fell that day--all the people of Ai.

column.name: text
column.value: For Joshua did not draw back the hand that held out his javelin until he had destroyed all who lived in Ai.

column.name: text
column.value: But Israel did carry off for themselves the livestock and plunder of this city, as the LORD had instructed Joshua.

column.name: text
column.value: So Joshua burned Ai and made it a permanent heap of ruins, a desolate place to this day.

column.name: text
column.value: He hung the king of Ai on a tree and left him there until evening. At sunset, Joshua ordered them to take his body from the tree and throw it down at the entrance of the city gate. And they raised a large pile of rocks over it, which remains to this day.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Joshua built on Mount Ebal an altar to the LORD, the God of Israel,

column.name: text
column.value: as Moses the servant of the LORD had commanded the Israelites. He built it according to what is written in the Book of the Law of Moses--an altar of uncut stones, on which no iron tool had been used. On it they offered to the LORD burnt offerings and sacrificed fellowship offerings.

column.name: text
column.value: There, in the presence of the Israelites, Joshua copied on stones the law of Moses, which he had written.

column.name: text
column.value: All Israel, aliens and citizens alike, with their elders, officials and judges, were standing on both sides of the ark of the covenant of the LORD, facing those who carried it--the priests, who were Levites. Half of the people stood in front of Mount Gerizim and half of them in front of Mount Ebal, as Moses the servant of the LORD had formerly commanded when he gave instructions to bless the people of Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: Afterward, Joshua read all the words of the law--the blessings and the curses--just as it is written in the Book of the Law.

column.name: text
column.value: There was not a word of all that Moses had commanded that Joshua did not read to the whole assembly of Israel, including the women and children, and the aliens who lived among them.

column.name: text
column.value: Now when all the kings west of the Jordan heard about these things--those in the hill country, in the western foothills, and along the entire coast of the Great Sea as far as Lebanon (the kings of the Hittites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites and Jebusites)--

column.name: text
column.value: they came together to make war against Joshua and Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: However, when the people of Gibeon heard what Joshua had done to Jericho and Ai,

column.name: text
column.value: they resorted to a ruse: They went as a delegation whose donkeys were loaded with worn-out sacks and old wineskins, cracked and mended.

column.name: text
column.value: The men put worn and patched sandals on their feet and wore old clothes. All the bread of their food supply was dry and moldy.

column.name: text
column.value: Then they went to Joshua in the camp at Gilgal and said to him and the men of Israel, "We have come from a distant country; make a treaty with us."

column.name: text
column.value: The men of Israel said to the Hivites, "But perhaps you live near us. How then can we make a treaty with you?"

column.name: text
column.value: "We are your servants," they said to Joshua. But Joshua asked, "Who are you and where do you come from?"

column.name: text
column.value: They answered: "Your servants have come from a very distant country because of the fame of the LORD your God. For we have heard reports of him: all that he did in Egypt,

column.name: text
column.value: and all that he did to the two kings of the Amorites east of the Jordan--Sihon king of Heshbon, and Og king of Bashan, who reigned in Ashtaroth.

column.name: text
column.value: And our elders and all those living in our country said to us, 'Take provisions for your journey; go and meet them and say to them, "We are your servants; make a treaty with us." '

column.name: text
column.value: This bread of ours was warm when we packed it at home on the day we left to come to you. But now see how dry and moldy it is.

column.name: text
column.value: And these wineskins that we filled were new, but see how cracked they are. And our clothes and sandals are worn out by the very long journey."

column.name: text
column.value: The men of Israel sampled their provisions but did not inquire of the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Joshua made a treaty of peace with them to let them live, and the leaders of the assembly ratified it by oath.

column.name: text
column.value: Three days after they made the treaty with the Gibeonites, the Israelites heard that they were neighbors, living near them.

column.name: text
column.value: So the Israelites set out and on the third day came to their cities: Gibeon, Kephirah, Beeroth and Kiriath Jearim.

column.name: text
column.value: But the Israelites did not attack them, because the leaders of the assembly had sworn an oath to them by the LORD, the God of Israel. The whole assembly grumbled against the leaders,

column.name: text
column.value: but all the leaders answered, "We have given them our oath by the LORD, the God of Israel, and we cannot touch them now.

column.name: text
column.value: This is what we will do to them: We will let them live, so that wrath will not fall on us for breaking the oath we swore to them."

column.name: text
column.value: They continued, "Let them live, but let them be woodcutters and water carriers for the entire community." So the leaders' promise to them was kept.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Joshua summoned the Gibeonites and said, "Why did you deceive us by saying, 'We live a long way from you,' while actually you live near us?

column.name: text
column.value: You are now under a curse: You will never cease to serve as woodcutters and water carriers for the house of my God."

column.name: text
column.value: They answered Joshua, "Your servants were clearly told how the LORD your God had commanded his servant Moses to give you the whole land and to wipe out all its inhabitants from before you. So we feared for our lives because of you, and that is why we did this.

column.name: text
column.value: We are now in your hands. Do to us whatever seems good and right to you."

column.name: text
column.value: So Joshua saved them from the Israelites, and they did not kill them.

column.name: text
column.value: That day he made the Gibeonites woodcutters and water carriers for the community and for the altar of the LORD at the place the LORD would choose. And that is what they are to this day.

column.name: text
column.value: When Jabin king of Hazor heard of this, he sent word to Jobab king of Madon, to the kings of Shimron and Acshaph,

column.name: text
column.value: and to the northern kings who were in the mountains, in the Arabah south of Kinnereth, in the western foothills and in Naphoth Dor on the west;

column.name: text
column.value: to the Canaanites in the east and west; to the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites and Jebusites in the hill country; and to the Hivites below Hermon in the region of Mizpah.

column.name: text
column.value: They came out with all their troops and a large number of horses and chariots--a huge army, as numerous as the sand on the seashore.

column.name: text
column.value: All these kings joined forces and made camp together at the Waters of Merom, to fight against Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD said to Joshua, "Do not be afraid of them, because by this time tomorrow I will hand all of them over to Israel, slain. You are to hamstring their horses and burn their chariots."

column.name: text
column.value: So Joshua and his whole army came against them suddenly at the Waters of Merom and attacked them,

column.name: text
column.value: and the LORD gave them into the hand of Israel. They defeated them and pursued them all the way to Greater Sidon, to Misrephoth Maim, and to the Valley of Mizpah on the east, until no survivors were left.

column.name: text
column.value: Joshua did to them as the LORD had directed: He hamstrung their horses and burned their chariots.

column.name: text
column.value: At that time Joshua turned back and captured Hazor and put its king to the sword. (Hazor had been the head of all these kingdoms.)

column.name: text
column.value: Everyone in it they put to the sword. They totally destroyed them, not sparing anything that breathed, and he burned up Hazor itself.

column.name: text
column.value: Joshua took all these royal cities and their kings and put them to the sword. He totally destroyed them, as Moses the servant of the LORD had commanded.

column.name: text
column.value: Yet Israel did not burn any of the cities built on their mounds--except Hazor, which Joshua burned.

column.name: text
column.value: The Israelites carried off for themselves all the plunder and livestock of these cities, but all the people they put to the sword until they completely destroyed them, not sparing anyone that breathed.

column.name: text
column.value: As the LORD commanded his servant Moses, so Moses commanded Joshua, and Joshua did it; he left nothing undone of all that the LORD commanded Moses.

column.name: text
column.value: So Joshua took this entire land: the hill country, all the Negev, the whole region of Goshen, the western foothills, the Arabah and the mountains of Israel with their foothills,

column.name: text
column.value: from Mount Halak, which rises toward Seir, to Baal Gad in the Valley of Lebanon below Mount Hermon. He captured all their kings and struck them down, putting them to death.

column.name: text
column.value: Joshua waged war against all these kings for a long time.

column.name: text
column.value: Except for the Hivites living in Gibeon, not one city made a treaty of peace with the Israelites, who took them all in battle.

column.name: text
column.value: For it was the LORD himself who hardened their hearts to wage war against Israel, so that he might destroy them totally, exterminating them without mercy, as the LORD had commanded Moses.

column.name: text
column.value: At that time Joshua went and destroyed the Anakites from the hill country: from Hebron, Debir and Anab, from all the hill country of Judah, and from all the hill country of Israel. Joshua totally destroyed them and their towns.

column.name: text
column.value: No Anakites were left in Israelite territory; only in Gaza, Gath and Ashdod did any survive.

column.name: text
column.value: So Joshua took the entire land, just as the LORD had directed Moses, and he gave it as an inheritance to Israel according to their tribal divisions. Then the land had rest from war.

column.name: text
column.value: Now Adoni-Zedek king of Jerusalem heard that Joshua had taken Ai and totally destroyed it, doing to Ai and its king as he had done to Jericho and its king, and that the people of Gibeon had made a treaty of peace with Israel and were living near them.

column.name: text
column.value: He and his people were very much alarmed at this, because Gibeon was an important city, like one of the royal cities; it was larger than Ai, and all its men were good fighters.

column.name: text
column.value: So Adoni-Zedek king of Jerusalem appealed to Hoham king of Hebron, Piram king of Jarmuth, Japhia king of Lachish and Debir king of Eglon.

column.name: text
column.value: "Come up and help me attack Gibeon," he said, "because it has made peace with Joshua and the Israelites."

column.name: text
column.value: Then the five kings of the Amorites--the kings of Jerusalem, Hebron, Jarmuth, Lachish and Eglon--joined forces. They moved up with all their troops and took up positions against Gibeon and attacked it.

column.name: text
column.value: The Gibeonites then sent word to Joshua in the camp at Gilgal: "Do not abandon your servants. Come up to us quickly and save us! Help us, because all the Amorite kings from the hill country have joined forces against us."

column.name: text
column.value: So Joshua marched up from Gilgal with his entire army, including all the best fighting men.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD said to Joshua, "Do not be afraid of them; I have given them into your hand. Not one of them will be able to withstand you."

column.name: text
column.value: After an all-night march from Gilgal, Joshua took them by surprise.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD threw them into confusion before Israel, who defeated them in a great victory at Gibeon. Israel pursued them along the road going up to Beth Horon and cut them down all the way to Azekah and Makkedah.

column.name: text
column.value: As they fled before Israel on the road down from Beth Horon to Azekah, the LORD hurled large hailstones down on them from the sky, and more of them died from the hailstones than were killed by the swords of the Israelites.

column.name: text
column.value: On the day the LORD gave the Amorites over to Israel, Joshua said to the LORD in the presence of Israel: "O sun, stand still over Gibeon, O moon, over the Valley of Aijalon."

column.name: text
column.value: So the sun stood still, and the moon stopped, till the nation avenged itself on its enemies, as it is written in the Book of Jashar. The sun stopped in the middle of the sky and delayed going down about a full day.

column.name: text
column.value: There has never been a day like it before or since, a day when the LORD listened to a man. Surely the LORD was fighting for Israel!

column.name: text
column.value: Then Joshua returned with all Israel to the camp at Gilgal.

column.name: text
column.value: Now the five kings had fled and hidden in the cave at Makkedah.

column.name: text
column.value: When Joshua was told that the five kings had been found hiding in the cave at Makkedah,

column.name: text
column.value: he said, "Roll large rocks up to the mouth of the cave, and post some men there to guard it.

column.name: text
column.value: But don't stop! Pursue your enemies, attack them from the rear and don't let them reach their cities, for the LORD your God has given them into your hand."

column.name: text
column.value: So Joshua and the Israelites destroyed them completely--almost to a man--but the few who were left reached their fortified cities.

column.name: text
column.value: The whole army then returned safely to Joshua in the camp at Makkedah, and no one uttered a word against the Israelites.

column.name: text
column.value: Joshua said, "Open the mouth of the cave and bring those five kings out to me."

column.name: text
column.value: So they brought the five kings out of the cave--the kings of Jerusalem, Hebron, Jarmuth, Lachish and Eglon.

column.name: text
column.value: When they had brought these kings to Joshua, he summoned all the men of Israel and said to the army commanders who had come with him, "Come here and put your feet on the necks of these kings." So they came forward and placed their feet on their necks.

column.name: text
column.value: Joshua said to them, "Do not be afraid; do not be discouraged. Be strong and courageous. This is what the LORD will do to all the enemies you are going to fight."

column.name: text
column.value: Then Joshua struck and killed the kings and hung them on five trees, and they were left hanging on the trees until evening.

column.name: text
column.value: At sunset Joshua gave the order and they took them down from the trees and threw them into the cave where they had been hiding. At the mouth of the cave they placed large rocks, which are there to this day.

column.name: text
