column.value: When she heard in Moab that the LORD had come to the aid of his people by providing food for them, Naomi and her daughters-in-law prepared to return home from there.

column.name: text
column.value: With her two daughters-in-law she left the place where she had been living and set out on the road that would take them back to the land of Judah.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Naomi said to her two daughters-in-law, "Go back, each of you, to your mother's home. May the LORD show kindness to you, as you have shown to your dead and to me.

column.name: text
column.value: May the LORD grant that each of you will find rest in the home of another husband." Then she kissed them and they wept aloud

column.name: text
column.value: and said to her, "We will go back with you to your people."

column.name: text
column.value: But Naomi said, "Return home, my daughters. Why would you come with me? Am I going to have any more sons, who could become your husbands?

column.name: text
column.value: Return home, my daughters; I am too old to have another husband. Even if I thought there was still hope for me--even if I had a husband tonight and then gave birth to sons--

column.name: text
column.value: would you wait until they grew up? Would you remain unmarried for them? No, my daughters. It is more bitter for me than for you, because the LORD'S hand has gone out against me!"

column.name: text
column.value: At this they wept again. Then Orpah kissed her mother-in-law good-by, but Ruth clung to her.

column.name: text
column.value: "Look," said Naomi, "your sister-in-law is going back to her people and her gods. Go back with her."

column.name: text
column.value: But Ruth replied, "Don't urge me to leave you or to turn back from you. Where you go I will go, and where you stay I will stay. Your people will be my people and your God my God.

column.name: text
column.value: Where you die I will die, and there I will be buried. May the LORD deal with me, be it ever so severely, if anything but death separates you and me."

column.name: text
column.value: When Naomi realized that Ruth was determined to go with her, she stopped urging her.

column.name: text
column.value: So the two women went on until they came to Bethlehem. When they arrived in Bethlehem, the whole town was stirred because of them, and the women exclaimed, "Can this be Naomi?"

column.name: text
column.value: "Don't call me Naomi," she told them. "Call me Mara, because the Almighty has made my life very bitter.

column.name: text
column.value: I went away full, but the LORD has brought me back empty. Why call me Naomi? The LORD has afflicted me; the Almighty has brought misfortune upon me."

column.name: text
column.value: So Naomi returned from Moab accompanied by Ruth the Moabitess, her daughter-in-law, arriving in Bethlehem as the barley harvest was beginning.

column.name: text
column.value: One day Naomi her mother-in-law said to her, "My daughter, should I not try to find a home for you, where you will be well provided for?

column.name: text
column.value: Is not Boaz, with whose servant girls you have been, a kinsman of ours? Tonight he will be winnowing barley on the threshing floor.

column.name: text
column.value: Wash and perfume yourself, and put on your best clothes. Then go down to the threshing floor, but don't let him know you are there until he has finished eating and drinking.

column.name: text
column.value: When he lies down, note the place where he is lying. Then go and uncover his feet and lie down. He will tell you what to do."

column.name: text
column.value: "I will do whatever you say," Ruth answered.

column.name: text
column.value: So she went down to the threshing floor and did everything her mother-in-law told her to do.

column.name: text
column.value: When Boaz had finished eating and drinking and was in good spirits, he went over to lie down at the far end of the grain pile. Ruth approached quietly, uncovered his feet and lay down.

column.name: text
column.value: In the middle of the night something startled the man, and he turned and discovered a woman lying at his feet.

column.name: text
column.value: "Who are you?" he asked. "I am your servant Ruth," she said. "Spread the corner of your garment over me, since you are a kinsman-redeemer."

column.name: text
column.value: "The LORD bless you, my daughter," he replied. "This kindness is greater than that which you showed earlier: You have not run after the younger men, whether rich or poor.

column.name: text
column.value: And now, my daughter, don't be afraid. I will do for you all you ask. All my fellow townsmen know that you are a woman of noble character.

column.name: text
column.value: Although it is true that I am near of kin, there is a kinsman-redeemer nearer than I.

column.name: text
column.value: Stay here for the night, and in the morning if he wants to redeem, good; let him redeem. But if he is not willing, as surely as the LORD lives I will do it. Lie here until morning."

column.name: text
column.value: So she lay at his feet until morning, but got up before anyone could be recognized; and he said, "Don't let it be known that a woman came to the threshing floor."

column.name: text
column.value: He also said, "Bring me the shawl you are wearing and hold it out." When she did so, he poured into it six measures of barley and put it on her. Then he went back to town.

column.name: text
column.value: When Ruth came to her mother-in-law, Naomi asked, "How did it go, my daughter?" Then she told her everything Boaz had done for her

column.name: text
column.value: and added, "He gave me these six measures of barley, saying, 'Don't go back to your mother-in-law empty-handed.'"

column.name: text
column.value: Then Naomi said, "Wait, my daughter, until you find out what happens. For the man will not rest until the matter is settled today."

column.name: text
column.value: Now Naomi had a relative on her husband's side, from the clan of Elimelech, a man of standing, whose name was Boaz.

column.name: text
column.value: And Ruth the Moabitess said to Naomi, "Let me go to the fields and pick up the leftover grain behind anyone in whose eyes I find favor." Naomi said to her, "Go ahead, my daughter."

column.name: text
column.value: So she went out and began to glean in the fields behind the harvesters. As it turned out, she found herself working in a field belonging to Boaz, who was from the clan of Elimelech.

column.name: text
column.value: Just then Boaz arrived from Bethlehem and greeted the harvesters, "The LORD be with you!" "The LORD bless you!" they called back.

column.name: text
column.value: Boaz asked the foreman of his harvesters, "Whose young woman is that?"

column.name: text
column.value: The foreman replied, "She is the Moabitess who came back from Moab with Naomi.

column.name: text
column.value: She said, 'Please let me glean and gather among the sheaves behind the harvesters.' She went into the field and has worked steadily from morning till now, except for a short rest in the shelter."

column.name: text
column.value: So Boaz said to Ruth, "My daughter, listen to me. Don't go and glean in another field and don't go away from here. Stay here with my servant girls.

column.name: text
column.value: Watch the field where the men are harvesting, and follow along after the girls. I have told the men not to touch you. And whenever you are thirsty, go and get a drink from the water jars the men have filled."

column.name: text
column.value: At this, she bowed down with her face to the ground. She exclaimed, "Why have I found such favor in your eyes that you notice me--a foreigner?"

column.name: text
column.value: Boaz replied, "I've been told all about what you have done for your mother-in-law since the death of your husband--how you left your father and mother and your homeland and came to live with a people you did not know before.

column.name: text
column.value: May the LORD repay you for what you have done. May you be richly rewarded by the LORD, the God of Israel, under whose wings you have come to take refuge."

column.name: text
column.value: "May I continue to find favor in your eyes, my lord," she said. "You have given me comfort and have spoken kindly to your servant--though I do not have the standing of one of your servant girls."

column.name: text
column.value: At mealtime Boaz said to her, "Come over here. Have some bread and dip it in the wine vinegar." When she sat down with the harvesters, he offered her some roasted grain. She ate all she wanted and had some left over.

column.name: text
column.value: As she got up to glean, Boaz gave orders to his men, "Even if she gathers among the sheaves, don't embarrass her.

column.name: text
column.value: Rather, pull out some stalks for her from the bundles and leave them for her to pick up, and don't rebuke her."

column.name: text
column.value: So Ruth gleaned in the field until evening. Then she threshed the barley she had gathered, and it amounted to about an ephah.

column.name: text
column.value: She carried it back to town, and her mother-in-law saw how much she had gathered. Ruth also brought out and gave her what she had left over after she had eaten enough.

column.name: text
column.value: Her mother-in-law asked her, "Where did you glean today? Where did you work? Blessed be the man who took notice of you!" Then Ruth told her mother-in-law about the one at whose place she had been working. "The name of the man I worked with today is Boaz," she said.

column.name: text
column.value: "The LORD bless him!" Naomi said to her daughter-in-law. "He has not stopped showing his kindness to the living and the dead." She added, "That man is our close relative; he is one of our kinsman-redeemers."

column.name: text
column.value: Then Ruth the Moabitess said, "He even said to me, 'Stay with my workers until they finish harvesting all my grain.'"

column.name: text
column.value: Naomi said to Ruth her daughter-in-law, "It will be good for you, my daughter, to go with his girls, because in someone else's field you might be harmed."

column.name: text
column.value: So Ruth stayed close to the servant girls of Boaz to glean until the barley and wheat harvests were finished. And she lived with her mother-in-law.

column.name: text
column.value: There was a certain man from Ramathaim, a Zuphite from the hill country of Ephraim, whose name was Elkanah son of Jeroham, the son of Elihu, the son of Tohu, the son of Zuph, an Ephraimite.

column.name: text
column.value: He had two wives; one was called Hannah and the other Peninnah. Peninnah had children, but Hannah had none.

column.name: text
column.value: Year after year this man went up from his town to worship and sacrifice to the LORD Almighty at Shiloh, where Hophni and Phinehas, the two sons of Eli, were priests of the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: Whenever the day came for Elkanah to sacrifice, he would give portions of the meat to his wife Peninnah and to all her sons and daughters.

column.name: text
column.value: But to Hannah he gave a double portion because he loved her, and the LORD had closed her womb.

column.name: text
column.value: And because the LORD had closed her womb, her rival kept provoking her in order to irritate her.

column.name: text
column.value: This went on year after year. Whenever Hannah went up to the house of the LORD, her rival provoked her till she wept and would not eat.

column.name: text
column.value: Elkanah her husband would say to her, "Hannah, why are you weeping? Why don't you eat? Why are you downhearted? Don't I mean more to you than ten sons?"

column.name: text
column.value: Once when they had finished eating and drinking in Shiloh, Hannah stood up. Now Eli the priest was sitting on a chair by the doorpost of the LORD'S temple.

column.name: text
column.value: In bitterness of soul Hannah wept much and prayed to the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: And she made a vow, saying, "O LORD Almighty, if you will only look upon your servant's misery and remember me, and not forget your servant but give her a son, then I will give him to the LORD for all the days of his life, and no razor will ever be used on his head."

column.name: text
column.value: As she kept on praying to the LORD, Eli observed her mouth.

column.name: text
column.value: Hannah was praying in her heart, and her lips were moving but her voice was not heard. Eli thought she was drunk

column.name: text
column.value: and said to her, "How long will you keep on getting drunk? Get rid of your wine."

column.name: text
column.value: "Not so, my lord," Hannah replied, "I am a woman who is deeply troubled. I have not been drinking wine or beer; I was pouring out my soul to the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: Do not take your servant for a wicked woman; I have been praying here out of my great anguish and grief."

column.name: text
column.value: Eli answered, "Go in peace, and may the God of Israel grant you what you have asked of him."

column.name: text
column.value: She said, "May your servant find favor in your eyes." Then she went her way and ate something, and her face was no longer downcast.

column.name: text
column.value: Early the next morning they arose and worshiped before the LORD and then went back to their home at Ramah. Elkanah lay with Hannah his wife, and the LORD remembered her.

column.name: text
column.value: So in the course of time Hannah conceived and gave birth to a son. She named him Samuel, saying, "Because I asked the LORD for him."

column.name: text
column.value: When the man Elkanah went up with all his family to offer the annual sacrifice to the LORD and to fulfill his vow,

column.name: text
column.value: Hannah did not go. She said to her husband, "After the boy is weaned, I will take him and present him before the LORD, and he will live there always."

column.name: text
column.value: "Do what seems best to you," Elkanah her husband told her. "Stay here until you have weaned him; only may the LORD make good his word." So the woman stayed at home and nursed her son until she had weaned him.

column.name: text
column.value: After he was weaned, she took the boy with her, young as he was, along with a three-year-old bull, an ephah of flour and a skin of wine, and brought him to the house of the LORD at Shiloh.

column.name: text
column.value: When they had slaughtered the bull, they brought the boy to Eli,

column.name: text
column.value: and she said to him, "As surely as you live, my lord, I am the woman who stood here beside you praying to the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: I prayed for this child, and the LORD has granted me what I asked of him.

column.name: text
column.value: So now I give him to the LORD. For his whole life he will be given over to the LORD." And he worshiped the LORD there.

column.name: text
column.value: Meanwhile Boaz went up to the town gate and sat there. When the kinsman-redeemer he had mentioned came along, Boaz said, "Come over here, my friend, and sit down." So he went over and sat down.

column.name: text
column.value: Boaz took ten of the elders of the town and said, "Sit here," and they did so.

column.name: text
column.value: Then he said to the kinsman-redeemer, "Naomi, who has come back from Moab, is selling the piece of land that belonged to our brother Elimelech.

column.name: text
column.value: I thought I should bring the matter to your attention and suggest that you buy it in the presence of these seated here and in the presence of the elders of my people. If you will redeem it, do so. But if you will not, tell me, so I will know. For no one has the right to do it except you, and I am next in line." "I will redeem it," he said.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Boaz said, "On the day you buy the land from Naomi and from Ruth the Moabitess, you acquire the dead man's widow, in order to maintain the name of the dead with his property."

column.name: text
column.value: At this, the kinsman-redeemer said, "Then I cannot redeem it because I might endanger my own estate. You redeem it yourself. I cannot do it."

column.name: text
column.value: (Now in earlier times in Israel, for the redemption and transfer of property to become final, one party took off his sandal and gave it to the other. This was the method of legalizing transactions in Israel.)

column.name: text
column.value: So the kinsman-redeemer said to Boaz, "Buy it yourself." And he removed his sandal.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Boaz announced to the elders and all the people, "Today you are witnesses that I have bought from Naomi all the property of Elimelech, Kilion and Mahlon.

column.name: text
column.value: I have also acquired Ruth the Moabitess, Mahlon's widow, as my wife, in order to maintain the name of the dead with his property, so that his name will not disappear from among his family or from the town records. Today you are witnesses!"

column.name: text
column.value: Then the elders and all those at the gate said, "We are witnesses. May the LORD make the woman who is coming into your home like Rachel and Leah, who together built up the house of Israel. May you have standing in Ephrathah and be famous in Bethlehem.

column.name: text
column.value: Through the offspring the LORD gives you by this young woman, may your family be like that of Perez, whom Tamar bore to Judah."

column.name: text
column.value: So Boaz took Ruth and she became his wife. Then he went to her, and the LORD enabled her to conceive, and she gave birth to a son.

column.name: text
column.value: The women said to Naomi: "Praise be to the LORD, who this day has not left you without a kinsman-redeemer. May he become famous throughout Israel!

column.name: text
column.value: He will renew your life and sustain you in your old age. For your daughter-in-law, who loves you and who is better to you than seven sons, has given him birth."

column.name: text
column.value: Then Naomi took the child, laid him in her lap and cared for him.

column.name: text
column.value: The women living there said, "Naomi has a son." And they named him Obed. He was the father of Jesse, the father of David.

column.name: text
column.value: This, then, is the family line of Perez: Perez was the father of Hezron,

column.name: text
column.value: Hezron the father of Ram, Ram the father of Amminadab,

column.name: text
column.value: Amminadab the father of Nahshon, Nahshon the father of Salmon,

column.name: text
column.value: Salmon the father of Boaz, Boaz the father of Obed,

column.name: text
column.value: Obed the father of Jesse, and Jesse the father of David.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Hannah prayed and said: "My heart rejoices in the LORD; in the LORD my horn is lifted high. My mouth boasts over my enemies, for I delight in your deliverance.

column.name: text
column.value: "There is no one holy like the LORD; there is no one besides you; there is no Rock like our God.

column.name: text
column.value: "Do not keep talking so proudly or let your mouth speak such arrogance, for the LORD is a God who knows, and by him deeds are weighed.

column.name: text
column.value: "The bows of the warriors are broken, but those who stumbled are armed with strength.

column.name: text
column.value: Those who were full hire themselves out for food, but those who were hungry hunger no more. She who was barren has borne seven children, but she who has had many sons pines away.

column.name: text
column.value: "The LORD brings death and makes alive; he brings down to the grave and raises up.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD sends poverty and wealth; he humbles and he exalts.

column.name: text
column.value: He raises the poor from the dust and lifts the needy from the ash heap; he seats them with princes and has them inherit a throne of honor. "For the foundations of the earth are the LORD'S; upon them he has set the world.

column.name: text
column.value: He will guard the feet of his saints, but the wicked will be silenced in darkness. "It is not by strength that one prevails;

column.name: text
column.value: those who oppose the LORD will be shattered. He will thunder against them from heaven; the LORD will judge the ends of the earth. "He will give strength to his king and exalt the horn of his anointed."

column.name: text
column.value: Then Elkanah went home to Ramah, but the boy ministered before the LORD under Eli the priest.

column.name: text
column.value: Eli's sons were wicked men; they had no regard for the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: Now it was the practice of the priests with the people that whenever anyone offered a sacrifice and while the meat was being boiled, the servant of the priest would come with a three-pronged fork in his hand.

column.name: text
column.value: He would plunge it into the pan or kettle or caldron or pot, and the priest would take for himself whatever the fork brought up. This is how they treated all the Israelites who came to Shiloh.

column.name: text
column.value: But even before the fat was burned, the servant of the priest would come and say to the man who was sacrificing, "Give the priest some meat to roast; he won't accept boiled meat from you, but only raw."

column.name: text
column.value: If the man said to him, "Let the fat be burned up first, and then take whatever you want," the servant would then answer, "No, hand it over now; if you don't, I'll take it by force."

column.name: text
column.value: This sin of the young men was very great in the LORD'S sight, for they were treating the LORD'S offering with contempt.

column.name: text
column.value: But Samuel was ministering before the LORD--a boy wearing a linen ephod.

column.name: text
column.value: Each year his mother made him a little robe and took it to him when she went up with her husband to offer the annual sacrifice.

column.name: text
column.value: Eli would bless Elkanah and his wife, saying, "May the LORD give you children by this woman to take the place of the one she prayed for and gave to the LORD." Then they would go home.

column.name: text
column.value: And the LORD was gracious to Hannah; she conceived and gave birth to three sons and two daughters. Meanwhile, the boy Samuel grew up in the presence of the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: Now Eli, who was very old, heard about everything his sons were doing to all Israel and how they slept with the women who served at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.

column.name: text
column.value: So he said to them, "Why do you do such things? I hear from all the people about these wicked deeds of yours.

column.name: text
column.value: No, my sons; it is not a good report that I hear spreading among the LORD'S people.

column.name: text
column.value: If a man sins against another man, God may mediate for him; but if a man sins against the LORD, who will intercede for him?" His sons, however, did not listen to their father's rebuke, for it was the LORD'S will to put them to death.

column.name: text
column.value: And the boy Samuel continued to grow in stature and in favor with the LORD and with men.

column.name: text
column.value: Now a man of God came to Eli and said to him, "This is what the LORD says: 'Did I not clearly reveal myself to your father's house when they were in Egypt under Pharaoh?

column.name: text
column.value: I chose your father out of all the tribes of Israel to be my priest, to go up to my altar, to burn incense, and to wear an ephod in my presence. I also gave your father's house all the offerings made with fire by the Israelites.

column.name: text
column.value: Why do you scorn my sacrifice and offering that I prescribed for my dwelling? Why do you honor your sons more than me by fattening yourselves on the choice parts of every offering made by my people Israel?'

column.name: text
column.value: "Therefore the LORD, the God of Israel, declares: 'I promised that your house and your father's house would minister before me forever.' But now the LORD declares: 'Far be it from me! Those who honor me I will honor, but those who despise me will be disdained.

column.name: text
column.value: The time is coming when I will cut short your strength and the strength of your father's house, so that there will not be an old man in your family line

column.name: text
column.value: and you will see distress in my dwelling. Although good will be done to Israel, in your family line there will never be an old man.

column.name: text
column.value: Every one of you that I do not cut off from my altar will be spared only to blind your eyes with tears and to grieve your heart, and all your descendants will die in the prime of life.

column.name: text
column.value: "'And what happens to your two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, will be a sign to you--they will both die on the same day.

column.name: text
column.value: I will raise up for myself a faithful priest, who will do according to what is in my heart and mind. I will firmly establish his house, and he will minister before my anointed one always.

column.name: text
column.value: Then everyone left in your family line will come and bow down before him for a piece of silver and a crust of bread and plead, "Appoint me to some priestly office so I can have food to eat."'"

column.name: text
column.value: The boy Samuel ministered before the LORD under Eli. In those days the word of the LORD was rare; there were not many visions.

column.name: text
column.value: One night Eli, whose eyes were becoming so weak that he could barely see, was lying down in his usual place.

column.name: text
column.value: The lamp of God had not yet gone out, and Samuel was lying down in the temple of the LORD, where the ark of God was.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD called Samuel. Samuel answered, "Here I am."

column.name: text
column.value: And he ran to Eli and said, "Here I am; you called me." But Eli said, "I did not call; go back and lie down." So he went and lay down.

column.name: text
column.value: Again the LORD called, "Samuel!" And Samuel got up and went to Eli and said, "Here I am; you called me." "My son," Eli said, "I did not call; go back and lie down."

column.name: text
column.value: Now Samuel did not yet know the LORD: The word of the LORD had not yet been revealed to him.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD called Samuel a third time, and Samuel got up and went to Eli and said, "Here I am; you called me." Then Eli realized that the LORD was calling the boy.

column.name: text
column.value: So Eli told Samuel, "Go and lie down, and if he calls you, say, 'Speak, LORD, for your servant is listening.'" So Samuel went and lay down in his place.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD came and stood there, calling as at the other times, "Samuel! Samuel!" Then Samuel said, "Speak, for your servant is listening."

column.name: text
column.value: And the LORD said to Samuel: "See, I am about to do something in Israel that will make the ears of everyone who hears of it tingle.

column.name: text
column.value: At that time I will carry out against Eli everything I spoke against his family--from beginning to end.

column.name: text
column.value: For I told him that I would judge his family forever because of the sin he knew about; his sons made themselves contemptible, and he failed to restrain them.

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore, I swore to the house of Eli, 'The guilt of Eli's house will never be atoned for by sacrifice or offering.'"

column.name: text
column.value: Samuel lay down until morning and then opened the doors of the house of the LORD. He was afraid to tell Eli the vision,

column.name: text
column.value: but Eli called him and said, "Samuel, my son." Samuel answered, "Here I am."

column.name: text
column.value: "What was it he said to you?" Eli asked. "Do not hide it from me. May God deal with you, be it ever so severely, if you hide from me anything he told you."

column.name: text
column.value: So Samuel told him everything, hiding nothing from him. Then Eli said, "He is the LORD; let him do what is good in his eyes."

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD was with Samuel as he grew up, and he let none of his words fall to the ground.

column.name: text
column.value: And all Israel from Dan to Beersheba recognized that Samuel was attested as a prophet of the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD continued to appear at Shiloh, and there he revealed himself to Samuel through his word.

column.name: text
column.value: And Samuel's word came to all Israel. Now the Israelites went out to fight against the Philistines. The Israelites camped at Ebenezer, and the Philistines at Aphek.

column.name: text
column.value: The Philistines deployed their forces to meet Israel, and as the battle spread, Israel was defeated by the Philistines, who killed about four thousand of them on the battlefield.

column.name: text
column.value: When the soldiers returned to camp, the elders of Israel asked, "Why did the LORD bring defeat upon us today before the Philistines? Let us bring the ark of the LORD'S covenant from Shiloh, so that it may go with us and save us from the hand of our enemies."

column.name: text
column.value: So the people sent men to Shiloh, and they brought back the ark of the covenant of the LORD Almighty, who is enthroned between the cherubim. And Eli's two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, were there with the ark of the covenant of God.

column.name: text
column.value: When the ark of the LORD'S covenant came into the camp, all Israel raised such a great shout that the ground shook.

column.name: text
column.value: Hearing the uproar, the Philistines asked, "What's all this shouting in the Hebrew camp?" When they learned that the ark of the LORD had come into the camp,

column.name: text
column.value: the Philistines were afraid. "A god has come into the camp," they said. "We're in trouble! Nothing like this has happened before.

column.name: text
column.value: Woe to us! Who will deliver us from the hand of these mighty gods? They are the gods who struck the Egyptians with all kinds of plagues in the desert.

column.name: text
column.value: Be strong, Philistines! Be men, or you will be subject to the Hebrews, as they have been to you. Be men, and fight!"

column.name: text
column.value: So the Philistines fought, and the Israelites were defeated and every man fled to his tent. The slaughter was very great; Israel lost thirty thousand foot soldiers.

column.name: text
column.value: The ark of God was captured, and Eli's two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, died.

column.name: text
column.value: That same day a Benjamite ran from the battle line and went to Shiloh, his clothes torn and dust on his head.

column.name: text
column.value: When he arrived, there was Eli sitting on his chair by the side of the road, watching, because his heart feared for the ark of God. When the man entered the town and told what had happened, the whole town sent up a cry.

column.name: text
column.value: Eli heard the outcry and asked, "What is the meaning of this uproar?" The man hurried over to Eli,

column.name: text
column.value: who was ninety-eight years old and whose eyes were set so that he could not see.

column.name: text
column.value: He told Eli, "I have just come from the battle line; I fled from it this very day." Eli asked, "What happened, my son?"

column.name: text
column.value: The man who brought the news replied, "Israel fled before the Philistines, and the army has suffered heavy losses. Also your two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, are dead, and the ark of God has been captured."

column.name: text
column.value: When he mentioned the ark of God, Eli fell backward off his chair by the side of the gate. His neck was broken and he died, for he was an old man and heavy. He had led Israel forty years.

column.name: text
column.value: His daughter-in-law, the wife of Phinehas, was pregnant and near the time of delivery. When she heard the news that the ark of God had been captured and that her father-in-law and her husband were dead, she went into labor and gave birth, but was overcome by her labor pains.

column.name: text
column.value: As she was dying, the women attending her said, "Don't despair; you have given birth to a son." But she did not respond or pay any attention.

column.name: text
column.value: She named the boy Ichabod, saying, "The glory has departed from Israel"--because of the capture of the ark of God and the deaths of her father-in-law and her husband.

column.name: text
column.value: She said, "The glory has departed from Israel, for the ark of God has been captured."

column.name: text
column.value: Then all the Israelites from Dan to Beersheba and from the land of Gilead came out as one man and assembled before the LORD in Mizpah.

column.name: text
column.value: The leaders of all the people of the tribes of Israel took their places in the assembly of the people of God, four hundred thousand soldiers armed with swords.

column.name: text
column.value: (The Benjamites heard that the Israelites had gone up to Mizpah.) Then the Israelites said, "Tell us how this awful thing happened."

column.name: text
column.value: So the Levite, the husband of the murdered woman, said, "I and my concubine came to Gibeah in Benjamin to spend the night.

column.name: text
column.value: During the night the men of Gibeah came after me and surrounded the house, intending to kill me. They raped my concubine, and she died.

column.name: text
column.value: I took my concubine, cut her into pieces and sent one piece to each region of Israel's inheritance, because they committed this lewd and disgraceful act in Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: Now, all you Israelites, speak up and give your verdict."

column.name: text
column.value: All the people rose as one man, saying, "None of us will go home. No, not one of us will return to his house.

column.name: text
column.value: But now this is what we'll do to Gibeah: We'll go up against it as the lot directs.

column.name: text
column.value: We'll take ten men out of every hundred from all the tribes of Israel, and a hundred from a thousand, and a thousand from ten thousand, to get provisions for the army. Then, when the army arrives at Gibeah in Benjamin, it can give them what they deserve for all this vileness done in Israel."

column.name: text
column.value: So all the men of Israel got together and united as one man against the city.

column.name: text
column.value: The tribes of Israel sent men throughout the tribe of Benjamin, saying, "What about this awful crime that was committed among you?

column.name: text
column.value: Now surrender those wicked men of Gibeah so that we may put them to death and purge the evil from Israel." But the Benjamites would not listen to their fellow Israelites.

column.name: text
column.value: From their towns they came together at Gibeah to fight against the Israelites.

column.name: text
column.value: At once the Benjamites mobilized twenty-six thousand swordsmen from their towns, in addition to seven hundred chosen men from those living in Gibeah.

column.name: text
column.value: Among all these soldiers there were seven hundred chosen men who were left-handed, each of whom could sling a stone at a hair and not miss.

column.name: text
column.value: Israel, apart from Benjamin, mustered four hundred thousand swordsmen, all of them fighting men.

column.name: text
column.value: The Israelites went up to Bethel and inquired of God. They said, "Who of us shall go first to fight against the Benjamites?" The LORD replied, "Judah shall go first."

column.name: text
column.value: The next morning the Israelites got up and pitched camp near Gibeah.

column.name: text
column.value: The men of Israel went out to fight the Benjamites and took up battle positions against them at Gibeah.

column.name: text
column.value: The Benjamites came out of Gibeah and cut down twenty-two thousand Israelites on the battlefield that day.

column.name: text
column.value: But the men of Israel encouraged one another and again took up their positions where they had stationed themselves the first day.

column.name: text
column.value: The Israelites went up and wept before the LORD until evening, and they inquired of the LORD. They said, "Shall we go up again to battle against the Benjamites, our brothers?" The LORD answered, "Go up against them."

column.name: text
column.value: Then the Israelites drew near to Benjamin the second day.

column.name: text
column.value: This time, when the Benjamites came out from Gibeah to oppose them, they cut down another eighteen thousand Israelites, all of them armed with swords.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the Israelites, all the people, went up to Bethel, and there they sat weeping before the LORD. They fasted that day until evening and presented burnt offerings and fellowship offerings to the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: And the Israelites inquired of the LORD. (In those days the ark of the covenant of God was there,

column.name: text
column.value: with Phinehas son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron, ministering before it.) They asked, "Shall we go up again to battle with Benjamin our brother, or not?" The LORD responded, "Go, for tomorrow I will give them into your hands."

column.name: text
column.value: Then Israel set an ambush around Gibeah.

column.name: text
column.value: They went up against the Benjamites on the third day and took up positions against Gibeah as they had done before.

column.name: text
column.value: The Benjamites came out to meet them and were drawn away from the city. They began to inflict casualties on the Israelites as before, so that about thirty men fell in the open field and on the roads--the one leading to Bethel and the other to Gibeah.

column.name: text
column.value: While the Benjamites were saying, "We are defeating them as before," the Israelites were saying, "Let's retreat and draw them away from the city to the roads."

column.name: text
column.value: All the men of Israel moved from their places and took up positions at Baal Tamar, and the Israelite ambush charged out of its place on the west of Gibeah.

column.name: text
column.value: Then ten thousand of Israel's finest men made a frontal attack on Gibeah. The fighting was so heavy that the Benjamites did not realize how near disaster was.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD defeated Benjamin before Israel, and on that day the Israelites struck down 25,100 Benjamites, all armed with swords.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the Benjamites saw that they were beaten. Now the men of Israel had given way before Benjamin, because they relied on the ambush they had set near Gibeah.

column.name: text
column.value: The men who had been in ambush made a sudden dash into Gibeah, spread out and put the whole city to the sword.

column.name: text
column.value: The men of Israel had arranged with the ambush that they should send up a great cloud of smoke from the city,

column.name: text
column.value: and then the men of Israel would turn in the battle. The Benjamites had begun to inflict casualties on the men of Israel (about thirty), and they said, "We are defeating them as in the first battle."

column.name: text
column.value: But when the column of smoke began to rise from the city, the Benjamites turned and saw the smoke of the whole city going up into the sky.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the men of Israel turned on them, and the men of Benjamin were terrified, because they realized that disaster had come upon them.

column.name: text
column.value: So they fled before the Israelites in the direction of the desert, but they could not escape the battle. And the men of Israel who came out of the towns cut them down there.

column.name: text
column.value: They surrounded the Benjamites, chased them and easily overran them in the vicinity of Gibeah on the east.

column.name: text
column.value: Eighteen thousand Benjamites fell, all of them valiant fighters.

column.name: text
column.value: As they turned and fled toward the desert to the rock of Rimmon, the Israelites cut down five thousand men along the roads. They kept pressing after the Benjamites as far as Gidom and struck down two thousand more.

column.name: text
column.value: On that day twenty-five thousand Benjamite swordsmen fell, all of them valiant fighters.

column.name: text
column.value: But six hundred men turned and fled into the desert to the rock of Rimmon, where they stayed four months.

column.name: text
column.value: The men of Israel went back to Benjamin and put all the towns to the sword, including the animals and everything else they found. All the towns they came across they set on fire.

column.name: text
column.value: After the Philistines had captured the ark of God, they took it from Ebenezer to Ashdod.

column.name: text
column.value: Then they carried the ark into Dagon's temple and set it beside Dagon.

column.name: text
column.value: When the people of Ashdod rose early the next day, there was Dagon, fallen on his face on the ground before the ark of the LORD! They took Dagon and put him back in his place.

column.name: text
column.value: But the following morning when they rose, there was Dagon, fallen on his face on the ground before the ark of the LORD! His head and hands had been broken off and were lying on the threshold; only his body remained.

column.name: text
column.value: That is why to this day neither the priests of Dagon nor any others who enter Dagon's temple at Ashdod step on the threshold.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD'S hand was heavy upon the people of Ashdod and its vicinity; he brought devastation upon them and afflicted them with tumors.

column.name: text
column.value: When the men of Ashdod saw what was happening, they said, "The ark of the god of Israel must not stay here with us, because his hand is heavy upon us and upon Dagon our god."

column.name: text
column.value: So they called together all the rulers of the Philistines and asked them, "What shall we do with the ark of the god of Israel?" They answered, "Have the ark of the god of Israel moved to Gath." So they moved the ark of the God of Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: But after they had moved it, the LORD'S hand was against that city, throwing it into a great panic. He afflicted the people of the city, both young and old, with an outbreak of tumors.

column.name: text
column.value: So they sent the ark of God to Ekron. As the ark of God was entering Ekron, the people of Ekron cried out, "They have brought the ark of the god of Israel around to us to kill us and our people."

column.name: text
column.value: So they called together all the rulers of the Philistines and said, "Send the ark of the god of Israel away; let it go back to its own place, or it will kill us and our people." For death had filled the city with panic; God's hand was very heavy upon it.

column.name: text
column.value: Those who did not die were afflicted with tumors, and the outcry of the city went up to heaven.

column.name: text
column.value: When the ark of the LORD had been in Philistine territory seven months,

column.name: text
column.value: the Philistines called for the priests and the diviners and said, "What shall we do with the ark of the LORD? Tell us how we should send it back to its place."

column.name: text
column.value: They answered, "If you return the ark of the god of Israel, do not send it away empty, but by all means send a guilt offering to him. Then you will be healed, and you will know why his hand has not been lifted from you."

column.name: text
column.value: The Philistines asked, "What guilt offering should we send to him?" They replied, "Five gold tumors and five gold rats, according to the number of the Philistine rulers, because the same plague has struck both you and your rulers.

column.name: text
column.value: Make models of the tumors and of the rats that are destroying the country, and pay honor to Israel's god. Perhaps he will lift his hand from you and your gods and your land.

column.name: text
column.value: Why do you harden your hearts as the Egyptians and Pharaoh did? When he treated them harshly, did they not send the Israelites out so they could go on their way?

column.name: text
column.value: "Now then, get a new cart ready, with two cows that have calved and have never been yoked. Hitch the cows to the cart, but take their calves away and pen them up.

column.name: text
column.value: Take the ark of the LORD and put it on the cart, and in a chest beside it put the gold objects you are sending back to him as a guilt offering. Send it on its way,

column.name: text
column.value: but keep watching it. If it goes up to its own territory, toward Beth Shemesh, then the LORD has brought this great disaster on us. But if it does not, then we will know that it was not his hand that struck us and that it happened to us by chance."

column.name: text
column.value: So they did this. They took two such cows and hitched them to the cart and penned up their calves.

column.name: text
column.value: They placed the ark of the LORD on the cart and along with it the chest containing the gold rats and the models of the tumors.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the cows went straight up toward Beth Shemesh, keeping on the road and lowing all the way; they did not turn to the right or to the left. The rulers of the Philistines followed them as far as the border of Beth Shemesh.

column.name: text
column.value: Now the people of Beth Shemesh were harvesting their wheat in the valley, and when they looked up and saw the ark, they rejoiced at the sight.

column.name: text
column.value: The cart came to the field of Joshua of Beth Shemesh, and there it stopped beside a large rock. The people chopped up the wood of the cart and sacrificed the cows as a burnt offering to the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: The Levites took down the ark of the LORD, together with the chest containing the gold objects, and placed them on the large rock. On that day the people of Beth Shemesh offered burnt offerings and made sacrifices to the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: The five rulers of the Philistines saw all this and then returned that same day to Ekron.

column.name: text
column.value: These are the gold tumors the Philistines sent as a guilt offering to the LORD--one each for Ashdod, Gaza, Ashkelon, Gath and Ekron.

column.name: text
column.value: And the number of the gold rats was according to the number of Philistine towns belonging to the five rulers--the fortified towns with their country villages. The large rock, on which they set the ark of the LORD, is a witness to this day in the field of Joshua of Beth Shemesh.

column.name: text
column.value: But God struck down some of the men of Beth Shemesh, putting seventy of them to death because they had looked into the ark of the LORD. The people mourned because of the heavy blow the LORD had dealt them,

column.name: text
column.value: and the men of Beth Shemesh asked, "Who can stand in the presence of the LORD, this holy God? To whom will the ark go up from here?"

column.name: text
column.value: Then they sent messengers to the people of Kiriath Jearim, saying, "The Philistines have returned the ark of the LORD. Come down and take it up to your place."

column.name: text
column.value: So the men of Kiriath Jearim came and took up the ark of the LORD. They took it to Abinadab's house on the hill and consecrated Eleazar his son to guard the ark of the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: It was a long time, twenty years in all, that the ark remained at Kiriath Jearim, and all the people of Israel mourned and sought after the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: And Samuel said to the whole house of Israel, "If you are returning to the LORD with all your hearts, then rid yourselves of the foreign gods and the Ashtoreths and commit yourselves to the LORD and serve him only, and he will deliver you out of the hand of the Philistines."

column.name: text
column.value: So the Israelites put away their Baals and Ashtoreths, and served the LORD only.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Samuel said, "Assemble all Israel at Mizpah and I will intercede with the LORD for you."

column.name: text
column.value: When they had assembled at Mizpah, they drew water and poured it out before the LORD. On that day they fasted and there they confessed, "We have sinned against the LORD." And Samuel was leader of Israel at Mizpah.

column.name: text
column.value: When the Philistines heard that Israel had assembled at Mizpah, the rulers of the Philistines came up to attack them. And when the Israelites heard of it, they were afraid because of the Philistines.

column.name: text
column.value: They said to Samuel, "Do not stop crying out to the LORD our God for us, that he may rescue us from the hand of the Philistines."

column.name: text
column.value: Then Samuel took a suckling lamb and offered it up as a whole burnt offering to the LORD. He cried out to the LORD on Israel's behalf, and the LORD answered him.

column.name: text
column.value: While Samuel was sacrificing the burnt offering, the Philistines drew near to engage Israel in battle. But that day the LORD thundered with loud thunder against the Philistines and threw them into such a panic that they were routed before the Israelites.

column.name: text
column.value: The men of Israel rushed out of Mizpah and pursued the Philistines, slaughtering them along the way to a point below Beth Car.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Samuel took a stone and set it up between Mizpah and Shen. He named it Ebenezer, saying, "Thus far has the LORD helped us."

column.name: text
column.value: So the Philistines were subdued and did not invade Israelite territory again. Throughout Samuel's lifetime, the hand of the LORD was against the Philistines.

column.name: text
column.value: The towns from Ekron to Gath that the Philistines had captured from Israel were restored to her, and Israel delivered the neighboring territory from the power of the Philistines. And there was peace between Israel and the Amorites.

column.name: text
column.value: Samuel continued as judge over Israel all the days of his life.

column.name: text
column.value: From year to year he went on a circuit from Bethel to Gilgal to Mizpah, judging Israel in all those places.

column.name: text
column.value: But he always went back to Ramah, where his home was, and there he also judged Israel. And he built an altar there to the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: When Samuel grew old, he appointed his sons as judges for Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: The name of his firstborn was Joel and the name of his second was Abijah, and they served at Beersheba.

column.name: text
column.value: But his sons did not walk in his ways. They turned aside after dishonest gain and accepted bribes and perverted justice.

column.name: text
column.value: So all the elders of Israel gathered together and came to Samuel at Ramah.

column.name: text
column.value: They said to him, "You are old, and your sons do not walk in your ways; now appoint a king to lead us, such as all the other nations have."

column.name: text
column.value: But when they said, "Give us a king to lead us," this displeased Samuel; so he prayed to the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: And the LORD told him: "Listen to all that the people are saying to you; it is not you they have rejected, but they have rejected me as their king.

column.name: text
column.value: As they have done from the day I brought them up out of Egypt until this day, forsaking me and serving other gods, so they are doing to you.

column.name: text
column.value: Now listen to them; but warn them solemnly and let them know what the king who will reign over them will do."

column.name: text
column.value: Samuel told all the words of the LORD to the people who were asking him for a king.

column.name: text
column.value: He said, "This is what the king who will reign over you will do: He will take your sons and make them serve with his chariots and horses, and they will run in front of his chariots.

column.name: text
column.value: Some he will assign to be commanders of thousands and commanders of fifties, and others to plow his ground and reap his harvest, and still others to make weapons of war and equipment for his chariots.

column.name: text
column.value: He will take your daughters to be perfumers and cooks and bakers.

column.name: text
column.value: He will take the best of your fields and vineyards and olive groves and give them to his attendants.

column.name: text
column.value: He will take a tenth of your grain and of your vintage and give it to his officials and attendants.

column.name: text
column.value: Your menservants and maidservants and the best of your cattle and donkeys he will take for his own use.

column.name: text
column.value: He will take a tenth of your flocks, and you yourselves will become his slaves.

column.name: text
column.value: When that day comes, you will cry out for relief from the king you have chosen, and the LORD will not answer you in that day."

column.name: text
column.value: But the people refused to listen to Samuel. "No!" they said. "We want a king over us.

column.name: text
column.value: Then we will be like all the other nations, with a king to lead us and to go out before us and fight our battles."

column.name: text
column.value: When Samuel heard all that the people said, he repeated it before the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD answered, "Listen to them and give them a king." Then Samuel said to the men of Israel, "Everyone go back to his town."

column.name: text
column.value: There was a Benjamite, a man of standing, whose name was Kish son of Abiel, the son of Zeror, the son of Becorath, the son of Aphiah of Benjamin.

column.name: text
column.value: He had a son named Saul, an impressive young man without equal among the Israelites--a head taller than any of the others.

column.name: text
column.value: Now the donkeys belonging to Saul's father Kish were lost, and Kish said to his son Saul, "Take one of the servants with you and go and look for the donkeys."

column.name: text
column.value: So he passed through the hill country of Ephraim and through the area around Shalisha, but they did not find them. They went on into the district of Shaalim, but the donkeys were not there. Then he passed through the territory of Benjamin, but they did not find them.

column.name: text
column.value: When they reached the district of Zuph, Saul said to the servant who was with him, "Come, let's go back, or my father will stop thinking about the donkeys and start worrying about us."

column.name: text
column.value: But the servant replied, "Look, in this town there is a man of God; he is highly respected, and everything he says comes true. Let's go there now. Perhaps he will tell us what way to take."

column.name: text
column.value: Saul said to his servant, "If we go, what can we give the man? The food in our sacks is gone. We have no gift to take to the man of God. What do we have?"

column.name: text
column.value: The servant answered him again. "Look," he said, "I have a quarter of a shekel of silver. I will give it to the man of God so that he will tell us what way to take."

column.name: text
column.value: (Formerly in Israel, if a man went to inquire of God, he would say, "Come, let us go to the seer," because the prophet of today used to be called a seer.)

column.name: text
column.value: "Good," Saul said to his servant. "Come, let's go." So they set out for the town where the man of God was.

column.name: text
column.value: As they were going up the hill to the town, they met some girls coming out to draw water, and they asked them, "Is the seer here?"

column.name: text
column.value: "He is," they answered. "He's ahead of you. Hurry now; he has just come to our town today, for the people have a sacrifice at the high place.

column.name: text
column.value: As soon as you enter the town, you will find him before he goes up to the high place to eat. The people will not begin eating until he comes, because he must bless the sacrifice; afterward, those who are invited will eat. Go up now; you should find him about this time."

column.name: text
column.value: They went up to the town, and as they were entering it, there was Samuel, coming toward them on his way up to the high place.

column.name: text
column.value: Now the day before Saul came, the LORD had revealed this to Samuel:

column.name: text
column.value: "About this time tomorrow I will send you a man from the land of Benjamin. Anoint him leader over my people Israel; he will deliver my people from the hand of the Philistines. I have looked upon my people, for their cry has reached me."

column.name: text
column.value: When Samuel caught sight of Saul, the LORD said to him, "This is the man I spoke to you about; he will govern my people."

column.name: text
column.value: Saul approached Samuel in the gateway and asked, "Would you please tell me where the seer's house is?"

column.name: text
column.value: "I am the seer," Samuel replied. "Go up ahead of me to the high place, for today you are to eat with me, and in the morning I will let you go and will tell you all that is in your heart.

column.name: text
column.value: As for the donkeys you lost three days ago, do not worry about them; they have been found. And to whom is all the desire of Israel turned, if not to you and all your father's family?"

column.name: text
column.value: Saul answered, "But am I not a Benjamite, from the smallest tribe of Israel, and is not my clan the least of all the clans of the tribe of Benjamin? Why do you say such a thing to me?"

column.name: text
column.value: Then Samuel brought Saul and his servant into the hall and seated them at the head of those who were invited--about thirty in number.

column.name: text
column.value: Samuel said to the cook, "Bring the piece of meat I gave you, the one I told you to lay aside."

column.name: text
column.value: So the cook took up the leg with what was on it and set it in front of Saul. Samuel said, "Here is what has been kept for you. Eat, because it was set aside for you for this occasion, from the time I said, 'I have invited guests.'" And Saul dined with Samuel that day.

column.name: text
column.value: After they came down from the high place to the town, Samuel talked with Saul on the roof of his house.

column.name: text
column.value: They rose about daybreak and Samuel called to Saul on the roof, "Get ready, and I will send you on your way." When Saul got ready, he and Samuel went outside together.

column.name: text
column.value: As they were going down to the edge of the town, Samuel said to Saul, "Tell the servant to go on ahead of us"--and the servant did so--"but you stay here awhile, so that I may give you a message from God."

column.name: text
column.value: Then Samuel took a flask of oil and poured it on Saul's head and kissed him, saying, "Has not the LORD anointed you leader over his inheritance?

column.name: text
column.value: When you leave me today, you will meet two men near Rachel's tomb, at Zelzah on the border of Benjamin. They will say to you, 'The donkeys you set out to look for have been found. And now your father has stopped thinking about them and is worried about you. He is asking, "What shall I do about my son?"'

column.name: text
column.value: "Then you will go on from there until you reach the great tree of Tabor. Three men going up to God at Bethel will meet you there. One will be carrying three young goats, another three loaves of bread, and another a skin of wine.

column.name: text
column.value: They will greet you and offer you two loaves of bread, which you will accept from them.

column.name: text
column.value: "After that you will go to Gibeah of God, where there is a Philistine outpost. As you approach the town, you will meet a procession of prophets coming down from the high place with lyres, tambourines, flutes and harps being played before them, and they will be prophesying.

column.name: text
column.value: The Spirit of the LORD will come upon you in power, and you will prophesy with them; and you will be changed into a different person.

column.name: text
column.value: Once these signs are fulfilled, do whatever your hand finds to do, for God is with you.

column.name: text
column.value: "Go down ahead of me to Gilgal. I will surely come down to you to sacrifice burnt offerings and fellowship offerings, but you must wait seven days until I come to you and tell you what you are to do."

column.name: text
column.value: As Saul turned to leave Samuel, God changed Saul's heart, and all these signs were fulfilled that day.

column.name: text
column.value: When they arrived at Gibeah, a procession of prophets met him; the Spirit of God came upon him in power, and he joined in their prophesying.

column.name: text
column.value: When all those who had formerly known him saw him prophesying with the prophets, they asked each other, "What is this that has happened to the son of Kish? Is Saul also among the prophets?"

column.name: text
column.value: A man who lived there answered, "And who is their father?" So it became a saying: "Is Saul also among the prophets?"

column.name: text
column.value: After Saul stopped prophesying, he went to the high place.

column.name: text
column.value: Now Saul's uncle asked him and his servant, "Where have you been?" "Looking for the donkeys," he said. "But when we saw they were not to be found, we went to Samuel."

column.name: text
column.value: Saul's uncle said, "Tell me what Samuel said to you."

column.name: text
column.value: Saul replied, "He assured us that the donkeys had been found." But he did not tell his uncle what Samuel had said about the kingship.

column.name: text
column.value: Samuel summoned the people of Israel to the LORD at Mizpah

column.name: text
column.value: and said to them, "This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: 'I brought Israel up out of Egypt, and I delivered you from the power of Egypt and all the kingdoms that oppressed you.'

column.name: text
column.value: But you have now rejected your God, who saves you out of all your calamities and distresses. And you have said, 'No, set a king over us.' So now present yourselves before the LORD by your tribes and clans."

column.name: text
column.value: When Samuel brought all the tribes of Israel near, the tribe of Benjamin was chosen.

column.name: text
column.value: Then he brought forward the tribe of Benjamin, clan by clan, and Matri's clan was chosen. Finally Saul son of Kish was chosen. But when they looked for him, he was not to be found.

column.name: text
column.value: So they inquired further of the LORD, "Has the man come here yet?" And the LORD said, "Yes, he has hidden himself among the baggage."

column.name: text
column.value: They ran and brought him out, and as he stood among the people he was a head taller than any of the others.

column.name: text
column.value: Samuel said to all the people, "Do you see the man the LORD has chosen? There is no one like him among all the people." Then the people shouted, "Long live the king!"

column.name: text
column.value: Samuel explained to the people the regulations of the kingship. He wrote them down on a scroll and deposited it before the LORD. Then Samuel dismissed the people, each to his own home.

column.name: text
column.value: Saul also went to his home in Gibeah, accompanied by valiant men whose hearts God had touched.

column.name: text
column.value: But some troublemakers said, "How can this fellow save us?" They despised him and brought him no gifts. But Saul kept silent.

column.name: text
column.value: Nahash the Ammonite went up and besieged Jabesh Gilead. And all the men of Jabesh said to him, "Make a treaty with us, and we will be subject to you."

column.name: text
column.value: But Nahash the Ammonite replied, "I will make a treaty with you only on the condition that I gouge out the right eye of every one of you and so bring disgrace on all Israel."

column.name: text
column.value: The elders of Jabesh said to him, "Give us seven days so we can send messengers throughout Israel; if no one comes to rescue us, we will surrender to you."

column.name: text
column.value: When the messengers came to Gibeah of Saul and reported these terms to the people, they all wept aloud.

column.name: text
column.value: Just then Saul was returning from the fields, behind his oxen, and he asked, "What is wrong with the people? Why are they weeping?" Then they repeated to him what the men of Jabesh had said.

column.name: text
column.value: When Saul heard their words, the Spirit of God came upon him in power, and he burned with anger.

column.name: text
column.value: He took a pair of oxen, cut them into pieces, and sent the pieces by messengers throughout Israel, proclaiming, "This is what will be done to the oxen of anyone who does not follow Saul and Samuel." Then the terror of the LORD fell on the people, and they turned out as one man.

column.name: text
column.value: When Saul mustered them at Bezek, the men of Israel numbered three hundred thousand and the men of Judah thirty thousand.

column.name: text
column.value: They told the messengers who had come, "Say to the men of Jabesh Gilead, 'By the time the sun is hot tomorrow, you will be delivered.'" When the messengers went and reported this to the men of Jabesh, they were elated.

column.name: text
column.value: They said to the Ammonites, "Tomorrow we will surrender to you, and you can do to us whatever seems good to you."

column.name: text
column.value: The next day Saul separated his men into three divisions; during the last watch of the night they broke into the camp of the Ammonites and slaughtered them until the heat of the day. Those who survived were scattered, so that no two of them were left together.

column.name: text
column.value: The people then said to Samuel, "Who was it that asked, 'Shall Saul reign over us?' Bring these men to us and we will put them to death."

column.name: text
column.value: But Saul said, "No one shall be put to death today, for this day the LORD has rescued Israel."

column.name: text
column.value: Then Samuel said to the people, "Come, let us go to Gilgal and there reaffirm the kingship."

column.name: text
column.value: So all the people went to Gilgal and confirmed Saul as king in the presence of the LORD. There they sacrificed fellowship offerings before the LORD, and Saul and all the Israelites held a great celebration.

column.name: text
column.value: Samuel said to all Israel, "I have listened to everything you said to me and have set a king over you.

column.name: text
column.value: Now you have a king as your leader. As for me, I am old and gray, and my sons are here with you. I have been your leader from my youth until this day.

column.name: text
column.value: Here I stand. Testify against me in the presence of the LORD and his anointed. Whose ox have I taken? Whose donkey have I taken? Whom have I cheated? Whom have I oppressed? From whose hand have I accepted a bribe to make me shut my eyes? If I have done any of these, I will make it right."

column.name: text
column.value: "You have not cheated or oppressed us," they replied. "You have not taken anything from anyone's hand."

column.name: text
column.value: Samuel said to them, "The LORD is witness against you, and also his anointed is witness this day, that you have not found anything in my hand." "He is witness," they said.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Samuel said to the people, "It is the LORD who appointed Moses and Aaron and brought your forefathers up out of Egypt.

column.name: text
column.value: Now then, stand here, because I am going to confront you with evidence before the LORD as to all the righteous acts performed by the LORD for you and your fathers.

column.name: text
column.value: "After Jacob entered Egypt, they cried to the LORD for help, and the LORD sent Moses and Aaron, who brought your forefathers out of Egypt and settled them in this place.

column.name: text
column.value: "But they forgot the LORD their God; so he sold them into the hand of Sisera, the commander of the army of Hazor, and into the hands of the Philistines and the king of Moab, who fought against them.

column.name: text
column.value: They cried out to the LORD and said, 'We have sinned; we have forsaken the LORD and served the Baals and the Ashtoreths. But now deliver us from the hands of our enemies, and we will serve you.'

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD sent Jerub-Baal, Barak, Jephthah and Samuel, and he delivered you from the hands of your enemies on every side, so that you lived securely.

column.name: text
column.value: "But when you saw that Nahash king of the Ammonites was moving against you, you said to me, 'No, we want a king to rule over us'--even though the LORD your God was your king.

column.name: text
column.value: Now here is the king you have chosen, the one you asked for; see, the LORD has set a king over you.

column.name: text
column.value: If you fear the LORD and serve and obey him and do not rebel against his commands, and if both you and the king who reigns over you follow the LORD your God--good!

column.name: text
column.value: But if you do not obey the LORD, and if you rebel against his commands, his hand will be against you, as it was against your fathers.

column.name: text
column.value: "Now then, stand still and see this great thing the LORD is about to do before your eyes!

column.name: text
column.value: Is it not wheat harvest now? I will call upon the LORD to send thunder and rain. And you will realize what an evil thing you did in the eyes of the LORD when you asked for a king."

column.name: text
column.value: Then Samuel called upon the LORD, and that same day the LORD sent thunder and rain. So all the people stood in awe of the LORD and of Samuel.

column.name: text
column.value: The people all said to Samuel, "Pray to the LORD your God for your servants so that we will not die, for we have added to all our other sins the evil of asking for a king."

column.name: text
column.value: "Do not be afraid," Samuel replied. "You have done all this evil; yet do not turn away from the LORD, but serve the LORD with all your heart.

column.name: text
column.value: Do not turn away after useless idols. They can do you no good, nor can they rescue you, because they are useless.

column.name: text
column.value: For the sake of his great name the LORD will not reject his people, because the LORD was pleased to make you his own.

column.name: text
column.value: As for me, far be it from me that I should sin against the LORD by failing to pray for you. And I will teach you the way that is good and right.

column.name: text
column.value: But be sure to fear the LORD and serve him faithfully with all your heart; consider what great things he has done for you.

column.name: text
column.value: Yet if you persist in doing evil, both you and your king will be swept away."

column.name: text
column.value: Saul was thirty years old when he became king, and he reigned over Israel forty- two years.

column.name: text
column.value: Saul chose three thousand men from Israel; two thousand were with him at Micmash and in the hill country of Bethel, and a thousand were with Jonathan at Gibeah in Benjamin. The rest of the men he sent back to their homes.

column.name: text
column.value: Jonathan attacked the Philistine outpost at Geba, and the Philistines heard about it. Then Saul had the trumpet blown throughout the land and said, "Let the Hebrews hear!"

column.name: text
column.value: So all Israel heard the news: "Saul has attacked the Philistine outpost, and now Israel has become a stench to the Philistines." And the people were summoned to join Saul at Gilgal.

column.name: text
column.value: The Philistines assembled to fight Israel, with three thousand chariots, six thousand charioteers, and soldiers as numerous as the sand on the seashore. They went up and camped at Micmash, east of Beth Aven.

column.name: text
column.value: When the men of Israel saw that their situation was critical and that their army was hard pressed, they hid in caves and thickets, among the rocks, and in pits and cisterns.

column.name: text
column.value: Some Hebrews even crossed the Jordan to the land of Gad and Gilead. Saul remained at Gilgal, and all the troops with him were quaking with fear.

column.name: text
column.value: He waited seven days, the time set by Samuel; but Samuel did not come to Gilgal, and Saul's men began to scatter.

column.name: text
column.value: So he said, "Bring me the burnt offering and the fellowship offerings." And Saul offered up the burnt offering.

column.name: text
column.value: Just as he finished making the offering, Samuel arrived, and Saul went out to greet him.

column.name: text
column.value: "What have you done?" asked Samuel. Saul replied, "When I saw that the men were scattering, and that you did not come at the set time, and that the Philistines were assembling at Micmash,

column.name: text
column.value: I thought, 'Now the Philistines will come down against me at Gilgal, and I have not sought the LORD'S favor.' So I felt compelled to offer the burnt offering."

column.name: text
column.value: "You acted foolishly," Samuel said. "You have not kept the command the LORD your God gave you; if you had, he would have established your kingdom over Israel for all time.

column.name: text
column.value: But now your kingdom will not endure; the LORD has sought out a man after his own heart and appointed him leader of his people, because you have not kept the LORD'S command."

column.name: text
column.value: Then Samuel left Gilgal and went up to Gibeah in Benjamin, and Saul counted the men who were with him. They numbered about six hundred.

column.name: text
column.value: Saul and his son Jonathan and the men with them were staying in Gibeah in Benjamin, while the Philistines camped at Micmash.

column.name: text
column.value: Raiding parties went out from the Philistine camp in three detachments. One turned toward Ophrah in the vicinity of Shual,

column.name: text
column.value: another toward Beth Horon, and the third toward the borderland overlooking the Valley of Zeboim facing the desert.

column.name: text
column.value: Not a blacksmith could be found in the whole land of Israel, because the Philistines had said, "Otherwise the Hebrews will make swords or spears!"

column.name: text
column.value: So all Israel went down to the Philistines to have their plowshares, mattocks, axes and sickles sharpened.

column.name: text
column.value: The price was two thirds of a shekel for sharpening plowshares and mattocks, and a third of a shekel for sharpening forks and axes and for repointing goads.

column.name: text
column.value: So on the day of the battle not a soldier with Saul and Jonathan had a sword or spear in his hand; only Saul and his son Jonathan had them.

column.name: text
column.value: Now a detachment of Philistines had gone out to the pass at Micmash.

column.name: text
column.value: One day Jonathan son of Saul said to the young man bearing his armor, "Come, let's go over to the Philistine outpost on the other side." But he did not tell his father.

column.name: text
column.value: Saul was staying on the outskirts of Gibeah under a pomegranate tree in Migron. With him were about six hundred men,

column.name: text
column.value: among whom was Ahijah, who was wearing an ephod. He was a son of Ichabod's brother Ahitub son of Phinehas, the son of Eli, the LORD'S priest in Shiloh. No one was aware that Jonathan had left.

column.name: text
column.value: On each side of the pass that Jonathan intended to cross to reach the Philistine outpost was a cliff; one was called Bozez, and the other Seneh.

column.name: text
column.value: One cliff stood to the north toward Micmash, the other to the south toward Geba.

column.name: text
column.value: Jonathan said to his young armor-bearer, "Come, let's go over to the outpost of those uncircumcised fellows. Perhaps the LORD will act in our behalf. Nothing can hinder the LORD from saving, whether by many or by few."

column.name: text
column.value: "Do all that you have in mind," his armor-bearer said. "Go ahead; I am with you heart and soul."

column.name: text
column.value: Jonathan said, "Come, then; we will cross over toward the men and let them see us.

column.name: text
column.value: If they say to us, 'Wait there until we come to you,' we will stay where we are and not go up to them.

column.name: text
column.value: But if they say, 'Come up to us,' we will climb up, because that will be our sign that the LORD has given them into our hands."

column.name: text
column.value: So both of them showed themselves to the Philistine outpost. "Look!" said the Philistines. "The Hebrews are crawling out of the holes they were hiding in."

column.name: text
column.value: The men of the outpost shouted to Jonathan and his armor-bearer, "Come up to us and we'll teach you a lesson." So Jonathan said to his armor-bearer, "Climb up after me; the LORD has given them into the hand of Israel."

column.name: text
column.value: Jonathan climbed up, using his hands and feet, with his armor-bearer right behind him. The Philistines fell before Jonathan, and his armor-bearer followed and killed behind him.

column.name: text
column.value: In that first attack Jonathan and his armor-bearer killed some twenty men in an area of about half an acre.

column.name: text
column.value: Then panic struck the whole army--those in the camp and field, and those in the outposts and raiding parties--and the ground shook. It was a panic sent by God.

column.name: text
column.value: Saul's lookouts at Gibeah in Benjamin saw the army melting away in all directions.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Saul said to the men who were with him, "Muster the forces and see who has left us." When they did, it was Jonathan and his armor-bearer who were not there.

column.name: text
column.value: Saul said to Ahijah, "Bring the ark of God." (At that time it was with the Israelites.)

column.name: text
column.value: While Saul was talking to the priest, the tumult in the Philistine camp increased more and more. So Saul said to the priest, "Withdraw your hand."

column.name: text
column.value: Then Saul and all his men assembled and went to the battle. They found the Philistines in total confusion, striking each other with their swords.

column.name: text
column.value: Those Hebrews who had previously been with the Philistines and had gone up with them to their camp went over to the Israelites who were with Saul and Jonathan.

column.name: text
column.value: When all the Israelites who had hidden in the hill country of Ephraim heard that the Philistines were on the run, they joined the battle in hot pursuit.

column.name: text
column.value: So the LORD rescued Israel that day, and the battle moved on beyond Beth Aven.

column.name: text
column.value: Now the men of Israel were in distress that day, because Saul had bound the people under an oath, saying, "Cursed be any man who eats food before evening comes, before I have avenged myself on my enemies!" So none of the troops tasted food.

column.name: text
column.value: The entire army entered the woods, and there was honey on the ground.

column.name: text
