column.value: When they went into the woods, they saw the honey oozing out, yet no one put his hand to his mouth, because they feared the oath.

column.name: text
column.value: But Jonathan had not heard that his father had bound the people with the oath, so he reached out the end of the staff that was in his hand and dipped it into the honeycomb. He raised his hand to his mouth, and his eyes brightened.

column.name: text
column.value: Then one of the soldiers told him, "Your father bound the army under a strict oath, saying, 'Cursed be any man who eats food today!' That is why the men are faint."

column.name: text
column.value: Jonathan said, "My father has made trouble for the country. See how my eyes brightened when I tasted a little of this honey.

column.name: text
column.value: How much better it would have been if the men had eaten today some of the plunder they took from their enemies. Would not the slaughter of the Philistines have been even greater?"

column.name: text
column.value: That day, after the Israelites had struck down the Philistines from Micmash to Aijalon, they were exhausted.

column.name: text
column.value: They pounced on the plunder and, taking sheep, cattle and calves, they butchered them on the ground and ate them, together with the blood.

column.name: text
column.value: Then someone said to Saul, "Look, the men are sinning against the LORD by eating meat that has blood in it." "You have broken faith," he said. "Roll a large stone over here at once."

column.name: text
column.value: Then he said, "Go out among the men and tell them, 'Each of you bring me your cattle and sheep, and slaughter them here and eat them. Do not sin against the LORD by eating meat with blood still in it.'" So everyone brought his ox that night and slaughtered it there.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Saul built an altar to the LORD; it was the first time he had done this.

column.name: text
column.value: Saul said, "Let us go down after the Philistines by night and plunder them till dawn, and let us not leave one of them alive." "Do whatever seems best to you," they replied. But the priest said, "Let us inquire of God here."

column.name: text
column.value: So Saul asked God, "Shall I go down after the Philistines? Will you give them into Israel's hand?" But God did not answer him that day.

column.name: text
column.value: Saul therefore said, "Come here, all you who are leaders of the army, and let us find out what sin has been committed today.

column.name: text
column.value: As surely as the LORD who rescues Israel lives, even if it lies with my son Jonathan, he must die." But not one of the men said a word.

column.name: text
column.value: Saul then said to all the Israelites, "You stand over there; I and Jonathan my son will stand over here." "Do what seems best to you," the men replied.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Saul prayed to the LORD, the God of Israel, "Give me the right answer." And Jonathan and Saul were taken by lot, and the men were cleared.

column.name: text
column.value: Saul said, "Cast the lot between me and Jonathan my son." And Jonathan was taken.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Saul said to Jonathan, "Tell me what you have done." So Jonathan told him, "I merely tasted a little honey with the end of my staff. And now must I die?"

column.name: text
column.value: Saul said, "May God deal with me, be it ever so severely, if you do not die, Jonathan."

column.name: text
column.value: But the men said to Saul, "Should Jonathan die--he who has brought about this great deliverance in Israel? Never! As surely as the LORD lives, not a hair of his head will fall to the ground, for he did this today with God's help." So the men rescued Jonathan, and he was not put to death.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Saul stopped pursuing the Philistines, and they withdrew to their own land.

column.name: text
column.value: After Saul had assumed rule over Israel, he fought against their enemies on every side: Moab, the Ammonites, Edom, the kings of Zobah, and the Philistines. Wherever he turned, he inflicted punishment on them.

column.name: text
column.value: He fought valiantly and defeated the Amalekites, delivering Israel from the hands of those who had plundered them.

column.name: text
column.value: Saul's sons were Jonathan, Ishvi and Malki-Shua. The name of his older daughter was Merab, and that of the younger was Michal.

column.name: text
column.value: His wife's name was Ahinoam daughter of Ahimaaz. The name of the commander of Saul's army was Abner son of Ner, and Ner was Saul's uncle.

column.name: text
column.value: Saul's father Kish and Abner's father Ner were sons of Abiel.

column.name: text
column.value: All the days of Saul there was bitter war with the Philistines, and whenever Saul saw a mighty or brave man, he took him into his service.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD said to Samuel, "How long will you mourn for Saul, since I have rejected him as king over Israel? Fill your horn with oil and be on your way; I am sending you to Jesse of Bethlehem. I have chosen one of his sons to be king."

column.name: text
column.value: But Samuel said, "How can I go? Saul will hear about it and kill me." The LORD said, "Take a heifer with you and say, 'I have come to sacrifice to the LORD.'

column.name: text
column.value: Invite Jesse to the sacrifice, and I will show you what to do. You are to anoint for me the one I indicate."

column.name: text
column.value: Samuel did what the LORD said. When he arrived at Bethlehem, the elders of the town trembled when they met him. They asked, "Do you come in peace?"

column.name: text
column.value: Samuel replied, "Yes, in peace; I have come to sacrifice to the LORD. Consecrate yourselves and come to the sacrifice with me." Then he consecrated Jesse and his sons and invited them to the sacrifice.

column.name: text
column.value: When they arrived, Samuel saw Eliab and thought, "Surely the LORD'S anointed stands here before the LORD."

column.name: text
column.value: But the LORD said to Samuel, "Do not consider his appearance or his height, for I have rejected him. The LORD does not look at the things man looks at. Man looks at the outward appearance, but the LORD looks at the heart."

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jesse called Abinadab and had him pass in front of Samuel. But Samuel said, "The LORD has not chosen this one either."

column.name: text
column.value: Jesse then had Shammah pass by, but Samuel said, "Nor has the LORD chosen this one."

column.name: text
column.value: Jesse had seven of his sons pass before Samuel, but Samuel said to him, "The LORD has not chosen these."

column.name: text
column.value: So he asked Jesse, "Are these all the sons you have?" "There is still the youngest," Jesse answered, "but he is tending the sheep." Samuel said, "Send for him; we will not sit down until he arrives."

column.name: text
column.value: So he sent and had him brought in. He was ruddy, with a fine appearance and handsome features. Then the LORD said, "Rise and anoint him; he is the one."

column.name: text
column.value: So Samuel took the horn of oil and anointed him in the presence of his brothers, and from that day on the Spirit of the LORD came upon David in power. Samuel then went to Ramah.

column.name: text
column.value: Now the Spirit of the LORD had departed from Saul, and an evil spirit from the LORD tormented him.

column.name: text
column.value: Saul's attendants said to him, "See, an evil spirit from God is tormenting you.

column.name: text
column.value: Let our lord command his servants here to search for someone who can play the harp. He will play when the evil spirit from God comes upon you, and you will feel better."

column.name: text
column.value: So Saul said to his attendants, "Find someone who plays well and bring him to me."

column.name: text
column.value: One of the servants answered, "I have seen a son of Jesse of Bethlehem who knows how to play the harp. He is a brave man and a warrior. He speaks well and is a fine-looking man. And the LORD is with him."

column.name: text
column.value: Then Saul sent messengers to Jesse and said, "Send me your son David, who is with the sheep."

column.name: text
column.value: So Jesse took a donkey loaded with bread, a skin of wine and a young goat and sent them with his son David to Saul.

column.name: text
column.value: David came to Saul and entered his service. Saul liked him very much, and David became one of his armor-bearers.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Saul sent word to Jesse, saying, "Allow David to remain in my service, for I am pleased with him."

column.name: text
column.value: Whenever the spirit from God came upon Saul, David would take his harp and play. Then relief would come to Saul; he would feel better, and the evil spirit would leave him.

column.name: text
column.value: Samuel said to Saul, "I am the one the LORD sent to anoint you king over his people Israel; so listen now to the message from the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: This is what the LORD Almighty says: 'I will punish the Amalekites for what they did to Israel when they waylaid them as they came up from Egypt.

column.name: text
column.value: Now go, attack the Amalekites and totally destroy everything that belongs to them. Do not spare them; put to death men and women, children and infants, cattle and sheep, camels and donkeys.'"

column.name: text
column.value: So Saul summoned the men and mustered them at Telaim--two hundred thousand foot soldiers and ten thousand men from Judah.

column.name: text
column.value: Saul went to the city of Amalek and set an ambush in the ravine.

column.name: text
column.value: Then he said to the Kenites, "Go away, leave the Amalekites so that I do not destroy you along with them; for you showed kindness to all the Israelites when they came up out of Egypt." So the Kenites moved away from the Amalekites.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Saul attacked the Amalekites all the way from Havilah to Shur, to the east of Egypt.

column.name: text
column.value: He took Agag king of the Amalekites alive, and all his people he totally destroyed with the sword.

column.name: text
column.value: But Saul and the army spared Agag and the best of the sheep and cattle, the fat calves and lambs--everything that was good. These they were unwilling to destroy completely, but everything that was despised and weak they totally destroyed.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the word of the LORD came to Samuel:

column.name: text
column.value: "I am grieved that I have made Saul king, because he has turned away from me and has not carried out my instructions." Samuel was troubled, and he cried out to the LORD all that night.

column.name: text
column.value: Early in the morning Samuel got up and went to meet Saul, but he was told, "Saul has gone to Carmel. There he has set up a monument in his own honor and has turned and gone on down to Gilgal."

column.name: text
column.value: When Samuel reached him, Saul said, "The LORD bless you! I have carried out the LORD'S instructions."

column.name: text
column.value: But Samuel said, "What then is this bleating of sheep in my ears? What is this lowing of cattle that I hear?"

column.name: text
column.value: Saul answered, "The soldiers brought them from the Amalekites; they spared the best of the sheep and cattle to sacrifice to the LORD your God, but we totally destroyed the rest."

column.name: text
column.value: "Stop!" Samuel said to Saul. "Let me tell you what the LORD said to me last night." "Tell me," Saul replied.

column.name: text
column.value: Samuel said, "Although you were once small in your own eyes, did you not become the head of the tribes of Israel? The LORD anointed you king over Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: And he sent you on a mission, saying, 'Go and completely destroy those wicked people, the Amalekites; make war on them until you have wiped them out.'

column.name: text
column.value: Why did you not obey the LORD? Why did you pounce on the plunder and do evil in the eyes of the LORD?"

column.name: text
column.value: "But I did obey the LORD," Saul said. "I went on the mission the LORD assigned me. I completely destroyed the Amalekites and brought back Agag their king.

column.name: text
column.value: The soldiers took sheep and cattle from the plunder, the best of what was devoted to God, in order to sacrifice them to the LORD your God at Gilgal."

column.name: text
column.value: But Samuel replied: "Does the LORD delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices as much as in obeying the voice of the LORD? To obey is better than sacrifice, and to heed is better than the fat of rams.

column.name: text
column.value: For rebellion is like the sin of divination, and arrogance like the evil of idolatry. Because you have rejected the word of the LORD, he has rejected you as king."

column.name: text
column.value: Then Saul said to Samuel, "I have sinned. I violated the LORD'S command and your instructions. I was afraid of the people and so I gave in to them.

column.name: text
column.value: Now I beg you, forgive my sin and come back with me, so that I may worship the LORD."

column.name: text
column.value: But Samuel said to him, "I will not go back with you. You have rejected the word of the LORD, and the LORD has rejected you as king over Israel!"

column.name: text
column.value: As Samuel turned to leave, Saul caught hold of the hem of his robe, and it tore.

column.name: text
column.value: Samuel said to him, "The LORD has torn the kingdom of Israel from you today and has given it to one of your neighbors--to one better than you.

column.name: text
column.value: He who is the Glory of Israel does not lie or change his mind; for he is not a man, that he should change his mind."

column.name: text
column.value: Saul replied, "I have sinned. But please honor me before the elders of my people and before Israel; come back with me, so that I may worship the LORD your God."

column.name: text
column.value: So Samuel went back with Saul, and Saul worshiped the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Samuel said, "Bring me Agag king of the Amalekites." Agag came to him confidently, thinking, "Surely the bitterness of death is past."

column.name: text
column.value: But Samuel said, "As your sword has made women childless, so will your mother be childless among women." And Samuel put Agag to death before the LORD at Gilgal.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Samuel left for Ramah, but Saul went up to his home in Gibeah of Saul.

column.name: text
column.value: Until the day Samuel died, he did not go to see Saul again, though Samuel mourned for him. And the LORD was grieved that he had made Saul king over Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: After David had finished talking with Saul, Jonathan became one in spirit with David, and he loved him as himself.

column.name: text
column.value: From that day Saul kept David with him and did not let him return to his father's house.

column.name: text
column.value: And Jonathan made a covenant with David because he loved him as himself.

column.name: text
column.value: Jonathan took off the robe he was wearing and gave it to David, along with his tunic, and even his sword, his bow and his belt.

column.name: text
column.value: Whatever Saul sent him to do, David did it so successfully that Saul gave him a high rank in the army. This pleased all the people, and Saul's officers as well.

column.name: text
column.value: When the men were returning home after David had killed the Philistine, the women came out from all the towns of Israel to meet King Saul with singing and dancing, with joyful songs and with tambourines and lutes.

column.name: text
column.value: As they danced, they sang: "Saul has slain his thousands, and David his tens of thousands."

column.name: text
column.value: Saul was very angry; this refrain galled him. "They have credited David with tens of thousands," he thought, "but me with only thousands. What more can he get but the kingdom?"

column.name: text
column.value: And from that time on Saul kept a jealous eye on David.

column.name: text
column.value: The next day an evil spirit from God came forcefully upon Saul. He was prophesying in his house, while David was playing the harp, as he usually did. Saul had a spear in his hand

column.name: text
column.value: and he hurled it, saying to himself, "I'll pin David to the wall." But David eluded him twice.

column.name: text
column.value: Saul was afraid of David, because the LORD was with David but had left Saul.

column.name: text
column.value: So he sent David away from him and gave him command over a thousand men, and David led the troops in their campaigns.

column.name: text
column.value: In everything he did he had great success, because the LORD was with him.

column.name: text
column.value: When Saul saw how successful he was, he was afraid of him.

column.name: text
column.value: But all Israel and Judah loved David, because he led them in their campaigns.

column.name: text
column.value: Saul said to David, "Here is my older daughter Merab. I will give her to you in marriage; only serve me bravely and fight the battles of the LORD." For Saul said to himself, "I will not raise a hand against him. Let the Philistines do that!"

column.name: text
column.value: But David said to Saul, "Who am I, and what is my family or my father's clan in Israel, that I should become the king's son-in-law?"

column.name: text
column.value: So when the time came for Merab, Saul's daughter, to be given to David, she was given in marriage to Adriel of Meholah.

column.name: text
column.value: Now Saul's daughter Michal was in love with David, and when they told Saul about it, he was pleased.

column.name: text
column.value: "I will give her to him," he thought, "so that she may be a snare to him and so that the hand of the Philistines may be against him." So Saul said to David, "Now you have a second opportunity to become my son-in-law."

column.name: text
column.value: Then Saul ordered his attendants: "Speak to David privately and say, 'Look, the king is pleased with you, and his attendants all like you; now become his son-in-law.'"

column.name: text
column.value: They repeated these words to David. But David said, "Do you think it is a small matter to become the king's son-in-law? I'm only a poor man and little known."

column.name: text
column.value: When Saul's servants told him what David had said,

column.name: text
column.value: Saul replied, "Say to David, 'The king wants no other price for the bride than a hundred Philistine foreskins, to take revenge on his enemies.'" Saul's plan was to have David fall by the hands of the Philistines.

column.name: text
column.value: When the attendants told David these things, he was pleased to become the king's son-in-law. So before the allotted time elapsed,

column.name: text
column.value: David and his men went out and killed two hundred Philistines. He brought their foreskins and presented the full number to the king so that he might become the king's son-in-law. Then Saul gave him his daughter Michal in marriage.

column.name: text
column.value: When Saul realized that the LORD was with David and that his daughter Michal loved David,

column.name: text
column.value: Saul became still more afraid of him, and he remained his enemy the rest of his days.

column.name: text
column.value: The Philistine commanders continued to go out to battle, and as often as they did, David met with more success than the rest of Saul's officers, and his name became well known.

column.name: text
column.value: Now the Philistines gathered their forces for war and assembled at Socoh in Judah. They pitched camp at Ephes Dammim, between Socoh and Azekah.

column.name: text
column.value: Saul and the Israelites assembled and camped in the Valley of Elah and drew up their battle line to meet the Philistines.

column.name: text
column.value: The Philistines occupied one hill and the Israelites another, with the valley between them.

column.name: text
column.value: A champion named Goliath, who was from Gath, came out of the Philistine camp. He was over nine feet tall.

column.name: text
column.value: He had a bronze helmet on his head and wore a coat of scale armor of bronze weighing five thousand shekels;

column.name: text
column.value: on his legs he wore bronze greaves, and a bronze javelin was slung on his back.

column.name: text
column.value: His spear shaft was like a weaver's rod, and its iron point weighed six hundred shekels. His shield bearer went ahead of him.

column.name: text
column.value: Goliath stood and shouted to the ranks of Israel, "Why do you come out and line up for battle? Am I not a Philistine, and are you not the servants of Saul? Choose a man and have him come down to me.

column.name: text
column.value: If he is able to fight and kill me, we will become your subjects; but if I overcome him and kill him, you will become our subjects and serve us."

column.name: text
column.value: Then the Philistine said, "This day I defy the ranks of Israel! Give me a man and let us fight each other."

column.name: text
column.value: On hearing the Philistine's words, Saul and all the Israelites were dismayed and terrified.

column.name: text
column.value: Now David was the son of an Ephrathite named Jesse, who was from Bethlehem in Judah. Jesse had eight sons, and in Saul's time he was old and well advanced in years.

column.name: text
column.value: Jesse's three oldest sons had followed Saul to the war: The firstborn was Eliab; the second, Abinadab; and the third, Shammah.

column.name: text
column.value: David was the youngest. The three oldest followed Saul,

column.name: text
column.value: but David went back and forth from Saul to tend his father's sheep at Bethlehem.

column.name: text
column.value: For forty days the Philistine came forward every morning and evening and took his stand.

column.name: text
column.value: Now Jesse said to his son David, "Take this ephah of roasted grain and these ten loaves of bread for your brothers and hurry to their camp.

column.name: text
column.value: Take along these ten cheeses to the commander of their unit. See how your brothers are and bring back some assurance from them.

column.name: text
column.value: They are with Saul and all the men of Israel in the Valley of Elah, fighting against the Philistines."

column.name: text
column.value: Early in the morning David left the flock with a shepherd, loaded up and set out, as Jesse had directed. He reached the camp as the army was going out to its battle positions, shouting the war cry.

column.name: text
column.value: Israel and the Philistines were drawing up their lines facing each other.

column.name: text
column.value: David left his things with the keeper of supplies, ran to the battle lines and greeted his brothers.

column.name: text
column.value: As he was talking with them, Goliath, the Philistine champion from Gath, stepped out from his lines and shouted his usual defiance, and David heard it.

column.name: text
column.value: When the Israelites saw the man, they all ran from him in great fear.

column.name: text
column.value: Now the Israelites had been saying, "Do you see how this man keeps coming out? He comes out to defy Israel. The king will give great wealth to the man who kills him. He will also give him his daughter in marriage and will exempt his father's family from taxes in Israel."

column.name: text
column.value: David asked the men standing near him, "What will be done for the man who kills this Philistine and removes this disgrace from Israel? Who is this uncircumcised Philistine that he should defy the armies of the living God?"

column.name: text
column.value: They repeated to him what they had been saying and told him, "This is what will be done for the man who kills him."

column.name: text
column.value: When Eliab, David's oldest brother, heard him speaking with the men, he burned with anger at him and asked, "Why have you come down here? And with whom did you leave those few sheep in the desert? I know how conceited you are and how wicked your heart is; you came down only to watch the battle."

column.name: text
column.value: "Now what have I done?" said David. "Can't I even speak?"

column.name: text
column.value: He then turned away to someone else and brought up the same matter, and the men answered him as before.

column.name: text
column.value: What David said was overheard and reported to Saul, and Saul sent for him.

column.name: text
column.value: David said to Saul, "Let no one lose heart on account of this Philistine; your servant will go and fight him."

column.name: text
column.value: Saul replied, "You are not able to go out against this Philistine and fight him; you are only a boy, and he has been a fighting man from his youth."

column.name: text
column.value: But David said to Saul, "Your servant has been keeping his father's sheep. When a lion or a bear came and carried off a sheep from the flock,

column.name: text
column.value: I went after it, struck it and rescued the sheep from its mouth. When it turned on me, I seized it by its hair, struck it and killed it.

column.name: text
column.value: Your servant has killed both the lion and the bear; this uncircumcised Philistine will be like one of them, because he has defied the armies of the living God.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD who delivered me from the paw of the lion and the paw of the bear will deliver me from the hand of this Philistine." Saul said to David, "Go, and the LORD be with you."

column.name: text
column.value: Then Saul dressed David in his own tunic. He put a coat of armor on him and a bronze helmet on his head.

column.name: text
column.value: David fastened on his sword over the tunic and tried walking around, because he was not used to them. "I cannot go in these," he said to Saul, "because I am not used to them." So he took them off.

column.name: text
column.value: Then he took his staff in his hand, chose five smooth stones from the stream, put them in the pouch of his shepherd's bag and, with his sling in his hand, approached the Philistine.

column.name: text
column.value: Meanwhile, the Philistine, with his shield bearer in front of him, kept coming closer to David.

column.name: text
column.value: He looked David over and saw that he was only a boy, ruddy and handsome, and he despised him.

column.name: text
column.value: He said to David, "Am I a dog, that you come at me with sticks?" And the Philistine cursed David by his gods.

column.name: text
column.value: "Come here," he said, "and I'll give your flesh to the birds of the air and the beasts of the field!"

column.name: text
column.value: David said to the Philistine, "You come against me with sword and spear and javelin, but I come against you in the name of the LORD Almighty, the God of the armies of Israel, whom you have defied.

column.name: text
column.value: This day the LORD will hand you over to me, and I'll strike you down and cut off your head. Today I will give the carcasses of the Philistine army to the birds of the air and the beasts of the earth, and the whole world will know that there is a God in Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: All those gathered here will know that it is not by sword or spear that the LORD saves; for the battle is the LORD'S, and he will give all of you into our hands."

column.name: text
column.value: As the Philistine moved closer to attack him, David ran quickly toward the battle line to meet him.

column.name: text
column.value: Reaching into his bag and taking out a stone, he slung it and struck the Philistine on the forehead. The stone sank into his forehead, and he fell facedown on the ground.

column.name: text
column.value: So David triumphed over the Philistine with a sling and a stone; without a sword in his hand he struck down the Philistine and killed him.

column.name: text
column.value: David ran and stood over him. He took hold of the Philistine's sword and drew it from the scabbard. After he killed him, he cut off his head with the sword. When the Philistines saw that their hero was dead, they turned and ran.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the men of Israel and Judah surged forward with a shout and pursued the Philistines to the entrance of Gath and to the gates of Ekron. Their dead were strewn along the Shaaraim road to Gath and Ekron.

column.name: text
column.value: When the Israelites returned from chasing the Philistines, they plundered their camp.

column.name: text
column.value: David took the Philistine's head and brought it to Jerusalem, and he put the Philistine's weapons in his own tent.

column.name: text
column.value: As Saul watched David going out to meet the Philistine, he said to Abner, commander of the army, "Abner, whose son is that young man?" Abner replied, "As surely as you live, O king, I don't know."

column.name: text
column.value: The king said, "Find out whose son this young man is."

column.name: text
column.value: As soon as David returned from killing the Philistine, Abner took him and brought him before Saul, with David still holding the Philistine's head.

column.name: text
column.value: "Whose son are you, young man?" Saul asked him. David said, "I am the son of your servant Jesse of Bethlehem."

column.name: text
column.value: Saul told his son Jonathan and all the attendants to kill David. But Jonathan was very fond of David

column.name: text
column.value: and warned him, "My father Saul is looking for a chance to kill you. Be on your guard tomorrow morning; go into hiding and stay there.

column.name: text
column.value: I will go out and stand with my father in the field where you are. I'll speak to him about you and will tell you what I find out."

column.name: text
column.value: Jonathan spoke well of David to Saul his father and said to him, "Let not the king do wrong to his servant David; he has not wronged you, and what he has done has benefited you greatly.

column.name: text
column.value: He took his life in his hands when he killed the Philistine. The LORD won a great victory for all Israel, and you saw it and were glad. Why then would you do wrong to an innocent man like David by killing him for no reason?"

column.name: text
column.value: Saul listened to Jonathan and took this oath: "As surely as the LORD lives, David will not be put to death."

column.name: text
column.value: So Jonathan called David and told him the whole conversation. He brought him to Saul, and David was with Saul as before.

column.name: text
column.value: Once more war broke out, and David went out and fought the Philistines. He struck them with such force that they fled before him.

column.name: text
column.value: But an evil spirit from the LORD came upon Saul as he was sitting in his house with his spear in his hand. While David was playing the harp,

column.name: text
column.value: Saul tried to pin him to the wall with his spear, but David eluded him as Saul drove the spear into the wall. That night David made good his escape.

column.name: text
column.value: Saul sent men to David's house to watch it and to kill him in the morning. But Michal, David's wife, warned him, "If you don't run for your life tonight, tomorrow you'll be killed."

column.name: text
column.value: So Michal let David down through a window, and he fled and escaped.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Michal took an idol and laid it on the bed, covering it with a garment and putting some goats' hair at the head.

column.name: text
column.value: When Saul sent the men to capture David, Michal said, "He is ill."

column.name: text
column.value: Then Saul sent the men back to see David and told them, "Bring him up to me in his bed so that I may kill him."

column.name: text
column.value: But when the men entered, there was the idol in the bed, and at the head was some goats' hair.

column.name: text
column.value: Saul said to Michal, "Why did you deceive me like this and send my enemy away so that he escaped?" Michal told him, "He said to me, 'Let me get away. Why should I kill you?'"

column.name: text
column.value: When David had fled and made his escape, he went to Samuel at Ramah and told him all that Saul had done to him. Then he and Samuel went to Naioth and stayed there.

column.name: text
column.value: Word came to Saul: "David is in Naioth at Ramah";

column.name: text
column.value: so he sent men to capture him. But when they saw a group of prophets prophesying, with Samuel standing there as their leader, the Spirit of God came upon Saul's men and they also prophesied.

column.name: text
column.value: Saul was told about it, and he sent more men, and they prophesied too. Saul sent men a third time, and they also prophesied.

column.name: text
column.value: Finally, he himself left for Ramah and went to the great cistern at Secu. And he asked, "Where are Samuel and David?" "Over in Naioth at Ramah," they said.

column.name: text
column.value: So Saul went to Naioth at Ramah. But the Spirit of God came even upon him, and he walked along prophesying until he came to Naioth.

column.name: text
column.value: He stripped off his robes and also prophesied in Samuel's presence. He lay that way all that day and night. This is why people say, "Is Saul also among the prophets?"

column.name: text
column.value: Then David fled from Naioth at Ramah and went to Jonathan and asked, "What have I done? What is my crime? How have I wronged your father, that he is trying to take my life?"

column.name: text
column.value: "Never!" Jonathan replied. "You are not going to die! Look, my father doesn't do anything, great or small, without confiding in me. Why would he hide this from me? It's not so!"

column.name: text
column.value: But David took an oath and said, "Your father knows very well that I have found favor in your eyes, and he has said to himself, 'Jonathan must not know this or he will be grieved.' Yet as surely as the LORD lives and as you live, there is only a step between me and death."

column.name: text
column.value: Jonathan said to David, "Whatever you want me to do, I'll do for you."

column.name: text
column.value: So David said, "Look, tomorrow is the New Moon festival, and I am supposed to dine with the king; but let me go and hide in the field until the evening of the day after tomorrow.

column.name: text
column.value: If your father misses me at all, tell him, 'David earnestly asked my permission to hurry to Bethlehem, his hometown, because an annual sacrifice is being made there for his whole clan.'

column.name: text
column.value: If he says, 'Very well,' then your servant is safe. But if he loses his temper, you can be sure that he is determined to harm me.

column.name: text
column.value: As for you, show kindness to your servant, for you have brought him into a covenant with you before the LORD. If I am guilty, then kill me yourself! Why hand me over to your father?"

column.name: text
column.value: "Never!" Jonathan said. "If I had the least inkling that my father was determined to harm you, wouldn't I tell you?"

column.name: text
column.value: David asked, "Who will tell me if your father answers you harshly?"

column.name: text
column.value: "Come," Jonathan said, "let's go out into the field." So they went there together.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jonathan said to David: "By the LORD, the God of Israel, I will surely sound out my father by this time the day after tomorrow! If he is favorably disposed toward you, will I not send you word and let you know?

column.name: text
column.value: But if my father is inclined to harm you, may the LORD deal with me, be it ever so severely, if I do not let you know and send you away safely. May the LORD be with you as he has been with my father.

column.name: text
column.value: But show me unfailing kindness like that of the LORD as long as I live, so that I may not be killed,

column.name: text
column.value: and do not ever cut off your kindness from my family--not even when the LORD has cut off every one of David's enemies from the face of the earth."

column.name: text
column.value: So Jonathan made a covenant with the house of David, saying, "May the LORD call David's enemies to account."

column.name: text
column.value: And Jonathan had David reaffirm his oath out of love for him, because he loved him as he loved himself.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jonathan said to David: "Tomorrow is the New Moon festival. You will be missed, because your seat will be empty.

column.name: text
column.value: The day after tomorrow, toward evening, go to the place where you hid when this trouble began, and wait by the stone Ezel.

column.name: text
column.value: I will shoot three arrows to the side of it, as though I were shooting at a target.

column.name: text
column.value: Then I will send a boy and say, 'Go, find the arrows.' If I say to him, 'Look, the arrows are on this side of you; bring them here,' then come, because, as surely as the LORD lives, you are safe; there is no danger.

column.name: text
column.value: But if I say to the boy, 'Look, the arrows are beyond you,' then you must go, because the LORD has sent you away.

column.name: text
column.value: And about the matter you and I discussed--remember, the LORD is witness between you and me forever."

column.name: text
column.value: So David hid in the field, and when the New Moon festival came, the king sat down to eat.

column.name: text
column.value: He sat in his customary place by the wall, opposite Jonathan, and Abner sat next to Saul, but David's place was empty.

column.name: text
column.value: Saul said nothing that day, for he thought, "Something must have happened to David to make him ceremonially unclean--surely he is unclean."

column.name: text
column.value: But the next day, the second day of the month, David's place was empty again. Then Saul said to his son Jonathan, "Why hasn't the son of Jesse come to the meal, either yesterday or today?"

column.name: text
column.value: Jonathan answered, "David earnestly asked me for permission to go to Bethlehem.

column.name: text
column.value: He said, 'Let me go, because our family is observing a sacrifice in the town and my brother has ordered me to be there. If I have found favor in your eyes, let me get away to see my brothers.' That is why he has not come to the king's table."

column.name: text
column.value: Saul's anger flared up at Jonathan and he said to him, "You son of a perverse and rebellious woman! Don't I know that you have sided with the son of Jesse to your own shame and to the shame of the mother who bore you?

column.name: text
column.value: As long as the son of Jesse lives on this earth, neither you nor your kingdom will be established. Now send and bring him to me, for he must die!"

column.name: text
column.value: "Why should he be put to death? What has he done?" Jonathan asked his father.

column.name: text
column.value: But Saul hurled his spear at him to kill him. Then Jonathan knew that his father intended to kill David.

column.name: text
column.value: Jonathan got up from the table in fierce anger; on that second day of the month he did not eat, because he was grieved at his father's shameful treatment of David.

column.name: text
column.value: In the morning Jonathan went out to the field for his meeting with David. He had a small boy with him,

column.name: text
column.value: and he said to the boy, "Run and find the arrows I shoot." As the boy ran, he shot an arrow beyond him.

column.name: text
column.value: When the boy came to the place where Jonathan's arrow had fallen, Jonathan called out after him, "Isn't the arrow beyond you?"

column.name: text
column.value: Then he shouted, "Hurry! Go quickly! Don't stop!" The boy picked up the arrow and returned to his master.

column.name: text
column.value: (The boy knew nothing of all this; only Jonathan and David knew.)

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jonathan gave his weapons to the boy and said, "Go, carry them back to town."

column.name: text
column.value: After the boy had gone, David got up from the south side of the stone and bowed down before Jonathan three times, with his face to the ground. Then they kissed each other and wept together--but David wept the most.

column.name: text
column.value: Jonathan said to David, "Go in peace, for we have sworn friendship with each other in the name of the LORD, saying, 'The LORD is witness between you and me, and between your descendants and my descendants forever.'" Then David left, and Jonathan went back to the town.

column.name: text
column.value: David went to Nob, to Ahimelech the priest. Ahimelech trembled when he met him, and asked, "Why are you alone? Why is no one with you?"

column.name: text
column.value: David answered Ahimelech the priest, "The king charged me with a certain matter and said to me, 'No one is to know anything about your mission and your instructions.' As for my men, I have told them to meet me at a certain place.

column.name: text
column.value: Now then, what do you have on hand? Give me five loaves of bread, or whatever you can find."

column.name: text
column.value: But the priest answered David, "I don't have any ordinary bread on hand; however, there is some consecrated bread here--provided the men have kept themselves from women."

column.name: text
column.value: David replied, "Indeed women have been kept from us, as usual whenever I set out. The men's things are holy even on missions that are not holy. How much more so today!"

column.name: text
column.value: So the priest gave him the consecrated bread, since there was no bread there except the bread of the Presence that had been removed from before the LORD and replaced by hot bread on the day it was taken away.

column.name: text
column.value: Now one of Saul's servants was there that day, detained before the LORD; he was Doeg the Edomite, Saul's head shepherd.

column.name: text
column.value: David asked Ahimelech, "Don't you have a spear or a sword here? I haven't brought my sword or any other weapon, because the king's business was urgent."

column.name: text
column.value: The priest replied, "The sword of Goliath the Philistine, whom you killed in the Valley of Elah, is here; it is wrapped in a cloth behind the ephod. If you want it, take it; there is no sword here but that one." David said, "There is none like it; give it to me."

column.name: text
column.value: That day David fled from Saul and went to Achish king of Gath.

column.name: text
column.value: But the servants of Achish said to him, "Isn't this David, the king of the land? Isn't he the one they sing about in their dances: "'Saul has slain his thousands, and David his tens of thousands'?"

column.name: text
column.value: David took these words to heart and was very much afraid of Achish king of Gath.

column.name: text
column.value: So he pretended to be insane in their presence; and while he was in their hands he acted like a madman, making marks on the doors of the gate and letting saliva run down his beard.

column.name: text
column.value: Achish said to his servants, "Look at the man! He is insane! Why bring him to me?

column.name: text
column.value: Am I so short of madmen that you have to bring this fellow here to carry on like this in front of me? Must this man come into my house?"

column.name: text
column.value: David left Gath and escaped to the cave of Adullam. When his brothers and his father's household heard about it, they went down to him there.

column.name: text
column.value: All those who were in distress or in debt or discontented gathered around him, and he became their leader. About four hundred men were with him.

column.name: text
column.value: From there David went to Mizpah in Moab and said to the king of Moab, "Would you let my father and mother come and stay with you until I learn what God will do for me?"

column.name: text
column.value: So he left them with the king of Moab, and they stayed with him as long as David was in the stronghold.

column.name: text
column.value: But the prophet Gad said to David, "Do not stay in the stronghold. Go into the land of Judah." So David left and went to the forest of Hereth.

column.name: text
column.value: Now Saul heard that David and his men had been discovered. And Saul, spear in hand, was seated under the tamarisk tree on the hill at Gibeah, with all his officials standing around him.

column.name: text
column.value: Saul said to them, "Listen, men of Benjamin! Will the son of Jesse give all of you fields and vineyards? Will he make all of you commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds?

column.name: text
column.value: Is that why you have all conspired against me? No one tells me when my son makes a covenant with the son of Jesse. None of you is concerned about me or tells me that my son has incited my servant to lie in wait for me, as he does today."

column.name: text
column.value: But Doeg the Edomite, who was standing with Saul's officials, said, "I saw the son of Jesse come to Ahimelech son of Ahitub at Nob.

column.name: text
column.value: Ahimelech inquired of the LORD for him; he also gave him provisions and the sword of Goliath the Philistine."

column.name: text
column.value: Then the king sent for the priest Ahimelech son of Ahitub and his father's whole family, who were the priests at Nob, and they all came to the king.

column.name: text
column.value: Saul said, "Listen now, son of Ahitub." "Yes, my lord," he answered.

column.name: text
column.value: Saul said to him, "Why have you conspired against me, you and the son of Jesse, giving him bread and a sword and inquiring of God for him, so that he has rebelled against me and lies in wait for me, as he does today?"

column.name: text
column.value: Ahimelech answered the king, "Who of all your servants is as loyal as David, the king's son-in-law, captain of your bodyguard and highly respected in your household?

column.name: text
column.value: Was that day the first time I inquired of God for him? Of course not! Let not the king accuse your servant or any of his father's family, for your servant knows nothing at all about this whole affair."

column.name: text
column.value: But the king said, "You will surely die, Ahimelech, you and your father's whole family."

column.name: text
column.value: Then the king ordered the guards at his side: "Turn and kill the priests of the LORD, because they too have sided with David. They knew he was fleeing, yet they did not tell me." But the king's officials were not willing to raise a hand to strike the priests of the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: The king then ordered Doeg, "You turn and strike down the priests." So Doeg the Edomite turned and struck them down. That day he killed eighty-five men who wore the linen ephod.

column.name: text
column.value: He also put to the sword Nob, the town of the priests, with its men and women, its children and infants, and its cattle, donkeys and sheep.

column.name: text
column.value: But Abiathar, a son of Ahimelech son of Ahitub, escaped and fled to join David.

column.name: text
column.value: He told David that Saul had killed the priests of the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: Then David said to Abiathar: "That day, when Doeg the Edomite was there, I knew he would be sure to tell Saul. I am responsible for the death of your father's whole family.

column.name: text
column.value: Stay with me; don't be afraid; the man who is seeking your life is seeking mine also. You will be safe with me."

column.name: text
column.value: When David was told, "Look, the Philistines are fighting against Keilah and are looting the threshing floors,"

column.name: text
column.value: he inquired of the LORD, saying, "Shall I go and attack these Philistines?" The LORD answered him, "Go, attack the Philistines and save Keilah."

column.name: text
column.value: But David's men said to him, "Here in Judah we are afraid. How much more, then, if we go to Keilah against the Philistine forces!"

column.name: text
column.value: Once again David inquired of the LORD, and the LORD answered him, "Go down to Keilah, for I am going to give the Philistines into your hand."

column.name: text
column.value: So David and his men went to Keilah, fought the Philistines and carried off their livestock. He inflicted heavy losses on the Philistines and saved the people of Keilah.

column.name: text
column.value: (Now Abiathar son of Ahimelech had brought the ephod down with him when he fled to David at Keilah.)

column.name: text
column.value: Saul was told that David had gone to Keilah, and he said, "God has handed him over to me, for David has imprisoned himself by entering a town with gates and bars."

column.name: text
column.value: And Saul called up all his forces for battle, to go down to Keilah to besiege David and his men.

column.name: text
column.value: When David learned that Saul was plotting against him, he said to Abiathar the priest, "Bring the ephod."

column.name: text
column.value: David said, "O LORD, God of Israel, your servant has heard definitely that Saul plans to come to Keilah and destroy the town on account of me.

column.name: text
column.value: Will the citizens of Keilah surrender me to him? Will Saul come down, as your servant has heard? O LORD, God of Israel, tell your servant." And the LORD said, "He will."

column.name: text
column.value: Again David asked, "Will the citizens of Keilah surrender me and my men to Saul?" And the LORD said, "They will."

column.name: text
column.value: So David and his men, about six hundred in number, left Keilah and kept moving from place to place. When Saul was told that David had escaped from Keilah, he did not go there.

column.name: text
column.value: David stayed in the desert strongholds and in the hills of the Desert of Ziph. Day after day Saul searched for him, but God did not give David into his hands.

column.name: text
column.value: While David was at Horesh in the Desert of Ziph, he learned that Saul had come out to take his life.

column.name: text
column.value: And Saul's son Jonathan went to David at Horesh and helped him find strength in God.

column.name: text
column.value: "Don't be afraid," he said. "My father Saul will not lay a hand on you. You will be king over Israel, and I will be second to you. Even my father Saul knows this."

column.name: text
column.value: The two of them made a covenant before the LORD. Then Jonathan went home, but David remained at Horesh.

column.name: text
column.value: The Ziphites went up to Saul at Gibeah and said, "Is not David hiding among us in the strongholds at Horesh, on the hill of Hakilah, south of Jeshimon?

column.name: text
column.value: Now, O king, come down whenever it pleases you to do so, and we will be responsible for handing him over to the king."

column.name: text
column.value: Saul replied, "The LORD bless you for your concern for me.

column.name: text
column.value: Go and make further preparation. Find out where David usually goes and who has seen him there. They tell me he is very crafty.

column.name: text
column.value: Find out about all the hiding places he uses and come back to me with definite information. Then I will go with you; if he is in the area, I will track him down among all the clans of Judah."

column.name: text
column.value: So they set out and went to Ziph ahead of Saul. Now David and his men were in the Desert of Maon, in the Arabah south of Jeshimon.

column.name: text
column.value: Saul and his men began the search, and when David was told about it, he went down to the rock and stayed in the Desert of Maon. When Saul heard this, he went into the Desert of Maon in pursuit of David.

column.name: text
column.value: Saul was going along one side of the mountain, and David and his men were on the other side, hurrying to get away from Saul. As Saul and his forces were closing in on David and his men to capture them,

column.name: text
column.value: a messenger came to Saul, saying, "Come quickly! The Philistines are raiding the land."

column.name: text
column.value: Then Saul broke off his pursuit of David and went to meet the Philistines. That is why they call this place Sela Hammahlekoth.

column.name: text
column.value: And David went up from there and lived in the strongholds of En Gedi.

column.name: text
column.value: Now Samuel died, and all Israel assembled and mourned for him; and they buried him at his home in Ramah. Then David moved down into the Desert of Maon.

column.name: text
column.value: A certain man in Maon, who had property there at Carmel, was very wealthy. He had a thousand goats and three thousand sheep, which he was shearing in Carmel.

column.name: text
column.value: His name was Nabal and his wife's name was Abigail. She was an intelligent and beautiful woman, but her husband, a Calebite, was surly and mean in his dealings.

column.name: text
column.value: While David was in the desert, he heard that Nabal was shearing sheep.

column.name: text
column.value: So he sent ten young men and said to them, "Go up to Nabal at Carmel and greet him in my name.

column.name: text
column.value: Say to him: 'Long life to you! Good health to you and your household! And good health to all that is yours!

column.name: text
column.value: "'Now I hear that it is sheep-shearing time. When your shepherds were with us, we did not mistreat them, and the whole time they were at Carmel nothing of theirs was missing.

column.name: text
column.value: Ask your own servants and they will tell you. Therefore be favorable toward my young men, since we come at a festive time. Please give your servants and your son David whatever you can find for them.'"

column.name: text
column.value: When David's men arrived, they gave Nabal this message in David's name. Then they waited.

column.name: text
column.value: Nabal answered David's servants, "Who is this David? Who is this son of Jesse? Many servants are breaking away from their masters these days.

column.name: text
column.value: Why should I take my bread and water, and the meat I have slaughtered for my shearers, and give it to men coming from who knows where?"

column.name: text
column.value: David's men turned around and went back. When they arrived, they reported every word.

column.name: text
column.value: David said to his men, "Put on your swords!" So they put on their swords, and David put on his. About four hundred men went up with David, while two hundred stayed with the supplies.

column.name: text
column.value: One of the servants told Nabal's wife Abigail: "David sent messengers from the desert to give our master his greetings, but he hurled insults at them.

column.name: text
column.value: Yet these men were very good to us. They did not mistreat us, and the whole time we were out in the fields near them nothing was missing.

column.name: text
column.value: Night and day they were a wall around us all the time we were herding our sheep near them.

column.name: text
column.value: Now think it over and see what you can do, because disaster is hanging over our master and his whole household. He is such a wicked man that no one can talk to him."

column.name: text
column.value: Abigail lost no time. She took two hundred loaves of bread, two skins of wine, five dressed sheep, five seahs of roasted grain, a hundred cakes of raisins and two hundred cakes of pressed figs, and loaded them on donkeys.

column.name: text
column.value: Then she told her servants, "Go on ahead; I'll follow you." But she did not tell her husband Nabal.

column.name: text
column.value: As she came riding her donkey into a mountain ravine, there were David and his men descending toward her, and she met them.

column.name: text
column.value: David had just said, "It's been useless--all my watching over this fellow's property in the desert so that nothing of his was missing. He has paid me back evil for good.

column.name: text
column.value: May God deal with David, be it ever so severely, if by morning I leave alive one male of all who belong to him!"

column.name: text
column.value: When Abigail saw David, she quickly got off her donkey and bowed down before David with her face to the ground.

column.name: text
column.value: She fell at his feet and said: "My lord, let the blame be on me alone. Please let your servant speak to you; hear what your servant has to say.

column.name: text
column.value: May my lord pay no attention to that wicked man Nabal. He is just like his name--his name is Fool, and folly goes with him. But as for me, your servant, I did not see the men my master sent.

column.name: text
column.value: "Now since the LORD has kept you, my master, from bloodshed and from avenging yourself with your own hands, as surely as the LORD lives and as you live, may your enemies and all who intend to harm my master be like Nabal.

column.name: text
column.value: And let this gift, which your servant has brought to my master, be given to the men who follow you.

column.name: text
column.value: Please forgive your servant's offense, for the LORD will certainly make a lasting dynasty for my master, because he fights the LORD'S battles. Let no wrongdoing be found in you as long as you live.

column.name: text
column.value: Even though someone is pursuing you to take your life, the life of my master will be bound securely in the bundle of the living by the LORD your God. But the lives of your enemies he will hurl away as from the pocket of a sling.

column.name: text
column.value: When the LORD has done for my master every good thing he promised concerning him and has appointed him leader over Israel,

column.name: text
column.value: my master will not have on his conscience the staggering burden of needless bloodshed or of having avenged himself. And when the LORD has brought my master success, remember your servant."

column.name: text
column.value: David said to Abigail, "Praise be to the LORD, the God of Israel, who has sent you today to meet me.

column.name: text
column.value: May you be blessed for your good judgment and for keeping me from bloodshed this day and from avenging myself with my own hands.

column.name: text
column.value: Otherwise, as surely as the LORD, the God of Israel, lives, who has kept me from harming you, if you had not come quickly to meet me, not one male belonging to Nabal would have been left alive by daybreak."

column.name: text
column.value: Then David accepted from her hand what she had brought him and said, "Go home in peace. I have heard your words and granted your request."

column.name: text
column.value: When Abigail went to Nabal, he was in the house holding a banquet like that of a king. He was in high spirits and very drunk. So she told him nothing until daybreak.

column.name: text
column.value: Then in the morning, when Nabal was sober, his wife told him all these things, and his heart failed him and he became like a stone.

column.name: text
column.value: About ten days later, the LORD struck Nabal and he died.

column.name: text
column.value: When David heard that Nabal was dead, he said, "Praise be to the LORD, who has upheld my cause against Nabal for treating me with contempt. He has kept his servant from doing wrong and has brought Nabal's wrongdoing down on his own head." Then David sent word to Abigail, asking her to become his wife.

column.name: text
column.value: His servants went to Carmel and said to Abigail, "David has sent us to you to take you to become his wife."

column.name: text
column.value: She bowed down with her face to the ground and said, "Here is your maidservant, ready to serve you and wash the feet of my master's servants."

column.name: text
column.value: Abigail quickly got on a donkey and, attended by her five maids, went with David's messengers and became his wife.

column.name: text
column.value: David had also married Ahinoam of Jezreel, and they both were his wives.

column.name: text
column.value: But Saul had given his daughter Michal, David's wife, to Paltiel son of Laish, who was from Gallim.

column.name: text
column.value: After Saul returned from pursuing the Philistines, he was told, "David is in the Desert of En Gedi."

column.name: text
column.value: So Saul took three thousand chosen men from all Israel and set out to look for David and his men near the Crags of the Wild Goats.

column.name: text
column.value: He came to the sheep pens along the way; a cave was there, and Saul went in to relieve himself. David and his men were far back in the cave.

column.name: text
column.value: The men said, "This is the day the LORD spoke of when he said to you, 'I will give your enemy into your hands for you to deal with as you wish.'" Then David crept up unnoticed and cut off a corner of Saul's robe.

column.name: text
column.value: Afterward, David was conscience-stricken for having cut off a corner of his robe.

column.name: text
column.value: He said to his men, "The LORD forbid that I should do such a thing to my master, the LORD'S anointed, or lift my hand against him; for he is the anointed of the LORD."

column.name: text
column.value: With these words David rebuked his men and did not allow them to attack Saul. And Saul left the cave and went his way.

column.name: text
column.value: Then David went out of the cave and called out to Saul, "My lord the king!" When Saul looked behind him, David bowed down and prostrated himself with his face to the ground.

column.name: text
column.value: He said to Saul, "Why do you listen when men say, 'David is bent on harming you'?

column.name: text
column.value: This day you have seen with your own eyes how the LORD delivered you into my hands in the cave. Some urged me to kill you, but I spared you; I said, 'I will not lift my hand against my master, because he is the LORD'S anointed.'

column.name: text
column.value: See, my father, look at this piece of your robe in my hand! I cut off the corner of your robe but did not kill you. Now understand and recognize that I am not guilty of wrongdoing or rebellion. I have not wronged you, but you are hunting me down to take my life.

column.name: text
column.value: May the LORD judge between you and me. And may the LORD avenge the wrongs you have done to me, but my hand will not touch you.

column.name: text
column.value: As the old saying goes, 'From evildoers come evil deeds,' so my hand will not touch you.

column.name: text
column.value: "Against whom has the king of Israel come out? Whom are you pursuing? A dead dog? A flea?

column.name: text
column.value: May the LORD be our judge and decide between us. May he consider my cause and uphold it; may he vindicate me by delivering me from your hand."

column.name: text
column.value: When David finished saying this, Saul asked, "Is that your voice, David my son?" And he wept aloud.

column.name: text
column.value: "You are more righteous than I," he said. "You have treated me well, but I have treated you badly.

column.name: text
column.value: You have just now told me of the good you did to me; the LORD delivered me into your hands, but you did not kill me.

column.name: text
column.value: When a man finds his enemy, does he let him get away unharmed? May the LORD reward you well for the way you treated me today.

column.name: text
column.value: I know that you will surely be king and that the kingdom of Israel will be established in your hands.

column.name: text
column.value: Now swear to me by the LORD that you will not cut off my descendants or wipe out my name from my father's family."

column.name: text
column.value: So David gave his oath to Saul. Then Saul returned home, but David and his men went up to the stronghold.

column.name: text
column.value: The Ziphites went to Saul at Gibeah and said, "Is not David hiding on the hill of Hakilah, which faces Jeshimon?"

column.name: text
column.value: So Saul went down to the Desert of Ziph, with his three thousand chosen men of Israel, to search there for David.

column.name: text
column.value: Saul made his camp beside the road on the hill of Hakilah facing Jeshimon, but David stayed in the desert. When he saw that Saul had followed him there,

column.name: text
column.value: he sent out scouts and learned that Saul had definitely arrived.

column.name: text
column.value: Then David set out and went to the place where Saul had camped. He saw where Saul and Abner son of Ner, the commander of the army, had lain down. Saul was lying inside the camp, with the army encamped around him.

column.name: text
column.value: David then asked Ahimelech the Hittite and Abishai son of Zeruiah, Joab's brother, "Who will go down into the camp with me to Saul?" "I'll go with you," said Abishai.

column.name: text
column.value: So David and Abishai went to the army by night, and there was Saul, lying asleep inside the camp with his spear stuck in the ground near his head. Abner and the soldiers were lying around him.

column.name: text
column.value: Abishai said to David, "Today God has delivered your enemy into your hands. Now let me pin him to the ground with one thrust of my spear; I won't strike him twice."

column.name: text
column.value: But David said to Abishai, "Don't destroy him! Who can lay a hand on the LORD'S anointed and be guiltless?

column.name: text
column.value: As surely as the LORD lives," he said, "the LORD himself will strike him; either his time will come and he will die, or he will go into battle and perish.

column.name: text
column.value: But the LORD forbid that I should lay a hand on the LORD'S anointed. Now get the spear and water jug that are near his head, and let's go."

column.name: text
column.value: So David took the spear and water jug near Saul's head, and they left. No one saw or knew about it, nor did anyone wake up. They were all sleeping, because the LORD had put them into a deep sleep.

column.name: text
column.value: Then David crossed over to the other side and stood on top of the hill some distance away; there was a wide space between them.

column.name: text
column.value: He called out to the army and to Abner son of Ner, "Aren't you going to answer me, Abner?" Abner replied, "Who are you who calls to the king?"

column.name: text
column.value: David said, "You're a man, aren't you? And who is like you in Israel? Why didn't you guard your lord the king? Someone came to destroy your lord the king.

column.name: text
column.value: What you have done is not good. As surely as the LORD lives, you and your men deserve to die, because you did not guard your master, the LORD'S anointed. Look around you. Where are the king's spear and water jug that were near his head?"

column.name: text
column.value: Saul recognized David's voice and said, "Is that your voice, David my son?" David replied, "Yes it is, my lord the king."

column.name: text
column.value: And he added, "Why is my lord pursuing his servant? What have I done, and what wrong am I guilty of?

column.name: text
column.value: Now let my lord the king listen to his servant's words. If the LORD has incited you against me, then may he accept an offering. If, however, men have done it, may they be cursed before the LORD! They have now driven me from my share in the LORD'S inheritance and have said, 'Go, serve other gods.'

column.name: text
column.value: Now do not let my blood fall to the ground far from the presence of the LORD. The king of Israel has come out to look for a flea--as one hunts a partridge in the mountains."

column.name: text
column.value: Then Saul said, "I have sinned. Come back, David my son. Because you considered my life precious today, I will not try to harm you again. Surely I have acted like a fool and have erred greatly."

column.name: text
column.value: "Here is the king's spear," David answered. "Let one of your young men come over and get it.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD rewards every man for his righteousness and faithfulness. The LORD delivered you into my hands today, but I would not lay a hand on the LORD'S anointed.

column.name: text
column.value: As surely as I valued your life today, so may the LORD value my life and deliver me from all trouble."

column.name: text
column.value: Then Saul said to David, "May you be blessed, my son David; you will do great things and surely triumph." So David went on his way, and Saul returned home.

column.name: text
column.value: But David thought to himself, "One of these days I will be destroyed by the hand of Saul. The best thing I can do is to escape to the land of the Philistines. Then Saul will give up searching for me anywhere in Israel, and I will slip out of his hand."

column.name: text
column.value: So David and the six hundred men with him left and went over to Achish son of Maoch king of Gath.

column.name: text
column.value: David and his men settled in Gath with Achish. Each man had his family with him, and David had his two wives: Ahinoam of Jezreel and Abigail of Carmel, the widow of Nabal.

column.name: text
column.value: When Saul was told that David had fled to Gath, he no longer searched for him.

column.name: text
column.value: Then David said to Achish, "If I have found favor in your eyes, let a place be assigned to me in one of the country towns, that I may live there. Why should your servant live in the royal city with you?"

column.name: text
column.value: So on that day Achish gave him Ziklag, and it has belonged to the kings of Judah ever since.

column.name: text
column.value: David lived in Philistine territory a year and four months.

column.name: text
column.value: Now David and his men went up and raided the Geshurites, the Girzites and the Amalekites. (From ancient times these peoples had lived in the land extending to Shur and Egypt.)

column.name: text
column.value: Whenever David attacked an area, he did not leave a man or woman alive, but took sheep and cattle, donkeys and camels, and clothes. Then he returned to Achish.

column.name: text
column.value: When Achish asked, "Where did you go raiding today?" David would say, "Against the Negev of Judah" or "Against the Negev of Jerahmeel" or "Against the Negev of the Kenites."

column.name: text
column.value: He did not leave a man or woman alive to be brought to Gath, for he thought, "They might inform on us and say, 'This is what David did.'" And such was his practice as long as he lived in Philistine territory.

column.name: text
column.value: Achish trusted David and said to himself, "He has become so odious to his people, the Israelites, that he will be my servant forever."

column.name: text
column.value: In those days the Philistines gathered their forces to fight against Israel. Achish said to David, "You must understand that you and your men will accompany me in the army."

column.name: text
column.value: David said, "Then you will see for yourself what your servant can do." Achish replied, "Very well, I will make you my bodyguard for life."

column.name: text
column.value: Now Samuel was dead, and all Israel had mourned for him and buried him in his own town of Ramah. Saul had expelled the mediums and spiritists from the land.

column.name: text
column.value: The Philistines assembled and came and set up camp at Shunem, while Saul gathered all the Israelites and set up camp at Gilboa.

column.name: text
column.value: When Saul saw the Philistine army, he was afraid; terror filled his heart.

column.name: text
column.value: He inquired of the LORD, but the LORD did not answer him by dreams or Urim or prophets.

column.name: text
column.value: Saul then said to his attendants, "Find me a woman who is a medium, so I may go and inquire of her." "There is one in Endor," they said.

column.name: text
column.value: So Saul disguised himself, putting on other clothes, and at night he and two men went to the woman. "Consult a spirit for me," he said, "and bring up for me the one I name."

column.name: text
column.value: But the woman said to him, "Surely you know what Saul has done. He has cut off the mediums and spiritists from the land. Why have you set a trap for my life to bring about my death?"

column.name: text
column.value: Saul swore to her by the LORD, "As surely as the LORD lives, you will not be punished for this."

column.name: text
column.value: Then the woman asked, "Whom shall I bring up for you?" "Bring up Samuel," he said.

column.name: text
column.value: When the woman saw Samuel, she cried out at the top of her voice and said to Saul, "Why have you deceived me? You are Saul!"

column.name: text
column.value: The king said to her, "Don't be afraid. What do you see?" The woman said, "I see a spirit coming up out of the ground."

column.name: text
column.value: "What does he look like?" he asked. "An old man wearing a robe is coming up," she said. Then Saul knew it was Samuel, and he bowed down and prostrated himself with his face to the ground.

column.name: text
column.value: Samuel said to Saul, "Why have you disturbed me by bringing me up?" "I am in great distress," Saul said. "The Philistines are fighting against me, and God has turned away from me. He no longer answers me, either by prophets or by dreams. So I have called on you to tell me what to do."

column.name: text
column.value: Samuel said, "Why do you consult me, now that the LORD has turned away from you and become your enemy?

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD has done what he predicted through me. The LORD has torn the kingdom out of your hands and given it to one of your neighbors--to David.

column.name: text
column.value: Because you did not obey the LORD or carry out his fierce wrath against the Amalekites, the LORD has done this to you today.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD will hand over both Israel and you to the Philistines, and tomorrow you and your sons will be with me. The LORD will also hand over the army of Israel to the Philistines."

column.name: text
column.value: Immediately Saul fell full length on the ground, filled with fear because of Samuel's words. His strength was gone, for he had eaten nothing all that day and night.

column.name: text
column.value: When the woman came to Saul and saw that he was greatly shaken, she said, "Look, your maidservant has obeyed you. I took my life in my hands and did what you told me to do.

column.name: text
column.value: Now please listen to your servant and let me give you some food so you may eat and have the strength to go on your way."

column.name: text
column.value: He refused and said, "I will not eat." But his men joined the woman in urging him, and he listened to them. He got up from the ground and sat on the couch.

column.name: text
column.value: The woman had a fattened calf at the house, which she butchered at once. She took some flour, kneaded it and baked bread without yeast.

column.name: text
column.value: Then she set it before Saul and his men, and they ate. That same night they got up and left.

column.name: text
column.value: David and his men reached Ziklag on the third day. Now the Amalekites had raided the Negev and Ziklag. They had attacked Ziklag and burned it,

column.name: text
column.value: and had taken captive the women and all who were in it, both young and old. They killed none of them, but carried them off as they went on their way.

column.name: text
column.value: When David and his men came to Ziklag, they found it destroyed by fire and their wives and sons and daughters taken captive.

column.name: text
column.value: So David and his men wept aloud until they had no strength left to weep.

column.name: text
column.value: David's two wives had been captured--Ahinoam of Jezreel and Abigail, the widow of Nabal of Carmel.

column.name: text
column.value: David was greatly distressed because the men were talking of stoning him; each one was bitter in spirit because of his sons and daughters. But David found strength in the LORD his God.

column.name: text
column.value: Then David said to Abiathar the priest, the son of Ahimelech, "Bring me the ephod." Abiathar brought it to him,

column.name: text
column.value: and David inquired of the LORD, "Shall I pursue this raiding party? Will I overtake them?" "Pursue them," he answered. "You will certainly overtake them and succeed in the rescue."

column.name: text
column.value: David and the six hundred men with him came to the Besor Ravine, where some stayed behind,

column.name: text
column.value: for two hundred men were too exhausted to cross the ravine. But David and four hundred men continued the pursuit.

column.name: text
column.value: They found an Egyptian in a field and brought him to David. They gave him water to drink and food to eat--

column.name: text
column.value: part of a cake of pressed figs and two cakes of raisins. He ate and was revived, for he had not eaten any food or drunk any water for three days and three nights.

column.name: text
column.value: David asked him, "To whom do you belong, and where do you come from?" He said, "I am an Egyptian, the slave of an Amalekite. My master abandoned me when I became ill three days ago.

column.name: text
column.value: We raided the Negev of the Kerethites and the territory belonging to Judah and the Negev of Caleb. And we burned Ziklag."

column.name: text
column.value: David asked him, "Can you lead me down to this raiding party?" He answered, "Swear to me before God that you will not kill me or hand me over to my master, and I will take you down to them."

column.name: text
column.value: He led David down, and there they were, scattered over the countryside, eating, drinking and reveling because of the great amount of plunder they had taken from the land of the Philistines and from Judah.

column.name: text
column.value: David fought them from dusk until the evening of the next day, and none of them got away, except four hundred young men who rode off on camels and fled.

column.name: text
column.value: David recovered everything the Amalekites had taken, including his two wives.

column.name: text
column.value: Nothing was missing: young or old, boy or girl, plunder or anything else they had taken. David brought everything back.

column.name: text
column.value: He took all the flocks and herds, and his men drove them ahead of the other livestock, saying, "This is David's plunder."

column.name: text
column.value: Then David came to the two hundred men who had been too exhausted to follow him and who were left behind at the Besor Ravine. They came out to meet David and the people with him. As David and his men approached, he greeted them.

column.name: text
column.value: But all the evil men and troublemakers among David's followers said, "Because they did not go out with us, we will not share with them the plunder we recovered. However, each man may take his wife and children and go."

column.name: text
column.value: David replied, "No, my brothers, you must not do that with what the LORD has given us. He has protected us and handed over to us the forces that came against us.

column.name: text
column.value: Who will listen to what you say? The share of the man who stayed with the supplies is to be the same as that of him who went down to the battle. All will share alike."

column.name: text
column.value: David made this a statute and ordinance for Israel from that day to this.

column.name: text
column.value: When David arrived in Ziklag, he sent some of the plunder to the elders of Judah, who were his friends, saying, "Here is a present for you from the plunder of the LORD'S enemies."

column.name: text
