column.value: He sent it to those who were in Bethel, Ramoth Negev and Jattir;

column.name: text
column.value: to those in Aroer, Siphmoth, Eshtemoa

column.name: text
column.value: and Racal; to those in the towns of the Jerahmeelites and the Kenites;

column.name: text
column.value: to those in Hormah, Bor Ashan, Athach

column.name: text
column.value: and Hebron; and to those in all the other places where David and his men had roamed.

column.name: text
column.value: The Philistines gathered all their forces at Aphek, and Israel camped by the spring in Jezreel.

column.name: text
column.value: As the Philistine rulers marched with their units of hundreds and thousands, David and his men were marching at the rear with Achish.

column.name: text
column.value: The commanders of the Philistines asked, "What about these Hebrews?" Achish replied, "Is this not David, who was an officer of Saul king of Israel? He has already been with me for over a year, and from the day he left Saul until now, I have found no fault in him."

column.name: text
column.value: But the Philistine commanders were angry with him and said, "Send the man back, that he may return to the place you assigned him. He must not go with us into battle, or he will turn against us during the fighting. How better could he regain his master's favor than by taking the heads of our own men?

column.name: text
column.value: Isn't this the David they sang about in their dances: "'Saul has slain his thousands, and David his tens of thousands'?"

column.name: text
column.value: So Achish called David and said to him, "As surely as the LORD lives, you have been reliable, and I would be pleased to have you serve with me in the army. From the day you came to me until now, I have found no fault in you, but the rulers don't approve of you.

column.name: text
column.value: Turn back and go in peace; do nothing to displease the Philistine rulers."

column.name: text
column.value: "But what have I done?" asked David. "What have you found against your servant from the day I came to you until now? Why can't I go and fight against the enemies of my lord the king?"

column.name: text
column.value: Achish answered, "I know that you have been as pleasing in my eyes as an angel of God; nevertheless, the Philistine commanders have said, 'He must not go up with us into battle.'

column.name: text
column.value: Now get up early, along with your master's servants who have come with you, and leave in the morning as soon as it is light."

column.name: text
column.value: So David and his men got up early in the morning to go back to the land of the Philistines, and the Philistines went up to Jezreel.

column.name: text
column.value: Now the Philistines fought against Israel; the Israelites fled before them, and many fell slain on Mount Gilboa.

column.name: text
column.value: The Philistines pressed hard after Saul and his sons, and they killed his sons Jonathan, Abinadab and Malki-Shua.

column.name: text
column.value: The fighting grew fierce around Saul, and when the archers overtook him, they wounded him critically.

column.name: text
column.value: Saul said to his armor-bearer, "Draw your sword and run me through, or these uncircumcised fellows will come and run me through and abuse me." But his armor-bearer was terrified and would not do it; so Saul took his own sword and fell on it.

column.name: text
column.value: When the armor-bearer saw that Saul was dead, he too fell on his sword and died with him.

column.name: text
column.value: So Saul and his three sons and his armor-bearer and all his men died together that same day.

column.name: text
column.value: When the Israelites along the valley and those across the Jordan saw that the Israelite army had fled and that Saul and his sons had died, they abandoned their towns and fled. And the Philistines came and occupied them.

column.name: text
column.value: The next day, when the Philistines came to strip the dead, they found Saul and his three sons fallen on Mount Gilboa.

column.name: text
column.value: They cut off his head and stripped off his armor, and they sent messengers throughout the land of the Philistines to proclaim the news in the temple of their idols and among their people.

column.name: text
column.value: They put his armor in the temple of the Ashtoreths and fastened his body to the wall of Beth Shan.

column.name: text
column.value: When the people of Jabesh Gilead heard of what the Philistines had done to Saul,

column.name: text
column.value: all their valiant men journeyed through the night to Beth Shan. They took down the bodies of Saul and his sons from the wall of Beth Shan and went to Jabesh, where they burned them.

column.name: text
column.value: Then they took their bones and buried them under a tamarisk tree at Jabesh, and they fasted seven days.

column.name: text
column.value: After the death of Saul, David returned from defeating the Amalekites and stayed in Ziklag two days.

column.name: text
column.value: On the third day a man arrived from Saul's camp, with his clothes torn and with dust on his head. When he came to David, he fell to the ground to pay him honor.

column.name: text
column.value: "Where have you come from?" David asked him. He answered, "I have escaped from the Israelite camp."

column.name: text
column.value: "What happened?" David asked. "Tell me." He said, "The men fled from the battle. Many of them fell and died. And Saul and his son Jonathan are dead."

column.name: text
column.value: Then David said to the young man who brought him the report, "How do you know that Saul and his son Jonathan are dead?"

column.name: text
column.value: "I happened to be on Mount Gilboa," the young man said, "and there was Saul, leaning on his spear, with the chariots and riders almost upon him.

column.name: text
column.value: When he turned around and saw me, he called out to me, and I said, 'What can I do?'

column.name: text
column.value: "He asked me, 'Who are you?' "'An Amalekite,' I answered.

column.name: text
column.value: "Then he said to me, 'Stand over me and kill me! I am in the throes of death, but I'm still alive.'

column.name: text
column.value: "So I stood over him and killed him, because I knew that after he had fallen he could not survive. And I took the crown that was on his head and the band on his arm and have brought them here to my lord."

column.name: text
column.value: Then David and all the men with him took hold of their clothes and tore them.

column.name: text
column.value: They mourned and wept and fasted till evening for Saul and his son Jonathan, and for the army of the LORD and the house of Israel, because they had fallen by the sword.

column.name: text
column.value: David said to the young man who brought him the report, "Where are you from?" "I am the son of an alien, an Amalekite," he answered.

column.name: text
column.value: David asked him, "Why were you not afraid to lift your hand to destroy the LORD'S anointed?"

column.name: text
column.value: Then David called one of his men and said, "Go, strike him down!" So he struck him down, and he died.

column.name: text
column.value: For David had said to him, "Your blood be on your own head. Your own mouth testified against you when you said, 'I killed the LORD'S anointed.'"

column.name: text
column.value: David took up this lament concerning Saul and his son Jonathan,

column.name: text
column.value: and ordered that the men of Judah be taught this lament of the bow (it is written in the Book of Jashar):

column.name: text
column.value: "Your glory, O Israel, lies slain on your heights. How the mighty have fallen!

column.name: text
column.value: "Tell it not in Gath, proclaim it not in the streets of Ashkelon, lest the daughters of the Philistines be glad, lest the daughters of the uncircumcised rejoice.

column.name: text
column.value: "O mountains of Gilboa, may you have neither dew nor rain, nor fields that yield offerings of grain. For there the shield of the mighty was defiled, the shield of Saul--no longer rubbed with oil.

column.name: text
column.value: From the blood of the slain, from the flesh of the mighty, the bow of Jonathan did not turn back, the sword of Saul did not return unsatisfied.

column.name: text
column.value: "Saul and Jonathan--in life they were loved and gracious, and in death they were not parted. They were swifter than eagles, they were stronger than lions.

column.name: text
column.value: "O daughters of Israel, weep for Saul, who clothed you in scarlet and finery, who adorned your garments with ornaments of gold.

column.name: text
column.value: "How the mighty have fallen in battle! Jonathan lies slain on your heights.

column.name: text
column.value: I grieve for you, Jonathan my brother; you were very dear to me. Your love for me was wonderful, more wonderful than that of women.

column.name: text
column.value: "How the mighty have fallen! The weapons of war have perished!"

column.name: text
column.value: In the course of time, David inquired of the LORD. "Shall I go up to one of the towns of Judah?" he asked. The LORD said, "Go up." David asked, "Where shall I go?" "To Hebron," the LORD answered.

column.name: text
column.value: So David went up there with his two wives, Ahinoam of Jezreel and Abigail, the widow of Nabal of Carmel.

column.name: text
column.value: David also took the men who were with him, each with his family, and they settled in Hebron and its towns.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the men of Judah came to Hebron and there they anointed David king over the house of Judah. When David was told that it was the men of Jabesh Gilead who had buried Saul,

column.name: text
column.value: he sent messengers to the men of Jabesh Gilead to say to them, "The LORD bless you for showing this kindness to Saul your master by burying him.

column.name: text
column.value: May the LORD now show you kindness and faithfulness, and I too will show you the same favor because you have done this.

column.name: text
column.value: Now then, be strong and brave, for Saul your master is dead, and the house of Judah has anointed me king over them."

column.name: text
column.value: Meanwhile, Abner son of Ner, the commander of Saul's army, had taken Ish-Bosheth son of Saul and brought him over to Mahanaim.

column.name: text
column.value: He made him king over Gilead, Ashuri and Jezreel, and also over Ephraim, Benjamin and all Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: Ish-Bosheth son of Saul was forty years old when he became king over Israel, and he reigned two years. The house of Judah, however, followed David.

column.name: text
column.value: The length of time David was king in Hebron over the house of Judah was seven years and six months.

column.name: text
column.value: Abner son of Ner, together with the men of Ish-Bosheth son of Saul, left Mahanaim and went to Gibeon.

column.name: text
column.value: Joab son of Zeruiah and David's men went out and met them at the pool of Gibeon. One group sat down on one side of the pool and one group on the other side.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Abner said to Joab, "Let's have some of the young men get up and fight hand to hand in front of us." "All right, let them do it," Joab said.

column.name: text
column.value: So they stood up and were counted off--twelve men for Benjamin and Ish-Bosheth son of Saul, and twelve for David.

column.name: text
column.value: Then each man grabbed his opponent by the head and thrust his dagger into his opponent's side, and they fell down together. So that place in Gibeon was called Helkath Hazzurim.

column.name: text
column.value: The battle that day was very fierce, and Abner and the men of Israel were defeated by David's men.

column.name: text
column.value: The three sons of Zeruiah were there: Joab, Abishai and Asahel. Now Asahel was as fleet-footed as a wild gazelle.

column.name: text
column.value: He chased Abner, turning neither to the right nor to the left as he pursued him.

column.name: text
column.value: Abner looked behind him and asked, "Is that you, Asahel?" "It is," he answered.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Abner said to him, "Turn aside to the right or to the left; take on one of the young men and strip him of his weapons." But Asahel would not stop chasing him.

column.name: text
column.value: Again Abner warned Asahel, "Stop chasing me! Why should I strike you down? How could I look your brother Joab in the face?"

column.name: text
column.value: But Asahel refused to give up the pursuit; so Abner thrust the butt of his spear into Asahel's stomach, and the spear came out through his back. He fell there and died on the spot. And every man stopped when he came to the place where Asahel had fallen and died.

column.name: text
column.value: But Joab and Abishai pursued Abner, and as the sun was setting, they came to the hill of Ammah, near Giah on the way to the wasteland of Gibeon.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the men of Benjamin rallied behind Abner. They formed themselves into a group and took their stand on top of a hill.

column.name: text
column.value: Abner called out to Joab, "Must the sword devour forever? Don't you realize that this will end in bitterness? How long before you order your men to stop pursuing their brothers?"

column.name: text
column.value: Joab answered, "As surely as God lives, if you had not spoken, the men would have continued the pursuit of their brothers until morning."

column.name: text
column.value: So Joab blew the trumpet, and all the men came to a halt; they no longer pursued Israel, nor did they fight anymore.

column.name: text
column.value: All that night Abner and his men marched through the Arabah. They crossed the Jordan, continued through the whole Bithron and came to Mahanaim.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Joab returned from pursuing Abner and assembled all his men. Besides Asahel, nineteen of David's men were found missing.

column.name: text
column.value: But David's men had killed three hundred and sixty Benjamites who were with Abner.

column.name: text
column.value: They took Asahel and buried him in his father's tomb at Bethlehem. Then Joab and his men marched all night and arrived at Hebron by daybreak.

column.name: text
column.value: When Ish-Bosheth son of Saul heard that Abner had died in Hebron, he lost courage, and all Israel became alarmed.

column.name: text
column.value: Now Saul's son had two men who were leaders of raiding bands. One was named Baanah and the other Recab; they were sons of Rimmon the Beerothite from the tribe of Benjamin--Beeroth is considered part of Benjamin,

column.name: text
column.value: because the people of Beeroth fled to Gittaim and have lived there as aliens to this day.

column.name: text
column.value: (Jonathan son of Saul had a son who was lame in both feet. He was five years old when the news about Saul and Jonathan came from Jezreel. His nurse picked him up and fled, but as she hurried to leave, he fell and became crippled. His name was Mephibosheth.)

column.name: text
column.value: Now Recab and Baanah, the sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, set out for the house of Ish-Bosheth, and they arrived there in the heat of the day while he was taking his noonday rest.

column.name: text
column.value: They went into the inner part of the house as if to get some wheat, and they stabbed him in the stomach. Then Recab and his brother Baanah slipped away.

column.name: text
column.value: They had gone into the house while he was lying on the bed in his bedroom. After they stabbed and killed him, they cut off his head. Taking it with them, they traveled all night by way of the Arabah.

column.name: text
column.value: They brought the head of Ish-Bosheth to David at Hebron and said to the king, "Here is the head of Ish-Bosheth son of Saul, your enemy, who tried to take your life. This day the LORD has avenged my lord the king against Saul and his offspring."

column.name: text
column.value: David answered Recab and his brother Baanah, the sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, "As surely as the LORD lives, who has delivered me out of all trouble,

column.name: text
column.value: when a man told me, 'Saul is dead,' and thought he was bringing good news, I seized him and put him to death in Ziklag. That was the reward I gave him for his news!

column.name: text
column.value: How much more--when wicked men have killed an innocent man in his own house and on his own bed--should I not now demand his blood from your hand and rid the earth of you!"

column.name: text
column.value: So David gave an order to his men, and they killed them. They cut off their hands and feet and hung the bodies by the pool in Hebron. But they took the head of Ish-Bosheth and buried it in Abner's tomb at Hebron.

column.name: text
column.value: The war between the house of Saul and the house of David lasted a long time. David grew stronger and stronger, while the house of Saul grew weaker and weaker.

column.name: text
column.value: Sons were born to David in Hebron: His firstborn was Amnon the son of Ahinoam of Jezreel;

column.name: text
column.value: his second, Kileab the son of Abigail the widow of Nabal of Carmel; the third, Absalom the son of Maacah daughter of Talmai king of Geshur;

column.name: text
column.value: the fourth, Adonijah the son of Haggith; the fifth, Shephatiah the son of Abital;

column.name: text
column.value: and the sixth, Ithream the son of David's wife Eglah. These were born to David in Hebron.

column.name: text
column.value: During the war between the house of Saul and the house of David, Abner had been strengthening his own position in the house of Saul.

column.name: text
column.value: Now Saul had had a concubine named Rizpah daughter of Aiah. And Ish-Bosheth said to Abner, "Why did you sleep with my father's concubine?"

column.name: text
column.value: Abner was very angry because of what Ish-Bosheth said and he answered, "Am I a dog's head--on Judah's side? This very day I am loyal to the house of your father Saul and to his family and friends. I haven't handed you over to David. Yet now you accuse me of an offense involving this woman!

column.name: text
column.value: May God deal with Abner, be it ever so severely, if I do not do for David what the LORD promised him on oath

column.name: text
column.value: and transfer the kingdom from the house of Saul and establish David's throne over Israel and Judah from Dan to Beersheba."

column.name: text
column.value: Ish-Bosheth did not dare to say another word to Abner, because he was afraid of him.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Abner sent messengers on his behalf to say to David, "Whose land is it? Make an agreement with me, and I will help you bring all Israel over to you."

column.name: text
column.value: "Good," said David. "I will make an agreement with you. But I demand one thing of you: Do not come into my presence unless you bring Michal daughter of Saul when you come to see me."

column.name: text
column.value: Then David sent messengers to Ish-Bosheth son of Saul, demanding, "Give me my wife Michal, whom I betrothed to myself for the price of a hundred Philistine foreskins."

column.name: text
column.value: So Ish-Bosheth gave orders and had her taken away from her husband Paltiel son of Laish.

column.name: text
column.value: Her husband, however, went with her, weeping behind her all the way to Bahurim. Then Abner said to him, "Go back home!" So he went back.

column.name: text
column.value: Abner conferred with the elders of Israel and said, "For some time you have wanted to make David your king.

column.name: text
column.value: Now do it! For the LORD promised David, 'By my servant David I will rescue my people Israel from the hand of the Philistines and from the hand of all their enemies.'"

column.name: text
column.value: Abner also spoke to the Benjamites in person. Then he went to Hebron to tell David everything that Israel and the whole house of Benjamin wanted to do.

column.name: text
column.value: When Abner, who had twenty men with him, came to David at Hebron, David prepared a feast for him and his men.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Abner said to David, "Let me go at once and assemble all Israel for my lord the king, so that they may make a compact with you, and that you may rule over all that your heart desires." So David sent Abner away, and he went in peace.

column.name: text
column.value: Just then David's men and Joab returned from a raid and brought with them a great deal of plunder. But Abner was no longer with David in Hebron, because David had sent him away, and he had gone in peace.

column.name: text
column.value: When Joab and all the soldiers with him arrived, he was told that Abner son of Ner had come to the king and that the king had sent him away and that he had gone in peace.

column.name: text
column.value: So Joab went to the king and said, "What have you done? Look, Abner came to you. Why did you let him go? Now he is gone!

column.name: text
column.value: You know Abner son of Ner; he came to deceive you and observe your movements and find out everything you are doing."

column.name: text
column.value: Joab then left David and sent messengers after Abner, and they brought him back from the well of Sirah. But David did not know it.

column.name: text
column.value: Now when Abner returned to Hebron, Joab took him aside into the gateway, as though to speak with him privately. And there, to avenge the blood of his brother Asahel, Joab stabbed him in the stomach, and he died.

column.name: text
column.value: Later, when David heard about this, he said, "I and my kingdom are forever innocent before the LORD concerning the blood of Abner son of Ner.

column.name: text
column.value: May his blood fall upon the head of Joab and upon all his father's house! May Joab's house never be without someone who has a running sore or leprosy or who leans on a crutch or who falls by the sword or who lacks food."

column.name: text
column.value: (Joab and his brother Abishai murdered Abner because he had killed their brother Asahel in the battle at Gibeon.)

column.name: text
column.value: Then David said to Joab and all the people with him, "Tear your clothes and put on sackcloth and walk in mourning in front of Abner." King David himself walked behind the bier.

column.name: text
column.value: They buried Abner in Hebron, and the king wept aloud at Abner's tomb. All the people wept also.

column.name: text
column.value: The king sang this lament for Abner: "Should Abner have died as the lawless die?

column.name: text
column.value: Your hands were not bound, your feet were not fettered. You fell as one falls before wicked men." And all the people wept over him again.

column.name: text
column.value: Then they all came and urged David to eat something while it was still day; but David took an oath, saying, "May God deal with me, be it ever so severely, if I taste bread or anything else before the sun sets!"

column.name: text
column.value: All the people took note and were pleased; indeed, everything the king did pleased them.

column.name: text
column.value: So on that day all the people and all Israel knew that the king had no part in the murder of Abner son of Ner.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the king said to his men, "Do you not realize that a prince and a great man has fallen in Israel this day?

column.name: text
column.value: And today, though I am the anointed king, I am weak, and these sons of Zeruiah are too strong for me. May the LORD repay the evildoer according to his evil deeds!"

column.name: text
column.value: All the tribes of Israel came to David at Hebron and said, "We are your own flesh and blood.

column.name: text
column.value: In the past, while Saul was king over us, you were the one who led Israel on their military campaigns. And the LORD said to you, 'You will shepherd my people Israel, and you will become their ruler.'"

column.name: text
column.value: When all the elders of Israel had come to King David at Hebron, the king made a compact with them at Hebron before the LORD, and they anointed David king over Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: David was thirty years old when he became king, and he reigned forty years.

column.name: text
column.value: In Hebron he reigned over Judah seven years and six months, and in Jerusalem he reigned over all Israel and Judah thirty-three years.

column.name: text
column.value: The king and his men marched to Jerusalem to attack the Jebusites, who lived there. The Jebusites said to David, "You will not get in here; even the blind and the lame can ward you off." They thought, "David cannot get in here."

column.name: text
column.value: Nevertheless, David captured the fortress of Zion, the City of David.

column.name: text
column.value: On that day, David said, "Anyone who conquers the Jebusites will have to use the water shaft to reach those 'lame and blind' who are David's enemies." That is why they say, "The 'blind and lame' will not enter the palace."

column.name: text
column.value: David then took up residence in the fortress and called it the City of David. He built up the area around it, from the supporting terraces inward.

column.name: text
column.value: And he became more and more powerful, because the LORD God Almighty was with him.

column.name: text
column.value: Now Hiram king of Tyre sent messengers to David, along with cedar logs and carpenters and stonemasons, and they built a palace for David.

column.name: text
column.value: And David knew that the LORD had established him as king over Israel and had exalted his kingdom for the sake of his people Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: After he left Hebron, David took more concubines and wives in Jerusalem, and more sons and daughters were born to him.

column.name: text
column.value: These are the names of the children born to him there: Shammua, Shobab, Nathan, Solomon,

column.name: text
column.value: Ibhar, Elishua, Nepheg, Japhia,

column.name: text
column.value: Elishama, Eliada and Eliphelet.

column.name: text
column.value: When the Philistines heard that David had been anointed king over Israel, they went up in full force to search for him, but David heard about it and went down to the stronghold.

column.name: text
column.value: Now the Philistines had come and spread out in the Valley of Rephaim;

column.name: text
column.value: so David inquired of the LORD, "Shall I go and attack the Philistines? Will you hand them over to me?" The LORD answered him, "Go, for I will surely hand the Philistines over to you."

column.name: text
column.value: So David went to Baal Perazim, and there he defeated them. He said, "As waters break out, the LORD has broken out against my enemies before me." So that place was called Baal Perazim.

column.name: text
column.value: The Philistines abandoned their idols there, and David and his men carried them off.

column.name: text
column.value: Once more the Philistines came up and spread out in the Valley of Rephaim;

column.name: text
column.value: so David inquired of the LORD, and he answered, "Do not go straight up, but circle around behind them and attack them in front of the balsam trees.

column.name: text
column.value: As soon as you hear the sound of marching in the tops of the balsam trees, move quickly, because that will mean the LORD has gone out in front of you to strike the Philistine army."

column.name: text
column.value: So David did as the LORD commanded him, and he struck down the Philistines all the way from Gibeon to Gezer.

column.name: text
column.value: David again brought together out of Israel chosen men, thirty thousand in all.

column.name: text
column.value: He and all his men set out from Baalah of Judah to bring up from there the ark of God, which is called by the Name, the name of the LORD Almighty, who is enthroned between the cherubim that are on the ark.

column.name: text
column.value: They set the ark of God on a new cart and brought it from the house of Abinadab, which was on the hill. Uzzah and Ahio, sons of Abinadab, were guiding the new cart

column.name: text
column.value: with the ark of God on it, and Ahio was walking in front of it.

column.name: text
column.value: David and the whole house of Israel were celebrating with all their might before the LORD, with songs and with harps, lyres, tambourines, sistrums and cymbals.

column.name: text
column.value: When they came to the threshing floor of Nacon, Uzzah reached out and took hold of the ark of God, because the oxen stumbled.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD'S anger burned against Uzzah because of his irreverent act; therefore God struck him down and he died there beside the ark of God.

column.name: text
column.value: Then David was angry because the LORD'S wrath had broken out against Uzzah, and to this day that place is called Perez Uzzah.

column.name: text
column.value: David was afraid of the LORD that day and said, "How can the ark of the LORD ever come to me?"

column.name: text
column.value: He was not willing to take the ark of the LORD to be with him in the City of David. Instead, he took it aside to the house of Obed-Edom the Gittite.

column.name: text
column.value: The ark of the LORD remained in the house of Obed-Edom the Gittite for three months, and the LORD blessed him and his entire household.

column.name: text
column.value: Now King David was told, "The LORD has blessed the household of Obed-Edom and everything he has, because of the ark of God." So David went down and brought up the ark of God from the house of Obed-Edom to the City of David with rejoicing.

column.name: text
column.value: When those who were carrying the ark of the LORD had taken six steps, he sacrificed a bull and a fattened calf.

column.name: text
column.value: David, wearing a linen ephod, danced before the LORD with all his might,

column.name: text
column.value: while he and the entire house of Israel brought up the ark of the LORD with shouts and the sound of trumpets.

column.name: text
column.value: As the ark of the LORD was entering the City of David, Michal daughter of Saul watched from a window. And when she saw King David leaping and dancing before the LORD, she despised him in her heart.

column.name: text
column.value: They brought the ark of the LORD and set it in its place inside the tent that David had pitched for it, and David sacrificed burnt offerings and fellowship offerings before the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: After he had finished sacrificing the burnt offerings and fellowship offerings, he blessed the people in the name of the LORD Almighty.

column.name: text
column.value: Then he gave a loaf of bread, a cake of dates and a cake of raisins to each person in the whole crowd of Israelites, both men and women. And all the people went to their homes.

column.name: text
column.value: When David returned home to bless his household, Michal daughter of Saul came out to meet him and said, "How the king of Israel has distinguished himself today, disrobing in the sight of the slave girls of his servants as any vulgar fellow would!"

column.name: text
column.value: David said to Michal, "It was before the LORD, who chose me rather than your father or anyone from his house when he appointed me ruler over the LORD'S people Israel--I will celebrate before the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: I will become even more undignified than this, and I will be humiliated in my own eyes. But by these slave girls you spoke of, I will be held in honor."

column.name: text
column.value: And Michal daughter of Saul had no children to the day of her death.

column.name: text
column.value: After the king was settled in his palace and the LORD had given him rest from all his enemies around him,

column.name: text
column.value: he said to Nathan the prophet, "Here I am, living in a palace of cedar, while the ark of God remains in a tent."

column.name: text
column.value: Nathan replied to the king, "Whatever you have in mind, go ahead and do it, for the LORD is with you."

column.name: text
column.value: That night the word of the LORD came to Nathan, saying:

column.name: text
column.value: "Go and tell my servant David, 'This is what the LORD says: Are you the one to build me a house to dwell in?

column.name: text
column.value: I have not dwelt in a house from the day I brought the Israelites up out of Egypt to this day. I have been moving from place to place with a tent as my dwelling.

column.name: text
column.value: Wherever I have moved with all the Israelites, did I ever say to any of their rulers whom I commanded to shepherd my people Israel, "Why have you not built me a house of cedar?" '

column.name: text
column.value: "Now then, tell my servant David, 'This is what the LORD Almighty says: I took you from the pasture and from following the flock to be ruler over my people Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: I have been with you wherever you have gone, and I have cut off all your enemies from before you. Now I will make your name great, like the names of the greatest men of the earth.

column.name: text
column.value: And I will provide a place for my people Israel and will plant them so that they can have a home of their own and no longer be disturbed. Wicked people will not oppress them anymore, as they did at the beginning

column.name: text
column.value: and have done ever since the time I appointed leaders over my people Israel. I will also give you rest from all your enemies. "'The LORD declares to you that the LORD himself will establish a house for you:

column.name: text
column.value: When your days are over and you rest with your fathers, I will raise up your offspring to succeed you, who will come from your own body, and I will establish his kingdom.

column.name: text
column.value: He is the one who will build a house for my Name, and I will establish the throne of his kingdom forever.

column.name: text
column.value: I will be his father, and he will be my son. When he does wrong, I will punish him with the rod of men, with floggings inflicted by men.

column.name: text
column.value: But my love will never be taken away from him, as I took it away from Saul, whom I removed from before you.

column.name: text
column.value: Your house and your kingdom will endure forever before me; your throne will be established forever.'"

column.name: text
column.value: Nathan reported to David all the words of this entire revelation.

column.name: text
column.value: Then King David went in and sat before the LORD, and he said: "Who am I, O Sovereign LORD, and what is my family, that you have brought me this far?

column.name: text
column.value: And as if this were not enough in your sight, O Sovereign LORD, you have also spoken about the future of the house of your servant. Is this your usual way of dealing with man, O Sovereign LORD?

column.name: text
column.value: "What more can David say to you? For you know your servant, O Sovereign LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: For the sake of your word and according to your will, you have done this great thing and made it known to your servant.

column.name: text
column.value: "How great you are, O Sovereign LORD! There is no one like you, and there is no God but you, as we have heard with our own ears.

column.name: text
column.value: And who is like your people Israel--the one nation on earth that God went out to redeem as a people for himself, and to make a name for himself, and to perform great and awesome wonders by driving out nations and their gods from before your people, whom you redeemed from Egypt?

column.name: text
column.value: You have established your people Israel as your very own forever, and you, O LORD, have become their God.

column.name: text
column.value: "And now, LORD God, keep forever the promise you have made concerning your servant and his house. Do as you promised,

column.name: text
column.value: so that your name will be great forever. Then men will say, 'The LORD Almighty is God over Israel!' And the house of your servant David will be established before you.

column.name: text
column.value: "O LORD Almighty, God of Israel, you have revealed this to your servant, saying, 'I will build a house for you.' So your servant has found courage to offer you this prayer.

column.name: text
column.value: O Sovereign LORD, you are God! Your words are trustworthy, and you have promised these good things to your servant.

column.name: text
column.value: Now be pleased to bless the house of your servant, that it may continue forever in your sight; for you, O Sovereign LORD, have spoken, and with your blessing the house of your servant will be blessed forever."

column.name: text
column.value: In the course of time, the king of the Ammonites died, and his son Hanun succeeded him as king.

column.name: text
column.value: David thought, "I will show kindness to Hanun son of Nahash, just as his father showed kindness to me." So David sent a delegation to express his sympathy to Hanun concerning his father. When David's men came to the land of the Ammonites,

column.name: text
column.value: the Ammonite nobles said to Hanun their lord, "Do you think David is honoring your father by sending men to you to express sympathy? Hasn't David sent them to you to explore the city and spy it out and overthrow it?"

column.name: text
column.value: So Hanun seized David's men, shaved off half of each man's beard, cut off their garments in the middle at the buttocks, and sent them away.

column.name: text
column.value: When David was told about this, he sent messengers to meet the men, for they were greatly humiliated. The king said, "Stay at Jericho till your beards have grown, and then come back."

column.name: text
column.value: When the Ammonites realized that they had become a stench in David's nostrils, they hired twenty thousand Aramean foot soldiers from Beth Rehob and Zobah, as well as the king of Maacah with a thousand men, and also twelve thousand men from Tob.

column.name: text
column.value: On hearing this, David sent Joab out with the entire army of fighting men.

column.name: text
column.value: The Ammonites came out and drew up in battle formation at the entrance to their city gate, while the Arameans of Zobah and Rehob and the men of Tob and Maacah were by themselves in the open country.

column.name: text
column.value: Joab saw that there were battle lines in front of him and behind him; so he selected some of the best troops in Israel and deployed them against the Arameans.

column.name: text
column.value: He put the rest of the men under the command of Abishai his brother and deployed them against the Ammonites.

column.name: text
column.value: Joab said, "If the Arameans are too strong for me, then you are to come to my rescue; but if the Ammonites are too strong for you, then I will come to rescue you.

column.name: text
column.value: Be strong and let us fight bravely for our people and the cities of our God. The LORD will do what is good in his sight."

column.name: text
column.value: Then Joab and the troops with him advanced to fight the Arameans, and they fled before him.

column.name: text
column.value: When the Ammonites saw that the Arameans were fleeing, they fled before Abishai and went inside the city. So Joab returned from fighting the Ammonites and came to Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: After the Arameans saw that they had been routed by Israel, they regrouped.

column.name: text
column.value: Hadadezer had Arameans brought from beyond the River; they went to Helam, with Shobach the commander of Hadadezer's army leading them.

column.name: text
column.value: When David was told of this, he gathered all Israel, crossed the Jordan and went to Helam. The Arameans formed their battle lines to meet David and fought against him.

column.name: text
column.value: But they fled before Israel, and David killed seven hundred of their charioteers and forty thousand of their foot soldiers. He also struck down Shobach the commander of their army, and he died there.

column.name: text
column.value: When all the kings who were vassals of Hadadezer saw that they had been defeated by Israel, they made peace with the Israelites and became subject to them. So the Arameans were afraid to help the Ammonites anymore.

column.name: text
column.value: David asked, "Is there anyone still left of the house of Saul to whom I can show kindness for Jonathan's sake?"

column.name: text
column.value: Now there was a servant of Saul's household named Ziba. They called him to appear before David, and the king said to him, "Are you Ziba?" "Your servant," he replied.

column.name: text
column.value: The king asked, "Is there no one still left of the house of Saul to whom I can show God's kindness?" Ziba answered the king, "There is still a son of Jonathan; he is crippled in both feet."

column.name: text
column.value: "Where is he?" the king asked. Ziba answered, "He is at the house of Makir son of Ammiel in Lo Debar."

column.name: text
column.value: So King David had him brought from Lo Debar, from the house of Makir son of Ammiel.

column.name: text
column.value: When Mephibosheth son of Jonathan, the son of Saul, came to David, he bowed down to pay him honor. David said, "Mephibosheth!" "Your servant," he replied.

column.name: text
column.value: "Don't be afraid," David said to him, "for I will surely show you kindness for the sake of your father Jonathan. I will restore to you all the land that belonged to your grandfather Saul, and you will always eat at my table."

column.name: text
column.value: Mephibosheth bowed down and said, "What is your servant, that you should notice a dead dog like me?"

column.name: text
column.value: Then the king summoned Ziba, Saul's servant, and said to him, "I have given your master's grandson everything that belonged to Saul and his family.

column.name: text
column.value: You and your sons and your servants are to farm the land for him and bring in the crops, so that your master's grandson may be provided for. And Mephibosheth, grandson of your master, will always eat at my table." (Now Ziba had fifteen sons and twenty servants.)

column.name: text
column.value: Then Ziba said to the king, "Your servant will do whatever my lord the king commands his servant to do." So Mephibosheth ate at David's table like one of the king's sons.

column.name: text
column.value: Mephibosheth had a young son named Mica, and all the members of Ziba's household were servants of Mephibosheth.

column.name: text
column.value: And Mephibosheth lived in Jerusalem, because he always ate at the king's table, and he was crippled in both feet.

column.name: text
column.value: In the spring, at the time when kings go off to war, David sent Joab out with the king's men and the whole Israelite army. They destroyed the Ammonites and besieged Rabbah. But David remained in Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: One evening David got up from his bed and walked around on the roof of the palace. From the roof he saw a woman bathing. The woman was very beautiful,

column.name: text
column.value: and David sent someone to find out about her. The man said, "Isn't this Bathsheba, the daughter of Eliam and the wife of Uriah the Hittite?"

column.name: text
column.value: Then David sent messengers to get her. She came to him, and he slept with her. (She had purified herself from her uncleanness.) Then she went back home.

column.name: text
column.value: The woman conceived and sent word to David, saying, "I am pregnant."

column.name: text
column.value: So David sent this word to Joab: "Send me Uriah the Hittite." And Joab sent him to David.

column.name: text
column.value: When Uriah came to him, David asked him how Joab was, how the soldiers were and how the war was going.

column.name: text
column.value: Then David said to Uriah, "Go down to your house and wash your feet." So Uriah left the palace, and a gift from the king was sent after him.

column.name: text
column.value: But Uriah slept at the entrance to the palace with all his master's servants and did not go down to his house.

column.name: text
column.value: When David was told, "Uriah did not go home," he asked him, "Haven't you just come from a distance? Why didn't you go home?"

column.name: text
column.value: Uriah said to David, "The ark and Israel and Judah are staying in tents, and my master Joab and my lord's men are camped in the open fields. How could I go to my house to eat and drink and lie with my wife? As surely as you live, I will not do such a thing!"

column.name: text
column.value: Then David said to him, "Stay here one more day, and tomorrow I will send you back." So Uriah remained in Jerusalem that day and the next.

column.name: text
column.value: At David's invitation, he ate and drank with him, and David made him drunk. But in the evening Uriah went out to sleep on his mat among his master's servants; he did not go home.

column.name: text
column.value: In the morning David wrote a letter to Joab and sent it with Uriah.

column.name: text
column.value: In it he wrote, "Put Uriah in the front line where the fighting is fiercest. Then withdraw from him so he will be struck down and die."

column.name: text
column.value: So while Joab had the city under siege, he put Uriah at a place where he knew the strongest defenders were.

column.name: text
column.value: When the men of the city came out and fought against Joab, some of the men in David's army fell; moreover, Uriah the Hittite died.

column.name: text
column.value: Joab sent David a full account of the battle.

column.name: text
column.value: He instructed the messenger: "When you have finished giving the king this account of the battle,

column.name: text
column.value: the king's anger may flare up, and he may ask you, 'Why did you get so close to the city to fight? Didn't you know they would shoot arrows from the wall?

column.name: text
column.value: Who killed Abimelech son of Jerub-Besheth? Didn't a woman throw an upper millstone on him from the wall, so that he died in Thebez? Why did you get so close to the wall?' If he asks you this, then say to him, 'Also, your servant Uriah the Hittite is dead.'"

column.name: text
column.value: The messenger set out, and when he arrived he told David everything Joab had sent him to say.

column.name: text
column.value: The messenger said to David, "The men overpowered us and came out against us in the open, but we drove them back to the entrance to the city gate.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the archers shot arrows at your servants from the wall, and some of the king's men died. Moreover, your servant Uriah the Hittite is dead."

column.name: text
column.value: David told the messenger, "Say this to Joab: 'Don't let this upset you; the sword devours one as well as another. Press the attack against the city and destroy it.' Say this to encourage Joab."

column.name: text
column.value: When Uriah's wife heard that her husband was dead, she mourned for him.

column.name: text
column.value: After the time of mourning was over, David had her brought to his house, and she became his wife and bore him a son. But the thing David had done displeased the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD sent Nathan to David. When he came to him, he said, "There were two men in a certain town, one rich and the other poor.

column.name: text
column.value: The rich man had a very large number of sheep and cattle,

column.name: text
column.value: but the poor man had nothing except one little ewe lamb he had bought. He raised it, and it grew up with him and his children. It shared his food, drank from his cup and even slept in his arms. It was like a daughter to him.

column.name: text
column.value: "Now a traveler came to the rich man, but the rich man refrained from taking one of his own sheep or cattle to prepare a meal for the traveler who had come to him. Instead, he took the ewe lamb that belonged to the poor man and prepared it for the one who had come to him."

column.name: text
column.value: David burned with anger against the man and said to Nathan, "As surely as the LORD lives, the man who did this deserves to die!

column.name: text
column.value: He must pay for that lamb four times over, because he did such a thing and had no pity."

column.name: text
column.value: Then Nathan said to David, "You are the man! This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: 'I anointed you king over Israel, and I delivered you from the hand of Saul.

column.name: text
column.value: I gave your master's house to you, and your master's wives into your arms. I gave you the house of Israel and Judah. And if all this had been too little, I would have given you even more.

column.name: text
column.value: Why did you despise the word of the LORD by doing what is evil in his eyes? You struck down Uriah the Hittite with the sword and took his wife to be your own. You killed him with the sword of the Ammonites.

column.name: text
column.value: Now, therefore, the sword will never depart from your house, because you despised me and took the wife of Uriah the Hittite to be your own.'

column.name: text
column.value: "This is what the LORD says: 'Out of your own household I am going to bring calamity upon you. Before your very eyes I will take your wives and give them to one who is close to you, and he will lie with your wives in broad daylight.

column.name: text
column.value: You did it in secret, but I will do this thing in broad daylight before all Israel.'"

column.name: text
column.value: Then David said to Nathan, "I have sinned against the LORD." Nathan replied, "The LORD has taken away your sin. You are not going to die.

column.name: text
column.value: But because by doing this you have made the enemies of the LORD show utter contempt, the son born to you will die."

column.name: text
column.value: After Nathan had gone home, the LORD struck the child that Uriah's wife had borne to David, and he became ill.

column.name: text
column.value: David pleaded with God for the child. He fasted and went into his house and spent the nights lying on the ground.

column.name: text
column.value: The elders of his household stood beside him to get him up from the ground, but he refused, and he would not eat any food with them.

column.name: text
column.value: On the seventh day the child died. David's servants were afraid to tell him that the child was dead, for they thought, "While the child was still living, we spoke to David but he would not listen to us. How can we tell him the child is dead? He may do something desperate."

column.name: text
column.value: David noticed that his servants were whispering among themselves and he realized the child was dead. "Is the child dead?" he asked. "Yes," they replied, "he is dead."

column.name: text
column.value: Then David got up from the ground. After he had washed, put on lotions and changed his clothes, he went into the house of the LORD and worshiped. Then he went to his own house, and at his request they served him food, and he ate.

column.name: text
column.value: His servants asked him, "Why are you acting this way? While the child was alive, you fasted and wept, but now that the child is dead, you get up and eat!"

column.name: text
column.value: He answered, "While the child was still alive, I fasted and wept. I thought, 'Who knows? The LORD may be gracious to me and let the child live.'

column.name: text
column.value: But now that he is dead, why should I fast? Can I bring him back again? I will go to him, but he will not return to me."

column.name: text
column.value: Then David comforted his wife Bathsheba, and he went to her and lay with her. She gave birth to a son, and they named him Solomon. The LORD loved him;

column.name: text
column.value: and because the LORD loved him, he sent word through Nathan the prophet to name him Jedidiah.

column.name: text
column.value: Meanwhile Joab fought against Rabbah of the Ammonites and captured the royal citadel.

column.name: text
column.value: Joab then sent messengers to David, saying, "I have fought against Rabbah and taken its water supply.

column.name: text
column.value: Now muster the rest of the troops and besiege the city and capture it. Otherwise I will take the city, and it will be named after me."

column.name: text
column.value: So David mustered the entire army and went to Rabbah, and attacked and captured it.

column.name: text
column.value: He took the crown from the head of their king--its weight was a talent of gold, and it was set with precious stones--and it was placed on David's head. He took a great quantity of plunder from the city

column.name: text
column.value: and brought out the people who were there, consigning them to labor with saws and with iron picks and axes, and he made them work at brickmaking. He did this to all the Ammonite towns. Then David and his entire army returned to Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: In the course of time, David defeated the Philistines and subdued them, and he took Metheg Ammah from the control of the Philistines.

column.name: text
column.value: David also defeated the Moabites. He made them lie down on the ground and measured them off with a length of cord. Every two lengths of them were put to death, and the third length was allowed to live. So the Moabites became subject to David and brought tribute.

column.name: text
column.value: Moreover, David fought Hadadezer son of Rehob, king of Zobah, when he went to restore his control along the Euphrates River.

column.name: text
column.value: David captured a thousand of his chariots, seven thousand charioteers and twenty thousand foot soldiers. He hamstrung all but a hundred of the chariot horses.

column.name: text
column.value: When the Arameans of Damascus came to help Hadadezer king of Zobah, David struck down twenty-two thousand of them.

column.name: text
column.value: He put garrisons in the Aramean kingdom of Damascus, and the Arameans became subject to him and brought tribute. The LORD gave David victory wherever he went.

column.name: text
column.value: David took the gold shields that belonged to the officers of Hadadezer and brought them to Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: From Tebah and Berothai, towns that belonged to Hadadezer, King David took a great quantity of bronze.

column.name: text
column.value: When Tou king of Hamath heard that David had defeated the entire army of Hadadezer,

column.name: text
column.value: he sent his son Joram to King David to greet him and congratulate him on his victory in battle over Hadadezer, who had been at war with Tou. Joram brought with him articles of silver and gold and bronze.

column.name: text
column.value: King David dedicated these articles to the LORD, as he had done with the silver and gold from all the nations he had subdued:

column.name: text
column.value: Edom and Moab, the Ammonites and the Philistines, and Amalek. He also dedicated the plunder taken from Hadadezer son of Rehob, king of Zobah.

column.name: text
column.value: And David became famous after he returned from striking down eighteen thousand Edomites in the Valley of Salt.

column.name: text
column.value: He put garrisons throughout Edom, and all the Edomites became subject to David. The LORD gave David victory wherever he went.

column.name: text
column.value: David reigned over all Israel, doing what was just and right for all his people.

column.name: text
column.value: Joab son of Zeruiah was over the army; Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud was recorder;

column.name: text
column.value: Zadok son of Ahitub and Ahimelech son of Abiathar were priests; Seraiah was secretary;

column.name: text
column.value: Benaiah son of Jehoiada was over the Kerethites and Pelethites; and David's sons were royal advisers.

column.name: text
column.value: In the course of time, Amnon son of David fell in love with Tamar, the beautiful sister of Absalom son of David.

column.name: text
column.value: Amnon became frustrated to the point of illness on account of his sister Tamar, for she was a virgin, and it seemed impossible for him to do anything to her.

column.name: text
column.value: Now Amnon had a friend named Jonadab son of Shimeah, David's brother. Jonadab was a very shrewd man.

column.name: text
column.value: He asked Amnon, "Why do you, the king's son, look so haggard morning after morning? Won't you tell me?" Amnon said to him, "I'm in love with Tamar, my brother Absalom's sister."

column.name: text
column.value: "Go to bed and pretend to be ill," Jonadab said. "When your father comes to see you, say to him, 'I would like my sister Tamar to come and give me something to eat. Let her prepare the food in my sight so I may watch her and then eat it from her hand.'"

column.name: text
column.value: So Amnon lay down and pretended to be ill. When the king came to see him, Amnon said to him, "I would like my sister Tamar to come and make some special bread in my sight, so I may eat from her hand."

column.name: text
column.value: David sent word to Tamar at the palace: "Go to the house of your brother Amnon and prepare some food for him."

column.name: text
column.value: So Tamar went to the house of her brother Amnon, who was lying down. She took some dough, kneaded it, made the bread in his sight and baked it.

column.name: text
column.value: Then she took the pan and served him the bread, but he refused to eat. "Send everyone out of here," Amnon said. So everyone left him.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Amnon said to Tamar, "Bring the food here into my bedroom so I may eat from your hand." And Tamar took the bread she had prepared and brought it to her brother Amnon in his bedroom.

column.name: text
column.value: But when she took it to him to eat, he grabbed her and said, "Come to bed with me, my sister."

column.name: text
column.value: "Don't, my brother!" she said to him. "Don't force me. Such a thing should not be done in Israel! Don't do this wicked thing.

column.name: text
column.value: What about me? Where could I get rid of my disgrace? And what about you? You would be like one of the wicked fools in Israel. Please speak to the king; he will not keep me from being married to you."

column.name: text
column.value: But he refused to listen to her, and since he was stronger than she, he raped her.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Amnon hated her with intense hatred. In fact, he hated her more than he had loved her. Amnon said to her, "Get up and get out!"

column.name: text
column.value: "No!" she said to him. "Sending me away would be a greater wrong than what you have already done to me." But he refused to listen to her.

column.name: text
column.value: He called his personal servant and said, "Get this woman out of here and bolt the door after her."

column.name: text
column.value: So his servant put her out and bolted the door after her. She was wearing a richly ornamented robe, for this was the kind of garment the virgin daughters of the king wore.

column.name: text
column.value: Tamar put ashes on her head and tore the ornamented robe she was wearing. She put her hand on her head and went away, weeping aloud as she went.

column.name: text
column.value: Her brother Absalom said to her, "Has that Amnon, your brother, been with you? Be quiet now, my sister; he is your brother. Don't take this thing to heart." And Tamar lived in her brother Absalom's house, a desolate woman.

column.name: text
column.value: When King David heard all this, he was furious.

column.name: text
column.value: Absalom never said a word to Amnon, either good or bad; he hated Amnon because he had disgraced his sister Tamar.

column.name: text
column.value: Two years later, when Absalom's sheepshearers were at Baal Hazor near the border of Ephraim, he invited all the king's sons to come there.

column.name: text
column.value: Absalom went to the king and said, "Your servant has had shearers come. Will the king and his officials please join me?"

column.name: text
column.value: "No, my son," the king replied. "All of us should not go; we would only be a burden to you." Although Absalom urged him, he still refused to go, but gave him his blessing.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Absalom said, "If not, please let my brother Amnon come with us." The king asked him, "Why should he go with you?"

column.name: text
column.value: But Absalom urged him, so he sent with him Amnon and the rest of the king's sons.

column.name: text
column.value: Absalom ordered his men, "Listen! When Amnon is in high spirits from drinking wine and I say to you, 'Strike Amnon down,' then kill him. Don't be afraid. Have not I given you this order? Be strong and brave."

column.name: text
column.value: So Absalom's men did to Amnon what Absalom had ordered. Then all the king's sons got up, mounted their mules and fled.

column.name: text
column.value: While they were on their way, the report came to David: "Absalom has struck down all the king's sons; not one of them is left."

column.name: text
column.value: The king stood up, tore his clothes and lay down on the ground; and all his servants stood by with their clothes torn.

column.name: text
column.value: But Jonadab son of Shimeah, David's brother, said, "My lord should not think that they killed all the princes; only Amnon is dead. This has been Absalom's expressed intention ever since the day Amnon raped his sister Tamar.

column.name: text
column.value: My lord the king should not be concerned about the report that all the king's sons are dead. Only Amnon is dead."

column.name: text
column.value: Meanwhile, Absalom had fled. Now the man standing watch looked up and saw many people on the road west of him, coming down the side of the hill. The watchman went and told the king, "I see men in the direction of Horonaim, on the side of the hill."

column.name: text
column.value: Jonadab said to the king, "See, the king's sons are here; it has happened just as your servant said."

column.name: text
column.value: As he finished speaking, the king's sons came in, wailing loudly. The king, too, and all his servants wept very bitterly.

column.name: text
column.value: Absalom fled and went to Talmai son of Ammihud, the king of Geshur. But King David mourned for his son every day.

column.name: text
column.value: After Absalom fled and went to Geshur, he stayed there three years.

column.name: text
column.value: And the spirit of the king longed to go to Absalom, for he was consoled concerning Amnon's death.

column.name: text
column.value: In the course of time, Absalom provided himself with a chariot and horses and with fifty men to run ahead of him.

column.name: text
column.value: He would get up early and stand by the side of the road leading to the city gate. Whenever anyone came with a complaint to be placed before the king for a decision, Absalom would call out to him, "What town are you from?" He would answer, "Your servant is from one of the tribes of Israel."

column.name: text
column.value: Then Absalom would say to him, "Look, your claims are valid and proper, but there is no representative of the king to hear you."

column.name: text
column.value: And Absalom would add, "If only I were appointed judge in the land! Then everyone who has a complaint or case could come to me and I would see that he gets justice."

column.name: text
column.value: Also, whenever anyone approached him to bow down before him, Absalom would reach out his hand, take hold of him and kiss him.

column.name: text
column.value: Absalom behaved in this way toward all the Israelites who came to the king asking for justice, and so he stole the hearts of the men of Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: At the end of four years, Absalom said to the king, "Let me go to Hebron and fulfill a vow I made to the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: While your servant was living at Geshur in Aram, I made this vow: 'If the LORD takes me back to Jerusalem, I will worship the LORD in Hebron.'"

column.name: text
column.value: The king said to him, "Go in peace." So he went to Hebron.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Absalom sent secret messengers throughout the tribes of Israel to say, "As soon as you hear the sound of the trumpets, then say, 'Absalom is king in Hebron.'"

column.name: text
column.value: Two hundred men from Jerusalem had accompanied Absalom. They had been invited as guests and went quite innocently, knowing nothing about the matter.

column.name: text
column.value: While Absalom was offering sacrifices, he also sent for Ahithophel the Gilonite, David's counselor, to come from Giloh, his hometown. And so the conspiracy gained strength, and Absalom's following kept on increasing.

column.name: text
column.value: A messenger came and told David, "The hearts of the men of Israel are with Absalom."

column.name: text
column.value: Then David said to all his officials who were with him in Jerusalem, "Come! We must flee, or none of us will escape from Absalom. We must leave immediately, or he will move quickly to overtake us and bring ruin upon us and put the city to the sword."

column.name: text
column.value: The king's officials answered him, "Your servants are ready to do whatever our lord the king chooses."

column.name: text
column.value: The king set out, with his entire household following him; but he left ten concubines to take care of the palace.

column.name: text
column.value: So the king set out, with all the people following him, and they halted at a place some distance away.

column.name: text
column.value: All his men marched past him, along with all the Kerethites and Pelethites; and all the six hundred Gittites who had accompanied him from Gath marched before the king.

column.name: text
column.value: The king said to Ittai the Gittite, "Why should you come along with us? Go back and stay with King Absalom. You are a foreigner, an exile from your homeland.

column.name: text
column.value: You came only yesterday. And today shall I make you wander about with us, when I do not know where I am going? Go back, and take your countrymen. May kindness and faithfulness be with you."

column.name: text
column.value: But Ittai replied to the king, "As surely as the LORD lives, and as my lord the king lives, wherever my lord the king may be, whether it means life or death, there will your servant be."

column.name: text
column.value: David said to Ittai, "Go ahead, march on." So Ittai the Gittite marched on with all his men and the families that were with him.

column.name: text
column.value: The whole countryside wept aloud as all the people passed by. The king also crossed the Kidron Valley, and all the people moved on toward the desert.

column.name: text
column.value: Zadok was there, too, and all the Levites who were with him were carrying the ark of the covenant of God. They set down the ark of God, and Abiathar offered sacrifices until all the people had finished leaving the city.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the king said to Zadok, "Take the ark of God back into the city. If I find favor in the LORD'S eyes, he will bring me back and let me see it and his dwelling place again.

column.name: text
column.value: But if he says, 'I am not pleased with you,' then I am ready; let him do to me whatever seems good to him."

column.name: text
column.value: The king also said to Zadok the priest, "Aren't you a seer? Go back to the city in peace, with your son Ahimaaz and Jonathan son of Abiathar. You and Abiathar take your two sons with you.

column.name: text
column.value: I will wait at the fords in the desert until word comes from you to inform me."

column.name: text
column.value: So Zadok and Abiathar took the ark of God back to Jerusalem and stayed there.

column.name: text
column.value: But David continued up the Mount of Olives, weeping as he went; his head was covered and he was barefoot. All the people with him covered their heads too and were weeping as they went up.

column.name: text
column.value: Now David had been told, "Ahithophel is among the conspirators with Absalom." So David prayed, "O LORD, turn Ahithophel's counsel into foolishness."

column.name: text
column.value: When David arrived at the summit, where people used to worship God, Hushai the Arkite was there to meet him, his robe torn and dust on his head.

column.name: text
column.value: David said to him, "If you go with me, you will be a burden to me.

column.name: text
column.value: But if you return to the city and say to Absalom, 'I will be your servant, O king; I was your father's servant in the past, but now I will be your servant,' then you can help me by frustrating Ahithophel's advice.

column.name: text
column.value: Won't the priests Zadok and Abiathar be there with you? Tell them anything you hear in the king's palace.

column.name: text
column.value: Their two sons, Ahimaaz son of Zadok and Jonathan son of Abiathar, are there with them. Send them to me with anything you hear."

column.name: text
column.value: So David's friend Hushai arrived at Jerusalem as Absalom was entering the city.

column.name: text
column.value: Joab son of Zeruiah knew that the king's heart longed for Absalom.

column.name: text
column.value: So Joab sent someone to Tekoa and had a wise woman brought from there. He said to her, "Pretend you are in mourning. Dress in mourning clothes, and don't use any cosmetic lotions. Act like a woman who has spent many days grieving for the dead.

column.name: text
column.value: Then go to the king and speak these words to him." And Joab put the words in her mouth.

column.name: text
column.value: When the woman from Tekoa went to the king, she fell with her face to the ground to pay him honor, and she said, "Help me, O king!"

column.name: text
column.value: The king asked her, "What is troubling you?" She said, "I am indeed a widow; my husband is dead.

column.name: text
column.value: I your servant had two sons. They got into a fight with each other in the field, and no one was there to separate them. One struck the other and killed him.

column.name: text
column.value: Now the whole clan has risen up against your servant; they say, 'Hand over the one who struck his brother down, so that we may put him to death for the life of his brother whom he killed; then we will get rid of the heir as well.' They would put out the only burning coal I have left, leaving my husband neither name nor descendant on the face of the earth."

column.name: text
column.value: The king said to the woman, "Go home, and I will issue an order in your behalf."

column.name: text
column.value: But the woman from Tekoa said to him, "My lord the king, let the blame rest on me and on my father's family, and let the king and his throne be without guilt."

column.name: text
column.value: The king replied, "If anyone says anything to you, bring him to me, and he will not bother you again."

column.name: text
column.value: She said, "Then let the king invoke the LORD his God to prevent the avenger of blood from adding to the destruction, so that my son will not be destroyed." "As surely as the LORD lives," he said, "not one hair of your son's head will fall to the ground."

column.name: text
column.value: Then the woman said, "Let your servant speak a word to my lord the king." "Speak," he replied.

column.name: text
column.value: The woman said, "Why then have you devised a thing like this against the people of God? When the king says this, does he not convict himself, for the king has not brought back his banished son?

column.name: text
column.value: Like water spilled on the ground, which cannot be recovered, so we must die. But God does not take away life; instead, he devises ways so that a banished person may not remain estranged from him.

column.name: text
column.value: "And now I have come to say this to my lord the king because the people have made me afraid. Your servant thought, 'I will speak to the king; perhaps he will do what his servant asks.

column.name: text
column.value: Perhaps the king will agree to deliver his servant from the hand of the man who is trying to cut off both me and my son from the inheritance God gave us.'

column.name: text
column.value: "And now your servant says, 'May the word of my lord the king bring me rest, for my lord the king is like an angel of God in discerning good and evil. May the LORD your God be with you.'"

column.name: text
column.value: Then the king said to the woman, "Do not keep from me the answer to what I am going to ask you." "Let my lord the king speak," the woman said.

column.name: text
column.value: The king asked, "Isn't the hand of Joab with you in all this?" The woman answered, "As surely as you live, my lord the king, no one can turn to the right or to the left from anything my lord the king says. Yes, it was your servant Joab who instructed me to do this and who put all these words into the mouth of your servant.

column.name: text
column.value: Your servant Joab did this to change the present situation. My lord has wisdom like that of an angel of God--he knows everything that happens in the land."

column.name: text
column.value: The king said to Joab, "Very well, I will do it. Go, bring back the young man Absalom."

column.name: text
column.value: Joab fell with his face to the ground to pay him honor, and he blessed the king. Joab said, "Today your servant knows that he has found favor in your eyes, my lord the king, because the king has granted his servant's request."

column.name: text
column.value: Then Joab went to Geshur and brought Absalom back to Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: But the king said, "He must go to his own house; he must not see my face." So Absalom went to his own house and did not see the face of the king.

column.name: text
column.value: In all Israel there was not a man so highly praised for his handsome appearance as Absalom. From the top of his head to the sole of his foot there was no blemish in him.

column.name: text
column.value: Whenever he cut the hair of his head--he used to cut his hair from time to time when it became too heavy for him--he would weigh it, and its weight was two hundred shekels by the royal standard.

column.name: text
column.value: Three sons and a daughter were born to Absalom. The daughter's name was Tamar, and she became a beautiful woman.

column.name: text
column.value: Absalom lived two years in Jerusalem without seeing the king's face.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Absalom sent for Joab in order to send him to the king, but Joab refused to come to him. So he sent a second time, but he refused to come.

column.name: text
column.value: Then he said to his servants, "Look, Joab's field is next to mine, and he has barley there. Go and set it on fire." So Absalom's servants set the field on fire.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Joab did go to Absalom's house and he said to him, "Why have your servants set my field on fire?"

column.name: text
column.value: Absalom said to Joab, "Look, I sent word to you and said, 'Come here so I can send you to the king to ask, "Why have I come from Geshur? It would be better for me if I were still there!" 'Now then, I want to see the king's face, and if I am guilty of anything, let him put me to death."

column.name: text
column.value: So Joab went to the king and told him this. Then the king summoned Absalom, and he came in and bowed down with his face to the ground before the king. And the king kissed Absalom.

column.name: text
column.value: When David had gone a short distance beyond the summit, there was Ziba, the steward of Mephibosheth, waiting to meet him. He had a string of donkeys saddled and loaded with two hundred loaves of bread, a hundred cakes of raisins, a hundred cakes of figs and a skin of wine.

column.name: text
column.value: The king asked Ziba, "Why have you brought these?" Ziba answered, "The donkeys are for the king's household to ride on, the bread and fruit are for the men to eat, and the wine is to refresh those who become exhausted in the desert."

column.name: text
column.value: The king then asked, "Where is your master's grandson?" Ziba said to him, "He is staying in Jerusalem, because he thinks, 'Today the house of Israel will give me back my grandfather's kingdom.'"

column.name: text
column.value: Then the king said to Ziba, "All that belonged to Mephibosheth is now yours." "I humbly bow," Ziba said. "May I find favor in your eyes, my lord the king."

column.name: text
column.value: As King David approached Bahurim, a man from the same clan as Saul's family came out from there. His name was Shimei son of Gera, and he cursed as he came out.

column.name: text
column.value: He pelted David and all the king's officials with stones, though all the troops and the special guard were on David's right and left.

column.name: text
column.value: As he cursed, Shimei said, "Get out, get out, you man of blood, you scoundrel!

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD has repaid you for all the blood you shed in the household of Saul, in whose place you have reigned. The LORD has handed the kingdom over to your son Absalom. You have come to ruin because you are a man of blood!"

column.name: text
column.value: Then Abishai son of Zeruiah said to the king, "Why should this dead dog curse my lord the king? Let me go over and cut off his head."

column.name: text
column.value: But the king said, "What do you and I have in common, you sons of Zeruiah? If he is cursing because the LORD said to him, 'Curse David,' who can ask, 'Why do you do this?'"

column.name: text
column.value: David then said to Abishai and all his officials, "My son, who is of my own flesh, is trying to take my life. How much more, then, this Benjamite! Leave him alone; let him curse, for the LORD has told him to.

column.name: text
column.value: It may be that the LORD will see my distress and repay me with good for the cursing I am receiving today."

column.name: text
column.value: So David and his men continued along the road while Shimei was going along the hillside opposite him, cursing as he went and throwing stones at him and showering him with dirt.

column.name: text
column.value: The king and all the people with him arrived at their destination exhausted. And there he refreshed himself.

column.name: text
column.value: Meanwhile, Absalom and all the men of Israel came to Jerusalem, and Ahithophel was with him.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Hushai the Arkite, David's friend, went to Absalom and said to him, "Long live the king! Long live the king!"

column.name: text
column.value: Absalom asked Hushai, "Is this the love you show your friend? Why didn't you go with your friend?"

column.name: text
column.value: Hushai said to Absalom, "No, the one chosen by the LORD, by these people, and by all the men of Israel--his I will be, and I will remain with him.

column.name: text
column.value: Furthermore, whom should I serve? Should I not serve the son? Just as I served your father, so I will serve you."

column.name: text
column.value: Absalom said to Ahithophel, "Give us your advice. What should we do?"

column.name: text
column.value: Ahithophel answered, "Lie with your father's concubines whom he left to take care of the palace. Then all Israel will hear that you have made yourself a stench in your father's nostrils, and the hands of everyone with you will be strengthened."

column.name: text
column.value: So they pitched a tent for Absalom on the roof, and he lay with his father's concubines in the sight of all Israel.

column.name: text
