column.value: Now in those days the advice Ahithophel gave was like that of one who inquires of God. That was how both David and Absalom regarded all of Ahithophel's advice.

column.name: text
column.value: Ahithophel said to Absalom, "I would choose twelve thousand men and set out tonight in pursuit of David.

column.name: text
column.value: I would attack him while he is weary and weak. I would strike him with terror, and then all the people with him will flee. I would strike down only the king

column.name: text
column.value: and bring all the people back to you. The death of the man you seek will mean the return of all; all the people will be unharmed."

column.name: text
column.value: This plan seemed good to Absalom and to all the elders of Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: But Absalom said, "Summon also Hushai the Arkite, so we can hear what he has to say."

column.name: text
column.value: When Hushai came to him, Absalom said, "Ahithophel has given this advice. Should we do what he says? If not, give us your opinion."

column.name: text
column.value: Hushai replied to Absalom, "The advice Ahithophel has given is not good this time.

column.name: text
column.value: You know your father and his men; they are fighters, and as fierce as a wild bear robbed of her cubs. Besides, your father is an experienced fighter; he will not spend the night with the troops.

column.name: text
column.value: Even now, he is hidden in a cave or some other place. If he should attack your troops first, whoever hears about it will say, 'There has been a slaughter among the troops who follow Absalom.'

column.name: text
column.value: Then even the bravest soldier, whose heart is like the heart of a lion, will melt with fear, for all Israel knows that your father is a fighter and that those with him are brave.

column.name: text
column.value: "So I advise you: Let all Israel, from Dan to Beersheba--as numerous as the sand on the seashore--be gathered to you, with you yourself leading them into battle.

column.name: text
column.value: Then we will attack him wherever he may be found, and we will fall on him as dew settles on the ground. Neither he nor any of his men will be left alive.

column.name: text
column.value: If he withdraws into a city, then all Israel will bring ropes to that city, and we will drag it down to the valley until not even a piece of it can be found."

column.name: text
column.value: Absalom and all the men of Israel said, "The advice of Hushai the Arkite is better than that of Ahithophel." For the LORD had determined to frustrate the good advice of Ahithophel in order to bring disaster on Absalom.

column.name: text
column.value: Hushai told Zadok and Abiathar, the priests, "Ahithophel has advised Absalom and the elders of Israel to do such and such, but I have advised them to do so and so.

column.name: text
column.value: Now send a message immediately and tell David, 'Do not spend the night at the fords in the desert; cross over without fail, or the king and all the people with him will be swallowed up.'"

column.name: text
column.value: Jonathan and Ahimaaz were staying at En Rogel. A servant girl was to go and inform them, and they were to go and tell King David, for they could not risk being seen entering the city.

column.name: text
column.value: But a young man saw them and told Absalom. So the two of them left quickly and went to the house of a man in Bahurim. He had a well in his courtyard, and they climbed down into it.

column.name: text
column.value: His wife took a covering and spread it out over the opening of the well and scattered grain over it. No one knew anything about it.

column.name: text
column.value: When Absalom's men came to the woman at the house, they asked, "Where are Ahimaaz and Jonathan?" The woman answered them, "They crossed over the brook." The men searched but found no one, so they returned to Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: After the men had gone, the two climbed out of the well and went to inform King David. They said to him, "Set out and cross the river at once; Ahithophel has advised such and such against you."

column.name: text
column.value: So David and all the people with him set out and crossed the Jordan. By daybreak, no one was left who had not crossed the Jordan.

column.name: text
column.value: When Ahithophel saw that his advice had not been followed, he saddled his donkey and set out for his house in his hometown. He put his house in order and then hanged himself. So he died and was buried in his father's tomb.

column.name: text
column.value: David went to Mahanaim, and Absalom crossed the Jordan with all the men of Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: Absalom had appointed Amasa over the army in place of Joab. Amasa was the son of a man named Jether, an Israelite who had married Abigail, the daughter of Nahash and sister of Zeruiah the mother of Joab.

column.name: text
column.value: The Israelites and Absalom camped in the land of Gilead.

column.name: text
column.value: When David came to Mahanaim, Shobi son of Nahash from Rabbah of the Ammonites, and Makir son of Ammiel from Lo Debar, and Barzillai the Gileadite from Rogelim

column.name: text
column.value: brought bedding and bowls and articles of pottery. They also brought wheat and barley, flour and roasted grain, beans and lentils,

column.name: text
column.value: honey and curds, sheep, and cheese from cows' milk for David and his people to eat. For they said, "The people have become hungry and tired and thirsty in the desert."

column.name: text
column.value: David mustered the men who were with him and appointed over them commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds.

column.name: text
column.value: David sent the troops out--a third under the command of Joab, a third under Joab's brother Abishai son of Zeruiah, and a third under Ittai the Gittite. The king told the troops, "I myself will surely march out with you."

column.name: text
column.value: But the men said, "You must not go out; if we are forced to flee, they won't care about us. Even if half of us die, they won't care; but you are worth ten thousand of us. It would be better now for you to give us support from the city."

column.name: text
column.value: The king answered, "I will do whatever seems best to you." So the king stood beside the gate while all the men marched out in units of hundreds and of thousands.

column.name: text
column.value: The king commanded Joab, Abishai and Ittai, "Be gentle with the young man Absalom for my sake." And all the troops heard the king giving orders concerning Absalom to each of the commanders.

column.name: text
column.value: The army marched into the field to fight Israel, and the battle took place in the forest of Ephraim.

column.name: text
column.value: There the army of Israel was defeated by David's men, and the casualties that day were great--twenty thousand men.

column.name: text
column.value: The battle spread out over the whole countryside, and the forest claimed more lives that day than the sword.

column.name: text
column.value: Now Absalom happened to meet David's men. He was riding his mule, and as the mule went under the thick branches of a large oak, Absalom's head got caught in the tree. He was left hanging in midair, while the mule he was riding kept on going.

column.name: text
column.value: When one of the men saw this, he told Joab, "I just saw Absalom hanging in an oak tree."

column.name: text
column.value: Joab said to the man who had told him this, "What! You saw him? Why didn't you strike him to the ground right there? Then I would have had to give you ten shekels of silver and a warrior's belt."

column.name: text
column.value: But the man replied, "Even if a thousand shekels were weighed out into my hands, I would not lift my hand against the king's son. In our hearing the king commanded you and Abishai and Ittai, 'Protect the young man Absalom for my sake.'

column.name: text
column.value: And if I had put my life in jeopardy--and nothing is hidden from the king--you would have kept your distance from me."

column.name: text
column.value: Joab said, "I'm not going to wait like this for you." So he took three javelins in his hand and plunged them into Absalom's heart while Absalom was still alive in the oak tree.

column.name: text
column.value: And ten of Joab's armor-bearers surrounded Absalom, struck him and killed him.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Joab sounded the trumpet, and the troops stopped pursuing Israel, for Joab halted them.

column.name: text
column.value: They took Absalom, threw him into a big pit in the forest and piled up a large heap of rocks over him. Meanwhile, all the Israelites fled to their homes.

column.name: text
column.value: During his lifetime Absalom had taken a pillar and erected it in the King's Valley as a monument to himself, for he thought, "I have no son to carry on the memory of my name." He named the pillar after himself, and it is called Absalom's Monument to this day.

column.name: text
column.value: Now Ahimaaz son of Zadok said, "Let me run and take the news to the king that the LORD has delivered him from the hand of his enemies."

column.name: text
column.value: "You are not the one to take the news today," Joab told him. "You may take the news another time, but you must not do so today, because the king's son is dead."

column.name: text
column.value: Then Joab said to a Cushite, "Go, tell the king what you have seen." The Cushite bowed down before Joab and ran off.

column.name: text
column.value: Ahimaaz son of Zadok again said to Joab, "Come what may, please let me run behind the Cushite." But Joab replied, "My son, why do you want to go? You don't have any news that will bring you a reward."

column.name: text
column.value: He said, "Come what may, I want to run." So Joab said, "Run!" Then Ahimaaz ran by way of the plain and outran the Cushite.

column.name: text
column.value: While David was sitting between the inner and outer gates, the watchman went up to the roof of the gateway by the wall. As he looked out, he saw a man running alone.

column.name: text
column.value: The watchman called out to the king and reported it. The king said, "If he is alone, he must have good news." And the man came closer and closer.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the watchman saw another man running, and he called down to the gatekeeper, "Look, another man running alone!" The king said, "He must be bringing good news, too."

column.name: text
column.value: The watchman said, "It seems to me that the first one runs like Ahimaaz son of Zadok." "He's a good man," the king said. "He comes with good news."

column.name: text
column.value: Then Ahimaaz called out to the king, "All is well!" He bowed down before the king with his face to the ground and said, "Praise be to the LORD your God! He has delivered up the men who lifted their hands against my lord the king."

column.name: text
column.value: The king asked, "Is the young man Absalom safe?" Ahimaaz answered, "I saw great confusion just as Joab was about to send the king's servant and me, your servant, but I don't know what it was."

column.name: text
column.value: The king said, "Stand aside and wait here." So he stepped aside and stood there.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the Cushite arrived and said, "My lord the king, hear the good news! The LORD has delivered you today from all who rose up against you."

column.name: text
column.value: The king asked the Cushite, "Is the young man Absalom safe?" The Cushite replied, "May the enemies of my lord the king and all who rise up to harm you be like that young man."

column.name: text
column.value: The king was shaken. He went up to the room over the gateway and wept. As he went, he said: "O my son Absalom! My son, my son Absalom! If only I had died instead of you--O Absalom, my son, my son!"

column.name: text
column.value: Joab was told, "The king is weeping and mourning for Absalom."

column.name: text
column.value: And for the whole army the victory that day was turned into mourning, because on that day the troops heard it said, "The king is grieving for his son."

column.name: text
column.value: The men stole into the city that day as men steal in who are ashamed when they flee from battle.

column.name: text
column.value: The king covered his face and cried aloud, "O my son Absalom! O Absalom, my son, my son!"

column.name: text
column.value: Then Joab went into the house to the king and said, "Today you have humiliated all your men, who have just saved your life and the lives of your sons and daughters and the lives of your wives and concubines.

column.name: text
column.value: You love those who hate you and hate those who love you. You have made it clear today that the commanders and their men mean nothing to you. I see that you would be pleased if Absalom were alive today and all of us were dead.

column.name: text
column.value: Now go out and encourage your men. I swear by the LORD that if you don't go out, not a man will be left with you by nightfall. This will be worse for you than all the calamities that have come upon you from your youth till now."

column.name: text
column.value: So the king got up and took his seat in the gateway. When the men were told, "The king is sitting in the gateway," they all came before him. Meanwhile, the Israelites had fled to their homes.

column.name: text
column.value: Throughout the tribes of Israel, the people were all arguing with each other, saying, "The king delivered us from the hand of our enemies; he is the one who rescued us from the hand of the Philistines. But now he has fled the country because of Absalom;

column.name: text
column.value: and Absalom, whom we anointed to rule over us, has died in battle. So why do you say nothing about bringing the king back?"

column.name: text
column.value: King David sent this message to Zadok and Abiathar, the priests: "Ask the elders of Judah, 'Why should you be the last to bring the king back to his palace, since what is being said throughout Israel has reached the king at his quarters?

column.name: text
column.value: You are my brothers, my own flesh and blood. So why should you be the last to bring back the king?'

column.name: text
column.value: And say to Amasa, 'Are you not my own flesh and blood? May God deal with me, be it ever so severely, if from now on you are not the commander of my army in place of Joab.'"

column.name: text
column.value: He won over the hearts of all the men of Judah as though they were one man. They sent word to the king, "Return, you and all your men."

column.name: text
column.value: Then the king returned and went as far as the Jordan. Now the men of Judah had come to Gilgal to go out and meet the king and bring him across the Jordan.

column.name: text
column.value: Shimei son of Gera, the Benjamite from Bahurim, hurried down with the men of Judah to meet King David.

column.name: text
column.value: With him were a thousand Benjamites, along with Ziba, the steward of Saul's household, and his fifteen sons and twenty servants. They rushed to the Jordan, where the king was.

column.name: text
column.value: They crossed at the ford to take the king's household over and to do whatever he wished. When Shimei son of Gera crossed the Jordan, he fell prostrate before the king

column.name: text
column.value: and said to him, "May my lord not hold me guilty. Do not remember how your servant did wrong on the day my lord the king left Jerusalem. May the king put it out of his mind.

column.name: text
column.value: For I your servant know that I have sinned, but today I have come here as the first of the whole house of Joseph to come down and meet my lord the king."

column.name: text
column.value: Then Abishai son of Zeruiah said, "Shouldn't Shimei be put to death for this? He cursed the LORD'S anointed."

column.name: text
column.value: David replied, "What do you and I have in common, you sons of Zeruiah? This day you have become my adversaries! Should anyone be put to death in Israel today? Do I not know that today I am king over Israel?"

column.name: text
column.value: So the king said to Shimei, "You shall not die." And the king promised him on oath.

column.name: text
column.value: Mephibosheth, Saul's grandson, also went down to meet the king. He had not taken care of his feet or trimmed his mustache or washed his clothes from the day the king left until the day he returned safely.

column.name: text
column.value: When he came from Jerusalem to meet the king, the king asked him, "Why didn't you go with me, Mephibosheth?"

column.name: text
column.value: He said, "My lord the king, since I your servant am lame, I said, 'I will have my donkey saddled and will ride on it, so I can go with the king.' But Ziba my servant betrayed me.

column.name: text
column.value: And he has slandered your servant to my lord the king. My lord the king is like an angel of God; so do whatever pleases you.

column.name: text
column.value: All my grandfather's descendants deserved nothing but death from my lord the king, but you gave your servant a place among those who sat at your table. So what right do I have to make any more appeals to the king?"

column.name: text
column.value: The king said to him, "Why say more? I order you and Ziba to divide the fields."

column.name: text
column.value: Mephibosheth said to the king, "Let him take everything, now that my lord the king has arrived home safely."

column.name: text
column.value: Barzillai the Gileadite also came down from Rogelim to cross the Jordan with the king and to send him on his way from there.

column.name: text
column.value: Now Barzillai was a very old man, eighty years of age. He had provided for the king during his stay in Mahanaim, for he was a very wealthy man.

column.name: text
column.value: The king said to Barzillai, "Cross over with me and stay with me in Jerusalem, and I will provide for you."

column.name: text
column.value: But Barzillai answered the king, "How many more years will I live, that I should go up to Jerusalem with the king?

column.name: text
column.value: I am now eighty years old. Can I tell the difference between what is good and what is not? Can your servant taste what he eats and drinks? Can I still hear the voices of men and women singers? Why should your servant be an added burden to my lord the king?

column.name: text
column.value: Your servant will cross over the Jordan with the king for a short distance, but why should the king reward me in this way?

column.name: text
column.value: Let your servant return, that I may die in my own town near the tomb of my father and mother. But here is your servant Kimham. Let him cross over with my lord the king. Do for him whatever pleases you."

column.name: text
column.value: The king said, "Kimham shall cross over with me, and I will do for him whatever pleases you. And anything you desire from me I will do for you."

column.name: text
column.value: So all the people crossed the Jordan, and then the king crossed over. The king kissed Barzillai and gave him his blessing, and Barzillai returned to his home.

column.name: text
column.value: When the king crossed over to Gilgal, Kimham crossed with him. All the troops of Judah and half the troops of Israel had taken the king over.

column.name: text
column.value: Soon all the men of Israel were coming to the king and saying to him, "Why did our brothers, the men of Judah, steal the king away and bring him and his household across the Jordan, together with all his men?"

column.name: text
column.value: All the men of Judah answered the men of Israel, "We did this because the king is closely related to us. Why are you angry about it? Have we eaten any of the king's provisions? Have we taken anything for ourselves?"

column.name: text
column.value: Then the men of Israel answered the men of Judah, "We have ten shares in the king; and besides, we have a greater claim on David than you have. So why do you treat us with contempt? Were we not the first to speak of bringing back our king?" But the men of Judah responded even more harshly than the men of Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: These are the last words of David: "The oracle of David son of Jesse, the oracle of the man exalted by the Most High, the man anointed by the God of Jacob, Israel's singer of songs:

column.name: text
column.value: "The Spirit of the LORD spoke through me; his word was on my tongue.

column.name: text
column.value: The God of Israel spoke, the Rock of Israel said to me: 'When one rules over men in righteousness, when he rules in the fear of God,

column.name: text
column.value: he is like the light of morning at sunrise on a cloudless morning, like the brightness after rain that brings the grass from the earth.'

column.name: text
column.value: "Is not my house right with God? Has he not made with me an everlasting covenant, arranged and secured in every part? Will he not bring to fruition my salvation and grant me my every desire?

column.name: text
column.value: But evil men are all to be cast aside like thorns, which are not gathered with the hand.

column.name: text
column.value: Whoever touches thorns uses a tool of iron or the shaft of a spear; they are burned up where they lie."

column.name: text
column.value: These are the names of David's mighty men: Josheb-Basshebeth, a Tahkemonite, was chief of the Three; he raised his spear against eight hundred men, whom he killed in one encounter.

column.name: text
column.value: Next to him was Eleazar son of Dodai the Ahohite. As one of the three mighty men, he was with David when they taunted the Philistines gathered at Pas Dammim for battle. Then the men of Israel retreated,

column.name: text
column.value: but he stood his ground and struck down the Philistines till his hand grew tired and froze to the sword. The LORD brought about a great victory that day. The troops returned to Eleazar, but only to strip the dead.

column.name: text
column.value: Next to him was Shammah son of Agee the Hararite. When the Philistines banded together at a place where there was a field full of lentils, Israel's troops fled from them.

column.name: text
column.value: But Shammah took his stand in the middle of the field. He defended it and struck the Philistines down, and the LORD brought about a great victory.

column.name: text
column.value: During harvest time, three of the thirty chief men came down to David at the cave of Adullam, while a band of Philistines was encamped in the Valley of Rephaim.

column.name: text
column.value: At that time David was in the stronghold, and the Philistine garrison was at Bethlehem.

column.name: text
column.value: David longed for water and said, "Oh, that someone would get me a drink of water from the well near the gate of Bethlehem!"

column.name: text
column.value: So the three mighty men broke through the Philistine lines, drew water from the well near the gate of Bethlehem and carried it back to David. But he refused to drink it; instead, he poured it out before the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: "Far be it from me, O LORD, to do this!" he said. "Is it not the blood of men who went at the risk of their lives?" And David would not drink it. Such were the exploits of the three mighty men.

column.name: text
column.value: Abishai the brother of Joab son of Zeruiah was chief of the Three. He raised his spear against three hundred men, whom he killed, and so he became as famous as the Three.

column.name: text
column.value: Was he not held in greater honor than the Three? He became their commander, even though he was not included among them.

column.name: text
column.value: Benaiah son of Jehoiada was a valiant fighter from Kabzeel, who performed great exploits. He struck down two of Moab's best men. He also went down into a pit on a snowy day and killed a lion.

column.name: text
column.value: And he struck down a huge Egyptian. Although the Egyptian had a spear in his hand, Benaiah went against him with a club. He snatched the spear from the Egyptian's hand and killed him with his own spear.

column.name: text
column.value: Such were the exploits of Benaiah son of Jehoiada; he too was as famous as the three mighty men.

column.name: text
column.value: He was held in greater honor than any of the Thirty, but he was not included among the Three. And David put him in charge of his bodyguard.

column.name: text
column.value: Among the Thirty were: Asahel the brother of Joab, Elhanan son of Dodo from Bethlehem,

column.name: text
column.value: Shammah the Harodite, Elika the Harodite,

column.name: text
column.value: Helez the Paltite, Ira son of Ikkesh from Tekoa,

column.name: text
column.value: Abiezer from Anathoth, Mebunnai the Hushathite,

column.name: text
column.value: Zalmon the Ahohite, Maharai the Netophathite,

column.name: text
column.value: Heled son of Baanah the Netophathite, Ithai son of Ribai from Gibeah in Benjamin,

column.name: text
column.value: Benaiah the Pirathonite, Hiddai from the ravines of Gaash,

column.name: text
column.value: Abi-Albon the Arbathite, Azmaveth the Barhumite,

column.name: text
column.value: Eliahba the Shaalbonite, the sons of Jashen, Jonathan

column.name: text
column.value: son of Shammah the Hararite, Ahiam son of Sharar the Hararite,

column.name: text
column.value: Eliphelet son of Ahasbai the Maacathite, Eliam son of Ahithophel the Gilonite,

column.name: text
column.value: Hezro the Carmelite, Paarai the Arbite,

column.name: text
column.value: Igal son of Nathan from Zobah, the son of Hagri,

column.name: text
column.value: Zelek the Ammonite, Naharai the Beerothite, the armor-bearer of Joab son of Zeruiah,

column.name: text
column.value: Ira the Ithrite, Gareb the Ithrite

column.name: text
column.value: and Uriah the Hittite. There were thirty-seven in all.

column.name: text
column.value: During the reign of David, there was a famine for three successive years; so David sought the face of the LORD. The LORD said, "It is on account of Saul and his blood-stained house; it is because he put the Gibeonites to death."

column.name: text
column.value: The king summoned the Gibeonites and spoke to them. (Now the Gibeonites were not a part of Israel but were survivors of the Amorites; the Israelites had sworn to spare them, but Saul in his zeal for Israel and Judah had tried to annihilate them.)

column.name: text
column.value: David asked the Gibeonites, "What shall I do for you? How shall I make amends so that you will bless the LORD'S inheritance?"

column.name: text
column.value: The Gibeonites answered him, "We have no right to demand silver or gold from Saul or his family, nor do we have the right to put anyone in Israel to death." "What do you want me to do for you?" David asked.

column.name: text
column.value: They answered the king, "As for the man who destroyed us and plotted against us so that we have been decimated and have no place anywhere in Israel,

column.name: text
column.value: let seven of his male descendants be given to us to be killed and exposed before the LORD at Gibeah of Saul--the Lord's chosen one." So the king said, "I will give them to you."

column.name: text
column.value: The king spared Mephibosheth son of Jonathan, the son of Saul, because of the oath before the LORD between David and Jonathan son of Saul.

column.name: text
column.value: But the king took Armoni and Mephibosheth, the two sons of Aiah's daughter Rizpah, whom she had borne to Saul, together with the five sons of Saul's daughter Merab, whom she had borne to Adriel son of Barzillai the Meholathite.

column.name: text
column.value: He handed them over to the Gibeonites, who killed and exposed them on a hill before the LORD. All seven of them fell together; they were put to death during the first days of the harvest, just as the barley harvest was beginning.

column.name: text
column.value: Rizpah daughter of Aiah took sackcloth and spread it out for herself on a rock. From the beginning of the harvest till the rain poured down from the heavens on the bodies, she did not let the birds of the air touch them by day or the wild animals by night.

column.name: text
column.value: When David was told what Aiah's daughter Rizpah, Saul's concubine, had done,

column.name: text
column.value: he went and took the bones of Saul and his son Jonathan from the citizens of Jabesh Gilead. (They had taken them secretly from the public square at Beth Shan, where the Philistines had hung them after they struck Saul down on Gilboa.)

column.name: text
column.value: David brought the bones of Saul and his son Jonathan from there, and the bones of those who had been killed and exposed were gathered up.

column.name: text
column.value: They buried the bones of Saul and his son Jonathan in the tomb of Saul's father Kish, at Zela in Benjamin, and did everything the king commanded. After that, God answered prayer in behalf of the land.

column.name: text
column.value: Once again there was a battle between the Philistines and Israel. David went down with his men to fight against the Philistines, and he became exhausted.

column.name: text
column.value: And Ishbi-Benob, one of the descendants of Rapha, whose bronze spearhead weighed three hundred shekels and who was armed with a new sword, said he would kill David.

column.name: text
column.value: But Abishai son of Zeruiah came to David's rescue; he struck the Philistine down and killed him. Then David's men swore to him, saying, "Never again will you go out with us to battle, so that the lamp of Israel will not be extinguished."

column.name: text
column.value: In the course of time, there was another battle with the Philistines, at Gob. At that time Sibbecai the Hushathite killed Saph, one of the descendants of Rapha.

column.name: text
column.value: In another battle with the Philistines at Gob, Elhanan son of Jaare-Oregim the Bethlehemite killed Goliath the Gittite, who had a spear with a shaft like a weaver's rod.

column.name: text
column.value: In still another battle, which took place at Gath, there was a huge man with six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot--twenty-four in all. He also was descended from Rapha.

column.name: text
column.value: When he taunted Israel, Jonathan son of Shimeah, David's brother, killed him.

column.name: text
column.value: These four were descendants of Rapha in Gath, and they fell at the hands of David and his men.

column.name: text
column.value: David sang to the LORD the words of this song when the LORD delivered him from the hand of all his enemies and from the hand of Saul.

column.name: text
column.value: He said: "The LORD is my rock, my fortress and my deliverer;

column.name: text
column.value: my God is my rock, in whom I take refuge, my shield and the horn of my salvation. He is my stronghold, my refuge and my savior--from violent men you save me.

column.name: text
column.value: I call to the LORD, who is worthy of praise, and I am saved from my enemies.

column.name: text
column.value: "The waves of death swirled about me; the torrents of destruction overwhelmed me.

column.name: text
column.value: The cords of the grave coiled around me; the snares of death confronted me.

column.name: text
column.value: In my distress I called to the LORD; I called out to my God. From his temple he heard my voice; my cry came to his ears.

column.name: text
column.value: "The earth trembled and quaked, the foundations of the heavens shook; they trembled because he was angry.

column.name: text
column.value: Smoke rose from his nostrils; consuming fire came from his mouth, burning coals blazed out of it.

column.name: text
column.value: He parted the heavens and came down; dark clouds were under his feet.

column.name: text
column.value: He mounted the cherubim and flew; he soared on the wings of the wind.

column.name: text
column.value: He made darkness his canopy around him--the dark rain clouds of the sky.

column.name: text
column.value: Out of the brightness of his presence bolts of lightning blazed forth.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD thundered from heaven; the voice of the Most High resounded.

column.name: text
column.value: He shot arrows and scattered the enemies, bolts of lightning and routed them.

column.name: text
column.value: The valleys of the sea were exposed and the foundations of the earth laid bare at the rebuke of the LORD, at the blast of breath from his nostrils.

column.name: text
column.value: "He reached down from on high and took hold of me; he drew me out of deep waters.

column.name: text
column.value: He rescued me from my powerful enemy, from my foes, who were too strong for me.

column.name: text
column.value: They confronted me in the day of my disaster, but the LORD was my support.

column.name: text
column.value: He brought me out into a spacious place; he rescued me because he delighted in me.

column.name: text
column.value: "The LORD has dealt with me according to my righteousness; according to the cleanness of my hands he has rewarded me.

column.name: text
column.value: For I have kept the ways of the LORD; I have not done evil by turning from my God.

column.name: text
column.value: All his laws are before me; I have not turned away from his decrees.

column.name: text
column.value: I have been blameless before him and have kept myself from sin.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD has rewarded me according to my righteousness, according to my cleanness in his sight.

column.name: text
column.value: "To the faithful you show yourself faithful, to the blameless you show yourself blameless,

column.name: text
column.value: to the pure you show yourself pure, but to the crooked you show yourself shrewd.

column.name: text
column.value: You save the humble, but your eyes are on the haughty to bring them low.

column.name: text
column.value: You are my lamp, O LORD; the LORD turns my darkness into light.

column.name: text
column.value: With your help I can advance against a troop; with my God I can scale a wall.

column.name: text
column.value: "As for God, his way is perfect; the word of the LORD is flawless. He is a shield for all who take refuge in him.

column.name: text
column.value: For who is God besides the LORD? And who is the Rock except our God?

column.name: text
column.value: It is God who arms me with strength and makes my way perfect.

column.name: text
column.value: He makes my feet like the feet of a deer; he enables me to stand on the heights.

column.name: text
column.value: He trains my hands for battle; my arms can bend a bow of bronze.

column.name: text
column.value: You give me your shield of victory; you stoop down to make me great.

column.name: text
column.value: You broaden the path beneath me, so that my ankles do not turn.

column.name: text
column.value: "I pursued my enemies and crushed them; I did not turn back till they were destroyed.

column.name: text
column.value: I crushed them completely, and they could not rise; they fell beneath my feet.

column.name: text
column.value: You armed me with strength for battle; you made my adversaries bow at my feet.

column.name: text
column.value: You made my enemies turn their backs in flight, and I destroyed my foes.

column.name: text
column.value: They cried for help, but there was no one to save them--to the LORD, but he did not answer.

column.name: text
column.value: I beat them as fine as the dust of the earth; I pounded and trampled them like mud in the streets.

column.name: text
column.value: "You have delivered me from the attacks of my people; you have preserved me as the head of nations. People I did not know are subject to me,

column.name: text
column.value: and foreigners come cringing to me; as soon as they hear me, they obey me.

column.name: text
column.value: They all lose heart; they come trembling from their strongholds.

column.name: text
column.value: "The LORD lives! Praise be to my Rock! Exalted be God, the Rock, my Savior!

column.name: text
column.value: He is the God who avenges me, who puts the nations under me,

column.name: text
column.value: who sets me free from my enemies. You exalted me above my foes; from violent men you rescued me.

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore I will praise you, O LORD, among the nations; I will sing praises to your name.

column.name: text
column.value: He gives his king great victories; he shows unfailing kindness to his anointed, to David and his descendants forever."

column.name: text
column.value: Now a troublemaker named Sheba son of Bicri, a Benjamite, happened to be there. He sounded the trumpet and shouted, "We have no share in David, no part in Jesse's son! Every man to his tent, O Israel!"

column.name: text
column.value: So all the men of Israel deserted David to follow Sheba son of Bicri. But the men of Judah stayed by their king all the way from the Jordan to Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: When David returned to his palace in Jerusalem, he took the ten concubines he had left to take care of the palace and put them in a house under guard. He provided for them, but did not lie with them. They were kept in confinement till the day of their death, living as widows.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the king said to Amasa, "Summon the men of Judah to come to me within three days, and be here yourself."

column.name: text
column.value: But when Amasa went to summon Judah, he took longer than the time the king had set for him.

column.name: text
column.value: David said to Abishai, "Now Sheba son of Bicri will do us more harm than Absalom did. Take your master's men and pursue him, or he will find fortified cities and escape from us."

column.name: text
column.value: So Joab's men and the Kerethites and Pelethites and all the mighty warriors went out under the command of Abishai. They marched out from Jerusalem to pursue Sheba son of Bicri.

column.name: text
column.value: While they were at the great rock in Gibeon, Amasa came to meet them. Joab was wearing his military tunic, and strapped over it at his waist was a belt with a dagger in its sheath. As he stepped forward, it dropped out of its sheath.

column.name: text
column.value: Joab said to Amasa, "How are you, my brother?" Then Joab took Amasa by the beard with his right hand to kiss him.

column.name: text
column.value: Amasa was not on his guard against the dagger in Joab's hand, and Joab plunged it into his belly, and his intestines spilled out on the ground. Without being stabbed again, Amasa died. Then Joab and his brother Abishai pursued Sheba son of Bicri.

column.name: text
column.value: One of Joab's men stood beside Amasa and said, "Whoever favors Joab, and whoever is for David, let him follow Joab!"

column.name: text
column.value: Amasa lay wallowing in his blood in the middle of the road, and the man saw that all the troops came to a halt there. When he realized that everyone who came up to Amasa stopped, he dragged him from the road into a field and threw a garment over him.

column.name: text
column.value: After Amasa had been removed from the road, all the men went on with Joab to pursue Sheba son of Bicri.

column.name: text
column.value: Sheba passed through all the tribes of Israel to Abel Beth Maacah and through the entire region of the Berites, who gathered together and followed him.

column.name: text
column.value: All the troops with Joab came and besieged Sheba in Abel Beth Maacah. They built a siege ramp up to the city, and it stood against the outer fortifications. While they were battering the wall to bring it down,

column.name: text
column.value: a wise woman called from the city, "Listen! Listen! Tell Joab to come here so I can speak to him."

column.name: text
column.value: He went toward her, and she asked, "Are you Joab?" "I am," he answered. She said, "Listen to what your servant has to say." "I'm listening," he said.

column.name: text
column.value: She continued, "Long ago they used to say, 'Get your answer at Abel,' and that settled it.

column.name: text
column.value: We are the peaceful and faithful in Israel. You are trying to destroy a city that is a mother in Israel. Why do you want to swallow up the LORD'S inheritance?"

column.name: text
column.value: "Far be it from me!" Joab replied, "Far be it from me to swallow up or destroy!

column.name: text
column.value: That is not the case. A man named Sheba son of Bicri, from the hill country of Ephraim, has lifted up his hand against the king, against David. Hand over this one man, and I'll withdraw from the city." The woman said to Joab, "His head will be thrown to you from the wall."

column.name: text
column.value: Then the woman went to all the people with her wise advice, and they cut off the head of Sheba son of Bicri and threw it to Joab. So he sounded the trumpet, and his men dispersed from the city, each returning to his home. And Joab went back to the king in Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: Joab was over Israel's entire army; Benaiah son of Jehoiada was over the Kerethites and Pelethites;

column.name: text
column.value: Adoniram was in charge of forced labor; Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud was recorder;

column.name: text
column.value: Sheva was secretary; Zadok and Abiathar were priests;

column.name: text
column.value: and Ira the Jairite was David's priest.

column.name: text
column.value: Again the anger of the LORD burned against Israel, and he incited David against them, saying, "Go and take a census of Israel and Judah."

column.name: text
column.value: So the king said to Joab and the army commanders with him, "Go throughout the tribes of Israel from Dan to Beersheba and enroll the fighting men, so that I may know how many there are."

column.name: text
column.value: But Joab replied to the king, "May the LORD your God multiply the troops a hundred times over, and may the eyes of my lord the king see it. But why does my lord the king want to do such a thing?"

column.name: text
column.value: The king's word, however, overruled Joab and the army commanders; so they left the presence of the king to enroll the fighting men of Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: After crossing the Jordan, they camped near Aroer, south of the town in the gorge, and then went through Gad and on to Jazer.

column.name: text
column.value: They went to Gilead and the region of Tahtim Hodshi, and on to Dan Jaan and around toward Sidon.

column.name: text
column.value: Then they went toward the fortress of Tyre and all the towns of the Hivites and Canaanites. Finally, they went on to Beersheba in the Negev of Judah.

column.name: text
column.value: After they had gone through the entire land, they came back to Jerusalem at the end of nine months and twenty days.

column.name: text
column.value: Joab reported the number of the fighting men to the king: In Israel there were eight hundred thousand able-bodied men who could handle a sword, and in Judah five hundred thousand.

column.name: text
column.value: David was conscience-stricken after he had counted the fighting men, and he said to the LORD, "I have sinned greatly in what I have done. Now, O LORD, I beg you, take away the guilt of your servant. I have done a very foolish thing."

column.name: text
column.value: Before David got up the next morning, the word of the LORD had come to Gad the prophet, David's seer:

column.name: text
column.value: "Go and tell David, 'This is what the LORD says: I am giving you three options. Choose one of them for me to carry out against you.'"

column.name: text
column.value: So Gad went to David and said to him, "Shall there come upon you three years of famine in your land? Or three months of fleeing from your enemies while they pursue you? Or three days of plague in your land? Now then, think it over and decide how I should answer the one who sent me."

column.name: text
column.value: David said to Gad, "I am in deep distress. Let us fall into the hands of the LORD, for his mercy is great; but do not let me fall into the hands of men."

column.name: text
column.value: So the LORD sent a plague on Israel from that morning until the end of the time designated, and seventy thousand of the people from Dan to Beersheba died.

column.name: text
column.value: When the angel stretched out his hand to destroy Jerusalem, the LORD was grieved because of the calamity and said to the angel who was afflicting the people, "Enough! Withdraw your hand." The angel of the LORD was then at the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite.

column.name: text
column.value: When David saw the angel who was striking down the people, he said to the LORD, "I am the one who has sinned and done wrong. These are but sheep. What have they done? Let your hand fall upon me and my family."

column.name: text
column.value: On that day Gad went to David and said to him, "Go up and build an altar to the LORD on the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite."

column.name: text
column.value: So David went up, as the LORD had commanded through Gad.

column.name: text
column.value: When Araunah looked and saw the king and his men coming toward him, he went out and bowed down before the king with his face to the ground.

column.name: text
column.value: Araunah said, "Why has my lord the king come to his servant?" "To buy your threshing floor," David answered, "so I can build an altar to the LORD, that the plague on the people may be stopped."

column.name: text
column.value: Araunah said to David, "Let my lord the king take whatever pleases him and offer it up. Here are oxen for the burnt offering, and here are threshing sledges and ox yokes for the wood.

column.name: text
column.value: O king, Araunah gives all this to the king." Araunah also said to him, "May the LORD your God accept you."

column.name: text
column.value: But the king replied to Araunah, "No, I insist on paying you for it. I will not sacrifice to the LORD my God burnt offerings that cost me nothing." So David bought the threshing floor and the oxen and paid fifty shekels of silver for them.

column.name: text
column.value: David built an altar to the LORD there and sacrificed burnt offerings and fellowship offerings. Then the LORD answered prayer in behalf of the land, and the plague on Israel was stopped.

column.name: text
column.value: When King David was old and well advanced in years, he could not keep warm even when they put covers over him.

column.name: text
column.value: So his servants said to him, "Let us look for a young virgin to attend the king and take care of him. She can lie beside him so that our lord the king may keep warm."

column.name: text
column.value: Then they searched throughout Israel for a beautiful girl and found Abishag, a Shunammite, and brought her to the king.

column.name: text
column.value: The girl was very beautiful; she took care of the king and waited on him, but the king had no intimate relations with her.

column.name: text
column.value: Now Adonijah, whose mother was Haggith, put himself forward and said, "I will be king." So he got chariots and horses ready, with fifty men to run ahead of him.

column.name: text
column.value: (His father had never interfered with him by asking, "Why do you behave as you do?" He was also very handsome and was born next after Absalom.)

column.name: text
column.value: Adonijah conferred with Joab son of Zeruiah and with Abiathar the priest, and they gave him their support.

column.name: text
column.value: But Zadok the priest, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, Nathan the prophet, Shimei and Rei and David's special guard did not join Adonijah.

column.name: text
column.value: Adonijah then sacrificed sheep, cattle and fattened calves at the Stone of Zoheleth near En Rogel. He invited all his brothers, the king's sons, and all the men of Judah who were royal officials,

column.name: text
column.value: but he did not invite Nathan the prophet or Benaiah or the special guard or his brother Solomon.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Nathan asked Bathsheba, Solomon's mother, "Have you not heard that Adonijah, the son of Haggith, has become king without our lord David's knowing it?

column.name: text
column.value: Now then, let me advise you how you can save your own life and the life of your son Solomon.

column.name: text
column.value: Go in to King David and say to him, 'My lord the king, did you not swear to me your servant: "Surely Solomon your son shall be king after me, and he will sit on my throne"? Why then has Adonijah become king?'

column.name: text
column.value: While you are still there talking to the king, I will come in and confirm what you have said."

column.name: text
column.value: So Bathsheba went to see the aged king in his room, where Abishag the Shunammite was attending him.

column.name: text
column.value: Bathsheba bowed low and knelt before the king. "What is it you want?" the king asked.

column.name: text
column.value: She said to him, "My lord, you yourself swore to me your servant by the LORD your God: 'Solomon your son shall be king after me, and he will sit on my throne.'

column.name: text
column.value: But now Adonijah has become king, and you, my lord the king, do not know about it.

column.name: text
column.value: He has sacrificed great numbers of cattle, fattened calves, and sheep, and has invited all the king's sons, Abiathar the priest and Joab the commander of the army, but he has not invited Solomon your servant.

column.name: text
column.value: My lord the king, the eyes of all Israel are on you, to learn from you who will sit on the throne of my lord the king after him.

column.name: text
column.value: Otherwise, as soon as my lord the king is laid to rest with his fathers, I and my son Solomon will be treated as criminals."

column.name: text
column.value: While she was still speaking with the king, Nathan the prophet arrived.

column.name: text
column.value: And they told the king, "Nathan the prophet is here." So he went before the king and bowed with his face to the ground.

column.name: text
column.value: Nathan said, "Have you, my lord the king, declared that Adonijah shall be king after you, and that he will sit on your throne?

column.name: text
column.value: Today he has gone down and sacrificed great numbers of cattle, fattened calves, and sheep. He has invited all the king's sons, the commanders of the army and Abiathar the priest. Right now they are eating and drinking with him and saying, 'Long live King Adonijah!'

column.name: text
column.value: But me your servant, and Zadok the priest, and Benaiah son of Jehoiada, and your servant Solomon he did not invite.

column.name: text
column.value: Is this something my lord the king has done without letting his servants know who should sit on the throne of my lord the king after him?"

column.name: text
column.value: Then King David said, "Call in Bathsheba." So she came into the king's presence and stood before him.

column.name: text
column.value: The king then took an oath: "As surely as the LORD lives, who has delivered me out of every trouble,

column.name: text
column.value: I will surely carry out today what I swore to you by the LORD, the God of Israel: Solomon your son shall be king after me, and he will sit on my throne in my place."

column.name: text
column.value: Then Bathsheba bowed low with her face to the ground and, kneeling before the king, said, "May my lord King David live forever!"

column.name: text
column.value: King David said, "Call in Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet and Benaiah son of Jehoiada." When they came before the king,

column.name: text
column.value: he said to them: "Take your lord's servants with you and set Solomon my son on my own mule and take him down to Gihon.

column.name: text
column.value: There have Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet anoint him king over Israel. Blow the trumpet and shout, 'Long live King Solomon!'

column.name: text
column.value: Then you are to go up with him, and he is to come and sit on my throne and reign in my place. I have appointed him ruler over Israel and Judah."

column.name: text
column.value: Benaiah son of Jehoiada answered the king, "Amen! May the LORD, the God of my lord the king, so declare it.

column.name: text
column.value: As the LORD was with my lord the king, so may he be with Solomon to make his throne even greater than the throne of my lord King David!"

column.name: text
column.value: So Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, the Kerethites and the Pelethites went down and put Solomon on King David's mule and escorted him to Gihon.

column.name: text
column.value: Zadok the priest took the horn of oil from the sacred tent and anointed Solomon. Then they sounded the trumpet and all the people shouted, "Long live King Solomon!"

column.name: text
column.value: And all the people went up after him, playing flutes and rejoicing greatly, so that the ground shook with the sound.

column.name: text
column.value: Adonijah and all the guests who were with him heard it as they were finishing their feast. On hearing the sound of the trumpet, Joab asked, "What's the meaning of all the noise in the city?"

column.name: text
column.value: Even as he was speaking, Jonathan son of Abiathar the priest arrived. Adonijah said, "Come in. A worthy man like you must be bringing good news."

column.name: text
column.value: "Not at all!" Jonathan answered. "Our lord King David has made Solomon king.

column.name: text
column.value: The king has sent with him Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, the Kerethites and the Pelethites, and they have put him on the king's mule,

column.name: text
column.value: and Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet have anointed him king at Gihon. From there they have gone up cheering, and the city resounds with it. That's the noise you hear.

column.name: text
column.value: Moreover, Solomon has taken his seat on the royal throne.

column.name: text
column.value: Also, the royal officials have come to congratulate our lord King David, saying, 'May your God make Solomon's name more famous than yours and his throne greater than yours!' And the king bowed in worship on his bed

column.name: text
column.value: and said, 'Praise be to the LORD, the God of Israel, who has allowed my eyes to see a successor on my throne today.'"

column.name: text
column.value: At this, all Adonijah's guests rose in alarm and dispersed.

column.name: text
column.value: But Adonijah, in fear of Solomon, went and took hold of the horns of the altar.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Solomon was told, "Adonijah is afraid of King Solomon and is clinging to the horns of the altar. He says, 'Let King Solomon swear to me today that he will not put his servant to death with the sword.'"

column.name: text
column.value: Solomon replied, "If he shows himself to be a worthy man, not a hair of his head will fall to the ground; but if evil is found in him, he will die."

column.name: text
column.value: Then King Solomon sent men, and they brought him down from the altar. And Adonijah came and bowed down to King Solomon, and Solomon said, "Go to your home."

column.name: text
column.value: When the time drew near for David to die, he gave a charge to Solomon his son.

column.name: text
column.value: "I am about to go the way of all the earth," he said. "So be strong, show yourself a man,

column.name: text
column.value: and observe what the LORD your God requires: Walk in his ways, and keep his decrees and commands, his laws and requirements, as written in the Law of Moses, so that you may prosper in all you do and wherever you go,

column.name: text
column.value: and that the LORD may keep his promise to me: 'If your descendants watch how they live, and if they walk faithfully before me with all their heart and soul, you will never fail to have a man on the throne of Israel.'

column.name: text
column.value: "Now you yourself know what Joab son of Zeruiah did to me--what he did to the two commanders of Israel's armies, Abner son of Ner and Amasa son of Jether. He killed them, shedding their blood in peacetime as if in battle, and with that blood stained the belt around his waist and the sandals on his feet.

column.name: text
column.value: Deal with him according to your wisdom, but do not let his gray head go down to the grave in peace.

column.name: text
column.value: "But show kindness to the sons of Barzillai of Gilead and let them be among those who eat at your table. They stood by me when I fled from your brother Absalom.

column.name: text
column.value: "And remember, you have with you Shimei son of Gera, the Benjamite from Bahurim, who called down bitter curses on me the day I went to Mahanaim. When he came down to meet me at the Jordan, I swore to him by the LORD: 'I will not put you to death by the sword.'

column.name: text
column.value: But now, do not consider him innocent. You are a man of wisdom; you will know what to do to him. Bring his gray head down to the grave in blood."

column.name: text
column.value: Then David rested with his fathers and was buried in the City of David.

column.name: text
column.value: He had reigned forty years over Israel--seven years in Hebron and thirty-three in Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: So Solomon sat on the throne of his father David, and his rule was firmly established.

column.name: text
column.value: Now Adonijah, the son of Haggith, went to Bathsheba, Solomon's mother. Bathsheba asked him, "Do you come peacefully?" He answered, "Yes, peacefully."

column.name: text
column.value: Then he added, "I have something to say to you." "You may say it," she replied.

column.name: text
column.value: "As you know," he said, "the kingdom was mine. All Israel looked to me as their king. But things changed, and the kingdom has gone to my brother; for it has come to him from the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: Now I have one request to make of you. Do not refuse me." "You may make it," she said.

column.name: text
column.value: So he continued, "Please ask King Solomon--he will not refuse you--to give me Abishag the Shunammite as my wife."

column.name: text
column.value: "Very well," Bathsheba replied, "I will speak to the king for you."

column.name: text
column.value: When Bathsheba went to King Solomon to speak to him for Adonijah, the king stood up to meet her, bowed down to her and sat down on his throne. He had a throne brought for the king's mother, and she sat down at his right hand.

column.name: text
column.value: "I have one small request to make of you," she said. "Do not refuse me." The king replied, "Make it, my mother; I will not refuse you."

column.name: text
column.value: So she said, "Let Abishag the Shunammite be given in marriage to your brother Adonijah."

column.name: text
column.value: King Solomon answered his mother, "Why do you request Abishag the Shunammite for Adonijah? You might as well request the kingdom for him--after all, he is my older brother--yes, for him and for Abiathar the priest and Joab son of Zeruiah!"

column.name: text
column.value: Then King Solomon swore by the LORD: "May God deal with me, be it ever so severely, if Adonijah does not pay with his life for this request!

column.name: text
column.value: And now, as surely as the LORD lives--he who has established me securely on the throne of my father David and has founded a dynasty for me as he promised--Adonijah shall be put to death today!"

column.name: text
column.value: So King Solomon gave orders to Benaiah son of Jehoiada, and he struck down Adonijah and he died.

column.name: text
column.value: To Abiathar the priest the king said, "Go back to your fields in Anathoth. You deserve to die, but I will not put you to death now, because you carried the ark of the Sovereign LORD before my father David and shared all my father's hardships."

column.name: text
column.value: So Solomon removed Abiathar from the priesthood of the LORD, fulfilling the word the LORD had spoken at Shiloh about the house of Eli.

column.name: text
column.value: When the news reached Joab, who had conspired with Adonijah though not with Absalom, he fled to the tent of the LORD and took hold of the horns of the altar.

column.name: text
column.value: King Solomon was told that Joab had fled to the tent of the LORD and was beside the altar. Then Solomon ordered Benaiah son of Jehoiada, "Go, strike him down!"

column.name: text
column.value: So Benaiah entered the tent of the LORD and said to Joab, "The king says, 'Come out!'" But he answered, "No, I will die here." Benaiah reported to the king, "This is how Joab answered me."

column.name: text
column.value: Then the king commanded Benaiah, "Do as he says. Strike him down and bury him, and so clear me and my father's house of the guilt of the innocent blood that Joab shed.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD will repay him for the blood he shed, because without the knowledge of my father David he attacked two men and killed them with the sword. Both of them--Abner son of Ner, commander of Israel's army, and Amasa son of Jether, commander of Judah's army--were better men and more upright than he.

column.name: text
column.value: May the guilt of their blood rest on the head of Joab and his descendants forever. But on David and his descendants, his house and his throne, may there be the LORD'S peace forever."

column.name: text
column.value: So Benaiah son of Jehoiada went up and struck down Joab and killed him, and he was buried on his own land in the desert.

column.name: text
column.value: The king put Benaiah son of Jehoiada over the army in Joab's position and replaced Abiathar with Zadok the priest.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the king sent for Shimei and said to him, "Build yourself a house in Jerusalem and live there, but do not go anywhere else.

column.name: text
column.value: The day you leave and cross the Kidron Valley, you can be sure you will die; your blood will be on your own head."

column.name: text
column.value: Shimei answered the king, "What you say is good. Your servant will do as my lord the king has said." And Shimei stayed in Jerusalem for a long time.

column.name: text
column.value: But three years later, two of Shimei's slaves ran off to Achish son of Maacah, king of Gath, and Shimei was told, "Your slaves are in Gath."

column.name: text
column.value: At this, he saddled his donkey and went to Achish at Gath in search of his slaves. So Shimei went away and brought the slaves back from Gath.

column.name: text
column.value: When Solomon was told that Shimei had gone from Jerusalem to Gath and had returned,

column.name: text
column.value: the king summoned Shimei and said to him, "Did I not make you swear by the LORD and warn you, 'On the day you leave to go anywhere else, you can be sure you will die'? At that time you said to me, 'What you say is good. I will obey.'

column.name: text
column.value: Why then did you not keep your oath to the LORD and obey the command I gave you?"

column.name: text
column.value: The king also said to Shimei, "You know in your heart all the wrong you did to my father David. Now the LORD will repay you for your wrongdoing.

column.name: text
column.value: But King Solomon will be blessed, and David's throne will remain secure before the LORD forever."

column.name: text
column.value: Then the king gave the order to Benaiah son of Jehoiada, and he went out and struck Shimei down and killed him. The kingdom was now firmly established in Solomon's hands.

column.name: text
column.value: So King Solomon ruled over all Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: And these were his chief officials: Azariah son of Zadok--the priest;

column.name: text
column.value: Elihoreph and Ahijah, sons of Shisha--secretaries; Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud--recorder;

column.name: text
column.value: Benaiah son of Jehoiada--commander in chief; Zadok and Abiathar--priests;

column.name: text
column.value: Azariah son of Nathan--in charge of the district officers; Zabud son of Nathan--a priest and personal adviser to the king;

column.name: text
column.value: Ahishar--in charge of the palace; Adoniram son of Abda--in charge of forced labor.

column.name: text
column.value: Solomon also had twelve district governors over all Israel, who supplied provisions for the king and the royal household. Each one had to provide supplies for one month in the year.

column.name: text
column.value: These are their names: Ben-Hur--in the hill country of Ephraim;

column.name: text
column.value: Ben-Deker--in Makaz, Shaalbim, Beth Shemesh and Elon Bethhanan;

column.name: text
column.value: Ben-Hesed--in Arubboth (Socoh and all the land of Hepher were his);

column.name: text
column.value: Ben-Abinadab--in Naphoth Dor (he was married to Taphath daughter of Solomon);

column.name: text
column.value: Baana son of Ahilud--in Taanach and Megiddo, and in all of Beth Shan next to Zarethan below Jezreel, from Beth Shan to Abel Meholah across to Jokmeam;

column.name: text
column.value: Ben-Geber--in Ramoth Gilead (the settlements of Jair son of Manasseh in Gilead were his, as well as the district of Argob in Bashan and its sixty large walled cities with bronze gate bars);

column.name: text
column.value: Ahinadab son of Iddo--in Mahanaim;

column.name: text
column.value: Ahimaaz--in Naphtali (he had married Basemath daughter of Solomon);

column.name: text
column.value: Baana son of Hushai--in Asher and in Aloth;

column.name: text
column.value: Jehoshaphat son of Paruah--in Issachar;

column.name: text
column.value: Shimei son of Ela--in Benjamin;

column.name: text
column.value: Geber son of Uri--in Gilead (the country of Sihon king of the Amorites and the country of Og king of Bashan). He was the only governor over the district.

column.name: text
column.value: The people of Judah and Israel were as numerous as the sand on the seashore; they ate, they drank and they were happy.

column.name: text
column.value: And Solomon ruled over all the kingdoms from the River to the land of the Philistines, as far as the border of Egypt. These countries brought tribute and were Solomon's subjects all his life.

column.name: text
column.value: Solomon's daily provisions were thirty cors of fine flour and sixty cors of meal,

column.name: text
column.value: ten head of stall-fed cattle, twenty of pasture-fed cattle and a hundred sheep and goats, as well as deer, gazelles, roebucks and choice fowl.

column.name: text
column.value: For he ruled over all the kingdoms west of the River, from Tiphsah to Gaza, and had peace on all sides.

column.name: text
column.value: During Solomon's lifetime Judah and Israel, from Dan to Beersheba, lived in safety, each man under his own vine and fig tree.

column.name: text
column.value: Solomon had four thousand stalls for chariot horses, and twelve thousand horses.

column.name: text
column.value: The district officers, each in his month, supplied provisions for King Solomon and all who came to the king's table. They saw to it that nothing was lacking.

column.name: text
column.value: They also brought to the proper place their quotas of barley and straw for the chariot horses and the other horses.

column.name: text
column.value: God gave Solomon wisdom and very great insight, and a breadth of understanding as measureless as the sand on the seashore.

column.name: text
column.value: Solomon's wisdom was greater than the wisdom of all the men of the East, and greater than all the wisdom of Egypt.

column.name: text
column.value: He was wiser than any other man, including Ethan the Ezrahite--wiser than Heman, Calcol and Darda, the sons of Mahol. And his fame spread to all the surrounding nations.

column.name: text
column.value: He spoke three thousand proverbs and his songs numbered a thousand and five.

column.name: text
column.value: He described plant life, from the cedar of Lebanon to the hyssop that grows out of walls. He also taught about animals and birds, reptiles and fish.

column.name: text
column.value: Men of all nations came to listen to Solomon's wisdom, sent by all the kings of the world, who had heard of his wisdom.

column.name: text
column.value: Solomon made an alliance with Pharaoh king of Egypt and married his daughter. He brought her to the City of David until he finished building his palace and the temple of the LORD, and the wall around Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: The people, however, were still sacrificing at the high places, because a temple had not yet been built for the Name of the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: Solomon showed his love for the LORD by walking according to the statutes of his father David, except that he offered sacrifices and burned incense on the high places.

column.name: text
column.value: The king went to Gibeon to offer sacrifices, for that was the most important high place, and Solomon offered a thousand burnt offerings on that altar.

column.name: text
column.value: At Gibeon the LORD appeared to Solomon during the night in a dream, and God said, "Ask for whatever you want me to give you."

column.name: text
column.value: Solomon answered, "You have shown great kindness to your servant, my father David, because he was faithful to you and righteous and upright in heart. You have continued this great kindness to him and have given him a son to sit on his throne this very day.

column.name: text
column.value: "Now, O LORD my God, you have made your servant king in place of my father David. But I am only a little child and do not know how to carry out my duties.

column.name: text
column.value: Your servant is here among the people you have chosen, a great people, too numerous to count or number.

column.name: text
column.value: So give your servant a discerning heart to govern your people and to distinguish between right and wrong. For who is able to govern this great people of yours?"

column.name: text
column.value: The Lord was pleased that Solomon had asked for this.

column.name: text
column.value: So God said to him, "Since you have asked for this and not for long life or wealth for yourself, nor have asked for the death of your enemies but for discernment in administering justice,

column.name: text
column.value: I will do what you have asked. I will give you a wise and discerning heart, so that there will never have been anyone like you, nor will there ever be.

column.name: text
column.value: Moreover, I will give you what you have not asked for--both riches and honor--so that in your lifetime you will have no equal among kings.

column.name: text
column.value: And if you walk in my ways and obey my statutes and commands as David your father did, I will give you a long life."

column.name: text
column.value: Then Solomon awoke--and he realized it had been a dream. He returned to Jerusalem, stood before the ark of the Lord's covenant and sacrificed burnt offerings and fellowship offerings. Then he gave a feast for all his court.

column.name: text
column.value: Now two prostitutes came to the king and stood before him.

column.name: text
column.value: One of them said, "My lord, this woman and I live in the same house. I had a baby while she was there with me.

column.name: text
column.value: The third day after my child was born, this woman also had a baby. We were alone; there was no one in the house but the two of us.

column.name: text
column.value: "During the night this woman's son died because she lay on him.

column.name: text
column.value: So she got up in the middle of the night and took my son from my side while I your servant was asleep. She put him by her breast and put her dead son by my breast.

column.name: text
column.value: The next morning, I got up to nurse my son--and he was dead! But when I looked at him closely in the morning light, I saw that it wasn't the son I had borne."

column.name: text
column.value: The other woman said, "No! The living one is my son; the dead one is yours." But the first one insisted, "No! The dead one is yours; the living one is mine." And so they argued before the king.

column.name: text
column.value: The king said, "This one says, 'My son is alive and your son is dead,' while that one says, 'No! Your son is dead and mine is alive.'"

column.name: text
column.value: Then the king said, "Bring me a sword." So they brought a sword for the king.

column.name: text
column.value: He then gave an order: "Cut the living child in two and give half to one and half to the other."

column.name: text
column.value: The woman whose son was alive was filled with compassion for her son and said to the king, "Please, my lord, give her the living baby! Don't kill him!" But the other said, "Neither I nor you shall have him. Cut him in two!"

column.name: text
column.value: Then the king gave his ruling: "Give the living baby to the first woman. Do not kill him; she is his mother."

column.name: text
column.value: When all Israel heard the verdict the king had given, they held the king in awe, because they saw that he had wisdom from God to administer justice.

column.name: text
column.value: When Hiram king of Tyre heard that Solomon had been anointed king to succeed his father David, he sent his envoys to Solomon, because he had always been on friendly terms with David.

column.name: text
column.value: Solomon sent back this message to Hiram:

column.name: text
column.value: "You know that because of the wars waged against my father David from all sides, he could not build a temple for the Name of the LORD his God until the LORD put his enemies under his feet.

column.name: text
column.value: But now the LORD my God has given me rest on every side, and there is no adversary or disaster.

column.name: text
column.value: I intend, therefore, to build a temple for the Name of the LORD my God, as the LORD told my father David, when he said, 'Your son whom I will put on the throne in your place will build the temple for my Name.'

column.name: text
column.value: "So give orders that cedars of Lebanon be cut for me. My men will work with yours, and I will pay you for your men whatever wages you set. You know that we have no one so skilled in felling timber as the Sidonians."

column.name: text
column.value: When Hiram heard Solomon's message, he was greatly pleased and said, "Praise be to the LORD today, for he has given David a wise son to rule over this great nation."

column.name: text
column.value: So Hiram sent word to Solomon: "I have received the message you sent me and will do all you want in providing the cedar and pine logs.

column.name: text
column.value: My men will haul them down from Lebanon to the sea, and I will float them in rafts by sea to the place you specify. There I will separate them and you can take them away. And you are to grant my wish by providing food for my royal household."

column.name: text
column.value: In this way Hiram kept Solomon supplied with all the cedar and pine logs he wanted,

column.name: text
column.value: and Solomon gave Hiram twenty thousand cors of wheat as food for his household, in addition to twenty thousand baths of pressed olive oil. Solomon continued to do this for Hiram year after year.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD gave Solomon wisdom, just as he had promised him. There were peaceful relations between Hiram and Solomon, and the two of them made a treaty.

column.name: text
column.value: King Solomon conscripted laborers from all Israel--thirty thousand men.

column.name: text
column.value: He sent them off to Lebanon in shifts of ten thousand a month, so that they spent one month in Lebanon and two months at home. Adoniram was in charge of the forced labor.

column.name: text
column.value: Solomon had seventy thousand carriers and eighty thousand stonecutters in the hills,

column.name: text
column.value: as well as thirty-three hundred foremen who supervised the project and directed the workmen.

column.name: text
column.value: At the king's command they removed from the quarry large blocks of quality stone to provide a foundation of dressed stone for the temple.

column.name: text
column.value: The craftsmen of Solomon and Hiram and the men of Gebal cut and prepared the timber and stone for the building of the temple.

column.name: text
column.value: In the four hundred and eightieth year after the Israelites had come out of Egypt, in the fourth year of Solomon's reign over Israel, in the month of Ziv, the second month, he began to build the temple of the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: The temple that King Solomon built for the LORD was sixty cubits long, twenty wide and thirty high.

column.name: text
column.value: The portico at the front of the main hall of the temple extended the width of the temple, that is twenty cubits, and projected ten cubits from the front of the temple.

column.name: text
column.value: He made narrow clerestory windows in the temple.

column.name: text
column.value: Against the walls of the main hall and inner sanctuary he built a structure around the building, in which there were side rooms.

column.name: text
column.value: The lowest floor was five cubits wide, the middle floor six cubits and the third floor seven. He made offset ledges around the outside of the temple so that nothing would be inserted into the temple walls.

column.name: text
column.value: In building the temple, only blocks dressed at the quarry were used, and no hammer, chisel or any other iron tool was heard at the temple site while it was being built.

column.name: text
column.value: The entrance to the lowest floor was on the south side of the temple; a stairway led up to the middle level and from there to the third.

column.name: text
column.value: So he built the temple and completed it, roofing it with beams and cedar planks.

column.name: text
column.value: And he built the side rooms all along the temple. The height of each was five cubits, and they were attached to the temple by beams of cedar.

column.name: text
column.value: The word of the LORD came to Solomon:

column.name: text
column.value: "As for this temple you are building, if you follow my decrees, carry out my regulations and keep all my commands and obey them, I will fulfill through you the promise I gave to David your father.

column.name: text
column.value: And I will live among the Israelites and will not abandon my people Israel."

column.name: text
column.value: So Solomon built the temple and completed it.

column.name: text
column.value: He lined its interior walls with cedar boards, paneling them from the floor of the temple to the ceiling, and covered the floor of the temple with planks of pine.

column.name: text
column.value: He partitioned off twenty cubits at the rear of the temple with cedar boards from floor to ceiling to form within the temple an inner sanctuary, the Most Holy Place.

column.name: text
column.value: The main hall in front of this room was forty cubits long.

column.name: text
column.value: The inside of the temple was cedar, carved with gourds and open flowers. Everything was cedar; no stone was to be seen.

column.name: text
column.value: He prepared the inner sanctuary within the temple to set the ark of the covenant of the LORD there.

column.name: text
column.value: The inner sanctuary was twenty cubits long, twenty wide and twenty high. He overlaid the inside with pure gold, and he also overlaid the altar of cedar.

column.name: text
column.value: Solomon covered the inside of the temple with pure gold, and he extended gold chains across the front of the inner sanctuary, which was overlaid with gold.

column.name: text
