column.value: So he overlaid the whole interior with gold. He also overlaid with gold the altar that belonged to the inner sanctuary.

column.name: text
column.value: In the inner sanctuary he made a pair of cherubim of olive wood, each ten cubits high.

column.name: text
column.value: One wing of the first cherub was five cubits long, and the other wing five cubits--ten cubits from wing tip to wing tip.

column.name: text
column.value: The second cherub also measured ten cubits, for the two cherubim were identical in size and shape.

column.name: text
column.value: The height of each cherub was ten cubits.

column.name: text
column.value: He placed the cherubim inside the innermost room of the temple, with their wings spread out. The wing of one cherub touched one wall, while the wing of the other touched the other wall, and their wings touched each other in the middle of the room.

column.name: text
column.value: He overlaid the cherubim with gold.

column.name: text
column.value: On the walls all around the temple, in both the inner and outer rooms, he carved cherubim, palm trees and open flowers.

column.name: text
column.value: He also covered the floors of both the inner and outer rooms of the temple with gold.

column.name: text
column.value: For the entrance of the inner sanctuary he made doors of olive wood with five-sided jambs.

column.name: text
column.value: And on the two olive wood doors he carved cherubim, palm trees and open flowers, and overlaid the cherubim and palm trees with beaten gold.

column.name: text
column.value: In the same way he made four-sided jambs of olive wood for the entrance to the main hall.

column.name: text
column.value: He also made two pine doors, each having two leaves that turned in sockets.

column.name: text
column.value: He carved cherubim, palm trees and open flowers on them and overlaid them with gold hammered evenly over the carvings.

column.name: text
column.value: And he built the inner courtyard of three courses of dressed stone and one course of trimmed cedar beams.

column.name: text
column.value: The foundation of the temple of the LORD was laid in the fourth year, in the month of Ziv.

column.name: text
column.value: In the eleventh year in the month of Bul, the eighth month, the temple was finished in all its details according to its specifications. He had spent seven years building it.

column.name: text
column.value: It took Solomon thirteen years, however, to complete the construction of his palace.

column.name: text
column.value: He built the Palace of the Forest of Lebanon a hundred cubits long, fifty wide and thirty high, with four rows of cedar columns supporting trimmed cedar beams.

column.name: text
column.value: It was roofed with cedar above the beams that rested on the columns--forty-five beams, fifteen to a row.

column.name: text
column.value: Its windows were placed high in sets of three, facing each other.

column.name: text
column.value: All the doorways had rectangular frames; they were in the front part in sets of three, facing each other.

column.name: text
column.value: He made a colonnade fifty cubits long and thirty wide. In front of it was a portico, and in front of that were pillars and an overhanging roof.

column.name: text
column.value: He built the throne hall, the Hall of Justice, where he was to judge, and he covered it with cedar from floor to ceiling.

column.name: text
column.value: And the palace in which he was to live, set farther back, was similar in design. Solomon also made a palace like this hall for Pharaoh's daughter, whom he had married.

column.name: text
column.value: All these structures, from the outside to the great courtyard and from foundation to eaves, were made of blocks of high-grade stone cut to size and trimmed with a saw on their inner and outer faces.

column.name: text
column.value: The foundations were laid with large stones of good quality, some measuring ten cubits and some eight.

column.name: text
column.value: Above were high-grade stones, cut to size, and cedar beams.

column.name: text
column.value: The great courtyard was surrounded by a wall of three courses of dressed stone and one course of trimmed cedar beams, as was the inner courtyard of the temple of the LORD with its portico.

column.name: text
column.value: King Solomon sent to Tyre and brought Huram,

column.name: text
column.value: whose mother was a widow from the tribe of Naphtali and whose father was a man of Tyre and a craftsman in bronze. Huram was highly skilled and experienced in all kinds of bronze work. He came to King Solomon and did all the work assigned to him.

column.name: text
column.value: He cast two bronze pillars, each eighteen cubits high and twelve cubits around, by line.

column.name: text
column.value: He also made two capitals of cast bronze to set on the tops of the pillars; each capital was five cubits high.

column.name: text
column.value: A network of interwoven chains festooned the capitals on top of the pillars, seven for each capital.

column.name: text
column.value: He made pomegranates in two rows encircling each network to decorate the capitals on top of the pillars. He did the same for each capital.

column.name: text
column.value: The capitals on top of the pillars in the portico were in the shape of lilies, four cubits high.

column.name: text
column.value: On the capitals of both pillars, above the bowl-shaped part next to the network, were the two hundred pomegranates in rows all around.

column.name: text
column.value: He erected the pillars at the portico of the temple. The pillar to the south he named Jakin and the one to the north Boaz.

column.name: text
column.value: The capitals on top were in the shape of lilies. And so the work on the pillars was completed.

column.name: text
column.value: He made the Sea of cast metal, circular in shape, measuring ten cubits from rim to rim and five cubits high. It took a line of thirty cubits to measure around it.

column.name: text
column.value: Below the rim, gourds encircled it--ten to a cubit. The gourds were cast in two rows in one piece with the Sea.

column.name: text
column.value: The Sea stood on twelve bulls, three facing north, three facing west, three facing south and three facing east. The Sea rested on top of them, and their hindquarters were toward the center.

column.name: text
column.value: It was a handbreadth in thickness, and its rim was like the rim of a cup, like a lily blossom. It held two thousand baths.

column.name: text
column.value: He also made ten movable stands of bronze; each was four cubits long, four wide and three high.

column.name: text
column.value: This is how the stands were made: They had side panels attached to uprights.

column.name: text
column.value: On the panels between the uprights were lions, bulls and cherubim--and on the uprights as well. Above and below the lions and bulls were wreaths of hammered work.

column.name: text
column.value: Each stand had four bronze wheels with bronze axles, and each had a basin resting on four supports, cast with wreaths on each side.

column.name: text
column.value: On the inside of the stand there was an opening that had a circular frame one cubit deep. This opening was round, and with its basework it measured a cubit and a half. Around its opening there was engraving. The panels of the stands were square, not round.

column.name: text
column.value: The four wheels were under the panels, and the axles of the wheels were attached to the stand. The diameter of each wheel was a cubit and a half.

column.name: text
column.value: The wheels were made like chariot wheels; the axles, rims, spokes and hubs were all of cast metal.

column.name: text
column.value: Each stand had four handles, one on each corner, projecting from the stand.

column.name: text
column.value: At the top of the stand there was a circular band half a cubit deep. The supports and panels were attached to the top of the stand.

column.name: text
column.value: He engraved cherubim, lions and palm trees on the surfaces of the supports and on the panels, in every available space, with wreaths all around.

column.name: text
column.value: This is the way he made the ten stands. They were all cast in the same molds and were identical in size and shape.

column.name: text
column.value: He then made ten bronze basins, each holding forty baths and measuring four cubits across, one basin to go on each of the ten stands.

column.name: text
column.value: He placed five of the stands on the south side of the temple and five on the north. He placed the Sea on the south side, at the southeast corner of the temple.

column.name: text
column.value: He also made the basins and shovels and sprinkling bowls. So Huram finished all the work he had undertaken for King Solomon in the temple of the LORD:

column.name: text
column.value: the two pillars; the two bowl-shaped capitals on top of the pillars; the two sets of network decorating the two bowl-shaped capitals on top of the pillars;

column.name: text
column.value: the four hundred pomegranates for the two sets of network (two rows of pomegranates for each network, decorating the bowl-shaped capitals on top of the pillars);

column.name: text
column.value: the ten stands with their ten basins;

column.name: text
column.value: the Sea and the twelve bulls under it;

column.name: text
column.value: the pots, shovels and sprinkling bowls. All these objects that Huram made for King Solomon for the temple of the LORD were of burnished bronze.

column.name: text
column.value: The king had them cast in clay molds in the plain of the Jordan between Succoth and Zarethan.

column.name: text
column.value: Solomon left all these things unweighed, because there were so many; the weight of the bronze was not determined.

column.name: text
column.value: Solomon also made all the furnishings that were in the LORD'S temple: the golden altar; the golden table on which was the bread of the Presence;

column.name: text
column.value: the lampstands of pure gold (five on the right and five on the left, in front of the inner sanctuary); the gold floral work and lamps and tongs;

column.name: text
column.value: the pure gold basins, wick trimmers, sprinkling bowls, dishes and censers; and the gold sockets for the doors of the innermost room, the Most Holy Place, and also for the doors of the main hall of the temple.

column.name: text
column.value: When all the work King Solomon had done for the temple of the LORD was finished, he brought in the things his father David had dedicated--the silver and gold and the furnishings--and he placed them in the treasuries of the LORD'S temple.

column.name: text
column.value: When Solomon had finished building the temple of the LORD and the royal palace, and had achieved all he had desired to do,

column.name: text
column.value: the LORD appeared to him a second time, as he had appeared to him at Gibeon.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD said to him: "I have heard the prayer and plea you have made before me; I have consecrated this temple, which you have built, by putting my Name there forever. My eyes and my heart will always be there.

column.name: text
column.value: "As for you, if you walk before me in integrity of heart and uprightness, as David your father did, and do all I command and observe my decrees and laws,

column.name: text
column.value: I will establish your royal throne over Israel forever, as I promised David your father when I said, 'You shall never fail to have a man on the throne of Israel.'

column.name: text
column.value: "But if you or your sons turn away from me and do not observe the commands and decrees I have given you and go off to serve other gods and worship them,

column.name: text
column.value: then I will cut off Israel from the land I have given them and will reject this temple I have consecrated for my Name. Israel will then become a byword and an object of ridicule among all peoples.

column.name: text
column.value: And though this temple is now imposing, all who pass by will be appalled and will scoff and say, 'Why has the LORD done such a thing to this land and to this temple?'

column.name: text
column.value: People will answer, 'Because they have forsaken the LORD their God, who brought their fathers out of Egypt, and have embraced other gods, worshiping and serving them--that is why the LORD brought all this disaster on them.'"

column.name: text
column.value: At the end of twenty years, during which Solomon built these two buildings--the temple of the LORD and the royal palace--

column.name: text
column.value: King Solomon gave twenty towns in Galilee to Hiram king of Tyre, because Hiram had supplied him with all the cedar and pine and gold he wanted.

column.name: text
column.value: But when Hiram went from Tyre to see the towns that Solomon had given him, he was not pleased with them.

column.name: text
column.value: "What kind of towns are these you have given me, my brother?" he asked. And he called them the Land of Cabul, a name they have to this day.

column.name: text
column.value: Now Hiram had sent to the king 120 talents of gold.

column.name: text
column.value: Here is the account of the forced labor King Solomon conscripted to build the LORD'S temple, his own palace, the supporting terraces, the wall of Jerusalem, and Hazor, Megiddo and Gezer.

column.name: text
column.value: (Pharaoh king of Egypt had attacked and captured Gezer. He had set it on fire. He killed its Canaanite inhabitants and then gave it as a wedding gift to his daughter, Solomon's wife.

column.name: text
column.value: And Solomon rebuilt Gezer.) He built up Lower Beth Horon,

column.name: text
column.value: Baalath, and Tadmor in the desert, within his land,

column.name: text
column.value: as well as all his store cities and the towns for his chariots and for his horses--whatever he desired to build in Jerusalem, in Lebanon and throughout all the territory he ruled.

column.name: text
column.value: All the people left from the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites and Jebusites (these peoples were not Israelites),

column.name: text
column.value: that is, their descendants remaining in the land, whom the Israelites could not exterminate--these Solomon conscripted for his slave labor force, as it is to this day.

column.name: text
column.value: But Solomon did not make slaves of any of the Israelites; they were his fighting men, his government officials, his officers, his captains, and the commanders of his chariots and charioteers.

column.name: text
column.value: They were also the chief officials in charge of Solomon's projects--550 officials supervising the men who did the work.

column.name: text
column.value: After Pharaoh's daughter had come up from the City of David to the palace Solomon had built for her, he constructed the supporting terraces.

column.name: text
column.value: Three times a year Solomon sacrificed burnt offerings and fellowship offerings on the altar he had built for the LORD, burning incense before the LORD along with them, and so fulfilled the temple obligations.

column.name: text
column.value: King Solomon also built ships at Ezion Geber, which is near Elath in Edom, on the shore of the Red Sea.

column.name: text
column.value: And Hiram sent his men--sailors who knew the sea--to serve in the fleet with Solomon's men.

column.name: text
column.value: They sailed to Ophir and brought back 420 talents of gold, which they delivered to King Solomon.

column.name: text
column.value: Rehoboam went to Shechem, for all the Israelites had gone there to make him king.

column.name: text
column.value: When Jeroboam son of Nebat heard this (he was still in Egypt, where he had fled from King Solomon), he returned from Egypt.

column.name: text
column.value: So they sent for Jeroboam, and he and the whole assembly of Israel went to Rehoboam and said to him:

column.name: text
column.value: "Your father put a heavy yoke on us, but now lighten the harsh labor and the heavy yoke he put on us, and we will serve you."

column.name: text
column.value: Rehoboam answered, "Go away for three days and then come back to me." So the people went away.

column.name: text
column.value: Then King Rehoboam consulted the elders who had served his father Solomon during his lifetime. "How would you advise me to answer these people?" he asked.

column.name: text
column.value: They replied, "If today you will be a servant to these people and serve them and give them a favorable answer, they will always be your servants."

column.name: text
column.value: But Rehoboam rejected the advice the elders gave him and consulted the young men who had grown up with him and were serving him.

column.name: text
column.value: He asked them, "What is your advice? How should we answer these people who say to me, 'Lighten the yoke your father put on us'?"

column.name: text
column.value: The young men who had grown up with him replied, "Tell these people who have said to you, 'Your father put a heavy yoke on us, but make our yoke lighter'--tell them, 'My little finger is thicker than my father's waist.

column.name: text
column.value: My father laid on you a heavy yoke; I will make it even heavier. My father scourged you with whips; I will scourge you with scorpions.'"

column.name: text
column.value: Three days later Jeroboam and all the people returned to Rehoboam, as the king had said, "Come back to me in three days."

column.name: text
column.value: The king answered the people harshly. Rejecting the advice given him by the elders,

column.name: text
column.value: he followed the advice of the young men and said, "My father made your yoke heavy; I will make it even heavier. My father scourged you with whips; I will scourge you with scorpions."

column.name: text
column.value: So the king did not listen to the people, for this turn of events was from the LORD, to fulfill the word the LORD had spoken to Jeroboam son of Nebat through Ahijah the Shilonite.

column.name: text
column.value: When all Israel saw that the king refused to listen to them, they answered the king: "What share do we have in David, what part in Jesse's son? To your tents, O Israel! Look after your own house, O David!" So the Israelites went home.

column.name: text
column.value: But as for the Israelites who were living in the towns of Judah, Rehoboam still ruled over them.

column.name: text
column.value: King Rehoboam sent out Adoniram, who was in charge of forced labor, but all Israel stoned him to death. King Rehoboam, however, managed to get into his chariot and escape to Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: So Israel has been in rebellion against the house of David to this day.

column.name: text
column.value: When all the Israelites heard that Jeroboam had returned, they sent and called him to the assembly and made him king over all Israel. Only the tribe of Judah remained loyal to the house of David.

column.name: text
column.value: When Rehoboam arrived in Jerusalem, he mustered the whole house of Judah and the tribe of Benjamin--a hundred and eighty thousand fighting men--to make war against the house of Israel and to regain the kingdom for Rehoboam son of Solomon.

column.name: text
column.value: But this word of God came to Shemaiah the man of God:

column.name: text
column.value: "Say to Rehoboam son of Solomon king of Judah, to the whole house of Judah and Benjamin, and to the rest of the people,

column.name: text
column.value: 'This is what the LORD says: Do not go up to fight against your brothers, the Israelites. Go home, every one of you, for this is my doing.'" So they obeyed the word of the LORD and went home again, as the LORD had ordered.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jeroboam fortified Shechem in the hill country of Ephraim and lived there. From there he went out and built up Peniel.

column.name: text
column.value: Jeroboam thought to himself, "The kingdom will now likely revert to the house of David.

column.name: text
column.value: If these people go up to offer sacrifices at the temple of the LORD in Jerusalem, they will again give their allegiance to their lord, Rehoboam king of Judah. They will kill me and return to King Rehoboam."

column.name: text
column.value: After seeking advice, the king made two golden calves. He said to the people, "It is too much for you to go up to Jerusalem. Here are your gods, O Israel, who brought you up out of Egypt."

column.name: text
column.value: One he set up in Bethel, and the other in Dan.

column.name: text
column.value: And this thing became a sin; the people went even as far as Dan to worship the one there.

column.name: text
column.value: Jeroboam built shrines on high places and appointed priests from all sorts of people, even though they were not Levites.

column.name: text
column.value: He instituted a festival on the fifteenth day of the eighth month, like the festival held in Judah, and offered sacrifices on the altar. This he did in Bethel, sacrificing to the calves he had made. And at Bethel he also installed priests at the high places he had made.

column.name: text
column.value: On the fifteenth day of the eighth month, a month of his own choosing, he offered sacrifices on the altar he had built at Bethel. So he instituted the festival for the Israelites and went up to the altar to make offerings.

column.name: text
column.value: King Solomon, however, loved many foreign women besides Pharaoh's daughter--Moabites, Ammonites, Edomites, Sidonians and Hittites.

column.name: text
column.value: They were from nations about which the LORD had told the Israelites, "You must not intermarry with them, because they will surely turn your hearts after their gods." Nevertheless, Solomon held fast to them in love.

column.name: text
column.value: He had seven hundred wives of royal birth and three hundred concubines, and his wives led him astray.

column.name: text
column.value: As Solomon grew old, his wives turned his heart after other gods, and his heart was not fully devoted to the LORD his God, as the heart of David his father had been.

column.name: text
column.value: He followed Ashtoreth the goddess of the Sidonians, and Molech the detestable god of the Ammonites.

column.name: text
column.value: So Solomon did evil in the eyes of the LORD; he did not follow the LORD completely, as David his father had done.

column.name: text
column.value: On a hill east of Jerusalem, Solomon built a high place for Chemosh the detestable god of Moab, and for Molech the detestable god of the Ammonites.

column.name: text
column.value: He did the same for all his foreign wives, who burned incense and offered sacrifices to their gods.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD became angry with Solomon because his heart had turned away from the LORD, the God of Israel, who had appeared to him twice.

column.name: text
column.value: Although he had forbidden Solomon to follow other gods, Solomon did not keep the LORD'S command.

column.name: text
column.value: So the LORD said to Solomon, "Since this is your attitude and you have not kept my covenant and my decrees, which I commanded you, I will most certainly tear the kingdom away from you and give it to one of your subordinates.

column.name: text
column.value: Nevertheless, for the sake of David your father, I will not do it during your lifetime. I will tear it out of the hand of your son.

column.name: text
column.value: Yet I will not tear the whole kingdom from him, but will give him one tribe for the sake of David my servant and for the sake of Jerusalem, which I have chosen."

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD raised up against Solomon an adversary, Hadad the Edomite, from the royal line of Edom.

column.name: text
column.value: Earlier when David was fighting with Edom, Joab the commander of the army, who had gone up to bury the dead, had struck down all the men in Edom.

column.name: text
column.value: Joab and all the Israelites stayed there for six months, until they had destroyed all the men in Edom.

column.name: text
column.value: But Hadad, still only a boy, fled to Egypt with some Edomite officials who had served his father.

column.name: text
column.value: They set out from Midian and went to Paran. Then taking men from Paran with them, they went to Egypt, to Pharaoh king of Egypt, who gave Hadad a house and land and provided him with food.

column.name: text
column.value: Pharaoh was so pleased with Hadad that he gave him a sister of his own wife, Queen Tahpenes, in marriage.

column.name: text
column.value: The sister of Tahpenes bore him a son named Genubath, whom Tahpenes brought up in the royal palace. There Genubath lived with Pharaoh's own children.

column.name: text
column.value: While he was in Egypt, Hadad heard that David rested with his fathers and that Joab the commander of the army was also dead. Then Hadad said to Pharaoh, "Let me go, that I may return to my own country."

column.name: text
column.value: "What have you lacked here that you want to go back to your own country?" Pharaoh asked. "Nothing," Hadad replied, "but do let me go!"

column.name: text
column.value: And God raised up against Solomon another adversary, Rezon son of Eliada, who had fled from his master, Hadadezer king of Zobah.

column.name: text
column.value: He gathered men around him and became the leader of a band of rebels when David destroyed the forces of Zobah; the rebels went to Damascus, where they settled and took control.

column.name: text
column.value: Rezon was Israel's adversary as long as Solomon lived, adding to the trouble caused by Hadad. So Rezon ruled in Aram and was hostile toward Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: Also, Jeroboam son of Nebat rebelled against the king. He was one of Solomon's officials, an Ephraimite from Zeredah, and his mother was a widow named Zeruah.

column.name: text
column.value: Here is the account of how he rebelled against the king: Solomon had built the supporting terraces and had filled in the gap in the wall of the city of David his father.

column.name: text
column.value: Now Jeroboam was a man of standing, and when Solomon saw how well the young man did his work, he put him in charge of the whole labor force of the house of Joseph.

column.name: text
column.value: About that time Jeroboam was going out of Jerusalem, and Ahijah the prophet of Shiloh met him on the way, wearing a new cloak. The two of them were alone out in the country,

column.name: text
column.value: and Ahijah took hold of the new cloak he was wearing and tore it into twelve pieces.

column.name: text
column.value: Then he said to Jeroboam, "Take ten pieces for yourself, for this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: 'See, I am going to tear the kingdom out of Solomon's hand and give you ten tribes.

column.name: text
column.value: But for the sake of my servant David and the city of Jerusalem, which I have chosen out of all the tribes of Israel, he will have one tribe.

column.name: text
column.value: I will do this because they have forsaken me and worshiped Ashtoreth the goddess of the Sidonians, Chemosh the god of the Moabites, and Molech the god of the Ammonites, and have not walked in my ways, nor done what is right in my eyes, nor kept my statutes and laws as David, Solomon's father, did.

column.name: text
column.value: " 'But I will not take the whole kingdom out of Solomon's hand; I have made him ruler all the days of his life for the sake of David my servant, whom I chose and who observed my commands and statutes.

column.name: text
column.value: I will take the kingdom from his son's hands and give you ten tribes.

column.name: text
column.value: I will give one tribe to his son so that David my servant may always have a lamp before me in Jerusalem, the city where I chose to put my Name.

column.name: text
column.value: However, as for you, I will take you, and you will rule over all that your heart desires; you will be king over Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: If you do whatever I command you and walk in my ways and do what is right in my eyes by keeping my statutes and commands, as David my servant did, I will be with you. I will build you a dynasty as enduring as the one I built for David and will give Israel to you.

column.name: text
column.value: I will humble David's descendants because of this, but not forever.'"

column.name: text
column.value: Solomon tried to kill Jeroboam, but Jeroboam fled to Egypt, to Shishak the king, and stayed there until Solomon's death.

column.name: text
column.value: As for the other events of Solomon's reign--all he did and the wisdom he displayed--are they not written in the book of the annals of Solomon?

column.name: text
column.value: Solomon reigned in Jerusalem over all Israel forty years.

column.name: text
column.value: Then he rested with his fathers and was buried in the city of David his father. And Rehoboam his son succeeded him as king.

column.name: text
column.value: When the queen of Sheba heard about the fame of Solomon and his relation to the name of the LORD, she came to test him with hard questions.

column.name: text
column.value: Arriving at Jerusalem with a very great caravan--with camels carrying spices, large quantities of gold, and precious stones--she came to Solomon and talked with him about all that she had on her mind.

column.name: text
column.value: Solomon answered all her questions; nothing was too hard for the king to explain to her.

column.name: text
column.value: When the queen of Sheba saw all the wisdom of Solomon and the palace he had built,

column.name: text
column.value: the food on his table, the seating of his officials, the attending servants in their robes, his cupbearers, and the burnt offerings he made at the temple of the LORD, she was overwhelmed.

column.name: text
column.value: She said to the king, "The report I heard in my own country about your achievements and your wisdom is true.

column.name: text
column.value: But I did not believe these things until I came and saw with my own eyes. Indeed, not even half was told me; in wisdom and wealth you have far exceeded the report I heard.

column.name: text
column.value: How happy your men must be! How happy your officials, who continually stand before you and hear your wisdom!

column.name: text
column.value: Praise be to the LORD your God, who has delighted in you and placed you on the throne of Israel. Because of the LORD'S eternal love for Israel, he has made you king, to maintain justice and righteousness."

column.name: text
column.value: And she gave the king 120 talents of gold, large quantities of spices, and precious stones. Never again were so many spices brought in as those the queen of Sheba gave to King Solomon.

column.name: text
column.value: (Hiram's ships brought gold from Ophir; and from there they brought great cargoes of almugwood and precious stones.

column.name: text
column.value: The king used the almugwood to make supports for the temple of the LORD and for the royal palace, and to make harps and lyres for the musicians. So much almugwood has never been imported or seen since that day.)

column.name: text
column.value: King Solomon gave the queen of Sheba all she desired and asked for, besides what he had given her out of his royal bounty. Then she left and returned with her retinue to her own country.

column.name: text
column.value: The weight of the gold that Solomon received yearly was 666 talents,

column.name: text
column.value: not including the revenues from merchants and traders and from all the Arabian kings and the governors of the land.

column.name: text
column.value: King Solomon made two hundred large shields of hammered gold; six hundred bekas of gold went into each shield.

column.name: text
column.value: He also made three hundred small shields of hammered gold, with three minas of gold in each shield. The king put them in the Palace of the Forest of Lebanon.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the king made a great throne inlaid with ivory and overlaid with fine gold.

column.name: text
column.value: The throne had six steps, and its back had a rounded top. On both sides of the seat were armrests, with a lion standing beside each of them.

column.name: text
column.value: Twelve lions stood on the six steps, one at either end of each step. Nothing like it had ever been made for any other kingdom.

column.name: text
column.value: All King Solomon's goblets were gold, and all the household articles in the Palace of the Forest of Lebanon were pure gold. Nothing was made of silver, because silver was considered of little value in Solomon's days.

column.name: text
column.value: The king had a fleet of trading ships at sea along with the ships of Hiram. Once every three years it returned, carrying gold, silver and ivory, and apes and baboons.

column.name: text
column.value: King Solomon was greater in riches and wisdom than all the other kings of the earth.

column.name: text
column.value: The whole world sought audience with Solomon to hear the wisdom God had put in his heart.

column.name: text
column.value: Year after year, everyone who came brought a gift--articles of silver and gold, robes, weapons and spices, and horses and mules.

column.name: text
column.value: Solomon accumulated chariots and horses; he had fourteen hundred chariots and twelve thousand horses, which he kept in the chariot cities and also with him in Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: The king made silver as common in Jerusalem as stones, and cedar as plentiful as sycamore-fig trees in the foothills.

column.name: text
column.value: Solomon's horses were imported from Egypt and from Kue--the royal merchants purchased them from Kue.

column.name: text
column.value: They imported a chariot from Egypt for six hundred shekels of silver, and a horse for a hundred and fifty. They also exported them to all the kings of the Hittites and of the Arameans.

column.name: text
column.value: Then King Solomon summoned into his presence at Jerusalem the elders of Israel, all the heads of the tribes and the chiefs of the Israelite families, to bring up the ark of the LORD'S covenant from Zion, the City of David.

column.name: text
column.value: All the men of Israel came together to King Solomon at the time of the festival in the month of Ethanim, the seventh month.

column.name: text
column.value: When all the elders of Israel had arrived, the priests took up the ark,

column.name: text
column.value: and they brought up the ark of the LORD and the Tent of Meeting and all the sacred furnishings in it. The priests and Levites carried them up,

column.name: text
column.value: and King Solomon and the entire assembly of Israel that had gathered about him were before the ark, sacrificing so many sheep and cattle that they could not be recorded or counted.

column.name: text
column.value: The priests then brought the ark of the LORD'S covenant to its place in the inner sanctuary of the temple, the Most Holy Place, and put it beneath the wings of the cherubim.

column.name: text
column.value: The cherubim spread their wings over the place of the ark and overshadowed the ark and its carrying poles.

column.name: text
column.value: These poles were so long that their ends could be seen from the Holy Place in front of the inner sanctuary, but not from outside the Holy Place; and they are still there today.

column.name: text
column.value: There was nothing in the ark except the two stone tablets that Moses had placed in it at Horeb, where the LORD made a covenant with the Israelites after they came out of Egypt.

column.name: text
column.value: When the priests withdrew from the Holy Place, the cloud filled the temple of the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: And the priests could not perform their service because of the cloud, for the glory of the LORD filled his temple.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Solomon said, "The LORD has said that he would dwell in a dark cloud;

column.name: text
column.value: I have indeed built a magnificent temple for you, a place for you to dwell forever."

column.name: text
column.value: While the whole assembly of Israel was standing there, the king turned around and blessed them.

column.name: text
column.value: Then he said: "Praise be to the LORD, the God of Israel, who with his own hand has fulfilled what he promised with his own mouth to my father David. For he said,

column.name: text
column.value: 'Since the day I brought my people Israel out of Egypt, I have not chosen a city in any tribe of Israel to have a temple built for my Name to be there, but I have chosen David to rule my people Israel.'

column.name: text
column.value: "My father David had it in his heart to build a temple for the Name of the LORD, the God of Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: But the LORD said to my father David, 'Because it was in your heart to build a temple for my Name, you did well to have this in your heart.

column.name: text
column.value: Nevertheless, you are not the one to build the temple, but your son, who is your own flesh and blood--he is the one who will build the temple for my Name.'

column.name: text
column.value: "The LORD has kept the promise he made: I have succeeded David my father and now I sit on the throne of Israel, just as the LORD promised, and I have built the temple for the Name of the LORD, the God of Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: I have provided a place there for the ark, in which is the covenant of the LORD that he made with our fathers when he brought them out of Egypt."

column.name: text
column.value: Then Solomon stood before the altar of the LORD in front of the whole assembly of Israel, spread out his hands toward heaven

column.name: text
column.value: and said: "O LORD, God of Israel, there is no God like you in heaven above or on earth below--you who keep your covenant of love with your servants who continue wholeheartedly in your way.

column.name: text
column.value: You have kept your promise to your servant David my father; with your mouth you have promised and with your hand you have fulfilled it--as it is today.

column.name: text
column.value: "Now LORD, God of Israel, keep for your servant David my father the promises you made to him when you said, 'You shall never fail to have a man to sit before me on the throne of Israel, if only your sons are careful in all they do to walk before me as you have done.'

column.name: text
column.value: And now, O God of Israel, let your word that you promised your servant David my father come true.

column.name: text
column.value: "But will God really dwell on earth? The heavens, even the highest heaven, cannot contain you. How much less this temple I have built!

column.name: text
column.value: Yet give attention to your servant's prayer and his plea for mercy, O LORD my God. Hear the cry and the prayer that your servant is praying in your presence this day.

column.name: text
column.value: May your eyes be open toward this temple night and day, this place of which you said, 'My Name shall be there,' so that you will hear the prayer your servant prays toward this place.

column.name: text
column.value: Hear the supplication of your servant and of your people Israel when they pray toward this place. Hear from heaven, your dwelling place, and when you hear, forgive.

column.name: text
column.value: "When a man wrongs his neighbor and is required to take an oath and he comes and swears the oath before your altar in this temple,

column.name: text
column.value: then hear from heaven and act. Judge between your servants, condemning the guilty and bringing down on his own head what he has done. Declare the innocent not guilty, and so establish his innocence.

column.name: text
column.value: "When your people Israel have been defeated by an enemy because they have sinned against you, and when they turn back to you and confess your name, praying and making supplication to you in this temple,

column.name: text
column.value: then hear from heaven and forgive the sin of your people Israel and bring them back to the land you gave to their fathers.

column.name: text
column.value: "When the heavens are shut up and there is no rain because your people have sinned against you, and when they pray toward this place and confess your name and turn from their sin because you have afflicted them,

column.name: text
column.value: then hear from heaven and forgive the sin of your servants, your people Israel. Teach them the right way to live, and send rain on the land you gave your people for an inheritance.

column.name: text
column.value: "When famine or plague comes to the land, or blight or mildew, locusts or grasshoppers, or when an enemy besieges them in any of their cities, whatever disaster or disease may come,

column.name: text
column.value: and when a prayer or plea is made by any of your people Israel--each one aware of the afflictions of his own heart, and spreading out his hands toward this temple--

column.name: text
column.value: then hear from heaven, your dwelling place. Forgive and act; deal with each man according to all he does, since you know his heart (for you alone know the hearts of all men),

column.name: text
column.value: so that they will fear you all the time they live in the land you gave our fathers.

column.name: text
column.value: "As for the foreigner who does not belong to your people Israel but has come from a distant land because of your name--

column.name: text
column.value: for men will hear of your great name and your mighty hand and your outstretched arm--when he comes and prays toward this temple,

column.name: text
column.value: then hear from heaven, your dwelling place, and do whatever the foreigner asks of you, so that all the peoples of the earth may know your name and fear you, as do your own people Israel, and may know that this house I have built bears your Name.

column.name: text
column.value: "When your people go to war against their enemies, wherever you send them, and when they pray to the LORD toward the city you have chosen and the temple I have built for your Name,

column.name: text
column.value: then hear from heaven their prayer and their plea, and uphold their cause.

column.name: text
column.value: "When they sin against you--for there is no one who does not sin--and you become angry with them and give them over to the enemy, who takes them captive to his own land, far away or near;

column.name: text
column.value: and if they have a change of heart in the land where they are held captive, and repent and plead with you in the land of their conquerors and say, 'We have sinned, we have done wrong, we have acted wickedly';

column.name: text
column.value: and if they turn back to you with all their heart and soul in the land of their enemies who took them captive, and pray to you toward the land you gave their fathers, toward the city you have chosen and the temple I have built for your Name;

column.name: text
column.value: then from heaven, your dwelling place, hear their prayer and their plea, and uphold their cause.

column.name: text
column.value: And forgive your people, who have sinned against you; forgive all the offenses they have committed against you, and cause their conquerors to show them mercy;

column.name: text
column.value: for they are your people and your inheritance, whom you brought out of Egypt, out of that iron-smelting furnace.

column.name: text
column.value: "May your eyes be open to your servant's plea and to the plea of your people Israel, and may you listen to them whenever they cry out to you.

column.name: text
column.value: For you singled them out from all the nations of the world to be your own inheritance, just as you declared through your servant Moses when you, O Sovereign LORD, brought our fathers out of Egypt."

column.name: text
column.value: When Solomon had finished all these prayers and supplications to the LORD, he rose from before the altar of the LORD, where he had been kneeling with his hands spread out toward heaven.

column.name: text
column.value: He stood and blessed the whole assembly of Israel in a loud voice, saying:

column.name: text
column.value: "Praise be to the LORD, who has given rest to his people Israel just as he promised. Not one word has failed of all the good promises he gave through his servant Moses.

column.name: text
column.value: May the LORD our God be with us as he was with our fathers; may he never leave us nor forsake us.

column.name: text
column.value: May he turn our hearts to him, to walk in all his ways and to keep the commands, decrees and regulations he gave our fathers.

column.name: text
column.value: And may these words of mine, which I have prayed before the LORD, be near to the LORD our God day and night, that he may uphold the cause of his servant and the cause of his people Israel according to each day's need,

column.name: text
column.value: so that all the peoples of the earth may know that the LORD is God and that there is no other.

column.name: text
column.value: But your hearts must be fully committed to the LORD our God, to live by his decrees and obey his commands, as at this time."

column.name: text
column.value: Then the king and all Israel with him offered sacrifices before the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: Solomon offered a sacrifice of fellowship offerings to the LORD: twenty-two thousand cattle and a hundred and twenty thousand sheep and goats. So the king and all the Israelites dedicated the temple of the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: On that same day the king consecrated the middle part of the courtyard in front of the temple of the LORD, and there he offered burnt offerings, grain offerings and the fat of the fellowship offerings, because the bronze altar before the LORD was too small to hold the burnt offerings, the grain offerings and the fat of the fellowship offerings.

column.name: text
column.value: So Solomon observed the festival at that time, and all Israel with him--a vast assembly, people from Lebo Hamath to the Wadi of Egypt. They celebrated it before the LORD our God for seven days and seven days more, fourteen days in all.

column.name: text
column.value: On the following day he sent the people away. They blessed the king and then went home, joyful and glad in heart for all the good things the LORD had done for his servant David and his people Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: By the word of the LORD a man of God came from Judah to Bethel, as Jeroboam was standing by the altar to make an offering.

column.name: text
column.value: He cried out against the altar by the word of the LORD: "O altar, altar! This is what the LORD says: 'A son named Josiah will be born to the house of David. On you he will sacrifice the priests of the high places who now make offerings here, and human bones will be burned on you.'"

column.name: text
column.value: That same day the man of God gave a sign: "This is the sign the LORD has declared: The altar will be split apart and the ashes on it will be poured out."

column.name: text
column.value: When King Jeroboam heard what the man of God cried out against the altar at Bethel, he stretched out his hand from the altar and said, "Seize him!" But the hand he stretched out toward the man shriveled up, so that he could not pull it back.

column.name: text
column.value: Also, the altar was split apart and its ashes poured out according to the sign given by the man of God by the word of the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the king said to the man of God, "Intercede with the LORD your God and pray for me that my hand may be restored." So the man of God interceded with the LORD, and the king's hand was restored and became as it was before.

column.name: text
column.value: The king said to the man of God, "Come home with me and have something to eat, and I will give you a gift."

column.name: text
column.value: But the man of God answered the king, "Even if you were to give me half your possessions, I would not go with you, nor would I eat bread or drink water here.

column.name: text
column.value: For I was commanded by the word of the LORD: 'You must not eat bread or drink water or return by the way you came.'"

column.name: text
column.value: So he took another road and did not return by the way he had come to Bethel.

column.name: text
column.value: Now there was a certain old prophet living in Bethel, whose sons came and told him all that the man of God had done there that day. They also told their father what he had said to the king.

column.name: text
column.value: Their father asked them, "Which way did he go?" And his sons showed him which road the man of God from Judah had taken.

column.name: text
column.value: So he said to his sons, "Saddle the donkey for me." And when they had saddled the donkey for him, he mounted it

column.name: text
column.value: and rode after the man of God. He found him sitting under an oak tree and asked, "Are you the man of God who came from Judah?" "I am," he replied.

column.name: text
column.value: So the prophet said to him, "Come home with me and eat."

column.name: text
column.value: The man of God said, "I cannot turn back and go with you, nor can I eat bread or drink water with you in this place.

column.name: text
column.value: I have been told by the word of the LORD: 'You must not eat bread or drink water there or return by the way you came.'"

column.name: text
column.value: The old prophet answered, "I too am a prophet, as you are. And an angel said to me by the word of the LORD: 'Bring him back with you to your house so that he may eat bread and drink water.'" (But he was lying to him.)

column.name: text
column.value: So the man of God returned with him and ate and drank in his house.

column.name: text
column.value: While they were sitting at the table, the word of the LORD came to the old prophet who had brought him back.

column.name: text
column.value: He cried out to the man of God who had come from Judah, "This is what the LORD says: 'You have defied the word of the LORD and have not kept the command the LORD your God gave you.

column.name: text
column.value: You came back and ate bread and drank water in the place where he told you not to eat or drink. Therefore your body will not be buried in the tomb of your fathers.'"

column.name: text
column.value: When the man of God had finished eating and drinking, the prophet who had brought him back saddled his donkey for him.

column.name: text
column.value: As he went on his way, a lion met him on the road and killed him, and his body was thrown down on the road, with both the donkey and the lion standing beside it.

column.name: text
column.value: Some people who passed by saw the body thrown down there, with the lion standing beside the body, and they went and reported it in the city where the old prophet lived.

column.name: text
column.value: When the prophet who had brought him back from his journey heard of it, he said, "It is the man of God who defied the word of the LORD. The LORD has given him over to the lion, which has mauled him and killed him, as the word of the LORD had warned him."

column.name: text
column.value: The prophet said to his sons, "Saddle the donkey for me," and they did so.

column.name: text
column.value: Then he went out and found the body thrown down on the road, with the donkey and the lion standing beside it. The lion had neither eaten the body nor mauled the donkey.

column.name: text
column.value: So the prophet picked up the body of the man of God, laid it on the donkey, and brought it back to his own city to mourn for him and bury him.

column.name: text
column.value: Then he laid the body in his own tomb, and they mourned over him and said, "Oh, my brother!"

column.name: text
column.value: After burying him, he said to his sons, "When I die, bury me in the grave where the man of God is buried; lay my bones beside his bones.

column.name: text
column.value: For the message he declared by the word of the LORD against the altar in Bethel and against all the shrines on the high places in the towns of Samaria will certainly come true."

column.name: text
column.value: Even after this, Jeroboam did not change his evil ways, but once more appointed priests for the high places from all sorts of people. Anyone who wanted to become a priest he consecrated for the high places.

column.name: text
column.value: This was the sin of the house of Jeroboam that led to its downfall and to its destruction from the face of the earth.

column.name: text
column.value: At that time Abijah son of Jeroboam became ill,

column.name: text
column.value: and Jeroboam said to his wife, "Go, disguise yourself, so you won't be recognized as the wife of Jeroboam. Then go to Shiloh. Ahijah the prophet is there--the one who told me I would be king over this people.

column.name: text
column.value: Take ten loaves of bread with you, some cakes and a jar of honey, and go to him. He will tell you what will happen to the boy."

column.name: text
column.value: So Jeroboam's wife did what he said and went to Ahijah's house in Shiloh. Now Ahijah could not see; his sight was gone because of his age.

column.name: text
column.value: But the LORD had told Ahijah, "Jeroboam's wife is coming to ask you about her son, for he is ill, and you are to give her such and such an answer. When she arrives, she will pretend to be someone else."

column.name: text
column.value: So when Ahijah heard the sound of her footsteps at the door, he said, "Come in, wife of Jeroboam. Why this pretense? I have been sent to you with bad news.

column.name: text
column.value: Go, tell Jeroboam that this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: 'I raised you up from among the people and made you a leader over my people Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: I tore the kingdom away from the house of David and gave it to you, but you have not been like my servant David, who kept my commands and followed me with all his heart, doing only what was right in my eyes.

column.name: text
column.value: You have done more evil than all who lived before you. You have made for yourself other gods, idols made of metal; you have provoked me to anger and thrust me behind your back.

column.name: text
column.value: " 'Because of this, I am going to bring disaster on the house of Jeroboam. I will cut off from Jeroboam every last male in Israel--slave or free. I will burn up the house of Jeroboam as one burns dung, until it is all gone.

column.name: text
column.value: Dogs will eat those belonging to Jeroboam who die in the city, and the birds of the air will feed on those who die in the country. The LORD has spoken!'

column.name: text
column.value: "As for you, go back home. When you set foot in your city, the boy will die.

column.name: text
column.value: All Israel will mourn for him and bury him. He is the only one belonging to Jeroboam who will be buried, because he is the only one in the house of Jeroboam in whom the LORD, the God of Israel, has found anything good.

column.name: text
column.value: "The LORD will raise up for himself a king over Israel who will cut off the family of Jeroboam. This is the day! What? Yes, even now.

column.name: text
column.value: And the LORD will strike Israel, so that it will be like a reed swaying in the water. He will uproot Israel from this good land that he gave to their forefathers and scatter them beyond the River, because they provoked the LORD to anger by making Asherah poles.

column.name: text
column.value: And he will give Israel up because of the sins Jeroboam has committed and has caused Israel to commit."

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jeroboam's wife got up and left and went to Tirzah. As soon as she stepped over the threshold of the house, the boy died.

column.name: text
column.value: They buried him, and all Israel mourned for him, as the LORD had said through his servant the prophet Ahijah.

column.name: text
column.value: The other events of Jeroboam's reign, his wars and how he ruled, are written in the book of the annals of the kings of Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: He reigned for twenty-two years and then rested with his fathers. And Nadab his son succeeded him as king.

column.name: text
column.value: Rehoboam son of Solomon was king in Judah. He was forty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned seventeen years in Jerusalem, the city the LORD had chosen out of all the tribes of Israel in which to put his Name. His mother's name was Naamah; she was an Ammonite.

column.name: text
column.value: Judah did evil in the eyes of the LORD. By the sins they committed they stirred up his jealous anger more than their fathers had done.

column.name: text
column.value: They also set up for themselves high places, sacred stones and Asherah poles on every high hill and under every spreading tree.

column.name: text
column.value: There were even male shrine prostitutes in the land; the people engaged in all the detestable practices of the nations the LORD had driven out before the Israelites.

column.name: text
column.value: In the fifth year of King Rehoboam, Shishak king of Egypt attacked Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: He carried off the treasures of the temple of the LORD and the treasures of the royal palace. He took everything, including all the gold shields Solomon had made.

column.name: text
column.value: So King Rehoboam made bronze shields to replace them and assigned these to the commanders of the guard on duty at the entrance to the royal palace.

column.name: text
column.value: Whenever the king went to the LORD'S temple, the guards bore the shields, and afterward they returned them to the guardroom.

column.name: text
column.value: As for the other events of Rehoboam's reign, and all he did, are they not written in the book of the annals of the kings of Judah?

column.name: text
column.value: There was continual warfare between Rehoboam and Jeroboam.

column.name: text
column.value: And Rehoboam rested with his fathers and was buried with them in the City of David. His mother's name was Naamah; she was an Ammonite. And Abijah his son succeeded him as king.

column.name: text
column.value: In the eighteenth year of the reign of Jeroboam son of Nebat, Abijah became king of Judah,

column.name: text
column.value: and he reigned in Jerusalem three years. His mother's name was Maacah daughter of Abishalom.

column.name: text
column.value: He committed all the sins his father had done before him; his heart was not fully devoted to the LORD his God, as the heart of David his forefather had been.

column.name: text
column.value: Nevertheless, for David's sake the LORD his God gave him a lamp in Jerusalem by raising up a son to succeed him and by making Jerusalem strong.

column.name: text
column.value: For David had done what was right in the eyes of the LORD and had not failed to keep any of the LORD'S commands all the days of his life--except in the case of Uriah the Hittite.

column.name: text
column.value: There was war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam throughout Abijah's lifetime.

column.name: text
column.value: As for the other events of Abijah's reign, and all he did, are they not written in the book of the annals of the kings of Judah? There was war between Abijah and Jeroboam.

column.name: text
column.value: And Abijah rested with his fathers and was buried in the City of David. And Asa his son succeeded him as king.

column.name: text
column.value: In the twentieth year of Jeroboam king of Israel, Asa became king of Judah,

column.name: text
column.value: and he reigned in Jerusalem forty-one years. His grandmother's name was Maacah daughter of Abishalom.

column.name: text
column.value: Asa did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, as his father David had done.

column.name: text
column.value: He expelled the male shrine prostitutes from the land and got rid of all the idols his fathers had made.

column.name: text
column.value: He even deposed his grandmother Maacah from her position as queen mother, because she had made a repulsive Asherah pole. Asa cut the pole down and burned it in the Kidron Valley.

column.name: text
column.value: Although he did not remove the high places, Asa's heart was fully committed to the LORD all his life.

column.name: text
column.value: He brought into the temple of the LORD the silver and gold and the articles that he and his father had dedicated.

column.name: text
column.value: There was war between Asa and Baasha king of Israel throughout their reigns.

column.name: text
column.value: Baasha king of Israel went up against Judah and fortified Ramah to prevent anyone from leaving or entering the territory of Asa king of Judah.

column.name: text
column.value: Asa then took all the silver and gold that was left in the treasuries of the LORD'S temple and of his own palace. He entrusted it to his officials and sent them to Ben-Hadad son of Tabrimmon, the son of Hezion, the king of Aram, who was ruling in Damascus.

column.name: text
column.value: "Let there be a treaty between me and you," he said, "as there was between my father and your father. See, I am sending you a gift of silver and gold. Now break your treaty with Baasha king of Israel so he will withdraw from me."

column.name: text
column.value: Ben-Hadad agreed with King Asa and sent the commanders of his forces against the towns of Israel. He conquered Ijon, Dan, Abel Beth Maacah and all Kinnereth in addition to Naphtali.

column.name: text
column.value: When Baasha heard this, he stopped building Ramah and withdrew to Tirzah.

column.name: text
column.value: Then King Asa issued an order to all Judah--no one was exempt--and they carried away from Ramah the stones and timber Baasha had been using there. With them King Asa built up Geba in Benjamin, and also Mizpah.

column.name: text
column.value: As for all the other events of Asa's reign, all his achievements, all he did and the cities he built, are they not written in the book of the annals of the kings of Judah? In his old age, however, his feet became diseased.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Asa rested with his fathers and was buried with them in the city of his father David. And Jehoshaphat his son succeeded him as king.

column.name: text
column.value: Nadab son of Jeroboam became king of Israel in the second year of Asa king of Judah, and he reigned over Israel two years.

column.name: text
column.value: He did evil in the eyes of the LORD, walking in the ways of his father and in his sin, which he had caused Israel to commit.

column.name: text
column.value: Baasha son of Ahijah of the house of Issachar plotted against him, and he struck him down at Gibbethon, a Philistine town, while Nadab and all Israel were besieging it.

column.name: text
column.value: Baasha killed Nadab in the third year of Asa king of Judah and succeeded him as king.

column.name: text
column.value: As soon as he began to reign, he killed Jeroboam's whole family. He did not leave Jeroboam anyone that breathed, but destroyed them all, according to the word of the LORD given through his servant Ahijah the Shilonite--

column.name: text
column.value: because of the sins Jeroboam had committed and had caused Israel to commit, and because he provoked the LORD, the God of Israel, to anger.

column.name: text
column.value: As for the other events of Nadab's reign, and all he did, are they not written in the book of the annals of the kings of Israel?

column.name: text
column.value: There was war between Asa and Baasha king of Israel throughout their reigns.

column.name: text
column.value: In the third year of Asa king of Judah, Baasha son of Ahijah became king of all Israel in Tirzah, and he reigned twenty-four years.

column.name: text
column.value: He did evil in the eyes of the LORD, walking in the ways of Jeroboam and in his sin, which he had caused Israel to commit.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the word of the LORD came to Jehu son of Hanani against Baasha:

column.name: text
column.value: "I lifted you up from the dust and made you leader of my people Israel, but you walked in the ways of Jeroboam and caused my people Israel to sin and to provoke me to anger by their sins.

column.name: text
column.value: So I am about to consume Baasha and his house, and I will make your house like that of Jeroboam son of Nebat.

column.name: text
column.value: Dogs will eat those belonging to Baasha who die in the city, and the birds of the air will feed on those who die in the country."

column.name: text
column.value: As for the other events of Baasha's reign, what he did and his achievements, are they not written in the book of the annals of the kings of Israel?

column.name: text
column.value: Baasha rested with his fathers and was buried in Tirzah. And Elah his son succeeded him as king.

column.name: text
column.value: Moreover, the word of the LORD came through the prophet Jehu son of Hanani to Baasha and his house, because of all the evil he had done in the eyes of the LORD, provoking him to anger by the things he did, and becoming like the house of Jeroboam--and also because he destroyed it.

column.name: text
column.value: In the twenty-sixth year of Asa king of Judah, Elah son of Baasha became king of Israel, and he reigned in Tirzah two years.

column.name: text
column.value: Zimri, one of his officials, who had command of half his chariots, plotted against him. Elah was in Tirzah at the time, getting drunk in the home of Arza, the man in charge of the palace at Tirzah.

column.name: text
column.value: Zimri came in, struck him down and killed him in the twenty-seventh year of Asa king of Judah. Then he succeeded him as king.

column.name: text
column.value: As soon as he began to reign and was seated on the throne, he killed off Baasha's whole family. He did not spare a single male, whether relative or friend.

column.name: text
column.value: So Zimri destroyed the whole family of Baasha, in accordance with the word of the LORD spoken against Baasha through the prophet Jehu--

column.name: text
column.value: because of all the sins Baasha and his son Elah had committed and had caused Israel to commit, so that they provoked the LORD, the God of Israel, to anger by their worthless idols.

column.name: text
column.value: As for the other events of Elah's reign, and all he did, are they not written in the book of the annals of the kings of Israel?

column.name: text
column.value: In the twenty-seventh year of Asa king of Judah, Zimri reigned in Tirzah seven days. The army was encamped near Gibbethon, a Philistine town.

column.name: text
column.value: When the Israelites in the camp heard that Zimri had plotted against the king and murdered him, they proclaimed Omri, the commander of the army, king over Israel that very day there in the camp.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Omri and all the Israelites with him withdrew from Gibbethon and laid siege to Tirzah.

column.name: text
column.value: When Zimri saw that the city was taken, he went into the citadel of the royal palace and set the palace on fire around him. So he died,

column.name: text
column.value: because of the sins he had committed, doing evil in the eyes of the LORD and walking in the ways of Jeroboam and in the sin he had committed and had caused Israel to commit.

column.name: text
column.value: As for the other events of Zimri's reign, and the rebellion he carried out, are they not written in the book of the annals of the kings of Israel?

column.name: text
column.value: Then the people of Israel were split into two factions; half supported Tibni son of Ginath for king, and the other half supported Omri.

column.name: text
column.value: But Omri's followers proved stronger than those of Tibni son of Ginath. So Tibni died and Omri became king.

column.name: text
column.value: In the thirty-first year of Asa king of Judah, Omri became king of Israel, and he reigned twelve years, six of them in Tirzah.

column.name: text
column.value: He bought the hill of Samaria from Shemer for two talents of silver and built a city on the hill, calling it Samaria, after Shemer, the name of the former owner of the hill.

column.name: text
column.value: But Omri did evil in the eyes of the LORD and sinned more than all those before him.

column.name: text
column.value: He walked in all the ways of Jeroboam son of Nebat and in his sin, which he had caused Israel to commit, so that they provoked the LORD, the God of Israel, to anger by their worthless idols.

column.name: text
column.value: As for the other events of Omri's reign, what he did and the things he achieved, are they not written in the book of the annals of the kings of Israel?

column.name: text
column.value: Omri rested with his fathers and was buried in Samaria. And Ahab his son succeeded him as king.

column.name: text
column.value: In the thirty-eighth year of Asa king of Judah, Ahab son of Omri became king of Israel, and he reigned in Samaria over Israel twenty-two years.

column.name: text
column.value: Ahab son of Omri did more evil in the eyes of the LORD than any of those before him.

column.name: text
column.value: He not only considered it trivial to commit the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, but he also married Jezebel daughter of Ethbaal king of the Sidonians, and began to serve Baal and worship him.

column.name: text
column.value: He set up an altar for Baal in the temple of Baal that he built in Samaria.

column.name: text
column.value: Ahab also made an Asherah pole and did more to provoke the LORD, the God of Israel, to anger than did all the kings of Israel before him.

column.name: text
column.value: In Ahab's time, Hiel of Bethel rebuilt Jericho. He laid its foundations at the cost of his firstborn son Abiram, and he set up its gates at the cost of his youngest son Segub, in accordance with the word of the LORD spoken by Joshua son of Nun.

column.name: text
column.value: Now Elijah the Tishbite, from Tishbe in Gilead, said to Ahab, "As the LORD, the God of Israel, lives, whom I serve, there will be neither dew nor rain in the next few years except at my word."

column.name: text
column.value: Then the word of the LORD came to Elijah:

column.name: text
column.value: "Leave here, turn eastward and hide in the Kerith Ravine, east of the Jordan.

column.name: text
column.value: You will drink from the brook, and I have ordered the ravens to feed you there."

column.name: text
column.value: So he did what the LORD had told him. He went to the Kerith Ravine, east of the Jordan, and stayed there.

column.name: text
column.value: The ravens brought him bread and meat in the morning and bread and meat in the evening, and he drank from the brook.

column.name: text
column.value: Some time later the brook dried up because there had been no rain in the land.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the word of the LORD came to him:

column.name: text
column.value: "Go at once to Zarephath of Sidon and stay there. I have commanded a widow in that place to supply you with food."

column.name: text
column.value: So he went to Zarephath. When he came to the town gate, a widow was there gathering sticks. He called to her and asked, "Would you bring me a little water in a jar so I may have a drink?"

column.name: text
column.value: As she was going to get it, he called, "And bring me, please, a piece of bread."

column.name: text
column.value: "As surely as the LORD your God lives," she replied, "I don't have any bread--only a handful of flour in a jar and a little oil in a jug. I am gathering a few sticks to take home and make a meal for myself and my son, that we may eat it--and die."

column.name: text
column.value: Elijah said to her, "Don't be afraid. Go home and do as you have said. But first make a small cake of bread for me from what you have and bring it to me, and then make something for yourself and your son.

column.name: text
column.value: For this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: 'The jar of flour will not be used up and the jug of oil will not run dry until the day the LORD gives rain on the land.'"

column.name: text
column.value: She went away and did as Elijah had told her. So there was food every day for Elijah and for the woman and her family.

column.name: text
column.value: For the jar of flour was not used up and the jug of oil did not run dry, in keeping with the word of the LORD spoken by Elijah.

column.name: text
column.value: Some time later the son of the woman who owned the house became ill. He grew worse and worse, and finally stopped breathing.

column.name: text
column.value: She said to Elijah, "What do you have against me, man of God? Did you come to remind me of my sin and kill my son?"

column.name: text
column.value: "Give me your son," Elijah replied. He took him from her arms, carried him to the upper room where he was staying, and laid him on his bed.

column.name: text
column.value: Then he cried out to the LORD, "O LORD my God, have you brought tragedy also upon this widow I am staying with, by causing her son to die?"

column.name: text
column.value: Then he stretched himself out on the boy three times and cried to the LORD, "O LORD my God, let this boy's life return to him!"

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD heard Elijah's cry, and the boy's life returned to him, and he lived.

column.name: text
column.value: Elijah picked up the child and carried him down from the room into the house. He gave him to his mother and said, "Look, your son is alive!"

column.name: text
column.value: Then the woman said to Elijah, "Now I know that you are a man of God and that the word of the LORD from your mouth is the truth."

column.name: text
column.value: After a long time, in the third year, the word of the LORD came to Elijah: "Go and present yourself to Ahab, and I will send rain on the land."

column.name: text
column.value: So Elijah went to present himself to Ahab. Now the famine was severe in Samaria,

column.name: text
column.value: and Ahab had summoned Obadiah, who was in charge of his palace. (Obadiah was a devout believer in the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: While Jezebel was killing off the LORD'S prophets, Obadiah had taken a hundred prophets and hidden them in two caves, fifty in each, and had supplied them with food and water.)

column.name: text
column.value: Ahab had said to Obadiah, "Go through the land to all the springs and valleys. Maybe we can find some grass to keep the horses and mules alive so we will not have to kill any of our animals."

column.name: text
column.value: So they divided the land they were to cover, Ahab going in one direction and Obadiah in another.

column.name: text
column.value: As Obadiah was walking along, Elijah met him. Obadiah recognized him, bowed down to the ground, and said, "Is it really you, my lord Elijah?"

column.name: text
column.value: "Yes," he replied. "Go tell your master, 'Elijah is here.'"

column.name: text
column.value: "What have I done wrong," asked Obadiah, "that you are handing your servant over to Ahab to be put to death?

column.name: text
column.value: As surely as the LORD your God lives, there is not a nation or kingdom where my master has not sent someone to look for you. And whenever a nation or kingdom claimed you were not there, he made them swear they could not find you.

column.name: text
column.value: But now you tell me to go to my master and say, 'Elijah is here.'

column.name: text
column.value: I don't know where the Spirit of the LORD may carry you when I leave you. If I go and tell Ahab and he doesn't find you, he will kill me. Yet I your servant have worshiped the LORD since my youth.

column.name: text
column.value: Haven't you heard, my lord, what I did while Jezebel was killing the prophets of the LORD? I hid a hundred of the LORD'S prophets in two caves, fifty in each, and supplied them with food and water.

column.name: text
column.value: And now you tell me to go to my master and say, 'Elijah is here.' He will kill me!"

column.name: text
column.value: Elijah said, "As the LORD Almighty lives, whom I serve, I will surely present myself to Ahab today."

column.name: text
column.value: So Obadiah went to meet Ahab and told him, and Ahab went to meet Elijah.

column.name: text
column.value: When he saw Elijah, he said to him, "Is that you, you troubler of Israel?"

column.name: text
column.value: "I have not made trouble for Israel," Elijah replied. "But you and your father's family have. You have abandoned the LORD'S commands and have followed the Baals.

column.name: text
column.value: Now summon the people from all over Israel to meet me on Mount Carmel. And bring the four hundred and fifty prophets of Baal and the four hundred prophets of Asherah, who eat at Jezebel's table."

column.name: text
column.value: So Ahab sent word throughout all Israel and assembled the prophets on Mount Carmel.

column.name: text
column.value: Elijah went before the people and said, "How long will you waver between two opinions? If the LORD is God, follow him; but if Baal is God, follow him." But the people said nothing.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Elijah said to them, "I am the only one of the LORD'S prophets left, but Baal has four hundred and fifty prophets.

column.name: text
column.value: Get two bulls for us. Let them choose one for themselves, and let them cut it into pieces and put it on the wood but not set fire to it. I will prepare the other bull and put it on the wood but not set fire to it.

column.name: text
column.value: Then you call on the name of your god, and I will call on the name of the LORD. The god who answers by fire--he is God." Then all the people said, "What you say is good."

column.name: text
column.value: Elijah said to the prophets of Baal, "Choose one of the bulls and prepare it first, since there are so many of you. Call on the name of your god, but do not light the fire."

column.name: text
column.value: So they took the bull given them and prepared it. Then they called on the name of Baal from morning till noon. "O Baal, answer us!" they shouted. But there was no response; no one answered. And they danced around the altar they had made.

column.name: text
column.value: At noon Elijah began to taunt them. "Shout louder!" he said. "Surely he is a god! Perhaps he is deep in thought, or busy, or traveling. Maybe he is sleeping and must be awakened."

column.name: text
column.value: So they shouted louder and slashed themselves with swords and spears, as was their custom, until their blood flowed.

column.name: text
column.value: Midday passed, and they continued their frantic prophesying until the time for the evening sacrifice. But there was no response, no one answered, no one paid attention.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Elijah said to all the people, "Come here to me." They came to him, and he repaired the altar of the LORD, which was in ruins.

column.name: text
column.value: Elijah took twelve stones, one for each of the tribes descended from Jacob, to whom the word of the LORD had come, saying, "Your name shall be Israel."

column.name: text
column.value: With the stones he built an altar in the name of the LORD, and he dug a trench around it large enough to hold two seahs of seed.

column.name: text
column.value: He arranged the wood, cut the bull into pieces and laid it on the wood. Then he said to them, "Fill four large jars with water and pour it on the offering and on the wood."

column.name: text
