column.value: "Do it again," he said, and they did it again. "Do it a third time," he ordered, and they did it the third time.

column.name: text
column.value: The water ran down around the altar and even filled the trench.

column.name: text
column.value: At the time of sacrifice, the prophet Elijah stepped forward and prayed: "O LORD, God of Abraham, Isaac and Israel, let it be known today that you are God in Israel and that I am your servant and have done all these things at your command.

column.name: text
column.value: Answer me, O LORD, answer me, so these people will know that you, O LORD, are God, and that you are turning their hearts back again."

column.name: text
column.value: Then the fire of the LORD fell and burned up the sacrifice, the wood, the stones and the soil, and also licked up the water in the trench.

column.name: text
column.value: When all the people saw this, they fell prostrate and cried, "The LORD--he is God! The LORD--he is God!"

column.name: text
column.value: Then Elijah commanded them, "Seize the prophets of Baal. Don't let anyone get away!" They seized them, and Elijah had them brought down to the Kishon Valley and slaughtered there.

column.name: text
column.value: And Elijah said to Ahab, "Go, eat and drink, for there is the sound of a heavy rain."

column.name: text
column.value: So Ahab went off to eat and drink, but Elijah climbed to the top of Carmel, bent down to the ground and put his face between his knees.

column.name: text
column.value: "Go and look toward the sea," he told his servant. And he went up and looked. "There is nothing there," he said. Seven times Elijah said, "Go back."

column.name: text
column.value: The seventh time the servant reported, "A cloud as small as a man's hand is rising from the sea." So Elijah said, "Go and tell Ahab, 'Hitch up your chariot and go down before the rain stops you.'"

column.name: text
column.value: Meanwhile, the sky grew black with clouds, the wind rose, a heavy rain came on and Ahab rode off to Jezreel.

column.name: text
column.value: The power of the LORD came upon Elijah and, tucking his cloak into his belt, he ran ahead of Ahab all the way to Jezreel.

column.name: text
column.value: Now Ahab told Jezebel everything Elijah had done and how he had killed all the prophets with the sword.

column.name: text
column.value: So Jezebel sent a messenger to Elijah to say, "May the gods deal with me, be it ever so severely, if by this time tomorrow I do not make your life like that of one of them."

column.name: text
column.value: Elijah was afraid and ran for his life. When he came to Beersheba in Judah, he left his servant there,

column.name: text
column.value: while he himself went a day's journey into the desert. He came to a broom tree, sat down under it and prayed that he might die. "I have had enough, LORD," he said. "Take my life; I am no better than my ancestors."

column.name: text
column.value: Then he lay down under the tree and fell asleep. All at once an angel touched him and said, "Get up and eat."

column.name: text
column.value: He looked around, and there by his head was a cake of bread baked over hot coals, and a jar of water. He ate and drank and then lay down again.

column.name: text
column.value: The angel of the LORD came back a second time and touched him and said, "Get up and eat, for the journey is too much for you."

column.name: text
column.value: So he got up and ate and drank. Strengthened by that food, he traveled forty days and forty nights until he reached Horeb, the mountain of God.

column.name: text
column.value: There he went into a cave and spent the night. And the word of the LORD came to him: "What are you doing here, Elijah?"

column.name: text
column.value: He replied, "I have been very zealous for the LORD God Almighty. The Israelites have rejected your covenant, broken down your altars, and put your prophets to death with the sword. I am the only one left, and now they are trying to kill me too."

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD said, "Go out and stand on the mountain in the presence of the LORD, for the LORD is about to pass by." Then a great and powerful wind tore the mountains apart and shattered the rocks before the LORD, but the LORD was not in the wind. After the wind there was an earthquake, but the LORD was not in the earthquake.

column.name: text
column.value: After the earthquake came a fire, but the LORD was not in the fire. And after the fire came a gentle whisper.

column.name: text
column.value: When Elijah heard it, he pulled his cloak over his face and went out and stood at the mouth of the cave. Then a voice said to him, "What are you doing here, Elijah?"

column.name: text
column.value: He replied, "I have been very zealous for the LORD God Almighty. The Israelites have rejected your covenant, broken down your altars, and put your prophets to death with the sword. I am the only one left, and now they are trying to kill me too."

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD said to him, "Go back the way you came, and go to the Desert of Damascus. When you get there, anoint Hazael king over Aram.

column.name: text
column.value: Also, anoint Jehu son of Nimshi king over Israel, and anoint Elisha son of Shaphat from Abel Meholah to succeed you as prophet.

column.name: text
column.value: Jehu will put to death any who escape the sword of Hazael, and Elisha will put to death any who escape the sword of Jehu.

column.name: text
column.value: Yet I reserve seven thousand in Israel--all whose knees have not bowed down to Baal and all whose mouths have not kissed him."

column.name: text
column.value: So Elijah went from there and found Elisha son of Shaphat. He was plowing with twelve yoke of oxen, and he himself was driving the twelfth pair. Elijah went up to him and threw his cloak around him.

column.name: text
column.value: Elisha then left his oxen and ran after Elijah. "Let me kiss my father and mother good-by," he said, "and then I will come with you." "Go back," Elijah replied. "What have I done to you?"

column.name: text
column.value: So Elisha left him and went back. He took his yoke of oxen and slaughtered them. He burned the plowing equipment to cook the meat and gave it to the people, and they ate. Then he set out to follow Elijah and became his attendant.

column.name: text
column.value: After Ahab's death, Moab rebelled against Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: Now Ahaziah had fallen through the lattice of his upper room in Samaria and injured himself. So he sent messengers, saying to them, "Go and consult Baal-Zebub, the god of Ekron, to see if I will recover from this injury."

column.name: text
column.value: But the angel of the LORD said to Elijah the Tishbite, "Go up and meet the messengers of the king of Samaria and ask them, 'Is it because there is no God in Israel that you are going off to consult Baal-Zebub, the god of Ekron?'

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore this is what the LORD says: 'You will not leave the bed you are lying on. You will certainly die!'" So Elijah went.

column.name: text
column.value: When the messengers returned to the king, he asked them, "Why have you come back?"

column.name: text
column.value: "A man came to meet us," they replied. "And he said to us, 'Go back to the king who sent you and tell him, "This is what the LORD says: Is it because there is no God in Israel that you are sending men to consult Baal-Zebub, the god of Ekron? Therefore you will not leave the bed you are lying on. You will certainly die!" '"

column.name: text
column.value: The king asked them, "What kind of man was it who came to meet you and told you this?"

column.name: text
column.value: They replied, "He was a man with a garment of hair and with a leather belt around his waist." The king said, "That was Elijah the Tishbite."

column.name: text
column.value: Then he sent to Elijah a captain with his company of fifty men. The captain went up to Elijah, who was sitting on the top of a hill, and said to him, "Man of God, the king says, 'Come down!'"

column.name: text
column.value: Elijah answered the captain, "If I am a man of God, may fire come down from heaven and consume you and your fifty men!" Then fire fell from heaven and consumed the captain and his men.

column.name: text
column.value: At this the king sent to Elijah another captain with his fifty men. The captain said to him, "Man of God, this is what the king says, 'Come down at once!'"

column.name: text
column.value: "If I am a man of God," Elijah replied, "may fire come down from heaven and consume you and your fifty men!" Then the fire of God fell from heaven and consumed him and his fifty men.

column.name: text
column.value: So the king sent a third captain with his fifty men. This third captain went up and fell on his knees before Elijah. "Man of God," he begged, "please have respect for my life and the lives of these fifty men, your servants!

column.name: text
column.value: See, fire has fallen from heaven and consumed the first two captains and all their men. But now have respect for my life!"

column.name: text
column.value: The angel of the LORD said to Elijah, "Go down with him; do not be afraid of him." So Elijah got up and went down with him to the king.

column.name: text
column.value: He told the king, "This is what the LORD says: Is it because there is no God in Israel for you to consult that you have sent messengers to consult Baal-Zebub, the god of Ekron? Because you have done this, you will never leave the bed you are lying on. You will certainly die!"

column.name: text
column.value: So he died, according to the word of the LORD that Elijah had spoken. Because Ahaziah had no son, Joram succeeded him as king in the second year of Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat king of Judah.

column.name: text
column.value: As for all the other events of Ahaziah's reign, and what he did, are they not written in the book of the annals of the kings of Israel?

column.name: text
column.value: Some time later there was an incident involving a vineyard belonging to Naboth the Jezreelite. The vineyard was in Jezreel, close to the palace of Ahab king of Samaria.

column.name: text
column.value: Ahab said to Naboth, "Let me have your vineyard to use for a vegetable garden, since it is close to my palace. In exchange I will give you a better vineyard or, if you prefer, I will pay you whatever it is worth."

column.name: text
column.value: But Naboth replied, "The LORD forbid that I should give you the inheritance of my fathers."

column.name: text
column.value: So Ahab went home, sullen and angry because Naboth the Jezreelite had said, "I will not give you the inheritance of my fathers." He lay on his bed sulking and refused to eat.

column.name: text
column.value: His wife Jezebel came in and asked him, "Why are you so sullen? Why won't you eat?"

column.name: text
column.value: He answered her, "Because I said to Naboth the Jezreelite, 'Sell me your vineyard; or if you prefer, I will give you another vineyard in its place.' But he said, 'I will not give you my vineyard.'"

column.name: text
column.value: Jezebel his wife said, "Is this how you act as king over Israel? Get up and eat! Cheer up. I'll get you the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite."

column.name: text
column.value: So she wrote letters in Ahab's name, placed his seal on them, and sent them to the elders and nobles who lived in Naboth's city with him.

column.name: text
column.value: In those letters she wrote: "Proclaim a day of fasting and seat Naboth in a prominent place among the people.

column.name: text
column.value: But seat two scoundrels opposite him and have them testify that he has cursed both God and the king. Then take him out and stone him to death."

column.name: text
column.value: So the elders and nobles who lived in Naboth's city did as Jezebel directed in the letters she had written to them.

column.name: text
column.value: They proclaimed a fast and seated Naboth in a prominent place among the people.

column.name: text
column.value: Then two scoundrels came and sat opposite him and brought charges against Naboth before the people, saying, "Naboth has cursed both God and the king." So they took him outside the city and stoned him to death.

column.name: text
column.value: Then they sent word to Jezebel: "Naboth has been stoned and is dead."

column.name: text
column.value: As soon as Jezebel heard that Naboth had been stoned to death, she said to Ahab, "Get up and take possession of the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite that he refused to sell you. He is no longer alive, but dead."

column.name: text
column.value: When Ahab heard that Naboth was dead, he got up and went down to take possession of Naboth's vineyard.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the word of the LORD came to Elijah the Tishbite:

column.name: text
column.value: "Go down to meet Ahab king of Israel, who rules in Samaria. He is now in Naboth's vineyard, where he has gone to take possession of it.

column.name: text
column.value: Say to him, 'This is what the LORD says: Have you not murdered a man and seized his property?' Then say to him, 'This is what the LORD says: In the place where dogs licked up Naboth's blood, dogs will lick up your blood--yes, yours!'"

column.name: text
column.value: Ahab said to Elijah, "So you have found me, my enemy!" "I have found you," he answered, "because you have sold yourself to do evil in the eyes of the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: 'I am going to bring disaster on you. I will consume your descendants and cut off from Ahab every last male in Israel--slave or free.

column.name: text
column.value: I will make your house like that of Jeroboam son of Nebat and that of Baasha son of Ahijah, because you have provoked me to anger and have caused Israel to sin.'

column.name: text
column.value: "And also concerning Jezebel the LORD says: 'Dogs will devour Jezebel by the wall of Jezreel.'

column.name: text
column.value: "Dogs will eat those belonging to Ahab who die in the city, and the birds of the air will feed on those who die in the country."

column.name: text
column.value: (There was never a man like Ahab, who sold himself to do evil in the eyes of the LORD, urged on by Jezebel his wife.

column.name: text
column.value: He behaved in the vilest manner by going after idols, like the Amorites the LORD drove out before Israel.)

column.name: text
column.value: When Ahab heard these words, he tore his clothes, put on sackcloth and fasted. He lay in sackcloth and went around meekly.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the word of the LORD came to Elijah the Tishbite:

column.name: text
column.value: "Have you noticed how Ahab has humbled himself before me? Because he has humbled himself, I will not bring this disaster in his day, but I will bring it on his house in the days of his son."

column.name: text
column.value: For three years there was no war between Aram and Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: But in the third year Jehoshaphat king of Judah went down to see the king of Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: The king of Israel had said to his officials, "Don't you know that Ramoth Gilead belongs to us and yet we are doing nothing to retake it from the king of Aram?"

column.name: text
column.value: So he asked Jehoshaphat, "Will you go with me to fight against Ramoth Gilead?" Jehoshaphat replied to the king of Israel, "I am as you are, my people as your people, my horses as your horses."

column.name: text
column.value: But Jehoshaphat also said to the king of Israel, "First seek the counsel of the LORD."

column.name: text
column.value: So the king of Israel brought together the prophets--about four hundred men--and asked them, "Shall I go to war against Ramoth Gilead, or shall I refrain?" "Go," they answered, "for the Lord will give it into the king's hand."

column.name: text
column.value: But Jehoshaphat asked, "Is there not a prophet of the LORD here whom we can inquire of?"

column.name: text
column.value: The king of Israel answered Jehoshaphat, "There is still one man through whom we can inquire of the LORD, but I hate him because he never prophesies anything good about me, but always bad. He is Micaiah son of Imlah." "The king should not say that," Jehoshaphat replied.

column.name: text
column.value: So the king of Israel called one of his officials and said, "Bring Micaiah son of Imlah at once."

column.name: text
column.value: Dressed in their royal robes, the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah were sitting on their thrones at the threshing floor by the entrance of the gate of Samaria, with all the prophets prophesying before them.

column.name: text
column.value: Now Zedekiah son of Kenaanah had made iron horns and he declared, "This is what the LORD says: 'With these you will gore the Arameans until they are destroyed.'"

column.name: text
column.value: All the other prophets were prophesying the same thing. "Attack Ramoth Gilead and be victorious," they said, "for the LORD will give it into the king's hand."

column.name: text
column.value: The messenger who had gone to summon Micaiah said to him, "Look, as one man the other prophets are predicting success for the king. Let your word agree with theirs, and speak favorably."

column.name: text
column.value: But Micaiah said, "As surely as the LORD lives, I can tell him only what the LORD tells me."

column.name: text
column.value: When he arrived, the king asked him, "Micaiah, shall we go to war against Ramoth Gilead, or shall I refrain?" "Attack and be victorious," he answered, "for the LORD will give it into the king's hand."

column.name: text
column.value: The king said to him, "How many times must I make you swear to tell me nothing but the truth in the name of the LORD?"

column.name: text
column.value: Then Micaiah answered, "I saw all Israel scattered on the hills like sheep without a shepherd, and the LORD said, 'These people have no master. Let each one go home in peace.'"

column.name: text
column.value: The king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, "Didn't I tell you that he never prophesies anything good about me, but only bad?"

column.name: text
column.value: Micaiah continued, "Therefore hear the word of the LORD: I saw the LORD sitting on his throne with all the host of heaven standing around him on his right and on his left.

column.name: text
column.value: And the LORD said, 'Who will entice Ahab into attacking Ramoth Gilead and going to his death there?' "One suggested this, and another that.

column.name: text
column.value: Finally, a spirit came forward, stood before the LORD and said, 'I will entice him.'

column.name: text
column.value: " 'By what means?' the LORD asked. " 'I will go out and be a lying spirit in the mouths of all his prophets,' he said. " 'You will succeed in enticing him,' said the LORD. 'Go and do it.'

column.name: text
column.value: "So now the LORD has put a lying spirit in the mouths of all these prophets of yours. The LORD has decreed disaster for you."

column.name: text
column.value: Then Zedekiah son of Kenaanah went up and slapped Micaiah in the face. "Which way did the spirit from the LORD go when he went from me to speak to you?" he asked.

column.name: text
column.value: Micaiah replied, "You will find out on the day you go to hide in an inner room."

column.name: text
column.value: The king of Israel then ordered, "Take Micaiah and send him back to Amon the ruler of the city and to Joash the king's son

column.name: text
column.value: and say, 'This is what the king says: Put this fellow in prison and give him nothing but bread and water until I return safely.'"

column.name: text
column.value: Micaiah declared, "If you ever return safely, the LORD has not spoken through me." Then he added, "Mark my words, all you people!"

column.name: text
column.value: So the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah went up to Ramoth Gilead.

column.name: text
column.value: The king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, "I will enter the battle in disguise, but you wear your royal robes." So the king of Israel disguised himself and went into battle.

column.name: text
column.value: Now the king of Aram had ordered his thirty-two chariot commanders, "Do not fight with anyone, small or great, except the king of Israel."

column.name: text
column.value: When the chariot commanders saw Jehoshaphat, they thought, "Surely this is the king of Israel." So they turned to attack him, but when Jehoshaphat cried out,

column.name: text
column.value: the chariot commanders saw that he was not the king of Israel and stopped pursuing him.

column.name: text
column.value: But someone drew his bow at random and hit the king of Israel between the sections of his armor. The king told his chariot driver, "Wheel around and get me out of the fighting. I've been wounded."

column.name: text
column.value: All day long the battle raged, and the king was propped up in his chariot facing the Arameans. The blood from his wound ran onto the floor of the chariot, and that evening he died.

column.name: text
column.value: As the sun was setting, a cry spread through the army: "Every man to his town; everyone to his land!"

column.name: text
column.value: So the king died and was brought to Samaria, and they buried him there.

column.name: text
column.value: They washed the chariot at a pool in Samaria (where the prostitutes bathed), and the dogs licked up his blood, as the word of the LORD had declared.

column.name: text
column.value: As for the other events of Ahab's reign, including all he did, the palace he built and inlaid with ivory, and the cities he fortified, are they not written in the book of the annals of the kings of Israel?

column.name: text
column.value: Ahab rested with his fathers. And Ahaziah his son succeeded him as king.

column.name: text
column.value: Jehoshaphat son of Asa became king of Judah in the fourth year of Ahab king of Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: Jehoshaphat was thirty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem twenty-five years. His mother's name was Azubah daughter of Shilhi.

column.name: text
column.value: In everything he walked in the ways of his father Asa and did not stray from them; he did what was right in the eyes of the LORD. The high places, however, were not removed, and the people continued to offer sacrifices and burn incense there.

column.name: text
column.value: Jehoshaphat was also at peace with the king of Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: As for the other events of Jehoshaphat's reign, the things he achieved and his military exploits, are they not written in the book of the annals of the kings of Judah?

column.name: text
column.value: He rid the land of the rest of the male shrine prostitutes who remained there even after the reign of his father Asa.

column.name: text
column.value: There was then no king in Edom; a deputy ruled.

column.name: text
column.value: Now Jehoshaphat built a fleet of trading ships to go to Ophir for gold, but they never set sail--they were wrecked at Ezion Geber.

column.name: text
column.value: At that time Ahaziah son of Ahab said to Jehoshaphat, "Let my men sail with your men," but Jehoshaphat refused.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jehoshaphat rested with his fathers and was buried with them in the city of David his father. And Jehoram his son succeeded him.

column.name: text
column.value: Ahaziah son of Ahab became king of Israel in Samaria in the seventeenth year of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, and he reigned over Israel two years.

column.name: text
column.value: He did evil in the eyes of the LORD, because he walked in the ways of his father and mother and in the ways of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin.

column.name: text
column.value: He served and worshiped Baal and provoked the LORD, the God of Israel, to anger, just as his father had done.

column.name: text
column.value: Now Ben-Hadad king of Aram mustered his entire army. Accompanied by thirty-two kings with their horses and chariots, he went up and besieged Samaria and attacked it.

column.name: text
column.value: He sent messengers into the city to Ahab king of Israel, saying, "This is what Ben-Hadad says:

column.name: text
column.value: 'Your silver and gold are mine, and the best of your wives and children are mine.'"

column.name: text
column.value: The king of Israel answered, "Just as you say, my lord the king. I and all I have are yours."

column.name: text
column.value: The messengers came again and said, "This is what Ben-Hadad says: 'I sent to demand your silver and gold, your wives and your children.

column.name: text
column.value: But about this time tomorrow I am going to send my officials to search your palace and the houses of your officials. They will seize everything you value and carry it away.'"

column.name: text
column.value: The king of Israel summoned all the elders of the land and said to them, "See how this man is looking for trouble! When he sent for my wives and my children, my silver and my gold, I did not refuse him."

column.name: text
column.value: The elders and the people all answered, "Don't listen to him or agree to his demands."

column.name: text
column.value: So he replied to Ben-Hadad's messengers, "Tell my lord the king, 'Your servant will do all you demanded the first time, but this demand I cannot meet.'" They left and took the answer back to Ben-Hadad.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Ben-Hadad sent another message to Ahab: "May the gods deal with me, be it ever so severely, if enough dust remains in Samaria to give each of my men a handful."

column.name: text
column.value: The king of Israel answered, "Tell him: 'One who puts on his armor should not boast like one who takes it off.'"

column.name: text
column.value: Ben-Hadad heard this message while he and the kings were drinking in their tents, and he ordered his men: "Prepare to attack." So they prepared to attack the city.

column.name: text
column.value: Meanwhile a prophet came to Ahab king of Israel and announced, "This is what the LORD says: 'Do you see this vast army? I will give it into your hand today, and then you will know that I am the LORD.'"

column.name: text
column.value: "But who will do this?" asked Ahab. The prophet replied, "This is what the LORD says: 'The young officers of the provincial commanders will do it.'" "And who will start the battle?" he asked. The prophet answered, "You will."

column.name: text
column.value: So Ahab summoned the young officers of the provincial commanders, 232 men. Then he assembled the rest of the Israelites, 7,000 in all.

column.name: text
column.value: They set out at noon while Ben-Hadad and the 32 kings allied with him were in their tents getting drunk.

column.name: text
column.value: The young officers of the provincial commanders went out first. Now Ben-Hadad had dispatched scouts, who reported, "Men are advancing from Samaria."

column.name: text
column.value: He said, "If they have come out for peace, take them alive; if they have come out for war, take them alive."

column.name: text
column.value: The young officers of the provincial commanders marched out of the city with the army behind them

column.name: text
column.value: and each one struck down his opponent. At that, the Arameans fled, with the Israelites in pursuit. But Ben-Hadad king of Aram escaped on horseback with some of his horsemen.

column.name: text
column.value: The king of Israel advanced and overpowered the horses and chariots and inflicted heavy losses on the Arameans.

column.name: text
column.value: Afterward, the prophet came to the king of Israel and said, "Strengthen your position and see what must be done, because next spring the king of Aram will attack you again."

column.name: text
column.value: Meanwhile, the officials of the king of Aram advised him, "Their gods are gods of the hills. That is why they were too strong for us. But if we fight them on the plains, surely we will be stronger than they.

column.name: text
column.value: Do this: Remove all the kings from their commands and replace them with other officers.

column.name: text
column.value: You must also raise an army like the one you lost--horse for horse and chariot for chariot--so we can fight Israel on the plains. Then surely we will be stronger than they." He agreed with them and acted accordingly.

column.name: text
column.value: The next spring Ben-Hadad mustered the Arameans and went up to Aphek to fight against Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: When the Israelites were also mustered and given provisions, they marched out to meet them. The Israelites camped opposite them like two small flocks of goats, while the Arameans covered the countryside.

column.name: text
column.value: The man of God came up and told the king of Israel, "This is what the LORD says: 'Because the Arameans think the LORD is a god of the hills and not a god of the valleys, I will deliver this vast army into your hands, and you will know that I am the LORD.'"

column.name: text
column.value: For seven days they camped opposite each other, and on the seventh day the battle was joined. The Israelites inflicted a hundred thousand casualties on the Aramean foot soldiers in one day.

column.name: text
column.value: The rest of them escaped to the city of Aphek, where the wall collapsed on twenty-seven thousand of them. And Ben-Hadad fled to the city and hid in an inner room.

column.name: text
column.value: His officials said to him, "Look, we have heard that the kings of the house of Israel are merciful. Let us go to the king of Israel with sackcloth around our waists and ropes around our heads. Perhaps he will spare your life."

column.name: text
column.value: Wearing sackcloth around their waists and ropes around their heads, they went to the king of Israel and said, "Your servant Ben-Hadad says: 'Please let me live.'" The king answered, "Is he still alive? He is my brother."

column.name: text
column.value: The men took this as a good sign and were quick to pick up his word. "Yes, your brother Ben-Hadad!" they said. "Go and get him," the king said. When Ben-Hadad came out, Ahab had him come up into his chariot.

column.name: text
column.value: "I will return the cities my father took from your father," Ben-Hadad offered. "You may set up your own market areas in Damascus, as my father did in Samaria." Ahab said,"On the basis of a treaty I will set you free." So he made a treaty with him, and let him go.

column.name: text
column.value: By the word of the LORD one of the sons of the prophets said to his companion, "Strike me with your weapon," but the man refused.

column.name: text
column.value: So the prophet said, "Because you have not obeyed the LORD, as soon as you leave me a lion will kill you." And after the man went away, a lion found him and killed him.

column.name: text
column.value: The prophet found another man and said, "Strike me, please." So the man struck him and wounded him.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the prophet went and stood by the road waiting for the king. He disguised himself with his headband down over his eyes.

column.name: text
column.value: As the king passed by, the prophet called out to him, "Your servant went into the thick of the battle, and someone came to me with a captive and said, 'Guard this man. If he is missing, it will be your life for his life, or you must pay a talent of silver.'

column.name: text
column.value: While your servant was busy here and there, the man disappeared." "That is your sentence," the king of Israel said. "You have pronounced it yourself."

column.name: text
column.value: Then the prophet quickly removed the headband from his eyes, and the king of Israel recognized him as one of the prophets.

column.name: text
column.value: He said to the king, "This is what the LORD says: 'You have set free a man I had determined should die. Therefore it is your life for his life, your people for his people.'"

column.name: text
column.value: Sullen and angry, the king of Israel went to his palace in Samaria.

column.name: text
column.value: When the LORD was about to take Elijah up to heaven in a whirlwind, Elijah and Elisha were on their way from Gilgal.

column.name: text
column.value: Elijah said to Elisha, "Stay here; the LORD has sent me to Bethel." But Elisha said, "As surely as the LORD lives and as you live, I will not leave you." So they went down to Bethel.

column.name: text
column.value: The company of the prophets at Bethel came out to Elisha and asked, "Do you know that the LORD is going to take your master from you today?" "Yes, I know," Elisha replied, "but do not speak of it."

column.name: text
column.value: Then Elijah said to him, "Stay here, Elisha; the LORD has sent me to Jericho." And he replied, "As surely as the LORD lives and as you live, I will not leave you." So they went to Jericho.

column.name: text
column.value: The company of the prophets at Jericho went up to Elisha and asked him, "Do you know that the LORD is going to take your master from you today?" "Yes, I know," he replied, "but do not speak of it."

column.name: text
column.value: Then Elijah said to him, "Stay here; the LORD has sent me to the Jordan." And he replied, "As surely as the LORD lives and as you live, I will not leave you." So the two of them walked on.

column.name: text
column.value: Fifty men of the company of the prophets went and stood at a distance, facing the place where Elijah and Elisha had stopped at the Jordan.

column.name: text
column.value: Elijah took his cloak, rolled it up and struck the water with it. The water divided to the right and to the left, and the two of them crossed over on dry ground.

column.name: text
column.value: When they had crossed, Elijah said to Elisha, "Tell me, what can I do for you before I am taken from you?" "Let me inherit a double portion of your spirit," Elisha replied.

column.name: text
column.value: "You have asked a difficult thing," Elijah said, "yet if you see me when I am taken from you, it will be yours--otherwise not."

column.name: text
column.value: As they were walking along and talking together, suddenly a chariot of fire and horses of fire appeared and separated the two of them, and Elijah went up to heaven in a whirlwind.

column.name: text
column.value: Elisha saw this and cried out, "My father! My father! The chariots and horsemen of Israel!" And Elisha saw him no more. Then he took hold of his own clothes and tore them apart.

column.name: text
column.value: He picked up the cloak that had fallen from Elijah and went back and stood on the bank of the Jordan.

column.name: text
column.value: Then he took the cloak that had fallen from him and struck the water with it. "Where now is the LORD, the God of Elijah?" he asked. When he struck the water, it divided to the right and to the left, and he crossed over.

column.name: text
column.value: The company of the prophets from Jericho, who were watching, said, "The spirit of Elijah is resting on Elisha." And they went to meet him and bowed to the ground before him.

column.name: text
column.value: "Look," they said, "we your servants have fifty able men. Let them go and look for your master. Perhaps the Spirit of the LORD has picked him up and set him down on some mountain or in some valley." "No," Elisha replied, "do not send them."

column.name: text
column.value: But they persisted until he was too ashamed to refuse. So he said, "Send them." And they sent fifty men, who searched for three days but did not find him.

column.name: text
column.value: When they returned to Elisha, who was staying in Jericho, he said to them, "Didn't I tell you not to go?"

column.name: text
column.value: The men of the city said to Elisha, "Look, our lord, this town is well situated, as you can see, but the water is bad and the land is unproductive."

column.name: text
column.value: "Bring me a new bowl," he said, "and put salt in it." So they brought it to him.

column.name: text
column.value: Then he went out to the spring and threw the salt into it, saying, "This is what the LORD says: 'I have healed this water. Never again will it cause death or make the land unproductive.'"

column.name: text
column.value: And the water has remained wholesome to this day, according to the word Elisha had spoken.

column.name: text
column.value: From there Elisha went up to Bethel. As he was walking along the road, some youths came out of the town and jeered at him. "Go on up, you baldhead!" they said. "Go on up, you baldhead!"

column.name: text
column.value: He turned around, looked at them and called down a curse on them in the name of the LORD. Then two bears came out of the woods and mauled forty-two of the youths.

column.name: text
column.value: And he went on to Mount Carmel and from there returned to Samaria.

column.name: text
column.value: Joram son of Ahab became king of Israel in Samaria in the eighteenth year of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, and he reigned twelve years.

column.name: text
column.value: He did evil in the eyes of the LORD, but not as his father and mother had done. He got rid of the sacred stone of Baal that his father had made.

column.name: text
column.value: Nevertheless he clung to the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, which he had caused Israel to commit; he did not turn away from them.

column.name: text
column.value: Now Mesha king of Moab raised sheep, and he had to supply the king of Israel with a hundred thousand lambs and with the wool of a hundred thousand rams.

column.name: text
column.value: But after Ahab died, the king of Moab rebelled against the king of Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: So at that time King Joram set out from Samaria and mobilized all Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: He also sent this message to Jehoshaphat king of Judah: "The king of Moab has rebelled against me. Will you go with me to fight against Moab?" "I will go with you," he replied. "I am as you are, my people as your people, my horses as your horses."

column.name: text
column.value: "By what route shall we attack?" he asked. "Through the Desert of Edom," he answered.

column.name: text
column.value: So the king of Israel set out with the king of Judah and the king of Edom. After a roundabout march of seven days, the army had no more water for themselves or for the animals with them.

column.name: text
column.value: "What!" exclaimed the king of Israel. "Has the LORD called us three kings together only to hand us over to Moab?"

column.name: text
column.value: But Jehoshaphat asked, "Is there no prophet of the LORD here, that we may inquire of the LORD through him?" An officer of the king of Israel answered, "Elisha son of Shaphat is here. He used to pour water on the hands of Elijah."

column.name: text
column.value: Jehoshaphat said, "The word of the LORD is with him." So the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat and the king of Edom went down to him.

column.name: text
column.value: Elisha said to the king of Israel, "What do we have to do with each other? Go to the prophets of your father and the prophets of your mother." "No," the king of Israel answered, "because it was the LORD who called us three kings together to hand us over to Moab."

column.name: text
column.value: Elisha said, "As surely as the LORD Almighty lives, whom I serve, if I did not have respect for the presence of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, I would not look at you or even notice you.

column.name: text
column.value: But now bring me a harpist." While the harpist was playing, the hand of the LORD came upon Elisha

column.name: text
column.value: and he said, "This is what the LORD says: Make this valley full of ditches.

column.name: text
column.value: For this is what the LORD says: You will see neither wind nor rain, yet this valley will be filled with water, and you, your cattle and your other animals will drink.

column.name: text
column.value: This is an easy thing in the eyes of the LORD; he will also hand Moab over to you.

column.name: text
column.value: You will overthrow every fortified city and every major town. You will cut down every good tree, stop up all the springs, and ruin every good field with stones."

column.name: text
column.value: The next morning, about the time for offering the sacrifice, there it was--water flowing from the direction of Edom! And the land was filled with water.

column.name: text
column.value: Now all the Moabites had heard that the kings had come to fight against them; so every man, young and old, who could bear arms was called up and stationed on the border.

column.name: text
column.value: When they got up early in the morning, the sun was shining on the water. To the Moabites across the way, the water looked red--like blood.

column.name: text
column.value: "That's blood!" they said. "Those kings must have fought and slaughtered each other. Now to the plunder, Moab!"

column.name: text
column.value: But when the Moabites came to the camp of Israel, the Israelites rose up and fought them until they fled. And the Israelites invaded the land and slaughtered the Moabites.

column.name: text
column.value: They destroyed the towns, and each man threw a stone on every good field until it was covered. They stopped up all the springs and cut down every good tree. Only Kir Hareseth was left with its stones in place, but men armed with slings surrounded it and attacked it as well.

column.name: text
column.value: When the king of Moab saw that the battle had gone against him, he took with him seven hundred swordsmen to break through to the king of Edom, but they failed.

column.name: text
column.value: Then he took his firstborn son, who was to succeed him as king, and offered him as a sacrifice on the city wall. The fury against Israel was great; they withdrew and returned to their own land.

column.name: text
column.value: The wife of a man from the company of the prophets cried out to Elisha, "Your servant my husband is dead, and you know that he revered the LORD. But now his creditor is coming to take my two boys as his slaves."

column.name: text
column.value: Elisha replied to her, "How can I help you? Tell me, what do you have in your house?" "Your servant has nothing there at all," she said, "except a little oil."

column.name: text
column.value: Elisha said, "Go around and ask all your neighbors for empty jars. Don't ask for just a few.

column.name: text
column.value: Then go inside and shut the door behind you and your sons. Pour oil into all the jars, and as each is filled, put it to one side."

column.name: text
column.value: She left him and afterward shut the door behind her and her sons. They brought the jars to her and she kept pouring.

column.name: text
column.value: When all the jars were full, she said to her son, "Bring me another one." But he replied, "There is not a jar left." Then the oil stopped flowing.

column.name: text
column.value: She went and told the man of God, and he said, "Go, sell the oil and pay your debts. You and your sons can live on what is left."

column.name: text
column.value: One day Elisha went to Shunem. And a well-to-do woman was there, who urged him to stay for a meal. So whenever he came by, he stopped there to eat.

column.name: text
column.value: She said to her husband, "I know that this man who often comes our way is a holy man of God.

column.name: text
column.value: Let's make a small room on the roof and put in it a bed and a table, a chair and a lamp for him. Then he can stay there whenever he comes to us."

column.name: text
column.value: One day when Elisha came, he went up to his room and lay down there.

column.name: text
column.value: He said to his servant Gehazi, "Call the Shunammite." So he called her, and she stood before him.

column.name: text
column.value: Elisha said to him, "Tell her, 'You have gone to all this trouble for us. Now what can be done for you? Can we speak on your behalf to the king or the commander of the army?'" She replied, "I have a home among my own people."

column.name: text
column.value: "What can be done for her?" Elisha asked. Gehazi said, "Well, she has no son and her husband is old."

column.name: text
column.value: Then Elisha said, "Call her." So he called her, and she stood in the doorway.

column.name: text
column.value: "About this time next year," Elisha said, "you will hold a son in your arms." "No, my lord," she objected. "Don't mislead your servant, O man of God!"

column.name: text
column.value: But the woman became pregnant, and the next year about that same time she gave birth to a son, just as Elisha had told her.

column.name: text
column.value: The child grew, and one day he went out to his father, who was with the reapers.

column.name: text
column.value: "My head! My head!" he said to his father. His father told a servant, "Carry him to his mother."

column.name: text
column.value: After the servant had lifted him up and carried him to his mother, the boy sat on her lap until noon, and then he died.

column.name: text
column.value: She went up and laid him on the bed of the man of God, then shut the door and went out.

column.name: text
column.value: She called her husband and said, "Please send me one of the servants and a donkey so I can go to the man of God quickly and return."

column.name: text
column.value: "Why go to him today?" he asked. "It's not the New Moon or the Sabbath." "It's all right," she said.

column.name: text
column.value: She saddled the donkey and said to her servant, "Lead on; don't slow down for me unless I tell you."

column.name: text
column.value: So she set out and came to the man of God at Mount Carmel. When he saw her in the distance, the man of God said to his servant Gehazi, "Look! There's the Shunammite!

column.name: text
column.value: Run to meet her and ask her, 'Are you all right? Is your husband all right? Is your child all right?'" "Everything is all right," she said.

column.name: text
column.value: When she reached the man of God at the mountain, she took hold of his feet. Gehazi came over to push her away, but the man of God said, "Leave her alone! She is in bitter distress, but the LORD has hidden it from me and has not told me why."

column.name: text
column.value: "Did I ask you for a son, my lord?" she said. "Didn't I tell you, 'Don't raise my hopes'?"

column.name: text
column.value: Elisha said to Gehazi, "Tuck your cloak into your belt, take my staff in your hand and run. If you meet anyone, do not greet him, and if anyone greets you, do not answer. Lay my staff on the boy's face."

column.name: text
column.value: But the child's mother said, "As surely as the LORD lives and as you live, I will not leave you." So he got up and followed her.

column.name: text
column.value: Gehazi went on ahead and laid the staff on the boy's face, but there was no sound or response. So Gehazi went back to meet Elisha and told him, "The boy has not awakened."

column.name: text
column.value: When Elisha reached the house, there was the boy lying dead on his couch.

column.name: text
column.value: He went in, shut the door on the two of them and prayed to the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: Then he got on the bed and lay upon the boy, mouth to mouth, eyes to eyes, hands to hands. As he stretched himself out upon him, the boy's body grew warm.

column.name: text
column.value: Elisha turned away and walked back and forth in the room and then got on the bed and stretched out upon him once more. The boy sneezed seven times and opened his eyes.

column.name: text
column.value: Elisha summoned Gehazi and said, "Call the Shunammite." And he did. When she came, he said, "Take your son."

column.name: text
column.value: She came in, fell at his feet and bowed to the ground. Then she took her son and went out.

column.name: text
column.value: Elisha returned to Gilgal and there was a famine in that region. While the company of the prophets was meeting with him, he said to his servant, "Put on the large pot and cook some stew for these men."

column.name: text
column.value: One of them went out into the fields to gather herbs and found a wild vine. He gathered some of its gourds and filled the fold of his cloak. When he returned, he cut them up into the pot of stew, though no one knew what they were.

column.name: text
column.value: The stew was poured out for the men, but as they began to eat it, they cried out, "O man of God, there is death in the pot!" And they could not eat it.

column.name: text
column.value: Elisha said, "Get some flour." He put it into the pot and said, "Serve it to the people to eat." And there was nothing harmful in the pot.

column.name: text
column.value: A man came from Baal Shalishah, bringing the man of God twenty loaves of barley bread baked from the first ripe grain, along with some heads of new grain. "Give it to the people to eat," Elisha said.

column.name: text
column.value: "How can I set this before a hundred men?" his servant asked. But Elisha answered, "Give it to the people to eat. For this is what the LORD says: 'They will eat and have some left over.'"

column.name: text
column.value: Then he set it before them, and they ate and had some left over, according to the word of the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: Now Naaman was commander of the army of the king of Aram. He was a great man in the sight of his master and highly regarded, because through him the LORD had given victory to Aram. He was a valiant soldier, but he had leprosy.

column.name: text
column.value: Now bands from Aram had gone out and had taken captive a young girl from Israel, and she served Naaman's wife.

column.name: text
column.value: She said to her mistress, "If only my master would see the prophet who is in Samaria! He would cure him of his leprosy."

column.name: text
column.value: Naaman went to his master and told him what the girl from Israel had said.

column.name: text
column.value: "By all means, go," the king of Aram replied. "I will send a letter to the king of Israel." So Naaman left, taking with him ten talents of silver, six thousand shekels of gold and ten sets of clothing.

column.name: text
column.value: The letter that he took to the king of Israel read: "With this letter I am sending my servant Naaman to you so that you may cure him of his leprosy."

column.name: text
column.value: As soon as the king of Israel read the letter, he tore his robes and said, "Am I God? Can I kill and bring back to life? Why does this fellow send someone to me to be cured of his leprosy? See how he is trying to pick a quarrel with me!"

column.name: text
column.value: When Elisha the man of God heard that the king of Israel had torn his robes, he sent him this message: "Why have you torn your robes? Have the man come to me and he will know that there is a prophet in Israel."

column.name: text
column.value: So Naaman went with his horses and chariots and stopped at the door of Elisha's house.

column.name: text
column.value: Elisha sent a messenger to say to him, "Go, wash yourself seven times in the Jordan, and your flesh will be restored and you will be cleansed."

column.name: text
column.value: But Naaman went away angry and said, "I thought that he would surely come out to me and stand and call on the name of the LORD his God, wave his hand over the spot and cure me of my leprosy.

column.name: text
column.value: Are not Abana and Pharpar, the rivers of Damascus, better than any of the waters of Israel? Couldn't I wash in them and be cleansed?" So he turned and went off in a rage.

column.name: text
column.value: Naaman's servants went to him and said, "My father, if the prophet had told you to do some great thing, would you not have done it? How much more, then, when he tells you, 'Wash and be cleansed'!"

column.name: text
column.value: So he went down and dipped himself in the Jordan seven times, as the man of God had told him, and his flesh was restored and became clean like that of a young boy.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Naaman and all his attendants went back to the man of God. He stood before him and said, "Now I know that there is no God in all the world except in Israel. Please accept now a gift from your servant."

column.name: text
column.value: The prophet answered, "As surely as the LORD lives, whom I serve, I will not accept a thing." And even though Naaman urged him, he refused.

column.name: text
column.value: "If you will not," said Naaman, "please let me, your servant, be given as much earth as a pair of mules can carry, for your servant will never again make burnt offerings and sacrifices to any other god but the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: But may the LORD forgive your servant for this one thing: When my master enters the temple of Rimmon to bow down and he is leaning on my arm and I bow there also--when I bow down in the temple of Rimmon, may the LORD forgive your servant for this."

column.name: text
column.value: "Go in peace," Elisha said. After Naaman had traveled some distance,

column.name: text
column.value: Gehazi, the servant of Elisha the man of God, said to himself, "My master was too easy on Naaman, this Aramean, by not accepting from him what he brought. As surely as the LORD lives, I will run after him and get something from him."

column.name: text
column.value: So Gehazi hurried after Naaman. When Naaman saw him running toward him, he got down from the chariot to meet him. "Is everything all right?" he asked.

column.name: text
column.value: "Everything is all right," Gehazi answered. "My master sent me to say, 'Two young men from the company of the prophets have just come to me from the hill country of Ephraim. Please give them a talent of silver and two sets of clothing.'"

column.name: text
column.value: "By all means, take two talents," said Naaman. He urged Gehazi to accept them, and then tied up the two talents of silver in two bags, with two sets of clothing. He gave them to two of his servants, and they carried them ahead of Gehazi.

column.name: text
column.value: When Gehazi came to the hill, he took the things from the servants and put them away in the house. He sent the men away and they left.

column.name: text
column.value: Then he went in and stood before his master Elisha. "Where have you been, Gehazi?" Elisha asked. "Your servant didn't go anywhere," Gehazi answered.

column.name: text
column.value: But Elisha said to him, "Was not my spirit with you when the man got down from his chariot to meet you? Is this the time to take money, or to accept clothes, olive groves, vineyards, flocks, herds, or menservants and maidservants?

column.name: text
column.value: Naaman's leprosy will cling to you and to your descendants forever." Then Gehazi went from Elisha's presence and he was leprous, as white as snow.

column.name: text
column.value: The company of the prophets said to Elisha, "Look, the place where we meet with you is too small for us.

column.name: text
column.value: Let us go to the Jordan, where each of us can get a pole; and let us build a place there for us to live." And he said, "Go."

column.name: text
column.value: Then one of them said, "Won't you please come with your servants?" "I will," Elisha replied.

column.name: text
column.value: And he went with them. They went to the Jordan and began to cut down trees.

column.name: text
column.value: As one of them was cutting down a tree, the iron axhead fell into the water. "Oh, my lord," he cried out, "it was borrowed!"

column.name: text
column.value: The man of God asked, "Where did it fall?" When he showed him the place, Elisha cut a stick and threw it there, and made the iron float.

column.name: text
column.value: "Lift it out," he said. Then the man reached out his hand and took it.

column.name: text
column.value: Now the king of Aram was at war with Israel. After conferring with his officers, he said, "I will set up my camp in such and such a place."

column.name: text
column.value: The man of God sent word to the king of Israel: "Beware of passing that place, because the Arameans are going down there."

column.name: text
column.value: So the king of Israel checked on the place indicated by the man of God. Time and again Elisha warned the king, so that he was on his guard in such places.

column.name: text
column.value: This enraged the king of Aram. He summoned his officers and demanded of them, "Will you not tell me which of us is on the side of the king of Israel?"

column.name: text
column.value: "None of us, my lord the king," said one of his officers, "but Elisha, the prophet who is in Israel, tells the king of Israel the very words you speak in your bedroom."

column.name: text
column.value: "Go, find out where he is," the king ordered, "so I can send men and capture him." The report came back: "He is in Dothan."

column.name: text
column.value: Then he sent horses and chariots and a strong force there. They went by night and surrounded the city.

column.name: text
column.value: When the servant of the man of God got up and went out early the next morning, an army with horses and chariots had surrounded the city. "Oh, my lord, what shall we do?" the servant asked.

column.name: text
column.value: "Don't be afraid," the prophet answered. "Those who are with us are more than those who are with them."

column.name: text
column.value: And Elisha prayed, "O LORD, open his eyes so he may see." Then the LORD opened the servant's eyes, and he looked and saw the hills full of horses and chariots of fire all around Elisha.

column.name: text
column.value: As the enemy came down toward him, Elisha prayed to the LORD, "Strike these people with blindness." So he struck them with blindness, as Elisha had asked.

column.name: text
column.value: Elisha told them, "This is not the road and this is not the city. Follow me, and I will lead you to the man you are looking for." And he led them to Samaria.

column.name: text
column.value: After they entered the city, Elisha said, "LORD, open the eyes of these men so they can see." Then the LORD opened their eyes and they looked, and there they were, inside Samaria.

column.name: text
column.value: When the king of Israel saw them, he asked Elisha, "Shall I kill them, my father? Shall I kill them?"

column.name: text
column.value: "Do not kill them," he answered. "Would you kill men you have captured with your own sword or bow? Set food and water before them so that they may eat and drink and then go back to their master."

column.name: text
column.value: So he prepared a great feast for them, and after they had finished eating and drinking, he sent them away, and they returned to their master. So the bands from Aram stopped raiding Israel's territory.

column.name: text
column.value: Some time later, Ben-Hadad king of Aram mobilized his entire army and marched up and laid siege to Samaria.

column.name: text
column.value: There was a great famine in the city; the siege lasted so long that a donkey's head sold for eighty shekels of silver, and a quarter of a cab of seed pods for five shekels.

column.name: text
column.value: As the king of Israel was passing by on the wall, a woman cried to him, "Help me, my lord the king!"

column.name: text
column.value: The king replied, "If the LORD does not help you, where can I get help for you? From the threshing floor? From the winepress?"

column.name: text
column.value: Then he asked her, "What's the matter?" She answered, "This woman said to me, 'Give up your son so we may eat him today, and tomorrow we'll eat my son.'

column.name: text
column.value: So we cooked my son and ate him. The next day I said to her, 'Give up your son so we may eat him,' but she had hidden him."

column.name: text
column.value: When the king heard the woman's words, he tore his robes. As he went along the wall, the people looked, and there, underneath, he had sackcloth on his body.

column.name: text
column.value: He said, "May God deal with me, be it ever so severely, if the head of Elisha son of Shaphat remains on his shoulders today!"

column.name: text
column.value: Now Elisha was sitting in his house, and the elders were sitting with him. The king sent a messenger ahead, but before he arrived, Elisha said to the elders, "Don't you see how this murderer is sending someone to cut off my head? Look, when the messenger comes, shut the door and hold it shut against him. Is not the sound of his master's footsteps behind him?"

column.name: text
column.value: While he was still talking to them, the messenger came down to him. And the king said, "This disaster is from the LORD. Why should I wait for the LORD any longer?"

column.name: text
column.value: Now Elisha had said to the woman whose son he had restored to life, "Go away with your family and stay for a while wherever you can, because the LORD has decreed a famine in the land that will last seven years."

column.name: text
column.value: The woman proceeded to do as the man of God said. She and her family went away and stayed in the land of the Philistines seven years.

column.name: text
column.value: At the end of the seven years she came back from the land of the Philistines and went to the king to beg for her house and land.

column.name: text
column.value: The king was talking to Gehazi, the servant of the man of God, and had said, "Tell me about all the great things Elisha has done."

column.name: text
column.value: Just as Gehazi was telling the king how Elisha had restored the dead to life, the woman whose son Elisha had brought back to life came to beg the king for her house and land. Gehazi said, "This is the woman, my lord the king, and this is her son whom Elisha restored to life."

column.name: text
column.value: The king asked the woman about it, and she told him. Then he assigned an official to her case and said to him, "Give back everything that belonged to her, including all the income from her land from the day she left the country until now."

column.name: text
column.value: Elisha went to Damascus, and Ben-Hadad king of Aram was ill. When the king was told, "The man of God has come all the way up here,"

column.name: text
column.value: he said to Hazael, "Take a gift with you and go to meet the man of God. Consult the LORD through him; ask him, 'Will I recover from this illness?'"

column.name: text
column.value: Hazael went to meet Elisha, taking with him as a gift forty camel-loads of all the finest wares of Damascus. He went in and stood before him, and said, "Your son Ben-Hadad king of Aram has sent me to ask, 'Will I recover from this illness?'"

column.name: text
column.value: Elisha answered, "Go and say to him, 'You will certainly recover'; but the LORD has revealed to me that he will in fact die."

column.name: text
column.value: He stared at him with a fixed gaze until Hazael felt ashamed. Then the man of God began to weep.

column.name: text
column.value: "Why is my lord weeping?" asked Hazael. "Because I know the harm you will do to the Israelites," he answered. "You will set fire to their fortified places, kill their young men with the sword, dash their little children to the ground, and rip open their pregnant women."

column.name: text
column.value: Hazael said, "How could your servant, a mere dog, accomplish such a feat?" "The LORD has shown me that you will become king of Aram," answered Elisha.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Hazael left Elisha and returned to his master. When Ben-Hadad asked, "What did Elisha say to you?" Hazael replied, "He told me that you would certainly recover."

column.name: text
column.value: But the next day he took a thick cloth, soaked it in water and spread it over the king's face, so that he died. Then Hazael succeeded him as king.

column.name: text
column.value: In the fifth year of Joram son of Ahab king of Israel, when Jehoshaphat was king of Judah, Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat began his reign as king of Judah.

column.name: text
column.value: He was thirty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem eight years.

column.name: text
column.value: He walked in the ways of the kings of Israel, as the house of Ahab had done, for he married a daughter of Ahab. He did evil in the eyes of the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: Nevertheless, for the sake of his servant David, the LORD was not willing to destroy Judah. He had promised to maintain a lamp for David and his descendants forever.

column.name: text
column.value: In the time of Jehoram, Edom rebelled against Judah and set up its own king.

column.name: text
column.value: So Jehoram went to Zair with all his chariots. The Edomites surrounded him and his chariot commanders, but he rose up and broke through by night; his army, however, fled back home.

column.name: text
column.value: To this day Edom has been in rebellion against Judah. Libnah revolted at the same time.

column.name: text
column.value: As for the other events of Jehoram's reign, and all he did, are they not written in the book of the annals of the kings of Judah?

column.name: text
column.value: Jehoram rested with his fathers and was buried with them in the City of David. And Ahaziah his son succeeded him as king.

column.name: text
column.value: In the twelfth year of Joram son of Ahab king of Israel, Ahaziah son of Jehoram king of Judah began to reign.

column.name: text
column.value: Ahaziah was twenty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem one year. His mother's name was Athaliah, a granddaughter of Omri king of Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: He walked in the ways of the house of Ahab and did evil in the eyes of the LORD, as the house of Ahab had done, for he was related by marriage to Ahab's family.

column.name: text
column.value: Ahaziah went with Joram son of Ahab to war against Hazael king of Aram at Ramoth Gilead. The Arameans wounded Joram;

column.name: text
column.value: so King Joram returned to Jezreel to recover from the wounds the Arameans had inflicted on him at Ramoth in his battle with Hazael king of Aram. Then Ahaziah son of Jehoram king of Judah went down to Jezreel to see Joram son of Ahab, because he had been wounded.

column.name: text
column.value: The prophet Elisha summoned a man from the company of the prophets and said to him, "Tuck your cloak into your belt, take this flask of oil with you and go to Ramoth Gilead.

column.name: text
column.value: When you get there, look for Jehu son of Jehoshaphat, the son of Nimshi. Go to him, get him away from his companions and take him into an inner room.

column.name: text
column.value: Then take the flask and pour the oil on his head and declare, 'This is what the LORD says: I anoint you king over Israel.' Then open the door and run; don't delay!"

column.name: text
column.value: So the young man, the prophet, went to Ramoth Gilead.

column.name: text
column.value: When he arrived, he found the army officers sitting together. "I have a message for you, commander," he said. "For which of us?" asked Jehu. "For you, commander," he replied.

column.name: text
column.value: Jehu got up and went into the house. Then the prophet poured the oil on Jehu's head and declared, "This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: 'I anoint you king over the LORD'S people Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: You are to destroy the house of Ahab your master, and I will avenge the blood of my servants the prophets and the blood of all the LORD'S servants shed by Jezebel.

column.name: text
column.value: The whole house of Ahab will perish. I will cut off from Ahab every last male in Israel--slave or free.

column.name: text
column.value: I will make the house of Ahab like the house of Jeroboam son of Nebat and like the house of Baasha son of Ahijah.

column.name: text
column.value: As for Jezebel, dogs will devour her on the plot of ground at Jezreel, and no one will bury her.'" Then he opened the door and ran.

column.name: text
column.value: When Jehu went out to his fellow officers, one of them asked him, "Is everything all right? Why did this madman come to you?" "You know the man and the sort of things he says," Jehu replied.

column.name: text
column.value: "That's not true!" they said. "Tell us." Jehu said, "Here is what he told me: 'This is what the LORD says: I anoint you king over Israel.'"

column.name: text
column.value: They hurried and took their cloaks and spread them under him on the bare steps. Then they blew the trumpet and shouted, "Jehu is king!"

column.name: text
column.value: So Jehu son of Jehoshaphat, the son of Nimshi, conspired against Joram. (Now Joram and all Israel had been defending Ramoth Gilead against Hazael king of Aram,

column.name: text
column.value: but King Joram had returned to Jezreel to recover from the wounds the Arameans had inflicted on him in the battle with Hazael king of Aram.) Jehu said, "If this is the way you feel, don't let anyone slip out of the city to go and tell the news in Jezreel."

column.name: text
column.value: Then he got into his chariot and rode to Jezreel, because Joram was resting there and Ahaziah king of Judah had gone down to see him.

column.name: text
column.value: When the lookout standing on the tower in Jezreel saw Jehu's troops approaching, he called out, "I see some troops coming." "Get a horseman," Joram ordered. "Send him to meet them and ask, 'Do you come in peace?'"

column.name: text
column.value: The horseman rode off to meet Jehu and said, "This is what the king says: 'Do you come in peace?'" "What do you have to do with peace?" Jehu replied. "Fall in behind me." The lookout reported, "The messenger has reached them, but he isn't coming back."

column.name: text
column.value: So the king sent out a second horseman. When he came to them he said, "This is what the king says: 'Do you come in peace?'" Jehu replied, "What do you have to do with peace? Fall in behind me."

column.name: text
column.value: The lookout reported, "He has reached them, but he isn't coming back either. The driving is like that of Jehu son of Nimshi--he drives like a madman."

column.name: text
column.value: "Hitch up my chariot," Joram ordered. And when it was hitched up, Joram king of Israel and Ahaziah king of Judah rode out, each in his own chariot, to meet Jehu. They met him at the plot of ground that had belonged to Naboth the Jezreelite.

column.name: text
column.value: When Joram saw Jehu he asked, "Have you come in peace, Jehu?" "How can there be peace," Jehu replied, "as long as all the idolatry and witchcraft of your mother Jezebel abound?"

column.name: text
column.value: Joram turned about and fled, calling out to Ahaziah, "Treachery, Ahaziah!"

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jehu drew his bow and shot Joram between the shoulders. The arrow pierced his heart and he slumped down in his chariot.

column.name: text
column.value: Jehu said to Bidkar, his chariot officer, "Pick him up and throw him on the field that belonged to Naboth the Jezreelite. Remember how you and I were riding together in chariots behind Ahab his father when the LORD made this prophecy about him:

column.name: text
column.value: 'Yesterday I saw the blood of Naboth and the blood of his sons, declares the LORD, and I will surely make you pay for it on this plot of ground, declares the LORD.' Now then, pick him up and throw him on that plot, in accordance with the word of the LORD."

column.name: text
column.value: When Ahaziah king of Judah saw what had happened, he fled up the road to Beth Haggan. Jehu chased him, shouting, "Kill him too!" They wounded him in his chariot on the way up to Gur near Ibleam, but he escaped to Megiddo and died there.

column.name: text
column.value: His servants took him by chariot to Jerusalem and buried him with his fathers in his tomb in the City of David.

column.name: text
column.value: (In the eleventh year of Joram son of Ahab, Ahaziah had become king of Judah.)

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jehu went to Jezreel. When Jezebel heard about it, she painted her eyes, arranged her hair and looked out of a window.

column.name: text
column.value: As Jehu entered the gate, she asked, "Have you come in peace, Zimri, you murderer of your master?"

column.name: text
column.value: He looked up at the window and called out, "Who is on my side? Who?" Two or three eunuchs looked down at him.

column.name: text
column.value: "Throw her down!" Jehu said. So they threw her down, and some of her blood spattered the wall and the horses as they trampled her underfoot.

column.name: text
column.value: Jehu went in and ate and drank. "Take care of that cursed woman," he said, "and bury her, for she was a king's daughter."

column.name: text
column.value: But when they went out to bury her, they found nothing except her skull, her feet and her hands.

column.name: text
column.value: They went back and told Jehu, who said, "This is the word of the LORD that he spoke through his servant Elijah the Tishbite: On the plot of ground at Jezreel dogs will devour Jezebel's flesh.

column.name: text
column.value: Jezebel's body will be like refuse on the ground in the plot at Jezreel, so that no one will be able to say, 'This is Jezebel.'"

column.name: text
column.value: Elisha said, "Hear the word of the LORD. This is what the LORD says: About this time tomorrow, a seah of flour will sell for a shekel and two seahs of barley for a shekel at the gate of Samaria."

column.name: text
column.value: The officer on whose arm the king was leaning said to the man of God, "Look, even if the LORD should open the floodgates of the heavens, could this happen?" "You will see it with your own eyes," answered Elisha, "but you will not eat any of it!"

column.name: text
column.value: Now there were four men with leprosy at the entrance of the city gate. They said to each other, "Why stay here until we die?

column.name: text
column.value: If we say, 'We'll go into the city'--the famine is there, and we will die. And if we stay here, we will die. So let's go over to the camp of the Arameans and surrender. If they spare us, we live; if they kill us, then we die."

column.name: text
column.value: At dusk they got up and went to the camp of the Arameans. When they reached the edge of the camp, not a man was there,

column.name: text
column.value: for the Lord had caused the Arameans to hear the sound of chariots and horses and a great army, so that they said to one another, "Look, the king of Israel has hired the Hittite and Egyptian kings to attack us!"

column.name: text
column.value: So they got up and fled in the dusk and abandoned their tents and their horses and donkeys. They left the camp as it was and ran for their lives.

column.name: text
column.value: The men who had leprosy reached the edge of the camp and entered one of the tents. They ate and drank, and carried away silver, gold and clothes, and went off and hid them. They returned and entered another tent and took some things from it and hid them also.

column.name: text
column.value: Then they said to each other, "We're not doing right. This is a day of good news and we are keeping it to ourselves. If we wait until daylight, punishment will overtake us. Let's go at once and report this to the royal palace."

column.name: text
column.value: So they went and called out to the city gatekeepers and told them, "We went into the Aramean camp and not a man was there--not a sound of anyone--only tethered horses and donkeys, and the tents left just as they were."

column.name: text
column.value: The gatekeepers shouted the news, and it was reported within the palace.

column.name: text
column.value: The king got up in the night and said to his officers, "I will tell you what the Arameans have done to us. They know we are starving; so they have left the camp to hide in the countryside, thinking, 'They will surely come out, and then we will take them alive and get into the city.'"

column.name: text
column.value: One of his officers answered, "Have some men take five of the horses that are left in the city. Their plight will be like that of all the Israelites left here--yes, they will only be like all these Israelites who are doomed. So let us send them to find out what happened."

column.name: text
column.value: So they selected two chariots with their horses, and the king sent them after the Aramean army. He commanded the drivers, "Go and find out what has happened."

column.name: text
column.value: They followed them as far as the Jordan, and they found the whole road strewn with the clothing and equipment the Arameans had thrown away in their headlong flight. So the messengers returned and reported to the king.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the people went out and plundered the camp of the Arameans. So a seah of flour sold for a shekel, and two seahs of barley sold for a shekel, as the LORD had said.

column.name: text
column.value: Now the king had put the officer on whose arm he leaned in charge of the gate, and the people trampled him in the gateway, and he died, just as the man of God had foretold when the king came down to his house.

column.name: text
column.value: It happened as the man of God had said to the king: "About this time tomorrow, a seah of flour will sell for a shekel and two seahs of barley for a shekel at the gate of Samaria."

column.name: text
column.value: The officer had said to the man of God, "Look, even if the LORD should open the floodgates of the heavens, could this happen?" The man of God had replied, "You will see it with your own eyes, but you will not eat any of it!"

column.name: text
column.value: And that is exactly what happened to him, for the people trampled him in the gateway, and he died.

column.name: text
column.value: In the seventh year of Jehu, Joash became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem forty years. His mother's name was Zibiah; she was from Beersheba.

column.name: text
column.value: Joash did what was right in the eyes of the LORD all the years Jehoiada the priest instructed him.

column.name: text
column.value: The high places, however, were not removed; the people continued to offer sacrifices and burn incense there.

column.name: text
column.value: Joash said to the priests, "Collect all the money that is brought as sacred offerings to the temple of the LORD--the money collected in the census, the money received from personal vows and the money brought voluntarily to the temple.

column.name: text
column.value: Let every priest receive the money from one of the treasurers, and let it be used to repair whatever damage is found in the temple."

column.name: text
column.value: But by the twenty-third year of King Joash the priests still had not repaired the temple.

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore King Joash summoned Jehoiada the priest and the other priests and asked them, "Why aren't you repairing the damage done to the temple? Take no more money from your treasurers, but hand it over for repairing the temple."

column.name: text
column.value: The priests agreed that they would not collect any more money from the people and that they would not repair the temple themselves.

column.name: text
column.value: Jehoiada the priest took a chest and bored a hole in its lid. He placed it beside the altar, on the right side as one enters the temple of the LORD. The priests who guarded the entrance put into the chest all the money that was brought to the temple of the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: Whenever they saw that there was a large amount of money in the chest, the royal secretary and the high priest came, counted the money that had been brought into the temple of the LORD and put it into bags.

column.name: text
