column.name: text
column.value: These were the kings who reigned in Edom before any Israelite king reigned: Bela son of Beor, whose city was named Dinhabah.

column.name: text
column.value: When Bela died, Jobab son of Zerah from Bozrah succeeded him as king.

column.name: text
column.value: When Jobab died, Husham from the land of the Temanites succeeded him as king.

column.name: text
column.value: When Husham died, Hadad son of Bedad, who defeated Midian in the country of Moab, succeeded him as king. His city was named Avith.

column.name: text
column.value: When Hadad died, Samlah from Masrekah succeeded him as king.

column.name: text
column.value: When Samlah died, Shaul from Rehoboth on the river succeeded him as king.

column.name: text
column.value: When Shaul died, Baal-Hanan son of Acbor succeeded him as king.

column.name: text
column.value: When Baal-Hanan died, Hadad succeeded him as king. His city was named Pau, and his wife's name was Mehetabel daughter of Matred, the daughter of Me-Zahab.

column.name: text
column.value: Hadad also died. The chiefs of Edom were: Timna, Alvah, Jetheth,

column.name: text
column.value: Oholibamah, Elah, Pinon,

column.name: text
column.value: Kenaz, Teman, Mibzar,

column.name: text
column.value: Magdiel and Iram. These were the chiefs of Edom.

column.name: text
column.value: During Jehoiakim's reign, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon invaded the land, and Jehoiakim became his vassal for three years. But then he changed his mind and rebelled against Nebuchadnezzar.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD sent Babylonian, Aramean, Moabite and Ammonite raiders against him. He sent them to destroy Judah, in accordance with the word of the LORD proclaimed by his servants the prophets.

column.name: text
column.value: Surely these things happened to Judah according to the LORD'S command, in order to remove them from his presence because of the sins of Manasseh and all he had done,

column.name: text
column.value: including the shedding of innocent blood. For he had filled Jerusalem with innocent blood, and the LORD was not willing to forgive.

column.name: text
column.value: As for the other events of Jehoiakim's reign, and all he did, are they not written in the book of the annals of the kings of Judah?

column.name: text
column.value: Jehoiakim rested with his fathers. And Jehoiachin his son succeeded him as king.

column.name: text
column.value: The king of Egypt did not march out from his own country again, because the king of Babylon had taken all his territory, from the Wadi of Egypt to the Euphrates River.

column.name: text
column.value: Jehoiachin was eighteen years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem three months. His mother's name was Nehushta daughter of Elnathan; she was from Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: He did evil in the eyes of the LORD, just as his father had done.

column.name: text
column.value: At that time the officers of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon advanced on Jerusalem and laid siege to it,

column.name: text
column.value: and Nebuchadnezzar himself came up to the city while his officers were besieging it.

column.name: text
column.value: Jehoiachin king of Judah, his mother, his attendants, his nobles and his officials all surrendered to him. In the eighth year of the reign of the king of Babylon, he took Jehoiachin prisoner.

column.name: text
column.value: As the LORD had declared, Nebuchadnezzar removed all the treasures from the temple of the LORD and from the royal palace, and took away all the gold articles that Solomon king of Israel had made for the temple of the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: He carried into exile all Jerusalem: all the officers and fighting men, and all the craftsmen and artisans--a total of ten thousand. Only the poorest people of the land were left.

column.name: text
column.value: Nebuchadnezzar took Jehoiachin captive to Babylon. He also took from Jerusalem to Babylon the king's mother, his wives, his officials and the leading men of the land.

column.name: text
column.value: The king of Babylon also deported to Babylon the entire force of seven thousand fighting men, strong and fit for war, and a thousand craftsmen and artisans.

column.name: text
column.value: He made Mattaniah, Jehoiachin's uncle, king in his place and changed his name to Zedekiah.

column.name: text
column.value: Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem eleven years. His mother's name was Hamutal daughter of Jeremiah; she was from Libnah.

column.name: text
column.value: He did evil in the eyes of the LORD, just as Jehoiakim had done.

column.name: text
column.value: It was because of the LORD'S anger that all this happened to Jerusalem and Judah, and in the end he thrust them from his presence. Now Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon.

column.name: text
column.value: So in the ninth year of Zedekiah's reign, on the tenth day of the tenth month, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon marched against Jerusalem with his whole army. He encamped outside the city and built siege works all around it.

column.name: text
column.value: The city was kept under siege until the eleventh year of King Zedekiah.

column.name: text
column.value: By the ninth day of the fourth month the famine in the city had become so severe that there was no food for the people to eat.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the city wall was broken through, and the whole army fled at night through the gate between the two walls near the king's garden, though the Babylonians were surrounding the city. They fled toward the Arabah,

column.name: text
column.value: but the Babylonian army pursued the king and overtook him in the plains of Jericho. All his soldiers were separated from him and scattered,

column.name: text
column.value: and he was captured. He was taken to the king of Babylon at Riblah, where sentence was pronounced on him.

column.name: text
column.value: They killed the sons of Zedekiah before his eyes. Then they put out his eyes, bound him with bronze shackles and took him to Babylon.

column.name: text
column.value: On the seventh day of the fifth month, in the nineteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, Nebuzaradan commander of the imperial guard, an official of the king of Babylon, came to Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: He set fire to the temple of the LORD, the royal palace and all the houses of Jerusalem. Every important building he burned down.

column.name: text
column.value: The whole Babylonian army, under the commander of the imperial guard, broke down the walls around Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: Nebuzaradan the commander of the guard carried into exile the people who remained in the city, along with the rest of the populace and those who had gone over to the king of Babylon.

column.name: text
column.value: But the commander left behind some of the poorest people of the land to work the vineyards and fields.

column.name: text
column.value: The Babylonians broke up the bronze pillars, the movable stands and the bronze Sea that were at the temple of the LORD and they carried the bronze to Babylon.

column.name: text
column.value: They also took away the pots, shovels, wick trimmers, dishes and all the bronze articles used in the temple service.

column.name: text
column.value: The commander of the imperial guard took away the censers and sprinkling bowls--all that were made of pure gold or silver.

column.name: text
column.value: The bronze from the two pillars, the Sea and the movable stands, which Solomon had made for the temple of the LORD, was more than could be weighed.

column.name: text
column.value: Each pillar was twenty-seven feet high. The bronze capital on top of one pillar was four and a half feet high and was decorated with a network and pomegranates of bronze all around. The other pillar, with its network, was similar.

column.name: text
column.value: The commander of the guard took as prisoners Seraiah the chief priest, Zephaniah the priest next in rank and the three doorkeepers.

column.name: text
column.value: Of those still in the city, he took the officer in charge of the fighting men and five royal advisers. He also took the secretary who was chief officer in charge of conscripting the people of the land and sixty of his men who were found in the city.

column.name: text
column.value: Nebuzaradan the commander took them all and brought them to the king of Babylon at Riblah.

column.name: text
column.value: There at Riblah, in the land of Hamath, the king had them executed. So Judah went into captivity, away from her land.

column.name: text
column.value: Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon appointed Gedaliah son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan, to be over the people he had left behind in Judah.

column.name: text
column.value: When all the army officers and their men heard that the king of Babylon had appointed Gedaliah as governor, they came to Gedaliah at Mizpah--Ishmael son of Nethaniah, Johanan son of Kareah, Seraiah son of Tanhumeth the Netophathite, Jaazaniah the son of the Maacathite, and their men.

column.name: text
column.value: Gedaliah took an oath to reassure them and their men. "Do not be afraid of the Babylonian officials," he said. "Settle down in the land and serve the king of Babylon, and it will go well with you."

column.name: text
column.value: In the seventh month, however, Ishmael son of Nethaniah, the son of Elishama, who was of royal blood, came with ten men and assassinated Gedaliah and also the men of Judah and the Babylonians who were with him at Mizpah.

column.name: text
column.value: At this, all the people from the least to the greatest, together with the army officers, fled to Egypt for fear of the Babylonians.

column.name: text
column.value: In the thirty-seventh year of the exile of Jehoiachin king of Judah, in the year Evil-Merodach became king of Babylon, he released Jehoiachin from prison on the twenty-seventh day of the twelfth month.

column.name: text
column.value: He spoke kindly to him and gave him a seat of honor higher than those of the other kings who were with him in Babylon.

column.name: text
column.value: So Jehoiachin put aside his prison clothes and for the rest of his life ate regularly at the king's table.

column.name: text
column.value: Day by day the king gave Jehoiachin a regular allowance as long as he lived.

column.name: text
column.value: These were the sons of Israel: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Zebulun,

column.name: text
column.value: Dan, Joseph, Benjamin, Naphtali, Gad and Asher.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Judah: Er, Onan and Shelah. These three were born to him by a Canaanite woman, the daughter of Shua. Er, Judah's firstborn, was wicked in the LORD'S sight; so the LORD put him to death.

column.name: text
column.value: Tamar, Judah's daughter-in-law, bore him Perez and Zerah. Judah had five sons in all.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Perez: Hezron and Hamul.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Zerah: Zimri, Ethan, Heman, Calcol and Darda--five in all.

column.name: text
column.value: The son of Carmi: Achar, who brought trouble on Israel by violating the ban on taking devoted things.

column.name: text
column.value: The son of Ethan: Azariah.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons born to Hezron were: Jerahmeel, Ram and Caleb.

column.name: text
column.value: Ram was the father of Amminadab, and Amminadab the father of Nahshon, the leader of the people of Judah.

column.name: text
column.value: Nahshon was the father of Salmon, Salmon the father of Boaz,

column.name: text
column.value: Boaz the father of Obed and Obed the father of Jesse.

column.name: text
column.value: Jesse was the father of Eliab his firstborn; the second son was Abinadab, the third Shimea,

column.name: text
column.value: the fourth Nethanel, the fifth Raddai,

column.name: text
column.value: the sixth Ozem and the seventh David.

column.name: text
column.value: Their sisters were Zeruiah and Abigail. Zeruiah's three sons were Abishai, Joab and Asahel.

column.name: text
column.value: Abigail was the mother of Amasa, whose father was Jether the Ishmaelite.

column.name: text
column.value: Caleb son of Hezron had children by his wife Azubah (and by Jerioth). These were her sons: Jesher, Shobab and Ardon.

column.name: text
column.value: When Azubah died, Caleb married Ephrath, who bore him Hur.

column.name: text
column.value: Hur was the father of Uri, and Uri the father of Bezalel.

column.name: text
column.value: Later, Hezron lay with the daughter of Makir the father of Gilead (he had married her when he was sixty years old), and she bore him Segub.

column.name: text
column.value: Segub was the father of Jair, who controlled twenty-three towns in Gilead.

column.name: text
column.value: (But Geshur and Aram captured Havvoth Jair, as well as Kenath with its surrounding settlements--sixty towns.) All these were descendants of Makir the father of Gilead.

column.name: text
column.value: After Hezron died in Caleb Ephrathah, Abijah the wife of Hezron bore him Ashhur the father of Tekoa.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Jerahmeel the firstborn of Hezron: Ram his firstborn, Bunah, Oren, Ozem and Ahijah.

column.name: text
column.value: Jerahmeel had another wife, whose name was Atarah; she was the mother of Onam.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Ram the firstborn of Jerahmeel: Maaz, Jamin and Eker.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Onam: Shammai and Jada. The sons of Shammai: Nadab and Abishur.

column.name: text
column.value: Abishur's wife was named Abihail, who bore him Ahban and Molid.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Nadab: Seled and Appaim. Seled died without children.

column.name: text
column.value: The son of Appaim: Ishi, who was the father of Sheshan. Sheshan was the father of Ahlai.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Jada, Shammai's brother: Jether and Jonathan. Jether died without children.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Jonathan: Peleth and Zaza. These were the descendants of Jerahmeel.

column.name: text
column.value: Sheshan had no sons--only daughters. He had an Egyptian servant named Jarha.

column.name: text
column.value: Sheshan gave his daughter in marriage to his servant Jarha, and she bore him Attai.

column.name: text
column.value: Attai was the father of Nathan, Nathan the father of Zabad,

column.name: text
column.value: Zabad the father of Ephlal, Ephlal the father of Obed,

column.name: text
column.value: Obed the father of Jehu, Jehu the father of Azariah,

column.name: text
column.value: Azariah the father of Helez, Helez the father of Eleasah,

column.name: text
column.value: Eleasah the father of Sismai, Sismai the father of Shallum,

column.name: text
column.value: Shallum the father of Jekamiah, and Jekamiah the father of Elishama.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Caleb the brother of Jerahmeel: Mesha his firstborn, who was the father of Ziph, and his son Mareshah, who was the father of Hebron.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Hebron: Korah, Tappuah, Rekem and Shema.

column.name: text
column.value: Shema was the father of Raham, and Raham the father of Jorkeam. Rekem was the father of Shammai.

column.name: text
column.value: The son of Shammai was Maon, and Maon was the father of Beth Zur.

column.name: text
column.value: Caleb's concubine Ephah was the mother of Haran, Moza and Gazez. Haran was the father of Gazez.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Jahdai: Regem, Jotham, Geshan, Pelet, Ephah and Shaaph.

column.name: text
column.value: Caleb's concubine Maacah was the mother of Sheber and Tirhanah.

column.name: text
column.value: She also gave birth to Shaaph the father of Madmannah and to Sheva the father of Macbenah and Gibea. Caleb's daughter was Acsah.

column.name: text
column.value: These were the descendants of Caleb. The sons of Hur the firstborn of Ephrathah: Shobal the father of Kiriath Jearim,

column.name: text
column.value: Salma the father of Bethlehem, and Hareph the father of Beth Gader.

column.name: text
column.value: The descendants of Shobal the father of Kiriath Jearim were: Haroeh, half the Manahathites,

column.name: text
column.value: and the clans of Kiriath Jearim: the Ithrites, Puthites, Shumathites and Mishraites. From these descended the Zorathites and Eshtaolites.

column.name: text
column.value: The descendants of Salma: Bethlehem, the Netophathites, Atroth Beth Joab, half the Manahathites, the Zorites,

column.name: text
column.value: and the clans of scribes who lived at Jabez: the Tirathites, Shimeathites and Sucathites. These are the Kenites who came from Hammath, the father of the house of Recab.

column.name: text
column.value: The descendants of Judah: Perez, Hezron, Carmi, Hur and Shobal.

column.name: text
column.value: Reaiah son of Shobal was the father of Jahath, and Jahath the father of Ahumai and Lahad. These were the clans of the Zorathites.

column.name: text
column.value: These were the sons of Etam: Jezreel, Ishma and Idbash. Their sister was named Hazzelelponi.

column.name: text
column.value: Penuel was the father of Gedor, and Ezer the father of Hushah. These were the descendants of Hur, the firstborn of Ephrathah and father of Bethlehem.

column.name: text
column.value: Ashhur the father of Tekoa had two wives, Helah and Naarah.

column.name: text
column.value: Naarah bore him Ahuzzam, Hepher, Temeni and Haahashtari. These were the descendants of Naarah.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Helah: Zereth, Zohar, Ethnan,

column.name: text
column.value: and Koz, who was the father of Anub and Hazzobebah and of the clans of Aharhel son of Harum.

column.name: text
column.value: Jabez was more honorable than his brothers. His mother had named him Jabez, saying, "I gave birth to him in pain."

column.name: text
column.value: Jabez cried out to the God of Israel, "Oh, that you would bless me and enlarge my territory! Let your hand be with me, and keep me from harm so that I will be free from pain." And God granted his request.

column.name: text
column.value: Kelub, Shuhah's brother, was the father of Mehir, who was the father of Eshton.

column.name: text
column.value: Eshton was the father of Beth Rapha, Paseah and Tehinnah the father of Ir Nahash. These were the men of Recah.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Kenaz: Othniel and Seraiah. The sons of Othniel: Hathath and Meonothai.

column.name: text
column.value: Meonothai was the father of Ophrah. Seraiah was the father of Joab, the father of Ge Harashim. It was called this because its people were craftsmen.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Caleb son of Jephunneh: Iru, Elah and Naam. The son of Elah: Kenaz.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Jehallelel: Ziph, Ziphah, Tiria and Asarel.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Ezrah: Jether, Mered, Epher and Jalon. One of Mered's wives gave birth to Miriam, Shammai and Ishbah the father of Eshtemoa.

column.name: text
column.value: (His Judean wife gave birth to Jered the father of Gedor, Heber the father of Soco, and Jekuthiel the father of Zanoah.) These were the children of Pharaoh's daughter Bithiah, whom Mered had married.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Hodiah's wife, the sister of Naham: the father of Keilah the Garmite, and Eshtemoa the Maacathite.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Shimon: Amnon, Rinnah, Ben-Hanan and Tilon. The descendants of Ishi: Zoheth and Ben-Zoheth.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Shelah son of Judah: Er the father of Lecah, Laadah the father of Mareshah and the clans of the linen workers at Beth Ashbea,

column.name: text
column.value: Jokim, the men of Cozeba, and Joash and Saraph, who ruled in Moab and Jashubi Lehem. (These records are from ancient times.)

column.name: text
column.value: They were the potters who lived at Netaim and Gederah; they stayed there and worked for the king.

column.name: text
column.value: The descendants of Simeon: Nemuel, Jamin, Jarib, Zerah and Shaul;

column.name: text
column.value: Shallum was Shaul's son, Mibsam his son and Mishma his son.

column.name: text
column.value: The descendants of Mishma: Hammuel his son, Zaccur his son and Shimei his son.

column.name: text
column.value: Shimei had sixteen sons and six daughters, but his brothers did not have many children; so their entire clan did not become as numerous as the people of Judah.

column.name: text
column.value: They lived in Beersheba, Moladah, Hazar Shual,

column.name: text
column.value: Bilhah, Ezem, Tolad,

column.name: text
column.value: Bethuel, Hormah, Ziklag,

column.name: text
column.value: Beth Marcaboth, Hazar Susim, Beth Biri and Shaaraim. These were their towns until the reign of David.

column.name: text
column.value: Their surrounding villages were Etam, Ain, Rimmon, Token and Ashan--five towns--

column.name: text
column.value: and all the villages around these towns as far as Baalath. These were their settlements. And they kept a genealogical record.

column.name: text
column.value: Meshobab, Jamlech, Joshah son of Amaziah,

column.name: text
column.value: Joel, Jehu son of Joshibiah, the son of Seraiah, the son of Asiel,

column.name: text
column.value: also Elioenai, Jaakobah, Jeshohaiah, Asaiah, Adiel, Jesimiel, Benaiah,

column.name: text
column.value: and Ziza son of Shiphi, the son of Allon, the son of Jedaiah, the son of Shimri, the son of Shemaiah.

column.name: text
column.value: The men listed above by name were leaders of their clans. Their families increased greatly,

column.name: text
column.value: and they went to the outskirts of Gedor to the east of the valley in search of pasture for their flocks.

column.name: text
column.value: They found rich, good pasture, and the land was spacious, peaceful and quiet. Some Hamites had lived there formerly.

column.name: text
column.value: The men whose names were listed came in the days of Hezekiah king of Judah. They attacked the Hamites in their dwellings and also the Meunites who were there and completely destroyed them, as is evident to this day. Then they settled in their place, because there was pasture for their flocks.

column.name: text
column.value: And five hundred of these Simeonites, led by Pelatiah, Neariah, Rephaiah and Uzziel, the sons of Ishi, invaded the hill country of Seir.

column.name: text
column.value: They killed the remaining Amalekites who had escaped, and they have lived there to this day.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath and Merari.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Kohath: Amram, Izhar, Hebron and Uzziel.

column.name: text
column.value: The children of Amram: Aaron, Moses and Miriam. The sons of Aaron: Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar.

column.name: text
column.value: Eleazar was the father of Phinehas, Phinehas the father of Abishua,

column.name: text
column.value: Abishua the father of Bukki, Bukki the father of Uzzi,

column.name: text
column.value: Uzzi the father of Zerahiah, Zerahiah the father of Meraioth,

column.name: text
column.value: Meraioth the father of Amariah, Amariah the father of Ahitub,

column.name: text
column.value: Ahitub the father of Zadok, Zadok the father of Ahimaaz,

column.name: text
column.value: Ahimaaz the father of Azariah, Azariah the father of Johanan,

column.name: text
column.value: Johanan the father of Azariah (it was he who served as priest in the temple Solomon built in Jerusalem),

column.name: text
column.value: Azariah the father of Amariah, Amariah the father of Ahitub,

column.name: text
column.value: Ahitub the father of Zadok, Zadok the father of Shallum,

column.name: text
column.value: Shallum the father of Hilkiah, Hilkiah the father of Azariah,

column.name: text
column.value: Azariah the father of Seraiah, and Seraiah the father of Jehozadak.

column.name: text
column.value: Jehozadak was deported when the LORD sent Judah and Jerusalem into exile by the hand of Nebuchadnezzar.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath and Merari.

column.name: text
column.value: These are the names of the sons of Gershon: Libni and Shimei.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Kohath: Amram, Izhar, Hebron and Uzziel.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi. These are the clans of the Levites listed according to their fathers:

column.name: text
column.value: Of Gershon: Libni his son, Jehath his son, Zimmah his son,

column.name: text
column.value: Joah his son, Iddo his son, Zerah his son and Jeatherai his son.

column.name: text
column.value: The descendants of Kohath: Amminadab his son, Korah his son, Assir his son,

column.name: text
column.value: Elkanah his son, Ebiasaph his son, Assir his son,

column.name: text
column.value: Tahath his son, Uriel his son, Uzziah his son and Shaul his son.

column.name: text
column.value: The descendants of Elkanah: Amasai, Ahimoth,

column.name: text
column.value: Elkanah his son, Zophai his son, Nahath his son,

column.name: text
column.value: Eliab his son, Jeroham his son, Elkanah his son and Samuel his son.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Samuel: Joel the firstborn and Abijah the second son.

column.name: text
column.value: The descendants of Merari: Mahli, Libni his son, Shimei his son, Uzzah his son,

column.name: text
column.value: Shimea his son, Haggiah his son and Asaiah his son.

column.name: text
column.value: These are the men David put in charge of the music in the house of the LORD after the ark came to rest there.

column.name: text
column.value: They ministered with music before the tabernacle, the Tent of Meeting, until Solomon built the temple of the LORD in Jerusalem. They performed their duties according to the regulations laid down for them.

column.name: text
column.value: Here are the men who served, together with their sons: From the Kohathites: Heman, the musician, the son of Joel, the son of Samuel,

column.name: text
column.value: the son of Elkanah, the son of Jeroham, the son of Eliel, the son of Toah,

column.name: text
column.value: the son of Zuph, the son of Elkanah, the son of Mahath, the son of Amasai,

column.name: text
column.value: the son of Elkanah, the son of Joel, the son of Azariah, the son of Zephaniah,

column.name: text
column.value: the son of Tahath, the son of Assir, the son of Ebiasaph, the son of Korah,

column.name: text
column.value: the son of Izhar, the son of Kohath, the son of Levi, the son of Israel;

column.name: text
column.value: and Heman's associate Asaph, who served at his right hand: Asaph son of Berekiah, the son of Shimea,

column.name: text
column.value: the son of Michael, the son of Baaseiah, the son of Malkijah,

column.name: text
column.value: the son of Ethni, the son of Zerah, the son of Adaiah,

column.name: text
column.value: the son of Ethan, the son of Zimmah, the son of Shimei,

column.name: text
column.value: the son of Jahath, the son of Gershon, the son of Levi;

column.name: text
column.value: and from their associates, the Merarites, at his left hand: Ethan son of Kishi, the son of Abdi, the son of Malluch,

column.name: text
column.value: the son of Hashabiah, the son of Amaziah, the son of Hilkiah,

column.name: text
column.value: the son of Amzi, the son of Bani, the son of Shemer,

column.name: text
column.value: the son of Mahli, the son of Mushi, the son of Merari, the son of Levi.

column.name: text
column.value: Their fellow Levites were assigned to all the other duties of the tabernacle, the house of God.

column.name: text
column.value: But Aaron and his descendants were the ones who presented offerings on the altar of burnt offering and on the altar of incense in connection with all that was done in the Most Holy Place, making atonement for Israel, in accordance with all that Moses the servant of God had commanded.

column.name: text
column.value: These were the descendants of Aaron: Eleazar his son, Phinehas his son, Abishua his son,

column.name: text
column.value: Bukki his son, Uzzi his son, Zerahiah his son,

column.name: text
column.value: Meraioth his son, Amariah his son, Ahitub his son,

column.name: text
column.value: Zadok his son and Ahimaaz his son.

column.name: text
column.value: These were the locations of their settlements allotted as their territory (they were assigned to the descendants of Aaron who were from the Kohathite clan, because the first lot was for them):

column.name: text
column.value: They were given Hebron in Judah with its surrounding pasturelands.

column.name: text
column.value: But the fields and villages around the city were given to Caleb son of Jephunneh.

column.name: text
column.value: So the descendants of Aaron were given Hebron (a city of refuge), and Libnah, Jattir, Eshtemoa,

column.name: text
column.value: Hilen, Debir,

column.name: text
column.value: Ashan, Juttah and Beth Shemesh, together with their pasturelands.

column.name: text
column.value: And from the tribe of Benjamin they were given Gibeon, Geba, Alemeth and Anathoth, together with their pasturelands. These towns, which were distributed among the Kohathite clans, were thirteen in all.

column.name: text
column.value: The rest of Kohath's descendants were allotted ten towns from the clans of half the tribe of Manasseh.

column.name: text
column.value: The descendants of Gershon, clan by clan, were allotted thirteen towns from the tribes of Issachar, Asher and Naphtali, and from the part of the tribe of Manasseh that is in Bashan.

column.name: text
column.value: The descendants of Merari, clan by clan, were allotted twelve towns from the tribes of Reuben, Gad and Zebulun.

column.name: text
column.value: So the Israelites gave the Levites these towns and their pasturelands.

column.name: text
column.value: From the tribes of Judah, Simeon and Benjamin they allotted the previously named towns.

column.name: text
column.value: Some of the Kohathite clans were given as their territory towns from the tribe of Ephraim.

column.name: text
column.value: In the hill country of Ephraim they were given Shechem (a city of refuge), and Gezer,

column.name: text
column.value: Jokmeam, Beth Horon,

column.name: text
column.value: Aijalon and Gath Rimmon, together with their pasturelands.

column.name: text
column.value: And from half the tribe of Manasseh the Israelites gave Aner and Bileam, together with their pasturelands, to the rest of the Kohathite clans.

column.name: text
column.value: The Gershonites received the following: From the clan of the half-tribe of Manasseh they received Golan in Bashan and also Ashtaroth, together with their pasturelands;

column.name: text
column.value: from the tribe of Issachar they received Kedesh, Daberath,

column.name: text
column.value: Ramoth and Anem, together with their pasturelands;

column.name: text
column.value: from the tribe of Asher they received Mashal, Abdon,

column.name: text
column.value: Hukok and Rehob, together with their pasturelands;

column.name: text
column.value: and from the tribe of Naphtali they received Kedesh in Galilee, Hammon and Kiriathaim, together with their pasturelands.

column.name: text
column.value: The Merarites (the rest of the Levites) received the following: From the tribe of Zebulun they received Jokneam, Kartah, Rimmono and Tabor, together with their pasturelands;

column.name: text
column.value: from the tribe of Reuben across the Jordan east of Jericho they received Bezer in the desert, Jahzah,

column.name: text
column.value: Kedemoth and Mephaath, together with their pasturelands;

column.name: text
column.value: and from the tribe of Gad they received Ramoth in Gilead, Mahanaim,

column.name: text
column.value: Heshbon and Jazer, together with their pasturelands.

column.name: text
column.value: These were the sons of David born to him in Hebron: The firstborn was Amnon the son of Ahinoam of Jezreel; the second, Daniel the son of Abigail of Carmel;

column.name: text
column.value: the third, Absalom the son of Maacah daughter of Talmai king of Geshur; the fourth, Adonijah the son of Haggith;

column.name: text
column.value: the fifth, Shephatiah the son of Abital; and the sixth, Ithream, by his wife Eglah.

column.name: text
column.value: These six were born to David in Hebron, where he reigned seven years and six months. David reigned in Jerusalem thirty-three years,

column.name: text
column.value: and these were the children born to him there: Shammua, Shobab, Nathan and Solomon. These four were by Bathsheba daughter of Ammiel.

column.name: text
column.value: There were also Ibhar, Elishua, Eliphelet,

column.name: text
column.value: Nogah, Nepheg, Japhia,

column.name: text
column.value: Elishama, Eliada and Eliphelet--nine in all.

column.name: text
column.value: All these were the sons of David, besides his sons by his concubines. And Tamar was their sister.

column.name: text
column.value: Solomon's son was Rehoboam, Abijah his son, Asa his son, Jehoshaphat his son,

column.name: text
column.value: Jehoram his son, Ahaziah his son, Joash his son,

column.name: text
column.value: Amaziah his son, Azariah his son, Jotham his son,

column.name: text
column.value: Ahaz his son, Hezekiah his son, Manasseh his son,

column.name: text
column.value: Amon his son, Josiah his son.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Josiah: Johanan the firstborn, Jehoiakim the second son, Zedekiah the third, Shallum the fourth.

column.name: text
column.value: The successors of Jehoiakim: Jehoiachin his son, and Zedekiah.

column.name: text
column.value: The descendants of Jehoiachin the captive: Shealtiel his son,

column.name: text
column.value: Malkiram, Pedaiah, Shenazzar, Jekamiah, Hoshama and Nedabiah.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Pedaiah: Zerubbabel and Shimei. The sons of Zerubbabel: Meshullam and Hananiah. Shelomith was their sister.

column.name: text
column.value: There were also five others: Hashubah, Ohel, Berekiah, Hasadiah and Jushab-Hesed.

column.name: text
column.value: The descendants of Hananiah: Pelatiah and Jeshaiah, and the sons of Rephaiah, of Arnan, of Obadiah and of Shecaniah.

column.name: text
column.value: The descendants of Shecaniah: Shemaiah and his sons: Hattush, Igal, Bariah, Neariah and Shaphat--six in all.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Neariah: Elioenai, Hizkiah and Azrikam--three in all.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Elioenai: Hodaviah, Eliashib, Pelaiah, Akkub, Johanan, Delaiah and Anani--seven in all.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Issachar: Tola, Puah, Jashub and Shimron--four in all.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Tola: Uzzi, Rephaiah, Jeriel, Jahmai, Ibsam and Samuel--heads of their families. During the reign of David, the descendants of Tola listed as fighting men in their genealogy numbered 22,600.

column.name: text
column.value: The son of Uzzi: Izrahiah. The sons of Izrahiah: Michael, Obadiah, Joel and Isshiah. All five of them were chiefs.

column.name: text
column.value: According to their family genealogy, they had 36,000 men ready for battle, for they had many wives and children.

column.name: text
column.value: The relatives who were fighting men belonging to all the clans of Issachar, as listed in their genealogy, were 87,000 in all.

column.name: text
column.value: Three sons of Benjamin: Bela, Beker and Jediael.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Bela: Ezbon, Uzzi, Uzziel, Jerimoth and Iri, heads of families--five in all. Their genealogical record listed 22,034 fighting men.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Beker: Zemirah, Joash, Eliezer, Elioenai, Omri, Jeremoth, Abijah, Anathoth and Alemeth. All these were the sons of Beker.

column.name: text
column.value: Their genealogical record listed the heads of families and 20,200 fighting men.

column.name: text
column.value: The son of Jediael: Bilhan. The sons of Bilhan: Jeush, Benjamin, Ehud, Kenaanah, Zethan, Tarshish and Ahishahar.

column.name: text
column.value: All these sons of Jediael were heads of families. There were 17,200 fighting men ready to go out to war.

column.name: text
column.value: The Shuppites and Huppites were the descendants of Ir, and the Hushites the descendants of Aher.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Naphtali: Jahziel, Guni, Jezer and Shillem--the descendants of Bilhah.

column.name: text
column.value: The descendants of Manasseh: Asriel was his descendant through his Aramean concubine. She gave birth to Makir the father of Gilead.

column.name: text
column.value: Makir took a wife from among the Huppites and Shuppites. His sister's name was Maacah. Another descendant was named Zelophehad, who had only daughters.

column.name: text
column.value: Makir's wife Maacah gave birth to a son and named him Peresh. His brother was named Sheresh, and his sons were Ulam and Rakem.

column.name: text
column.value: The son of Ulam: Bedan. These were the sons of Gilead son of Makir, the son of Manasseh.

column.name: text
column.value: His sister Hammoleketh gave birth to Ishhod, Abiezer and Mahlah.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Shemida were: Ahian, Shechem, Likhi and Aniam.

column.name: text
column.value: The descendants of Ephraim: Shuthelah, Bered his son, Tahath his son, Eleadah his son, Tahath his son,

column.name: text
column.value: Zabad his son and Shuthelah his son. Ezer and Elead were killed by the native-born men of Gath, when they went down to seize their livestock.

column.name: text
column.value: Their father Ephraim mourned for them many days, and his relatives came to comfort him.

column.name: text
column.value: Then he lay with his wife again, and she became pregnant and gave birth to a son. He named him Beriah, because there had been misfortune in his family.

column.name: text
column.value: His daughter was Sheerah, who built Lower and Upper Beth Horon as well as Uzzen Sheerah.

column.name: text
column.value: Rephah was his son, Resheph his son, Telah his son, Tahan his son,

column.name: text
column.value: Ladan his son, Ammihud his son, Elishama his son,

column.name: text
column.value: Nun his son and Joshua his son.

column.name: text
column.value: Their lands and settlements included Bethel and its surrounding villages, Naaran to the east, Gezer and its villages to the west, and Shechem and its villages all the way to Ayyah and its villages.

column.name: text
column.value: Along the borders of Manasseh were Beth Shan, Taanach, Megiddo and Dor, together with their villages. The descendants of Joseph son of Israel lived in these towns.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Asher: Imnah, Ishvah, Ishvi and Beriah. Their sister was Serah.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Beriah: Heber and Malkiel, who was the father of Birzaith.

column.name: text
column.value: Heber was the father of Japhlet, Shomer and Hotham and of their sister Shua.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Japhlet: Pasach, Bimhal and Ashvath. These were Japhlet's sons.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Shomer: Ahi, Rohgah, Hubbah and Aram.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of his brother Helem: Zophah, Imna, Shelesh and Amal.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Zophah: Suah, Harnepher, Shual, Beri, Imrah,

column.name: text
column.value: Bezer, Hod, Shamma, Shilshah, Ithran and Beera.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Jether: Jephunneh, Pispah and Ara.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Ulla: Arah, Hanniel and Rizia.

column.name: text
column.value: All these were descendants of Asher--heads of families, choice men, brave warriors and outstanding leaders. The number of men ready for battle, as listed in their genealogy, was 26,000.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Reuben the firstborn of Israel (he was the firstborn, but when he defiled his father's marriage bed, his rights as firstborn were given to the sons of Joseph son of Israel; so he could not be listed in the genealogical record in accordance with his birthright,

column.name: text
column.value: and though Judah was the strongest of his brothers and a ruler came from him, the rights of the firstborn belonged to Joseph)--

column.name: text
column.value: the sons of Reuben the firstborn of Israel: Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron and Carmi.

column.name: text
column.value: The descendants of Joel: Shemaiah his son, Gog his son, Shimei his son,

column.name: text
column.value: Micah his son, Reaiah his son, Baal his son,

column.name: text
column.value: and Beerah his son, whom Tiglath-Pileser king of Assyria took into exile. Beerah was a leader of the Reubenites.

column.name: text
column.value: Their relatives by clans, listed according to their genealogical records: Jeiel the chief, Zechariah,

column.name: text
column.value: and Bela son of Azaz, the son of Shema, the son of Joel. They settled in the area from Aroer to Nebo and Baal Meon.

column.name: text
column.value: To the east they occupied the land up to the edge of the desert that extends to the Euphrates River, because their livestock had increased in Gilead.

column.name: text
column.value: During Saul's reign they waged war against the Hagrites, who were defeated at their hands; they occupied the dwellings of the Hagrites throughout the entire region east of Gilead.

column.name: text
column.value: The Gadites lived next to them in Bashan, as far as Salecah:

column.name: text
column.value: Joel was the chief, Shapham the second, then Janai and Shaphat, in Bashan.

column.name: text
column.value: Their relatives, by families, were: Michael, Meshullam, Sheba, Jorai, Jacan, Zia and Eber--seven in all.

column.name: text
column.value: These were the sons of Abihail son of Huri, the son of Jaroah, the son of Gilead, the son of Michael, the son of Jeshishai, the son of Jahdo, the son of Buz.

column.name: text
column.value: Ahi son of Abdiel, the son of Guni, was head of their family.

column.name: text
column.value: The Gadites lived in Gilead, in Bashan and its outlying villages, and on all the pasturelands of Sharon as far as they extended.

column.name: text
column.value: All these were entered in the genealogical records during the reigns of Jotham king of Judah and Jeroboam king of Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: The Reubenites, the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh had 44,760 men ready for military service--able-bodied men who could handle shield and sword, who could use a bow, and who were trained for battle.

column.name: text
column.value: They waged war against the Hagrites, Jetur, Naphish and Nodab.

column.name: text
column.value: They were helped in fighting them, and God handed the Hagrites and all their allies over to them, because they cried out to him during the battle. He answered their prayers, because they trusted in him.

column.name: text
column.value: They seized the livestock of the Hagrites--fifty thousand camels, two hundred fifty thousand sheep and two thousand donkeys. They also took one hundred thousand people captive,

column.name: text
column.value: and many others fell slain, because the battle was God's. And they occupied the land until the exile.

column.name: text
column.value: The people of the half-tribe of Manasseh were numerous; they settled in the land from Bashan to Baal Hermon, that is, to Senir (Mount Hermon).

column.name: text
column.value: These were the heads of their families: Epher, Ishi, Eliel, Azriel, Jeremiah, Hodaviah and Jahdiel. They were brave warriors, famous men, and heads of their families.

column.name: text
column.value: But they were unfaithful to the God of their fathers and prostituted themselves to the gods of the peoples of the land, whom God had destroyed before them.

column.name: text
column.value: So the God of Israel stirred up the spirit of Pul king of Assyria (that is, Tiglath-Pileser king of Assyria), who took the Reubenites, the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh into exile. He took them to Halah, Habor, Hara and the river of Gozan, where they are to this day.

column.name: text
column.value: Benjamin was the father of Bela his firstborn, Ashbel the second son, Aharah the third,

column.name: text
column.value: Nohah the fourth and Rapha the fifth.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Bela were: Addar, Gera, Abihud,

column.name: text
column.value: Abishua, Naaman, Ahoah,

column.name: text
column.value: Gera, Shephuphan and Huram.

column.name: text
column.value: These were the descendants of Ehud, who were heads of families of those living in Geba and were deported to Manahath:

column.name: text
column.value: Naaman, Ahijah, and Gera, who deported them and who was the father of Uzza and Ahihud.

column.name: text
column.value: Sons were born to Shaharaim in Moab after he had divorced his wives Hushim and Baara.

column.name: text
column.value: By his wife Hodesh he had Jobab, Zibia, Mesha, Malcam,

column.name: text
column.value: Jeuz, Sakia and Mirmah. These were his sons, heads of families.

column.name: text
column.value: By Hushim he had Abitub and Elpaal.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Elpaal: Eber, Misham, Shemed (who built Ono and Lod with its surrounding villages),

column.name: text
column.value: and Beriah and Shema, who were heads of families of those living in Aijalon and who drove out the inhabitants of Gath.

column.name: text
column.value: Ahio, Shashak, Jeremoth,

column.name: text
column.value: Zebadiah, Arad, Eder,

column.name: text
column.value: Michael, Ishpah and Joha were the sons of Beriah.

column.name: text
column.value: Zebadiah, Meshullam, Hizki, Heber,

column.name: text
column.value: Ishmerai, Izliah and Jobab were the sons of Elpaal.

column.name: text
column.value: Jakim, Zicri, Zabdi,

column.name: text
column.value: Elienai, Zillethai, Eliel,

column.name: text
column.value: Adaiah, Beraiah and Shimrath were the sons of Shimei.

column.name: text
column.value: Ishpan, Eber, Eliel,

column.name: text
column.value: Abdon, Zicri, Hanan,

column.name: text
column.value: Hananiah, Elam, Anthothijah,

column.name: text
column.value: Iphdeiah and Penuel were the sons of Shashak.

column.name: text
column.value: Shamsherai, Shehariah, Athaliah,

column.name: text
column.value: Jaareshiah, Elijah and Zicri were the sons of Jeroham.

column.name: text
column.value: All these were heads of families, chiefs as listed in their genealogy, and they lived in Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: Jeiel the father of Gibeon lived in Gibeon. His wife's name was Maacah,

column.name: text
column.value: and his firstborn son was Abdon, followed by Zur, Kish, Baal, Ner, Nadab,

column.name: text
column.value: Gedor, Ahio, Zeker

column.name: text
column.value: and Mikloth, who was the father of Shimeah. They too lived near their relatives in Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: Ner was the father of Kish, Kish the father of Saul, and Saul the father of Jonathan, Malki-Shua, Abinadab and Esh-Baal.

column.name: text
column.value: The son of Jonathan: Merib-Baal, who was the father of Micah.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Micah: Pithon, Melech, Tarea and Ahaz.

column.name: text
column.value: Ahaz was the father of Jehoaddah, Jehoaddah was the father of Alemeth, Azmaveth and Zimri, and Zimri was the father of Moza.

column.name: text
column.value: Moza was the father of Binea; Raphah was his son, Eleasah his son and Azel his son.

column.name: text
column.value: Azel had six sons, and these were their names: Azrikam, Bokeru, Ishmael, Sheariah, Obadiah and Hanan. All these were the sons of Azel.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of his brother Eshek: Ulam his firstborn, Jeush the second son and Eliphelet the third.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Ulam were brave warriors who could handle the bow. They had many sons and grandsons--150 in all. All these were the descendants of Benjamin.

column.name: text
column.value: All Israel was listed in the genealogies recorded in the book of the kings of Israel. The people of Judah were taken captive to Babylon because of their unfaithfulness.

column.name: text
column.value: Now the first to resettle on their own property in their own towns were some Israelites, priests, Levites and temple servants.

column.name: text
column.value: Those from Judah, from Benjamin, and from Ephraim and Manasseh who lived in Jerusalem were:

column.name: text
column.value: Uthai son of Ammihud, the son of Omri, the son of Imri, the son of Bani, a descendant of Perez son of Judah.

column.name: text
column.value: Of the Shilonites: Asaiah the firstborn and his sons.

column.name: text
column.value: Of the Zerahites: Jeuel. The people from Judah numbered 690.

column.name: text
column.value: Of the Benjamites: Sallu son of Meshullam, the son of Hodaviah, the son of Hassenuah;

column.name: text
column.value: Ibneiah son of Jeroham; Elah son of Uzzi, the son of Micri; and Meshullam son of Shephatiah, the son of Reuel, the son of Ibnijah.

column.name: text
column.value: The people from Benjamin, as listed in their genealogy, numbered 956. All these men were heads of their families.

column.name: text
column.value: Of the priests: Jedaiah; Jehoiarib; Jakin;

column.name: text
column.value: Azariah son of Hilkiah, the son of Meshullam, the son of Zadok, the son of Meraioth, the son of Ahitub, the official in charge of the house of God;

column.name: text
column.value: Adaiah son of Jeroham, the son of Pashhur, the son of Malkijah; and Maasai son of Adiel, the son of Jahzerah, the son of Meshullam, the son of Meshillemith, the son of Immer.

column.name: text
column.value: The priests, who were heads of families, numbered 1,760. They were able men, responsible for ministering in the house of God.

column.name: text
column.value: Of the Levites: Shemaiah son of Hasshub, the son of Azrikam, the son of Hashabiah, a Merarite;

column.name: text
column.value: Bakbakkar, Heresh, Galal and Mattaniah son of Mica, the son of Zicri, the son of Asaph;

column.name: text
column.value: Obadiah son of Shemaiah, the son of Galal, the son of Jeduthun; and Berekiah son of Asa, the son of Elkanah, who lived in the villages of the Netophathites.

column.name: text
column.value: The gatekeepers: Shallum, Akkub, Talmon, Ahiman and their brothers, Shallum their chief

column.name: text
column.value: being stationed at the King's Gate on the east, up to the present time. These were the gatekeepers belonging to the camp of the Levites.

column.name: text
column.value: Shallum son of Kore, the son of Ebiasaph, the son of Korah, and his fellow gatekeepers from his family (the Korahites) were responsible for guarding the thresholds of the Tent just as their fathers had been responsible for guarding the entrance to the dwelling of the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: In earlier times Phinehas son of Eleazar was in charge of the gatekeepers, and the LORD was with him.

column.name: text
column.value: Zechariah son of Meshelemiah was the gatekeeper at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.

column.name: text
column.value: Altogether, those chosen to be gatekeepers at the thresholds numbered 212. They were registered by genealogy in their villages. The gatekeepers had been assigned to their positions of trust by David and Samuel the seer.

column.name: text
column.value: They and their descendants were in charge of guarding the gates of the house of the LORD--the house called the Tent.

column.name: text
column.value: The gatekeepers were on the four sides: east, west, north and south.

column.name: text
column.value: Their brothers in their villages had to come from time to time and share their duties for seven-day periods.

column.name: text
column.value: But the four principal gatekeepers, who were Levites, were entrusted with the responsibility for the rooms and treasuries in the house of God.

column.name: text
column.value: They would spend the night stationed around the house of God, because they had to guard it; and they had charge of the key for opening it each morning.

column.name: text
column.value: Some of them were in charge of the articles used in the temple service; they counted them when they were brought in and when they were taken out.

column.name: text
column.value: Others were assigned to take care of the furnishings and all the other articles of the sanctuary, as well as the flour and wine, and the oil, incense and spices.

column.name: text
column.value: But some of the priests took care of mixing the spices.

column.name: text
column.value: A Levite named Mattithiah, the firstborn son of Shallum the Korahite, was entrusted with the responsibility for baking the offering bread.

column.name: text
column.value: Some of their Kohathite brothers were in charge of preparing for every Sabbath the bread set out on the table.

column.name: text
column.value: Those who were musicians, heads of Levite families, stayed in the rooms of the temple and were exempt from other duties because they were responsible for the work day and night.

column.name: text
column.value: All these were heads of Levite families, chiefs as listed in their genealogy, and they lived in Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: Jeiel the father of Gibeon lived in Gibeon. His wife's name was Maacah,

column.name: text
column.value: and his firstborn son was Abdon, followed by Zur, Kish, Baal, Ner, Nadab,

column.name: text
column.value: Gedor, Ahio, Zechariah and Mikloth.

column.name: text
column.value: Mikloth was the father of Shimeam. They too lived near their relatives in Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: Ner was the father of Kish, Kish the father of Saul, and Saul the father of Jonathan, Malki-Shua, Abinadab and Esh-Baal.

column.name: text
column.value: The son of Jonathan: Merib-Baal, who was the father of Micah.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Micah: Pithon, Melech, Tahrea and Ahaz.

column.name: text
column.value: Ahaz was the father of Jadah, Jadah was the father of Alemeth, Azmaveth and Zimri, and Zimri was the father of Moza.

column.name: text
column.value: Moza was the father of Binea; Rephaiah was his son, Eleasah his son and Azel his son.

column.name: text
column.value: Azel had six sons, and these were their names: Azrikam, Bokeru, Ishmael, Sheariah, Obadiah and Hanan. These were the sons of Azel.

column.name: text
column.value: Now the Philistines fought against Israel; the Israelites fled before them, and many fell slain on Mount Gilboa.

column.name: text
column.value: The Philistines pressed hard after Saul and his sons, and they killed his sons Jonathan, Abinadab and Malki-Shua.

column.name: text
column.value: The fighting grew fierce around Saul, and when the archers overtook him, they wounded him.

column.name: text
column.value: Saul said to his armor-bearer, "Draw your sword and run me through, or these uncircumcised fellows will come and abuse me." But his armor-bearer was terrified and would not do it; so Saul took his own sword and fell on it.

column.name: text
column.value: When the armor-bearer saw that Saul was dead, he too fell on his sword and died.

column.name: text
column.value: So Saul and his three sons died, and all his house died together.

column.name: text
column.value: When all the Israelites in the valley saw that the army had fled and that Saul and his sons had died, they abandoned their towns and fled. And the Philistines came and occupied them.

column.name: text
column.value: The next day, when the Philistines came to strip the dead, they found Saul and his sons fallen on Mount Gilboa.

column.name: text
column.value: They stripped him and took his head and his armor, and sent messengers throughout the land of the Philistines to proclaim the news among their idols and their people.

column.name: text
column.value: They put his armor in the temple of their gods and hung up his head in the temple of Dagon.

column.name: text
column.value: When all the inhabitants of Jabesh Gilead heard of everything the Philistines had done to Saul,

column.name: text
column.value: all their valiant men went and took the bodies of Saul and his sons and brought them to Jabesh. Then they buried their bones under the great tree in Jabesh, and they fasted seven days.

column.name: text
column.value: Saul died because he was unfaithful to the LORD; he did not keep the word of the LORD and even consulted a medium for guidance,

column.name: text
column.value: and did not inquire of the LORD. So the LORD put him to death and turned the kingdom over to David son of Jesse.

column.name: text
column.value: These were the men who came to David at Ziklag, while he was banished from the presence of Saul son of Kish (they were among the warriors who helped him in battle;

column.name: text
column.value: they were armed with bows and were able to shoot arrows or to sling stones right-handed or left-handed; they were kinsmen of Saul from the tribe of Benjamin):

column.name: text
column.value: Ahiezer their chief and Joash the sons of Shemaah the Gibeathite; Jeziel and Pelet the sons of Azmaveth; Beracah, Jehu the Anathothite,

column.name: text
column.value: and Ishmaiah the Gibeonite, a mighty man among the Thirty, who was a leader of the Thirty; Jeremiah, Jahaziel, Johanan, Jozabad the Gederathite,

column.name: text
column.value: Eluzai, Jerimoth, Bealiah, Shemariah and Shephatiah the Haruphite;

column.name: text
column.value: Elkanah, Isshiah, Azarel, Joezer and Jashobeam the Korahites;

column.name: text
column.value: and Joelah and Zebadiah the sons of Jeroham from Gedor.

column.name: text
column.value: Some Gadites defected to David at his stronghold in the desert. They were brave warriors, ready for battle and able to handle the shield and spear. Their faces were the faces of lions, and they were as swift as gazelles in the mountains.

column.name: text
column.value: Ezer was the chief, Obadiah the second in command, Eliab the third,

column.name: text
column.value: Mishmannah the fourth, Jeremiah the fifth,

column.name: text
column.value: Attai the sixth, Eliel the seventh,

column.name: text
column.value: Johanan the eighth, Elzabad the ninth,

column.name: text
column.value: Jeremiah the tenth and Macbannai the eleventh.

column.name: text
column.value: These Gadites were army commanders; the least was a match for a hundred, and the greatest for a thousand.

column.name: text
column.value: It was they who crossed the Jordan in the first month when it was overflowing all its banks, and they put to flight everyone living in the valleys, to the east and to the west.

column.name: text
column.value: Other Benjamites and some men from Judah also came to David in his stronghold.

column.name: text
column.value: David went out to meet them and said to them, "If you have come to me in peace, to help me, I am ready to have you unite with me. But if you have come to betray me to my enemies when my hands are free from violence, may the God of our fathers see it and judge you."

column.name: text
column.value: Then the Spirit came upon Amasai, chief of the Thirty, and he said: "We are yours, O David! We are with you, O son of Jesse! Success, success to you, and success to those who help you, for your God will help you." So David received them and made them leaders of his raiding bands.

column.name: text
column.value: Some of the men of Manasseh defected to David when he went with the Philistines to fight against Saul. (He and his men did not help the Philistines because, after consultation, their rulers sent him away. They said, "It will cost us our heads if he deserts to his master Saul.")

column.name: text
column.value: When David went to Ziklag, these were the men of Manasseh who defected to him: Adnah, Jozabad, Jediael, Michael, Jozabad, Elihu and Zillethai, leaders of units of a thousand in Manasseh.

column.name: text
column.value: They helped David against raiding bands, for all of them were brave warriors, and they were commanders in his army.

column.name: text
column.value: Day after day men came to help David, until he had a great army, like the army of God.

column.name: text
column.value: These are the numbers of the men armed for battle who came to David at Hebron to turn Saul's kingdom over to him, as the LORD had said:

column.name: text
column.value: men of Judah, carrying shield and spear--6,800 armed for battle;

column.name: text
column.value: men of Simeon, warriors ready for battle--7,100;

column.name: text
column.value: men of Levi--4,600,

column.name: text
column.value: including Jehoiada, leader of the family of Aaron, with 3,700 men,

column.name: text
column.value: and Zadok, a brave young warrior, with 22 officers from his family;

column.name: text
column.value: men of Benjamin, Saul's kinsmen--3,000, most of whom had remained loyal to Saul's house until then;

column.name: text
column.value: men of Ephraim, brave warriors, famous in their own clans--20,800;

column.name: text
column.value: men of half the tribe of Manasseh, designated by name to come and make David king--18,000;

column.name: text
column.value: men of Issachar, who understood the times and knew what Israel should do--200 chiefs, with all their relatives under their command;

column.name: text
column.value: men of Zebulun, experienced soldiers prepared for battle with every type of weapon, to help David with undivided loyalty--50,000;

column.name: text
column.value: men of Naphtali--1,000 officers, together with 37,000 men carrying shields and spears;

column.name: text
column.value: men of Dan, ready for battle--28,600;

column.name: text
column.value: men of Asher, experienced soldiers prepared for battle--40,000;

column.name: text
column.value: and from east of the Jordan, men of Reuben, Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh, armed with every type of weapon--120,000.

column.name: text
column.value: All these were fighting men who volunteered to serve in the ranks. They came to Hebron fully determined to make David king over all Israel. All the rest of the Israelites were also of one mind to make David king.

column.name: text
column.value: The men spent three days there with David, eating and drinking, for their families had supplied provisions for them.

column.name: text
column.value: Also, their neighbors from as far away as Issachar, Zebulun and Naphtali came bringing food on donkeys, camels, mules and oxen. There were plentiful supplies of flour, fig cakes, raisin cakes, wine, oil, cattle and sheep, for there was joy in Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: Now Hiram king of Tyre sent messengers to David, along with cedar logs, stonemasons and carpenters to build a palace for him.

column.name: text
column.value: And David knew that the LORD had established him as king over Israel and that his kingdom had been highly exalted for the sake of his people Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: In Jerusalem David took more wives and became the father of more sons and daughters.

column.name: text
column.value: These are the names of the children born to him there: Shammua, Shobab, Nathan, Solomon,

column.name: text
column.value: Ibhar, Elishua, Elpelet,

column.name: text
column.value: Nogah, Nepheg, Japhia,

column.name: text
column.value: Elishama, Beeliada and Eliphelet.

column.name: text
column.value: When the Philistines heard that David had been anointed king over all Israel, they went up in full force to search for him, but David heard about it and went out to meet them.

column.name: text
column.value: Now the Philistines had come and raided the Valley of Rephaim;

column.name: text
column.value: so David inquired of God: "Shall I go and attack the Philistines? Will you hand them over to me?" The LORD answered him, "Go, I will hand them over to you."

column.name: text
column.value: So David and his men went up to Baal Perazim, and there he defeated them. He said, "As waters break out, God has broken out against my enemies by my hand." So that place was called Baal Perazim.

column.name: text
column.value: The Philistines had abandoned their gods there, and David gave orders to burn them in the fire.

column.name: text
column.value: Once more the Philistines raided the valley;

column.name: text
column.value: so David inquired of God again, and God answered him, "Do not go straight up, but circle around them and attack them in front of the balsam trees.

column.name: text
column.value: As soon as you hear the sound of marching in the tops of the balsam trees, move out to battle, because that will mean God has gone out in front of you to strike the Philistine army."

column.name: text
column.value: So David did as God commanded him, and they struck down the Philistine army, all the way from Gibeon to Gezer.

column.name: text
column.value: So David's fame spread throughout every land, and the LORD made all the nations fear him.

column.name: text
column.value: All Israel came together to David at Hebron and said, "We are your own flesh and blood.

column.name: text
column.value: In the past, even while Saul was king, you were the one who led Israel on their military campaigns. And the LORD your God said to you, 'You will shepherd my people Israel, and you will become their ruler.'"

column.name: text
column.value: When all the elders of Israel had come to King David at Hebron, he made a compact with them at Hebron before the LORD, and they anointed David king over Israel, as the LORD had promised through Samuel.

column.name: text
column.value: David and all the Israelites marched to Jerusalem (that is, Jebus). The Jebusites who lived there

column.name: text
column.value: said to David, "You will not get in here." Nevertheless, David captured the fortress of Zion, the City of David.

column.name: text
column.value: David had said, "Whoever leads the attack on the Jebusites will become commander-in-chief." Joab son of Zeruiah went up first, and so he received the command.

column.name: text
column.value: David then took up residence in the fortress, and so it was called the City of David.

column.name: text
column.value: He built up the city around it, from the supporting terraces to the surrounding wall, while Joab restored the rest of the city.

column.name: text
column.value: And David became more and more powerful, because the LORD Almighty was with him.

column.name: text
column.value: These were the chiefs of David's mighty men--they, together with all Israel, gave his kingship strong support to extend it over the whole land, as the LORD had promised--

column.name: text
column.value: this is the list of David's mighty men: Jashobeam, a Hacmonite, was chief of the officers; he raised his spear against three hundred men, whom he killed in one encounter.

column.name: text
column.value: Next to him was Eleazar son of Dodai the Ahohite, one of the three mighty men.

column.name: text
column.value: He was with David at Pas Dammim when the Philistines gathered there for battle. At a place where there was a field full of barley, the troops fled from the Philistines.

column.name: text
column.value: But they took their stand in the middle of the field. They defended it and struck the Philistines down, and the LORD brought about a great victory.

column.name: text
column.value: Three of the thirty chiefs came down to David to the rock at the cave of Adullam, while a band of Philistines was encamped in the Valley of Rephaim.

column.name: text
column.value: At that time David was in the stronghold, and the Philistine garrison was at Bethlehem.

column.name: text
column.value: David longed for water and said, "Oh, that someone would get me a drink of water from the well near the gate of Bethlehem!"

column.name: text
column.value: So the Three broke through the Philistine lines, drew water from the well near the gate of Bethlehem and carried it back to David. But he refused to drink it; instead, he poured it out before the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: "God forbid that I should do this!" he said. "Should I drink the blood of these men who went at the risk of their lives?" Because they risked their lives to bring it back, David would not drink it. Such were the exploits of the three mighty men.

column.name: text
column.value: Abishai the brother of Joab was chief of the Three. He raised his spear against three hundred men, whom he killed, and so he became as famous as the Three.

column.name: text
column.value: He was doubly honored above the Three and became their commander, even though he was not included among them.

column.name: text
column.value: Benaiah son of Jehoiada was a valiant fighter from Kabzeel, who performed great exploits. He struck down two of Moab's best men. He also went down into a pit on a snowy day and killed a lion.

column.name: text
column.value: And he struck down an Egyptian who was seven and a half feet tall. Although the Egyptian had a spear like a weaver's rod in his hand, Benaiah went against him with a club. He snatched the spear from the Egyptian's hand and killed him with his own spear.

column.name: text
column.value: Such were the exploits of Benaiah son of Jehoiada; he too was as famous as the three mighty men.

column.name: text
column.value: He was held in greater honor than any of the Thirty, but he was not included among the Three. And David put him in charge of his bodyguard.

column.name: text
column.value: The mighty men were: Asahel the brother of Joab, Elhanan son of Dodo from Bethlehem,

column.name: text
column.value: Shammoth the Harorite, Helez the Pelonite,

column.name: text
column.value: Ira son of Ikkesh from Tekoa, Abiezer from Anathoth,

column.name: text
column.value: Sibbecai the Hushathite, Ilai the Ahohite,

column.name: text
column.value: Maharai the Netophathite, Heled son of Baanah the Netophathite,

column.name: text
column.value: Ithai son of Ribai from Gibeah in Benjamin, Benaiah the Pirathonite,

column.name: text
column.value: Hurai from the ravines of Gaash, Abiel the Arbathite,

column.name: text
column.value: Azmaveth the Baharumite, Eliahba the Shaalbonite,

column.name: text
column.value: the sons of Hashem the Gizonite, Jonathan son of Shagee the Hararite,

column.name: text
column.value: Ahiam son of Sacar the Hararite, Eliphal son of Ur,

column.name: text
column.value: Hepher the Mekerathite, Ahijah the Pelonite,

column.name: text
column.value: Hezro the Carmelite, Naarai son of Ezbai,

column.name: text
column.value: Joel the brother of Nathan, Mibhar son of Hagri,

column.name: text
column.value: Zelek the Ammonite, Naharai the Berothite, the armor-bearer of Joab son of Zeruiah,

column.name: text
column.value: Ira the Ithrite, Gareb the Ithrite,

column.name: text
column.value: Uriah the Hittite, Zabad son of Ahlai,

column.name: text
column.value: Adina son of Shiza the Reubenite, who was chief of the Reubenites, and the thirty with him,

column.name: text
column.value: Hanan son of Maacah, Joshaphat the Mithnite,

column.name: text
column.value: Uzzia the Ashterathite, Shama and Jeiel the sons of Hotham the Aroerite,

column.name: text
column.value: Jediael son of Shimri, his brother Joha the Tizite,

column.name: text
column.value: Eliel the Mahavite, Jeribai and Joshaviah the sons of Elnaam, Ithmah the Moabite,

column.name: text
column.value: Eliel, Obed and Jaasiel the Mezobaite.

column.name: text
column.value: David conferred with each of his officers, the commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds.

column.name: text
column.value: He then said to the whole assembly of Israel, "If it seems good to you and if it is the will of the LORD our God, let us send word far and wide to the rest of our brothers throughout the territories of Israel, and also to the priests and Levites who are with them in their towns and pasturelands, to come and join us.

column.name: text
column.value: Let us bring the ark of our God back to us, for we did not inquire of it during the reign of Saul."

column.name: text
column.value: The whole assembly agreed to do this, because it seemed right to all the people.

column.name: text
column.value: So David assembled all the Israelites, from the Shihor River in Egypt to Lebo Hamath, to bring the ark of God from Kiriath Jearim.

column.name: text
column.value: David and all the Israelites with him went to Baalah of Judah (Kiriath Jearim) to bring up from there the ark of God the LORD, who is enthroned between the cherubim--the ark that is called by the Name.

column.name: text
column.value: They moved the ark of God from Abinadab's house on a new cart, with Uzzah and Ahio guiding it.

column.name: text
column.value: David and all the Israelites were celebrating with all their might before God, with songs and with harps, lyres, tambourines, cymbals and trumpets.

column.name: text
column.value: When they came to the threshing floor of Kidon, Uzzah reached out his hand to steady the ark, because the oxen stumbled.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD'S anger burned against Uzzah, and he struck him down because he had put his hand on the ark. So he died there before God.

column.name: text
column.value: Then David was angry because the LORD'S wrath had broken out against Uzzah, and to this day that place is called Perez Uzzah.

column.name: text
column.value: David was afraid of God that day and asked, "How can I ever bring the ark of God to me?"

column.name: text
column.value: He did not take the ark to be with him in the City of David. Instead, he took it aside to the house of Obed-Edom the Gittite.

column.name: text
column.value: The ark of God remained with the family of Obed-Edom in his house for three months, and the LORD blessed his household and everything he had.

column.name: text
column.value: After David had constructed buildings for himself in the City of David, he prepared a place for the ark of God and pitched a tent for it.

column.name: text
column.value: Then David said, "No one but the Levites may carry the ark of God, because the LORD chose them to carry the ark of the LORD and to minister before him forever."

column.name: text
column.value: David assembled all Israel in Jerusalem to bring up the ark of the LORD to the place he had prepared for it.

column.name: text
column.value: He called together the descendants of Aaron and the Levites:

column.name: text
column.value: From the descendants of Kohath, Uriel the leader and 120 relatives;

column.name: text
column.value: from the descendants of Merari, Asaiah the leader and 220 relatives;

column.name: text
column.value: from the descendants of Gershon, Joel the leader and 130 relatives;

column.name: text
column.value: from the descendants of Elizaphan, Shemaiah the leader and 200 relatives;

column.name: text
column.value: from the descendants of Hebron, Eliel the leader and 80 relatives;

column.name: text
column.value: from the descendants of Uzziel, Amminadab the leader and 112 relatives.

column.name: text
column.value: Then David summoned Zadok and Abiathar the priests, and Uriel, Asaiah, Joel, Shemaiah, Eliel and Amminadab the Levites.

column.name: text
column.value: He said to them, "You are the heads of the Levitical families; you and your fellow Levites are to consecrate yourselves and bring up the ark of the LORD, the God of Israel, to the place I have prepared for it.

column.name: text
column.value: It was because you, the Levites, did not bring it up the first time that the LORD our God broke out in anger against us. We did not inquire of him about how to do it in the prescribed way."

column.name: text
column.value: So the priests and Levites consecrated themselves in order to bring up the ark of the LORD, the God of Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: And the Levites carried the ark of God with the poles on their shoulders, as Moses had commanded in accordance with the word of the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: David told the leaders of the Levites to appoint their brothers as singers to sing joyful songs, accompanied by musical instruments: lyres, harps and cymbals.

column.name: text
column.value: So the Levites appointed Heman son of Joel; from his brothers, Asaph son of Berekiah; and from their brothers the Merarites, Ethan son of Kushaiah;

column.name: text
column.value: and with them their brothers next in rank: Zechariah, Jaaziel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Unni, Eliab, Benaiah, Maaseiah, Mattithiah, Eliphelehu, Mikneiah, Obed-Edom and Jeiel, the gatekeepers.

column.name: text
column.value: The musicians Heman, Asaph and Ethan were to sound the bronze cymbals;

column.name: text
column.value: Zechariah, Aziel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Unni, Eliab, Maaseiah and Benaiah were to play the lyres according to alamoth,

column.name: text
column.value: and Mattithiah, Eliphelehu, Mikneiah, Obed-Edom, Jeiel and Azaziah were to play the harps, directing according to sheminith.

column.name: text
column.value: Kenaniah the head Levite was in charge of the singing; that was his responsibility because he was skillful at it.

column.name: text
column.value: Berekiah and Elkanah were to be doorkeepers for the ark.

column.name: text
column.value: Shebaniah, Joshaphat, Nethanel, Amasai, Zechariah, Benaiah and Eliezer the priests were to blow trumpets before the ark of God. Obed-Edom and Jehiah were also to be doorkeepers for the ark.

column.name: text
column.value: So David and the elders of Israel and the commanders of units of a thousand went to bring up the ark of the covenant of the LORD from the house of Obed-Edom, with rejoicing.

column.name: text
column.value: Because God had helped the Levites who were carrying the ark of the covenant of the LORD, seven bulls and seven rams were sacrificed.

column.name: text
column.value: Now David was clothed in a robe of fine linen, as were all the Levites who were carrying the ark, and as were the singers, and Kenaniah, who was in charge of the singing of the choirs. David also wore a linen ephod.

column.name: text
column.value: So all Israel brought up the ark of the covenant of the LORD with shouts, with the sounding of rams' horns and trumpets, and of cymbals, and the playing of lyres and harps.

column.name: text
column.value: As the ark of the covenant of the LORD was entering the City of David, Michal daughter of Saul watched from a window. And when she saw King David dancing and celebrating, she despised him in her heart.

column.name: text
column.value: They brought the ark of God and set it inside the tent that David had pitched for it, and they presented burnt offerings and fellowship offerings before God.

column.name: text
column.value: After David had finished sacrificing the burnt offerings and fellowship offerings, he blessed the people in the name of the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: Then he gave a loaf of bread, a cake of dates and a cake of raisins to each Israelite man and woman.

column.name: text
column.value: He appointed some of the Levites to minister before the ark of the LORD, to make petition, to give thanks, and to praise the LORD, the God of Israel:

column.name: text
column.value: Asaph was the chief, Zechariah second, then Jeiel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Mattithiah, Eliab, Benaiah, Obed-Edom and Jeiel. They were to play the lyres and harps, Asaph was to sound the cymbals,

column.name: text
column.value: and Benaiah and Jahaziel the priests were to blow the trumpets regularly before the ark of the covenant of God.

column.name: text
column.value: That day David first committed to Asaph and his associates this psalm of thanks to the LORD:

column.name: text
