column.value: Give thanks to the LORD, call on his name; make known among the nations what he has done.

column.name: text
column.value: Sing to him, sing praise to him; tell of all his wonderful acts.

column.name: text
column.value: Glory in his holy name; let the hearts of those who seek the LORD rejoice.

column.name: text
column.value: Look to the LORD and his strength; seek his face always.

column.name: text
column.value: Remember the wonders he has done, his miracles, and the judgments he pronounced,

column.name: text
column.value: O descendants of Israel his servant, O sons of Jacob, his chosen ones.

column.name: text
column.value: He is the LORD our God; his judgments are in all the earth.

column.name: text
column.value: He remembers his covenant forever, the word he commanded, for a thousand generations,

column.name: text
column.value: the covenant he made with Abraham, the oath he swore to Isaac.

column.name: text
column.value: He confirmed it to Jacob as a decree, to Israel as an everlasting covenant:

column.name: text
column.value: "To you I will give the land of Canaan as the portion you will inherit."

column.name: text
column.value: When they were but few in number, few indeed, and strangers in it,

column.name: text
column.value: they wandered from nation to nation, from one kingdom to another.

column.name: text
column.value: He allowed no man to oppress them; for their sake he rebuked kings:

column.name: text
column.value: "Do not touch my anointed ones; do my prophets no harm."

column.name: text
column.value: Sing to the LORD, all the earth; proclaim his salvation day after day.

column.name: text
column.value: Declare his glory among the nations, his marvelous deeds among all peoples.

column.name: text
column.value: For great is the LORD and most worthy of praise; he is to be feared above all gods.

column.name: text
column.value: For all the gods of the nations are idols, but the LORD made the heavens.

column.name: text
column.value: Splendor and majesty are before him; strength and joy in his dwelling place.

column.name: text
column.value: Ascribe to the LORD, O families of nations, ascribe to the LORD glory and strength,

column.name: text
column.value: ascribe to the LORD the glory due his name. Bring an offering and come before him; worship the LORD in the splendor of his holiness.

column.name: text
column.value: Tremble before him, all the earth! The world is firmly established; it cannot be moved.

column.name: text
column.value: Let the heavens rejoice, let the earth be glad; let them say among the nations, "The LORD reigns!"

column.name: text
column.value: Let the sea resound, and all that is in it; let the fields be jubilant, and everything in them!

column.name: text
column.value: Then the trees of the forest will sing, they will sing for joy before the LORD, for he comes to judge the earth.

column.name: text
column.value: Give thanks to the LORD, for he is good; his love endures forever.

column.name: text
column.value: Cry out, "Save us, O God our Savior; gather us and deliver us from the nations, that we may give thanks to your holy name, that we may glory in your praise."

column.name: text
column.value: Praise be to the LORD, the God of Israel, from everlasting to everlasting. Then all the people said "Amen" and "Praise the LORD."

column.name: text
column.value: David left Asaph and his associates before the ark of the covenant of the LORD to minister there regularly, according to each day's requirements.

column.name: text
column.value: He also left Obed-Edom and his sixty-eight associates to minister with them. Obed-Edom son of Jeduthun, and also Hosah, were gatekeepers.

column.name: text
column.value: David left Zadok the priest and his fellow priests before the tabernacle of the LORD at the high place in Gibeon

column.name: text
column.value: to present burnt offerings to the LORD on the altar of burnt offering regularly, morning and evening, in accordance with everything written in the Law of the LORD, which he had given Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: With them were Heman and Jeduthun and the rest of those chosen and designated by name to give thanks to the LORD, "for his love endures forever."

column.name: text
column.value: Heman and Jeduthun were responsible for the sounding of the trumpets and cymbals and for the playing of the other instruments for sacred song. The sons of Jeduthun were stationed at the gate.

column.name: text
column.value: Then all the people left, each for his own home, and David returned home to bless his family.

column.name: text
column.value: In the course of time, David defeated the Philistines and subdued them, and he took Gath and its surrounding villages from the control of the Philistines.

column.name: text
column.value: David also defeated the Moabites, and they became subject to him and brought tribute.

column.name: text
column.value: Moreover, David fought Hadadezer king of Zobah, as far as Hamath, when he went to establish his control along the Euphrates River.

column.name: text
column.value: David captured a thousand of his chariots, seven thousand charioteers and twenty thousand foot soldiers. He hamstrung all but a hundred of the chariot horses.

column.name: text
column.value: When the Arameans of Damascus came to help Hadadezer king of Zobah, David struck down twenty-two thousand of them.

column.name: text
column.value: He put garrisons in the Aramean kingdom of Damascus, and the Arameans became subject to him and brought tribute. The LORD gave David victory everywhere he went.

column.name: text
column.value: David took the gold shields carried by the officers of Hadadezer and brought them to Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: From Tebah and Cun, towns that belonged to Hadadezer, David took a great quantity of bronze, which Solomon used to make the bronze Sea, the pillars and various bronze articles.

column.name: text
column.value: When Tou king of Hamath heard that David had defeated the entire army of Hadadezer king of Zobah,

column.name: text
column.value: he sent his son Hadoram to King David to greet him and congratulate him on his victory in battle over Hadadezer, who had been at war with Tou. Hadoram brought all kinds of articles of gold and silver and bronze.

column.name: text
column.value: King David dedicated these articles to the LORD, as he had done with the silver and gold he had taken from all these nations: Edom and Moab, the Ammonites and the Philistines, and Amalek.

column.name: text
column.value: Abishai son of Zeruiah struck down eighteen thousand Edomites in the Valley of Salt.

column.name: text
column.value: He put garrisons in Edom, and all the Edomites became subject to David. The LORD gave David victory everywhere he went.

column.name: text
column.value: David reigned over all Israel, doing what was just and right for all his people.

column.name: text
column.value: Joab son of Zeruiah was over the army; Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud was recorder;

column.name: text
column.value: Zadok son of Ahitub and Ahimelech son of Abiathar were priests; Shavsha was secretary;

column.name: text
column.value: Benaiah son of Jehoiada was over the Kerethites and Pelethites; and David's sons were chief officials at the king's side.

column.name: text
column.value: In the course of time, Nahash king of the Ammonites died, and his son succeeded him as king.

column.name: text
column.value: David thought, "I will show kindness to Hanun son of Nahash, because his father showed kindness to me." So David sent a delegation to express his sympathy to Hanun concerning his father. When David's men came to Hanun in the land of the Ammonites to express sympathy to him,

column.name: text
column.value: the Ammonite nobles said to Hanun, "Do you think David is honoring your father by sending men to you to express sympathy? Haven't his men come to you to explore and spy out the country and overthrow it?"

column.name: text
column.value: So Hanun seized David's men, shaved them, cut off their garments in the middle at the buttocks, and sent them away.

column.name: text
column.value: When someone came and told David about the men, he sent messengers to meet them, for they were greatly humiliated. The king said, "Stay at Jericho till your beards have grown, and then come back."

column.name: text
column.value: When the Ammonites realized that they had become a stench in David's nostrils, Hanun and the Ammonites sent a thousand talents of silver to hire chariots and charioteers from Aram Naharaim, Aram Maacah and Zobah.

column.name: text
column.value: They hired thirty-two thousand chariots and charioteers, as well as the king of Maacah with his troops, who came and camped near Medeba, while the Ammonites were mustered from their towns and moved out for battle.

column.name: text
column.value: On hearing this, David sent Joab out with the entire army of fighting men.

column.name: text
column.value: The Ammonites came out and drew up in battle formation at the entrance to their city, while the kings who had come were by themselves in the open country.

column.name: text
column.value: Joab saw that there were battle lines in front of him and behind him; so he selected some of the best troops in Israel and deployed them against the Arameans.

column.name: text
column.value: He put the rest of the men under the command of Abishai his brother, and they were deployed against the Ammonites.

column.name: text
column.value: Joab said, "If the Arameans are too strong for me, then you are to rescue me; but if the Ammonites are too strong for you, then I will rescue you.

column.name: text
column.value: Be strong and let us fight bravely for our people and the cities of our God. The LORD will do what is good in his sight."

column.name: text
column.value: Then Joab and the troops with him advanced to fight the Arameans, and they fled before him.

column.name: text
column.value: When the Ammonites saw that the Arameans were fleeing, they too fled before his brother Abishai and went inside the city. So Joab went back to Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: After the Arameans saw that they had been routed by Israel, they sent messengers and had Arameans brought from beyond the River, with Shophach the commander of Hadadezer's army leading them.

column.name: text
column.value: When David was told of this, he gathered all Israel and crossed the Jordan; he advanced against them and formed his battle lines opposite them. David formed his lines to meet the Arameans in battle, and they fought against him.

column.name: text
column.value: But they fled before Israel, and David killed seven thousand of their charioteers and forty thousand of their foot soldiers. He also killed Shophach the commander of their army.

column.name: text
column.value: When the vassals of Hadadezer saw that they had been defeated by Israel, they made peace with David and became subject to him. So the Arameans were not willing to help the Ammonites anymore.

column.name: text
column.value: After David was settled in his palace, he said to Nathan the prophet, "Here I am, living in a palace of cedar, while the ark of the covenant of the LORD is under a tent."

column.name: text
column.value: Nathan replied to David, "Whatever you have in mind, do it, for God is with you."

column.name: text
column.value: That night the word of God came to Nathan, saying:

column.name: text
column.value: "Go and tell my servant David, 'This is what the LORD says: You are not the one to build me a house to dwell in.

column.name: text
column.value: I have not dwelt in a house from the day I brought Israel up out of Egypt to this day. I have moved from one tent site to another, from one dwelling place to another.

column.name: text
column.value: Wherever I have moved with all the Israelites, did I ever say to any of their leaders whom I commanded to shepherd my people, "Why have you not built me a house of cedar?" '

column.name: text
column.value: "Now then, tell my servant David, 'This is what the LORD Almighty says: I took you from the pasture and from following the flock, to be ruler over my people Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: I have been with you wherever you have gone, and I have cut off all your enemies from before you. Now I will make your name like the names of the greatest men of the earth.

column.name: text
column.value: And I will provide a place for my people Israel and will plant them so that they can have a home of their own and no longer be disturbed. Wicked people will not oppress them anymore, as they did at the beginning

column.name: text
column.value: and have done ever since the time I appointed leaders over my people Israel. I will also subdue all your enemies. "'I declare to you that the LORD will build a house for you:

column.name: text
column.value: When your days are over and you go to be with your fathers, I will raise up your offspring to succeed you, one of your own sons, and I will establish his kingdom.

column.name: text
column.value: He is the one who will build a house for me, and I will establish his throne forever.

column.name: text
column.value: I will be his father, and he will be my son. I will never take my love away from him, as I took it away from your predecessor.

column.name: text
column.value: I will set him over my house and my kingdom forever; his throne will be established forever.'"

column.name: text
column.value: Nathan reported to David all the words of this entire revelation.

column.name: text
column.value: Then King David went in and sat before the LORD, and he said: "Who am I, O LORD God, and what is my family, that you have brought me this far?

column.name: text
column.value: And as if this were not enough in your sight, O God, you have spoken about the future of the house of your servant. You have looked on me as though I were the most exalted of men, O LORD God.

column.name: text
column.value: "What more can David say to you for honoring your servant? For you know your servant,

column.name: text
column.value: O LORD. For the sake of your servant and according to your will, you have done this great thing and made known all these great promises.

column.name: text
column.value: "There is no one like you, O LORD, and there is no God but you, as we have heard with our own ears.

column.name: text
column.value: And who is like your people Israel--the one nation on earth whose God went out to redeem a people for himself, and to make a name for yourself, and to perform great and awesome wonders by driving out nations from before your people, whom you redeemed from Egypt?

column.name: text
column.value: You made your people Israel your very own forever, and you, O LORD, have become their God.

column.name: text
column.value: "And now, LORD, let the promise you have made concerning your servant and his house be established forever. Do as you promised,

column.name: text
column.value: so that it will be established and that your name will be great forever. Then men will say, 'The LORD Almighty, the God over Israel, is Israel's God!' And the house of your servant David will be established before you.

column.name: text
column.value: "You, my God, have revealed to your servant that you will build a house for him. So your servant has found courage to pray to you.

column.name: text
column.value: O LORD, you are God! You have promised these good things to your servant.

column.name: text
column.value: Now you have been pleased to bless the house of your servant, that it may continue forever in your sight; for you, O LORD, have blessed it, and it will be blessed forever."

column.name: text
column.value: Satan rose up against Israel and incited David to take a census of Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: So David said to Joab and the commanders of the troops, "Go and count the Israelites from Beersheba to Dan. Then report back to me so that I may know how many there are."

column.name: text
column.value: But Joab replied, "May the LORD multiply his troops a hundred times over. My lord the king, are they not all my lord's subjects? Why does my lord want to do this? Why should he bring guilt on Israel?"

column.name: text
column.value: The king's word, however, overruled Joab; so Joab left and went throughout Israel and then came back to Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: Joab reported the number of the fighting men to David: In all Israel there were one million one hundred thousand men who could handle a sword, including four hundred and seventy thousand in Judah.

column.name: text
column.value: But Joab did not include Levi and Benjamin in the numbering, because the king's command was repulsive to him.

column.name: text
column.value: This command was also evil in the sight of God; so he punished Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: Then David said to God, "I have sinned greatly by doing this. Now, I beg you, take away the guilt of your servant. I have done a very foolish thing."

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD said to Gad, David's seer,

column.name: text
column.value: "Go and tell David, 'This is what the LORD says: I am giving you three options. Choose one of them for me to carry out against you.'"

column.name: text
column.value: So Gad went to David and said to him, "This is what the LORD says: 'Take your choice:

column.name: text
column.value: three years of famine, three months of being swept away before your enemies, with their swords overtaking you, or three days of the sword of the LORD--days of plague in the land, with the angel of the LORD ravaging every part of Israel.' Now then, decide how I should answer the one who sent me."

column.name: text
column.value: David said to Gad, "I am in deep distress. Let me fall into the hands of the LORD, for his mercy is very great; but do not let me fall into the hands of men."

column.name: text
column.value: So the LORD sent a plague on Israel, and seventy thousand men of Israel fell dead.

column.name: text
column.value: And God sent an angel to destroy Jerusalem. But as the angel was doing so, the LORD saw it and was grieved because of the calamity and said to the angel who was destroying the people, "Enough! Withdraw your hand." The angel of the LORD was then standing at the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite.

column.name: text
column.value: David looked up and saw the angel of the LORD standing between heaven and earth, with a drawn sword in his hand extended over Jerusalem. Then David and the elders, clothed in sackcloth, fell facedown.

column.name: text
column.value: David said to God, "Was it not I who ordered the fighting men to be counted? I am the one who has sinned and done wrong. These are but sheep. What have they done? O LORD my God, let your hand fall upon me and my family, but do not let this plague remain on your people."

column.name: text
column.value: Then the angel of the LORD ordered Gad to tell David to go up and build an altar to the LORD on the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite.

column.name: text
column.value: So David went up in obedience to the word that Gad had spoken in the name of the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: While Araunah was threshing wheat, he turned and saw the angel; his four sons who were with him hid themselves.

column.name: text
column.value: Then David approached, and when Araunah looked and saw him, he left the threshing floor and bowed down before David with his face to the ground.

column.name: text
column.value: David said to him, "Let me have the site of your threshing floor so I can build an altar to the LORD, that the plague on the people may be stopped. Sell it to me at the full price."

column.name: text
column.value: Araunah said to David, "Take it! Let my lord the king do whatever pleases him. Look, I will give the oxen for the burnt offerings, the threshing sledges for the wood, and the wheat for the grain offering. I will give all this."

column.name: text
column.value: But King David replied to Araunah, "No, I insist on paying the full price. I will not take for the LORD what is yours, or sacrifice a burnt offering that costs me nothing."

column.name: text
column.value: So David paid Araunah six hundred shekels of gold for the site.

column.name: text
column.value: David built an altar to the LORD there and sacrificed burnt offerings and fellowship offerings. He called on the LORD, and the LORD answered him with fire from heaven on the altar of burnt offering.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD spoke to the angel, and he put his sword back into its sheath.

column.name: text
column.value: At that time, when David saw that the LORD had answered him on the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite, he offered sacrifices there.

column.name: text
column.value: The tabernacle of the LORD, which Moses had made in the desert, and the altar of burnt offering were at that time on the high place at Gibeon.

column.name: text
column.value: But David could not go before it to inquire of God, because he was afraid of the sword of the angel of the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: Then David said, "The house of the LORD God is to be here, and also the altar of burnt offering for Israel."

column.name: text
column.value: So David gave orders to assemble the aliens living in Israel, and from among them he appointed stonecutters to prepare dressed stone for building the house of God.

column.name: text
column.value: He provided a large amount of iron to make nails for the doors of the gateways and for the fittings, and more bronze than could be weighed.

column.name: text
column.value: He also provided more cedar logs than could be counted, for the Sidonians and Tyrians had brought large numbers of them to David.

column.name: text
column.value: David said, "My son Solomon is young and inexperienced, and the house to be built for the LORD should be of great magnificence and fame and splendor in the sight of all the nations. Therefore I will make preparations for it." So David made extensive preparations before his death.

column.name: text
column.value: Then he called for his son Solomon and charged him to build a house for the LORD, the God of Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: David said to Solomon: "My son, I had it in my heart to build a house for the Name of the LORD my God.

column.name: text
column.value: But this word of the LORD came to me: 'You have shed much blood and have fought many wars. You are not to build a house for my Name, because you have shed much blood on the earth in my sight.

column.name: text
column.value: But you will have a son who will be a man of peace and rest, and I will give him rest from all his enemies on every side. His name will be Solomon, and I will grant Israel peace and quiet during his reign.

column.name: text
column.value: He is the one who will build a house for my Name. He will be my son, and I will be his father. And I will establish the throne of his kingdom over Israel forever.'

column.name: text
column.value: "Now, my son, the LORD be with you, and may you have success and build the house of the LORD your God, as he said you would.

column.name: text
column.value: May the LORD give you discretion and understanding when he puts you in command over Israel, so that you may keep the law of the LORD your God.

column.name: text
column.value: Then you will have success if you are careful to observe the decrees and laws that the LORD gave Moses for Israel. Be strong and courageous. Do not be afraid or discouraged.

column.name: text
column.value: "I have taken great pains to provide for the temple of the LORD a hundred thousand talents of gold, a million talents of silver, quantities of bronze and iron too great to be weighed, and wood and stone. And you may add to them.

column.name: text
column.value: You have many workmen: stonecutters, masons and carpenters, as well as men skilled in every kind of work

column.name: text
column.value: in gold and silver, bronze and iron--craftsmen beyond number. Now begin the work, and the LORD be with you."

column.name: text
column.value: Then David ordered all the leaders of Israel to help his son Solomon.

column.name: text
column.value: He said to them, "Is not the LORD your God with you? And has he not granted you rest on every side? For he has handed the inhabitants of the land over to me, and the land is subject to the LORD and to his people.

column.name: text
column.value: Now devote your heart and soul to seeking the LORD your God. Begin to build the sanctuary of the LORD God, so that you may bring the ark of the covenant of the LORD and the sacred articles belonging to God into the temple that will be built for the Name of the LORD."

column.name: text
column.value: The divisions of the gatekeepers: From the Korahites: Meshelemiah son of Kore, one of the sons of Asaph.

column.name: text
column.value: Meshelemiah had sons: Zechariah the firstborn, Jediael the second, Zebadiah the third, Jathniel the fourth,

column.name: text
column.value: Elam the fifth, Jehohanan the sixth and Eliehoenai the seventh.

column.name: text
column.value: Obed-Edom also had sons: Shemaiah the firstborn, Jehozabad the second, Joah the third, Sacar the fourth, Nethanel the fifth,

column.name: text
column.value: Ammiel the sixth, Issachar the seventh and Peullethai the eighth. (For God had blessed Obed-Edom.)

column.name: text
column.value: His son Shemaiah also had sons, who were leaders in their father's family because they were very capable men.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Shemaiah: Othni, Rephael, Obed and Elzabad; his relatives Elihu and Semakiah were also able men.

column.name: text
column.value: All these were descendants of Obed-Edom; they and their sons and their relatives were capable men with the strength to do the work--descendants of Obed-Edom, 62 in all.

column.name: text
column.value: Meshelemiah had sons and relatives, who were able men--18 in all.

column.name: text
column.value: Hosah the Merarite had sons: Shimri the first (although he was not the firstborn, his father had appointed him the first),

column.name: text
column.value: Hilkiah the second, Tabaliah the third and Zechariah the fourth. The sons and relatives of Hosah were 13 in all.

column.name: text
column.value: These divisions of the gatekeepers, through their chief men, had duties for ministering in the temple of the LORD, just as their relatives had.

column.name: text
column.value: Lots were cast for each gate, according to their families, young and old alike.

column.name: text
column.value: The lot for the East Gate fell to Shelemiah. Then lots were cast for his son Zechariah, a wise counselor, and the lot for the North Gate fell to him.

column.name: text
column.value: The lot for the South Gate fell to Obed-Edom, and the lot for the storehouse fell to his sons.

column.name: text
column.value: The lots for the West Gate and the Shalleketh Gate on the upper road fell to Shuppim and Hosah. Guard was alongside of guard:

column.name: text
column.value: There were six Levites a day on the east, four a day on the north, four a day on the south and two at a time at the storehouse.

column.name: text
column.value: As for the court to the west, there were four at the road and two at the court itself.

column.name: text
column.value: These were the divisions of the gatekeepers who were descendants of Korah and Merari.

column.name: text
column.value: Their fellow Levites were in charge of the treasuries of the house of God and the treasuries for the dedicated things.

column.name: text
column.value: The descendants of Ladan, who were Gershonites through Ladan and who were heads of families belonging to Ladan the Gershonite, were Jehieli,

column.name: text
column.value: the sons of Jehieli, Zetham and his brother Joel. They were in charge of the treasuries of the temple of the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: From the Amramites, the Izharites, the Hebronites and the Uzzielites:

column.name: text
column.value: Shubael, a descendant of Gershom son of Moses, was the officer in charge of the treasuries.

column.name: text
column.value: His relatives through Eliezer: Rehabiah his son, Jeshaiah his son, Joram his son, Zicri his son and Shelomith his son.

column.name: text
column.value: Shelomith and his relatives were in charge of all the treasuries for the things dedicated by King David, by the heads of families who were the commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds, and by the other army commanders.

column.name: text
column.value: Some of the plunder taken in battle they dedicated for the repair of the temple of the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: And everything dedicated by Samuel the seer and by Saul son of Kish, Abner son of Ner and Joab son of Zeruiah, and all the other dedicated things were in the care of Shelomith and his relatives.

column.name: text
column.value: From the Izharites: Kenaniah and his sons were assigned duties away from the temple, as officials and judges over Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: From the Hebronites: Hashabiah and his relatives--seventeen hundred able men--were responsible in Israel west of the Jordan for all the work of the LORD and for the king's service.

column.name: text
column.value: As for the Hebronites, Jeriah was their chief according to the genealogical records of their families. In the fortieth year of David's reign a search was made in the records, and capable men among the Hebronites were found at Jazer in Gilead.

column.name: text
column.value: Jeriah had twenty-seven hundred relatives, who were able men and heads of families, and King David put them in charge of the Reubenites, the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh for every matter pertaining to God and for the affairs of the king.

column.name: text
column.value: David, together with the commanders of the army, set apart some of the sons of Asaph, Heman and Jeduthun for the ministry of prophesying, accompanied by harps, lyres and cymbals. Here is the list of the men who performed this service:

column.name: text
column.value: From the sons of Asaph: Zaccur, Joseph, Nethaniah and Asarelah. The sons of Asaph were under the supervision of Asaph, who prophesied under the king's supervision.

column.name: text
column.value: As for Jeduthun, from his sons: Gedaliah, Zeri, Jeshaiah, Shimei, Hashabiah and Mattithiah, six in all, under the supervision of their father Jeduthun, who prophesied, using the harp in thanking and praising the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: As for Heman, from his sons: Bukkiah, Mattaniah, Uzziel, Shubael and Jerimoth; Hananiah, Hanani, Eliathah, Giddalti and Romamti-Ezer; Joshbekashah, Mallothi, Hothir and Mahazioth.

column.name: text
column.value: All these were sons of Heman the king's seer. They were given him through the promises of God to exalt him. God gave Heman fourteen sons and three daughters.

column.name: text
column.value: All these men were under the supervision of their fathers for the music of the temple of the LORD, with cymbals, lyres and harps, for the ministry at the house of God. Asaph, Jeduthun and Heman were under the supervision of the king.

column.name: text
column.value: Along with their relatives--all of them trained and skilled in music for the LORD--they numbered 288.

column.name: text
column.value: Young and old alike, teacher as well as student, cast lots for their duties.

column.name: text
column.value: The first lot, which was for Asaph, fell to Joseph, his sons and relatives, 12 the second to Gedaliah, he and his relatives and sons, 12

column.name: text
column.value: the third to Zaccur, his sons and relatives, 12

column.name: text
column.value: the fourth to Izri, his sons and relatives, 12

column.name: text
column.value: the fifth to Nethaniah, his sons and relatives, 12

column.name: text
column.value: the sixth to Bukkiah, his sons and relatives, 12

column.name: text
column.value: the seventh to Jesarelah, his sons and relatives, 12

column.name: text
column.value: the eighth to Jeshaiah, his sons and relatives, 12

column.name: text
column.value: the ninth to Mattaniah, his sons and relatives, 12

column.name: text
column.value: the tenth to Shimei, his sons and relatives, 12

column.name: text
column.value: the eleventh to Azarel, his sons and relatives, 12

column.name: text
column.value: the twelfth to Hashabiah, his sons and relatives, 12

column.name: text
column.value: the thirteenth to Shubael, his sons and relatives, 12

column.name: text
column.value: the fourteenth to Mattithiah, his sons and relatives, 12

column.name: text
column.value: the fifteenth to Jerimoth, his sons and relatives, 12

column.name: text
column.value: the sixteenth to Hananiah, his sons and relatives, 12

column.name: text
column.value: the seventeenth to Joshbekashah, his sons and relatives, 12

column.name: text
column.value: the eighteenth to Hanani, his sons and relatives, 12

column.name: text
column.value: the nineteenth to Mallothi, his sons and relatives, 12

column.name: text
column.value: the twentieth to Eliathah, his sons and relatives, 12

column.name: text
column.value: the twenty-first to Hothir, his sons and relatives, 12

column.name: text
column.value: the twenty-second to Giddalti, his sons and relatives, 12

column.name: text
column.value: the twenty-third to Mahazioth, his sons and relatives, 12

column.name: text
column.value: the twenty-fourth to Romamti-Ezer, his sons and relatives, 12

column.name: text
column.value: When David was old and full of years, he made his son Solomon king over Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: He also gathered together all the leaders of Israel, as well as the priests and Levites.

column.name: text
column.value: The Levites thirty years old or more were counted, and the total number of men was thirty-eight thousand.

column.name: text
column.value: David said, "Of these, twenty-four thousand are to supervise the work of the temple of the LORD and six thousand are to be officials and judges.

column.name: text
column.value: Four thousand are to be gatekeepers and four thousand are to praise the LORD with the musical instruments I have provided for that purpose."

column.name: text
column.value: David divided the Levites into groups corresponding to the sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath and Merari.

column.name: text
column.value: Belonging to the Gershonites: Ladan and Shimei.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Ladan: Jehiel the first, Zetham and Joel--three in all.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Shimei: Shelomoth, Haziel and Haran--three in all. These were the heads of the families of Ladan.

column.name: text
column.value: And the sons of Shimei: Jahath, Ziza, Jeush and Beriah. These were the sons of Shimei--four in all.

column.name: text
column.value: Jahath was the first and Ziza the second, but Jeush and Beriah did not have many sons; so they were counted as one family with one assignment.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Kohath: Amram, Izhar, Hebron and Uzziel--four in all.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Amram: Aaron and Moses. Aaron was set apart, he and his descendants forever, to consecrate the most holy things, to offer sacrifices before the LORD, to minister before him and to pronounce blessings in his name forever.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Moses the man of God were counted as part of the tribe of Levi.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Moses: Gershom and Eliezer.

column.name: text
column.value: The descendants of Gershom: Shubael was the first.

column.name: text
column.value: The descendants of Eliezer: Rehabiah was the first. Eliezer had no other sons, but the sons of Rehabiah were very numerous.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Izhar: Shelomith was the first.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Hebron: Jeriah the first, Amariah the second, Jahaziel the third and Jekameam the fourth.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Uzziel: Micah the first and Isshiah the second.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi. The sons of Mahli: Eleazar and Kish.

column.name: text
column.value: Eleazar died without having sons: he had only daughters. Their cousins, the sons of Kish, married them.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Mushi: Mahli, Eder and Jerimoth--three in all.

column.name: text
column.value: These were the descendants of Levi by their families--the heads of families as they were registered under their names and counted individually, that is, the workers twenty years old or more who served in the temple of the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: For David had said, "Since the LORD, the God of Israel, has granted rest to his people and has come to dwell in Jerusalem forever,

column.name: text
column.value: the Levites no longer need to carry the tabernacle or any of the articles used in its service."

column.name: text
column.value: According to the last instructions of David, the Levites were counted from those twenty years old or more.

column.name: text
column.value: The duty of the Levites was to help Aaron's descendants in the service of the temple of the LORD: to be in charge of the courtyards, the side rooms, the purification of all sacred things and the performance of other duties at the house of God.

column.name: text
column.value: They were in charge of the bread set out on the table, the flour for the grain offerings, the unleavened wafers, the baking and the mixing, and all measurements of quantity and size.

column.name: text
column.value: They were also to stand every morning to thank and praise the LORD. They were to do the same in the evening

column.name: text
column.value: and whenever burnt offerings were presented to the LORD on Sabbaths and at New Moon festivals and at appointed feasts. They were to serve before the LORD regularly in the proper number and in the way prescribed for them.

column.name: text
column.value: And so the Levites carried out their responsibilities for the Tent of Meeting, for the Holy Place and, under their brothers the descendants of Aaron, for the service of the temple of the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: In the spring, at the time when kings go off to war, Joab led out the armed forces. He laid waste the land of the Ammonites and went to Rabbah and besieged it, but David remained in Jerusalem. Joab attacked Rabbah and left it in ruins.

column.name: text
column.value: David took the crown from the head of their king--its weight was found to be a talent of gold, and it was set with precious stones--and it was placed on David's head. He took a great quantity of plunder from the city

column.name: text
column.value: and brought out the people who were there, consigning them to labor with saws and with iron picks and axes. David did this to all the Ammonite towns. Then David and his entire army returned to Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: In the course of time, war broke out with the Philistines, at Gezer. At that time Sibbecai the Hushathite killed Sippai, one of the descendants of the Rephaites, and the Philistines were subjugated.

column.name: text
column.value: In another battle with the Philistines, Elhanan son of Jair killed Lahmi the brother of Goliath the Gittite, who had a spear with a shaft like a weaver's rod.

column.name: text
column.value: In still another battle, which took place at Gath, there was a huge man with six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot--twenty-four in all. He also was descended from Rapha.

column.name: text
column.value: When he taunted Israel, Jonathan son of Shimea, David's brother, killed him.

column.name: text
column.value: These were descendants of Rapha in Gath, and they fell at the hands of David and his men.

column.name: text
column.value: These were the divisions of the sons of Aaron: The sons of Aaron were Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar.

column.name: text
column.value: But Nadab and Abihu died before their father did, and they had no sons; so Eleazar and Ithamar served as the priests.

column.name: text
column.value: With the help of Zadok a descendant of Eleazar and Ahimelech a descendant of Ithamar, David separated them into divisions for their appointed order of ministering.

column.name: text
column.value: A larger number of leaders were found among Eleazar's descendants than among Ithamar's, and they were divided accordingly: sixteen heads of families from Eleazar's descendants and eight heads of families from Ithamar's descendants.

column.name: text
column.value: They divided them impartially by drawing lots, for there were officials of the sanctuary and officials of God among the descendants of both Eleazar and Ithamar.

column.name: text
column.value: The scribe Shemaiah son of Nethanel, a Levite, recorded their names in the presence of the king and of the officials: Zadok the priest, Ahimelech son of Abiathar and the heads of families of the priests and of the Levites--one family being taken from Eleazar and then one from Ithamar.

column.name: text
column.value: The first lot fell to Jehoiarib, the second to Jedaiah,

column.name: text
column.value: the third to Harim, the fourth to Seorim,

column.name: text
column.value: the fifth to Malkijah, the sixth to Mijamin,

column.name: text
column.value: the seventh to Hakkoz, the eighth to Abijah,

column.name: text
column.value: the ninth to Jeshua, the tenth to Shecaniah,

column.name: text
column.value: the eleventh to Eliashib, the twelfth to Jakim,

column.name: text
column.value: the thirteenth to Huppah, the fourteenth to Jeshebeab,

column.name: text
column.value: the fifteenth to Bilgah, the sixteenth to Immer,

column.name: text
column.value: the seventeenth to Hezir, the eighteenth to Happizzez,

column.name: text
column.value: the nineteenth to Pethahiah, the twentieth to Jehezkel,

column.name: text
column.value: the twenty-first to Jakin, the twenty-second to Gamul,

column.name: text
column.value: the twenty-third to Delaiah and the twenty-fourth to Maaziah.

column.name: text
column.value: This was their appointed order of ministering when they entered the temple of the LORD, according to the regulations prescribed for them by their forefather Aaron, as the LORD, the God of Israel, had commanded him.

column.name: text
column.value: As for the rest of the descendants of Levi: from the sons of Amram: Shubael; from the sons of Shubael: Jehdeiah.

column.name: text
column.value: As for Rehabiah, from his sons: Isshiah was the first.

column.name: text
column.value: From the Izharites: Shelomoth; from the sons of Shelomoth: Jahath.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Hebron: Jeriah the first, Amariah the second, Jahaziel the third and Jekameam the fourth.

column.name: text
column.value: The son of Uzziel: Micah; from the sons of Micah: Shamir.

column.name: text
column.value: The brother of Micah: Isshiah; from the sons of Isshiah: Zechariah.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi. The son of Jaaziah: Beno.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Merari: from Jaaziah: Beno, Shoham, Zaccur and Ibri.

column.name: text
column.value: From Mahli: Eleazar, who had no sons.

column.name: text
column.value: From Kish: the son of Kish: Jerahmeel.

column.name: text
column.value: And the sons of Mushi: Mahli, Eder and Jerimoth. These were the Levites, according to their families.

column.name: text
column.value: They also cast lots, just as their brothers the descendants of Aaron did, in the presence of King David and of Zadok, Ahimelech, and the heads of families of the priests and of the Levites. The families of the oldest brother were treated the same as those of the youngest.

column.name: text
column.value: This is the list of the Israelites--heads of families, commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds, and their officers, who served the king in all that concerned the army divisions that were on duty month by month throughout the year. Each division consisted of 24,000 men.

column.name: text
column.value: In charge of the first division, for the first month, was Jashobeam son of Zabdiel. There were 24,000 men in his division.

column.name: text
column.value: He was a descendant of Perez and chief of all the army officers for the first month.

column.name: text
column.value: In charge of the division for the second month was Dodai the Ahohite; Mikloth was the leader of his division. There were 24,000 men in his division.

column.name: text
column.value: The third army commander, for the third month, was Benaiah son of Jehoiada the priest. He was chief and there were 24,000 men in his division.

column.name: text
column.value: This was the Benaiah who was a mighty man among the Thirty and was over the Thirty. His son Ammizabad was in charge of his division.

column.name: text
column.value: The fourth, for the fourth month, was Asahel the brother of Joab; his son Zebadiah was his successor. There were 24,000 men in his division.

column.name: text
column.value: The fifth, for the fifth month, was the commander Shamhuth the Izrahite. There were 24,000 men in his division.

column.name: text
column.value: The sixth, for the sixth month, was Ira the son of Ikkesh the Tekoite. There were 24,000 men in his division.

column.name: text
column.value: The seventh, for the seventh month, was Helez the Pelonite, an Ephraimite. There were 24,000 men in his division.

column.name: text
column.value: The eighth, for the eighth month, was Sibbecai the Hushathite, a Zerahite. There were 24,000 men in his division.

column.name: text
column.value: The ninth, for the ninth month, was Abiezer the Anathothite, a Benjamite. There were 24,000 men in his division.

column.name: text
column.value: The tenth, for the tenth month, was Maharai the Netophathite, a Zerahite. There were 24,000 men in his division.

column.name: text
column.value: The eleventh, for the eleventh month, was Benaiah the Pirathonite, an Ephraimite. There were 24,000 men in his division.

column.name: text
column.value: The twelfth, for the twelfth month, was Heldai the Netophathite, from the family of Othniel. There were 24,000 men in his division.

column.name: text
column.value: The officers over the tribes of Israel: over the Reubenites: Eliezer son of Zicri; over the Simeonites: Shephatiah son of Maacah;

column.name: text
column.value: over Levi: Hashabiah son of Kemuel; over Aaron: Zadok;

column.name: text
column.value: over Judah: Elihu, a brother of David; over Issachar: Omri son of Michael;

column.name: text
column.value: over Zebulun: Ishmaiah son of Obadiah; over Naphtali: Jerimoth son of Azriel;

column.name: text
column.value: over the Ephraimites: Hoshea son of Azaziah; over half the tribe of Manasseh: Joel son of Pedaiah;

column.name: text
column.value: over the half-tribe of Manasseh in Gilead: Iddo son of Zechariah; over Benjamin: Jaasiel son of Abner;

column.name: text
column.value: over Dan: Azarel son of Jeroham. These were the officers over the tribes of Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: David did not take the number of the men twenty years old or less, because the LORD had promised to make Israel as numerous as the stars in the sky.

column.name: text
column.value: Joab son of Zeruiah began to count the men but did not finish. Wrath came on Israel on account of this numbering, and the number was not entered in the book of the annals of King David.

column.name: text
column.value: Azmaveth son of Adiel was in charge of the royal storehouses. Jonathan son of Uzziah was in charge of the storehouses in the outlying districts, in the towns, the villages and the watchtowers.

column.name: text
column.value: Ezri son of Kelub was in charge of the field workers who farmed the land.

column.name: text
column.value: Shimei the Ramathite was in charge of the vineyards. Zabdi the Shiphmite was in charge of the produce of the vineyards for the wine vats.

column.name: text
column.value: Baal-Hanan the Gederite was in charge of the olive and sycamore-fig trees in the western foothills. Joash was in charge of the supplies of olive oil.

column.name: text
column.value: Shitrai the Sharonite was in charge of the herds grazing in Sharon. Shaphat son of Adlai was in charge of the herds in the valleys.

column.name: text
column.value: Obil the Ishmaelite was in charge of the camels. Jehdeiah the Meronothite was in charge of the donkeys.

column.name: text
column.value: Jaziz the Hagrite was in charge of the flocks. All these were the officials in charge of King David's property.

column.name: text
column.value: Jonathan, David's uncle, was a counselor, a man of insight and a scribe. Jehiel son of Hacmoni took care of the king's sons.

column.name: text
column.value: Ahithophel was the king's counselor. Hushai the Arkite was the king's friend.

column.name: text
column.value: Ahithophel was succeeded by Jehoiada son of Benaiah and by Abiathar. Joab was the commander of the royal army.

column.name: text
column.value: David summoned all the officials of Israel to assemble at Jerusalem: the officers over the tribes, the commanders of the divisions in the service of the king, the commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds, and the officials in charge of all the property and livestock belonging to the king and his sons, together with the palace officials, the mighty men and all the brave warriors.

column.name: text
column.value: King David rose to his feet and said: "Listen to me, my brothers and my people. I had it in my heart to build a house as a place of rest for the ark of the covenant of the LORD, for the footstool of our God, and I made plans to build it.

column.name: text
column.value: But God said to me, 'You are not to build a house for my Name, because you are a warrior and have shed blood.'

column.name: text
column.value: "Yet the LORD, the God of Israel, chose me from my whole family to be king over Israel forever. He chose Judah as leader, and from the house of Judah he chose my family, and from my father's sons he was pleased to make me king over all Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: Of all my sons--and the LORD has given me many--he has chosen my son Solomon to sit on the throne of the kingdom of the LORD over Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: He said to me: 'Solomon your son is the one who will build my house and my courts, for I have chosen him to be my son, and I will be his father.

column.name: text
column.value: I will establish his kingdom forever if he is unswerving in carrying out my commands and laws, as is being done at this time.'

column.name: text
column.value: "So now I charge you in the sight of all Israel and of the assembly of the LORD, and in the hearing of our God: Be careful to follow all the commands of the LORD your God, that you may possess this good land and pass it on as an inheritance to your descendants forever.

column.name: text
column.value: "And you, my son Solomon, acknowledge the God of your father, and serve him with wholehearted devotion and with a willing mind, for the LORD searches every heart and understands every motive behind the thoughts. If you seek him, he will be found by you; but if you forsake him, he will reject you forever.

column.name: text
column.value: Consider now, for the LORD has chosen you to build a temple as a sanctuary. Be strong and do the work."

column.name: text
column.value: Then David gave his son Solomon the plans for the portico of the temple, its buildings, its storerooms, its upper parts, its inner rooms and the place of atonement.

column.name: text
column.value: He gave him the plans of all that the Spirit had put in his mind for the courts of the temple of the LORD and all the surrounding rooms, for the treasuries of the temple of God and for the treasuries for the dedicated things.

column.name: text
column.value: He gave him instructions for the divisions of the priests and Levites, and for all the work of serving in the temple of the LORD, as well as for all the articles to be used in its service.

column.name: text
column.value: He designated the weight of gold for all the gold articles to be used in various kinds of service, and the weight of silver for all the silver articles to be used in various kinds of service:

column.name: text
column.value: the weight of gold for the gold lampstands and their lamps, with the weight for each lampstand and its lamps; and the weight of silver for each silver lampstand and its lamps, according to the use of each lampstand;

column.name: text
column.value: the weight of gold for each table for consecrated bread; the weight of silver for the silver tables;

column.name: text
column.value: the weight of pure gold for the forks, sprinkling bowls and pitchers; the weight of gold for each gold dish; the weight of silver for each silver dish;

column.name: text
column.value: and the weight of the refined gold for the altar of incense. He also gave him the plan for the chariot, that is, the cherubim of gold that spread their wings and shelter the ark of the covenant of the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: "All this," David said, "I have in writing from the hand of the LORD upon me, and he gave me understanding in all the details of the plan."

column.name: text
column.value: David also said to Solomon his son, "Be strong and courageous, and do the work. Do not be afraid or discouraged, for the LORD God, my God, is with you. He will not fail you or forsake you until all the work for the service of the temple of the LORD is finished.

column.name: text
column.value: The divisions of the priests and Levites are ready for all the work on the temple of God, and every willing man skilled in any craft will help you in all the work. The officials and all the people will obey your every command."

column.name: text
column.value: Solomon son of David established himself firmly over his kingdom, for the LORD his God was with him and made him exceedingly great.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Solomon spoke to all Israel--to the commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds, to the judges and to all the leaders in Israel, the heads of families--

column.name: text
column.value: and Solomon and the whole assembly went to the high place at Gibeon, for God's Tent of Meeting was there, which Moses the LORD'S servant had made in the desert.

column.name: text
column.value: Now David had brought up the ark of God from Kiriath Jearim to the place he had prepared for it, because he had pitched a tent for it in Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: But the bronze altar that Bezalel son of Uri, the son of Hur, had made was in Gibeon in front of the tabernacle of the LORD; so Solomon and the assembly inquired of him there.

column.name: text
column.value: Solomon went up to the bronze altar before the LORD in the Tent of Meeting and offered a thousand burnt offerings on it.

column.name: text
column.value: That night God appeared to Solomon and said to him, "Ask for whatever you want me to give you."

column.name: text
column.value: Solomon answered God, "You have shown great kindness to David my father and have made me king in his place.

column.name: text
column.value: Now, LORD God, let your promise to my father David be confirmed, for you have made me king over a people who are as numerous as the dust of the earth.

column.name: text
column.value: Give me wisdom and knowledge, that I may lead this people, for who is able to govern this great people of yours?"

column.name: text
column.value: God said to Solomon, "Since this is your heart's desire and you have not asked for wealth, riches or honor, nor for the death of your enemies, and since you have not asked for a long life but for wisdom and knowledge to govern my people over whom I have made you king,

column.name: text
column.value: therefore wisdom and knowledge will be given you. And I will also give you wealth, riches and honor, such as no king who was before you ever had and none after you will have."

column.name: text
column.value: Then Solomon went to Jerusalem from the high place at Gibeon, from before the Tent of Meeting. And he reigned over Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: Solomon accumulated chariots and horses; he had fourteen hundred chariots and twelve thousand horses, which he kept in the chariot cities and also with him in Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: The king made silver and gold as common in Jerusalem as stones, and cedar as plentiful as sycamore-fig trees in the foothills.

column.name: text
column.value: Solomon's horses were imported from Egypt and from Kue--the royal merchants purchased them from Kue.

column.name: text
column.value: They imported a chariot from Egypt for six hundred shekels of silver, and a horse for a hundred and fifty. They also exported them to all the kings of the Hittites and of the Arameans.

column.name: text
column.value: Solomon gave orders to build a temple for the Name of the LORD and a royal palace for himself.

column.name: text
column.value: He conscripted seventy thousand men as carriers and eighty thousand as stonecutters in the hills and thirty-six hundred as foremen over them.

column.name: text
column.value: Solomon sent this message to Hiram king of Tyre: "Send me cedar logs as you did for my father David when you sent him cedar to build a palace to live in.

column.name: text
column.value: Now I am about to build a temple for the Name of the LORD my God and to dedicate it to him for burning fragrant incense before him, for setting out the consecrated bread regularly, and for making burnt offerings every morning and evening and on Sabbaths and New Moons and at the appointed feasts of the LORD our God. This is a lasting ordinance for Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: "The temple I am going to build will be great, because our God is greater than all other gods.

column.name: text
column.value: But who is able to build a temple for him, since the heavens, even the highest heavens, cannot contain him? Who then am I to build a temple for him, except as a place to burn sacrifices before him?

column.name: text
column.value: "Send me, therefore, a man skilled to work in gold and silver, bronze and iron, and in purple, crimson and blue yarn, and experienced in the art of engraving, to work in Judah and Jerusalem with my skilled craftsmen, whom my father David provided.

column.name: text
column.value: "Send me also cedar, pine and algum logs from Lebanon, for I know that your men are skilled in cutting timber there. My men will work with yours

column.name: text
column.value: to provide me with plenty of lumber, because the temple I build must be large and magnificent.

column.name: text
column.value: I will give your servants, the woodsmen who cut the timber, twenty thousand cors of ground wheat, twenty thousand cors of barley, twenty thousand baths of wine and twenty thousand baths of olive oil."

column.name: text
column.value: Hiram king of Tyre replied by letter to Solomon: "Because the LORD loves his people, he has made you their king."

column.name: text
column.value: And Hiram added: "Praise be to the LORD, the God of Israel, who made heaven and earth! He has given King David a wise son, endowed with intelligence and discernment, who will build a temple for the LORD and a palace for himself.

column.name: text
column.value: "I am sending you Huram-Abi, a man of great skill,

column.name: text
column.value: whose mother was from Dan and whose father was from Tyre. He is trained to work in gold and silver, bronze and iron, stone and wood, and with purple and blue and crimson yarn and fine linen. He is experienced in all kinds of engraving and can execute any design given to him. He will work with your craftsmen and with those of my lord, David your father.

column.name: text
column.value: "Now let my lord send his servants the wheat and barley and the olive oil and wine he promised,

column.name: text
column.value: and we will cut all the logs from Lebanon that you need and will float them in rafts by sea down to Joppa. You can then take them up to Jerusalem."

column.name: text
column.value: Solomon took a census of all the aliens who were in Israel, after the census his father David had taken; and they were found to be 153,600.

column.name: text
column.value: He assigned 70,000 of them to be carriers and 80,000 to be stonecutters in the hills, with 3,600 foremen over them to keep the people working.

column.name: text
column.value: Then King David said to the whole assembly: "My son Solomon, the one whom God has chosen, is young and inexperienced. The task is great, because this palatial structure is not for man but for the LORD God.

column.name: text
column.value: With all my resources I have provided for the temple of my God--gold for the gold work, silver for the silver, bronze for the bronze, iron for the iron and wood for the wood, as well as onyx for the settings, turquoise, stones of various colors, and all kinds of fine stone and marble--all of these in large quantities.

column.name: text
column.value: Besides, in my devotion to the temple of my God I now give my personal treasures of gold and silver for the temple of my God, over and above everything I have provided for this holy temple:

column.name: text
column.value: three thousand talents of gold (gold of Ophir) and seven thousand talents of refined silver, for the overlaying of the walls of the buildings,

column.name: text
column.value: for the gold work and the silver work, and for all the work to be done by the craftsmen. Now, who is willing to consecrate himself today to the LORD?"

column.name: text
column.value: Then the leaders of families, the officers of the tribes of Israel, the commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds, and the officials in charge of the king's work gave willingly.

column.name: text
column.value: They gave toward the work on the temple of God five thousand talents and ten thousand darics of gold, ten thousand talents of silver, eighteen thousand talents of bronze and a hundred thousand talents of iron.

column.name: text
column.value: Any who had precious stones gave them to the treasury of the temple of the LORD in the custody of Jehiel the Gershonite.

column.name: text
column.value: The people rejoiced at the willing response of their leaders, for they had given freely and wholeheartedly to the LORD. David the king also rejoiced greatly.

column.name: text
column.value: David praised the LORD in the presence of the whole assembly, saying, "Praise be to you, O LORD, God of our father Israel, from everlasting to everlasting.

column.name: text
column.value: Yours, O LORD, is the greatness and the power and the glory and the majesty and the splendor, for everything in heaven and earth is yours. Yours, O LORD, is the kingdom; you are exalted as head over all.

column.name: text
column.value: Wealth and honor come from you; you are the ruler of all things. In your hands are strength and power to exalt and give strength to all.

column.name: text
column.value: Now, our God, we give you thanks, and praise your glorious name.

column.name: text
column.value: "But who am I, and who are my people, that we should be able to give as generously as this? Everything comes from you, and we have given you only what comes from your hand.

column.name: text
column.value: We are aliens and strangers in your sight, as were all our forefathers. Our days on earth are like a shadow, without hope.

column.name: text
column.value: O LORD our God, as for all this abundance that we have provided for building you a temple for your Holy Name, it comes from your hand, and all of it belongs to you.

column.name: text
column.value: I know, my God, that you test the heart and are pleased with integrity. All these things have I given willingly and with honest intent. And now I have seen with joy how willingly your people who are here have given to you.

column.name: text
column.value: O LORD, God of our fathers Abraham, Isaac and Israel, keep this desire in the hearts of your people forever, and keep their hearts loyal to you.

column.name: text
column.value: And give my son Solomon the wholehearted devotion to keep your commands, requirements and decrees and to do everything to build the palatial structure for which I have provided."

column.name: text
column.value: Then David said to the whole assembly, "Praise the LORD your God." So they all praised the LORD, the God of their fathers; they bowed low and fell prostrate before the LORD and the king.

column.name: text
column.value: The next day they made sacrifices to the LORD and presented burnt offerings to him: a thousand bulls, a thousand rams and a thousand male lambs, together with their drink offerings, and other sacrifices in abundance for all Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: They ate and drank with great joy in the presence of the LORD that day. Then they acknowledged Solomon son of David as king a second time, anointing him before the LORD to be ruler and Zadok to be priest.

column.name: text
column.value: So Solomon sat on the throne of the LORD as king in place of his father David. He prospered and all Israel obeyed him.

column.name: text
column.value: All the officers and mighty men, as well as all of King David's sons, pledged their submission to King Solomon.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD highly exalted Solomon in the sight of all Israel and bestowed on him royal splendor such as no king over Israel ever had before.

column.name: text
column.value: David son of Jesse was king over all Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: He ruled over Israel forty years--seven in Hebron and thirty-three in Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: He died at a good old age, having enjoyed long life, wealth and honor. His son Solomon succeeded him as king.

column.name: text
column.value: As for the events of King David's reign, from beginning to end, they are written in the records of Samuel the seer, the records of Nathan the prophet and the records of Gad the seer,

column.name: text
column.value: together with the details of his reign and power, and the circumstances that surrounded him and Israel and the kingdoms of all the other lands.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Solomon began to build the temple of the LORD in Jerusalem on Mount Moriah, where the LORD had appeared to his father David. It was on the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite, the place provided by David.

column.name: text
column.value: He began building on the second day of the second month in the fourth year of his reign.

column.name: text
column.value: The foundation Solomon laid for building the temple of God was sixty cubits long and twenty cubits wide (using the cubit of the old standard).

column.name: text
column.value: The portico at the front of the temple was twenty cubits long across the width of the building and twenty cubits high. He overlaid the inside with pure gold.

column.name: text
column.value: He paneled the main hall with pine and covered it with fine gold and decorated it with palm tree and chain designs.

column.name: text
column.value: He adorned the temple with precious stones. And the gold he used was gold of Parvaim.

column.name: text
column.value: He overlaid the ceiling beams, doorframes, walls and doors of the temple with gold, and he carved cherubim on the walls.

column.name: text
column.value: He built the Most Holy Place, its length corresponding to the width of the temple--twenty cubits long and twenty cubits wide. He overlaid the inside with six hundred talents of fine gold.

column.name: text
column.value: The gold nails weighed fifty shekels. He also overlaid the upper parts with gold.

column.name: text
column.value: In the Most Holy Place he made a pair of sculptured cherubim and overlaid them with gold.

column.name: text
column.value: The total wingspan of the cherubim was twenty cubits. One wing of the first cherub was five cubits long and touched the temple wall, while its other wing, also five cubits long, touched the wing of the other cherub.

column.name: text
column.value: Similarly one wing of the second cherub was five cubits long and touched the other temple wall, and its other wing, also five cubits long, touched the wing of the first cherub.

column.name: text
column.value: The wings of these cherubim extended twenty cubits. They stood on their feet, facing the main hall.

column.name: text
column.value: He made the curtain of blue, purple and crimson yarn and fine linen, with cherubim worked into it.

column.name: text
column.value: In the front of the temple he made two pillars, which together were thirty-five cubits long, each with a capital on top measuring five cubits.

column.name: text
column.value: He made interwoven chains and put them on top of the pillars. He also made a hundred pomegranates and attached them to the chains.

column.name: text
column.value: He erected the pillars in the front of the temple, one to the south and one to the north. The one to the south he named Jakin and the one to the north Boaz.

column.name: text
column.value: He made a bronze altar twenty cubits long, twenty cubits wide and ten cubits high.

column.name: text
column.value: He made the Sea of cast metal, circular in shape, measuring ten cubits from rim to rim and five cubits high. It took a line of thirty cubits to measure around it.

column.name: text
column.value: Below the rim, figures of bulls encircled it--ten to a cubit. The bulls were cast in two rows in one piece with the Sea.

column.name: text
column.value: The Sea stood on twelve bulls, three facing north, three facing west, three facing south and three facing east. The Sea rested on top of them, and their hindquarters were toward the center.

column.name: text
column.value: It was a handbreadth in thickness, and its rim was like the rim of a cup, like a lily blossom. It held three thousand baths.

column.name: text
column.value: He then made ten basins for washing and placed five on the south side and five on the north. In them the things to be used for the burnt offerings were rinsed, but the Sea was to be used by the priests for washing.

column.name: text
column.value: He made ten gold lampstands according to the specifications for them and placed them in the temple, five on the south side and five on the north.

column.name: text
column.value: He made ten tables and placed them in the temple, five on the south side and five on the north. He also made a hundred gold sprinkling bowls.

column.name: text
column.value: He made the courtyard of the priests, and the large court and the doors for the court, and overlaid the doors with bronze.

column.name: text
column.value: He placed the Sea on the south side, at the southeast corner.

column.name: text
column.value: He also made the pots and shovels and sprinkling bowls. So Huram finished the work he had undertaken for King Solomon in the temple of God:

column.name: text
column.value: the two pillars; the two bowl-shaped capitals on top of the pillars; the two sets of network decorating the two bowl-shaped capitals on top of the pillars;

column.name: text
column.value: the four hundred pomegranates for the two sets of network (two rows of pomegranates for each network, decorating the bowl-shaped capitals on top of the pillars);

column.name: text
column.value: the stands with their basins;

column.name: text
column.value: the Sea and the twelve bulls under it;

column.name: text
column.value: the pots, shovels, meat forks and all related articles. All the objects that Huram-Abi made for King Solomon for the temple of the LORD were of polished bronze.

column.name: text
column.value: The king had them cast in clay molds in the plain of the Jordan between Succoth and Zarethan.

column.name: text
column.value: All these things that Solomon made amounted to so much that the weight of the bronze was not determined.

column.name: text
column.value: Solomon also made all the furnishings that were in God's temple: the golden altar; the tables on which was the bread of the Presence;

column.name: text
column.value: the lampstands of pure gold with their lamps, to burn in front of the inner sanctuary as prescribed;

column.name: text
column.value: the gold floral work and lamps and tongs (they were solid gold);

column.name: text
column.value: the pure gold wick trimmers, sprinkling bowls, dishes and censers; and the gold doors of the temple: the inner doors to the Most Holy Place and the doors of the main hall.

column.name: text
column.value: When all the work Solomon had done for the temple of the LORD was finished, he brought in the things his father David had dedicated--the silver and gold and all the furnishings--and he placed them in the treasuries of God's temple.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Solomon summoned to Jerusalem the elders of Israel, all the heads of the tribes and the chiefs of the Israelite families, to bring up the ark of the LORD'S covenant from Zion, the City of David.

column.name: text
column.value: And all the men of Israel came together to the king at the time of the festival in the seventh month.

column.name: text
column.value: When all the elders of Israel had arrived, the Levites took up the ark,

column.name: text
column.value: and they brought up the ark and the Tent of Meeting and all the sacred furnishings in it. The priests, who were Levites, carried them up;

column.name: text
column.value: and King Solomon and the entire assembly of Israel that had gathered about him were before the ark, sacrificing so many sheep and cattle that they could not be recorded or counted.

column.name: text
column.value: The priests then brought the ark of the LORD'S covenant to its place in the inner sanctuary of the temple, the Most Holy Place, and put it beneath the wings of the cherubim.

column.name: text
column.value: The cherubim spread their wings over the place of the ark and covered the ark and its carrying poles.

column.name: text
column.value: These poles were so long that their ends, extending from the ark, could be seen from in front of the inner sanctuary, but not from outside the Holy Place; and they are still there today.

column.name: text
column.value: There was nothing in the ark except the two tablets that Moses had placed in it at Horeb, where the LORD made a covenant with the Israelites after they came out of Egypt.

column.name: text
column.value: The priests then withdrew from the Holy Place. All the priests who were there had consecrated themselves, regardless of their divisions.

column.name: text
column.value: All the Levites who were musicians--Asaph, Heman, Jeduthun and their sons and relatives--stood on the east side of the altar, dressed in fine linen and playing cymbals, harps and lyres. They were accompanied by 120 priests sounding trumpets.

column.name: text
column.value: The trumpeters and singers joined in unison, as with one voice, to give praise and thanks to the LORD. Accompanied by trumpets, cymbals and other instruments, they raised their voices in praise to the LORD and sang: "He is good; his love endures forever." Then the temple of the LORD was filled with a cloud,

column.name: text
column.value: and the priests could not perform their service because of the cloud, for the glory of the LORD filled the temple of God.

column.name: text
column.value: When Solomon finished praying, fire came down from heaven and consumed the burnt offering and the sacrifices, and the glory of the LORD filled the temple.

column.name: text
column.value: The priests could not enter the temple of the LORD because the glory of the LORD filled it.

column.name: text
column.value: When all the Israelites saw the fire coming down and the glory of the LORD above the temple, they knelt on the pavement with their faces to the ground, and they worshiped and gave thanks to the LORD, saying, "He is good; his love endures forever."

column.name: text
column.value: Then the king and all the people offered sacrifices before the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: And King Solomon offered a sacrifice of twenty-two thousand head of cattle and a hundred and twenty thousand sheep and goats. So the king and all the people dedicated the temple of God.

column.name: text
column.value: The priests took their positions, as did the Levites with the LORD'S musical instruments, which King David had made for praising the LORD and which were used when he gave thanks, saying, "His love endures forever." Opposite the Levites, the priests blew their trumpets, and all the Israelites were standing.

column.name: text
column.value: Solomon consecrated the middle part of the courtyard in front of the temple of the LORD, and there he offered burnt offerings and the fat of the fellowship offerings, because the bronze altar he had made could not hold the burnt offerings, the grain offerings and the fat portions.

column.name: text
column.value: So Solomon observed the festival at that time for seven days, and all Israel with him--a vast assembly, people from Lebo Hamath to the Wadi of Egypt.

column.name: text
column.value: On the eighth day they held an assembly, for they had celebrated the dedication of the altar for seven days and the festival for seven days more.

column.name: text
column.value: On the twenty-third day of the seventh month he sent the people to their homes, joyful and glad in heart for the good things the LORD had done for David and Solomon and for his people Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: When Solomon had finished the temple of the LORD and the royal palace, and had succeeded in carrying out all he had in mind to do in the temple of the LORD and in his own palace,

column.name: text
column.value: the LORD appeared to him at night and said: "I have heard your prayer and have chosen this place for myself as a temple for sacrifices.

column.name: text
column.value: "When I shut up the heavens so that there is no rain, or command locusts to devour the land or send a plague among my people,

column.name: text
column.value: if my people, who are called by my name, will humble themselves and pray and seek my face and turn from their wicked ways, then will I hear from heaven and will forgive their sin and will heal their land.

column.name: text
column.value: Now my eyes will be open and my ears attentive to the prayers offered in this place.

column.name: text
column.value: I have chosen and consecrated this temple so that my Name may be there forever. My eyes and my heart will always be there.

column.name: text
column.value: "As for you, if you walk before me as David your father did, and do all I command, and observe my decrees and laws,

column.name: text
column.value: I will establish your royal throne, as I covenanted with David your father when I said, 'You shall never fail to have a man to rule over Israel.'

column.name: text
column.value: "But if you turn away and forsake the decrees and commands I have given you and go off to serve other gods and worship them,

column.name: text
column.value: then I will uproot Israel from my land, which I have given them, and will reject this temple I have consecrated for my Name. I will make it a byword and an object of ridicule among all peoples.

column.name: text
column.value: And though this temple is now so imposing, all who pass by will be appalled and say, 'Why has the LORD done such a thing to this land and to this temple?'

column.name: text
