column.value: People will answer, 'Because they have forsaken the LORD, the God of their fathers, who brought them out of Egypt, and have embraced other gods, worshiping and serving them--that is why he brought all this disaster on them.'"

column.name: text
column.value: At the end of twenty years, during which Solomon built the temple of the LORD and his own palace,

column.name: text
column.value: Solomon rebuilt the villages that Hiram had given him, and settled Israelites in them.

column.name: text
column.value: Solomon then went to Hamath Zobah and captured it.

column.name: text
column.value: He also built up Tadmor in the desert and all the store cities he had built in Hamath.

column.name: text
column.value: He rebuilt Upper Beth Horon and Lower Beth Horon as fortified cities, with walls and with gates and bars,

column.name: text
column.value: as well as Baalath and all his store cities, and all the cities for his chariots and for his horses--whatever he desired to build in Jerusalem, in Lebanon and throughout all the territory he ruled.

column.name: text
column.value: All the people left from the Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites and Jebusites (these peoples were not Israelites),

column.name: text
column.value: that is, their descendants remaining in the land, whom the Israelites had not destroyed--these Solomon conscripted for his slave labor force, as it is to this day.

column.name: text
column.value: But Solomon did not make slaves of the Israelites for his work; they were his fighting men, commanders of his captains, and commanders of his chariots and charioteers.

column.name: text
column.value: They were also King Solomon's chief officials--two hundred and fifty officials supervising the men.

column.name: text
column.value: Solomon brought Pharaoh's daughter up from the City of David to the palace he had built for her, for he said, "My wife must not live in the palace of David king of Israel, because the places the ark of the LORD has entered are holy."

column.name: text
column.value: On the altar of the LORD that he had built in front of the portico, Solomon sacrificed burnt offerings to the LORD,

column.name: text
column.value: according to the daily requirement for offerings commanded by Moses for Sabbaths, New Moons and the three annual feasts--the Feast of Unleavened Bread, the Feast of Weeks and the Feast of Tabernacles.

column.name: text
column.value: In keeping with the ordinance of his father David, he appointed the divisions of the priests for their duties, and the Levites to lead the praise and to assist the priests according to each day's requirement. He also appointed the gatekeepers by divisions for the various gates, because this was what David the man of God had ordered.

column.name: text
column.value: They did not deviate from the king's commands to the priests or to the Levites in any matter, including that of the treasuries.

column.name: text
column.value: All Solomon's work was carried out, from the day the foundation of the temple of the LORD was laid until its completion. So the temple of the LORD was finished.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Solomon went to Ezion Geber and Elath on the coast of Edom.

column.name: text
column.value: And Hiram sent him ships commanded by his own officers, men who knew the sea. These, with Solomon's men, sailed to Ophir and brought back four hundred and fifty talents of gold, which they delivered to King Solomon.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Solomon said, "The LORD has said that he would dwell in a dark cloud;

column.name: text
column.value: I have built a magnificent temple for you, a place for you to dwell forever."

column.name: text
column.value: While the whole assembly of Israel was standing there, the king turned around and blessed them.

column.name: text
column.value: Then he said: "Praise be to the LORD, the God of Israel, who with his hands has fulfilled what he promised with his mouth to my father David. For he said,

column.name: text
column.value: 'Since the day I brought my people out of Egypt, I have not chosen a city in any tribe of Israel to have a temple built for my Name to be there, nor have I chosen anyone to be the leader over my people Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: But now I have chosen Jerusalem for my Name to be there, and I have chosen David to rule my people Israel.'

column.name: text
column.value: "My father David had it in his heart to build a temple for the Name of the LORD, the God of Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: But the LORD said to my father David, 'Because it was in your heart to build a temple for my Name, you did well to have this in your heart.

column.name: text
column.value: Nevertheless, you are not the one to build the temple, but your son, who is your own flesh and blood--he is the one who will build the temple for my Name.'

column.name: text
column.value: "The LORD has kept the promise he made. I have succeeded David my father and now I sit on the throne of Israel, just as the LORD promised, and I have built the temple for the Name of the LORD, the God of Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: There I have placed the ark, in which is the covenant of the LORD that he made with the people of Israel."

column.name: text
column.value: Then Solomon stood before the altar of the LORD in front of the whole assembly of Israel and spread out his hands.

column.name: text
column.value: Now he had made a bronze platform, five cubits long, five cubits wide and three cubits high, and had placed it in the center of the outer court. He stood on the platform and then knelt down before the whole assembly of Israel and spread out his hands toward heaven.

column.name: text
column.value: He said: "O LORD, God of Israel, there is no God like you in heaven or on earth--you who keep your covenant of love with your servants who continue wholeheartedly in your way.

column.name: text
column.value: You have kept your promise to your servant David my father; with your mouth you have promised and with your hand you have fulfilled it--as it is today.

column.name: text
column.value: "Now LORD, God of Israel, keep for your servant David my father the promises you made to him when you said, 'You shall never fail to have a man to sit before me on the throne of Israel, if only your sons are careful in all they do to walk before me according to my law, as you have done.'

column.name: text
column.value: And now, O LORD, God of Israel, let your word that you promised your servant David come true.

column.name: text
column.value: "But will God really dwell on earth with men? The heavens, even the highest heavens, cannot contain you. How much less this temple I have built!

column.name: text
column.value: Yet give attention to your servant's prayer and his plea for mercy, O LORD my God. Hear the cry and the prayer that your servant is praying in your presence.

column.name: text
column.value: May your eyes be open toward this temple day and night, this place of which you said you would put your Name there. May you hear the prayer your servant prays toward this place.

column.name: text
column.value: Hear the supplications of your servant and of your people Israel when they pray toward this place. Hear from heaven, your dwelling place; and when you hear, forgive.

column.name: text
column.value: "When a man wrongs his neighbor and is required to take an oath and he comes and swears the oath before your altar in this temple,

column.name: text
column.value: then hear from heaven and act. Judge between your servants, repaying the guilty by bringing down on his own head what he has done. Declare the innocent not guilty and so establish his innocence.

column.name: text
column.value: "When your people Israel have been defeated by an enemy because they have sinned against you and when they turn back and confess your name, praying and making supplication before you in this temple,

column.name: text
column.value: then hear from heaven and forgive the sin of your people Israel and bring them back to the land you gave to them and their fathers.

column.name: text
column.value: "When the heavens are shut up and there is no rain because your people have sinned against you, and when they pray toward this place and confess your name and turn from their sin because you have afflicted them,

column.name: text
column.value: then hear from heaven and forgive the sin of your servants, your people Israel. Teach them the right way to live, and send rain on the land you gave your people for an inheritance.

column.name: text
column.value: "When famine or plague comes to the land, or blight or mildew, locusts or grasshoppers, or when enemies besiege them in any of their cities, whatever disaster or disease may come,

column.name: text
column.value: and when a prayer or plea is made by any of your people Israel--each one aware of his afflictions and pains, and spreading out his hands toward this temple--

column.name: text
column.value: then hear from heaven, your dwelling place. Forgive, and deal with each man according to all he does, since you know his heart (for you alone know the hearts of men),

column.name: text
column.value: so that they will fear you and walk in your ways all the time they live in the land you gave our fathers.

column.name: text
column.value: "As for the foreigner who does not belong to your people Israel but has come from a distant land because of your great name and your mighty hand and your outstretched arm--when he comes and prays toward this temple,

column.name: text
column.value: then hear from heaven, your dwelling place, and do whatever the foreigner asks of you, so that all the peoples of the earth may know your name and fear you, as do your own people Israel, and may know that this house I have built bears your Name.

column.name: text
column.value: "When your people go to war against their enemies, wherever you send them, and when they pray to you toward this city you have chosen and the temple I have built for your Name,

column.name: text
column.value: then hear from heaven their prayer and their plea, and uphold their cause.

column.name: text
column.value: "When they sin against you--for there is no one who does not sin--and you become angry with them and give them over to the enemy, who takes them captive to a land far away or near;

column.name: text
column.value: and if they have a change of heart in the land where they are held captive, and repent and plead with you in the land of their captivity and say, 'We have sinned, we have done wrong and acted wickedly';

column.name: text
column.value: and if they turn back to you with all their heart and soul in the land of their captivity where they were taken, and pray toward the land you gave their fathers, toward the city you have chosen and toward the temple I have built for your Name;

column.name: text
column.value: then from heaven, your dwelling place, hear their prayer and their pleas, and uphold their cause. And forgive your people, who have sinned against you.

column.name: text
column.value: "Now, my God, may your eyes be open and your ears attentive to the prayers offered in this place.

column.name: text
column.value: "Now arise, O LORD God, and come to your resting place, you and the ark of your might. May your priests, O LORD God, be clothed with salvation, may your saints rejoice in your goodness.

column.name: text
column.value: O LORD God, do not reject your anointed one. Remember the great love promised to David your servant."

column.name: text
column.value: When the queen of Sheba heard of Solomon's fame, she came to Jerusalem to test him with hard questions. Arriving with a very great caravan--with camels carrying spices, large quantities of gold, and precious stones--she came to Solomon and talked with him about all she had on her mind.

column.name: text
column.value: Solomon answered all her questions; nothing was too hard for him to explain to her.

column.name: text
column.value: When the queen of Sheba saw the wisdom of Solomon, as well as the palace he had built,

column.name: text
column.value: the food on his table, the seating of his officials, the attending servants in their robes, the cupbearers in their robes and the burnt offerings he made at the temple of the LORD, she was overwhelmed.

column.name: text
column.value: She said to the king, "The report I heard in my own country about your achievements and your wisdom is true.

column.name: text
column.value: But I did not believe what they said until I came and saw with my own eyes. Indeed, not even half the greatness of your wisdom was told me; you have far exceeded the report I heard.

column.name: text
column.value: How happy your men must be! How happy your officials, who continually stand before you and hear your wisdom!

column.name: text
column.value: Praise be to the LORD your God, who has delighted in you and placed you on his throne as king to rule for the LORD your God. Because of the love of your God for Israel and his desire to uphold them forever, he has made you king over them, to maintain justice and righteousness."

column.name: text
column.value: Then she gave the king 120 talents of gold, large quantities of spices, and precious stones. There had never been such spices as those the queen of Sheba gave to King Solomon.

column.name: text
column.value: (The men of Hiram and the men of Solomon brought gold from Ophir; they also brought algumwood and precious stones.

column.name: text
column.value: The king used the algumwood to make steps for the temple of the LORD and for the royal palace, and to make harps and lyres for the musicians. Nothing like them had ever been seen in Judah.)

column.name: text
column.value: King Solomon gave the queen of Sheba all she desired and asked for; he gave her more than she had brought to him. Then she left and returned with her retinue to her own country.

column.name: text
column.value: The weight of the gold that Solomon received yearly was 666 talents,

column.name: text
column.value: not including the revenues brought in by merchants and traders. Also all the kings of Arabia and the governors of the land brought gold and silver to Solomon.

column.name: text
column.value: King Solomon made two hundred large shields of hammered gold; six hundred bekas of hammered gold went into each shield.

column.name: text
column.value: He also made three hundred small shields of hammered gold, with three hundred bekas of gold in each shield. The king put them in the Palace of the Forest of Lebanon.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the king made a great throne inlaid with ivory and overlaid with pure gold.

column.name: text
column.value: The throne had six steps, and a footstool of gold was attached to it. On both sides of the seat were armrests, with a lion standing beside each of them.

column.name: text
column.value: Twelve lions stood on the six steps, one at either end of each step. Nothing like it had ever been made for any other kingdom.

column.name: text
column.value: All King Solomon's goblets were gold, and all the household articles in the Palace of the Forest of Lebanon were pure gold. Nothing was made of silver, because silver was considered of little value in Solomon's day.

column.name: text
column.value: The king had a fleet of trading ships manned by Hiram's men. Once every three years it returned, carrying gold, silver and ivory, and apes and baboons.

column.name: text
column.value: King Solomon was greater in riches and wisdom than all the other kings of the earth.

column.name: text
column.value: All the kings of the earth sought audience with Solomon to hear the wisdom God had put in his heart.

column.name: text
column.value: Year after year, everyone who came brought a gift--articles of silver and gold, and robes, weapons and spices, and horses and mules.

column.name: text
column.value: Solomon had four thousand stalls for horses and chariots, and twelve thousand horses, which he kept in the chariot cities and also with him in Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: He ruled over all the kings from the River to the land of the Philistines, as far as the border of Egypt.

column.name: text
column.value: The king made silver as common in Jerusalem as stones, and cedar as plentiful as sycamore-fig trees in the foothills.

column.name: text
column.value: Solomon's horses were imported from Egypt and from all other countries.

column.name: text
column.value: As for the other events of Solomon's reign, from beginning to end, are they not written in the records of Nathan the prophet, in the prophecy of Ahijah the Shilonite and in the visions of Iddo the seer concerning Jeroboam son of Nebat?

column.name: text
column.value: Solomon reigned in Jerusalem over all Israel forty years.

column.name: text
column.value: Then he rested with his fathers and was buried in the city of David his father. And Rehoboam his son succeeded him as king.

column.name: text
column.value: Rehoboam went to Shechem, for all the Israelites had gone there to make him king.

column.name: text
column.value: When Jeroboam son of Nebat heard this (he was in Egypt, where he had fled from King Solomon), he returned from Egypt.

column.name: text
column.value: So they sent for Jeroboam, and he and all Israel went to Rehoboam and said to him:

column.name: text
column.value: "Your father put a heavy yoke on us, but now lighten the harsh labor and the heavy yoke he put on us, and we will serve you."

column.name: text
column.value: Rehoboam answered, "Come back to me in three days." So the people went away.

column.name: text
column.value: Then King Rehoboam consulted the elders who had served his father Solomon during his lifetime. "How would you advise me to answer these people?" he asked.

column.name: text
column.value: They replied, "If you will be kind to these people and please them and give them a favorable answer, they will always be your servants."

column.name: text
column.value: But Rehoboam rejected the advice the elders gave him and consulted the young men who had grown up with him and were serving him.

column.name: text
column.value: He asked them, "What is your advice? How should we answer these people who say to me, 'Lighten the yoke your father put on us'?"

column.name: text
column.value: The young men who had grown up with him replied, "Tell the people who have said to you, 'Your father put a heavy yoke on us, but make our yoke lighter'--tell them, 'My little finger is thicker than my father's waist.

column.name: text
column.value: My father laid on you a heavy yoke; I will make it even heavier. My father scourged you with whips; I will scourge you with scorpions.'"

column.name: text
column.value: Three days later Jeroboam and all the people returned to Rehoboam, as the king had said, "Come back to me in three days."

column.name: text
column.value: The king answered them harshly. Rejecting the advice of the elders,

column.name: text
column.value: he followed the advice of the young men and said, "My father made your yoke heavy; I will make it even heavier. My father scourged you with whips; I will scourge you with scorpions."

column.name: text
column.value: So the king did not listen to the people, for this turn of events was from God, to fulfill the word the LORD had spoken to Jeroboam son of Nebat through Ahijah the Shilonite.

column.name: text
column.value: When all Israel saw that the king refused to listen to them, they answered the king: "What share do we have in David, what part in Jesse's son? To your tents, O Israel! Look after your own house, O David!" So all the Israelites went home.

column.name: text
column.value: But as for the Israelites who were living in the towns of Judah, Rehoboam still ruled over them.

column.name: text
column.value: King Rehoboam sent out Adoniram, who was in charge of forced labor, but the Israelites stoned him to death. King Rehoboam, however, managed to get into his chariot and escape to Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: So Israel has been in rebellion against the house of David to this day.

column.name: text
column.value: When Rehoboam arrived in Jerusalem, he mustered the house of Judah and Benjamin--a hundred and eighty thousand fighting men--to make war against Israel and to regain the kingdom for Rehoboam.

column.name: text
column.value: But this word of the LORD came to Shemaiah the man of God:

column.name: text
column.value: "Say to Rehoboam son of Solomon king of Judah and to all the Israelites in Judah and Benjamin,

column.name: text
column.value: 'This is what the LORD says: Do not go up to fight against your brothers. Go home, every one of you, for this is my doing.'" So they obeyed the words of the LORD and turned back from marching against Jeroboam.

column.name: text
column.value: Rehoboam lived in Jerusalem and built up towns for defense in Judah:

column.name: text
column.value: Bethlehem, Etam, Tekoa,

column.name: text
column.value: Beth Zur, Soco, Adullam,

column.name: text
column.value: Gath, Mareshah, Ziph,

column.name: text
column.value: Adoraim, Lachish, Azekah,

column.name: text
column.value: Zorah, Aijalon and Hebron. These were fortified cities in Judah and Benjamin.

column.name: text
column.value: He strengthened their defenses and put commanders in them, with supplies of food, olive oil and wine.

column.name: text
column.value: He put shields and spears in all the cities, and made them very strong. So Judah and Benjamin were his.

column.name: text
column.value: The priests and Levites from all their districts throughout Israel sided with him.

column.name: text
column.value: The Levites even abandoned their pasturelands and property, and came to Judah and Jerusalem because Jeroboam and his sons had rejected them as priests of the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: And he appointed his own priests for the high places and for the goat and calf idols he had made.

column.name: text
column.value: Those from every tribe of Israel who set their hearts on seeking the LORD, the God of Israel, followed the Levites to Jerusalem to offer sacrifices to the LORD, the God of their fathers.

column.name: text
column.value: They strengthened the kingdom of Judah and supported Rehoboam son of Solomon three years, walking in the ways of David and Solomon during this time.

column.name: text
column.value: Rehoboam married Mahalath, who was the daughter of David's son Jerimoth and of Abihail, the daughter of Jesse's son Eliab.

column.name: text
column.value: She bore him sons: Jeush, Shemariah and Zaham.

column.name: text
column.value: Then he married Maacah daughter of Absalom, who bore him Abijah, Attai, Ziza and Shelomith.

column.name: text
column.value: Rehoboam loved Maacah daughter of Absalom more than any of his other wives and concubines. In all, he had eighteen wives and sixty concubines, twenty-eight sons and sixty daughters.

column.name: text
column.value: Rehoboam appointed Abijah son of Maacah to be the chief prince among his brothers, in order to make him king.

column.name: text
column.value: He acted wisely, dispersing some of his sons throughout the districts of Judah and Benjamin, and to all the fortified cities. He gave them abundant provisions and took many wives for them.

column.name: text
column.value: In the eighteenth year of the reign of Jeroboam, Abijah became king of Judah,

column.name: text
column.value: and he reigned in Jerusalem three years. His mother's name was Maacah, a daughter of Uriel of Gibeah. There was war between Abijah and Jeroboam.

column.name: text
column.value: Abijah went into battle with a force of four hundred thousand able fighting men, and Jeroboam drew up a battle line against him with eight hundred thousand able troops.

column.name: text
column.value: Abijah stood on Mount Zemaraim, in the hill country of Ephraim, and said, "Jeroboam and all Israel, listen to me!

column.name: text
column.value: Don't you know that the LORD, the God of Israel, has given the kingship of Israel to David and his descendants forever by a covenant of salt?

column.name: text
column.value: Yet Jeroboam son of Nebat, an official of Solomon son of David, rebelled against his master.

column.name: text
column.value: Some worthless scoundrels gathered around him and opposed Rehoboam son of Solomon when he was young and indecisive and not strong enough to resist them.

column.name: text
column.value: "And now you plan to resist the kingdom of the LORD, which is in the hands of David's descendants. You are indeed a vast army and have with you the golden calves that Jeroboam made to be your gods.

column.name: text
column.value: But didn't you drive out the priests of the LORD, the sons of Aaron, and the Levites, and make priests of your own as the peoples of other lands do? Whoever comes to consecrate himself with a young bull and seven rams may become a priest of what are not gods.

column.name: text
column.value: "As for us, the LORD is our God, and we have not forsaken him. The priests who serve the LORD are sons of Aaron, and the Levites assist them.

column.name: text
column.value: Every morning and evening they present burnt offerings and fragrant incense to the LORD. They set out the bread on the ceremonially clean table and light the lamps on the gold lampstand every evening. We are observing the requirements of the LORD our God. But you have forsaken him.

column.name: text
column.value: God is with us; he is our leader. His priests with their trumpets will sound the battle cry against you. Men of Israel, do not fight against the LORD, the God of your fathers, for you will not succeed."

column.name: text
column.value: Now Jeroboam had sent troops around to the rear, so that while he was in front of Judah the ambush was behind them.

column.name: text
column.value: Judah turned and saw that they were being attacked at both front and rear. Then they cried out to the LORD. The priests blew their trumpets

column.name: text
column.value: and the men of Judah raised the battle cry. At the sound of their battle cry, God routed Jeroboam and all Israel before Abijah and Judah.

column.name: text
column.value: The Israelites fled before Judah, and God delivered them into their hands.

column.name: text
column.value: Abijah and his men inflicted heavy losses on them, so that there were five hundred thousand casualties among Israel's able men.

column.name: text
column.value: The men of Israel were subdued on that occasion, and the men of Judah were victorious because they relied on the LORD, the God of their fathers.

column.name: text
column.value: Abijah pursued Jeroboam and took from him the towns of Bethel, Jeshanah and Ephron, with their surrounding villages.

column.name: text
column.value: Jeroboam did not regain power during the time of Abijah. And the LORD struck him down and he died.

column.name: text
column.value: But Abijah grew in strength. He married fourteen wives and had twenty-two sons and sixteen daughters.

column.name: text
column.value: The other events of Abijah's reign, what he did and what he said, are written in the annotations of the prophet Iddo.

column.name: text
column.value: After Rehoboam's position as king was established and he had become strong, he and all Israel with him abandoned the law of the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: Because they had been unfaithful to the LORD, Shishak king of Egypt attacked Jerusalem in the fifth year of King Rehoboam.

column.name: text
column.value: With twelve hundred chariots and sixty thousand horsemen and the innumerable troops of Libyans, Sukkites and Cushites that came with him from Egypt,

column.name: text
column.value: he captured the fortified cities of Judah and came as far as Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the prophet Shemaiah came to Rehoboam and to the leaders of Judah who had assembled in Jerusalem for fear of Shishak, and he said to them, "This is what the LORD says, 'You have abandoned me; therefore, I now abandon you to Shishak.'"

column.name: text
column.value: The leaders of Israel and the king humbled themselves and said, "The LORD is just."

column.name: text
column.value: When the LORD saw that they humbled themselves, this word of the LORD came to Shemaiah: "Since they have humbled themselves, I will not destroy them but will soon give them deliverance. My wrath will not be poured out on Jerusalem through Shishak.

column.name: text
column.value: They will, however, become subject to him, so that they may learn the difference between serving me and serving the kings of other lands."

column.name: text
column.value: When Shishak king of Egypt attacked Jerusalem, he carried off the treasures of the temple of the LORD and the treasures of the royal palace. He took everything, including the gold shields Solomon had made.

column.name: text
column.value: So King Rehoboam made bronze shields to replace them and assigned these to the commanders of the guard on duty at the entrance to the royal palace.

column.name: text
column.value: Whenever the king went to the LORD'S temple, the guards went with him, bearing the shields, and afterward they returned them to the guardroom.

column.name: text
column.value: Because Rehoboam humbled himself, the LORD'S anger turned from him, and he was not totally destroyed. Indeed, there was some good in Judah.

column.name: text
column.value: King Rehoboam established himself firmly in Jerusalem and continued as king. He was forty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned seventeen years in Jerusalem, the city the LORD had chosen out of all the tribes of Israel in which to put his Name. His mother's name was Naamah; she was an Ammonite.

column.name: text
column.value: He did evil because he had not set his heart on seeking the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: As for the events of Rehoboam's reign, from beginning to end, are they not written in the records of Shemaiah the prophet and of Iddo the seer that deal with genealogies? There was continual warfare between Rehoboam and Jeroboam.

column.name: text
column.value: Rehoboam rested with his fathers and was buried in the City of David. And Abijah his son succeeded him as king.

column.name: text
column.value: And Abijah rested with his fathers and was buried in the City of David. Asa his son succeeded him as king, and in his days the country was at peace for ten years.

column.name: text
column.value: Asa did what was good and right in the eyes of the LORD his God.

column.name: text
column.value: He removed the foreign altars and the high places, smashed the sacred stones and cut down the Asherah poles.

column.name: text
column.value: He commanded Judah to seek the LORD, the God of their fathers, and to obey his laws and commands.

column.name: text
column.value: He removed the high places and incense altars in every town in Judah, and the kingdom was at peace under him.

column.name: text
column.value: He built up the fortified cities of Judah, since the land was at peace. No one was at war with him during those years, for the LORD gave him rest.

column.name: text
column.value: "Let us build up these towns," he said to Judah, "and put walls around them, with towers, gates and bars. The land is still ours, because we have sought the LORD our God; we sought him and he has given us rest on every side." So they built and prospered.

column.name: text
column.value: Asa had an army of three hundred thousand men from Judah, equipped with large shields and with spears, and two hundred and eighty thousand from Benjamin, armed with small shields and with bows. All these were brave fighting men.

column.name: text
column.value: Zerah the Cushite marched out against them with a vast army and three hundred chariots, and came as far as Mareshah.

column.name: text
column.value: Asa went out to meet him, and they took up battle positions in the Valley of Zephathah near Mareshah.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Asa called to the LORD his God and said, "LORD, there is no one like you to help the powerless against the mighty. Help us, O LORD our God, for we rely on you, and in your name we have come against this vast army. O LORD, you are our God; do not let man prevail against you."

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD struck down the Cushites before Asa and Judah. The Cushites fled,

column.name: text
column.value: and Asa and his army pursued them as far as Gerar. Such a great number of Cushites fell that they could not recover; they were crushed before the LORD and his forces. The men of Judah carried off a large amount of plunder.

column.name: text
column.value: They destroyed all the villages around Gerar, for the terror of the LORD had fallen upon them. They plundered all these villages, since there was much booty there.

column.name: text
column.value: They also attacked the camps of the herdsmen and carried off droves of sheep and goats and camels. Then they returned to Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: The Spirit of God came upon Azariah son of Oded.

column.name: text
column.value: He went out to meet Asa and said to him, "Listen to me, Asa and all Judah and Benjamin. The LORD is with you when you are with him. If you seek him, he will be found by you, but if you forsake him, he will forsake you.

column.name: text
column.value: For a long time Israel was without the true God, without a priest to teach and without the law.

column.name: text
column.value: But in their distress they turned to the LORD, the God of Israel, and sought him, and he was found by them.

column.name: text
column.value: In those days it was not safe to travel about, for all the inhabitants of the lands were in great turmoil.

column.name: text
column.value: One nation was being crushed by another and one city by another, because God was troubling them with every kind of distress.

column.name: text
column.value: But as for you, be strong and do not give up, for your work will be rewarded."

column.name: text
column.value: When Asa heard these words and the prophecy of Azariah son of Oded the prophet, he took courage. He removed the detestable idols from the whole land of Judah and Benjamin and from the towns he had captured in the hills of Ephraim. He repaired the altar of the LORD that was in front of the portico of the LORD'S temple.

column.name: text
column.value: Then he assembled all Judah and Benjamin and the people from Ephraim, Manasseh and Simeon who had settled among them, for large numbers had come over to him from Israel when they saw that the LORD his God was with him.

column.name: text
column.value: They assembled at Jerusalem in the third month of the fifteenth year of Asa's reign.

column.name: text
column.value: At that time they sacrificed to the LORD seven hundred head of cattle and seven thousand sheep and goats from the plunder they had brought back.

column.name: text
column.value: They entered into a covenant to seek the LORD, the God of their fathers, with all their heart and soul.

column.name: text
column.value: All who would not seek the LORD, the God of Israel, were to be put to death, whether small or great, man or woman.

column.name: text
column.value: They took an oath to the LORD with loud acclamation, with shouting and with trumpets and horns.

column.name: text
column.value: All Judah rejoiced about the oath because they had sworn it wholeheartedly. They sought God eagerly, and he was found by them. So the LORD gave them rest on every side.

column.name: text
column.value: King Asa also deposed his grandmother Maacah from her position as queen mother, because she had made a repulsive Asherah pole. Asa cut the pole down, broke it up and burned it in the Kidron Valley.

column.name: text
column.value: Although he did not remove the high places from Israel, Asa's heart was fully committed to the LORD all his life.

column.name: text
column.value: He brought into the temple of God the silver and gold and the articles that he and his father had dedicated.

column.name: text
column.value: There was no more war until the thirty-fifth year of Asa's reign.

column.name: text
column.value: In the thirty-sixth year of Asa's reign Baasha king of Israel went up against Judah and fortified Ramah to prevent anyone from leaving or entering the territory of Asa king of Judah.

column.name: text
column.value: Asa then took the silver and gold out of the treasuries of the LORD'S temple and of his own palace and sent it to Ben-Hadad king of Aram, who was ruling in Damascus.

column.name: text
column.value: "Let there be a treaty between me and you," he said, "as there was between my father and your father. See, I am sending you silver and gold. Now break your treaty with Baasha king of Israel so he will withdraw from me."

column.name: text
column.value: Ben-Hadad agreed with King Asa and sent the commanders of his forces against the towns of Israel. They conquered Ijon, Dan, Abel Maim and all the store cities of Naphtali.

column.name: text
column.value: When Baasha heard this, he stopped building Ramah and abandoned his work.

column.name: text
column.value: Then King Asa brought all the men of Judah, and they carried away from Ramah the stones and timber Baasha had been using. With them he built up Geba and Mizpah.

column.name: text
column.value: At that time Hanani the seer came to Asa king of Judah and said to him: "Because you relied on the king of Aram and not on the LORD your God, the army of the king of Aram has escaped from your hand.

column.name: text
column.value: Were not the Cushites and Libyans a mighty army with great numbers of chariots and horsemen? Yet when you relied on the LORD, he delivered them into your hand.

column.name: text
column.value: For the eyes of the LORD range throughout the earth to strengthen those whose hearts are fully committed to him. You have done a foolish thing, and from now on you will be at war."

column.name: text
column.value: Asa was angry with the seer because of this; he was so enraged that he put him in prison. At the same time Asa brutally oppressed some of the people.

column.name: text
column.value: The events of Asa's reign, from beginning to end, are written in the book of the kings of Judah and Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: In the thirty-ninth year of his reign Asa was afflicted with a disease in his feet. Though his disease was severe, even in his illness he did not seek help from the LORD, but only from the physicians.

column.name: text
column.value: Then in the forty-first year of his reign Asa died and rested with his fathers.

column.name: text
column.value: They buried him in the tomb that he had cut out for himself in the City of David. They laid him on a bier covered with spices and various blended perfumes, and they made a huge fire in his honor.

column.name: text
column.value: Jehoshaphat his son succeeded him as king and strengthened himself against Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: He stationed troops in all the fortified cities of Judah and put garrisons in Judah and in the towns of Ephraim that his father Asa had captured.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD was with Jehoshaphat because in his early years he walked in the ways his father David had followed. He did not consult the Baals

column.name: text
column.value: but sought the God of his father and followed his commands rather than the practices of Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD established the kingdom under his control; and all Judah brought gifts to Jehoshaphat, so that he had great wealth and honor.

column.name: text
column.value: His heart was devoted to the ways of the LORD; furthermore, he removed the high places and the Asherah poles from Judah.

column.name: text
column.value: In the third year of his reign he sent his officials Ben-Hail, Obadiah, Zechariah, Nethanel and Micaiah to teach in the towns of Judah.

column.name: text
column.value: With them were certain Levites--Shemaiah, Nethaniah, Zebadiah, Asahel, Shemiramoth, Jehonathan, Adonijah, Tobijah and Tob-Adonijah--and the priests Elishama and Jehoram.

column.name: text
column.value: They taught throughout Judah, taking with them the Book of the Law of the LORD; they went around to all the towns of Judah and taught the people.

column.name: text
column.value: The fear of the LORD fell on all the kingdoms of the lands surrounding Judah, so that they did not make war with Jehoshaphat.

column.name: text
column.value: Some Philistines brought Jehoshaphat gifts and silver as tribute, and the Arabs brought him flocks: seven thousand seven hundred rams and seven thousand seven hundred goats.

column.name: text
column.value: Jehoshaphat became more and more powerful; he built forts and store cities in Judah

column.name: text
column.value: and had large supplies in the towns of Judah. He also kept experienced fighting men in Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: Their enrollment by families was as follows: From Judah, commanders of units of 1,000: Adnah the commander, with 300,000 fighting men;

column.name: text
column.value: next, Jehohanan the commander, with 280,000;

column.name: text
column.value: next, Amasiah son of Zicri, who volunteered himself for the service of the LORD, with 200,000.

column.name: text
column.value: From Benjamin: Eliada, a valiant soldier, with 200,000 men armed with bows and shields;

column.name: text
column.value: next, Jehozabad, with 180,000 men armed for battle.

column.name: text
column.value: These were the men who served the king, besides those he stationed in the fortified cities throughout Judah.

column.name: text
column.value: Now Jehoshaphat had great wealth and honor, and he allied himself with Ahab by marriage.

column.name: text
column.value: Some years later he went down to visit Ahab in Samaria. Ahab slaughtered many sheep and cattle for him and the people with him and urged him to attack Ramoth Gilead.

column.name: text
column.value: Ahab king of Israel asked Jehoshaphat king of Judah, "Will you go with me against Ramoth Gilead?" Jehoshaphat replied, "I am as you are, and my people as your people; we will join you in the war."

column.name: text
column.value: But Jehoshaphat also said to the king of Israel, "First seek the counsel of the LORD."

column.name: text
column.value: So the king of Israel brought together the prophets--four hundred men--and asked them, "Shall we go to war against Ramoth Gilead, or shall I refrain?" "Go," they answered, "for God will give it into the king's hand."

column.name: text
column.value: But Jehoshaphat asked, "Is there not a prophet of the LORD here whom we can inquire of?"

column.name: text
column.value: The king of Israel answered Jehoshaphat, "There is still one man through whom we can inquire of the LORD, but I hate him because he never prophesies anything good about me, but always bad. He is Micaiah son of Imlah." "The king should not say that," Jehoshaphat replied.

column.name: text
column.value: So the king of Israel called one of his officials and said, "Bring Micaiah son of Imlah at once."

column.name: text
column.value: Dressed in their royal robes, the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah were sitting on their thrones at the threshing floor by the entrance to the gate of Samaria, with all the prophets prophesying before them.

column.name: text
column.value: Now Zedekiah son of Kenaanah had made iron horns, and he declared, "This is what the LORD says: 'With these you will gore the Arameans until they are destroyed.'"

column.name: text
column.value: All the other prophets were prophesying the same thing. "Attack Ramoth Gilead and be victorious," they said, "for the LORD will give it into the king's hand."

column.name: text
column.value: The messenger who had gone to summon Micaiah said to him, "Look, as one man the other prophets are predicting success for the king. Let your word agree with theirs, and speak favorably."

column.name: text
column.value: But Micaiah said, "As surely as the LORD lives, I can tell him only what my God says."

column.name: text
column.value: When he arrived, the king asked him, "Micaiah, shall we go to war against Ramoth Gilead, or shall I refrain?" "Attack and be victorious," he answered, "for they will be given into your hand."

column.name: text
column.value: The king said to him, "How many times must I make you swear to tell me nothing but the truth in the name of the LORD?"

column.name: text
column.value: Then Micaiah answered, "I saw all Israel scattered on the hills like sheep without a shepherd, and the LORD said, 'These people have no master. Let each one go home in peace.'"

column.name: text
column.value: The king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, "Didn't I tell you that he never prophesies anything good about me, but only bad?"

column.name: text
column.value: Micaiah continued, "Therefore hear the word of the LORD: I saw the LORD sitting on his throne with all the host of heaven standing on his right and on his left.

column.name: text
column.value: And the LORD said, 'Who will entice Ahab king of Israel into attacking Ramoth Gilead and going to his death there?' "One suggested this, and another that.

column.name: text
column.value: Finally, a spirit came forward, stood before the LORD and said, 'I will entice him.' "'By what means?' the LORD asked.

column.name: text
column.value: "'I will go and be a lying spirit in the mouths of all his prophets,' he said. "'You will succeed in enticing him,' said the LORD. 'Go and do it.'

column.name: text
column.value: "So now the LORD has put a lying spirit in the mouths of these prophets of yours. The LORD has decreed disaster for you."

column.name: text
column.value: Then Zedekiah son of Kenaanah went up and slapped Micaiah in the face. "Which way did the spirit from the LORD go when he went from me to speak to you?" he asked.

column.name: text
column.value: Micaiah replied, "You will find out on the day you go to hide in an inner room."

column.name: text
column.value: The king of Israel then ordered, "Take Micaiah and send him back to Amon the ruler of the city and to Joash the king's son,

column.name: text
column.value: and say, 'This is what the king says: Put this fellow in prison and give him nothing but bread and water until I return safely.'"

column.name: text
column.value: Micaiah declared, "If you ever return safely, the LORD has not spoken through me." Then he added, "Mark my words, all you people!"

column.name: text
column.value: So the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah went up to Ramoth Gilead.

column.name: text
column.value: The king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, "I will enter the battle in disguise, but you wear your royal robes." So the king of Israel disguised himself and went into battle.

column.name: text
column.value: Now the king of Aram had ordered his chariot commanders, "Do not fight with anyone, small or great, except the king of Israel."

column.name: text
column.value: When the chariot commanders saw Jehoshaphat, they thought, "This is the king of Israel." So they turned to attack him, but Jehoshaphat cried out, and the LORD helped him. God drew them away from him,

column.name: text
column.value: for when the chariot commanders saw that he was not the king of Israel, they stopped pursuing him.

column.name: text
column.value: But someone drew his bow at random and hit the king of Israel between the sections of his armor. The king told the chariot driver, "Wheel around and get me out of the fighting. I've been wounded."

column.name: text
column.value: All day long the battle raged, and the king of Israel propped himself up in his chariot facing the Arameans until evening. Then at sunset he died.

column.name: text
column.value: After this, the Moabites and Ammonites with some of the Meunites came to make war on Jehoshaphat.

column.name: text
column.value: Some men came and told Jehoshaphat, "A vast army is coming against you from Edom, from the other side of the Sea. It is already in Hazazon Tamar" (that is, En Gedi).

column.name: text
column.value: Alarmed, Jehoshaphat resolved to inquire of the LORD, and he proclaimed a fast for all Judah.

column.name: text
column.value: The people of Judah came together to seek help from the LORD; indeed, they came from every town in Judah to seek him.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jehoshaphat stood up in the assembly of Judah and Jerusalem at the temple of the LORD in the front of the new courtyard

column.name: text
column.value: and said: "O LORD, God of our fathers, are you not the God who is in heaven? You rule over all the kingdoms of the nations. Power and might are in your hand, and no one can withstand you.

column.name: text
column.value: O our God, did you not drive out the inhabitants of this land before your people Israel and give it forever to the descendants of Abraham your friend?

column.name: text
column.value: They have lived in it and have built in it a sanctuary for your Name, saying,

column.name: text
column.value: 'If calamity comes upon us, whether the sword of judgment, or plague or famine, we will stand in your presence before this temple that bears your Name and will cry out to you in our distress, and you will hear us and save us.'

column.name: text
column.value: "But now here are men from Ammon, Moab and Mount Seir, whose territory you would not allow Israel to invade when they came from Egypt; so they turned away from them and did not destroy them.

column.name: text
column.value: See how they are repaying us by coming to drive us out of the possession you gave us as an inheritance.

column.name: text
column.value: O our God, will you not judge them? For we have no power to face this vast army that is attacking us. We do not know what to do, but our eyes are upon you."

column.name: text
column.value: All the men of Judah, with their wives and children and little ones, stood there before the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the Spirit of the LORD came upon Jahaziel son of Zechariah, the son of Benaiah, the son of Jeiel, the son of Mattaniah, a Levite and descendant of Asaph, as he stood in the assembly.

column.name: text
column.value: He said: "Listen, King Jehoshaphat and all who live in Judah and Jerusalem! This is what the LORD says to you: 'Do not be afraid or discouraged because of this vast army. For the battle is not yours, but God's.

column.name: text
column.value: Tomorrow march down against them. They will be climbing up by the Pass of Ziz, and you will find them at the end of the gorge in the Desert of Jeruel.

column.name: text
column.value: You will not have to fight this battle. Take up your positions; stand firm and see the deliverance the LORD will give you, O Judah and Jerusalem. Do not be afraid; do not be discouraged. Go out to face them tomorrow, and the LORD will be with you.'"

column.name: text
column.value: Jehoshaphat bowed with his face to the ground, and all the people of Judah and Jerusalem fell down in worship before the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: Then some Levites from the Kohathites and Korahites stood up and praised the LORD, the God of Israel, with very loud voice.

column.name: text
column.value: Early in the morning they left for the Desert of Tekoa. As they set out, Jehoshaphat stood and said, "Listen to me, Judah and people of Jerusalem! Have faith in the LORD your God and you will be upheld; have faith in his prophets and you will be successful."

column.name: text
column.value: After consulting the people, Jehoshaphat appointed men to sing to the LORD and to praise him for the splendor of his holiness as they went out at the head of the army, saying: "Give thanks to the LORD, for his love endures forever."

column.name: text
column.value: As they began to sing and praise, the LORD set ambushes against the men of Ammon and Moab and Mount Seir who were invading Judah, and they were defeated.

column.name: text
column.value: The men of Ammon and Moab rose up against the men from Mount Seir to destroy and annihilate them. After they finished slaughtering the men from Seir, they helped to destroy one another.

column.name: text
column.value: When the men of Judah came to the place that overlooks the desert and looked toward the vast army, they saw only dead bodies lying on the ground; no one had escaped.

column.name: text
column.value: So Jehoshaphat and his men went to carry off their plunder, and they found among them a great amount of equipment and clothing and also articles of value--more than they could take away. There was so much plunder that it took three days to collect it.

column.name: text
column.value: On the fourth day they assembled in the Valley of Beracah, where they praised the LORD. This is why it is called the Valley of Beracah to this day.

column.name: text
column.value: Then, led by Jehoshaphat, all the men of Judah and Jerusalem returned joyfully to Jerusalem, for the LORD had given them cause to rejoice over their enemies.

column.name: text
column.value: They entered Jerusalem and went to the temple of the LORD with harps and lutes and trumpets.

column.name: text
column.value: The fear of God came upon all the kingdoms of the countries when they heard how the LORD had fought against the enemies of Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: And the kingdom of Jehoshaphat was at peace, for his God had given him rest on every side.

column.name: text
column.value: So Jehoshaphat reigned over Judah. He was thirty-five years old when he became king of Judah, and he reigned in Jerusalem twenty-five years. His mother's name was Azubah daughter of Shilhi.

column.name: text
column.value: He walked in the ways of his father Asa and did not stray from them; he did what was right in the eyes of the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: The high places, however, were not removed, and the people still had not set their hearts on the God of their fathers.

column.name: text
column.value: The other events of Jehoshaphat's reign, from beginning to end, are written in the annals of Jehu son of Hanani, which are recorded in the book of the kings of Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: Later, Jehoshaphat king of Judah made an alliance with Ahaziah king of Israel, who was guilty of wickedness.

column.name: text
column.value: He agreed with him to construct a fleet of trading ships. After these were built at Ezion Geber,

column.name: text
column.value: Eliezer son of Dodavahu of Mareshah prophesied against Jehoshaphat, saying, "Because you have made an alliance with Ahaziah, the LORD will destroy what you have made." The ships were wrecked and were not able to set sail to trade.

column.name: text
column.value: When Jehoshaphat king of Judah returned safely to his palace in Jerusalem,

column.name: text
column.value: Jehu the seer, the son of Hanani, went out to meet him and said to the king, "Should you help the wicked and love those who hate the LORD? Because of this, the wrath of the LORD is upon you.

column.name: text
column.value: There is, however, some good in you, for you have rid the land of the Asherah poles and have set your heart on seeking God."

column.name: text
column.value: Jehoshaphat lived in Jerusalem, and he went out again among the people from Beersheba to the hill country of Ephraim and turned them back to the LORD, the God of their fathers.

column.name: text
column.value: He appointed judges in the land, in each of the fortified cities of Judah.

column.name: text
column.value: He told them, "Consider carefully what you do, because you are not judging for man but for the LORD, who is with you whenever you give a verdict.

column.name: text
column.value: Now let the fear of the LORD be upon you. Judge carefully, for with the LORD our God there is no injustice or partiality or bribery."

column.name: text
column.value: In Jerusalem also, Jehoshaphat appointed some of the Levites, priests and heads of Israelite families to administer the law of the LORD and to settle disputes. And they lived in Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: He gave them these orders: "You must serve faithfully and wholeheartedly in the fear of the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: In every case that comes before you from your fellow countrymen who live in the cities--whether bloodshed or other concerns of the law, commands, decrees or ordinances--you are to warn them not to sin against the LORD; otherwise his wrath will come on you and your brothers. Do this, and you will not sin.

column.name: text
column.value: "Amariah the chief priest will be over you in any matter concerning the LORD, and Zebadiah son of Ishmael, the leader of the tribe of Judah, will be over you in any matter concerning the king, and the Levites will serve as officials before you. Act with courage, and may the LORD be with those who do well."

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jehoshaphat rested with his fathers and was buried with them in the City of David. And Jehoram his son succeeded him as king.

column.name: text
column.value: Jehoram's brothers, the sons of Jehoshaphat, were Azariah, Jehiel, Zechariah, Azariahu, Michael and Shephatiah. All these were sons of Jehoshaphat king of Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: Their father had given them many gifts of silver and gold and articles of value, as well as fortified cities in Judah, but he had given the kingdom to Jehoram because he was his firstborn son.

column.name: text
column.value: When Jehoram established himself firmly over his father's kingdom, he put all his brothers to the sword along with some of the princes of Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: Jehoram was thirty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem eight years.

column.name: text
column.value: He walked in the ways of the kings of Israel, as the house of Ahab had done, for he married a daughter of Ahab. He did evil in the eyes of the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: Nevertheless, because of the covenant the LORD had made with David, the LORD was not willing to destroy the house of David. He had promised to maintain a lamp for him and his descendants forever.

column.name: text
column.value: In the time of Jehoram, Edom rebelled against Judah and set up its own king.

column.name: text
column.value: So Jehoram went there with his officers and all his chariots. The Edomites surrounded him and his chariot commanders, but he rose up and broke through by night.

column.name: text
column.value: To this day Edom has been in rebellion against Judah. Libnah revolted at the same time, because Jehoram had forsaken the LORD, the God of his fathers.

column.name: text
column.value: He had also built high places on the hills of Judah and had caused the people of Jerusalem to prostitute themselves and had led Judah astray.

column.name: text
column.value: Jehoram received a letter from Elijah the prophet, which said: "This is what the LORD, the God of your father David, says: 'You have not walked in the ways of your father Jehoshaphat or of Asa king of Judah.

column.name: text
column.value: But you have walked in the ways of the kings of Israel, and you have led Judah and the people of Jerusalem to prostitute themselves, just as the house of Ahab did. You have also murdered your own brothers, members of your father's house, men who were better than you.

column.name: text
column.value: So now the LORD is about to strike your people, your sons, your wives and everything that is yours, with a heavy blow.

column.name: text
column.value: You yourself will be very ill with a lingering disease of the bowels, until the disease causes your bowels to come out.'"

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD aroused against Jehoram the hostility of the Philistines and of the Arabs who lived near the Cushites.

column.name: text
column.value: They attacked Judah, invaded it and carried off all the goods found in the king's palace, together with his sons and wives. Not a son was left to him except Ahaziah, the youngest.

column.name: text
column.value: After all this, the LORD afflicted Jehoram with an incurable disease of the bowels.

column.name: text
column.value: In the course of time, at the end of the second year, his bowels came out because of the disease, and he died in great pain. His people made no fire in his honor, as they had for his fathers.

column.name: text
column.value: Jehoram was thirty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem eight years. He passed away, to no one's regret, and was buried in the City of David, but not in the tombs of the kings.

column.name: text
column.value: The people of Jerusalem made Ahaziah, Jehoram's youngest son, king in his place, since the raiders, who came with the Arabs into the camp, had killed all the older sons. So Ahaziah son of Jehoram king of Judah began to reign.

column.name: text
column.value: Ahaziah was twenty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem one year. His mother's name was Athaliah, a granddaughter of Omri.

column.name: text
column.value: He too walked in the ways of the house of Ahab, for his mother encouraged him in doing wrong.

column.name: text
column.value: He did evil in the eyes of the LORD, as the house of Ahab had done, for after his father's death they became his advisers, to his undoing.

column.name: text
column.value: He also followed their counsel when he went with Joram son of Ahab king of Israel to war against Hazael king of Aram at Ramoth Gilead. The Arameans wounded Joram;

column.name: text
column.value: so he returned to Jezreel to recover from the wounds they had inflicted on him at Ramoth in his battle with Hazael king of Aram. Then Ahaziah son of Jehoram king of Judah went down to Jezreel to see Joram son of Ahab because he had been wounded.

column.name: text
column.value: Through Ahaziah's visit to Joram, God brought about Ahaziah's downfall. When Ahaziah arrived, he went out with Joram to meet Jehu son of Nimshi, whom the LORD had anointed to destroy the house of Ahab.

column.name: text
column.value: While Jehu was executing judgment on the house of Ahab, he found the princes of Judah and the sons of Ahaziah's relatives, who had been attending Ahaziah, and he killed them.

column.name: text
column.value: He then went in search of Ahaziah, and his men captured him while he was hiding in Samaria. He was brought to Jehu and put to death. They buried him, for they said, "He was a son of Jehoshaphat, who sought the LORD with all his heart." So there was no one in the house of Ahaziah powerful enough to retain the kingdom.

column.name: text
column.value: When Athaliah the mother of Ahaziah saw that her son was dead, she proceeded to destroy the whole royal family of the house of Judah.

column.name: text
column.value: But Jehosheba, the daughter of King Jehoram, took Joash son of Ahaziah and stole him away from among the royal princes who were about to be murdered and put him and his nurse in a bedroom. Because Jehosheba, the daughter of King Jehoram and wife of the priest Jehoiada, was Ahaziah's sister, she hid the child from Athaliah so she could not kill him.

column.name: text
column.value: He remained hidden with them at the temple of God for six years while Athaliah ruled the land.

column.name: text
column.value: In the seventh year Jehoiada showed his strength. He made a covenant with the commanders of units of a hundred: Azariah son of Jeroham, Ishmael son of Jehohanan, Azariah son of Obed, Maaseiah son of Adaiah, and Elishaphat son of Zicri.

column.name: text
column.value: They went throughout Judah and gathered the Levites and the heads of Israelite families from all the towns. When they came to Jerusalem,

column.name: text
column.value: the whole assembly made a covenant with the king at the temple of God. Jehoiada said to them, "The king's son shall reign, as the LORD promised concerning the descendants of David.

column.name: text
column.value: Now this is what you are to do: A third of you priests and Levites who are going on duty on the Sabbath are to keep watch at the doors,

column.name: text
column.value: a third of you at the royal palace and a third at the Foundation Gate, and all the other men are to be in the courtyards of the temple of the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: No one is to enter the temple of the LORD except the priests and Levites on duty; they may enter because they are consecrated, but all the other men are to guard what the LORD has assigned to them.

column.name: text
column.value: The Levites are to station themselves around the king, each man with his weapons in his hand. Anyone who enters the temple must be put to death. Stay close to the king wherever he goes."

column.name: text
column.value: The Levites and all the men of Judah did just as Jehoiada the priest ordered. Each one took his men--those who were going on duty on the Sabbath and those who were going off duty--for Jehoiada the priest had not released any of the divisions.

column.name: text
column.value: Then he gave the commanders of units of a hundred the spears and the large and small shields that had belonged to King David and that were in the temple of God.

column.name: text
column.value: He stationed all the men, each with his weapon in his hand, around the king--near the altar and the temple, from the south side to the north side of the temple.

column.name: text
column.value: Jehoiada and his sons brought out the king's son and put the crown on him; they presented him with a copy of the covenant and proclaimed him king. They anointed him and shouted, "Long live the king!"

column.name: text
column.value: When Athaliah heard the noise of the people running and cheering the king, she went to them at the temple of the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: She looked, and there was the king, standing by his pillar at the entrance. The officers and the trumpeters were beside the king, and all the people of the land were rejoicing and blowing trumpets, and singers with musical instruments were leading the praises. Then Athaliah tore her robes and shouted, "Treason! Treason!"

column.name: text
column.value: Jehoiada the priest sent out the commanders of units of a hundred, who were in charge of the troops, and said to them: "Bring her out between the ranks and put to the sword anyone who follows her." For the priest had said, "Do not put her to death at the temple of the LORD."

column.name: text
column.value: So they seized her as she reached the entrance of the Horse Gate on the palace grounds, and there they put her to death.

column.name: text
column.value: Jehoiada then made a covenant that he and the people and the king would be the LORD'S people.

column.name: text
column.value: All the people went to the temple of Baal and tore it down. They smashed the altars and idols and killed Mattan the priest of Baal in front of the altars.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jehoiada placed the oversight of the temple of the LORD in the hands of the priests, who were Levites, to whom David had made assignments in the temple, to present the burnt offerings of the LORD as written in the Law of Moses, with rejoicing and singing, as David had ordered.

column.name: text
column.value: He also stationed doorkeepers at the gates of the LORD'S temple so that no one who was in any way unclean might enter.

column.name: text
column.value: He took with him the commanders of hundreds, the nobles, the rulers of the people and all the people of the land and brought the king down from the temple of the LORD. They went into the palace through the Upper Gate and seated the king on the royal throne,

column.name: text
column.value: and all the people of the land rejoiced. And the city was quiet, because Athaliah had been slain with the sword.

column.name: text
column.value: Then all the people of Judah took Uzziah, who was sixteen years old, and made him king in place of his father Amaziah.

column.name: text
column.value: He was the one who rebuilt Elath and restored it to Judah after Amaziah rested with his fathers.

column.name: text
column.value: Uzziah was sixteen years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem fifty-two years. His mother's name was Jecoliah; she was from Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: He did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, just as his father Amaziah had done.

column.name: text
column.value: He sought God during the days of Zechariah, who instructed him in the fear of God. As long as he sought the LORD, God gave him success.

column.name: text
column.value: He went to war against the Philistines and broke down the walls of Gath, Jabneh and Ashdod. He then rebuilt towns near Ashdod and elsewhere among the Philistines.

column.name: text
column.value: God helped him against the Philistines and against the Arabs who lived in Gur Baal and against the Meunites.

column.name: text
column.value: The Ammonites brought tribute to Uzziah, and his fame spread as far as the border of Egypt, because he had become very powerful.

column.name: text
column.value: Uzziah built towers in Jerusalem at the Corner Gate, at the Valley Gate and at the angle of the wall, and he fortified them.

column.name: text
column.value: He also built towers in the desert and dug many cisterns, because he had much livestock in the foothills and in the plain. He had people working his fields and vineyards in the hills and in the fertile lands, for he loved the soil.

column.name: text
column.value: Uzziah had a well-trained army, ready to go out by divisions according to their numbers as mustered by Jeiel the secretary and Maaseiah the officer under the direction of Hananiah, one of the royal officials.

column.name: text
column.value: The total number of family leaders over the fighting men was 2,600.

column.name: text
column.value: Under their command was an army of 307,500 men trained for war, a powerful force to support the king against his enemies.

column.name: text
column.value: Uzziah provided shields, spears, helmets, coats of armor, bows and slingstones for the entire army.

column.name: text
column.value: In Jerusalem he made machines designed by skillful men for use on the towers and on the corner defenses to shoot arrows and hurl large stones. His fame spread far and wide, for he was greatly helped until he became powerful.

column.name: text
column.value: But after Uzziah became powerful, his pride led to his downfall. He was unfaithful to the LORD his God, and entered the temple of the LORD to burn incense on the altar of incense.

column.name: text
column.value: Azariah the priest with eighty other courageous priests of the LORD followed him in.

column.name: text
column.value: They confronted him and said, "It is not right for you, Uzziah, to burn incense to the LORD. That is for the priests, the descendants of Aaron, who have been consecrated to burn incense. Leave the sanctuary, for you have been unfaithful; and you will not be honored by the LORD God."

column.name: text
column.value: Uzziah, who had a censer in his hand ready to burn incense, became angry. While he was raging at the priests in their presence before the incense altar in the LORD'S temple, leprosy broke out on his forehead.

column.name: text
column.value: When Azariah the chief priest and all the other priests looked at him, they saw that he had leprosy on his forehead, so they hurried him out. Indeed, he himself was eager to leave, because the LORD had afflicted him.

column.name: text
column.value: King Uzziah had leprosy until the day he died. He lived in a separate house --leprous, and excluded from the temple of the LORD. Jotham his son had charge of the palace and governed the people of the land.

column.name: text
column.value: The other events of Uzziah's reign, from beginning to end, are recorded by the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz.

column.name: text
column.value: Uzziah rested with his fathers and was buried near them in a field for burial that belonged to the kings, for people said, "He had leprosy." And Jotham his son succeeded him as king.

column.name: text
column.value: Amaziah was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem twenty-nine years. His mother's name was Jehoaddin; she was from Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: He did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, but not wholeheartedly.

column.name: text
column.value: After the kingdom was firmly in his control, he executed the officials who had murdered his father the king.

column.name: text
column.value: Yet he did not put their sons to death, but acted in accordance with what is written in the Law, in the Book of Moses, where the LORD commanded: "Fathers shall not be put to death for their children, nor children put to death for their fathers; each is to die for his own sins."

column.name: text
column.value: Amaziah called the people of Judah together and assigned them according to their families to commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds for all Judah and Benjamin. He then mustered those twenty years old or more and found that there were three hundred thousand men ready for military service, able to handle the spear and shield.

column.name: text
column.value: He also hired a hundred thousand fighting men from Israel for a hundred talents of silver.

column.name: text
column.value: But a man of God came to him and said, "O king, these troops from Israel must not march with you, for the LORD is not with Israel--not with any of the people of Ephraim.

column.name: text
column.value: Even if you go and fight courageously in battle, God will overthrow you before the enemy, for God has the power to help or to overthrow."

column.name: text
column.value: Amaziah asked the man of God, "But what about the hundred talents I paid for these Israelite troops?" The man of God replied, "The LORD can give you much more than that."

column.name: text
column.value: So Amaziah dismissed the troops who had come to him from Ephraim and sent them home. They were furious with Judah and left for home in a great rage.

column.name: text
column.value: Amaziah then marshaled his strength and led his army to the Valley of Salt, where he killed ten thousand men of Seir.

column.name: text
column.value: The army of Judah also captured ten thousand men alive, took them to the top of a cliff and threw them down so that all were dashed to pieces.

column.name: text
column.value: Meanwhile the troops that Amaziah had sent back and had not allowed to take part in the war raided Judean towns from Samaria to Beth Horon. They killed three thousand people and carried off great quantities of plunder.

column.name: text
column.value: When Amaziah returned from slaughtering the Edomites, he brought back the gods of the people of Seir. He set them up as his own gods, bowed down to them and burned sacrifices to them.

column.name: text
column.value: The anger of the LORD burned against Amaziah, and he sent a prophet to him, who said, "Why do you consult this people's gods, which could not save their own people from your hand?"

column.name: text
column.value: While he was still speaking, the king said to him, "Have we appointed you an adviser to the king? Stop! Why be struck down?" So the prophet stopped but said, "I know that God has determined to destroy you, because you have done this and have not listened to my counsel."

column.name: text
column.value: After Amaziah king of Judah consulted his advisers, he sent this challenge to Jehoash son of Jehoahaz, the son of Jehu, king of Israel: "Come, meet me face to face."

column.name: text
column.value: But Jehoash king of Israel replied to Amaziah king of Judah: "A thistle in Lebanon sent a message to a cedar in Lebanon, 'Give your daughter to my son in marriage.' Then a wild beast in Lebanon came along and trampled the thistle underfoot.

column.name: text
column.value: You say to yourself that you have defeated Edom, and now you are arrogant and proud. But stay at home! Why ask for trouble and cause your own downfall and that of Judah also?"

column.name: text
column.value: Amaziah, however, would not listen, for God so worked that he might hand them over to Jehoash, because they sought the gods of Edom.

column.name: text
column.value: So Jehoash king of Israel attacked. He and Amaziah king of Judah faced each other at Beth Shemesh in Judah.

column.name: text
column.value: Judah was routed by Israel, and every man fled to his home.

column.name: text
column.value: Jehoash king of Israel captured Amaziah king of Judah, the son of Joash, the son of Ahaziah, at Beth Shemesh. Then Jehoash brought him to Jerusalem and broke down the wall of Jerusalem from the Ephraim Gate to the Corner Gate--a section about six hundred feet long.

column.name: text
column.value: He took all the gold and silver and all the articles found in the temple of God that had been in the care of Obed-Edom, together with the palace treasures and the hostages, and returned to Samaria.

column.name: text
column.value: Amaziah son of Joash king of Judah lived for fifteen years after the death of Jehoash son of Jehoahaz king of Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: As for the other events of Amaziah's reign, from beginning to end, are they not written in the book of the kings of Judah and Israel?

column.name: text
column.value: From the time that Amaziah turned away from following the LORD, they conspired against him in Jerusalem and he fled to Lachish, but they sent men after him to Lachish and killed him there.

column.name: text
column.value: He was brought back by horse and was buried with his fathers in the City of Judah.

column.name: text
column.value: Joash was seven years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem forty years. His mother's name was Zibiah; she was from Beersheba.

column.name: text
column.value: Joash did what was right in the eyes of the LORD all the years of Jehoiada the priest.

column.name: text
column.value: Jehoiada chose two wives for him, and he had sons and daughters.

column.name: text
column.value: Some time later Joash decided to restore the temple of the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: He called together the priests and Levites and said to them, "Go to the towns of Judah and collect the money due annually from all Israel, to repair the temple of your God. Do it now." But the Levites did not act at once.

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore the king summoned Jehoiada the chief priest and said to him, "Why haven't you required the Levites to bring in from Judah and Jerusalem the tax imposed by Moses the servant of the LORD and by the assembly of Israel for the Tent of the Testimony?"

column.name: text
column.value: Now the sons of that wicked woman Athaliah had broken into the temple of God and had used even its sacred objects for the Baals.

column.name: text
column.value: At the king's command, a chest was made and placed outside, at the gate of the temple of the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: A proclamation was then issued in Judah and Jerusalem that they should bring to the LORD the tax that Moses the servant of God had required of Israel in the desert.

column.name: text
column.value: All the officials and all the people brought their contributions gladly, dropping them into the chest until it was full.

column.name: text
column.value: Whenever the chest was brought in by the Levites to the king's officials and they saw that there was a large amount of money, the royal secretary and the officer of the chief priest would come and empty the chest and carry it back to its place. They did this regularly and collected a great amount of money.

column.name: text
