column.name: text
column.value: Neziah and Hatipha

column.name: text
column.value: The descendants of the servants of Solomon: the descendants of Sotai, Hassophereth, Peruda,

column.name: text
column.value: Jaala, Darkon, Giddel,

column.name: text
column.value: Shephatiah, Hattil, Pokereth-Hazzebaim and Ami

column.name: text
column.value: The temple servants and the descendants of the servants of Solomon 392

column.name: text
column.value: The following came up from the towns of Tel Melah, Tel Harsha, Kerub, Addon and Immer, but they could not show that their families were descended from Israel:

column.name: text
column.value: The descendants of Delaiah, Tobiah and Nekoda 652

column.name: text
column.value: And from among the priests: The descendants of Hobaiah, Hakkoz and Barzillai (a man who had married a daughter of Barzillai the Gileadite and was called by that name).

column.name: text
column.value: These searched for their family records, but they could not find them and so were excluded from the priesthood as unclean.

column.name: text
column.value: The governor ordered them not to eat any of the most sacred food until there was a priest ministering with the Urim and Thummim.

column.name: text
column.value: The whole company numbered 42,360,

column.name: text
column.value: besides their 7,337 menservants and maidservants; and they also had 200 men and women singers.

column.name: text
column.value: They had 736 horses, 245 mules,

column.name: text
column.value: 435 camels and 6,720 donkeys.

column.name: text
column.value: When they arrived at the house of the LORD in Jerusalem, some of the heads of the families gave freewill offerings toward the rebuilding of the house of God on its site.

column.name: text
column.value: According to their ability they gave to the treasury for this work 61,000 drachmas of gold, 5,000 minas of silver and 100 priestly garments.

column.name: text
column.value: The priests, the Levites, the singers, the gatekeepers and the temple servants settled in their own towns, along with some of the other people, and the rest of the Israelites settled in their towns.

column.name: text
column.value: And the people of the land took Jehoahaz son of Josiah and made him king in Jerusalem in place of his father.

column.name: text
column.value: Jehoahaz was twenty-three years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem three months.

column.name: text
column.value: The king of Egypt dethroned him in Jerusalem and imposed on Judah a levy of a hundred talents of silver and a talent of gold.

column.name: text
column.value: The king of Egypt made Eliakim, a brother of Jehoahaz, king over Judah and Jerusalem and changed Eliakim's name to Jehoiakim. But Neco took Eliakim's brother Jehoahaz and carried him off to Egypt.

column.name: text
column.value: Jehoiakim was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem eleven years. He did evil in the eyes of the LORD his God.

column.name: text
column.value: Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon attacked him and bound him with bronze shackles to take him to Babylon.

column.name: text
column.value: Nebuchadnezzar also took to Babylon articles from the temple of the LORD and put them in his temple there.

column.name: text
column.value: The other events of Jehoiakim's reign, the detestable things he did and all that was found against him, are written in the book of the kings of Israel and Judah. And Jehoiachin his son succeeded him as king.

column.name: text
column.value: Jehoiachin was eighteen years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem three months and ten days. He did evil in the eyes of the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: In the spring, King Nebuchadnezzar sent for him and brought him to Babylon, together with articles of value from the temple of the LORD, and he made Jehoiachin's uncle, Zedekiah, king over Judah and Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem eleven years.

column.name: text
column.value: He did evil in the eyes of the LORD his God and did not humble himself before Jeremiah the prophet, who spoke the word of the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: He also rebelled against King Nebuchadnezzar, who had made him take an oath in God's name. He became stiff-necked and hardened his heart and would not turn to the LORD, the God of Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: Furthermore, all the leaders of the priests and the people became more and more unfaithful, following all the detestable practices of the nations and defiling the temple of the LORD, which he had consecrated in Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD, the God of their fathers, sent word to them through his messengers again and again, because he had pity on his people and on his dwelling place.

column.name: text
column.value: But they mocked God's messengers, despised his words and scoffed at his prophets until the wrath of the LORD was aroused against his people and there was no remedy.

column.name: text
column.value: He brought up against them the king of the Babylonians, who killed their young men with the sword in the sanctuary, and spared neither young man nor young woman, old man or aged. God handed all of them over to Nebuchadnezzar.

column.name: text
column.value: He carried to Babylon all the articles from the temple of God, both large and small, and the treasures of the LORD'S temple and the treasures of the king and his officials.

column.name: text
column.value: They set fire to God's temple and broke down the wall of Jerusalem; they burned all the palaces and destroyed everything of value there.

column.name: text
column.value: He carried into exile to Babylon the remnant, who escaped from the sword, and they became servants to him and his sons until the kingdom of Persia came to power.

column.name: text
column.value: The land enjoyed its sabbath rests; all the time of its desolation it rested, until the seventy years were completed in fulfillment of the word of the LORD spoken by Jeremiah.

column.name: text
column.value: In the first year of Cyrus king of Persia, in order to fulfill the word of the LORD spoken by Jeremiah, the LORD moved the heart of Cyrus king of Persia to make a proclamation throughout his realm and to put it in writing:

column.name: text
column.value: "This is what Cyrus king of Persia says: "'The LORD, the God of heaven, has given me all the kingdoms of the earth and he has appointed me to build a temple for him at Jerusalem in Judah. Anyone of his people among you--may the LORD his God be with him, and let him go up.'"

column.name: text
column.value: When the seventh month came and the Israelites had settled in their towns, the people assembled as one man in Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jeshua son of Jozadak and his fellow priests and Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and his associates began to build the altar of the God of Israel to sacrifice burnt offerings on it, in accordance with what is written in the Law of Moses the man of God.

column.name: text
column.value: Despite their fear of the peoples around them, they built the altar on its foundation and sacrificed burnt offerings on it to the LORD, both the morning and evening sacrifices.

column.name: text
column.value: Then in accordance with what is written, they celebrated the Feast of Tabernacles with the required number of burnt offerings prescribed for each day.

column.name: text
column.value: After that, they presented the regular burnt offerings, the New Moon sacrifices and the sacrifices for all the appointed sacred feasts of the LORD, as well as those brought as freewill offerings to the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: On the first day of the seventh month they began to offer burnt offerings to the LORD, though the foundation of the LORD'S temple had not yet been laid.

column.name: text
column.value: Then they gave money to the masons and carpenters, and gave food and drink and oil to the people of Sidon and Tyre, so that they would bring cedar logs by sea from Lebanon to Joppa, as authorized by Cyrus king of Persia.

column.name: text
column.value: In the second month of the second year after their arrival at the house of God in Jerusalem, Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, Jeshua son of Jozadak and the rest of their brothers (the priests and the Levites and all who had returned from the captivity to Jerusalem) began the work, appointing Levites twenty years of age and older to supervise the building of the house of the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: Jeshua and his sons and brothers and Kadmiel and his sons (descendants of Hodaviah) and the sons of Henadad and their sons and brothers--all Levites--joined together in supervising those working on the house of God.

column.name: text
column.value: When the builders laid the foundation of the temple of the LORD, the priests in their vestments and with trumpets, and the Levites (the sons of Asaph) with cymbals, took their places to praise the LORD, as prescribed by David king of Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: With praise and thanksgiving they sang to the LORD: "He is good; his love to Israel endures forever." And all the people gave a great shout of praise to the LORD, because the foundation of the house of the LORD was laid.

column.name: text
column.value: But many of the older priests and Levites and family heads, who had seen the former temple, wept aloud when they saw the foundation of this temple being laid, while many others shouted for joy.

column.name: text
column.value: No one could distinguish the sound of the shouts of joy from the sound of weeping, because the people made so much noise. And the sound was heard far away.

column.name: text
column.value: When the enemies of Judah and Benjamin heard that the exiles were building a temple for the LORD, the God of Israel,

column.name: text
column.value: they came to Zerubbabel and to the heads of the families and said, "Let us help you build because, like you, we seek your God and have been sacrificing to him since the time of Esarhaddon king of Assyria, who brought us here."

column.name: text
column.value: But Zerubbabel, Jeshua and the rest of the heads of the families of Israel answered, "You have no part with us in building a temple to our God. We alone will build it for the LORD, the God of Israel, as King Cyrus, the king of Persia, commanded us."

column.name: text
column.value: Then the peoples around them set out to discourage the people of Judah and make them afraid to go on building.

column.name: text
column.value: They hired counselors to work against them and frustrate their plans during the entire reign of Cyrus king of Persia and down to the reign of Darius king of Persia.

column.name: text
column.value: At the beginning of the reign of Xerxes, they lodged an accusation against the people of Judah and Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: And in the days of Artaxerxes king of Persia, Bishlam, Mithredath, Tabeel and the rest of his associates wrote a letter to Artaxerxes. The letter was written in Aramaic script and in the Aramaic language.

column.name: text
column.value: Rehum the commanding officer and Shimshai the secretary wrote a letter against Jerusalem to Artaxerxes the king as follows:

column.name: text
column.value: Rehum the commanding officer and Shimshai the secretary, together with the rest of their associates--the judges and officials over the men from Tripolis, Persia, Erech and Babylon, the Elamites of Susa,

column.name: text
column.value: and the other people whom the great and honorable Ashurbanipal deported and settled in the city of Samaria and elsewhere in Trans-Euphrates.

column.name: text
column.value: (This is a copy of the letter they sent him.) To King Artaxerxes, From your servants, the men of Trans-Euphrates:

column.name: text
column.value: The king should know that the Jews who came up to us from you have gone to Jerusalem and are rebuilding that rebellious and wicked city. They are restoring the walls and repairing the foundations.

column.name: text
column.value: Furthermore, the king should know that if this city is built and its walls are restored, no more taxes, tribute or duty will be paid, and the royal revenues will suffer.

column.name: text
column.value: Now since we are under obligation to the palace and it is not proper for us to see the king dishonored, we are sending this message to inform the king,

column.name: text
column.value: so that a search may be made in the archives of your predecessors. In these records you will find that this city is a rebellious city, troublesome to kings and provinces, a place of rebellion from ancient times. That is why this city was destroyed.

column.name: text
column.value: We inform the king that if this city is built and its walls are restored, you will be left with nothing in Trans-Euphrates.

column.name: text
column.value: The king sent this reply: To Rehum the commanding officer, Shimshai the secretary and the rest of their associates living in Samaria and elsewhere in Trans-Euphrates: Greetings.

column.name: text
column.value: The letter you sent us has been read and translated in my presence.

column.name: text
column.value: I issued an order and a search was made, and it was found that this city has a long history of revolt against kings and has been a place of rebellion and sedition.

column.name: text
column.value: Jerusalem has had powerful kings ruling over the whole of Trans-Euphrates, and taxes, tribute and duty were paid to them.

column.name: text
column.value: Now issue an order to these men to stop work, so that this city will not be rebuilt until I so order.

column.name: text
column.value: Be careful not to neglect this matter. Why let this threat grow, to the detriment of the royal interests?

column.name: text
column.value: As soon as the copy of the letter of King Artaxerxes was read to Rehum and Shimshai the secretary and their associates, they went immediately to the Jews in Jerusalem and compelled them by force to stop.

column.name: text
column.value: Thus the work on the house of God in Jerusalem came to a standstill until the second year of the reign of Darius king of Persia.

column.name: text
column.value: Now Haggai the prophet and Zechariah the prophet, a descendant of Iddo, prophesied to the Jews in Judah and Jerusalem in the name of the God of Israel, who was over them.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and Jeshua son of Jozadak set to work to rebuild the house of God in Jerusalem. And the prophets of God were with them, helping them.

column.name: text
column.value: At that time Tattenai, governor of Trans-Euphrates, and Shethar-Bozenai and their associates went to them and asked, "Who authorized you to rebuild this temple and restore this structure?"

column.name: text
column.value: They also asked, "What are the names of the men constructing this building?"

column.name: text
column.value: But the eye of their God was watching over the elders of the Jews, and they were not stopped until a report could go to Darius and his written reply be received.

column.name: text
column.value: This is a copy of the letter that Tattenai, governor of Trans-Euphrates, and Shethar-Bozenai and their associates, the officials of Trans-Euphrates, sent to King Darius.

column.name: text
column.value: The report they sent him read as follows: To King Darius: Cordial greetings.

column.name: text
column.value: The king should know that we went to the district of Judah, to the temple of the great God. The people are building it with large stones and placing the timbers in the walls. The work is being carried on with diligence and is making rapid progress under their direction.

column.name: text
column.value: We questioned the elders and asked them, "Who authorized you to rebuild this temple and restore this structure?"

column.name: text
column.value: We also asked them their names, so that we could write down the names of their leaders for your information.

column.name: text
column.value: This is the answer they gave us: "We are the servants of the God of heaven and earth, and we are rebuilding the temple that was built many years ago, one that a great king of Israel built and finished.

column.name: text
column.value: But because our fathers angered the God of heaven, he handed them over to Nebuchadnezzar the Chaldean, king of Babylon, who destroyed this temple and deported the people to Babylon.

column.name: text
column.value: "However, in the first year of Cyrus king of Babylon, King Cyrus issued a decree to rebuild this house of God.

column.name: text
column.value: He even removed from the temple of Babylon the gold and silver articles of the house of God, which Nebuchadnezzar had taken from the temple in Jerusalem and brought to the temple in Babylon. "Then King Cyrus gave them to a man named Sheshbazzar, whom he had appointed governor,

column.name: text
column.value: and he told him, 'Take these articles and go and deposit them in the temple in Jerusalem. And rebuild the house of God on its site.'

column.name: text
column.value: So this Sheshbazzar came and laid the foundations of the house of God in Jerusalem. From that day to the present it has been under construction but is not yet finished."

column.name: text
column.value: Now if it pleases the king, let a search be made in the royal archives of Babylon to see if King Cyrus did in fact issue a decree to rebuild this house of God in Jerusalem. Then let the king send us his decision in this matter.

column.name: text
column.value: After all that Hezekiah had so faithfully done, Sennacherib king of Assyria came and invaded Judah. He laid siege to the fortified cities, thinking to conquer them for himself.

column.name: text
column.value: When Hezekiah saw that Sennacherib had come and that he intended to make war on Jerusalem,

column.name: text
column.value: he consulted with his officials and military staff about blocking off the water from the springs outside the city, and they helped him.

column.name: text
column.value: A large force of men assembled, and they blocked all the springs and the stream that flowed through the land. "Why should the kings of Assyria come and find plenty of water?" they said.

column.name: text
column.value: Then he worked hard repairing all the broken sections of the wall and building towers on it. He built another wall outside that one and reinforced the supporting terraces of the City of David. He also made large numbers of weapons and shields.

column.name: text
column.value: He appointed military officers over the people and assembled them before him in the square at the city gate and encouraged them with these words:

column.name: text
column.value: "Be strong and courageous. Do not be afraid or discouraged because of the king of Assyria and the vast army with him, for there is a greater power with us than with him.

column.name: text
column.value: With him is only the arm of flesh, but with us is the LORD our God to help us and to fight our battles." And the people gained confidence from what Hezekiah the king of Judah said.

column.name: text
column.value: Later, when Sennacherib king of Assyria and all his forces were laying siege to Lachish, he sent his officers to Jerusalem with this message for Hezekiah king of Judah and for all the people of Judah who were there:

column.name: text
column.value: "This is what Sennacherib king of Assyria says: On what are you basing your confidence, that you remain in Jerusalem under siege?

column.name: text
column.value: When Hezekiah says, 'The LORD our God will save us from the hand of the king of Assyria,' he is misleading you, to let you die of hunger and thirst.

column.name: text
column.value: Did not Hezekiah himself remove this god's high places and altars, saying to Judah and Jerusalem, 'You must worship before one altar and burn sacrifices on it'?

column.name: text
column.value: "Do you not know what I and my fathers have done to all the peoples of the other lands? Were the gods of those nations ever able to deliver their land from my hand?

column.name: text
column.value: Who of all the gods of these nations that my fathers destroyed has been able to save his people from me? How then can your god deliver you from my hand?

column.name: text
column.value: Now do not let Hezekiah deceive you and mislead you like this. Do not believe him, for no god of any nation or kingdom has been able to deliver his people from my hand or the hand of my fathers. How much less will your god deliver you from my hand!"

column.name: text
column.value: Sennacherib's officers spoke further against the LORD God and against his servant Hezekiah.

column.name: text
column.value: The king also wrote letters insulting the LORD, the God of Israel, and saying this against him: "Just as the gods of the peoples of the other lands did not rescue their people from my hand, so the god of Hezekiah will not rescue his people from my hand."

column.name: text
column.value: Then they called out in Hebrew to the people of Jerusalem who were on the wall, to terrify them and make them afraid in order to capture the city.

column.name: text
column.value: They spoke about the God of Jerusalem as they did about the gods of the other peoples of the world--the work of men's hands.

column.name: text
column.value: King Hezekiah and the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz cried out in prayer to heaven about this.

column.name: text
column.value: And the LORD sent an angel, who annihilated all the fighting men and the leaders and officers in the camp of the Assyrian king. So he withdrew to his own land in disgrace. And when he went into the temple of his god, some of his sons cut him down with the sword.

column.name: text
column.value: So the LORD saved Hezekiah and the people of Jerusalem from the hand of Sennacherib king of Assyria and from the hand of all others. He took care of them on every side.

column.name: text
column.value: Many brought offerings to Jerusalem for the LORD and valuable gifts for Hezekiah king of Judah. From then on he was highly regarded by all the nations.

column.name: text
column.value: In those days Hezekiah became ill and was at the point of death. He prayed to the LORD, who answered him and gave him a miraculous sign.

column.name: text
column.value: But Hezekiah's heart was proud and he did not respond to the kindness shown him; therefore the LORD'S wrath was on him and on Judah and Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Hezekiah repented of the pride of his heart, as did the people of Jerusalem; therefore the LORD'S wrath did not come upon them during the days of Hezekiah.

column.name: text
column.value: Hezekiah had very great riches and honor, and he made treasuries for his silver and gold and for his precious stones, spices, shields and all kinds of valuables.

column.name: text
column.value: He also made buildings to store the harvest of grain, new wine and oil; and he made stalls for various kinds of cattle, and pens for the flocks.

column.name: text
column.value: He built villages and acquired great numbers of flocks and herds, for God had given him very great riches.

column.name: text
column.value: It was Hezekiah who blocked the upper outlet of the Gihon spring and channeled the water down to the west side of the City of David. He succeeded in everything he undertook.

column.name: text
column.value: But when envoys were sent by the rulers of Babylon to ask him about the miraculous sign that had occurred in the land, God left him to test him and to know everything that was in his heart.

column.name: text
column.value: The other events of Hezekiah's reign and his acts of devotion are written in the vision of the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz in the book of the kings of Judah and Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: Hezekiah rested with his fathers and was buried on the hill where the tombs of David's descendants are. All Judah and the people of Jerusalem honored him when he died. And Manasseh his son succeeded him as king.

column.name: text
column.value: King Darius then issued an order, and they searched in the archives stored in the treasury at Babylon.

column.name: text
column.value: A scroll was found in the citadel of Ecbatana in the province of Media, and this was written on it: Memorandum:

column.name: text
column.value: In the first year of King Cyrus, the king issued a decree concerning the temple of God in Jerusalem: Let the temple be rebuilt as a place to present sacrifices, and let its foundations be laid. It is to be ninety feet high and ninety feet wide,

column.name: text
column.value: with three courses of large stones and one of timbers. The costs are to be paid by the royal treasury.

column.name: text
column.value: Also, the gold and silver articles of the house of God, which Nebuchadnezzar took from the temple in Jerusalem and brought to Babylon, are to be returned to their places in the temple in Jerusalem; they are to be deposited in the house of God.

column.name: text
column.value: Now then, Tattenai, governor of Trans-Euphrates, and Shethar-Bozenai and you, their fellow officials of that province, stay away from there.

column.name: text
column.value: Do not interfere with the work on this temple of God. Let the governor of the Jews and the Jewish elders rebuild this house of God on its site.

column.name: text
column.value: Moreover, I hereby decree what you are to do for these elders of the Jews in the construction of this house of God: The expenses of these men are to be fully paid out of the royal treasury, from the revenues of Trans-Euphrates, so that the work will not stop.

column.name: text
column.value: Whatever is needed--young bulls, rams, male lambs for burnt offerings to the God of heaven, and wheat, salt, wine and oil, as requested by the priests in Jerusalem--must be given them daily without fail,

column.name: text
column.value: so that they may offer sacrifices pleasing to the God of heaven and pray for the well-being of the king and his sons.

column.name: text
column.value: Furthermore, I decree that if anyone changes this edict, a beam is to be pulled from his house and he is to be lifted up and impaled on it. And for this crime his house is to be made a pile of rubble.

column.name: text
column.value: May God, who has caused his Name to dwell there, overthrow any king or people who lifts a hand to change this decree or to destroy this temple in Jerusalem. I Darius have decreed it. Let it be carried out with diligence.

column.name: text
column.value: Then, because of the decree King Darius had sent, Tattenai, governor of Trans-Euphrates, and Shethar-Bozenai and their associates carried it out with diligence.

column.name: text
column.value: So the elders of the Jews continued to build and prosper under the preaching of Haggai the prophet and Zechariah, a descendant of Iddo. They finished building the temple according to the command of the God of Israel and the decrees of Cyrus, Darius and Artaxerxes, kings of Persia.

column.name: text
column.value: The temple was completed on the third day of the month Adar, in the sixth year of the reign of King Darius.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the people of Israel--the priests, the Levites and the rest of the exiles--celebrated the dedication of the house of God with joy.

column.name: text
column.value: For the dedication of this house of God they offered a hundred bulls, two hundred rams, four hundred male lambs and, as a sin offering for all Israel, twelve male goats, one for each of the tribes of Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: And they installed the priests in their divisions and the Levites in their groups for the service of God at Jerusalem, according to what is written in the Book of Moses.

column.name: text
column.value: On the fourteenth day of the first month, the exiles celebrated the Passover.

column.name: text
column.value: The priests and Levites had purified themselves and were all ceremonially clean. The Levites slaughtered the Passover lamb for all the exiles, for their brothers the priests and for themselves.

column.name: text
column.value: So the Israelites who had returned from the exile ate it, together with all who had separated themselves from the unclean practices of their Gentile neighbors in order to seek the LORD, the God of Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: For seven days they celebrated with joy the Feast of Unleavened Bread, because the LORD had filled them with joy by changing the attitude of the king of Assyria, so that he assisted them in the work on the house of God, the God of Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: After these things, during the reign of Artaxerxes king of Persia, Ezra son of Seraiah, the son of Azariah, the son of Hilkiah,

column.name: text
column.value: the son of Shallum, the son of Zadok, the son of Ahitub,

column.name: text
column.value: the son of Amariah, the son of Azariah, the son of Meraioth,

column.name: text
column.value: the son of Zerahiah, the son of Uzzi, the son of Bukki,

column.name: text
column.value: the son of Abishua, the son of Phinehas, the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the chief priest--

column.name: text
column.value: this Ezra came up from Babylon. He was a teacher well versed in the Law of Moses, which the LORD, the God of Israel, had given. The king had granted him everything he asked, for the hand of the LORD his God was on him.

column.name: text
column.value: Some of the Israelites, including priests, Levites, singers, gatekeepers and temple servants, also came up to Jerusalem in the seventh year of King Artaxerxes.

column.name: text
column.value: Ezra arrived in Jerusalem in the fifth month of the seventh year of the king.

column.name: text
column.value: He had begun his journey from Babylon on the first day of the first month, and he arrived in Jerusalem on the first day of the fifth month, for the gracious hand of his God was on him.

column.name: text
column.value: For Ezra had devoted himself to the study and observance of the Law of the LORD, and to teaching its decrees and laws in Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: This is a copy of the letter King Artaxerxes had given to Ezra the priest and teacher, a man learned in matters concerning the commands and decrees of the LORD for Israel:

column.name: text
column.value: Artaxerxes, king of kings, To Ezra the priest, a teacher of the Law of the God of heaven: Greetings.

column.name: text
column.value: Now I decree that any of the Israelites in my kingdom, including priests and Levites, who wish to go to Jerusalem with you, may go.

column.name: text
column.value: You are sent by the king and his seven advisers to inquire about Judah and Jerusalem with regard to the Law of your God, which is in your hand.

column.name: text
column.value: Moreover, you are to take with you the silver and gold that the king and his advisers have freely given to the God of Israel, whose dwelling is in Jerusalem,

column.name: text
column.value: together with all the silver and gold you may obtain from the province of Babylon, as well as the freewill offerings of the people and priests for the temple of their God in Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: With this money be sure to buy bulls, rams and male lambs, together with their grain offerings and drink offerings, and sacrifice them on the altar of the temple of your God in Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: You and your brother Jews may then do whatever seems best with the rest of the silver and gold, in accordance with the will of your God.

column.name: text
column.value: Deliver to the God of Jerusalem all the articles entrusted to you for worship in the temple of your God.

column.name: text
column.value: And anything else needed for the temple of your God that you may have occasion to supply, you may provide from the royal treasury.

column.name: text
column.value: Now I, King Artaxerxes, order all the treasurers of Trans-Euphrates to provide with diligence whatever Ezra the priest, a teacher of the Law of the God of heaven, may ask of you--

column.name: text
column.value: up to a hundred talents of silver, a hundred cors of wheat, a hundred baths of wine, a hundred baths of olive oil, and salt without limit.

column.name: text
column.value: Whatever the God of heaven has prescribed, let it be done with diligence for the temple of the God of heaven. Why should there be wrath against the realm of the king and of his sons?

column.name: text
column.value: You are also to know that you have no authority to impose taxes, tribute or duty on any of the priests, Levites, singers, gatekeepers, temple servants or other workers at this house of God.

column.name: text
column.value: And you, Ezra, in accordance with the wisdom of your God, which you possess, appoint magistrates and judges to administer justice to all the people of Trans-Euphrates--all who know the laws of your God. And you are to teach any who do not know them.

column.name: text
column.value: Whoever does not obey the law of your God and the law of the king must surely be punished by death, banishment, confiscation of property, or imprisonment.

column.name: text
column.value: Praise be to the LORD, the God of our fathers, who has put it into the king's heart to bring honor to the house of the LORD in Jerusalem in this way

column.name: text
column.value: and who has extended his good favor to me before the king and his advisers and all the king's powerful officials. Because the hand of the LORD my God was on me, I took courage and gathered leading men from Israel to go up with me.

column.name: text
column.value: These are the family heads and those registered with them who came up with me from Babylon during the reign of King Artaxerxes:

column.name: text
column.value: of the descendants of Phinehas, Gershom; of the descendants of Ithamar, Daniel; of the descendants of David, Hattush

column.name: text
column.value: of the descendants of Shecaniah; of the descendants of Parosh, Zechariah, and with him were registered 150 men;

column.name: text
column.value: of the descendants of Pahath-Moab, Eliehoenai son of Zerahiah, and with him 200 men;

column.name: text
column.value: of the descendants of Zattu, Shecaniah son of Jahaziel, and with him 300 men;

column.name: text
column.value: of the descendants of Adin, Ebed son of Jonathan, and with him 50 men;

column.name: text
column.value: of the descendants of Elam, Jeshaiah son of Athaliah, and with him 70 men;

column.name: text
column.value: of the descendants of Shephatiah, Zebadiah son of Michael, and with him 80 men;

column.name: text
column.value: of the descendants of Joab, Obadiah son of Jehiel, and with him 218 men;

column.name: text
column.value: of the descendants of Bani, Shelomith son of Josiphiah, and with him 160 men;

column.name: text
column.value: of the descendants of Bebai, Zechariah son of Bebai, and with him 28 men;

column.name: text
column.value: of the descendants of Azgad, Johanan son of Hakkatan, and with him 110 men;

column.name: text
column.value: of the descendants of Adonikam, the last ones, whose names were Eliphelet, Jeuel and Shemaiah, and with them 60 men;

column.name: text
column.value: of the descendants of Bigvai, Uthai and Zaccur, and with them 70 men.

column.name: text
column.value: I assembled them at the canal that flows toward Ahava, and we camped there three days. When I checked among the people and the priests, I found no Levites there.

column.name: text
column.value: So I summoned Eliezer, Ariel, Shemaiah, Elnathan, Jarib, Elnathan, Nathan, Zechariah and Meshullam, who were leaders, and Joiarib and Elnathan, who were men of learning,

column.name: text
column.value: and I sent them to Iddo, the leader in Casiphia. I told them what to say to Iddo and his kinsmen, the temple servants in Casiphia, so that they might bring attendants to us for the house of our God.

column.name: text
column.value: Because the gracious hand of our God was on us, they brought us Sherebiah, a capable man, from the descendants of Mahli son of Levi, the son of Israel, and Sherebiah's sons and brothers, 18 men;

column.name: text
column.value: and Hashabiah, together with Jeshaiah from the descendants of Merari, and his brothers and nephews, 20 men.

column.name: text
column.value: They also brought 220 of the temple servants--a body that David and the officials had established to assist the Levites. All were registered by name.

column.name: text
column.value: There, by the Ahava Canal, I proclaimed a fast, so that we might humble ourselves before our God and ask him for a safe journey for us and our children, with all our possessions.

column.name: text
column.value: I was ashamed to ask the king for soldiers and horsemen to protect us from enemies on the road, because we had told the king, "The gracious hand of our God is on everyone who looks to him, but his great anger is against all who forsake him."

column.name: text
column.value: So we fasted and petitioned our God about this, and he answered our prayer.

column.name: text
column.value: Then I set apart twelve of the leading priests, together with Sherebiah, Hashabiah and ten of their brothers,

column.name: text
column.value: and I weighed out to them the offering of silver and gold and the articles that the king, his advisers, his officials and all Israel present there had donated for the house of our God.

column.name: text
column.value: I weighed out to them 650 talents of silver, silver articles weighing 100 talents, 100 talents of gold,

column.name: text
column.value: 20 bowls of gold valued at 1,000 darics, and two fine articles of polished bronze, as precious as gold.

column.name: text
column.value: I said to them, "You as well as these articles are consecrated to the LORD. The silver and gold are a freewill offering to the LORD, the God of your fathers.

column.name: text
column.value: Guard them carefully until you weigh them out in the chambers of the house of the LORD in Jerusalem before the leading priests and the Levites and the family heads of Israel."

column.name: text
column.value: Then the priests and Levites received the silver and gold and sacred articles that had been weighed out to be taken to the house of our God in Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: On the twelfth day of the first month we set out from the Ahava Canal to go to Jerusalem. The hand of our God was on us, and he protected us from enemies and bandits along the way.

column.name: text
column.value: So we arrived in Jerusalem, where we rested three days.

column.name: text
column.value: On the fourth day, in the house of our God, we weighed out the silver and gold and the sacred articles into the hands of Meremoth son of Uriah, the priest. Eleazar son of Phinehas was with him, and so were the Levites Jozabad son of Jeshua and Noadiah son of Binnui.

column.name: text
column.value: Everything was accounted for by number and weight, and the entire weight was recorded at that time.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the exiles who had returned from captivity sacrificed burnt offerings to the God of Israel: twelve bulls for all Israel, ninety-six rams, seventy-seven male lambs and, as a sin offering, twelve male goats. All this was a burnt offering to the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: They also delivered the king's orders to the royal satraps and to the governors of Trans-Euphrates, who then gave assistance to the people and to the house of God.

column.name: text
column.value: After these things had been done, the leaders came to me and said, "The people of Israel, including the priests and the Levites, have not kept themselves separate from the neighboring peoples with their detestable practices, like those of the Canaanites, Hittites, Perizzites, Jebusites, Ammonites, Moabites, Egyptians and Amorites.

column.name: text
column.value: They have taken some of their daughters as wives for themselves and their sons, and have mingled the holy race with the peoples around them. And the leaders and officials have led the way in this unfaithfulness."

column.name: text
column.value: When I heard this, I tore my tunic and cloak, pulled hair from my head and beard and sat down appalled.

column.name: text
column.value: Then everyone who trembled at the words of the God of Israel gathered around me because of this unfaithfulness of the exiles. And I sat there appalled until the evening sacrifice.

column.name: text
column.value: Then, at the evening sacrifice, I rose from my self-abasement, with my tunic and cloak torn, and fell on my knees with my hands spread out to the LORD my God

column.name: text
column.value: and prayed: "O my God, I am too ashamed and disgraced to lift up my face to you, my God, because our sins are higher than our heads and our guilt has reached to the heavens.

column.name: text
column.value: From the days of our forefathers until now, our guilt has been great. Because of our sins, we and our kings and our priests have been subjected to the sword and captivity, to pillage and humiliation at the hand of foreign kings, as it is today.

column.name: text
column.value: "But now, for a brief moment, the LORD our God has been gracious in leaving us a remnant and giving us a firm place in his sanctuary, and so our God gives light to our eyes and a little relief in our bondage.

column.name: text
column.value: Though we are slaves, our God has not deserted us in our bondage. He has shown us kindness in the sight of the kings of Persia: He has granted us new life to rebuild the house of our God and repair its ruins, and he has given us a wall of protection in Judah and Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: "But now, O our God, what can we say after this? For we have disregarded the commands

column.name: text
column.value: you gave through your servants the prophets when you said: 'The land you are entering to possess is a land polluted by the corruption of its peoples. By their detestable practices they have filled it with their impurity from one end to the other.

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore, do not give your daughters in marriage to their sons or take their daughters for your sons. Do not seek a treaty of friendship with them at any time, that you may be strong and eat the good things of the land and leave it to your children as an everlasting inheritance.'

column.name: text
column.value: "What has happened to us is a result of our evil deeds and our great guilt, and yet, our God, you have punished us less than our sins have deserved and have given us a remnant like this.

column.name: text
column.value: Shall we again break your commands and intermarry with the peoples who commit such detestable practices? Would you not be angry enough with us to destroy us, leaving us no remnant or survivor?

column.name: text
column.value: O LORD, God of Israel, you are righteous! We are left this day as a remnant. Here we are before you in our guilt, though because of it not one of us can stand in your presence."

column.name: text
column.value: While Ezra was praying and confessing, weeping and throwing himself down before the house of God, a large crowd of Israelites--men, women and children--gathered around him. They too wept bitterly.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Shecaniah son of Jehiel, one of the descendants of Elam, said to Ezra, "We have been unfaithful to our God by marrying foreign women from the peoples around us. But in spite of this, there is still hope for Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: Now let us make a covenant before our God to send away all these women and their children, in accordance with the counsel of my lord and of those who fear the commands of our God. Let it be done according to the Law.

column.name: text
column.value: Rise up; this matter is in your hands. We will support you, so take courage and do it."

column.name: text
column.value: So Ezra rose up and put the leading priests and Levites and all Israel under oath to do what had been suggested. And they took the oath.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Ezra withdrew from before the house of God and went to the room of Jehohanan son of Eliashib. While he was there, he ate no food and drank no water, because he continued to mourn over the unfaithfulness of the exiles.

column.name: text
column.value: A proclamation was then issued throughout Judah and Jerusalem for all the exiles to assemble in Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: Anyone who failed to appear within three days would forfeit all his property, in accordance with the decision of the officials and elders, and would himself be expelled from the assembly of the exiles.

column.name: text
column.value: Within the three days, all the men of Judah and Benjamin had gathered in Jerusalem. And on the twentieth day of the ninth month, all the people were sitting in the square before the house of God, greatly distressed by the occasion and because of the rain.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Ezra the priest stood up and said to them, "You have been unfaithful; you have married foreign women, adding to Israel's guilt.

column.name: text
column.value: Now make confession to the LORD, the God of your fathers, and do his will. Separate yourselves from the peoples around you and from your foreign wives."

column.name: text
column.value: The whole assembly responded with a loud voice: "You are right! We must do as you say.

column.name: text
column.value: But there are many people here and it is the rainy season; so we cannot stand outside. Besides, this matter cannot be taken care of in a day or two, because we have sinned greatly in this thing.

column.name: text
column.value: Let our officials act for the whole assembly. Then let everyone in our towns who has married a foreign woman come at a set time, along with the elders and judges of each town, until the fierce anger of our God in this matter is turned away from us."

column.name: text
column.value: Only Jonathan son of Asahel and Jahzeiah son of Tikvah, supported by Meshullam and Shabbethai the Levite, opposed this.

column.name: text
column.value: So the exiles did as was proposed. Ezra the priest selected men who were family heads, one from each family division, and all of them designated by name. On the first day of the tenth month they sat down to investigate the cases,

column.name: text
column.value: and by the first day of the first month they finished dealing with all the men who had married foreign women.

column.name: text
column.value: Among the descendants of the priests, the following had married foreign women: From the descendants of Jeshua son of Jozadak, and his brothers: Maaseiah, Eliezer, Jarib and Gedaliah.

column.name: text
column.value: (They all gave their hands in pledge to put away their wives, and for their guilt they each presented a ram from the flock as a guilt offering.)

column.name: text
column.value: From the descendants of Immer: Hanani and Zebadiah.

column.name: text
column.value: From the descendants of Harim: Maaseiah, Elijah, Shemaiah, Jehiel and Uzziah.

column.name: text
column.value: From the descendants of Pashhur: Elioenai, Maaseiah, Ishmael, Nethanel, Jozabad and Elasah.

column.name: text
column.value: Among the Levites: Jozabad, Shimei, Kelaiah (that is, Kelita), Pethahiah, Judah and Eliezer.

column.name: text
column.value: From the singers: Eliashib. From the gatekeepers: Shallum, Telem and Uri.

column.name: text
column.value: And among the other Israelites: From the descendants of Parosh: Ramiah, Izziah, Malkijah, Mijamin, Eleazar, Malkijah and Benaiah.

column.name: text
column.value: From the descendants of Elam: Mattaniah, Zechariah, Jehiel, Abdi, Jeremoth and Elijah.

column.name: text
column.value: From the descendants of Zattu: Elioenai, Eliashib, Mattaniah, Jeremoth, Zabad and Aziza.

column.name: text
column.value: From the descendants of Bebai: Jehohanan, Hananiah, Zabbai and Athlai.

column.name: text
column.value: From the descendants of Bani: Meshullam, Malluch, Adaiah, Jashub, Sheal and Jeremoth.

column.name: text
column.value: From the descendants of Pahath-Moab: Adna, Kelal, Benaiah, Maaseiah, Mattaniah, Bezalel, Binnui and Manasseh.

column.name: text
column.value: From the descendants of Harim: Eliezer, Ishijah, Malkijah, Shemaiah, Shimeon,

column.name: text
column.value: Benjamin, Malluch and Shemariah.

column.name: text
column.value: From the descendants of Hashum: Mattenai, Mattattah, Zabad, Eliphelet, Jeremai, Manasseh and Shimei.

column.name: text
column.value: From the descendants of Bani: Maadai, Amram, Uel,

column.name: text
column.value: Benaiah, Bedeiah, Keluhi,

column.name: text
column.value: Vaniah, Meremoth, Eliashib,

column.name: text
column.value: Mattaniah, Mattenai and Jaasu.

column.name: text
column.value: From the descendants of Binnui: Shimei,

column.name: text
column.value: Shelemiah, Nathan, Adaiah,

column.name: text
column.value: Macnadebai, Shashai, Sharai,

column.name: text
column.value: Azarel, Shelemiah, Shemariah,

column.name: text
column.value: Shallum, Amariah and Joseph.

column.name: text
column.value: From the descendants of Nebo: Jeiel, Mattithiah, Zabad, Zebina, Jaddai, Joel and Benaiah.

column.name: text
column.value: All these had married foreign women, and some of them had children by these wives.

column.name: text
column.value: The words of Nehemiah son of Hacaliah: In the month of Kislev in the twentieth year, while I was in the citadel of Susa,

column.name: text
column.value: Hanani, one of my brothers, came from Judah with some other men, and I questioned them about the Jewish remnant that survived the exile, and also about Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: They said to me, "Those who survived the exile and are back in the province are in great trouble and disgrace. The wall of Jerusalem is broken down, and its gates have been burned with fire."

column.name: text
column.value: When I heard these things, I sat down and wept. For some days I mourned and fasted and prayed before the God of heaven.

column.name: text
column.value: Then I said: "O LORD, God of heaven, the great and awesome God, who keeps his covenant of love with those who love him and obey his commands,

column.name: text
column.value: let your ear be attentive and your eyes open to hear the prayer your servant is praying before you day and night for your servants, the people of Israel. I confess the sins we Israelites, including myself and my father's house, have committed against you.

column.name: text
column.value: We have acted very wickedly toward you. We have not obeyed the commands, decrees and laws you gave your servant Moses.

column.name: text
column.value: "Remember the instruction you gave your servant Moses, saying, 'If you are unfaithful, I will scatter you among the nations,

column.name: text
column.value: but if you return to me and obey my commands, then even if your exiled people are at the farthest horizon, I will gather them from there and bring them to the place I have chosen as a dwelling for my Name.'

column.name: text
column.value: "They are your servants and your people, whom you redeemed by your great strength and your mighty hand.

column.name: text
column.value: O Lord, let your ear be attentive to the prayer of this your servant and to the prayer of your servants who delight in revering your name. Give your servant success today by granting him favor in the presence of this man." I was cupbearer to the king.

column.name: text
column.value: Eliashib the high priest and his fellow priests went to work and rebuilt the Sheep Gate. They dedicated it and set its doors in place, building as far as the Tower of the Hundred, which they dedicated, and as far as the Tower of Hananel.

column.name: text
column.value: The men of Jericho built the adjoining section, and Zaccur son of Imri built next to them.

column.name: text
column.value: The Fish Gate was rebuilt by the sons of Hassenaah. They laid its beams and put its doors and bolts and bars in place.

column.name: text
column.value: Meremoth son of Uriah, the son of Hakkoz, repaired the next section. Next to him Meshullam son of Berekiah, the son of Meshezabel, made repairs, and next to him Zadok son of Baana also made repairs.

column.name: text
column.value: The next section was repaired by the men of Tekoa, but their nobles would not put their shoulders to the work under their supervisors.

column.name: text
column.value: The Jeshanah Gate was repaired by Joiada son of Paseah and Meshullam son of Besodeiah. They laid its beams and put its doors and bolts and bars in place.

column.name: text
column.value: Next to them, repairs were made by men from Gibeon and Mizpah--Melatiah of Gibeon and Jadon of Meronoth--places under the authority of the governor of Trans-Euphrates.

column.name: text
column.value: Uzziel son of Harhaiah, one of the goldsmiths, repaired the next section; and Hananiah, one of the perfume-makers, made repairs next to that. They restored Jerusalem as far as the Broad Wall.

column.name: text
column.value: Rephaiah son of Hur, ruler of a half-district of Jerusalem, repaired the next section.

column.name: text
column.value: Adjoining this, Jedaiah son of Harumaph made repairs opposite his house, and Hattush son of Hashabneiah made repairs next to him.

column.name: text
column.value: Malkijah son of Harim and Hasshub son of Pahath-Moab repaired another section and the Tower of the Ovens.

column.name: text
column.value: Shallum son of Hallohesh, ruler of a half-district of Jerusalem, repaired the next section with the help of his daughters.

column.name: text
column.value: The Valley Gate was repaired by Hanun and the residents of Zanoah. They rebuilt it and put its doors and bolts and bars in place. They also repaired five hundred yards of the wall as far as the Dung Gate.

column.name: text
column.value: The Dung Gate was repaired by Malkijah son of Recab, ruler of the district of Beth Hakkerem. He rebuilt it and put its doors and bolts and bars in place.

column.name: text
column.value: The Fountain Gate was repaired by Shallun son of Col-Hozeh, ruler of the district of Mizpah. He rebuilt it, roofing it over and putting its doors and bolts and bars in place. He also repaired the wall of the Pool of Siloam, by the King's Garden, as far as the steps going down from the City of David.

column.name: text
column.value: Beyond him, Nehemiah son of Azbuk, ruler of a half-district of Beth Zur, made repairs up to a point opposite the tombs of David, as far as the artificial pool and the House of the Heroes.

column.name: text
column.value: Next to him, the repairs were made by the Levites under Rehum son of Bani. Beside him, Hashabiah, ruler of half the district of Keilah, carried out repairs for his district.

column.name: text
column.value: Next to him, the repairs were made by their countrymen under Binnui son of Henadad, ruler of the other half-district of Keilah.

column.name: text
column.value: Next to him, Ezer son of Jeshua, ruler of Mizpah, repaired another section, from a point facing the ascent to the armory as far as the angle.

column.name: text
column.value: Next to him, Baruch son of Zabbai zealously repaired another section, from the angle to the entrance of the house of Eliashib the high priest.

column.name: text
column.value: Next to him, Meremoth son of Uriah, the son of Hakkoz, repaired another section, from the entrance of Eliashib's house to the end of it.

column.name: text
column.value: The repairs next to him were made by the priests from the surrounding region.

column.name: text
column.value: Beyond them, Benjamin and Hasshub made repairs in front of their house; and next to them, Azariah son of Maaseiah, the son of Ananiah, made repairs beside his house.

column.name: text
column.value: Next to him, Binnui son of Henadad repaired another section, from Azariah's house to the angle and the corner,

column.name: text
column.value: and Palal son of Uzai worked opposite the angle and the tower projecting from the upper palace near the court of the guard. Next to him, Pedaiah son of Parosh

column.name: text
column.value: and the temple servants living on the hill of Ophel made repairs up to a point opposite the Water Gate toward the east and the projecting tower.

column.name: text
column.value: Next to them, the men of Tekoa repaired another section, from the great projecting tower to the wall of Ophel.

column.name: text
column.value: Above the Horse Gate, the priests made repairs, each in front of his own house.

column.name: text
column.value: Next to them, Zadok son of Immer made repairs opposite his house. Next to him, Shemaiah son of Shecaniah, the guard at the East Gate, made repairs.

column.name: text
column.value: Next to him, Hananiah son of Shelemiah, and Hanun, the sixth son of Zalaph, repaired another section. Next to them, Meshullam son of Berekiah made repairs opposite his living quarters.

column.name: text
column.value: Next to him, Malkijah, one of the goldsmiths, made repairs as far as the house of the temple servants and the merchants, opposite the Inspection Gate, and as far as the room above the corner;

column.name: text
column.value: and between the room above the corner and the Sheep Gate the goldsmiths and merchants made repairs.

column.name: text
column.value: When Sanballat heard that we were rebuilding the wall, he became angry and was greatly incensed. He ridiculed the Jews,

column.name: text
column.value: and in the presence of his associates and the army of Samaria, he said, "What are those feeble Jews doing? Will they restore their wall? Will they offer sacrifices? Will they finish in a day? Can they bring the stones back to life from those heaps of rubble--burned as they are?"

column.name: text
column.value: Tobiah the Ammonite, who was at his side, said, "What they are building--if even a fox climbed up on it, he would break down their wall of stones!"

column.name: text
column.value: Hear us, O our God, for we are despised. Turn their insults back on their own heads. Give them over as plunder in a land of captivity.

column.name: text
column.value: Do not cover up their guilt or blot out their sins from your sight, for they have thrown insults in the face of the builders.

column.name: text
column.value: So we rebuilt the wall till all of it reached half its height, for the people worked with all their heart.

column.name: text
column.value: But when Sanballat, Tobiah, the Arabs, the Ammonites and the men of Ashdod heard that the repairs to Jerusalem's walls had gone ahead and that the gaps were being closed, they were very angry.

column.name: text
column.value: They all plotted together to come and fight against Jerusalem and stir up trouble against it.

column.name: text
column.value: But we prayed to our God and posted a guard day and night to meet this threat.

column.name: text
column.value: Meanwhile, the people in Judah said, "The strength of the laborers is giving out, and there is so much rubble that we cannot rebuild the wall."

column.name: text
column.value: Also our enemies said, "Before they know it or see us, we will be right there among them and will kill them and put an end to the work."

column.name: text
column.value: Then the Jews who lived near them came and told us ten times over, "Wherever you turn, they will attack us."

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore I stationed some of the people behind the lowest points of the wall at the exposed places, posting them by families, with their swords, spears and bows.

column.name: text
column.value: After I looked things over, I stood up and said to the nobles, the officials and the rest of the people, "Don't be afraid of them. Remember the Lord, who is great and awesome, and fight for your brothers, your sons and your daughters, your wives and your homes."

column.name: text
column.value: When our enemies heard that we were aware of their plot and that God had frustrated it, we all returned to the wall, each to his own work.

column.name: text
column.value: From that day on, half of my men did the work, while the other half were equipped with spears, shields, bows and armor. The officers posted themselves behind all the people of Judah

column.name: text
column.value: who were building the wall. Those who carried materials did their work with one hand and held a weapon in the other,

column.name: text
column.value: and each of the builders wore his sword at his side as he worked. But the man who sounded the trumpet stayed with me.

column.name: text
column.value: Then I said to the nobles, the officials and the rest of the people, "The work is extensive and spread out, and we are widely separated from each other along the wall.

column.name: text
column.value: Wherever you hear the sound of the trumpet, join us there. Our God will fight for us!"

column.name: text
column.value: So we continued the work with half the men holding spears, from the first light of dawn till the stars came out.

column.name: text
column.value: At that time I also said to the people, "Have every man and his helper stay inside Jerusalem at night, so they can serve us as guards by night and workmen by day."

column.name: text
column.value: Neither I nor my brothers nor my men nor the guards with me took off our clothes; each had his weapon, even when he went for water.

column.name: text
column.value: In the month of Nisan in the twentieth year of King Artaxerxes, when wine was brought for him, I took the wine and gave it to the king. I had not been sad in his presence before;

column.name: text
column.value: so the king asked me, "Why does your face look so sad when you are not ill? This can be nothing but sadness of heart." I was very much afraid,

column.name: text
column.value: but I said to the king, "May the king live forever! Why should my face not look sad when the city where my fathers are buried lies in ruins, and its gates have been destroyed by fire?"

column.name: text
column.value: The king said to me, "What is it you want?" Then I prayed to the God of heaven,

column.name: text
column.value: and I answered the king, "If it pleases the king and if your servant has found favor in his sight, let him send me to the city in Judah where my fathers are buried so that I can rebuild it."

column.name: text
column.value: Then the king, with the queen sitting beside him, asked me, "How long will your journey take, and when will you get back?" It pleased the king to send me; so I set a time.

column.name: text
column.value: I also said to him, "If it pleases the king, may I have letters to the governors of Trans-Euphrates, so that they will provide me safe-conduct until I arrive in Judah?

column.name: text
column.value: And may I have a letter to Asaph, keeper of the king's forest, so he will give me timber to make beams for the gates of the citadel by the temple and for the city wall and for the residence I will occupy?" And because the gracious hand of my God was upon me, the king granted my requests.

column.name: text
column.value: So I went to the governors of Trans-Euphrates and gave them the king's letters. The king had also sent army officers and cavalry with me.

column.name: text
column.value: When Sanballat the Horonite and Tobiah the Ammonite official heard about this, they were very much disturbed that someone had come to promote the welfare of the Israelites.

column.name: text
column.value: I went to Jerusalem, and after staying there three days

column.name: text
column.value: I set out during the night with a few men. I had not told anyone what my God had put in my heart to do for Jerusalem. There were no mounts with me except the one I was riding on.

column.name: text
column.value: By night I went out through the Valley Gate toward the Jackal Well and the Dung Gate, examining the walls of Jerusalem, which had been broken down, and its gates, which had been destroyed by fire.

column.name: text
column.value: Then I moved on toward the Fountain Gate and the King's Pool, but there was not enough room for my mount to get through;

column.name: text
column.value: so I went up the valley by night, examining the wall. Finally, I turned back and reentered through the Valley Gate.

column.name: text
column.value: The officials did not know where I had gone or what I was doing, because as yet I had said nothing to the Jews or the priests or nobles or officials or any others who would be doing the work.

column.name: text
column.value: Then I said to them, "You see the trouble we are in: Jerusalem lies in ruins, and its gates have been burned with fire. Come, let us rebuild the wall of Jerusalem, and we will no longer be in disgrace."

column.name: text
column.value: I also told them about the gracious hand of my God upon me and what the king had said to me. They replied, "Let us start rebuilding." So they began this good work.

column.name: text
column.value: But when Sanballat the Horonite, Tobiah the Ammonite official and Geshem the Arab heard about it, they mocked and ridiculed us. "What is this you are doing?" they asked. "Are you rebelling against the king?"

column.name: text
column.value: I answered them by saying, "The God of heaven will give us success. We his servants will start rebuilding, but as for you, you have no share in Jerusalem or any claim or historic right to it."

column.name: text
column.value: Now the men and their wives raised a great outcry against their Jewish brothers.

column.name: text
column.value: Some were saying, "We and our sons and daughters are numerous; in order for us to eat and stay alive, we must get grain."

column.name: text
column.value: Others were saying, "We are mortgaging our fields, our vineyards and our homes to get grain during the famine."

column.name: text
column.value: Still others were saying, "We have had to borrow money to pay the king's tax on our fields and vineyards.

column.name: text
column.value: Although we are of the same flesh and blood as our countrymen and though our sons are as good as theirs, yet we have to subject our sons and daughters to slavery. Some of our daughters have already been enslaved, but we are powerless, because our fields and our vineyards belong to others."

column.name: text
column.value: When I heard their outcry and these charges, I was very angry.

column.name: text
column.value: I pondered them in my mind and then accused the nobles and officials. I told them, "You are exacting usury from your own countrymen!" So I called together a large meeting to deal with them

column.name: text
column.value: and said: "As far as possible, we have bought back our Jewish brothers who were sold to the Gentiles. Now you are selling your brothers, only for them to be sold back to us!" They kept quiet, because they could find nothing to say.

column.name: text
column.value: So I continued, "What you are doing is not right. Shouldn't you walk in the fear of our God to avoid the reproach of our Gentile enemies?

column.name: text
column.value: I and my brothers and my men are also lending the people money and grain. But let the exacting of usury stop!

column.name: text
column.value: Give back to them immediately their fields, vineyards, olive groves and houses, and also the usury you are charging them--the hundredth part of the money, grain, new wine and oil."

column.name: text
column.value: "We will give it back," they said. "And we will not demand anything more from them. We will do as you say." Then I summoned the priests and made the nobles and officials take an oath to do what they had promised.

column.name: text
column.value: I also shook out the folds of my robe and said, "In this way may God shake out of his house and possessions every man who does not keep this promise. So may such a man be shaken out and emptied!" At this the whole assembly said, "Amen," and praised the LORD. And the people did as they had promised.

column.name: text
column.value: Moreover, from the twentieth year of King Artaxerxes, when I was appointed to be their governor in the land of Judah, until his thirty-second year--twelve years--neither I nor my brothers ate the food allotted to the governor.

column.name: text
column.value: But the earlier governors--those preceding me--placed a heavy burden on the people and took forty shekels of silver from them in addition to food and wine. Their assistants also lorded it over the people. But out of reverence for God I did not act like that.

column.name: text
column.value: Instead, I devoted myself to the work on this wall. All my men were assembled there for the work; we did not acquire any land.

column.name: text
column.value: Furthermore, a hundred and fifty Jews and officials ate at my table, as well as those who came to us from the surrounding nations.

column.name: text
column.value: Each day one ox, six choice sheep and some poultry were prepared for me, and every ten days an abundant supply of wine of all kinds. In spite of all this, I never demanded the food allotted to the governor, because the demands were heavy on these people.

column.name: text
column.value: Remember me with favor, O my God, for all I have done for these people.

column.name: text
column.value: After the wall had been rebuilt and I had set the doors in place, the gatekeepers and the singers and the Levites were appointed.

column.name: text
column.value: I put in charge of Jerusalem my brother Hanani, along with Hananiah the commander of the citadel, because he was a man of integrity and feared God more than most men do.

column.name: text
column.value: I said to them, "The gates of Jerusalem are not to be opened until the sun is hot. While the gatekeepers are still on duty, have them shut the doors and bar them. Also appoint residents of Jerusalem as guards, some at their posts and some near their own houses."

column.name: text
column.value: Now the city was large and spacious, but there were few people in it, and the houses had not yet been rebuilt.

column.name: text
column.value: So my God put it into my heart to assemble the nobles, the officials and the common people for registration by families. I found the genealogical record of those who had been the first to return. This is what I found written there:

column.name: text
column.value: These are the people of the province who came up from the captivity of the exiles whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had taken captive (they returned to Jerusalem and Judah, each to his own town,

column.name: text
column.value: in company with Zerubbabel, Jeshua, Nehemiah, Azariah, Raamiah, Nahamani, Mordecai, Bilshan, Mispereth, Bigvai, Nehum and Baanah): The list of the men of Israel:

column.name: text
column.value: The following came up from the towns of Tel Melah, Tel Harsha, Kerub, Addon and Immer, but they could not show that their families were descended from Israel:

column.name: text
column.value: the descendants of Delaiah, Tobiah and Nekoda 642

column.name: text
column.value: And from among the priests: the descendants of Hobaiah, Hakkoz and Barzillai (a man who had married a daughter of Barzillai the Gileadite and was called by that name).

column.name: text
column.value: These searched for their family records, but they could not find them and so were excluded from the priesthood as unclean.

column.name: text
column.value: The governor, therefore, ordered them not to eat any of the most sacred food until there should be a priest ministering with the Urim and Thummim.

column.name: text
column.value: The whole company numbered 42,360,

column.name: text
column.value: besides their 7,337 menservants and maidservants; and they also had 245 men and women singers.

column.name: text
column.value: There were 736 horses, 245 mules,

column.name: text
column.value: 435 camels and 6,720 donkeys.

column.name: text
column.value: Some of the heads of the families contributed to the work. The governor gave to the treasury 1,000 drachmas of gold, 50 bowls and 530 garments for priests.

column.name: text
column.value: Some of the heads of the families gave to the treasury for the work 20,000 drachmas of gold and 2,200 minas of silver.

column.name: text
column.value: The total given by the rest of the people was 20,000 drachmas of gold, 2,000 minas of silver and 67 garments for priests.

column.name: text
column.value: The priests, the Levites, the gatekeepers, the singers and the temple servants, along with certain of the people and the rest of the Israelites, settled in their own towns. When the seventh month came and the Israelites had settled in their towns,

column.name: text
column.value: When word came to Sanballat, Tobiah, Geshem the Arab and the rest of our enemies that I had rebuilt the wall and not a gap was left in it--though up to that time I had not set the doors in the gates--

column.name: text
column.value: Sanballat and Geshem sent me this message: "Come, let us meet together in one of the villages on the plain of Ono." But they were scheming to harm me;

column.name: text
column.value: so I sent messengers to them with this reply: "I am carrying on a great project and cannot go down. Why should the work stop while I leave it and go down to you?"

column.name: text
column.value: Four times they sent me the same message, and each time I gave them the same answer.

column.name: text
column.value: Then, the fifth time, Sanballat sent his aide to me with the same message, and in his hand was an unsealed letter

column.name: text
column.value: in which was written: "It is reported among the nations--and Geshem says it is true--that you and the Jews are plotting to revolt, and therefore you are building the wall. Moreover, according to these reports you are about to become their king

column.name: text
column.value: and have even appointed prophets to make this proclamation about you in Jerusalem: 'There is a king in Judah!' Now this report will get back to the king; so come, let us confer together."

column.name: text
column.value: I sent him this reply: "Nothing like what you are saying is happening; you are just making it up out of your head."

column.name: text
column.value: They were all trying to frighten us, thinking, "Their hands will get too weak for the work, and it will not be completed." But I prayed,"Now strengthen my hands."

column.name: text
column.value: One day I went to the house of Shemaiah son of Delaiah, the son of Mehetabel, who was shut in at his home. He said, "Let us meet in the house of God, inside the temple, and let us close the temple doors, because men are coming to kill you--by night they are coming to kill you."

column.name: text
column.value: But I said, "Should a man like me run away? Or should one like me go into the temple to save his life? I will not go!"

column.name: text
column.value: I realized that God had not sent him, but that he had prophesied against me because Tobiah and Sanballat had hired him.

column.name: text
column.value: He had been hired to intimidate me so that I would commit a sin by doing this, and then they would give me a bad name to discredit me.

column.name: text
column.value: Remember Tobiah and Sanballat, O my God, because of what they have done; remember also the prophetess Noadiah and the rest of the prophets who have been trying to intimidate me.

column.name: text
column.value: So the wall was completed on the twenty-fifth of Elul, in fifty-two days.

column.name: text
column.value: When all our enemies heard about this, all the surrounding nations were afraid and lost their self-confidence, because they realized that this work had been done with the help of our God.

column.name: text
column.value: Also, in those days the nobles of Judah were sending many letters to Tobiah, and replies from Tobiah kept coming to them.

column.name: text
column.value: For many in Judah were under oath to him, since he was son-in-law to Shecaniah son of Arah, and his son Jehohanan had married the daughter of Meshullam son of Berekiah.

column.name: text
column.value: Moreover, they kept reporting to me his good deeds and then telling him what I said. And Tobiah sent letters to intimidate me.

column.name: text
column.value: all the people assembled as one man in the square before the Water Gate. They told Ezra the scribe to bring out the Book of the Law of Moses, which the LORD had commanded for Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: So on the first day of the seventh month Ezra the priest brought the Law before the assembly, which was made up of men and women and all who were able to understand.

column.name: text
column.value: He read it aloud from daybreak till noon as he faced the square before the Water Gate in the presence of the men, women and others who could understand. And all the people listened attentively to the Book of the Law.

column.name: text
column.value: Ezra the scribe stood on a high wooden platform built for the occasion. Beside him on his right stood Mattithiah, Shema, Anaiah, Uriah, Hilkiah and Maaseiah; and on his left were Pedaiah, Mishael, Malkijah, Hashum, Hashbaddanah, Zechariah and Meshullam.

column.name: text
column.value: Ezra opened the book. All the people could see him because he was standing above them; and as he opened it, the people all stood up.

column.name: text
column.value: Ezra praised the LORD, the great God; and all the people lifted their hands and responded, "Amen! Amen!" Then they bowed down and worshiped the LORD with their faces to the ground.

column.name: text
column.value: The Levites--Jeshua, Bani, Sherebiah, Jamin, Akkub, Shabbethai, Hodiah, Maaseiah, Kelita, Azariah, Jozabad, Hanan and Pelaiah--instructed the people in the Law while the people were standing there.

column.name: text
column.value: They read from the Book of the Law of God, making it clear and giving the meaning so that the people could understand what was being read.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Nehemiah the governor, Ezra the priest and scribe, and the Levites who were instructing the people said to them all, "This day is sacred to the LORD your God. Do not mourn or weep." For all the people had been weeping as they listened to the words of the Law.

column.name: text
column.value: Nehemiah said, "Go and enjoy choice food and sweet drinks, and send some to those who have nothing prepared. This day is sacred to our Lord. Do not grieve, for the joy of the LORD is your strength."

column.name: text
column.value: The Levites calmed all the people, saying, "Be still, for this is a sacred day. Do not grieve."

column.name: text
column.value: Then all the people went away to eat and drink, to send portions of food and to celebrate with great joy, because they now understood the words that had been made known to them.

column.name: text
column.value: On the second day of the month, the heads of all the families, along with the priests and the Levites, gathered around Ezra the scribe to give attention to the words of the Law.

column.name: text
column.value: They found written in the Law, which the LORD had commanded through Moses, that the Israelites were to live in booths during the feast of the seventh month

column.name: text
column.value: and that they should proclaim this word and spread it throughout their towns and in Jerusalem: "Go out into the hill country and bring back branches from olive and wild olive trees, and from myrtles, palms and shade trees, to make booths"--as it is written.

column.name: text
