column.value: So the people went out and brought back branches and built themselves booths on their own roofs, in their courtyards, in the courts of the house of God and in the square by the Water Gate and the one by the Gate of Ephraim.

column.name: text
column.value: The whole company that had returned from exile built booths and lived in them. From the days of Joshua son of Nun until that day, the Israelites had not celebrated it like this. And their joy was very great.

column.name: text
column.value: Day after day, from the first day to the last, Ezra read from the Book of the Law of God. They celebrated the feast for seven days, and on the eighth day, in accordance with the regulation, there was an assembly.

column.name: text
column.value: On the twenty-fourth day of the same month, the Israelites gathered together, fasting and wearing sackcloth and having dust on their heads.

column.name: text
column.value: Those of Israelite descent had separated themselves from all foreigners. They stood in their places and confessed their sins and the wickedness of their fathers.

column.name: text
column.value: They stood where they were and read from the Book of the Law of the LORD their God for a quarter of the day, and spent another quarter in confession and in worshiping the LORD their God.

column.name: text
column.value: Standing on the stairs were the Levites--Jeshua, Bani, Kadmiel, Shebaniah, Bunni, Sherebiah, Bani and Kenani--who called with loud voices to the LORD their God.

column.name: text
column.value: And the Levites--Jeshua, Kadmiel, Bani, Hashabneiah, Sherebiah, Hodiah, Shebaniah and Pethahiah--said: "Stand up and praise the LORD your God, who is from everlasting to everlasting." "Blessed be your glorious name, and may it be exalted above all blessing and praise.

column.name: text
column.value: You alone are the LORD. You made the heavens, even the highest heavens, and all their starry host, the earth and all that is on it, the seas and all that is in them. You give life to everything, and the multitudes of heaven worship you.

column.name: text
column.value: "You are the LORD God, who chose Abram and brought him out of Ur of the Chaldeans and named him Abraham.

column.name: text
column.value: You found his heart faithful to you, and you made a covenant with him to give to his descendants the land of the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Jebusites and Girgashites. You have kept your promise because you are righteous.

column.name: text
column.value: "You saw the suffering of our forefathers in Egypt; you heard their cry at the Red Sea.

column.name: text
column.value: You sent miraculous signs and wonders against Pharaoh, against all his officials and all the people of his land, for you knew how arrogantly the Egyptians treated them. You made a name for yourself, which remains to this day.

column.name: text
column.value: You divided the sea before them, so that they passed through it on dry ground, but you hurled their pursuers into the depths, like a stone into mighty waters.

column.name: text
column.value: By day you led them with a pillar of cloud, and by night with a pillar of fire to give them light on the way they were to take.

column.name: text
column.value: "You came down on Mount Sinai; you spoke to them from heaven. You gave them regulations and laws that are just and right, and decrees and commands that are good.

column.name: text
column.value: You made known to them your holy Sabbath and gave them commands, decrees and laws through your servant Moses.

column.name: text
column.value: In their hunger you gave them bread from heaven and in their thirst you brought them water from the rock; you told them to go in and take possession of the land you had sworn with uplifted hand to give them.

column.name: text
column.value: "But they, our forefathers, became arrogant and stiff-necked, and did not obey your commands.

column.name: text
column.value: They refused to listen and failed to remember the miracles you performed among them. They became stiff-necked and in their rebellion appointed a leader in order to return to their slavery. But you are a forgiving God, gracious and compassionate, slow to anger and abounding in love. Therefore you did not desert them,

column.name: text
column.value: even when they cast for themselves an image of a calf and said, 'This is your god, who brought you up out of Egypt,' or when they committed awful blasphemies.

column.name: text
column.value: "Because of your great compassion you did not abandon them in the desert. By day the pillar of cloud did not cease to guide them on their path, nor the pillar of fire by night to shine on the way they were to take.

column.name: text
column.value: You gave your good Spirit to instruct them. You did not withhold your manna from their mouths, and you gave them water for their thirst.

column.name: text
column.value: For forty years you sustained them in the desert; they lacked nothing, their clothes did not wear out nor did their feet become swollen.

column.name: text
column.value: "You gave them kingdoms and nations, allotting to them even the remotest frontiers. They took over the country of Sihon king of Heshbon and the country of Og king of Bashan.

column.name: text
column.value: You made their sons as numerous as the stars in the sky, and you brought them into the land that you told their fathers to enter and possess.

column.name: text
column.value: Their sons went in and took possession of the land. You subdued before them the Canaanites, who lived in the land; you handed the Canaanites over to them, along with their kings and the peoples of the land, to deal with them as they pleased.

column.name: text
column.value: They captured fortified cities and fertile land; they took possession of houses filled with all kinds of good things, wells already dug, vineyards, olive groves and fruit trees in abundance. They ate to the full and were well-nourished; they reveled in your great goodness.

column.name: text
column.value: "But they were disobedient and rebelled against you; they put your law behind their backs. They killed your prophets, who had admonished them in order to turn them back to you; they committed awful blasphemies.

column.name: text
column.value: So you handed them over to their enemies, who oppressed them. But when they were oppressed they cried out to you. From heaven you heard them, and in your great compassion you gave them deliverers, who rescued them from the hand of their enemies.

column.name: text
column.value: "But as soon as they were at rest, they again did what was evil in your sight. Then you abandoned them to the hand of their enemies so that they ruled over them. And when they cried out to you again, you heard from heaven, and in your compassion you delivered them time after time.

column.name: text
column.value: "You warned them to return to your law, but they became arrogant and disobeyed your commands. They sinned against your ordinances, by which a man will live if he obeys them. Stubbornly they turned their backs on you, became stiff-necked and refused to listen.

column.name: text
column.value: For many years you were patient with them. By your Spirit you admonished them through your prophets. Yet they paid no attention, so you handed them over to the neighboring peoples.

column.name: text
column.value: But in your great mercy you did not put an end to them or abandon them, for you are a gracious and merciful God.

column.name: text
column.value: "Now therefore, O our God, the great, mighty and awesome God, who keeps his covenant of love, do not let all this hardship seem trifling in your eyes--the hardship that has come upon us, upon our kings and leaders, upon our priests and prophets, upon our fathers and all your people, from the days of the kings of Assyria until today.

column.name: text
column.value: In all that has happened to us, you have been just; you have acted faithfully, while we did wrong.

column.name: text
column.value: Our kings, our leaders, our priests and our fathers did not follow your law; they did not pay attention to your commands or the warnings you gave them.

column.name: text
column.value: Even while they were in their kingdom, enjoying your great goodness to them in the spacious and fertile land you gave them, they did not serve you or turn from their evil ways.

column.name: text
column.value: "But see, we are slaves today, slaves in the land you gave our forefathers so they could eat its fruit and the other good things it produces.

column.name: text
column.value: Because of our sins, its abundant harvest goes to the kings you have placed over us. They rule over our bodies and our cattle as they please. We are in great distress.

column.name: text
column.value: "In view of all this, we are making a binding agreement, putting it in writing, and our leaders, our Levites and our priests are affixing their seals to it."

column.name: text
column.value: Those who sealed it were: Nehemiah the governor, the son of Hacaliah. Zedekiah,

column.name: text
column.value: Seraiah, Azariah, Jeremiah,

column.name: text
column.value: Pashhur, Amariah, Malkijah,

column.name: text
column.value: Hattush, Shebaniah, Malluch,

column.name: text
column.value: Harim, Meremoth, Obadiah,

column.name: text
column.value: Daniel, Ginnethon, Baruch,

column.name: text
column.value: Meshullam, Abijah, Mijamin,

column.name: text
column.value: Maaziah, Bilgai and Shemaiah. These were the priests.

column.name: text
column.value: The Levites: Jeshua son of Azaniah, Binnui of the sons of Henadad, Kadmiel,

column.name: text
column.value: and their associates: Shebaniah, Hodiah, Kelita, Pelaiah, Hanan,

column.name: text
column.value: Mica, Rehob, Hashabiah,

column.name: text
column.value: Zaccur, Sherebiah, Shebaniah,

column.name: text
column.value: Hodiah, Bani and Beninu.

column.name: text
column.value: The leaders of the people: Parosh, Pahath-Moab, Elam, Zattu, Bani,

column.name: text
column.value: Bunni, Azgad, Bebai,

column.name: text
column.value: Adonijah, Bigvai, Adin,

column.name: text
column.value: Ater, Hezekiah, Azzur,

column.name: text
column.value: Hodiah, Hashum, Bezai,

column.name: text
column.value: Hariph, Anathoth, Nebai,

column.name: text
column.value: Magpiash, Meshullam, Hezir,

column.name: text
column.value: Meshezabel, Zadok, Jaddua,

column.name: text
column.value: Pelatiah, Hanan, Anaiah,

column.name: text
column.value: Hoshea, Hananiah, Hasshub,

column.name: text
column.value: Hallohesh, Pilha, Shobek,

column.name: text
column.value: Rehum, Hashabnah, Maaseiah,

column.name: text
column.value: Ahiah, Hanan, Anan,

column.name: text
column.value: Malluch, Harim and Baanah.

column.name: text
column.value: "The rest of the people--priests, Levites, gatekeepers, singers, temple servants and all who separated themselves from the neighboring peoples for the sake of the Law of God, together with their wives and all their sons and daughters who are able to understand--

column.name: text
column.value: all these now join their brothers the nobles, and bind themselves with a curse and an oath to follow the Law of God given through Moses the servant of God and to obey carefully all the commands, regulations and decrees of the LORD our Lord.

column.name: text
column.value: "We promise not to give our daughters in marriage to the peoples around us or take their daughters for our sons.

column.name: text
column.value: "When the neighboring peoples bring merchandise or grain to sell on the Sabbath, we will not buy from them on the Sabbath or on any holy day. Every seventh year we will forgo working the land and will cancel all debts.

column.name: text
column.value: "We assume the responsibility for carrying out the commands to give a third of a shekel each year for the service of the house of our God:

column.name: text
column.value: for the bread set out on the table; for the regular grain offerings and burnt offerings; for the offerings on the Sabbaths, New Moon festivals and appointed feasts; for the holy offerings; for sin offerings to make atonement for Israel; and for all the duties of the house of our God.

column.name: text
column.value: "We--the priests, the Levites and the people--have cast lots to determine when each of our families is to bring to the house of our God at set times each year a contribution of wood to burn on the altar of the LORD our God, as it is written in the Law.

column.name: text
column.value: "We also assume responsibility for bringing to the house of the LORD each year the firstfruits of our crops and of every fruit tree.

column.name: text
column.value: "As it is also written in the Law, we will bring the firstborn of our sons and of our cattle, of our herds and of our flocks to the house of our God, to the priests ministering there.

column.name: text
column.value: "Moreover, we will bring to the storerooms of the house of our God, to the priests, the first of our ground meal, of our grain offerings, of the fruit of all our trees and of our new wine and oil. And we will bring a tithe of our crops to the Levites, for it is the Levites who collect the tithes in all the towns where we work.

column.name: text
column.value: A priest descended from Aaron is to accompany the Levites when they receive the tithes, and the Levites are to bring a tenth of the tithes up to the house of our God, to the storerooms of the treasury.

column.name: text
column.value: The people of Israel, including the Levites, are to bring their contributions of grain, new wine and oil to the storerooms where the articles for the sanctuary are kept and where the ministering priests, the gatekeepers and the singers stay. "We will not neglect the house of our God."

column.name: text
column.value: Now the leaders of the people settled in Jerusalem, and the rest of the people cast lots to bring one out of every ten to live in Jerusalem, the holy city, while the remaining nine were to stay in their own towns.

column.name: text
column.value: The people commended all the men who volunteered to live in Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: These are the provincial leaders who settled in Jerusalem (now some Israelites, priests, Levites, temple servants and descendants of Solomon's servants lived in the towns of Judah, each on his own property in the various towns,

column.name: text
column.value: while other people from both Judah and Benjamin lived in Jerusalem): From the descendants of Judah: Athaiah son of Uzziah, the son of Zechariah, the son of Amariah, the son of Shephatiah, the son of Mahalalel, a descendant of Perez;

column.name: text
column.value: and Maaseiah son of Baruch, the son of Col-Hozeh, the son of Hazaiah, the son of Adaiah, the son of Joiarib, the son of Zechariah, a descendant of Shelah.

column.name: text
column.value: The descendants of Perez who lived in Jerusalem totaled 468 able men.

column.name: text
column.value: From the descendants of Benjamin: Sallu son of Meshullam, the son of Joed, the son of Pedaiah, the son of Kolaiah, the son of Maaseiah, the son of Ithiel, the son of Jeshaiah,

column.name: text
column.value: and his followers, Gabbai and Sallai--928 men.

column.name: text
column.value: Joel son of Zicri was their chief officer, and Judah son of Hassenuah was over the Second District of the city.

column.name: text
column.value: From the priests: Jedaiah; the son of Joiarib; Jakin;

column.name: text
column.value: Seraiah son of Hilkiah, the son of Meshullam, the son of Zadok, the son of Meraioth, the son of Ahitub, supervisor in the house of God,

column.name: text
column.value: and their associates, who carried on work for the temple--822 men; Adaiah son of Jeroham, the son of Pelaliah, the son of Amzi, the son of Zechariah, the son of Pashhur, the son of Malkijah,

column.name: text
column.value: and his associates, who were heads of families--242 men; Amashsai son of Azarel, the son of Ahzai, the son of Meshillemoth, the son of Immer,

column.name: text
column.value: and his associates, who were able men--128. Their chief officer was Zabdiel son of Haggedolim.

column.name: text
column.value: From the Levites: Shemaiah son of Hasshub, the son of Azrikam, the son of Hashabiah, the son of Bunni;

column.name: text
column.value: Shabbethai and Jozabad, two of the heads of the Levites, who had charge of the outside work of the house of God;

column.name: text
column.value: Mattaniah son of Mica, the son of Zabdi, the son of Asaph, the director who led in thanksgiving and prayer; Bakbukiah, second among his associates; and Abda son of Shammua, the son of Galal, the son of Jeduthun.

column.name: text
column.value: The Levites in the holy city totaled 284.

column.name: text
column.value: The gatekeepers: Akkub, Talmon and their associates, who kept watch at the gates--172 men.

column.name: text
column.value: The rest of the Israelites, with the priests and Levites, were in all the towns of Judah, each on his ancestral property.

column.name: text
column.value: The temple servants lived on the hill of Ophel, and Ziha and Gishpa were in charge of them.

column.name: text
column.value: The chief officer of the Levites in Jerusalem was Uzzi son of Bani, the son of Hashabiah, the son of Mattaniah, the son of Mica. Uzzi was one of Asaph's descendants, who were the singers responsible for the service of the house of God.

column.name: text
column.value: The singers were under the king's orders, which regulated their daily activity.

column.name: text
column.value: Pethahiah son of Meshezabel, one of the descendants of Zerah son of Judah, was the king's agent in all affairs relating to the people.

column.name: text
column.value: As for the villages with their fields, some of the people of Judah lived in Kiriath Arba and its surrounding settlements, in Dibon and its settlements, in Jekabzeel and its villages,

column.name: text
column.value: in Jeshua, in Moladah, in Beth Pelet,

column.name: text
column.value: in Hazar Shual, in Beersheba and its settlements,

column.name: text
column.value: in Ziklag, in Meconah and its settlements,

column.name: text
column.value: in En Rimmon, in Zorah, in Jarmuth,

column.name: text
column.value: Zanoah, Adullam and their villages, in Lachish and its fields, and in Azekah and its settlements. So they were living all the way from Beersheba to the Valley of Hinnom.

column.name: text
column.value: The descendants of the Benjamites from Geba lived in Micmash, Aija, Bethel and its settlements,

column.name: text
column.value: in Anathoth, Nob and Ananiah,

column.name: text
column.value: in Hazor, Ramah and Gittaim,

column.name: text
column.value: in Hadid, Zeboim and Neballat,

column.name: text
column.value: in Lod and Ono, and in the Valley of the Craftsmen.

column.name: text
column.value: Some of the divisions of the Levites of Judah settled in Benjamin.

column.name: text
column.value: These were the priests and Levites who returned with Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and with Jeshua: Seraiah, Jeremiah, Ezra,

column.name: text
column.value: Amariah, Malluch, Hattush,

column.name: text
column.value: Shecaniah, Rehum, Meremoth,

column.name: text
column.value: Iddo, Ginnethon, Abijah,

column.name: text
column.value: Mijamin, Moadiah, Bilgah,

column.name: text
column.value: Shemaiah, Joiarib, Jedaiah,

column.name: text
column.value: Sallu, Amok, Hilkiah and Jedaiah. These were the leaders of the priests and their associates in the days of Jeshua.

column.name: text
column.value: The Levites were Jeshua, Binnui, Kadmiel, Sherebiah, Judah, and also Mattaniah, who, together with his associates, was in charge of the songs of thanksgiving.

column.name: text
column.value: Bakbukiah and Unni, their associates, stood opposite them in the services.

column.name: text
column.value: Jeshua was the father of Joiakim, Joiakim the father of Eliashib, Eliashib the father of Joiada,

column.name: text
column.value: Joiada the father of Jonathan, and Jonathan the father of Jaddua.

column.name: text
column.value: In the days of Joiakim, these were the heads of the priestly families: of Seraiah's family, Meraiah; of Jeremiah's, Hananiah;

column.name: text
column.value: of Ezra's, Meshullam; of Amariah's, Jehohanan;

column.name: text
column.value: of Malluch's, Jonathan; of Shecaniah's, Joseph;

column.name: text
column.value: of Harim's, Adna; of Meremoth's, Helkai;

column.name: text
column.value: of Iddo's, Zechariah; of Ginnethon's, Meshullam;

column.name: text
column.value: of Abijah's, Zicri; of Miniamin's and of Moadiah's, Piltai;

column.name: text
column.value: of Bilgah's, Shammua; of Shemaiah's, Jehonathan;

column.name: text
column.value: of Joiarib's, Mattenai; of Jedaiah's, Uzzi;

column.name: text
column.value: of Sallu's, Kallai; of Amok's, Eber;

column.name: text
column.value: of Hilkiah's, Hashabiah; of Jedaiah's, Nethanel.

column.name: text
column.value: The family heads of the Levites in the days of Eliashib, Joiada, Johanan and Jaddua, as well as those of the priests, were recorded in the reign of Darius the Persian.

column.name: text
column.value: The family heads among the descendants of Levi up to the time of Johanan son of Eliashib were recorded in the book of the annals.

column.name: text
column.value: And the leaders of the Levites were Hashabiah, Sherebiah, Jeshua son of Kadmiel, and their associates, who stood opposite them to give praise and thanksgiving, one section responding to the other, as prescribed by David the man of God.

column.name: text
column.value: Mattaniah, Bakbukiah, Obadiah, Meshullam, Talmon and Akkub were gatekeepers who guarded the storerooms at the gates.

column.name: text
column.value: They served in the days of Joiakim son of Jeshua, the son of Jozadak, and in the days of Nehemiah the governor and of Ezra the priest and scribe.

column.name: text
column.value: At the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem, the Levites were sought out from where they lived and were brought to Jerusalem to celebrate joyfully the dedication with songs of thanksgiving and with the music of cymbals, harps and lyres.

column.name: text
column.value: The singers also were brought together from the region around Jerusalem--from the villages of the Netophathites,

column.name: text
column.value: from Beth Gilgal, and from the area of Geba and Azmaveth, for the singers had built villages for themselves around Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: When the priests and Levites had purified themselves ceremonially, they purified the people, the gates and the wall.

column.name: text
column.value: I had the leaders of Judah go up on top of the wall. I also assigned two large choirs to give thanks. One was to proceed on top of the wall to the right, toward the Dung Gate.

column.name: text
column.value: Hoshaiah and half the leaders of Judah followed them,

column.name: text
column.value: along with Azariah, Ezra, Meshullam,

column.name: text
column.value: Judah, Benjamin, Shemaiah, Jeremiah,

column.name: text
column.value: as well as some priests with trumpets, and also Zechariah son of Jonathan, the son of Shemaiah, the son of Mattaniah, the son of Micaiah, the son of Zaccur, the son of Asaph,

column.name: text
column.value: and his associates--Shemaiah, Azarel, Milalai, Gilalai, Maai, Nethanel, Judah and Hanani--with musical instruments prescribed by David the man of God. Ezra the scribe led the procession.

column.name: text
column.value: At the Fountain Gate they continued directly up the steps of the City of David on the ascent to the wall and passed above the house of David to the Water Gate on the east.

column.name: text
column.value: The second choir proceeded in the opposite direction. I followed them on top of the wall, together with half the people--past the Tower of the Ovens to the Broad Wall,

column.name: text
column.value: over the Gate of Ephraim, the Jeshanah Gate, the Fish Gate, the Tower of Hananel and the Tower of the Hundred, as far as the Sheep Gate. At the Gate of the Guard they stopped.

column.name: text
column.value: The two choirs that gave thanks then took their places in the house of God; so did I, together with half the officials,

column.name: text
column.value: as well as the priests--Eliakim, Maaseiah, Miniamin, Micaiah, Elioenai, Zechariah and Hananiah with their trumpets--

column.name: text
column.value: and also Maaseiah, Shemaiah, Eleazar, Uzzi, Jehohanan, Malkijah, Elam and Ezer. The choirs sang under the direction of Jezrahiah.

column.name: text
column.value: And on that day they offered great sacrifices, rejoicing because God had given them great joy. The women and children also rejoiced. The sound of rejoicing in Jerusalem could be heard far away.

column.name: text
column.value: At that time men were appointed to be in charge of the storerooms for the contributions, firstfruits and tithes. From the fields around the towns they were to bring into the storerooms the portions required by the Law for the priests and the Levites, for Judah was pleased with the ministering priests and Levites.

column.name: text
column.value: They performed the service of their God and the service of purification, as did also the singers and gatekeepers, according to the commands of David and his son Solomon.

column.name: text
column.value: For long ago, in the days of David and Asaph, there had been directors for the singers and for the songs of praise and thanksgiving to God.

column.name: text
column.value: So in the days of Zerubbabel and of Nehemiah, all Israel contributed the daily portions for the singers and gatekeepers. They also set aside the portion for the other Levites, and the Levites set aside the portion for the descendants of Aaron.

column.name: text
column.value: On that day the Book of Moses was read aloud in the hearing of the people and there it was found written that no Ammonite or Moabite should ever be admitted into the assembly of God,

column.name: text
column.value: because they had not met the Israelites with food and water but had hired Balaam to call a curse down on them. (Our God, however, turned the curse into a blessing.)

column.name: text
column.value: When the people heard this law, they excluded from Israel all who were of foreign descent.

column.name: text
column.value: Before this, Eliashib the priest had been put in charge of the storerooms of the house of our God. He was closely associated with Tobiah,

column.name: text
column.value: and he had provided him with a large room formerly used to store the grain offerings and incense and temple articles, and also the tithes of grain, new wine and oil prescribed for the Levites, singers and gatekeepers, as well as the contributions for the priests.

column.name: text
column.value: But while all this was going on, I was not in Jerusalem, for in the thirty-second year of Artaxerxes king of Babylon I had returned to the king. Some time later I asked his permission

column.name: text
column.value: and came back to Jerusalem. Here I learned about the evil thing Eliashib had done in providing Tobiah a room in the courts of the house of God.

column.name: text
column.value: I was greatly displeased and threw all Tobiah's household goods out of the room.

column.name: text
column.value: I gave orders to purify the rooms, and then I put back into them the equipment of the house of God, with the grain offerings and the incense.

column.name: text
column.value: I also learned that the portions assigned to the Levites had not been given to them, and that all the Levites and singers responsible for the service had gone back to their own fields.

column.name: text
column.value: So I rebuked the officials and asked them, "Why is the house of God neglected?" Then I called them together and stationed them at their posts.

column.name: text
column.value: All Judah brought the tithes of grain, new wine and oil into the storerooms.

column.name: text
column.value: I put Shelemiah the priest, Zadok the scribe, and a Levite named Pedaiah in charge of the storerooms and made Hanan son of Zaccur, the son of Mattaniah, their assistant, because these men were considered trustworthy. They were made responsible for distributing the supplies to their brothers.

column.name: text
column.value: Remember me for this, O my God, and do not blot out what I have so faithfully done for the house of my God and its services.

column.name: text
column.value: In those days I saw men in Judah treading winepresses on the Sabbath and bringing in grain and loading it on donkeys, together with wine, grapes, figs and all other kinds of loads. And they were bringing all this into Jerusalem on the Sabbath. Therefore I warned them against selling food on that day.

column.name: text
column.value: Men from Tyre who lived in Jerusalem were bringing in fish and all kinds of merchandise and selling them in Jerusalem on the Sabbath to the people of Judah.

column.name: text
column.value: I rebuked the nobles of Judah and said to them, "What is this wicked thing you are doing--desecrating the Sabbath day?

column.name: text
column.value: Didn't your forefathers do the same things, so that our God brought all this calamity upon us and upon this city? Now you are stirring up more wrath against Israel by desecrating the Sabbath."

column.name: text
column.value: When evening shadows fell on the gates of Jerusalem before the Sabbath, I ordered the doors to be shut and not opened until the Sabbath was over. I stationed some of my own men at the gates so that no load could be brought in on the Sabbath day.

column.name: text
column.value: Once or twice the merchants and sellers of all kinds of goods spent the night outside Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: But I warned them and said, "Why do you spend the night by the wall? If you do this again, I will lay hands on you." From that time on they no longer came on the Sabbath.

column.name: text
column.value: Then I commanded the Levites to purify themselves and go and guard the gates in order to keep the Sabbath day holy. Remember me for this also, O my God, and show mercy to me according to your great love.

column.name: text
column.value: Moreover, in those days I saw men of Judah who had married women from Ashdod, Ammon and Moab.

column.name: text
column.value: Half of their children spoke the language of Ashdod or the language of one of the other peoples, and did not know how to speak the language of Judah.

column.name: text
column.value: I rebuked them and called curses down on them. I beat some of the men and pulled out their hair. I made them take an oath in God's name and said: "You are not to give your daughters in marriage to their sons, nor are you to take their daughters in marriage for your sons or for yourselves.

column.name: text
column.value: Was it not because of marriages like these that Solomon king of Israel sinned? Among the many nations there was no king like him. He was loved by his God, and God made him king over all Israel, but even he was led into sin by foreign women.

column.name: text
column.value: Must we hear now that you too are doing all this terrible wickedness and are being unfaithful to our God by marrying foreign women?"

column.name: text
column.value: One of the sons of Joiada son of Eliashib the high priest was son-in-law to Sanballat the Horonite. And I drove him away from me.

column.name: text
column.value: Remember them, O my God, because they defiled the priestly office and the covenant of the priesthood and of the Levites.

column.name: text
column.value: So I purified the priests and the Levites of everything foreign, and assigned them duties, each to his own task.

column.name: text
column.value: I also made provision for contributions of wood at designated times, and for the firstfruits. Remember me with favor, O my God.

column.name: text
column.value: This is what happened during the time of Xerxes, the Xerxes who ruled over 127 provinces stretching from India to Cush:

column.name: text
column.value: At that time King Xerxes reigned from his royal throne in the citadel of Susa,

column.name: text
column.value: and in the third year of his reign he gave a banquet for all his nobles and officials. The military leaders of Persia and Media, the princes, and the nobles of the provinces were present.

column.name: text
column.value: For a full 180 days he displayed the vast wealth of his kingdom and the splendor and glory of his majesty.

column.name: text
column.value: When these days were over, the king gave a banquet, lasting seven days, in the enclosed garden of the king's palace, for all the people from the least to the greatest, who were in the citadel of Susa.

column.name: text
column.value: The garden had hangings of white and blue linen, fastened with cords of white linen and purple material to silver rings on marble pillars. There were couches of gold and silver on a mosaic pavement of porphyry, marble, mother-of-pearl and other costly stones.

column.name: text
column.value: Wine was served in goblets of gold, each one different from the other, and the royal wine was abundant, in keeping with the king's liberality.

column.name: text
column.value: By the king's command each guest was allowed to drink in his own way, for the king instructed all the wine stewards to serve each man what he wished.

column.name: text
column.value: Queen Vashti also gave a banquet for the women in the royal palace of King Xerxes.

column.name: text
column.value: On the seventh day, when King Xerxes was in high spirits from wine, he commanded the seven eunuchs who served him--Mehuman, Biztha, Harbona, Bigtha, Abagtha, Zethar and Carcas--

column.name: text
column.value: to bring before him Queen Vashti, wearing her royal crown, in order to display her beauty to the people and nobles, for she was lovely to look at.

column.name: text
column.value: But when the attendants delivered the king's command, Queen Vashti refused to come. Then the king became furious and burned with anger.

column.name: text
column.value: Since it was customary for the king to consult experts in matters of law and justice, he spoke with the wise men who understood the times

column.name: text
column.value: and were closest to the king--Carshena, Shethar, Admatha, Tarshish, Meres, Marsena and Memucan, the seven nobles of Persia and Media who had special access to the king and were highest in the kingdom.

column.name: text
column.value: "According to law, what must be done to Queen Vashti?" he asked. "She has not obeyed the command of King Xerxes that the eunuchs have taken to her."

column.name: text
column.value: Then Memucan replied in the presence of the king and the nobles, "Queen Vashti has done wrong, not only against the king but also against all the nobles and the peoples of all the provinces of King Xerxes.

column.name: text
column.value: For the queen's conduct will become known to all the women, and so they will despise their husbands and say, 'King Xerxes commanded Queen Vashti to be brought before him, but she would not come.'

column.name: text
column.value: This very day the Persian and Median women of the nobility who have heard about the queen's conduct will respond to all the king's nobles in the same way. There will be no end of disrespect and discord.

column.name: text
column.value: "Therefore, if it pleases the king, let him issue a royal decree and let it be written in the laws of Persia and Media, which cannot be repealed, that Vashti is never again to enter the presence of King Xerxes. Also let the king give her royal position to someone else who is better than she.

column.name: text
column.value: Then when the king's edict is proclaimed throughout all his vast realm, all the women will respect their husbands, from the least to the greatest."

column.name: text
column.value: The king and his nobles were pleased with this advice, so the king did as Memucan proposed.

column.name: text
column.value: He sent dispatches to all parts of the kingdom, to each province in its own script and to each people in its own language, proclaiming in each people's tongue that every man should be ruler over his own household.

column.name: text
column.value: When Mordecai learned of all that had been done, he tore his clothes, put on sackcloth and ashes, and went out into the city, wailing loudly and bitterly.

column.name: text
column.value: But he went only as far as the king's gate, because no one clothed in sackcloth was allowed to enter it.

column.name: text
column.value: In every province to which the edict and order of the king came, there was great mourning among the Jews, with fasting, weeping and wailing. Many lay in sackcloth and ashes.

column.name: text
column.value: When Esther's maids and eunuchs came and told her about Mordecai, she was in great distress. She sent clothes for him to put on instead of his sackcloth, but he would not accept them.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Esther summoned Hathach, one of the king's eunuchs assigned to attend her, and ordered him to find out what was troubling Mordecai and why.

column.name: text
column.value: So Hathach went out to Mordecai in the open square of the city in front of the king's gate.

column.name: text
column.value: Mordecai told him everything that had happened to him, including the exact amount of money Haman had promised to pay into the royal treasury for the destruction of the Jews.

column.name: text
column.value: He also gave him a copy of the text of the edict for their annihilation, which had been published in Susa, to show to Esther and explain it to her, and he told him to urge her to go into the king's presence to beg for mercy and plead with him for her people.

column.name: text
column.value: Hathach went back and reported to Esther what Mordecai had said.

column.name: text
column.value: Then she instructed him to say to Mordecai,

column.name: text
column.value: "All the king's officials and the people of the royal provinces know that for any man or woman who approaches the king in the inner court without being summoned the king has but one law: that he be put to death. The only exception to this is for the king to extend the gold scepter to him and spare his life. But thirty days have passed since I was called to go to the king."

column.name: text
column.value: When Esther's words were reported to Mordecai,

column.name: text
column.value: he sent back this answer: "Do not think that because you are in the king's house you alone of all the Jews will escape.

column.name: text
column.value: For if you remain silent at this time, relief and deliverance for the Jews will arise from another place, but you and your father's family will perish. And who knows but that you have come to royal position for such a time as this?"

column.name: text
column.value: Then Esther sent this reply to Mordecai:

column.name: text
column.value: "Go, gather together all the Jews who are in Susa, and fast for me. Do not eat or drink for three days, night or day. I and my maids will fast as you do. When this is done, I will go to the king, even though it is against the law. And if I perish, I perish."

column.name: text
column.value: So Mordecai went away and carried out all of Esther's instructions.

column.name: text
column.value: Later when the anger of King Xerxes had subsided, he remembered Vashti and what she had done and what he had decreed about her.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the king's personal attendants proposed, "Let a search be made for beautiful young virgins for the king.

column.name: text
column.value: Let the king appoint commissioners in every province of his realm to bring all these beautiful girls into the harem at the citadel of Susa. Let them be placed under the care of Hegai, the king's eunuch, who is in charge of the women; and let beauty treatments be given to them.

column.name: text
column.value: Then let the girl who pleases the king be queen instead of Vashti." This advice appealed to the king, and he followed it.

column.name: text
column.value: Now there was in the citadel of Susa a Jew of the tribe of Benjamin, named Mordecai son of Jair, the son of Shimei, the son of Kish,

column.name: text
column.value: who had been carried into exile from Jerusalem by Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, among those taken captive with Jehoiachin king of Judah.

column.name: text
column.value: Mordecai had a cousin named Hadassah, whom he had brought up because she had neither father nor mother. This girl, who was also known as Esther, was lovely in form and features, and Mordecai had taken her as his own daughter when her father and mother died.

column.name: text
column.value: When the king's order and edict had been proclaimed, many girls were brought to the citadel of Susa and put under the care of Hegai. Esther also was taken to the king's palace and entrusted to Hegai, who had charge of the harem.

column.name: text
column.value: The girl pleased him and won his favor. Immediately he provided her with her beauty treatments and special food. He assigned to her seven maids selected from the king's palace and moved her and her maids into the best place in the harem.

column.name: text
column.value: Esther had not revealed her nationality and family background, because Mordecai had forbidden her to do so.

column.name: text
column.value: Every day he walked back and forth near the courtyard of the harem to find out how Esther was and what was happening to her.

column.name: text
column.value: Before a girl's turn came to go in to King Xerxes, she had to complete twelve months of beauty treatments prescribed for the women, six months with oil of myrrh and six with perfumes and cosmetics.

column.name: text
column.value: And this is how she would go to the king: Anything she wanted was given her to take with her from the harem to the king's palace.

column.name: text
column.value: In the evening she would go there and in the morning return to another part of the harem to the care of Shaashgaz, the king's eunuch who was in charge of the concubines. She would not return to the king unless he was pleased with her and summoned her by name.

column.name: text
column.value: When the turn came for Esther (the girl Mordecai had adopted, the daughter of his uncle Abihail) to go to the king, she asked for nothing other than what Hegai, the king's eunuch who was in charge of the harem, suggested. And Esther won the favor of everyone who saw her.

column.name: text
column.value: She was taken to King Xerxes in the royal residence in the tenth month, the month of Tebeth, in the seventh year of his reign.

column.name: text
column.value: Now the king was attracted to Esther more than to any of the other women, and she won his favor and approval more than any of the other virgins. So he set a royal crown on her head and made her queen instead of Vashti.

column.name: text
column.value: And the king gave a great banquet, Esther's banquet, for all his nobles and officials. He proclaimed a holiday throughout the provinces and distributed gifts with royal liberality.

column.name: text
column.value: When the virgins were assembled a second time, Mordecai was sitting at the king's gate.

column.name: text
column.value: But Esther had kept secret her family background and nationality just as Mordecai had told her to do, for she continued to follow Mordecai's instructions as she had done when he was bringing her up.

column.name: text
column.value: During the time Mordecai was sitting at the king's gate, Bigthana and Teresh, two of the king's officers who guarded the doorway, became angry and conspired to assassinate King Xerxes.

column.name: text
column.value: But Mordecai found out about the plot and told Queen Esther, who in turn reported it to the king, giving credit to Mordecai.

column.name: text
column.value: And when the report was investigated and found to be true, the two officials were hanged on a gallows. All this was recorded in the book of the annals in the presence of the king.

column.name: text
column.value: After these events, King Xerxes honored Haman son of Hammedatha, the Agagite, elevating him and giving him a seat of honor higher than that of all the other nobles.

column.name: text
column.value: All the royal officials at the king's gate knelt down and paid honor to Haman, for the king had commanded this concerning him. But Mordecai would not kneel down or pay him honor.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the royal officials at the king's gate asked Mordecai, "Why do you disobey the king's command?"

column.name: text
column.value: Day after day they spoke to him but he refused to comply. Therefore they told Haman about it to see whether Mordecai's behavior would be tolerated, for he had told them he was a Jew.

column.name: text
column.value: When Haman saw that Mordecai would not kneel down or pay him honor, he was enraged.

column.name: text
column.value: Yet having learned who Mordecai's people were, he scorned the idea of killing only Mordecai. Instead Haman looked for a way to destroy all Mordecai's people, the Jews, throughout the whole kingdom of Xerxes.

column.name: text
column.value: In the twelfth year of King Xerxes, in the first month, the month of Nisan, they cast the pur (that is, the lot) in the presence of Haman to select a day and month. And the lot fell on the twelfth month, the month of Adar.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Haman said to King Xerxes, "There is a certain people dispersed and scattered among the peoples in all the provinces of your kingdom whose customs are different from those of all other people and who do not obey the king's laws; it is not in the king's best interest to tolerate them.

column.name: text
column.value: If it pleases the king, let a decree be issued to destroy them, and I will put ten thousand talents of silver into the royal treasury for the men who carry out this business."

column.name: text
column.value: So the king took his signet ring from his finger and gave it to Haman son of Hammedatha, the Agagite, the enemy of the Jews.

column.name: text
column.value: "Keep the money," the king said to Haman, "and do with the people as you please."

column.name: text
column.value: Then on the thirteenth day of the first month the royal secretaries were summoned. They wrote out in the script of each province and in the language of each people all Haman's orders to the king's satraps, the governors of the various provinces and the nobles of the various peoples. These were written in the name of King Xerxes himself and sealed with his own ring.

column.name: text
column.value: Dispatches were sent by couriers to all the king's provinces with the order to destroy, kill and annihilate all the Jews--young and old, women and little children--on a single day, the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, the month of Adar, and to plunder their goods.

column.name: text
column.value: A copy of the text of the edict was to be issued as law in every province and made known to the people of every nationality so they would be ready for that day.

column.name: text
column.value: Spurred on by the king's command, the couriers went out, and the edict was issued in the citadel of Susa. The king and Haman sat down to drink, but the city of Susa was bewildered.

column.name: text
column.value: That night the king could not sleep; so he ordered the book of the chronicles, the record of his reign, to be brought in and read to him.

column.name: text
column.value: It was found recorded there that Mordecai had exposed Bigthana and Teresh, two of the king's officers who guarded the doorway, who had conspired to assassinate King Xerxes.

column.name: text
column.value: "What honor and recognition has Mordecai received for this?" the king asked. "Nothing has been done for him," his attendants answered.

column.name: text
column.value: The king said, "Who is in the court?" Now Haman had just entered the outer court of the palace to speak to the king about hanging Mordecai on the gallows he had erected for him.

column.name: text
column.value: His attendants answered, "Haman is standing in the court." "Bring him in," the king ordered.

column.name: text
column.value: When Haman entered, the king asked him, "What should be done for the man the king delights to honor?" Now Haman thought to himself, "Who is there that the king would rather honor than me?"

column.name: text
column.value: So he answered the king, "For the man the king delights to honor,

column.name: text
column.value: have them bring a royal robe the king has worn and a horse the king has ridden, one with a royal crest placed on its head.

column.name: text
column.value: Then let the robe and horse be entrusted to one of the king's most noble princes. Let them robe the man the king delights to honor, and lead him on the horse through the city streets, proclaiming before him, 'This is what is done for the man the king delights to honor!'"

column.name: text
column.value: "Go at once," the king commanded Haman. "Get the robe and the horse and do just as you have suggested for Mordecai the Jew, who sits at the king's gate. Do not neglect anything you have recommended."

column.name: text
column.value: So Haman got the robe and the horse. He robed Mordecai, and led him on horseback through the city streets, proclaiming before him, "This is what is done for the man the king delights to honor!"

column.name: text
column.value: Afterward Mordecai returned to the king's gate. But Haman rushed home, with his head covered in grief,

column.name: text
column.value: and told Zeresh his wife and all his friends everything that had happened to him. His advisers and his wife Zeresh said to him, "Since Mordecai, before whom your downfall has started, is of Jewish origin, you cannot stand against him--you will surely come to ruin!"

column.name: text
column.value: While they were still talking with him, the king's eunuchs arrived and hurried Haman away to the banquet Esther had prepared.

column.name: text
column.value: On the third day Esther put on her royal robes and stood in the inner court of the palace, in front of the king's hall. The king was sitting on his royal throne in the hall, facing the entrance.

column.name: text
column.value: When he saw Queen Esther standing in the court, he was pleased with her and held out to her the gold scepter that was in his hand. So Esther approached and touched the tip of the scepter.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the king asked, "What is it, Queen Esther? What is your request? Even up to half the kingdom, it will be given you."

column.name: text
column.value: "If it pleases the king," replied Esther, "let the king, together with Haman, come today to a banquet I have prepared for him."

column.name: text
column.value: "Bring Haman at once," the king said, "so that we may do what Esther asks." So the king and Haman went to the banquet Esther had prepared.

column.name: text
column.value: As they were drinking wine, the king again asked Esther, "Now what is your petition? It will be given you. And what is your request? Even up to half the kingdom, it will be granted."

column.name: text
column.value: Esther replied, "My petition and my request is this:

column.name: text
column.value: If the king regards me with favor and if it pleases the king to grant my petition and fulfill my request, let the king and Haman come tomorrow to the banquet I will prepare for them. Then I will answer the king's question."

column.name: text
column.value: Haman went out that day happy and in high spirits. But when he saw Mordecai at the king's gate and observed that he neither rose nor showed fear in his presence, he was filled with rage against Mordecai.

column.name: text
column.value: Nevertheless, Haman restrained himself and went home. Calling together his friends and Zeresh, his wife,

column.name: text
column.value: Haman boasted to them about his vast wealth, his many sons, and all the ways the king had honored him and how he had elevated him above the other nobles and officials.

column.name: text
column.value: "And that's not all," Haman added. "I'm the only person Queen Esther invited to accompany the king to the banquet she gave. And she has invited me along with the king tomorrow.

column.name: text
column.value: But all this gives me no satisfaction as long as I see that Jew Mordecai sitting at the king's gate."

column.name: text
column.value: His wife Zeresh and all his friends said to him, "Have a gallows built, seventy-five feet high, and ask the king in the morning to have Mordecai hanged on it. Then go with the king to the dinner and be happy." This suggestion delighted Haman, and he had the gallows built.

column.name: text
column.value: So the king and Haman went to dine with Queen Esther,

column.name: text
column.value: and as they were drinking wine on that second day, the king again asked, "Queen Esther, what is your petition? It will be given you. What is your request? Even up to half the kingdom, it will be granted."

column.name: text
column.value: Then Queen Esther answered, "If I have found favor with you, O king, and if it pleases your majesty, grant me my life--this is my petition. And spare my people--this is my request.

column.name: text
column.value: For I and my people have been sold for destruction and slaughter and annihilation. If we had merely been sold as male and female slaves, I would have kept quiet, because no such distress would justify disturbing the king."

column.name: text
column.value: King Xerxes asked Queen Esther, "Who is he? Where is the man who has dared to do such a thing?"

column.name: text
column.value: Esther said, "The adversary and enemy is this vile Haman." Then Haman was terrified before the king and queen.

column.name: text
column.value: The king got up in a rage, left his wine and went out into the palace garden. But Haman, realizing that the king had already decided his fate, stayed behind to beg Queen Esther for his life.

column.name: text
column.value: Just as the king returned from the palace garden to the banquet hall, Haman was falling on the couch where Esther was reclining. The king exclaimed, "Will he even molest the queen while she is with me in the house?" As soon as the word left the king's mouth, they covered Haman's face.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Harbona, one of the eunuchs attending the king, said, "A gallows seventy-five feet high stands by Haman's house. He had it made for Mordecai, who spoke up to help the king." The king said, "Hang him on it!"

column.name: text
column.value: So they hanged Haman on the gallows he had prepared for Mordecai. Then the king's fury subsided.

column.name: text
column.value: That same day King Xerxes gave Queen Esther the estate of Haman, the enemy of the Jews. And Mordecai came into the presence of the king, for Esther had told how he was related to her.

column.name: text
column.value: The king took off his signet ring, which he had reclaimed from Haman, and presented it to Mordecai. And Esther appointed him over Haman's estate.

column.name: text
column.value: Esther again pleaded with the king, falling at his feet and weeping. She begged him to put an end to the evil plan of Haman the Agagite, which he had devised against the Jews.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the king extended the gold scepter to Esther and she arose and stood before him.

column.name: text
column.value: "If it pleases the king," she said, "and if he regards me with favor and thinks it the right thing to do, and if he is pleased with me, let an order be written overruling the dispatches that Haman son of Hammedatha, the Agagite, devised and wrote to destroy the Jews in all the king's provinces.

column.name: text
column.value: For how can I bear to see disaster fall on my people? How can I bear to see the destruction of my family?"

column.name: text
column.value: King Xerxes replied to Queen Esther and to Mordecai the Jew, "Because Haman attacked the Jews, I have given his estate to Esther, and they have hanged him on the gallows.

column.name: text
column.value: Now write another decree in the king's name in behalf of the Jews as seems best to you, and seal it with the king's signet ring--for no document written in the king's name and sealed with his ring can be revoked."

column.name: text
column.value: At once the royal secretaries were summoned--on the twenty-third day of the third month, the month of Sivan. They wrote out all Mordecai's orders to the Jews, and to the satraps, governors and nobles of the 127 provinces stretching from India to Cush. These orders were written in the script of each province and the language of each people and also to the Jews in their own script and language.

column.name: text
column.value: Mordecai wrote in the name of King Xerxes, sealed the dispatches with the king's signet ring, and sent them by mounted couriers, who rode fast horses especially bred for the king.

column.name: text
column.value: The king's edict granted the Jews in every city the right to assemble and protect themselves; to destroy, kill and annihilate any armed force of any nationality or province that might attack them and their women and children; and to plunder the property of their enemies.

column.name: text
column.value: The day appointed for the Jews to do this in all the provinces of King Xerxes was the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, the month of Adar.

column.name: text
column.value: A copy of the text of the edict was to be issued as law in every province and made known to the people of every nationality so that the Jews would be ready on that day to avenge themselves on their enemies.

column.name: text
column.value: The couriers, riding the royal horses, raced out, spurred on by the king's command. And the edict was also issued in the citadel of Susa.

column.name: text
column.value: Mordecai left the king's presence wearing royal garments of blue and white, a large crown of gold and a purple robe of fine linen. And the city of Susa held a joyous celebration.

column.name: text
column.value: For the Jews it was a time of happiness and joy, gladness and honor.

column.name: text
column.value: In every province and in every city, wherever the edict of the king went, there was joy and gladness among the Jews, with feasting and celebrating. And many people of other nationalities became Jews because fear of the Jews had seized them.

column.name: text
column.value: On the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, the month of Adar, the edict commanded by the king was to be carried out. On this day the enemies of the Jews had hoped to overpower them, but now the tables were turned and the Jews got the upper hand over those who hated them.

column.name: text
column.value: The Jews assembled in their cities in all the provinces of King Xerxes to attack those seeking their destruction. No one could stand against them, because the people of all the other nationalities were afraid of them.

column.name: text
column.value: And all the nobles of the provinces, the satraps, the governors and the king's administrators helped the Jews, because fear of Mordecai had seized them.

column.name: text
column.value: Mordecai was prominent in the palace; his reputation spread throughout the provinces, and he became more and more powerful.

column.name: text
column.value: The Jews struck down all their enemies with the sword, killing and destroying them, and they did what they pleased to those who hated them.

column.name: text
column.value: In the citadel of Susa, the Jews killed and destroyed five hundred men.

column.name: text
column.value: They also killed Parshandatha, Dalphon, Aspatha,

column.name: text
column.value: Poratha, Adalia, Aridatha,

column.name: text
column.value: Parmashta, Arisai, Aridai and Vaizatha,

column.name: text
column.value: the ten sons of Haman son of Hammedatha, the enemy of the Jews. But they did not lay their hands on the plunder.

column.name: text
column.value: The number of those slain in the citadel of Susa was reported to the king that same day.

column.name: text
column.value: The king said to Queen Esther, "The Jews have killed and destroyed five hundred men and the ten sons of Haman in the citadel of Susa. What have they done in the rest of the king's provinces? Now what is your petition? It will be given you. What is your request? It will also be granted."

column.name: text
column.value: "If it pleases the king," Esther answered, "give the Jews in Susa permission to carry out this day's edict tomorrow also, and let Haman's ten sons be hanged on gallows."

column.name: text
column.value: So the king commanded that this be done. An edict was issued in Susa, and they hanged the ten sons of Haman.

column.name: text
column.value: The Jews in Susa came together on the fourteenth day of the month of Adar, and they put to death in Susa three hundred men, but they did not lay their hands on the plunder.

column.name: text
column.value: Meanwhile, the remainder of the Jews who were in the king's provinces also assembled to protect themselves and get relief from their enemies. They killed seventy-five thousand of them but did not lay their hands on the plunder.

column.name: text
column.value: This happened on the thirteenth day of the month of Adar, and on the fourteenth they rested and made it a day of feasting and joy.

column.name: text
column.value: The Jews in Susa, however, had assembled on the thirteenth and fourteenth, and then on the fifteenth they rested and made it a day of feasting and joy.

column.name: text
column.value: That is why rural Jews--those living in villages--observe the fourteenth of the month of Adar as a day of joy and feasting, a day for giving presents to each other.

column.name: text
column.value: Mordecai recorded these events, and he sent letters to all the Jews throughout the provinces of King Xerxes, near and far,

column.name: text
column.value: to have them celebrate annually the fourteenth and fifteenth days of the month of Adar

column.name: text
column.value: as the time when the Jews got relief from their enemies, and as the month when their sorrow was turned into joy and their mourning into a day of celebration. He wrote them to observe the days as days of feasting and joy and giving presents of food to one another and gifts to the poor.

column.name: text
column.value: So the Jews agreed to continue the celebration they had begun, doing what Mordecai had written to them.

column.name: text
column.value: For Haman son of Hammedatha, the Agagite, the enemy of all the Jews, had plotted against the Jews to destroy them and had cast the pur (that is, the lot) for their ruin and destruction.

column.name: text
column.value: But when the plot came to the king's attention, he issued written orders that the evil scheme Haman had devised against the Jews should come back onto his own head, and that he and his sons should be hanged on the gallows.

column.name: text
column.value: (Therefore these days were called Purim, from the word pur .) Because of everything written in this letter and because of what they had seen and what had happened to them,

column.name: text
column.value: the Jews took it upon themselves to establish the custom that they and their descendants and all who join them should without fail observe these two days every year, in the way prescribed and at the time appointed.

column.name: text
column.value: These days should be remembered and observed in every generation by every family, and in every province and in every city. And these days of Purim should never cease to be celebrated by the Jews, nor should the memory of them die out among their descendants.

column.name: text
column.value: So Queen Esther, daughter of Abihail, along with Mordecai the Jew, wrote with full authority to confirm this second letter concerning Purim.

column.name: text
column.value: And Mordecai sent letters to all the Jews in the 127 provinces of the kingdom of Xerxes--words of goodwill and assurance--

column.name: text
column.value: to establish these days of Purim at their designated times, as Mordecai the Jew and Queen Esther had decreed for them, and as they had established for themselves and their descendants in regard to their times of fasting and lamentation.

column.name: text
column.value: Esther's decree confirmed these regulations about Purim, and it was written down in the records.

column.name: text
column.value: King Xerxes imposed tribute throughout the empire, to its distant shores.

column.name: text
column.value: And all his acts of power and might, together with a full account of the greatness of Mordecai to which the king had raised him, are they not written in the book of the annals of the kings of Media and Persia?

column.name: text
column.value: Mordecai the Jew was second in rank to King Xerxes, preeminent among the Jews, and held in high esteem by his many fellow Jews, because he worked for the good of his people and spoke up for the welfare of all the Jews.

column.name: text
column.value: In the land of Uz there lived a man whose name was Job. This man was blameless and upright; he feared God and shunned evil.

column.name: text
column.value: He had seven sons and three daughters,

column.name: text
column.value: and he owned seven thousand sheep, three thousand camels, five hundred yoke of oxen and five hundred donkeys, and had a large number of servants. He was the greatest man among all the people of the East.

column.name: text
column.value: His sons used to take turns holding feasts in their homes, and they would invite their three sisters to eat and drink with them.

column.name: text
column.value: When a period of feasting had run its course, Job would send and have them purified. Early in the morning he would sacrifice a burnt offering for each of them, thinking, "Perhaps my children have sinned and cursed God in their hearts." This was Job's regular custom.

column.name: text
column.value: One day the angels came to present themselves before the LORD, and Satan also came with them.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD said to Satan, "Where have you come from?" Satan answered the LORD, "From roaming through the earth and going back and forth in it."

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD said to Satan, "Have you considered my servant Job? There is no one on earth like him; he is blameless and upright, a man who fears God and shuns evil."

column.name: text
column.value: "Does Job fear God for nothing?" Satan replied.

column.name: text
column.value: "Have you not put a hedge around him and his household and everything he has? You have blessed the work of his hands, so that his flocks and herds are spread throughout the land.

column.name: text
column.value: But stretch out your hand and strike everything he has, and he will surely curse you to your face."

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD said to Satan, "Very well, then, everything he has is in your hands, but on the man himself do not lay a finger." Then Satan went out from the presence of the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: One day when Job's sons and daughters were feasting and drinking wine at the oldest brother's house,

column.name: text
column.value: a messenger came to Job and said, "The oxen were plowing and the donkeys were grazing nearby,

column.name: text
column.value: and the Sabeans attacked and carried them off. They put the servants to the sword, and I am the only one who has escaped to tell you!"

column.name: text
column.value: While he was still speaking, another messenger came and said, "The fire of God fell from the sky and burned up the sheep and the servants, and I am the only one who has escaped to tell you!"

column.name: text
column.value: While he was still speaking, another messenger came and said, "The Chaldeans formed three raiding parties and swept down on your camels and carried them off. They put the servants to the sword, and I am the only one who has escaped to tell you!"

column.name: text
column.value: While he was still speaking, yet another messenger came and said, "Your sons and daughters were feasting and drinking wine at the oldest brother's house,

column.name: text
column.value: when suddenly a mighty wind swept in from the desert and struck the four corners of the house. It collapsed on them and they are dead, and I am the only one who has escaped to tell you!"

column.name: text
column.value: At this, Job got up and tore his robe and shaved his head. Then he fell to the ground in worship

column.name: text
column.value: and said: "Naked I came from my mother's womb, and naked I will depart. The LORD gave and the LORD has taken away; may the name of the LORD be praised."

column.name: text
column.value: In all this, Job did not sin by charging God with wrongdoing.

column.name: text
column.value: On another day the angels came to present themselves before the LORD, and Satan also came with them to present himself before him.

column.name: text
column.value: And the LORD said to Satan, "Where have you come from?" Satan answered the LORD, "From roaming through the earth and going back and forth in it."

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD said to Satan, "Have you considered my servant Job? There is no one on earth like him; he is blameless and upright, a man who fears God and shuns evil. And he still maintains his integrity, though you incited me against him to ruin him without any reason."

column.name: text
column.value: "Skin for skin!" Satan replied. "A man will give all he has for his own life.

column.name: text
column.value: But stretch out your hand and strike his flesh and bones, and he will surely curse you to your face."

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD said to Satan, "Very well, then, he is in your hands; but you must spare his life."

column.name: text
column.value: So Satan went out from the presence of the LORD and afflicted Job with painful sores from the soles of his feet to the top of his head.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Job took a piece of broken pottery and scraped himself with it as he sat among the ashes.

column.name: text
column.value: His wife said to him, "Are you still holding on to your integrity? Curse God and die!"

column.name: text
column.value: He replied, "You are talking like a foolish woman. Shall we accept good from God, and not trouble?" In all this, Job did not sin in what he said.

column.name: text
column.value: When Job's three friends, Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite and Zophar the Naamathite, heard about all the troubles that had come upon him, they set out from their homes and met together by agreement to go and sympathize with him and comfort him.

column.name: text
column.value: When they saw him from a distance, they could hardly recognize him; they began to weep aloud, and they tore their robes and sprinkled dust on their heads.

column.name: text
column.value: Then they sat on the ground with him for seven days and seven nights. No one said a word to him, because they saw how great his suffering was.

column.name: text
column.value: After this, Job opened his mouth and cursed the day of his birth.

column.name: text
column.value: He said:

column.name: text
column.value: "May the day of my birth perish, and the night it was said, 'A boy is born!'

column.name: text
column.value: That day--may it turn to darkness; may God above not care about it; may no light shine upon it.

column.name: text
column.value: May darkness and deep shadow claim it once more; may a cloud settle over it; may blackness overwhelm its light.

column.name: text
column.value: That night--may thick darkness seize it; may it not be included among the days of the year nor be entered in any of the months.

column.name: text
column.value: May that night be barren; may no shout of joy be heard in it.

column.name: text
column.value: May those who curse days curse that day, those who are ready to rouse Leviathan.

column.name: text
column.value: May its morning stars become dark; may it wait for daylight in vain and not see the first rays of dawn,

column.name: text
column.value: for it did not shut the doors of the womb on me to hide trouble from my eyes.

column.name: text
column.value: "Why did I not perish at birth, and die as I came from the womb?

column.name: text
column.value: Why were there knees to receive me and breasts that I might be nursed?

column.name: text
column.value: For now I would be lying down in peace; I would be asleep and at rest

column.name: text
column.value: with kings and counselors of the earth, who built for themselves places now lying in ruins,

column.name: text
column.value: with rulers who had gold, who filled their houses with silver.

column.name: text
column.value: Or why was I not hidden in the ground like a stillborn child, like an infant who never saw the light of day?

column.name: text
column.value: There the wicked cease from turmoil, and there the weary are at rest.

column.name: text
column.value: Captives also enjoy their ease; they no longer hear the slave driver's shout.

column.name: text
column.value: The small and the great are there, and the slave is freed from his master.

column.name: text
column.value: "Why is light given to those in misery, and life to the bitter of soul,

column.name: text
column.value: to those who long for death that does not come, who search for it more than for hidden treasure,

column.name: text
column.value: who are filled with gladness and rejoice when they reach the grave?

column.name: text
column.value: Why is life given to a man whose way is hidden, whom God has hedged in?

column.name: text
column.value: For sighing comes to me instead of food; my groans pour out like water.

column.name: text
column.value: What I feared has come upon me; what I dreaded has happened to me.

column.name: text
column.value: I have no peace, no quietness; I have no rest, but only turmoil."

column.name: text
column.value: Then Eliphaz the Temanite replied:

column.name: text
column.value: "If someone ventures a word with you, will you be impatient? But who can keep from speaking?

column.name: text
column.value: Think how you have instructed many, how you have strengthened feeble hands.

column.name: text
column.value: Your words have supported those who stumbled; you have strengthened faltering knees.

column.name: text
column.value: But now trouble comes to you, and you are discouraged; it strikes you, and you are dismayed.

column.name: text
column.value: Should not your piety be your confidence and your blameless ways your hope?

column.name: text
column.value: "Consider now: Who, being innocent, has ever perished? Where were the upright ever destroyed?

column.name: text
column.value: As I have observed, those who plow evil and those who sow trouble reap it.

column.name: text
column.value: At the breath of God they are destroyed; at the blast of his anger they perish.

column.name: text
column.value: The lions may roar and growl, yet the teeth of the great lions are broken.

column.name: text
column.value: The lion perishes for lack of prey, and the cubs of the lioness are scattered.

column.name: text
column.value: "A word was secretly brought to me, my ears caught a whisper of it.

column.name: text
column.value: Amid disquieting dreams in the night, when deep sleep falls on men,

column.name: text
column.value: fear and trembling seized me and made all my bones shake.

column.name: text
column.value: A spirit glided past my face, and the hair on my body stood on end.

column.name: text
column.value: It stopped, but I could not tell what it was. A form stood before my eyes, and I heard a hushed voice:

column.name: text
column.value: 'Can a mortal be more righteous than God? Can a man be more pure than his Maker?

column.name: text
column.value: If God places no trust in his servants, if he charges his angels with error,

column.name: text
column.value: how much more those who live in houses of clay, whose foundations are in the dust, who are crushed more readily than a moth!

column.name: text
column.value: Between dawn and dusk they are broken to pieces; unnoticed, they perish forever.

column.name: text
column.value: Are not the cords of their tent pulled up, so that they die without wisdom?'

column.name: text
column.value: "Call if you will, but who will answer you? To which of the holy ones will you turn?

column.name: text
column.value: Resentment kills a fool, and envy slays the simple.

column.name: text
column.value: I myself have seen a fool taking root, but suddenly his house was cursed.

column.name: text
column.value: His children are far from safety, crushed in court without a defender.

column.name: text
column.value: The hungry consume his harvest, taking it even from among thorns, and the thirsty pant after his wealth.

column.name: text
column.value: For hardship does not spring from the soil, nor does trouble sprout from the ground.

column.name: text
column.value: Yet man is born to trouble as surely as sparks fly upward.

column.name: text
column.value: "But if it were I, I would appeal to God; I would lay my cause before him.

column.name: text
column.value: He performs wonders that cannot be fathomed, miracles that cannot be counted.

column.name: text
column.value: He bestows rain on the earth; he sends water upon the countryside.

column.name: text
column.value: The lowly he sets on high, and those who mourn are lifted to safety.

column.name: text
column.value: He thwarts the plans of the crafty, so that their hands achieve no success.

column.name: text
column.value: He catches the wise in their craftiness, and the schemes of the wily are swept away.

column.name: text
column.value: Darkness comes upon them in the daytime; at noon they grope as in the night.

column.name: text
column.value: He saves the needy from the sword in their mouth; he saves them from the clutches of the powerful.

column.name: text
column.value: So the poor have hope, and injustice shuts its mouth.

column.name: text
column.value: "Blessed is the man whom God corrects; so do not despise the discipline of the Almighty.

column.name: text
column.value: For he wounds, but he also binds up; he injures, but his hands also heal.

column.name: text
column.value: From six calamities he will rescue you; in seven no harm will befall you.

column.name: text
column.value: In famine he will ransom you from death, and in battle from the stroke of the sword.

column.name: text
column.value: You will be protected from the lash of the tongue, and need not fear when destruction comes.

column.name: text
column.value: You will laugh at destruction and famine, and need not fear the beasts of the earth.

column.name: text
column.value: For you will have a covenant with the stones of the field, and the wild animals will be at peace with you.

column.name: text
column.value: You will know that your tent is secure; you will take stock of your property and find nothing missing.

column.name: text
column.value: You will know that your children will be many, and your descendants like the grass of the earth.

column.name: text
column.value: You will come to the grave in full vigor, like sheaves gathered in season.

column.name: text
column.value: "We have examined this, and it is true. So hear it and apply it to yourself."

column.name: text
column.value: "Does not man have hard service on earth? Are not his days like those of a hired man?

column.name: text
column.value: Like a slave longing for the evening shadows, or a hired man waiting eagerly for his wages,

column.name: text
