column.value: so I have been allotted months of futility, and nights of misery have been assigned to me.

column.name: text
column.value: When I lie down I think, 'How long before I get up?' The night drags on, and I toss till dawn.

column.name: text
column.value: My body is clothed with worms and scabs, my skin is broken and festering.

column.name: text
column.value: "My days are swifter than a weaver's shuttle, and they come to an end without hope.

column.name: text
column.value: Remember, O God, that my life is but a breath; my eyes will never see happiness again.

column.name: text
column.value: The eye that now sees me will see me no longer; you will look for me, but I will be no more.

column.name: text
column.value: As a cloud vanishes and is gone, so he who goes down to the grave does not return.

column.name: text
column.value: He will never come to his house again; his place will know him no more.

column.name: text
column.value: "Therefore I will not keep silent; I will speak out in the anguish of my spirit, I will complain in the bitterness of my soul.

column.name: text
column.value: Am I the sea, or the monster of the deep, that you put me under guard?

column.name: text
column.value: When I think my bed will comfort me and my couch will ease my complaint,

column.name: text
column.value: even then you frighten me with dreams and terrify me with visions,

column.name: text
column.value: so that I prefer strangling and death, rather than this body of mine.

column.name: text
column.value: I despise my life; I would not live forever. Let me alone; my days have no meaning.

column.name: text
column.value: "What is man that you make so much of him, that you give him so much attention,

column.name: text
column.value: that you examine him every morning and test him every moment?

column.name: text
column.value: Will you never look away from me, or let me alone even for an instant?

column.name: text
column.value: If I have sinned, what have I done to you, O watcher of men? Why have you made me your target? Have I become a burden to you?

column.name: text
column.value: Why do you not pardon my offenses and forgive my sins? For I will soon lie down in the dust; you will search for me, but I will be no more."

column.name: text
column.value: Then Bildad the Shuhite replied:

column.name: text
column.value: "How long will you say such things? Your words are a blustering wind.

column.name: text
column.value: Does God pervert justice? Does the Almighty pervert what is right?

column.name: text
column.value: When your children sinned against him, he gave them over to the penalty of their sin.

column.name: text
column.value: But if you will look to God and plead with the Almighty,

column.name: text
column.value: if you are pure and upright, even now he will rouse himself on your behalf and restore you to your rightful place.

column.name: text
column.value: Your beginnings will seem humble, so prosperous will your future be.

column.name: text
column.value: "Ask the former generations and find out what their fathers learned,

column.name: text
column.value: for we were born only yesterday and know nothing, and our days on earth are but a shadow.

column.name: text
column.value: Will they not instruct you and tell you? Will they not bring forth words from their understanding?

column.name: text
column.value: Can papyrus grow tall where there is no marsh? Can reeds thrive without water?

column.name: text
column.value: While still growing and uncut, they wither more quickly than grass.

column.name: text
column.value: Such is the destiny of all who forget God; so perishes the hope of the godless.

column.name: text
column.value: What he trusts in is fragile; what he relies on is a spider's web.

column.name: text
column.value: He leans on his web, but it gives way; he clings to it, but it does not hold.

column.name: text
column.value: He is like a well-watered plant in the sunshine, spreading its shoots over the garden;

column.name: text
column.value: it entwines its roots around a pile of rocks and looks for a place among the stones.

column.name: text
column.value: But when it is torn from its spot, that place disowns it and says, 'I never saw you.'

column.name: text
column.value: Surely its life withers away, and from the soil other plants grow.

column.name: text
column.value: "Surely God does not reject a blameless man or strengthen the hands of evildoers.

column.name: text
column.value: He will yet fill your mouth with laughter and your lips with shouts of joy.

column.name: text
column.value: Your enemies will be clothed in shame, and the tents of the wicked will be no more."

column.name: text
column.value: Then Job replied:

column.name: text
column.value: "Indeed, I know that this is true. But how can a mortal be righteous before God?

column.name: text
column.value: Though one wished to dispute with him, he could not answer him one time out of a thousand.

column.name: text
column.value: His wisdom is profound, his power is vast. Who has resisted him and come out unscathed?

column.name: text
column.value: He moves mountains without their knowing it and overturns them in his anger.

column.name: text
column.value: He shakes the earth from its place and makes its pillars tremble.

column.name: text
column.value: He speaks to the sun and it does not shine; he seals off the light of the stars.

column.name: text
column.value: He alone stretches out the heavens and treads on the waves of the sea.

column.name: text
column.value: He is the Maker of the Bear and Orion, the Pleiades and the constellations of the south.

column.name: text
column.value: He performs wonders that cannot be fathomed, miracles that cannot be counted.

column.name: text
column.value: When he passes me, I cannot see him; when he goes by, I cannot perceive him.

column.name: text
column.value: If he snatches away, who can stop him? Who can say to him, 'What are you doing?'

column.name: text
column.value: God does not restrain his anger; even the cohorts of Rahab cowered at his feet.

column.name: text
column.value: "How then can I dispute with him? How can I find words to argue with him?

column.name: text
column.value: Though I were innocent, I could not answer him; I could only plead with my Judge for mercy.

column.name: text
column.value: Even if I summoned him and he responded, I do not believe he would give me a hearing.

column.name: text
column.value: He would crush me with a storm and multiply my wounds for no reason.

column.name: text
column.value: He would not let me regain my breath but would overwhelm me with misery.

column.name: text
column.value: If it is a matter of strength, he is mighty! And if it is a matter of justice, who will summon him?

column.name: text
column.value: Even if I were innocent, my mouth would condemn me; if I were blameless, it would pronounce me guilty.

column.name: text
column.value: "Although I am blameless, I have no concern for myself; I despise my own life.

column.name: text
column.value: It is all the same; that is why I say, 'He destroys both the blameless and the wicked.'

column.name: text
column.value: When a scourge brings sudden death, he mocks the despair of the innocent.

column.name: text
column.value: When a land falls into the hands of the wicked, he blindfolds its judges. If it is not he, then who is it?

column.name: text
column.value: "My days are swifter than a runner; they fly away without a glimpse of joy.

column.name: text
column.value: They skim past like boats of papyrus, like eagles swooping down on their prey.

column.name: text
column.value: If I say, 'I will forget my complaint, I will change my expression, and smile,'

column.name: text
column.value: I still dread all my sufferings, for I know you will not hold me innocent.

column.name: text
column.value: Since I am already found guilty, why should I struggle in vain?

column.name: text
column.value: Even if I washed myself with soap and my hands with washing soda,

column.name: text
column.value: you would plunge me into a slime pit so that even my clothes would detest me.

column.name: text
column.value: "He is not a man like me that I might answer him, that we might confront each other in court.

column.name: text
column.value: If only there were someone to arbitrate between us, to lay his hand upon us both,

column.name: text
column.value: someone to remove God's rod from me, so that his terror would frighten me no more.

column.name: text
column.value: Then I would speak up without fear of him, but as it now stands with me, I cannot.

column.name: text
column.value: "I loathe my very life; therefore I will give free rein to my complaint and speak out in the bitterness of my soul.

column.name: text
column.value: I will say to God: Do not condemn me, but tell me what charges you have against me.

column.name: text
column.value: Does it please you to oppress me, to spurn the work of your hands, while you smile on the schemes of the wicked?

column.name: text
column.value: Do you have eyes of flesh? Do you see as a mortal sees?

column.name: text
column.value: Are your days like those of a mortal or your years like those of a man,

column.name: text
column.value: that you must search out my faults and probe after my sin--

column.name: text
column.value: though you know that I am not guilty and that no one can rescue me from your hand?

column.name: text
column.value: "Your hands shaped me and made me. Will you now turn and destroy me?

column.name: text
column.value: Remember that you molded me like clay. Will you now turn me to dust again?

column.name: text
column.value: Did you not pour me out like milk and curdle me like cheese,

column.name: text
column.value: clothe me with skin and flesh and knit me together with bones and sinews?

column.name: text
column.value: You gave me life and showed me kindness, and in your providence watched over my spirit.

column.name: text
column.value: "But this is what you concealed in your heart, and I know that this was in your mind:

column.name: text
column.value: If I sinned, you would be watching me and would not let my offense go unpunished.

column.name: text
column.value: If I am guilty--woe to me! Even if I am innocent, I cannot lift my head, for I am full of shame and drowned in my affliction.

column.name: text
column.value: If I hold my head high, you stalk me like a lion and again display your awesome power against me.

column.name: text
column.value: You bring new witnesses against me and increase your anger toward me; your forces come against me wave upon wave.

column.name: text
column.value: "Why then did you bring me out of the womb? I wish I had died before any eye saw me.

column.name: text
column.value: If only I had never come into being, or had been carried straight from the womb to the grave!

column.name: text
column.value: Are not my few days almost over? Turn away from me so I can have a moment's joy

column.name: text
column.value: before I go to the place of no return, to the land of gloom and deep shadow,

column.name: text
column.value: to the land of deepest night, of deep shadow and disorder, where even the light is like darkness."

column.name: text
column.value: Then Zophar the Naamathite replied:

column.name: text
column.value: "Are all these words to go unanswered? Is this talker to be vindicated?

column.name: text
column.value: Will your idle talk reduce men to silence? Will no one rebuke you when you mock?

column.name: text
column.value: You say to God, 'My beliefs are flawless and I am pure in your sight.'

column.name: text
column.value: Oh, how I wish that God would speak, that he would open his lips against you

column.name: text
column.value: and disclose to you the secrets of wisdom, for true wisdom has two sides. Know this: God has even forgotten some of your sin.

column.name: text
column.value: "Can you fathom the mysteries of God? Can you probe the limits of the Almighty?

column.name: text
column.value: They are higher than the heavens--what can you do? They are deeper than the depths of the grave--what can you know?

column.name: text
column.value: Their measure is longer than the earth and wider than the sea.

column.name: text
column.value: "If he comes along and confines you in prison and convenes a court, who can oppose him?

column.name: text
column.value: Surely he recognizes deceitful men; and when he sees evil, does he not take note?

column.name: text
column.value: But a witless man can no more become wise than a wild donkey's colt can be born a man.

column.name: text
column.value: "Yet if you devote your heart to him and stretch out your hands to him,

column.name: text
column.value: if you put away the sin that is in your hand and allow no evil to dwell in your tent,

column.name: text
column.value: then you will lift up your face without shame; you will stand firm and without fear.

column.name: text
column.value: You will surely forget your trouble, recalling it only as waters gone by.

column.name: text
column.value: Life will be brighter than noonday, and darkness will become like morning.

column.name: text
column.value: You will be secure, because there is hope; you will look about you and take your rest in safety.

column.name: text
column.value: You will lie down, with no one to make you afraid, and many will court your favor.

column.name: text
column.value: But the eyes of the wicked will fail, and escape will elude them; their hope will become a dying gasp."

column.name: text
column.value: Then Job replied:

column.name: text
column.value: "Doubtless you are the people, and wisdom will die with you!

column.name: text
column.value: But I have a mind as well as you; I am not inferior to you. Who does not know all these things?

column.name: text
column.value: "I have become a laughingstock to my friends, though I called upon God and he answered--a mere laughingstock, though righteous and blameless!

column.name: text
column.value: Men at ease have contempt for misfortune as the fate of those whose feet are slipping.

column.name: text
column.value: The tents of marauders are undisturbed, and those who provoke God are secure--those who carry their god in their hands.

column.name: text
column.value: "But ask the animals, and they will teach you, or the birds of the air, and they will tell you;

column.name: text
column.value: or speak to the earth, and it will teach you, or let the fish of the sea inform you.

column.name: text
column.value: Which of all these does not know that the hand of the LORD has done this?

column.name: text
column.value: In his hand is the life of every creature and the breath of all mankind.

column.name: text
column.value: Does not the ear test words as the tongue tastes food?

column.name: text
column.value: Is not wisdom found among the aged? Does not long life bring understanding?

column.name: text
column.value: "To God belong wisdom and power; counsel and understanding are his.

column.name: text
column.value: What he tears down cannot be rebuilt; the man he imprisons cannot be released.

column.name: text
column.value: If he holds back the waters, there is drought; if he lets them loose, they devastate the land.

column.name: text
column.value: To him belong strength and victory; both deceived and deceiver are his.

column.name: text
column.value: He leads counselors away stripped and makes fools of judges.

column.name: text
column.value: He takes off the shackles put on by kings and ties a loincloth around their waist.

column.name: text
column.value: He leads priests away stripped and overthrows men long established.

column.name: text
column.value: He silences the lips of trusted advisers and takes away the discernment of elders.

column.name: text
column.value: He pours contempt on nobles and disarms the mighty.

column.name: text
column.value: He reveals the deep things of darkness and brings deep shadows into the light.

column.name: text
column.value: He makes nations great, and destroys them; he enlarges nations, and disperses them.

column.name: text
column.value: He deprives the leaders of the earth of their reason; he sends them wandering through a trackless waste.

column.name: text
column.value: They grope in darkness with no light; he makes them stagger like drunkards.

column.name: text
column.value: "Man born of woman is of few days and full of trouble.

column.name: text
column.value: He springs up like a flower and withers away; like a fleeting shadow, he does not endure.

column.name: text
column.value: Do you fix your eye on such a one? Will you bring him before you for judgment?

column.name: text
column.value: Who can bring what is pure from the impure? No one!

column.name: text
column.value: Man's days are determined; you have decreed the number of his months and have set limits he cannot exceed.

column.name: text
column.value: So look away from him and let him alone, till he has put in his time like a hired man.

column.name: text
column.value: "At least there is hope for a tree: If it is cut down, it will sprout again, and its new shoots will not fail.

column.name: text
column.value: Its roots may grow old in the ground and its stump die in the soil,

column.name: text
column.value: yet at the scent of water it will bud and put forth shoots like a plant.

column.name: text
column.value: But man dies and is laid low; he breathes his last and is no more.

column.name: text
column.value: As water disappears from the sea or a riverbed becomes parched and dry,

column.name: text
column.value: so man lies down and does not rise; till the heavens are no more, men will not awake or be roused from their sleep.

column.name: text
column.value: "If only you would hide me in the grave and conceal me till your anger has passed! If only you would set me a time and then remember me!

column.name: text
column.value: If a man dies, will he live again? All the days of my hard service I will wait for my renewal to come.

column.name: text
column.value: You will call and I will answer you; you will long for the creature your hands have made.

column.name: text
column.value: Surely then you will count my steps but not keep track of my sin.

column.name: text
column.value: My offenses will be sealed up in a bag; you will cover over my sin.

column.name: text
column.value: "But as a mountain erodes and crumbles and as a rock is moved from its place,

column.name: text
column.value: as water wears away stones and torrents wash away the soil, so you destroy man's hope.

column.name: text
column.value: You overpower him once for all, and he is gone; you change his countenance and send him away.

column.name: text
column.value: If his sons are honored, he does not know it; if they are brought low, he does not see it.

column.name: text
column.value: He feels but the pain of his own body and mourns only for himself."

column.name: text
column.value: "My eyes have seen all this, my ears have heard and understood it.

column.name: text
column.value: What you know, I also know; I am not inferior to you.

column.name: text
column.value: But I desire to speak to the Almighty and to argue my case with God.

column.name: text
column.value: You, however, smear me with lies; you are worthless physicians, all of you!

column.name: text
column.value: If only you would be altogether silent! For you, that would be wisdom.

column.name: text
column.value: Hear now my argument; listen to the plea of my lips.

column.name: text
column.value: Will you speak wickedly on God's behalf? Will you speak deceitfully for him?

column.name: text
column.value: Will you show him partiality? Will you argue the case for God?

column.name: text
column.value: Would it turn out well if he examined you? Could you deceive him as you might deceive men?

column.name: text
column.value: He would surely rebuke you if you secretly showed partiality.

column.name: text
column.value: Would not his splendor terrify you? Would not the dread of him fall on you?

column.name: text
column.value: Your maxims are proverbs of ashes; your defenses are defenses of clay.

column.name: text
column.value: "Keep silent and let me speak; then let come to me what may.

column.name: text
column.value: Why do I put myself in jeopardy and take my life in my hands?

column.name: text
column.value: Though he slay me, yet will I hope in him; I will surely defend my ways to his face.

column.name: text
column.value: Indeed, this will turn out for my deliverance, for no godless man would dare come before him!

column.name: text
column.value: Listen carefully to my words; let your ears take in what I say.

column.name: text
column.value: Now that I have prepared my case, I know I will be vindicated.

column.name: text
column.value: Can anyone bring charges against me? If so, I will be silent and die.

column.name: text
column.value: "Only grant me these two things, O God, and then I will not hide from you:

column.name: text
column.value: Withdraw your hand far from me, and stop frightening me with your terrors.

column.name: text
column.value: Then summon me and I will answer, or let me speak, and you reply.

column.name: text
column.value: How many wrongs and sins have I committed? Show me my offense and my sin.

column.name: text
column.value: Why do you hide your face and consider me your enemy?

column.name: text
column.value: Will you torment a windblown leaf? Will you chase after dry chaff?

column.name: text
column.value: For you write down bitter things against me and make me inherit the sins of my youth.

column.name: text
column.value: You fasten my feet in shackles; you keep close watch on all my paths by putting marks on the soles of my feet.

column.name: text
column.value: "So man wastes away like something rotten, like a garment eaten by moths.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Job replied:

column.name: text
column.value: "If only my anguish could be weighed and all my misery be placed on the scales!

column.name: text
column.value: It would surely outweigh the sand of the seas--no wonder my words have been impetuous.

column.name: text
column.value: The arrows of the Almighty are in me, my spirit drinks in their poison; God's terrors are marshaled against me.

column.name: text
column.value: Does a wild donkey bray when it has grass, or an ox bellow when it has fodder?

column.name: text
column.value: Is tasteless food eaten without salt, or is there flavor in the white of an egg?

column.name: text
column.value: I refuse to touch it; such food makes me ill.

column.name: text
column.value: "Oh, that I might have my request, that God would grant what I hope for,

column.name: text
column.value: that God would be willing to crush me, to let loose his hand and cut me off!

column.name: text
column.value: Then I would still have this consolation--my joy in unrelenting pain--that I had not denied the words of the Holy One.

column.name: text
column.value: "What strength do I have, that I should still hope? What prospects, that I should be patient?

column.name: text
column.value: Do I have the strength of stone? Is my flesh bronze?

column.name: text
column.value: Do I have any power to help myself, now that success has been driven from me?

column.name: text
column.value: "A despairing man should have the devotion of his friends, even though he forsakes the fear of the Almighty.

column.name: text
column.value: But my brothers are as undependable as intermittent streams, as the streams that overflow

column.name: text
column.value: when darkened by thawing ice and swollen with melting snow,

column.name: text
column.value: but that cease to flow in the dry season, and in the heat vanish from their channels.

column.name: text
column.value: Caravans turn aside from their routes; they go up into the wasteland and perish.

column.name: text
column.value: The caravans of Tema look for water, the traveling merchants of Sheba look in hope.

column.name: text
column.value: They are distressed, because they had been confident; they arrive there, only to be disappointed.

column.name: text
column.value: Now you too have proved to be of no help; you see something dreadful and are afraid.

column.name: text
column.value: Have I ever said, 'Give something on my behalf, pay a ransom for me from your wealth,

column.name: text
column.value: deliver me from the hand of the enemy, ransom me from the clutches of the ruthless'?

column.name: text
column.value: "Teach me, and I will be quiet; show me where I have been wrong.

column.name: text
column.value: How painful are honest words! But what do your arguments prove?

column.name: text
column.value: Do you mean to correct what I say, and treat the words of a despairing man as wind?

column.name: text
column.value: You would even cast lots for the fatherless and barter away your friend.

column.name: text
column.value: "But now be so kind as to look at me. Would I lie to your face?

column.name: text
column.value: Relent, do not be unjust; reconsider, for my integrity is at stake.

column.name: text
column.value: Is there any wickedness on my lips? Can my mouth not discern malice?

column.name: text
column.value: Then Eliphaz the Temanite replied:

column.name: text
column.value: "Would a wise man answer with empty notions or fill his belly with the hot east wind?

column.name: text
column.value: Would he argue with useless words, with speeches that have no value?

column.name: text
column.value: But you even undermine piety and hinder devotion to God.

column.name: text
column.value: Your sin prompts your mouth; you adopt the tongue of the crafty.

column.name: text
column.value: Your own mouth condemns you, not mine; your own lips testify against you.

column.name: text
column.value: "Are you the first man ever born? Were you brought forth before the hills?

column.name: text
column.value: Do you listen in on God's council? Do you limit wisdom to yourself?

column.name: text
column.value: What do you know that we do not know? What insights do you have that we do not have?

column.name: text
column.value: The gray-haired and the aged are on our side, men even older than your father.

column.name: text
column.value: Are God's consolations not enough for you, words spoken gently to you?

column.name: text
column.value: Why has your heart carried you away, and why do your eyes flash,

column.name: text
column.value: so that you vent your rage against God and pour out such words from your mouth?

column.name: text
column.value: "What is man, that he could be pure, or one born of woman, that he could be righteous?

column.name: text
column.value: If God places no trust in his holy ones, if even the heavens are not pure in his eyes,

column.name: text
column.value: how much less man, who is vile and corrupt, who drinks up evil like water!

column.name: text
column.value: "Listen to me and I will explain to you; let me tell you what I have seen,

column.name: text
column.value: what wise men have declared, hiding nothing received from their fathers

column.name: text
column.value: (to whom alone the land was given when no alien passed among them):

column.name: text
column.value: All his days the wicked man suffers torment, the ruthless through all the years stored up for him.

column.name: text
column.value: Terrifying sounds fill his ears; when all seems well, marauders attack him.

column.name: text
column.value: He despairs of escaping the darkness; he is marked for the sword.

column.name: text
column.value: He wanders about--food for vultures; he knows the day of darkness is at hand.

column.name: text
column.value: Distress and anguish fill him with terror; they overwhelm him, like a king poised to attack,

column.name: text
column.value: because he shakes his fist at God and vaunts himself against the Almighty,

column.name: text
column.value: defiantly charging against him with a thick, strong shield.

column.name: text
column.value: "Though his face is covered with fat and his waist bulges with flesh,

column.name: text
column.value: he will inhabit ruined towns and houses where no one lives, houses crumbling to rubble.

column.name: text
column.value: He will no longer be rich and his wealth will not endure, nor will his possessions spread over the land.

column.name: text
column.value: He will not escape the darkness; a flame will wither his shoots, and the breath of God's mouth will carry him away.

column.name: text
column.value: Let him not deceive himself by trusting what is worthless, for he will get nothing in return.

column.name: text
column.value: Before his time he will be paid in full, and his branches will not flourish.

column.name: text
column.value: He will be like a vine stripped of its unripe grapes, like an olive tree shedding its blossoms.

column.name: text
column.value: For the company of the godless will be barren, and fire will consume the tents of those who love bribes.

column.name: text
column.value: They conceive trouble and give birth to evil; their womb fashions deceit."

column.name: text
column.value: Then Job replied:

column.name: text
column.value: "I have heard many things like these; miserable comforters are you all!

column.name: text
column.value: Will your long-winded speeches never end? What ails you that you keep on arguing?

column.name: text
column.value: I also could speak like you, if you were in my place; I could make fine speeches against you and shake my head at you.

column.name: text
column.value: But my mouth would encourage you; comfort from my lips would bring you relief.

column.name: text
column.value: "Yet if I speak, my pain is not relieved; and if I refrain, it does not go away.

column.name: text
column.value: Surely, O God, you have worn me out; you have devastated my entire household.

column.name: text
column.value: You have bound me--and it has become a witness; my gauntness rises up and testifies against me.

column.name: text
column.value: God assails me and tears me in his anger and gnashes his teeth at me; my opponent fastens on me his piercing eyes.

column.name: text
column.value: Men open their mouths to jeer at me; they strike my cheek in scorn and unite together against me.

column.name: text
column.value: God has turned me over to evil men and thrown me into the clutches of the wicked.

column.name: text
column.value: All was well with me, but he shattered me; he seized me by the neck and crushed me. He has made me his target;

column.name: text
column.value: his archers surround me. Without pity, he pierces my kidneys and spills my gall on the ground.

column.name: text
column.value: Again and again he bursts upon me; he rushes at me like a warrior.

column.name: text
column.value: "I have sewed sackcloth over my skin and buried my brow in the dust.

column.name: text
column.value: My face is red with weeping, deep shadows ring my eyes;

column.name: text
column.value: yet my hands have been free of violence and my prayer is pure.

column.name: text
column.value: "O earth, do not cover my blood; may my cry never be laid to rest!

column.name: text
column.value: Even now my witness is in heaven; my advocate is on high.

column.name: text
column.value: My intercessor is my friend as my eyes pour out tears to God;

column.name: text
column.value: on behalf of a man he pleads with God as a man pleads for his friend.

column.name: text
column.value: "Only a few years will pass before I go on the journey of no return.

column.name: text
column.value: My spirit is broken, my days are cut short, the grave awaits me.

column.name: text
column.value: Surely mockers surround me; my eyes must dwell on their hostility.

column.name: text
column.value: "Give me, O God, the pledge you demand. Who else will put up security for me?

column.name: text
column.value: You have closed their minds to understanding; therefore you will not let them triumph.

column.name: text
column.value: If a man denounces his friends for reward, the eyes of his children will fail.

column.name: text
column.value: "God has made me a byword to everyone, a man in whose face people spit.

column.name: text
column.value: My eyes have grown dim with grief; my whole frame is but a shadow.

column.name: text
column.value: Upright men are appalled at this; the innocent are aroused against the ungodly.

column.name: text
column.value: Nevertheless, the righteous will hold to their ways, and those with clean hands will grow stronger.

column.name: text
column.value: "But come on, all of you, try again! I will not find a wise man among you.

column.name: text
column.value: My days have passed, my plans are shattered, and so are the desires of my heart.

column.name: text
column.value: These men turn night into day; in the face of darkness they say, 'Light is near.'

column.name: text
column.value: If the only home I hope for is the grave, if I spread out my bed in darkness,

column.name: text
column.value: if I say to corruption, 'You are my father,' and to the worm, 'My mother' or 'My sister,'

column.name: text
column.value: where then is my hope? Who can see any hope for me?

column.name: text
column.value: Will it go down to the gates of death? Will we descend together into the dust?"

column.name: text
column.value: Then Bildad the Shuhite replied:

column.name: text
column.value: "When will you end these speeches? Be sensible, and then we can talk.

column.name: text
column.value: Why are we regarded as cattle and considered stupid in your sight?

column.name: text
column.value: You who tear yourself to pieces in your anger, is the earth to be abandoned for your sake? Or must the rocks be moved from their place?

column.name: text
column.value: "The lamp of the wicked is snuffed out; the flame of his fire stops burning.

column.name: text
column.value: The light in his tent becomes dark; the lamp beside him goes out.

column.name: text
column.value: The vigor of his step is weakened; his own schemes throw him down.

column.name: text
column.value: His feet thrust him into a net and he wanders into its mesh.

column.name: text
column.value: A trap seizes him by the heel; a snare holds him fast.

column.name: text
column.value: A noose is hidden for him on the ground; a trap lies in his path.

column.name: text
column.value: Terrors startle him on every side and dog his every step.

column.name: text
column.value: Calamity is hungry for him; disaster is ready for him when he falls.

column.name: text
column.value: It eats away parts of his skin; death's firstborn devours his limbs.

column.name: text
column.value: He is torn from the security of his tent and marched off to the king of terrors.

column.name: text
column.value: Fire resides in his tent; burning sulfur is scattered over his dwelling.

column.name: text
column.value: His roots dry up below and his branches wither above.

column.name: text
column.value: The memory of him perishes from the earth; he has no name in the land.

column.name: text
column.value: He is driven from light into darkness and is banished from the world.

column.name: text
column.value: He has no offspring or descendants among his people, no survivor where once he lived.

column.name: text
column.value: Men of the west are appalled at his fate; men of the east are seized with horror.

column.name: text
column.value: Surely such is the dwelling of an evil man; such is the place of one who knows not God."

column.name: text
column.value: Then Job replied:

column.name: text
column.value: "How long will you torment me and crush me with words?

column.name: text
column.value: Ten times now you have reproached me; shamelessly you attack me.

column.name: text
column.value: If it is true that I have gone astray, my error remains my concern alone.

column.name: text
column.value: If indeed you would exalt yourselves above me and use my humiliation against me,

column.name: text
column.value: then know that God has wronged me and drawn his net around me.

column.name: text
column.value: "Though I cry, 'I've been wronged!' I get no response; though I call for help, there is no justice.

column.name: text
column.value: He has blocked my way so I cannot pass; he has shrouded my paths in darkness.

column.name: text
column.value: He has stripped me of my honor and removed the crown from my head.

column.name: text
column.value: He tears me down on every side till I am gone; he uproots my hope like a tree.

column.name: text
column.value: His anger burns against me; he counts me among his enemies.

column.name: text
column.value: His troops advance in force; they build a siege ramp against me and encamp around my tent.

column.name: text
column.value: "He has alienated my brothers from me; my acquaintances are completely estranged from me.

column.name: text
column.value: My kinsmen have gone away; my friends have forgotten me.

column.name: text
column.value: My guests and my maidservants count me a stranger; they look upon me as an alien.

column.name: text
column.value: I summon my servant, but he does not answer, though I beg him with my own mouth.

column.name: text
column.value: My breath is offensive to my wife; I am loathsome to my own brothers.

column.name: text
column.value: Even the little boys scorn me; when I appear, they ridicule me.

column.name: text
column.value: All my intimate friends detest me; those I love have turned against me.

column.name: text
column.value: I am nothing but skin and bones; I have escaped with only the skin of my teeth.

column.name: text
column.value: "Have pity on me, my friends, have pity, for the hand of God has struck me.

column.name: text
column.value: Why do you pursue me as God does? Will you never get enough of my flesh?

column.name: text
column.value: "Oh, that my words were recorded, that they were written on a scroll,

column.name: text
column.value: that they were inscribed with an iron tool on lead, or engraved in rock forever!

column.name: text
column.value: I know that my Redeemer lives, and that in the end he will stand upon the earth.

column.name: text
column.value: And after my skin has been destroyed, yet in my flesh I will see God;

column.name: text
column.value: I myself will see him with my own eyes--I, and not another. How my heart yearns within me!

column.name: text
column.value: "If you say, 'How we will hound him, since the root of the trouble lies in him,'

column.name: text
column.value: you should fear the sword yourselves; for wrath will bring punishment by the sword, and then you will know that there is judgment."

column.name: text
column.value: Then Zophar the Naamathite replied:

column.name: text
column.value: "My troubled thoughts prompt me to answer because I am greatly disturbed.

column.name: text
column.value: I hear a rebuke that dishonors me, and my understanding inspires me to reply.

column.name: text
column.value: "Surely you know how it has been from of old, ever since man was placed on the earth,

column.name: text
column.value: that the mirth of the wicked is brief, the joy of the godless lasts but a moment.

column.name: text
column.value: Though his pride reaches to the heavens and his head touches the clouds,

column.name: text
column.value: he will perish forever, like his own dung; those who have seen him will say, 'Where is he?'

column.name: text
column.value: Like a dream he flies away, no more to be found, banished like a vision of the night.

column.name: text
column.value: The eye that saw him will not see him again; his place will look on him no more.

column.name: text
column.value: His children must make amends to the poor; his own hands must give back his wealth.

column.name: text
column.value: The youthful vigor that fills his bones will lie with him in the dust.

column.name: text
column.value: "Though evil is sweet in his mouth and he hides it under his tongue,

column.name: text
column.value: though he cannot bear to let it go and keeps it in his mouth,

column.name: text
column.value: yet his food will turn sour in his stomach; it will become the venom of serpents within him.

column.name: text
column.value: He will spit out the riches he swallowed; God will make his stomach vomit them up.

column.name: text
column.value: He will suck the poison of serpents; the fangs of an adder will kill him.

column.name: text
column.value: He will not enjoy the streams, the rivers flowing with honey and cream.

column.name: text
column.value: What he toiled for he must give back uneaten; he will not enjoy the profit from his trading.

column.name: text
column.value: For he has oppressed the poor and left them destitute; he has seized houses he did not build.

column.name: text
column.value: "Surely he will have no respite from his craving; he cannot save himself by his treasure.

column.name: text
column.value: Nothing is left for him to devour; his prosperity will not endure.

column.name: text
column.value: In the midst of his plenty, distress will overtake him; the full force of misery will come upon him.

column.name: text
column.value: When he has filled his belly, God will vent his burning anger against him and rain down his blows upon him.

column.name: text
column.value: Though he flees from an iron weapon, a bronze-tipped arrow pierces him.

column.name: text
column.value: He pulls it out of his back, the gleaming point out of his liver. Terrors will come over him;

column.name: text
column.value: total darkness lies in wait for his treasures. A fire unfanned will consume him and devour what is left in his tent.

column.name: text
column.value: The heavens will expose his guilt; the earth will rise up against him.

column.name: text
column.value: A flood will carry off his house, rushing waters on the day of God's wrath.

column.name: text
column.value: Such is the fate God allots the wicked, the heritage appointed for them by God."

column.name: text
column.value: Then Job replied:

column.name: text
column.value: "Listen carefully to my words; let this be the consolation you give me.

column.name: text
column.value: Bear with me while I speak, and after I have spoken, mock on.

column.name: text
column.value: "Is my complaint directed to man? Why should I not be impatient?

column.name: text
column.value: Look at me and be astonished; clap your hand over your mouth.

column.name: text
column.value: When I think about this, I am terrified; trembling seizes my body.

column.name: text
column.value: Why do the wicked live on, growing old and increasing in power?

column.name: text
column.value: They see their children established around them, their offspring before their eyes.

column.name: text
column.value: Their homes are safe and free from fear; the rod of God is not upon them.

column.name: text
column.value: Their bulls never fail to breed; their cows calve and do not miscarry.

column.name: text
column.value: They send forth their children as a flock; their little ones dance about.

column.name: text
column.value: They sing to the music of tambourine and harp; they make merry to the sound of the flute.

column.name: text
column.value: They spend their years in prosperity and go down to the grave in peace.

column.name: text
column.value: Yet they say to God, 'Leave us alone! We have no desire to know your ways.

column.name: text
column.value: Who is the Almighty, that we should serve him? What would we gain by praying to him?'

column.name: text
column.value: But their prosperity is not in their own hands, so I stand aloof from the counsel of the wicked.

column.name: text
column.value: "Yet how often is the lamp of the wicked snuffed out? How often does calamity come upon them, the fate God allots in his anger?

column.name: text
column.value: How often are they like straw before the wind, like chaff swept away by a gale?

column.name: text
column.value: It is said,'God stores up a man's punishment for his sons.' Let him repay the man himself, so that he will know it!

column.name: text
column.value: Let his own eyes see his destruction; let him drink of the wrath of the Almighty.

column.name: text
column.value: For what does he care about the family he leaves behind when his allotted months come to an end?

column.name: text
column.value: "Can anyone teach knowledge to God, since he judges even the highest?

column.name: text
column.value: One man dies in full vigor, completely secure and at ease,

column.name: text
column.value: his body well nourished, his bones rich with marrow.

column.name: text
column.value: Another man dies in bitterness of soul, never having enjoyed anything good.

column.name: text
column.value: Side by side they lie in the dust, and worms cover them both.

column.name: text
column.value: "I know full well what you are thinking, the schemes by which you would wrong me.

column.name: text
column.value: You say, 'Where now is the great man's house, the tents where wicked men lived?'

column.name: text
column.value: Have you never questioned those who travel? Have you paid no regard to their accounts--

column.name: text
column.value: that the evil man is spared from the day of calamity, that he is delivered from the day of wrath?

column.name: text
column.value: Who denounces his conduct to his face? Who repays him for what he has done?

column.name: text
column.value: He is carried to the grave, and watch is kept over his tomb.

column.name: text
column.value: The soil in the valley is sweet to him; all men follow after him, and a countless throng goes before him.

column.name: text
column.value: "So how can you console me with your nonsense? Nothing is left of your answers but falsehood!"

column.name: text
column.value: Then Eliphaz the Temanite replied:

column.name: text
column.value: "Can a man be of benefit to God? Can even a wise man benefit him?

column.name: text
column.value: What pleasure would it give the Almighty if you were righteous? What would he gain if your ways were blameless?

column.name: text
column.value: "Is it for your piety that he rebukes you and brings charges against you?

column.name: text
column.value: Is not your wickedness great? Are not your sins endless?

column.name: text
column.value: You demanded security from your brothers for no reason; you stripped men of their clothing, leaving them naked.

column.name: text
column.value: You gave no water to the weary and you withheld food from the hungry,

column.name: text
column.value: though you were a powerful man, owning land--an honored man, living on it.

column.name: text
column.value: And you sent widows away empty-handed and broke the strength of the fatherless.

column.name: text
column.value: That is why snares are all around you, why sudden peril terrifies you,

column.name: text
column.value: why it is so dark you cannot see, and why a flood of water covers you.

column.name: text
column.value: "Is not God in the heights of heaven? And see how lofty are the highest stars!

column.name: text
column.value: Yet you say, 'What does God know? Does he judge through such darkness?

column.name: text
column.value: Thick clouds veil him, so he does not see us as he goes about in the vaulted heavens.'

column.name: text
column.value: Will you keep to the old path that evil men have trod?

column.name: text
column.value: They were carried off before their time, their foundations washed away by a flood.

column.name: text
column.value: They said to God, 'Leave us alone! What can the Almighty do to us?'

column.name: text
column.value: Yet it was he who filled their houses with good things, so I stand aloof from the counsel of the wicked.

column.name: text
column.value: "The righteous see their ruin and rejoice; the innocent mock them, saying,

column.name: text
column.value: 'Surely our foes are destroyed, and fire devours their wealth.'

column.name: text
column.value: "Submit to God and be at peace with him; in this way prosperity will come to you.

column.name: text
column.value: Accept instruction from his mouth and lay up his words in your heart.

column.name: text
column.value: If you return to the Almighty, you will be restored: If you remove wickedness far from your tent

column.name: text
column.value: and assign your nuggets to the dust, your gold of Ophir to the rocks in the ravines,

column.name: text
column.value: then the Almighty will be your gold, the choicest silver for you.

column.name: text
column.value: Surely then you will find delight in the Almighty and will lift up your face to God.

column.name: text
column.value: You will pray to him, and he will hear you, and you will fulfill your vows.

column.name: text
column.value: What you decide on will be done, and light will shine on your ways.

column.name: text
column.value: When men are brought low and you say, 'Lift them up!' then he will save the downcast.

column.name: text
column.value: He will deliver even one who is not innocent, who will be delivered through the cleanness of your hands."

column.name: text
column.value: Then Job replied:

column.name: text
column.value: "Even today my complaint is bitter; his hand is heavy in spite of my groaning.

column.name: text
column.value: If only I knew where to find him; if only I could go to his dwelling!

column.name: text
column.value: I would state my case before him and fill my mouth with arguments.

column.name: text
column.value: I would find out what he would answer me, and consider what he would say.

column.name: text
column.value: Would he oppose me with great power? No, he would not press charges against me.

column.name: text
column.value: There an upright man could present his case before him, and I would be delivered forever from my judge.

column.name: text
column.value: "But if I go to the east, he is not there; if I go to the west, I do not find him.

column.name: text
column.value: When he is at work in the north, I do not see him; when he turns to the south, I catch no glimpse of him.

column.name: text
column.value: But he knows the way that I take; when he has tested me, I will come forth as gold.

column.name: text
column.value: My feet have closely followed his steps; I have kept to his way without turning aside.

column.name: text
column.value: I have not departed from the commands of his lips; I have treasured the words of his mouth more than my daily bread.

column.name: text
column.value: "But he stands alone, and who can oppose him? He does whatever he pleases.

column.name: text
column.value: He carries out his decree against me, and many such plans he still has in store.

column.name: text
column.value: That is why I am terrified before him; when I think of all this, I fear him.

column.name: text
column.value: God has made my heart faint; the Almighty has terrified me.

column.name: text
column.value: Yet I am not silenced by the darkness, by the thick darkness that covers my face.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Bildad the Shuhite replied:

column.name: text
column.value: "Dominion and awe belong to God; he establishes order in the heights of heaven.

column.name: text
column.value: Can his forces be numbered? Upon whom does his light not rise?

column.name: text
column.value: How then can a man be righteous before God? How can one born of woman be pure?

column.name: text
column.value: If even the moon is not bright and the stars are not pure in his eyes,

column.name: text
column.value: how much less man, who is but a maggot--a son of man, who is only a worm!"

column.name: text
column.value: Then Job replied:

column.name: text
column.value: "How you have helped the powerless! How you have saved the arm that is feeble!

column.name: text
column.value: What advice you have offered to one without wisdom! And what great insight you have displayed!

column.name: text
column.value: Who has helped you utter these words? And whose spirit spoke from your mouth?

column.name: text
column.value: "The dead are in deep anguish, those beneath the waters and all that live in them.

column.name: text
column.value: Death is naked before God; Destruction lies uncovered.

column.name: text
column.value: He spreads out the northern skies over empty space; he suspends the earth over nothing.

column.name: text
column.value: He wraps up the waters in his clouds, yet the clouds do not burst under their weight.

column.name: text
column.value: He covers the face of the full moon, spreading his clouds over it.

column.name: text
column.value: He marks out the horizon on the face of the waters for a boundary between light and darkness.

column.name: text
column.value: The pillars of the heavens quake, aghast at his rebuke.

column.name: text
column.value: By his power he churned up the sea; by his wisdom he cut Rahab to pieces.

column.name: text
column.value: By his breath the skies became fair; his hand pierced the gliding serpent.

column.name: text
column.value: And these are but the outer fringe of his works; how faint the whisper we hear of him! Who then can understand the thunder of his power?"

column.name: text
column.value: "Why does the Almighty not set times for judgment? Why must those who know him look in vain for such days?

column.name: text
column.value: Men move boundary stones; they pasture flocks they have stolen.

column.name: text
column.value: They drive away the orphan's donkey and take the widow's ox in pledge.

column.name: text
column.value: They thrust the needy from the path and force all the poor of the land into hiding.

column.name: text
column.value: Like wild donkeys in the desert, the poor go about their labor of foraging food; the wasteland provides food for their children.

column.name: text
column.value: They gather fodder in the fields and glean in the vineyards of the wicked.

column.name: text
column.value: Lacking clothes, they spend the night naked; they have nothing to cover themselves in the cold.

column.name: text
column.value: They are drenched by mountain rains and hug the rocks for lack of shelter.

column.name: text
column.value: The fatherless child is snatched from the breast; the infant of the poor is seized for a debt.

column.name: text
column.value: Lacking clothes, they go about naked; they carry the sheaves, but still go hungry.

column.name: text
column.value: They crush olives among the terraces; they tread the winepresses, yet suffer thirst.

column.name: text
column.value: The groans of the dying rise from the city, and the souls of the wounded cry out for help. But God charges no one with wrongdoing.

column.name: text
column.value: "There are those who rebel against the light, who do not know its ways or stay in its paths.

column.name: text
column.value: When daylight is gone, the murderer rises up and kills the poor and needy; in the night he steals forth like a thief.

column.name: text
column.value: The eye of the adulterer watches for dusk; he thinks, 'No eye will see me,' and he keeps his face concealed.

column.name: text
column.value: In the dark, men break into houses, but by day they shut themselves in; they want nothing to do with the light.

column.name: text
column.value: For all of them, deep darkness is their morning; they make friends with the terrors of darkness.

column.name: text
column.value: "Yet they are foam on the surface of the water; their portion of the land is cursed, so that no one goes to the vineyards.

column.name: text
column.value: As heat and drought snatch away the melted snow, so the grave snatches away those who have sinned.

column.name: text
column.value: The womb forgets them, the worm feasts on them; evil men are no longer remembered but are broken like a tree.

column.name: text
column.value: They prey on the barren and childless woman, and to the widow show no kindness.

column.name: text
column.value: But God drags away the mighty by his power; though they become established, they have no assurance of life.

column.name: text
column.value: He may let them rest in a feeling of security, but his eyes are on their ways.

column.name: text
column.value: For a little while they are exalted, and then they are gone; they are brought low and gathered up like all others; they are cut off like heads of grain.

column.name: text
column.value: "If this is not so, who can prove me false and reduce my words to nothing?"

column.name: text
column.value: And Job continued his discourse:

column.name: text
column.value: "As surely as God lives, who has denied me justice, the Almighty, who has made me taste bitterness of soul,

column.name: text
column.value: as long as I have life within me, the breath of God in my nostrils,

column.name: text
column.value: my lips will not speak wickedness, and my tongue will utter no deceit.

column.name: text
column.value: I will never admit you are in the right; till I die, I will not deny my integrity.

column.name: text
column.value: I will maintain my righteousness and never let go of it; my conscience will not reproach me as long as I live.

column.name: text
column.value: "May my enemies be like the wicked, my adversaries like the unjust!

column.name: text
column.value: For what hope has the godless when he is cut off, when God takes away his life?

column.name: text
column.value: Does God listen to his cry when distress comes upon him?

column.name: text
column.value: Will he find delight in the Almighty? Will he call upon God at all times?

column.name: text
column.value: "I will teach you about the power of God; the ways of the Almighty I will not conceal.

column.name: text
column.value: You have all seen this yourselves. Why then this meaningless talk?

column.name: text
column.value: "Here is the fate God allots to the wicked, the heritage a ruthless man receives from the Almighty:

column.name: text
column.value: However many his children, their fate is the sword; his offspring will never have enough to eat.

column.name: text
column.value: The plague will bury those who survive him, and their widows will not weep for them.

column.name: text
column.value: Though he heaps up silver like dust and clothes like piles of clay,

column.name: text
column.value: what he lays up the righteous will wear, and the innocent will divide his silver.

column.name: text
column.value: The house he builds is like a moth's cocoon, like a hut made by a watchman.

column.name: text
column.value: He lies down wealthy, but will do so no more; when he opens his eyes, all is gone.

column.name: text
column.value: Terrors overtake him like a flood; a tempest snatches him away in the night.

column.name: text
column.value: The east wind carries him off, and he is gone; it sweeps him out of his place.

column.name: text
column.value: It hurls itself against him without mercy as he flees headlong from its power.

column.name: text
column.value: It claps its hands in derision and hisses him out of his place.

column.name: text
column.value: "There is a mine for silver and a place where gold is refined.

column.name: text
column.value: Iron is taken from the earth, and copper is smelted from ore.

column.name: text
column.value: Man puts an end to the darkness; he searches the farthest recesses for ore in the blackest darkness.

column.name: text
column.value: Far from where people dwell he cuts a shaft, in places forgotten by the foot of man; far from men he dangles and sways.

column.name: text
column.value: The earth, from which food comes, is transformed below as by fire;

column.name: text
column.value: sapphires come from its rocks, and its dust contains nuggets of gold.

column.name: text
column.value: No bird of prey knows that hidden path, no falcon's eye has seen it.

column.name: text
column.value: Proud beasts do not set foot on it, and no lion prowls there.

column.name: text
column.value: Man's hand assaults the flinty rock and lays bare the roots of the mountains.

column.name: text
column.value: He tunnels through the rock; his eyes see all its treasures.

column.name: text
column.value: He searches the sources of the rivers and brings hidden things to light.

column.name: text
column.value: "But where can wisdom be found? Where does understanding dwell?

column.name: text
column.value: Man does not comprehend its worth; it cannot be found in the land of the living.

column.name: text
column.value: The deep says, 'It is not in me'; the sea says, 'It is not with me.'

column.name: text
column.value: It cannot be bought with the finest gold, nor can its price be weighed in silver.

column.name: text
column.value: It cannot be bought with the gold of Ophir, with precious onyx or sapphires.

column.name: text
column.value: Neither gold nor crystal can compare with it, nor can it be had for jewels of gold.

column.name: text
column.value: Coral and jasper are not worthy of mention; the price of wisdom is beyond rubies.

column.name: text
column.value: The topaz of Cush cannot compare with it; it cannot be bought with pure gold.

column.name: text
column.value: "Where then does wisdom come from? Where does understanding dwell?

column.name: text
column.value: It is hidden from the eyes of every living thing, concealed even from the birds of the air.

column.name: text
column.value: Destruction and Death say, 'Only a rumor of it has reached our ears.'

column.name: text
column.value: God understands the way to it and he alone knows where it dwells,

column.name: text
column.value: for he views the ends of the earth and sees everything under the heavens.

column.name: text
column.value: When he established the force of the wind and measured out the waters,

column.name: text
column.value: when he made a decree for the rain and a path for the thunderstorm,

column.name: text
column.value: then he looked at wisdom and appraised it; he confirmed it and tested it.

column.name: text
column.value: And he said to man, 'The fear of the Lord--that is wisdom, and to shun evil is understanding.'"

column.name: text
column.value: Job continued his discourse:

column.name: text
column.value: "How I long for the months gone by, for the days when God watched over me,

column.name: text
column.value: when his lamp shone upon my head and by his light I walked through darkness!

column.name: text
column.value: Oh, for the days when I was in my prime, when God's intimate friendship blessed my house,

column.name: text
column.value: when the Almighty was still with me and my children were around me,

column.name: text
column.value: when my path was drenched with cream and the rock poured out for me streams of olive oil.

column.name: text
column.value: "When I went to the gate of the city and took my seat in the public square,

column.name: text
column.value: the young men saw me and stepped aside and the old men rose to their feet;

column.name: text
column.value: the chief men refrained from speaking and covered their mouths with their hands;

column.name: text
column.value: the voices of the nobles were hushed, and their tongues stuck to the roof of their mouths.

column.name: text
column.value: Whoever heard me spoke well of me, and those who saw me commended me,

column.name: text
column.value: because I rescued the poor who cried for help, and the fatherless who had none to assist him.

column.name: text
column.value: The man who was dying blessed me; I made the widow's heart sing.

column.name: text
column.value: I put on righteousness as my clothing; justice was my robe and my turban.

column.name: text
column.value: I was eyes to the blind and feet to the lame.

column.name: text
column.value: I was a father to the needy; I took up the case of the stranger.

column.name: text
column.value: I broke the fangs of the wicked and snatched the victims from their teeth.

column.name: text
column.value: "I thought, 'I will die in my own house, my days as numerous as the grains of sand.

column.name: text
column.value: My roots will reach to the water, and the dew will lie all night on my branches.

column.name: text
column.value: My glory will remain fresh in me, the bow ever new in my hand.'

column.name: text
column.value: "Men listened to me expectantly, waiting in silence for my counsel.

column.name: text
column.value: After I had spoken, they spoke no more; my words fell gently on their ears.

column.name: text
column.value: They waited for me as for showers and drank in my words as the spring rain.

column.name: text
column.value: When I smiled at them, they scarcely believed it; the light of my face was precious to them.

column.name: text
column.value: I chose the way for them and sat as their chief; I dwelt as a king among his troops; I was like one who comforts mourners.

column.name: text
column.value: "But now they mock me, men younger than I, whose fathers I would have disdained to put with my sheep dogs.

column.name: text
column.value: Of what use was the strength of their hands to me, since their vigor had gone from them?

column.name: text
column.value: Haggard from want and hunger, they roamed the parched land in desolate wastelands at night.

column.name: text
column.value: In the brush they gathered salt herbs, and their food was the root of the broom tree.

column.name: text
column.value: They were banished from their fellow men, shouted at as if they were thieves.

column.name: text
column.value: They were forced to live in the dry stream beds, among the rocks and in holes in the ground.

column.name: text
column.value: They brayed among the bushes and huddled in the undergrowth.

column.name: text
column.value: A base and nameless brood, they were driven out of the land.

column.name: text
column.value: "And now their sons mock me in song; I have become a byword among them.

column.name: text
column.value: They detest me and keep their distance; they do not hesitate to spit in my face.

column.name: text
column.value: Now that God has unstrung my bow and afflicted me, they throw off restraint in my presence.

column.name: text
column.value: On my right the tribe attacks; they lay snares for my feet, they build their siege ramps against me.

column.name: text
column.value: They break up my road; they succeed in destroying me--without anyone's helping them.

column.name: text
column.value: They advance as through a gaping breach; amid the ruins they come rolling in.

column.name: text
column.value: Terrors overwhelm me; my dignity is driven away as by the wind, my safety vanishes like a cloud.

column.name: text
column.value: "And now my life ebbs away; days of suffering grip me.

column.name: text
column.value: Night pierces my bones; my gnawing pains never rest.

column.name: text
column.value: In his great power God becomes like clothing to me; he binds me like the neck of my garment.

column.name: text
column.value: He throws me into the mud, and I am reduced to dust and ashes.

column.name: text
column.value: "I cry out to you, O God, but you do not answer; I stand up, but you merely look at me.

column.name: text
column.value: You turn on me ruthlessly; with the might of your hand you attack me.

column.name: text
column.value: You snatch me up and drive me before the wind; you toss me about in the storm.

column.name: text
column.value: I know you will bring me down to death, to the place appointed for all the living.

column.name: text
column.value: "Surely no one lays a hand on a broken man when he cries for help in his distress.

column.name: text
column.value: Have I not wept for those in trouble? Has not my soul grieved for the poor?

column.name: text
column.value: Yet when I hoped for good, evil came; when I looked for light, then came darkness.

column.name: text
column.value: The churning inside me never stops; days of suffering confront me.

column.name: text
column.value: I go about blackened, but not by the sun; I stand up in the assembly and cry for help.

column.name: text
column.value: I have become a brother of jackals, a companion of owls.

column.name: text
column.value: My skin grows black and peels; my body burns with fever.

column.name: text
column.value: My harp is tuned to mourning, and my flute to the sound of wailing.

column.name: text
column.value: "I made a covenant with my eyes not to look lustfully at a girl.

column.name: text
column.value: For what is man's lot from God above, his heritage from the Almighty on high?

column.name: text
column.value: Is it not ruin for the wicked, disaster for those who do wrong?

column.name: text
column.value: Does he not see my ways and count my every step?

column.name: text
column.value: "If I have walked in falsehood or my foot has hurried after deceit--

column.name: text
column.value: let God weigh me in honest scales and he will know that I am blameless--

column.name: text
column.value: if my steps have turned from the path, if my heart has been led by my eyes, or if my hands have been defiled,

column.name: text
column.value: then may others eat what I have sown, and may my crops be uprooted.

column.name: text
column.value: "If my heart has been enticed by a woman, or if I have lurked at my neighbor's door,

column.name: text
column.value: then may my wife grind another man's grain, and may other men sleep with her.

column.name: text
column.value: For that would have been shameful, a sin to be judged.

column.name: text
column.value: It is a fire that burns to Destruction; it would have uprooted my harvest.

column.name: text
column.value: "If I have denied justice to my menservants and maidservants when they had a grievance against me,

column.name: text
column.value: what will I do when God confronts me? What will I answer when called to account?

column.name: text
column.value: Did not he who made me in the womb make them? Did not the same one form us both within our mothers?

column.name: text
column.value: "If I have denied the desires of the poor or let the eyes of the widow grow weary,

column.name: text
column.value: if I have kept my bread to myself, not sharing it with the fatherless--

column.name: text
column.value: but from my youth I reared him as would a father, and from my birth I guided the widow--

column.name: text
column.value: if I have seen anyone perishing for lack of clothing, or a needy man without a garment,

column.name: text
column.value: and his heart did not bless me for warming him with the fleece from my sheep,

column.name: text
column.value: if I have raised my hand against the fatherless, knowing that I had influence in court,

column.name: text
column.value: then let my arm fall from the shoulder, let it be broken off at the joint.

column.name: text
column.value: For I dreaded destruction from God, and for fear of his splendor I could not do such things.

column.name: text
column.value: "If I have put my trust in gold or said to pure gold, 'You are my security,'

column.name: text
column.value: if I have rejoiced over my great wealth, the fortune my hands had gained,

column.name: text
column.value: if I have regarded the sun in its radiance or the moon moving in splendor,

column.name: text
column.value: so that my heart was secretly enticed and my hand offered them a kiss of homage,

column.name: text
column.value: then these also would be sins to be judged, for I would have been unfaithful to God on high.

column.name: text
column.value: "If I have rejoiced at my enemy's misfortune or gloated over the trouble that came to him--

column.name: text
column.value: I have not allowed my mouth to sin by invoking a curse against his life--

column.name: text
column.value: if the men of my household have never said, 'Who has not had his fill of Job's meat?'--

column.name: text
column.value: but no stranger had to spend the night in the street, for my door was always open to the traveler--

column.name: text
column.value: if I have concealed my sin as men do, by hiding my guilt in my heart

column.name: text
column.value: because I so feared the crowd and so dreaded the contempt of the clans that I kept silent and would not go outside

column.name: text
column.value: ("Oh, that I had someone to hear me! I sign now my defense--let the Almighty answer me; let my accuser put his indictment in writing.

column.name: text
column.value: Surely I would wear it on my shoulder, I would put it on like a crown.

column.name: text
column.value: I would give him an account of my every step; like a prince I would approach him.)--

column.name: text
column.value: "if my land cries out against me and all its furrows are wet with tears,

column.name: text
column.value: if I have devoured its yield without payment or broken the spirit of its tenants,

column.name: text
column.value: then let briers come up instead of wheat and weeds instead of barley." The words of Job are ended.

column.name: text
column.value: So these three men stopped answering Job, because he was righteous in his own eyes.

column.name: text
column.value: But Elihu son of Barakel the Buzite, of the family of Ram, became very angry with Job for justifying himself rather than God.

column.name: text
column.value: He was also angry with the three friends, because they had found no way to refute Job, and yet had condemned him.

column.name: text
column.value: Now Elihu had waited before speaking to Job because they were older than he.

column.name: text
column.value: But when he saw that the three men had nothing more to say, his anger was aroused.

column.name: text
column.value: So Elihu son of Barakel the Buzite said: "I am young in years, and you are old; that is why I was fearful, not daring to tell you what I know.

column.name: text
column.value: I thought, 'Age should speak; advanced years should teach wisdom.'

column.name: text
column.value: But it is the spirit in a man, the breath of the Almighty, that gives him understanding.

column.name: text
column.value: It is not only the old who are wise, not only the aged who understand what is right.

column.name: text
column.value: "Therefore I say: Listen to me; I too will tell you what I know.

column.name: text
column.value: I waited while you spoke, I listened to your reasoning; while you were searching for words,

column.name: text
column.value: I gave you my full attention. But not one of you has proved Job wrong; none of you has answered his arguments.

column.name: text
column.value: Do not say, 'We have found wisdom; let God refute him, not man.'

column.name: text
column.value: But Job has not marshaled his words against me, and I will not answer him with your arguments.

column.name: text
column.value: "They are dismayed and have no more to say; words have failed them.

column.name: text
column.value: Must I wait, now that they are silent, now that they stand there with no reply?

column.name: text
column.value: I too will have my say; I too will tell what I know.

column.name: text
column.value: For I am full of words, and the spirit within me compels me;

column.name: text
column.value: inside I am like bottled-up wine, like new wineskins ready to burst.

column.name: text
column.value: I must speak and find relief; I must open my lips and reply.

column.name: text
column.value: I will show partiality to no one, nor will I flatter any man;

column.name: text
column.value: for if I were skilled in flattery, my Maker would soon take me away.

column.name: text
column.value: "But now, Job, listen to my words; pay attention to everything I say.

column.name: text
column.value: I am about to open my mouth; my words are on the tip of my tongue.

column.name: text
column.value: My words come from an upright heart; my lips sincerely speak what I know.

column.name: text
column.value: The Spirit of God has made me; the breath of the Almighty gives me life.

column.name: text
column.value: Answer me then, if you can; prepare yourself and confront me.

column.name: text
column.value: I am just like you before God; I too have been taken from clay.

column.name: text
column.value: No fear of me should alarm you, nor should my hand be heavy upon you.

column.name: text
column.value: "But you have said in my hearing--I heard the very words--

column.name: text
column.value: 'I am pure and without sin; I am clean and free from guilt.

column.name: text
column.value: Yet God has found fault with me; he considers me his enemy.

column.name: text
column.value: He fastens my feet in shackles; he keeps close watch on all my paths.'

column.name: text
column.value: "But I tell you, in this you are not right, for God is greater than man.

column.name: text
column.value: Why do you complain to him that he answers none of man's words?

column.name: text
column.value: For God does speak--now one way, now another--though man may not perceive it.

column.name: text
column.value: In a dream, in a vision of the night, when deep sleep falls on men as they slumber in their beds,

column.name: text
column.value: he may speak in their ears and terrify them with warnings,

column.name: text
column.value: to turn man from wrongdoing and keep him from pride,

column.name: text
column.value: to preserve his soul from the pit, his life from perishing by the sword.

column.name: text
column.value: Or a man may be chastened on a bed of pain with constant distress in his bones,

column.name: text
column.value: so that his very being finds food repulsive and his soul loathes the choicest meal.

column.name: text
column.value: His flesh wastes away to nothing, and his bones, once hidden, now stick out.

column.name: text
column.value: His soul draws near to the pit, and his life to the messengers of death.

column.name: text
column.value: "Yet if there is an angel on his side as a mediator, one out of a thousand, to tell a man what is right for him,

column.name: text
column.value: to be gracious to him and say, 'Spare him from going down to the pit; I have found a ransom for him'--

column.name: text
column.value: then his flesh is renewed like a child's; it is restored as in the days of his youth.

column.name: text
column.value: He prays to God and finds favor with him, he sees God's face and shouts for joy; he is restored by God to his righteous state.

column.name: text
column.value: Then he comes to men and says, 'I sinned, and perverted what was right, but I did not get what I deserved.

column.name: text
column.value: He redeemed my soul from going down to the pit, and I will live to enjoy the light.'

column.name: text
column.value: "God does all these things to a man--twice, even three times--

column.name: text
column.value: to turn back his soul from the pit, that the light of life may shine on him.

column.name: text
column.value: "Pay attention, Job, and listen to me; be silent, and I will speak.

column.name: text
column.value: If you have anything to say, answer me; speak up, for I want you to be cleared.

column.name: text
column.value: But if not, then listen to me; be silent, and I will teach you wisdom."

column.name: text
column.value: Then Elihu said:

column.name: text
column.value: "Hear my words, you wise men; listen to me, you men of learning.

column.name: text
column.value: For the ear tests words as the tongue tastes food.

column.name: text
column.value: Let us discern for ourselves what is right; let us learn together what is good.

column.name: text
column.value: "Job says, 'I am innocent, but God denies me justice.

column.name: text
column.value: Although I am right, I am considered a liar; although I am guiltless, his arrow inflicts an incurable wound.'

column.name: text
column.value: What man is like Job, who drinks scorn like water?

column.name: text
column.value: He keeps company with evildoers; he associates with wicked men.

column.name: text
column.value: For he says, 'It profits a man nothing when he tries to please God.'

column.name: text
column.value: "So listen to me, you men of understanding. Far be it from God to do evil, from the Almighty to do wrong.

column.name: text
