column.value: and poverty will come on you like a bandit and scarcity like an armed man.

column.name: text
column.value: These are more proverbs of Solomon, copied by the men of Hezekiah king of Judah:

column.name: text
column.value: It is the glory of God to conceal a matter; to search out a matter is the glory of kings.

column.name: text
column.value: As the heavens are high and the earth is deep, so the hearts of kings are unsearchable.

column.name: text
column.value: Remove the dross from the silver, and out comes material for the silversmith;

column.name: text
column.value: remove the wicked from the king's presence, and his throne will be established through righteousness.

column.name: text
column.value: Do not exalt yourself in the king's presence, and do not claim a place among great men;

column.name: text
column.value: it is better for him to say to you, "Come up here," than for him to humiliate you before a nobleman. What you have seen with your eyes

column.name: text
column.value: do not bring hastily to court, for what will you do in the end if your neighbor puts you to shame?

column.name: text
column.value: If you argue your case with a neighbor, do not betray another man's confidence,

column.name: text
column.value: or he who hears it may shame you and you will never lose your bad reputation.

column.name: text
column.value: A word aptly spoken is like apples of gold in settings of silver.

column.name: text
column.value: Like an earring of gold or an ornament of fine gold is a wise man's rebuke to a listening ear.

column.name: text
column.value: Like the coolness of snow at harvest time is a trustworthy messenger to those who send him; he refreshes the spirit of his masters.

column.name: text
column.value: Like clouds and wind without rain is a man who boasts of gifts he does not give.

column.name: text
column.value: Through patience a ruler can be persuaded, and a gentle tongue can break a bone.

column.name: text
column.value: If you find honey, eat just enough--too much of it, and you will vomit.

column.name: text
column.value: Seldom set foot in your neighbor's house--too much of you, and he will hate you.

column.name: text
column.value: Like a club or a sword or a sharp arrow is the man who gives false testimony against his neighbor.

column.name: text
column.value: Like a bad tooth or a lame foot is reliance on the unfaithful in times of trouble.

column.name: text
column.value: Like one who takes away a garment on a cold day, or like vinegar poured on soda, is one who sings songs to a heavy heart.

column.name: text
column.value: If your enemy is hungry, give him food to eat; if he is thirsty, give him water to drink.

column.name: text
column.value: In doing this, you will heap burning coals on his head, and the LORD will reward you.

column.name: text
column.value: As a north wind brings rain, so a sly tongue brings angry looks.

column.name: text
column.value: Better to live on a corner of the roof than share a house with a quarrelsome wife.

column.name: text
column.value: Like cold water to a weary soul is good news from a distant land.

column.name: text
column.value: Like a muddied spring or a polluted well is a righteous man who gives way to the wicked.

column.name: text
column.value: It is not good to eat too much honey, nor is it honorable to seek one's own honor.

column.name: text
column.value: Like a city whose walls are broken down is a man who lacks self-control.

column.name: text
column.value: When you sit to dine with a ruler, note well what is before you,

column.name: text
column.value: and put a knife to your throat if you are given to gluttony.

column.name: text
column.value: Do not crave his delicacies, for that food is deceptive.

column.name: text
column.value: Do not wear yourself out to get rich; have the wisdom to show restraint.

column.name: text
column.value: Cast but a glance at riches, and they are gone, for they will surely sprout wings and fly off to the sky like an eagle.

column.name: text
column.value: Do not eat the food of a stingy man, do not crave his delicacies;

column.name: text
column.value: for he is the kind of man who is always thinking about the cost. "Eat and drink," he says to you, but his heart is not with you.

column.name: text
column.value: You will vomit up the little you have eaten and will have wasted your compliments.

column.name: text
column.value: Do not speak to a fool, for he will scorn the wisdom of your words.

column.name: text
column.value: Do not move an ancient boundary stone or encroach on the fields of the fatherless,

column.name: text
column.value: for their Defender is strong; he will take up their case against you.

column.name: text
column.value: Apply your heart to instruction and your ears to words of knowledge.

column.name: text
column.value: Do not withhold discipline from a child; if you punish him with the rod, he will not die.

column.name: text
column.value: Punish him with the rod and save his soul from death.

column.name: text
column.value: My son, if your heart is wise, then my heart will be glad;

column.name: text
column.value: my inmost being will rejoice when your lips speak what is right.

column.name: text
column.value: Do not let your heart envy sinners, but always be zealous for the fear of the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: There is surely a future hope for you, and your hope will not be cut off.

column.name: text
column.value: Listen, my son, and be wise, and keep your heart on the right path.

column.name: text
column.value: Do not join those who drink too much wine or gorge themselves on meat,

column.name: text
column.value: for drunkards and gluttons become poor, and drowsiness clothes them in rags.

column.name: text
column.value: Listen to your father, who gave you life, and do not despise your mother when she is old.

column.name: text
column.value: Buy the truth and do not sell it; get wisdom, discipline and understanding.

column.name: text
column.value: The father of a righteous man has great joy; he who has a wise son delights in him.

column.name: text
column.value: May your father and mother be glad; may she who gave you birth rejoice!

column.name: text
column.value: My son, give me your heart and let your eyes keep to my ways,

column.name: text
column.value: for a prostitute is a deep pit and a wayward wife is a narrow well.

column.name: text
column.value: Like a bandit she lies in wait, and multiplies the unfaithful among men.

column.name: text
column.value: Who has woe? Who has sorrow? Who has strife? Who has complaints? Who has needless bruises? Who has bloodshot eyes?

column.name: text
column.value: Those who linger over wine, who go to sample bowls of mixed wine.

column.name: text
column.value: Do not gaze at wine when it is red, when it sparkles in the cup, when it goes down smoothly!

column.name: text
column.value: In the end it bites like a snake and poisons like a viper.

column.name: text
column.value: Your eyes will see strange sights and your mind imagine confusing things.

column.name: text
column.value: You will be like one sleeping on the high seas, lying on top of the rigging.

column.name: text
column.value: "They hit me," you will say, "but I'm not hurt! They beat me, but I don't feel it! When will I wake up so I can find another drink?"

column.name: text
column.value: Like snow in summer or rain in harvest, honor is not fitting for a fool.

column.name: text
column.value: Like a fluttering sparrow or a darting swallow, an undeserved curse does not come to rest.

column.name: text
column.value: A whip for the horse, a halter for the donkey, and a rod for the backs of fools!

column.name: text
column.value: Do not answer a fool according to his folly, or you will be like him yourself.

column.name: text
column.value: Answer a fool according to his folly, or he will be wise in his own eyes.

column.name: text
column.value: Like cutting off one's feet or drinking violence is the sending of a message by the hand of a fool.

column.name: text
column.value: Like a lame man's legs that hang limp is a proverb in the mouth of a fool.

column.name: text
column.value: Like tying a stone in a sling is the giving of honor to a fool.

column.name: text
column.value: Like a thornbush in a drunkard's hand is a proverb in the mouth of a fool.

column.name: text
column.value: Like an archer who wounds at random is he who hires a fool or any passer-by.

column.name: text
column.value: As a dog returns to its vomit, so a fool repeats his folly.

column.name: text
column.value: Do you see a man wise in his own eyes? There is more hope for a fool than for him.

column.name: text
column.value: The sluggard says, "There is a lion in the road, a fierce lion roaming the streets!"

column.name: text
column.value: As a door turns on its hinges, so a sluggard turns on his bed.

column.name: text
column.value: The sluggard buries his hand in the dish; he is too lazy to bring it back to his mouth.

column.name: text
column.value: The sluggard is wiser in his own eyes than seven men who answer discreetly.

column.name: text
column.value: Like one who seizes a dog by the ears is a passer-by who meddles in a quarrel not his own.

column.name: text
column.value: Like a madman shooting firebrands or deadly arrows

column.name: text
column.value: is a man who deceives his neighbor and says, "I was only joking!"

column.name: text
column.value: Without wood a fire goes out; without gossip a quarrel dies down.

column.name: text
column.value: As charcoal to embers and as wood to fire, so is a quarrelsome man for kindling strife.

column.name: text
column.value: The words of a gossip are like choice morsels; they go down to a man's inmost parts.

column.name: text
column.value: Like a coating of glaze over earthenware are fervent lips with an evil heart.

column.name: text
column.value: A malicious man disguises himself with his lips, but in his heart he harbors deceit.

column.name: text
column.value: Though his speech is charming, do not believe him, for seven abominations fill his heart.

column.name: text
column.value: His malice may be concealed by deception, but his wickedness will be exposed in the assembly.

column.name: text
column.value: If a man digs a pit, he will fall into it; if a man rolls a stone, it will roll back on him.

column.name: text
column.value: A lying tongue hates those it hurts, and a flattering mouth works ruin.

column.name: text
column.value: The sayings of King Lemuel--an oracle his mother taught him:

column.name: text
column.value: "O my son, O son of my womb, O son of my vows,

column.name: text
column.value: do not spend your strength on women, your vigor on those who ruin kings.

column.name: text
column.value: "It is not for kings, O Lemuel--not for kings to drink wine, not for rulers to crave beer,

column.name: text
column.value: lest they drink and forget what the law decrees, and deprive all the oppressed of their rights.

column.name: text
column.value: Give beer to those who are perishing, wine to those who are in anguish;

column.name: text
column.value: let them drink and forget their poverty and remember their misery no more.

column.name: text
column.value: "Speak up for those who cannot speak for themselves, for the rights of all who are destitute.

column.name: text
column.value: Speak up and judge fairly; defend the rights of the poor and needy."

column.name: text
column.value: A wife of noble character who can find? She is worth far more than rubies.

column.name: text
column.value: Her husband has full confidence in her and lacks nothing of value.

column.name: text
column.value: She brings him good, not harm, all the days of her life.

column.name: text
column.value: She selects wool and flax and works with eager hands.

column.name: text
column.value: She is like the merchant ships, bringing her food from afar.

column.name: text
column.value: She gets up while it is still dark; she provides food for her family and portions for her servant girls.

column.name: text
column.value: She considers a field and buys it; out of her earnings she plants a vineyard.

column.name: text
column.value: She sets about her work vigorously; her arms are strong for her tasks.

column.name: text
column.value: She sees that her trading is profitable, and her lamp does not go out at night.

column.name: text
column.value: In her hand she holds the distaff and grasps the spindle with her fingers.

column.name: text
column.value: She opens her arms to the poor and extends her hands to the needy.

column.name: text
column.value: When it snows, she has no fear for her household; for all of them are clothed in scarlet.

column.name: text
column.value: She makes coverings for her bed; she is clothed in fine linen and purple.

column.name: text
column.value: Her husband is respected at the city gate, where he takes his seat among the elders of the land.

column.name: text
column.value: She makes linen garments and sells them, and supplies the merchants with sashes.

column.name: text
column.value: She is clothed with strength and dignity; she can laugh at the days to come.

column.name: text
column.value: She speaks with wisdom, and faithful instruction is on her tongue.

column.name: text
column.value: She watches over the affairs of her household and does not eat the bread of idleness.

column.name: text
column.value: Her children arise and call her blessed; her husband also, and he praises her:

column.name: text
column.value: "Many women do noble things, but you surpass them all."

column.name: text
column.value: Charm is deceptive, and beauty is fleeting; but a woman who fears the LORD is to be praised.

column.name: text
column.value: Give her the reward she has earned, and let her works bring her praise at the city gate.

column.name: text
column.value: The wicked man flees though no one pursues, but the righteous are as bold as a lion.

column.name: text
column.value: When a country is rebellious, it has many rulers, but a man of understanding and knowledge maintains order.

column.name: text
column.value: A ruler who oppresses the poor is like a driving rain that leaves no crops.

column.name: text
column.value: Those who forsake the law praise the wicked, but those who keep the law resist them.

column.name: text
column.value: Evil men do not understand justice, but those who seek the LORD understand it fully.

column.name: text
column.value: Better a poor man whose walk is blameless than a rich man whose ways are perverse.

column.name: text
column.value: He who keeps the law is a discerning son, but a companion of gluttons disgraces his father.

column.name: text
column.value: He who increases his wealth by exorbitant interest amasses it for another, who will be kind to the poor.

column.name: text
column.value: If anyone turns a deaf ear to the law, even his prayers are detestable.

column.name: text
column.value: He who leads the upright along an evil path will fall into his own trap, but the blameless will receive a good inheritance.

column.name: text
column.value: A rich man may be wise in his own eyes, but a poor man who has discernment sees through him.

column.name: text
column.value: When the righteous triumph, there is great elation; but when the wicked rise to power, men go into hiding.

column.name: text
column.value: He who conceals his sins does not prosper, but whoever confesses and renounces them finds mercy.

column.name: text
column.value: Blessed is the man who always fears the LORD, but he who hardens his heart falls into trouble.

column.name: text
column.value: Like a roaring lion or a charging bear is a wicked man ruling over a helpless people.

column.name: text
column.value: A tyrannical ruler lacks judgment, but he who hates ill-gotten gain will enjoy a long life.

column.name: text
column.value: A man tormented by the guilt of murder will be a fugitive till death; let no one support him.

column.name: text
column.value: He whose walk is blameless is kept safe, but he whose ways are perverse will suddenly fall.

column.name: text
column.value: He who works his land will have abundant food, but the one who chases fantasies will have his fill of poverty.

column.name: text
column.value: A faithful man will be richly blessed, but one eager to get rich will not go unpunished.

column.name: text
column.value: To show partiality is not good--yet a man will do wrong for a piece of bread.

column.name: text
column.value: A stingy man is eager to get rich and is unaware that poverty awaits him.

column.name: text
column.value: He who rebukes a man will in the end gain more favor than he who has a flattering tongue.

column.name: text
column.value: He who robs his father or mother and says, "It's not wrong"--he is partner to him who destroys.

column.name: text
column.value: A greedy man stirs up dissension, but he who trusts in the LORD will prosper.

column.name: text
column.value: He who trusts in himself is a fool, but he who walks in wisdom is kept safe.

column.name: text
column.value: He who gives to the poor will lack nothing, but he who closes his eyes to them receives many curses.

column.name: text
column.value: When the wicked rise to power, people go into hiding; but when the wicked perish, the righteous thrive.

column.name: text
column.value: Do not boast about tomorrow, for you do not know what a day may bring forth.

column.name: text
column.value: Let another praise you, and not your own mouth; someone else, and not your own lips.

column.name: text
column.value: Stone is heavy and sand a burden, but provocation by a fool is heavier than both.

column.name: text
column.value: Anger is cruel and fury overwhelming, but who can stand before jealousy?

column.name: text
column.value: Better is open rebuke than hidden love.

column.name: text
column.value: Wounds from a friend can be trusted, but an enemy multiplies kisses.

column.name: text
column.value: He who is full loathes honey, but to the hungry even what is bitter tastes sweet.

column.name: text
column.value: Like a bird that strays from its nest is a man who strays from his home.

column.name: text
column.value: Perfume and incense bring joy to the heart, and the pleasantness of one's friend springs from his earnest counsel.

column.name: text
column.value: Do not forsake your friend and the friend of your father, and do not go to your brother's house when disaster strikes you--better a neighbor nearby than a brother far away.

column.name: text
column.value: Be wise, my son, and bring joy to my heart; then I can answer anyone who treats me with contempt.

column.name: text
column.value: The prudent see danger and take refuge, but the simple keep going and suffer for it.

column.name: text
column.value: Take the garment of one who puts up security for a stranger; hold it in pledge if he does it for a wayward woman.

column.name: text
column.value: If a man loudly blesses his neighbor early in the morning, it will be taken as a curse.

column.name: text
column.value: A quarrelsome wife is like a constant dripping on a rainy day;

column.name: text
column.value: restraining her is like restraining the wind or grasping oil with the hand.

column.name: text
column.value: As iron sharpens iron, so one man sharpens another.

column.name: text
column.value: He who tends a fig tree will eat its fruit, and he who looks after his master will be honored.

column.name: text
column.value: As water reflects a face, so a man's heart reflects the man.

column.name: text
column.value: Death and Destruction are never satisfied, and neither are the eyes of man.

column.name: text
column.value: The crucible for silver and the furnace for gold, but man is tested by the praise he receives.

column.name: text
column.value: Though you grind a fool in a mortar, grinding him like grain with a pestle, you will not remove his folly from him.

column.name: text
column.value: Be sure you know the condition of your flocks, give careful attention to your herds;

column.name: text
column.value: for riches do not endure forever, and a crown is not secure for all generations.

column.name: text
column.value: When the hay is removed and new growth appears and the grass from the hills is gathered in,

column.name: text
column.value: the lambs will provide you with clothing, and the goats with the price of a field.

column.name: text
column.value: You will have plenty of goats' milk to feed you and your family and to nourish your servant girls.

column.name: text
column.value: A man who remains stiff-necked after many rebukes will suddenly be destroyed--without remedy.

column.name: text
column.value: When the righteous thrive, the people rejoice; when the wicked rule, the people groan.

column.name: text
column.value: A man who loves wisdom brings joy to his father, but a companion of prostitutes squanders his wealth.

column.name: text
column.value: By justice a king gives a country stability, but one who is greedy for bribes tears it down.

column.name: text
column.value: Whoever flatters his neighbor is spreading a net for his feet.

column.name: text
column.value: An evil man is snared by his own sin, but a righteous one can sing and be glad.

column.name: text
column.value: The righteous care about justice for the poor, but the wicked have no such concern.

column.name: text
column.value: Mockers stir up a city, but wise men turn away anger.

column.name: text
column.value: If a wise man goes to court with a fool, the fool rages and scoffs, and there is no peace.

column.name: text
column.value: Bloodthirsty men hate a man of integrity and seek to kill the upright.

column.name: text
column.value: A fool gives full vent to his anger, but a wise man keeps himself under control.

column.name: text
column.value: If a ruler listens to lies, all his officials become wicked.

column.name: text
column.value: The poor man and the oppressor have this in common: The LORD gives sight to the eyes of both.

column.name: text
column.value: If a king judges the poor with fairness, his throne will always be secure.

column.name: text
column.value: The rod of correction imparts wisdom, but a child left to himself disgraces his mother.

column.name: text
column.value: When the wicked thrive, so does sin, but the righteous will see their downfall.

column.name: text
column.value: Discipline your son, and he will give you peace; he will bring delight to your soul.

column.name: text
column.value: Where there is no revelation, the people cast off restraint; but blessed is he who keeps the law.

column.name: text
column.value: A servant cannot be corrected by mere words; though he understands, he will not respond.

column.name: text
column.value: Do you see a man who speaks in haste? There is more hope for a fool than for him.

column.name: text
column.value: If a man pampers his servant from youth, he will bring grief in the end.

column.name: text
column.value: An angry man stirs up dissension, and a hot-tempered one commits many sins.

column.name: text
column.value: A man's pride brings him low, but a man of lowly spirit gains honor.

column.name: text
column.value: The accomplice of a thief is his own enemy; he is put under oath and dare not testify.

column.name: text
column.value: Fear of man will prove to be a snare, but whoever trusts in the LORD is kept safe.

column.name: text
column.value: Many seek an audience with a ruler, but it is from the LORD that man gets justice.

column.name: text
column.value: The righteous detest the dishonest; the wicked detest the upright.

column.name: text
column.value: The sayings of Agur son of Jakeh--an oracle: This man declared to Ithiel, to Ithiel and to Ucal:

column.name: text
column.value: "I am the most ignorant of men; I do not have a man's understanding.

column.name: text
column.value: I have not learned wisdom, nor have I knowledge of the Holy One.

column.name: text
column.value: Who has gone up to heaven and come down? Who has gathered up the wind in the hollow of his hands? Who has wrapped up the waters in his cloak? Who has established all the ends of the earth? What is his name, and the name of his son? Tell me if you know!

column.name: text
column.value: "Every word of God is flawless; he is a shield to those who take refuge in him.

column.name: text
column.value: Do not add to his words, or he will rebuke you and prove you a liar.

column.name: text
column.value: "Two things I ask of you, O LORD; do not refuse me before I die:

column.name: text
column.value: Keep falsehood and lies far from me; give me neither poverty nor riches, but give me only my daily bread.

column.name: text
column.value: Otherwise, I may have too much and disown you and say, 'Who is the LORD?' Or I may become poor and steal, and so dishonor the name of my God.

column.name: text
column.value: "Do not slander a servant to his master, or he will curse you, and you will pay for it.

column.name: text
column.value: "There are those who curse their fathers and do not bless their mothers;

column.name: text
column.value: those who are pure in their own eyes and yet are not cleansed of their filth;

column.name: text
column.value: those whose eyes are ever so haughty, whose glances are so disdainful;

column.name: text
column.value: those whose teeth are swords and whose jaws are set with knives to devour the poor from the earth, the needy from among mankind.

column.name: text
column.value: "The leech has two daughters. 'Give! Give!' they cry. "There are three things that are never satisfied, four that never say, 'Enough!':

column.name: text
column.value: the grave, the barren womb, land, which is never satisfied with water, and fire, which never says, 'Enough!'

column.name: text
column.value: "The eye that mocks a father, that scorns obedience to a mother, will be pecked out by the ravens of the valley, will be eaten by the vultures.

column.name: text
column.value: "There are three things that are too amazing for me, four that I do not understand:

column.name: text
column.value: the way of an eagle in the sky, the way of a snake on a rock, the way of a ship on the high seas, and the way of a man with a maiden.

column.name: text
column.value: "This is the way of an adulteress: She eats and wipes her mouth and says, 'I've done nothing wrong.'

column.name: text
column.value: "Under three things the earth trembles, under four it cannot bear up:

column.name: text
column.value: a servant who becomes king, a fool who is full of food,

column.name: text
column.value: an unloved woman who is married, and a maidservant who displaces her mistress.

column.name: text
column.value: "Four things on earth are small, yet they are extremely wise:

column.name: text
column.value: Ants are creatures of little strength, yet they store up their food in the summer;

column.name: text
column.value: coneys are creatures of little power, yet they make their home in the crags;

column.name: text
column.value: locusts have no king, yet they advance together in ranks;

column.name: text
column.value: a lizard can be caught with the hand, yet it is found in kings' palaces.

column.name: text
column.value: "There are three things that are stately in their stride, four that move with stately bearing:

column.name: text
column.value: a lion, mighty among beasts, who retreats before nothing;

column.name: text
column.value: a strutting rooster, a he-goat, and a king with his army around him.

column.name: text
column.value: "If you have played the fool and exalted yourself, or if you have planned evil, clap your hand over your mouth!

column.name: text
column.value: For as churning the milk produces butter, and as twisting the nose produces blood, so stirring up anger produces strife."

column.name: text
column.value: The words of the Teacher, son of David, king in Jerusalem:

column.name: text
column.value: "Meaningless! Meaningless!" says the Teacher. "Utterly meaningless! Everything is meaningless."

column.name: text
column.value: What does man gain from all his labor at which he toils under the sun?

column.name: text
column.value: Generations come and generations go, but the earth remains forever.

column.name: text
column.value: The sun rises and the sun sets, and hurries back to where it rises.

column.name: text
column.value: The wind blows to the south and turns to the north; round and round it goes, ever returning on its course.

column.name: text
column.value: All streams flow into the sea, yet the sea is never full. To the place the streams come from, there they return again.

column.name: text
column.value: All things are wearisome, more than one can say. The eye never has enough of seeing, nor the ear its fill of hearing.

column.name: text
column.value: What has been will be again, what has been done will be done again; there is nothing new under the sun.

column.name: text
column.value: Is there anything of which one can say, "Look! This is something new"? It was here already, long ago; it was here before our time.

column.name: text
column.value: There is no remembrance of men of old, and even those who are yet to come will not be remembered by those who follow.

column.name: text
column.value: I, the Teacher, was king over Israel in Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: I devoted myself to study and to explore by wisdom all that is done under heaven. What a heavy burden God has laid on men!

column.name: text
column.value: I have seen all the things that are done under the sun; all of them are meaningless, a chasing after the wind.

column.name: text
column.value: What is twisted cannot be straightened; what is lacking cannot be counted.

column.name: text
column.value: I thought to myself, "Look, I have grown and increased in wisdom more than anyone who has ruled over Jerusalem before me; I have experienced much of wisdom and knowledge."

column.name: text
column.value: Then I applied myself to the understanding of wisdom, and also of madness and folly, but I learned that this, too, is a chasing after the wind.

column.name: text
column.value: For with much wisdom comes much sorrow; the more knowledge, the more grief.

column.name: text
column.value: I thought in my heart, "Come now, I will test you with pleasure to find out what is good." But that also proved to be meaningless.

column.name: text
column.value: "Laughter," I said, "is foolish. And what does pleasure accomplish?"

column.name: text
column.value: I tried cheering myself with wine, and embracing folly--my mind still guiding me with wisdom. I wanted to see what was worthwhile for men to do under heaven during the few days of their lives.

column.name: text
column.value: I undertook great projects: I built houses for myself and planted vineyards.

column.name: text
column.value: I made gardens and parks and planted all kinds of fruit trees in them.

column.name: text
column.value: I made reservoirs to water groves of flourishing trees.

column.name: text
column.value: I bought male and female slaves and had other slaves who were born in my house. I also owned more herds and flocks than anyone in Jerusalem before me.

column.name: text
column.value: I amassed silver and gold for myself, and the treasure of kings and provinces. I acquired men and women singers, and a harem as well--the delights of the heart of man.

column.name: text
column.value: I became greater by far than anyone in Jerusalem before me. In all this my wisdom stayed with me.

column.name: text
column.value: I denied myself nothing my eyes desired; I refused my heart no pleasure. My heart took delight in all my work, and this was the reward for all my labor.

column.name: text
column.value: Yet when I surveyed all that my hands had done and what I had toiled to achieve, everything was meaningless, a chasing after the wind; nothing was gained under the sun.

column.name: text
column.value: Then I turned my thoughts to consider wisdom, and also madness and folly. What more can the king's successor do than what has already been done?

column.name: text
column.value: I saw that wisdom is better than folly, just as light is better than darkness.

column.name: text
column.value: The wise man has eyes in his head, while the fool walks in the darkness; but I came to realize that the same fate overtakes them both.

column.name: text
column.value: Then I thought in my heart, "The fate of the fool will overtake me also. What then do I gain by being wise?" I said in my heart, "This too is meaningless."

column.name: text
column.value: For the wise man, like the fool, will not be long remembered; in days to come both will be forgotten. Like the fool, the wise man too must die!

column.name: text
column.value: So I hated life, because the work that is done under the sun was grievous to me. All of it is meaningless, a chasing after the wind.

column.name: text
column.value: I hated all the things I had toiled for under the sun, because I must leave them to the one who comes after me.

column.name: text
column.value: And who knows whether he will be a wise man or a fool? Yet he will have control over all the work into which I have poured my effort and skill under the sun. This too is meaningless.

column.name: text
column.value: So my heart began to despair over all my toilsome labor under the sun.

column.name: text
column.value: For a man may do his work with wisdom, knowledge and skill, and then he must leave all he owns to someone who has not worked for it. This too is meaningless and a great misfortune.

column.name: text
column.value: What does a man get for all the toil and anxious striving with which he labors under the sun?

column.name: text
column.value: All his days his work is pain and grief; even at night his mind does not rest. This too is meaningless.

column.name: text
column.value: A man can do nothing better than to eat and drink and find satisfaction in his work. This too, I see, is from the hand of God,

column.name: text
column.value: for without him, who can eat or find enjoyment?

column.name: text
column.value: To the man who pleases him, God gives wisdom, knowledge and happiness, but to the sinner he gives the task of gathering and storing up wealth to hand it over to the one who pleases God. This too is meaningless, a chasing after the wind.

column.name: text
column.value: There is a time for everything, and a season for every activity under heaven:

column.name: text
column.value: a time to be born and a time to die, a time to plant and a time to uproot,

column.name: text
column.value: a time to kill and a time to heal, a time to tear down and a time to build,

column.name: text
column.value: a time to weep and a time to laugh, a time to mourn and a time to dance,

column.name: text
column.value: a time to scatter stones and a time to gather them, a time to embrace and a time to refrain,

column.name: text
column.value: a time to search and a time to give up, a time to keep and a time to throw away,

column.name: text
column.value: a time to tear and a time to mend, a time to be silent and a time to speak,

column.name: text
column.value: a time to love and a time to hate, a time for war and a time for peace.

column.name: text
column.value: What does the worker gain from his toil?

column.name: text
column.value: I have seen the burden God has laid on men.

column.name: text
column.value: He has made everything beautiful in its time. He has also set eternity in the hearts of men; yet they cannot fathom what God has done from beginning to end.

column.name: text
column.value: I know that there is nothing better for men than to be happy and do good while they live.

column.name: text
column.value: That everyone may eat and drink, and find satisfaction in all his toil--this is the gift of God.

column.name: text
column.value: I know that everything God does will endure forever; nothing can be added to it and nothing taken from it. God does it so that men will revere him.

column.name: text
column.value: Whatever is has already been, and what will be has been before; and God will call the past to account.

column.name: text
column.value: And I saw something else under the sun: In the place of judgment--wickedness was there, in the place of justice--wickedness was there.

column.name: text
column.value: I thought in my heart, "God will bring to judgment both the righteous and the wicked, for there will be a time for every activity, a time for every deed."

column.name: text
column.value: I also thought, "As for men, God tests them so that they may see that they are like the animals.

column.name: text
column.value: Man's fate is like that of the animals; the same fate awaits them both: As one dies, so dies the other. All have the same breath; man has no advantage over the animal. Everything is meaningless.

column.name: text
column.value: All go to the same place; all come from dust, and to dust all return.

column.name: text
column.value: Who knows if the spirit of man rises upward and if the spirit of the animal goes down into the earth?"

column.name: text
column.value: So I saw that there is nothing better for a man than to enjoy his work, because that is his lot. For who can bring him to see what will happen after him?

column.name: text
column.value: Again I looked and saw all the oppression that was taking place under the sun: I saw the tears of the oppressed--and they have no comforter; power was on the side of their oppressors--and they have no comforter.

column.name: text
column.value: And I declared that the dead, who had already died, are happier than the living, who are still alive.

column.name: text
column.value: But better than both is he who has not yet been, who has not seen the evil that is done under the sun.

column.name: text
column.value: And I saw that all labor and all achievement spring from man's envy of his neighbor. This too is meaningless, a chasing after the wind.

column.name: text
column.value: The fool folds his hands and ruins himself.

column.name: text
column.value: Better one handful with tranquillity than two handfuls with toil and chasing after the wind.

column.name: text
column.value: Again I saw something meaningless under the sun:

column.name: text
column.value: There was a man all alone; he had neither son nor brother. There was no end to his toil, yet his eyes were not content with his wealth. "For whom am I toiling," he asked, "and why am I depriving myself of enjoyment?" This too is meaningless--a miserable business!

column.name: text
column.value: Two are better than one, because they have a good return for their work:

column.name: text
column.value: If one falls down, his friend can help him up. But pity the man who falls and has no one to help him up!

column.name: text
column.value: Also, if two lie down together, they will keep warm. But how can one keep warm alone?

column.name: text
column.value: Though one may be overpowered, two can defend themselves. A cord of three strands is not quickly broken.

column.name: text
column.value: Better a poor but wise youth than an old but foolish king who no longer knows how to take warning.

column.name: text
column.value: The youth may have come from prison to the kingship, or he may have been born in poverty within his kingdom.

column.name: text
column.value: I saw that all who lived and walked under the sun followed the youth, the king's successor.

column.name: text
column.value: There was no end to all the people who were before them. But those who came later were not pleased with the successor. This too is meaningless, a chasing after the wind.

column.name: text
column.value: Guard your steps when you go to the house of God. Go near to listen rather than to offer the sacrifice of fools, who do not know that they do wrong.

column.name: text
column.value: Do not be quick with your mouth, do not be hasty in your heart to utter anything before God. God is in heaven and you are on earth, so let your words be few.

column.name: text
column.value: As a dream comes when there are many cares, so the speech of a fool when there are many words.

column.name: text
column.value: When you make a vow to God, do not delay in fulfilling it. He has no pleasure in fools; fulfill your vow.

column.name: text
column.value: It is better not to vow than to make a vow and not fulfill it.

column.name: text
column.value: Do not let your mouth lead you into sin. And do not protest to the temple messenger, "My vow was a mistake." Why should God be angry at what you say and destroy the work of your hands?

column.name: text
column.value: Much dreaming and many words are meaningless. Therefore stand in awe of God.

column.name: text
column.value: If you see the poor oppressed in a district, and justice and rights denied, do not be surprised at such things; for one official is eyed by a higher one, and over them both are others higher still.

column.name: text
column.value: The increase from the land is taken by all; the king himself profits from the fields.

column.name: text
column.value: Whoever loves money never has money enough; whoever loves wealth is never satisfied with his income. This too is meaningless.

column.name: text
column.value: As goods increase, so do those who consume them. And what benefit are they to the owner except to feast his eyes on them?

column.name: text
column.value: The sleep of a laborer is sweet, whether he eats little or much, but the abundance of a rich man permits him no sleep.

column.name: text
column.value: I have seen a grievous evil under the sun: wealth hoarded to the harm of its owner,

column.name: text
column.value: or wealth lost through some misfortune, so that when he has a son there is nothing left for him.

column.name: text
column.value: Naked a man comes from his mother's womb, and as he comes, so he departs. He takes nothing from his labor that he can carry in his hand.

column.name: text
column.value: This too is a grievous evil: As a man comes, so he departs, and what does he gain, since he toils for the wind?

column.name: text
column.value: All his days he eats in darkness, with great frustration, affliction and anger.

column.name: text
column.value: Then I realized that it is good and proper for a man to eat and drink, and to find satisfaction in his toilsome labor under the sun during the few days of life God has given him--for this is his lot.

column.name: text
column.value: Moreover, when God gives any man wealth and possessions, and enables him to enjoy them, to accept his lot and be happy in his work--this is a gift of God.

column.name: text
column.value: He seldom reflects on the days of his life, because God keeps him occupied with gladness of heart.

column.name: text
column.value: I have seen another evil under the sun, and it weighs heavily on men:

column.name: text
column.value: God gives a man wealth, possessions and honor, so that he lacks nothing his heart desires, but God does not enable him to enjoy them, and a stranger enjoys them instead. This is meaningless, a grievous evil.

column.name: text
column.value: A man may have a hundred children and live many years; yet no matter how long he lives, if he cannot enjoy his prosperity and does not receive proper burial, I say that a stillborn child is better off than he.

column.name: text
column.value: It comes without meaning, it departs in darkness, and in darkness its name is shrouded.

column.name: text
column.value: Though it never saw the sun or knew anything, it has more rest than does that man--

column.name: text
column.value: even if he lives a thousand years twice over but fails to enjoy his prosperity. Do not all go to the same place?

column.name: text
column.value: All man's efforts are for his mouth, yet his appetite is never satisfied.

column.name: text
column.value: What advantage has a wise man over a fool? What does a poor man gain by knowing how to conduct himself before others?

column.name: text
column.value: Better what the eye sees than the roving of the appetite. This too is meaningless, a chasing after the wind.

column.name: text
column.value: Whatever exists has already been named, and what man is has been known; no man can contend with one who is stronger than he.

column.name: text
column.value: The more the words, the less the meaning, and how does that profit anyone?

column.name: text
column.value: For who knows what is good for a man in life, during the few and meaningless days he passes through like a shadow? Who can tell him what will happen under the sun after he is gone?

column.name: text
column.value: A good name is better than fine perfume, and the day of death better than the day of birth.

column.name: text
column.value: It is better to go to a house of mourning than to go to a house of feasting, for death is the destiny of every man; the living should take this to heart.

column.name: text
column.value: Sorrow is better than laughter, because a sad face is good for the heart.

column.name: text
column.value: The heart of the wise is in the house of mourning, but the heart of fools is in the house of pleasure.

column.name: text
column.value: It is better to heed a wise man's rebuke than to listen to the song of fools.

column.name: text
column.value: Like the crackling of thorns under the pot, so is the laughter of fools. This too is meaningless.

column.name: text
column.value: Extortion turns a wise man into a fool, and a bribe corrupts the heart.

column.name: text
column.value: The end of a matter is better than its beginning, and patience is better than pride.

column.name: text
column.value: Do not be quickly provoked in your spirit, for anger resides in the lap of fools.

column.name: text
column.value: Do not say, "Why were the old days better than these?" For it is not wise to ask such questions.

column.name: text
column.value: Wisdom, like an inheritance, is a good thing and benefits those who see the sun.

column.name: text
column.value: Wisdom is a shelter as money is a shelter, but the advantage of knowledge is this: that wisdom preserves the life of its possessor.

column.name: text
column.value: Consider what God has done: Who can straighten what he has made crooked?

column.name: text
column.value: When times are good, be happy; but when times are bad, consider: God has made the one as well as the other. Therefore, a man cannot discover anything about his future.

column.name: text
column.value: In this meaningless life of mine I have seen both of these: a righteous man perishing in his righteousness, and a wicked man living long in his wickedness.

column.name: text
column.value: Do not be overrighteous, neither be overwise--why destroy yourself?

column.name: text
column.value: Do not be overwicked, and do not be a fool--why die before your time?

column.name: text
column.value: It is good to grasp the one and not let go of the other. The man who fears God will avoid all extremes.

column.name: text
column.value: Wisdom makes one wise man more powerful than ten rulers in a city.

column.name: text
column.value: There is not a righteous man on earth who does what is right and never sins.

column.name: text
column.value: Do not pay attention to every word people say, or you may hear your servant cursing you--

column.name: text
column.value: for you know in your heart that many times you yourself have cursed others.

column.name: text
column.value: All this I tested by wisdom and I said, "I am determined to be wise"--but this was beyond me.

column.name: text
column.value: Whatever wisdom may be, it is far off and most profound--who can discover it?

column.name: text
column.value: So I turned my mind to understand, to investigate and to search out wisdom and the scheme of things and to understand the stupidity of wickedness and the madness of folly.

column.name: text
column.value: I find more bitter than death the woman who is a snare, whose heart is a trap and whose hands are chains. The man who pleases God will escape her, but the sinner she will ensnare.

column.name: text
column.value: "Look," says the Teacher, "this is what I have discovered: "Adding one thing to another to discover the scheme of things--

column.name: text
column.value: while I was still searching but not finding--I found one upright man among a thousand, but not one upright woman among them all.

column.name: text
column.value: This only have I found: God made mankind upright, but men have gone in search of many schemes."

column.name: text
column.value: Who is like the wise man? Who knows the explanation of things? Wisdom brightens a man's face and changes its hard appearance.

column.name: text
column.value: Obey the king's command, I say, because you took an oath before God.

column.name: text
column.value: Do not be in a hurry to leave the king's presence. Do not stand up for a bad cause, for he will do whatever he pleases.

column.name: text
column.value: Since a king's word is supreme, who can say to him, "What are you doing?"

column.name: text
column.value: Whoever obeys his command will come to no harm, and the wise heart will know the proper time and procedure.

column.name: text
column.value: For there is a proper time and procedure for every matter, though a man's misery weighs heavily upon him.

column.name: text
column.value: Since no man knows the future, who can tell him what is to come?

column.name: text
column.value: No man has power over the wind to contain it; so no one has power over the day of his death. As no one is discharged in time of war, so wickedness will not release those who practice it.

column.name: text
column.value: All this I saw, as I applied my mind to everything done under the sun. There is a time when a man lords it over others to his own hurt.

column.name: text
column.value: Then too, I saw the wicked buried--those who used to come and go from the holy place and receive praise in the city where they did this. This too is meaningless.

column.name: text
column.value: When the sentence for a crime is not quickly carried out, the hearts of the people are filled with schemes to do wrong.

column.name: text
column.value: Although a wicked man commits a hundred crimes and still lives a long time, I know that it will go better with God-fearing men, who are reverent before God.

column.name: text
column.value: Yet because the wicked do not fear God, it will not go well with them, and their days will not lengthen like a shadow.

column.name: text
column.value: There is something else meaningless that occurs on earth: righteous men who get what the wicked deserve, and wicked men who get what the righteous deserve. This too, I say, is meaningless.

column.name: text
column.value: So I commend the enjoyment of life, because nothing is better for a man under the sun than to eat and drink and be glad. Then joy will accompany him in his work all the days of the life God has given him under the sun.

column.name: text
column.value: When I applied my mind to know wisdom and to observe man's labor on earth--his eyes not seeing sleep day or night--

column.name: text
column.value: then I saw all that God has done. No one can comprehend what goes on under the sun. Despite all his efforts to search it out, man cannot discover its meaning. Even if a wise man claims he knows, he cannot really comprehend it.

column.name: text
column.value: So I reflected on all this and concluded that the righteous and the wise and what they do are in God's hands, but no man knows whether love or hate awaits him.

column.name: text
column.value: All share a common destiny--the righteous and the wicked, the good and the bad, the clean and the unclean, those who offer sacrifices and those who do not. As it is with the good man, so with the sinner; as it is with those who take oaths, so with those who are afraid to take them.

column.name: text
column.value: This is the evil in everything that happens under the sun: The same destiny overtakes all. The hearts of men, moreover, are full of evil and there is madness in their hearts while they live, and afterward they join the dead.

column.name: text
column.value: Anyone who is among the living has hope--even a live dog is better off than a dead lion!

column.name: text
column.value: For the living know that they will die, but the dead know nothing; they have no further reward, and even the memory of them is forgotten.

column.name: text
column.value: Their love, their hate and their jealousy have long since vanished; never again will they have a part in anything that happens under the sun.

column.name: text
column.value: Go, eat your food with gladness, and drink your wine with a joyful heart, for it is now that God favors what you do.

column.name: text
column.value: Always be clothed in white, and always anoint your head with oil.

column.name: text
column.value: Enjoy life with your wife, whom you love, all the days of this meaningless life that God has given you under the sun--all your meaningless days. For this is your lot in life and in your toilsome labor under the sun.

column.name: text
column.value: Whatever your hand finds to do, do it with all your might, for in the grave, where you are going, there is neither working nor planning nor knowledge nor wisdom.

column.name: text
column.value: I have seen something else under the sun: The race is not to the swift or the battle to the strong, nor does food come to the wise or wealth to the brilliant or favor to the learned; but time and chance happen to them all.

column.name: text
column.value: Moreover, no man knows when his hour will come: As fish are caught in a cruel net, or birds are taken in a snare, so men are trapped by evil times that fall unexpectedly upon them.

column.name: text
column.value: I also saw under the sun this example of wisdom that greatly impressed me:

column.name: text
column.value: There was once a small city with only a few people in it. And a powerful king came against it, surrounded it and built huge siegeworks against it.

column.name: text
column.value: Now there lived in that city a man poor but wise, and he saved the city by his wisdom. But nobody remembered that poor man.

column.name: text
column.value: So I said, "Wisdom is better than strength." But the poor man's wisdom is despised, and his words are no longer heeded.

column.name: text
column.value: The quiet words of the wise are more to be heeded than the shouts of a ruler of fools.

column.name: text
column.value: Wisdom is better than weapons of war, but one sinner destroys much good.

column.name: text
column.value: Cast your bread upon the waters, for after many days you will find it again.

column.name: text
column.value: Give portions to seven, yes to eight, for you do not know what disaster may come upon the land.

column.name: text
column.value: If clouds are full of water, they pour rain upon the earth. Whether a tree falls to the south or to the north, in the place where it falls, there will it lie.

column.name: text
column.value: Whoever watches the wind will not plant; whoever looks at the clouds will not reap.

column.name: text
column.value: As you do not know the path of the wind, or how the body is formed in a mother's womb, so you cannot understand the work of God, the Maker of all things.

column.name: text
column.value: Sow your seed in the morning, and at evening let not your hands be idle, for you do not know which will succeed, whether this or that, or whether both will do equally well.

column.name: text
column.value: Light is sweet, and it pleases the eyes to see the sun.

column.name: text
column.value: However many years a man may live, let him enjoy them all. But let him remember the days of darkness, for they will be many. Everything to come is meaningless.

column.name: text
column.value: Be happy, young man, while you are young, and let your heart give you joy in the days of your youth. Follow the ways of your heart and whatever your eyes see, but know that for all these things God will bring you to judgment.

column.name: text
column.value: So then, banish anxiety from your heart and cast off the troubles of your body, for youth and vigor are meaningless.

column.name: text
column.value: I am a rose of Sharon, a lily of the valleys.

column.name: text
column.value: Like a lily among thorns is my darling among the maidens.

column.name: text
column.value: Like an apple tree among the trees of the forest is my lover among the young men. I delight to sit in his shade, and his fruit is sweet to my taste.

column.name: text
column.value: He has taken me to the banquet hall, and his banner over me is love.

column.name: text
column.value: Strengthen me with raisins, refresh me with apples, for I am faint with love.

column.name: text
column.value: His left arm is under my head, and his right arm embraces me.

column.name: text
column.value: Daughters of Jerusalem, I charge you by the gazelles and by the does of the field: Do not arouse or awaken love until it so desires.

column.name: text
column.value: Listen! My lover! Look! Here he comes, leaping across the mountains, bounding over the hills.

column.name: text
column.value: My lover is like a gazelle or a young stag. Look! There he stands behind our wall, gazing through the windows, peering through the lattice.

column.name: text
column.value: My lover spoke and said to me, "Arise, my darling, my beautiful one, and come with me.

column.name: text
column.value: See! The winter is past; the rains are over and gone.

column.name: text
column.value: Flowers appear on the earth; the season of singing has come, the cooing of doves is heard in our land.

column.name: text
column.value: The fig tree forms its early fruit; the blossoming vines spread their fragrance. Arise, come, my darling; my beautiful one, come with me."

column.name: text
column.value: My dove in the clefts of the rock, in the hiding places on the mountainside, show me your face, let me hear your voice; for your voice is sweet, and your face is lovely.

column.name: text
column.value: Catch for us the foxes, the little foxes that ruin the vineyards, our vineyards that are in bloom.

column.name: text
column.value: My lover is mine and I am his; he browses among the lilies.

column.name: text
column.value: Until the day breaks and the shadows flee, turn, my lover, and be like a gazelle or like a young stag on the rugged hills.

column.name: text
column.value: All night long on my bed I looked for the one my heart loves; I looked for him but did not find him.

column.name: text
column.value: I will get up now and go about the city, through its streets and squares; I will search for the one my heart loves. So I looked for him but did not find him.

column.name: text
column.value: The watchmen found me as they made their rounds in the city. "Have you seen the one my heart loves?"

column.name: text
column.value: Scarcely had I passed them when I found the one my heart loves. I held him and would not let him go till I had brought him to my mother's house, to the room of the one who conceived me.

column.name: text
column.value: Daughters of Jerusalem, I charge you by the gazelles and by the does of the field: Do not arouse or awaken love until it so desires.

column.name: text
column.value: Who is this coming up from the desert like a column of smoke, perfumed with myrrh and incense made from all the spices of the merchant?

column.name: text
column.value: Look! It is Solomon's carriage, escorted by sixty warriors, the noblest of Israel,

column.name: text
column.value: all of them wearing the sword, all experienced in battle, each with his sword at his side, prepared for the terrors of the night.

column.name: text
column.value: King Solomon made for himself the carriage; he made it of wood from Lebanon.

column.name: text
column.value: Its posts he made of silver, its base of gold. Its seat was upholstered with purple, its interior lovingly inlaid by the daughters of Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: Come out, you daughters of Zion, and look at King Solomon wearing the crown, the crown with which his mother crowned him on the day of his wedding, the day his heart rejoiced.

column.name: text
column.value: Remember your Creator in the days of your youth, before the days of trouble come and the years approach when you will say, "I find no pleasure in them"--

column.name: text
column.value: before the sun and the light and the moon and the stars grow dark, and the clouds return after the rain;

column.name: text
column.value: when the keepers of the house tremble, and the strong men stoop, when the grinders cease because they are few, and those looking through the windows grow dim;

column.name: text
column.value: when the doors to the street are closed and the sound of grinding fades; when men rise up at the sound of birds, but all their songs grow faint;

column.name: text
column.value: when men are afraid of heights and of dangers in the streets; when the almond tree blossoms and the grasshopper drags himself along and desire no longer is stirred. Then man goes to his eternal home and mourners go about the streets.

column.name: text
column.value: Remember him--before the silver cord is severed, or the golden bowl is broken; before the pitcher is shattered at the spring, or the wheel broken at the well,

column.name: text
column.value: and the dust returns to the ground it came from, and the spirit returns to God who gave it.

column.name: text
column.value: "Meaningless! Meaningless!" says the Teacher. "Everything is meaningless!"

column.name: text
column.value: Not only was the Teacher wise, but also he imparted knowledge to the people. He pondered and searched out and set in order many proverbs.

column.name: text
column.value: The Teacher searched to find just the right words, and what he wrote was upright and true.

column.name: text
column.value: The words of the wise are like goads, their collected sayings like firmly embedded nails--given by one Shepherd.

column.name: text
column.value: Be warned, my son, of anything in addition to them. Of making many books there is no end, and much study wearies the body.

column.name: text
column.value: Now all has been heard; here is the conclusion of the matter: Fear God and keep his commandments, for this is the whole duty of man.

column.name: text
column.value: For God will bring every deed into judgment, including every hidden thing, whether it is good or evil.

column.name: text
column.value: As dead flies give perfume a bad smell, so a little folly outweighs wisdom and honor.

column.name: text
column.value: The heart of the wise inclines to the right, but the heart of the fool to the left.

column.name: text
column.value: Even as he walks along the road, the fool lacks sense and shows everyone how stupid he is.

column.name: text
column.value: If a ruler's anger rises against you, do not leave your post; calmness can lay great errors to rest.

column.name: text
column.value: There is an evil I have seen under the sun, the sort of error that arises from a ruler:

column.name: text
column.value: Fools are put in many high positions, while the rich occupy the low ones.

column.name: text
column.value: I have seen slaves on horseback, while princes go on foot like slaves.

column.name: text
column.value: Whoever digs a pit may fall into it; whoever breaks through a wall may be bitten by a snake.

column.name: text
column.value: Whoever quarries stones may be injured by them; whoever splits logs may be endangered by them.

column.name: text
column.value: If the ax is dull and its edge unsharpened, more strength is needed but skill will bring success.

column.name: text
column.value: If a snake bites before it is charmed, there is no profit for the charmer.

column.name: text
column.value: Words from a wise man's mouth are gracious, but a fool is consumed by his own lips.

column.name: text
column.value: At the beginning his words are folly; at the end they are wicked madness--

column.name: text
column.value: and the fool multiplies words. No one knows what is coming--who can tell him what will happen after him?

column.name: text
column.value: A fool's work wearies him; he does not know the way to town.

column.name: text
column.value: Woe to you, O land whose king was a servant and whose princes feast in the morning.

column.name: text
column.value: Blessed are you, O land whose king is of noble birth and whose princes eat at a proper time--for strength and not for drunkenness.

column.name: text
column.value: If a man is lazy, the rafters sag; if his hands are idle, the house leaks.

column.name: text
column.value: A feast is made for laughter, and wine makes life merry, but money is the answer for everything.

column.name: text
column.value: Do not revile the king even in your thoughts, or curse the rich in your bedroom, because a bird of the air may carry your words, and a bird on the wing may report what you say.

column.name: text
column.value: Solomon's Song of Songs.

column.name: text
column.value: Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth--for your love is more delightful than wine.

column.name: text
column.value: Pleasing is the fragrance of your perfumes; your name is like perfume poured out. No wonder the maidens love you!

column.name: text
column.value: Take me away with you--let us hurry! Let the king bring me into his chambers. We rejoice and delight in you; we will praise your love more than wine. How right they are to adore you!

column.name: text
column.value: Dark am I, yet lovely, O daughters of Jerusalem, dark like the tents of Kedar, like the tent curtains of Solomon.

column.name: text
column.value: Do not stare at me because I am dark, because I am darkened by the sun. My mother's sons were angry with me and made me take care of the vineyards; my own vineyard I have neglected.

column.name: text
column.value: Tell me, you whom I love, where you graze your flock and where you rest your sheep at midday. Why should I be like a veiled woman beside the flocks of your friends?

column.name: text
column.value: If you do not know, most beautiful of women, follow the tracks of the sheep and graze your young goats by the tents of the shepherds.

column.name: text
column.value: I liken you, my darling, to a mare harnessed to one of the chariots of Pharaoh.

column.name: text
column.value: Your cheeks are beautiful with earrings, your neck with strings of jewels.

column.name: text
column.value: We will make you earrings of gold, studded with silver.

column.name: text
column.value: While the king was at his table, my perfume spread its fragrance.

column.name: text
column.value: My lover is to me a sachet of myrrh resting between my breasts.

column.name: text
column.value: My lover is to me a cluster of henna blossoms from the vineyards of En Gedi.

column.name: text
column.value: How beautiful you are, my darling! Oh, how beautiful! Your eyes are doves.

column.name: text
column.value: How handsome you are, my lover! Oh, how charming! And our bed is verdant.

column.name: text
column.value: The beams of our house are cedars; our rafters are firs.

column.name: text
column.value: I have come into my garden, my sister, my bride; I have gathered my myrrh with my spice. I have eaten my honeycomb and my honey; I have drunk my wine and my milk. Eat, O friends, and drink; drink your fill, O lovers.

column.name: text
column.value: I slept but my heart was awake. Listen! My lover is knocking: "Open to me, my sister, my darling, my dove, my flawless one. My head is drenched with dew, my hair with the dampness of the night."

column.name: text
column.value: I have taken off my robe--must I put it on again? I have washed my feet--must I soil them again?

column.name: text
column.value: My lover thrust his hand through the latch-opening; my heart began to pound for him.

column.name: text
column.value: I arose to open for my lover, and my hands dripped with myrrh, my fingers with flowing myrrh, on the handles of the lock.

column.name: text
column.value: I opened for my lover, but my lover had left; he was gone. My heart sank at his departure. I looked for him but did not find him. I called him but he did not answer.

column.name: text
column.value: The watchmen found me as they made their rounds in the city. They beat me, they bruised me; they took away my cloak, those watchmen of the walls!

column.name: text
column.value: O daughters of Jerusalem, I charge you--if you find my lover, what will you tell him? Tell him I am faint with love.

column.name: text
column.value: How is your beloved better than others, most beautiful of women? How is your beloved better than others, that you charge us so?

column.name: text
column.value: My lover is radiant and ruddy, outstanding among ten thousand.

column.name: text
column.value: His head is purest gold; his hair is wavy and black as a raven.

column.name: text
column.value: His eyes are like doves by the water streams, washed in milk, mounted like jewels.

column.name: text
column.value: His cheeks are like beds of spice yielding perfume. His lips are like lilies dripping with myrrh.

column.name: text
column.value: His arms are rods of gold set with chrysolite. His body is like polished ivory decorated with sapphires.

column.name: text
column.value: His legs are pillars of marble set on bases of pure gold. His appearance is like Lebanon, choice as its cedars.

column.name: text
column.value: His mouth is sweetness itself; he is altogether lovely. This is my lover, this my friend, O daughters of Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: How beautiful you are, my darling! Oh, how beautiful! Your eyes behind your veil are doves. Your hair is like a flock of goats descending from Mount Gilead.

column.name: text
column.value: Your teeth are like a flock of sheep just shorn, coming up from the washing. Each has its twin; not one of them is alone.

column.name: text
column.value: Your lips are like a scarlet ribbon; your mouth is lovely. Your temples behind your veil are like the halves of a pomegranate.

column.name: text
column.value: Your neck is like the tower of David, built with elegance; on it hang a thousand shields, all of them shields of warriors.

column.name: text
column.value: Your two breasts are like two fawns, like twin fawns of a gazelle that browse among the lilies.

column.name: text
column.value: Until the day breaks and the shadows flee, I will go to the mountain of myrrh and to the hill of incense.

column.name: text
column.value: All beautiful you are, my darling; there is no flaw in you.

column.name: text
column.value: Come with me from Lebanon, my bride, come with me from Lebanon. Descend from the crest of Amana, from the top of Senir, the summit of Hermon, from the lions' dens and the mountain haunts of the leopards.

column.name: text
column.value: You have stolen my heart, my sister, my bride; you have stolen my heart with one glance of your eyes, with one jewel of your necklace.

column.name: text
column.value: How delightful is your love, my sister, my bride! How much more pleasing is your love than wine, and the fragrance of your perfume than any spice!

column.name: text
column.value: Your lips drop sweetness as the honeycomb, my bride; milk and honey are under your tongue. The fragrance of your garments is like that of Lebanon.

column.name: text
column.value: You are a garden locked up, my sister, my bride; you are a spring enclosed, a sealed fountain.

column.name: text
column.value: Your plants are an orchard of pomegranates with choice fruits, with henna and nard,

column.name: text
column.value: nard and saffron, calamus and cinnamon, with every kind of incense tree, with myrrh and aloes and all the finest spices.

column.name: text
column.value: You are a garden fountain, a well of flowing water streaming down from Lebanon.

column.name: text
column.value: Awake, north wind, and come, south wind! Blow on my garden, that its fragrance may spread abroad. Let my lover come into his garden and taste its choice fruits.

column.name: text
column.value: Where has your lover gone, most beautiful of women? Which way did your lover turn, that we may look for him with you?

column.name: text
column.value: My lover has gone down to his garden, to the beds of spices, to browse in the gardens and to gather lilies.

column.name: text
column.value: I am my lover's and my lover is mine; he browses among the lilies.

column.name: text
column.value: You are beautiful, my darling, as Tirzah, lovely as Jerusalem, majestic as troops with banners.

column.name: text
column.value: Turn your eyes from me; they overwhelm me. Your hair is like a flock of goats descending from Gilead.

column.name: text
column.value: Your teeth are like a flock of sheep coming up from the washing. Each has its twin, not one of them is alone.

column.name: text
column.value: Your temples behind your veil are like the halves of a pomegranate.

column.name: text
column.value: Sixty queens there may be, and eighty concubines, and virgins beyond number;

column.name: text
column.value: but my dove, my perfect one, is unique, the only daughter of her mother, the favorite of the one who bore her. The maidens saw her and called her blessed; the queens and concubines praised her.

column.name: text
column.value: Who is this that appears like the dawn, fair as the moon, bright as the sun, majestic as the stars in procession?

column.name: text
column.value: I went down to the grove of nut trees to look at the new growth in the valley, to see if the vines had budded or the pomegranates were in bloom.

column.name: text
column.value: Before I realized it, my desire set me among the royal chariots of my people.

column.name: text
column.value: Come back, come back, O Shulammite; come back, come back, that we may gaze on you! Why would you gaze on the Shulammite as on the dance of Mahanaim?

column.name: text
column.value: How beautiful your sandaled feet, O prince's daughter! Your graceful legs are like jewels, the work of a craftsman's hands.

column.name: text
column.value: Your navel is a rounded goblet that never lacks blended wine. Your waist is a mound of wheat encircled by lilies.

column.name: text
column.value: Your breasts are like two fawns, twins of a gazelle.

column.name: text
column.value: Your neck is like an ivory tower. Your eyes are the pools of Heshbon by the gate of Bath Rabbim. Your nose is like the tower of Lebanon looking toward Damascus.

column.name: text
column.value: Your head crowns you like Mount Carmel. Your hair is like royal tapestry; the king is held captive by its tresses.

column.name: text
column.value: How beautiful you are and how pleasing, O love, with your delights!

column.name: text
column.value: Your stature is like that of the palm, and your breasts like clusters of fruit.

column.name: text
column.value: I said, "I will climb the palm tree; I will take hold of its fruit." May your breasts be like the clusters of the vine, the fragrance of your breath like apples,

column.name: text
column.value: and your mouth like the best wine. May the wine go straight to my lover, flowing gently over lips and teeth.

column.name: text
column.value: I belong to my lover, and his desire is for me.

column.name: text
column.value: Come, my lover, let us go to the countryside, let us spend the night in the villages.

column.name: text
column.value: Let us go early to the vineyards to see if the vines have budded, if their blossoms have opened, and if the pomegranates are in bloom--there I will give you my love.

column.name: text
column.value: The mandrakes send out their fragrance, and at our door is every delicacy, both new and old, that I have stored up for you, my lover.

column.name: text
column.value: If only you were to me like a brother, who was nursed at my mother's breasts! Then, if I found you outside, I would kiss you, and no one would despise me.

column.name: text
column.value: I would lead you and bring you to my mother's house--she who has taught me. I would give you spiced wine to drink, the nectar of my pomegranates.

column.name: text
column.value: His left arm is under my head and his right arm embraces me.

column.name: text
column.value: Daughters of Jerusalem, I charge you: Do not arouse or awaken love until it so desires.

column.name: text
column.value: Who is this coming up from the desert leaning on her lover? Under the apple tree I roused you; there your mother conceived you, there she who was in labor gave you birth.

column.name: text
column.value: Place me like a seal over your heart, like a seal on your arm; for love is as strong as death, its jealousy unyielding as the grave. It burns like blazing fire, like a mighty flame.

column.name: text
column.value: Many waters cannot quench love; rivers cannot wash it away. If one were to give all the wealth of his house for love, it would be utterly scorned.

column.name: text
column.value: We have a young sister, and her breasts are not yet grown. What shall we do for our sister for the day she is spoken for?

column.name: text
column.value: If she is a wall, we will build towers of silver on her. If she is a door, we will enclose her with panels of cedar.

column.name: text
column.value: I am a wall, and my breasts are like towers. Thus I have become in his eyes like one bringing contentment.

column.name: text
column.value: Solomon had a vineyard in Baal Hamon; he let out his vineyard to tenants. Each was to bring for its fruit a thousand shekels of silver.

column.name: text
column.value: But my own vineyard is mine to give; the thousand shekels are for you, O Solomon, and two hundred are for those who tend its fruit.

column.name: text
column.value: You who dwell in the gardens with friends in attendance, let me hear your voice!

column.name: text
column.value: Come away, my lover, and be like a gazelle or like a young stag on the spice-laden mountains.

column.name: text
column.value: The vision concerning Judah and Jerusalem that Isaiah son of Amoz saw during the reigns of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz and Hezekiah, kings of Judah.

column.name: text
column.value: Hear, O heavens! Listen, O earth! For the LORD has spoken: "I reared children and brought them up, but they have rebelled against me.

column.name: text
column.value: The ox knows his master, the donkey his owner's manger, but Israel does not know, my people do not understand."

column.name: text
column.value: Ah, sinful nation, a people loaded with guilt, a brood of evildoers, children given to corruption! They have forsaken the LORD; they have spurned the Holy One of Israel and turned their backs on him.

column.name: text
column.value: Why should you be beaten anymore? Why do you persist in rebellion? Your whole head is injured, your whole heart afflicted.

column.name: text
column.value: From the sole of your foot to the top of your head there is no soundness--only wounds and welts and open sores, not cleansed or bandaged or soothed with oil.

column.name: text
column.value: Your country is desolate, your cities burned with fire; your fields are being stripped by foreigners right before you, laid waste as when overthrown by strangers.

column.name: text
column.value: The Daughter of Zion is left like a shelter in a vineyard, like a hut in a field of melons, like a city under siege.

column.name: text
column.value: Unless the LORD Almighty had left us some survivors, we would have become like Sodom, we would have been like Gomorrah.

column.name: text
column.value: Hear the word of the LORD, you rulers of Sodom; listen to the law of our God, you people of Gomorrah!

column.name: text
