column.value: But if you do not obey these commands, declares the LORD, I swear by myself that this palace will become a ruin.'"

column.name: text
column.value: For this is what the LORD says about the palace of the king of Judah: "Though you are like Gilead to me, like the summit of Lebanon, I will surely make you like a desert, like towns not inhabited.

column.name: text
column.value: I will send destroyers against you, each man with his weapons, and they will cut up your fine cedar beams and throw them into the fire.

column.name: text
column.value: "People from many nations will pass by this city and will ask one another, 'Why has the LORD done such a thing to this great city?'

column.name: text
column.value: And the answer will be: 'Because they have forsaken the covenant of the LORD their God and have worshiped and served other gods.'"

column.name: text
column.value: Do not weep for the dead king or mourn his loss; rather, weep bitterly for him who is exiled, because he will never return nor see his native land again.

column.name: text
column.value: For this is what the LORD says about Shallum son of Josiah, who succeeded his father as king of Judah but has gone from this place: "He will never return.

column.name: text
column.value: He will die in the place where they have led him captive; he will not see this land again."

column.name: text
column.value: "Woe to him who builds his palace by unrighteousness, his upper rooms by injustice, making his countrymen work for nothing, not paying them for their labor.

column.name: text
column.value: He says, 'I will build myself a great palace with spacious upper rooms.' So he makes large windows in it, panels it with cedar and decorates it in red.

column.name: text
column.value: "Does it make you a king to have more and more cedar? Did not your father have food and drink? He did what was right and just, so all went well with him.

column.name: text
column.value: He defended the cause of the poor and needy, and so all went well. Is that not what it means to know me?" declares the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: "But your eyes and your heart are set only on dishonest gain, on shedding innocent blood and on oppression and extortion."

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore this is what the LORD says about Jehoiakim son of Josiah king of Judah: "They will not mourn for him: 'Alas, my brother! Alas, my sister!' They will not mourn for him: 'Alas, my master! Alas, his splendor!'

column.name: text
column.value: He will have the burial of a donkey--dragged away and thrown outside the gates of Jerusalem."

column.name: text
column.value: "Go up to Lebanon and cry out, let your voice be heard in Bashan, cry out from Abarim, for all your allies are crushed.

column.name: text
column.value: I warned you when you felt secure, but you said, 'I will not listen!' This has been your way from your youth; you have not obeyed me.

column.name: text
column.value: The wind will drive all your shepherds away, and your allies will go into exile. Then you will be ashamed and disgraced because of all your wickedness.

column.name: text
column.value: You who live in 'Lebanon,' who are nestled in cedar buildings, how you will groan when pangs come upon you, pain like that of a woman in labor!

column.name: text
column.value: "As surely as I live," declares the LORD, "even if you, Jehoiachin son of Jehoiakim king of Judah, were a signet ring on my right hand, I would still pull you off.

column.name: text
column.value: I will hand you over to those who seek your life, those you fear--to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and to the Babylonians.

column.name: text
column.value: I will hurl you and the mother who gave you birth into another country, where neither of you was born, and there you both will die.

column.name: text
column.value: You will never come back to the land you long to return to."

column.name: text
column.value: Is this man Jehoiachin a despised, broken pot, an object no one wants? Why will he and his children be hurled out, cast into a land they do not know?

column.name: text
column.value: O land, land, land, hear the word of the LORD!

column.name: text
column.value: This is what the LORD says: "Record this man as if childless, a man who will not prosper in his lifetime, for none of his offspring will prosper, none will sit on the throne of David or rule anymore in Judah."

column.name: text
column.value: After Jehoiachin son of Jehoiakim king of Judah and the officials, the craftsmen and the artisans of Judah were carried into exile from Jerusalem to Babylon by Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, the LORD showed me two baskets of figs placed in front of the temple of the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: One basket had very good figs, like those that ripen early; the other basket had very poor figs, so bad they could not be eaten.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD asked me, "What do you see, Jeremiah?" "Figs," I answered. "The good ones are very good, but the poor ones are so bad they cannot be eaten."

column.name: text
column.value: Then the word of the LORD came to me:

column.name: text
column.value: "This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: 'Like these good figs, I regard as good the exiles from Judah, whom I sent away from this place to the land of the Babylonians.

column.name: text
column.value: My eyes will watch over them for their good, and I will bring them back to this land. I will build them up and not tear them down; I will plant them and not uproot them.

column.name: text
column.value: I will give them a heart to know me, that I am the LORD. They will be my people, and I will be their God, for they will return to me with all their heart.

column.name: text
column.value: "'But like the poor figs, which are so bad they cannot be eaten,' says the LORD, 'so will I deal with Zedekiah king of Judah, his officials and the survivors from Jerusalem, whether they remain in this land or live in Egypt.

column.name: text
column.value: I will make them abhorrent and an offense to all the kingdoms of the earth, a reproach and a byword, an object of ridicule and cursing, wherever I banish them.

column.name: text
column.value: I will send the sword, famine and plague against them until they are destroyed from the land I gave to them and their fathers.'"

column.name: text
column.value: The word came to Jeremiah concerning all the people of Judah in the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah king of Judah, which was the first year of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon.

column.name: text
column.value: So Jeremiah the prophet said to all the people of Judah and to all those living in Jerusalem:

column.name: text
column.value: For twenty-three years--from the thirteenth year of Josiah son of Amon king of Judah until this very day--the word of the LORD has come to me and I have spoken to you again and again, but you have not listened.

column.name: text
column.value: And though the LORD has sent all his servants the prophets to you again and again, you have not listened or paid any attention.

column.name: text
column.value: They said, "Turn now, each of you, from your evil ways and your evil practices, and you can stay in the land the LORD gave to you and your fathers for ever and ever.

column.name: text
column.value: Do not follow other gods to serve and worship them; do not provoke me to anger with what your hands have made. Then I will not harm you."

column.name: text
column.value: "But you did not listen to me," declares the LORD, "and you have provoked me with what your hands have made, and you have brought harm to yourselves."

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore the LORD Almighty says this: "Because you have not listened to my words,

column.name: text
column.value: I will summon all the peoples of the north and my servant Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon," declares the LORD, "and I will bring them against this land and its inhabitants and against all the surrounding nations. I will completely destroy them and make them an object of horror and scorn, and an everlasting ruin.

column.name: text
column.value: I will banish from them the sounds of joy and gladness, the voices of bride and bridegroom, the sound of millstones and the light of the lamp.

column.name: text
column.value: This whole country will become a desolate wasteland, and these nations will serve the king of Babylon seventy years.

column.name: text
column.value: "But when the seventy years are fulfilled, I will punish the king of Babylon and his nation, the land of the Babylonians, for their guilt," declares the LORD, "and will make it desolate forever.

column.name: text
column.value: I will bring upon that land all the things I have spoken against it, all that are written in this book and prophesied by Jeremiah against all the nations.

column.name: text
column.value: They themselves will be enslaved by many nations and great kings; I will repay them according to their deeds and the work of their hands."

column.name: text
column.value: This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, said to me: "Take from my hand this cup filled with the wine of my wrath and make all the nations to whom I send you drink it.

column.name: text
column.value: When they drink it, they will stagger and go mad because of the sword I will send among them."

column.name: text
column.value: So I took the cup from the LORD'S hand and made all the nations to whom he sent me drink it:

column.name: text
column.value: Jerusalem and the towns of Judah, its kings and officials, to make them a ruin and an object of horror and scorn and cursing, as they are today;

column.name: text
column.value: Pharaoh king of Egypt, his attendants, his officials and all his people,

column.name: text
column.value: and all the foreign people there; all the kings of Uz; all the kings of the Philistines (those of Ashkelon, Gaza, Ekron, and the people left at Ashdod);

column.name: text
column.value: Edom, Moab and Ammon;

column.name: text
column.value: all the kings of Tyre and Sidon; the kings of the coastlands across the sea;

column.name: text
column.value: Dedan, Tema, Buz and all who are in distant places;

column.name: text
column.value: all the kings of Arabia and all the kings of the foreign people who live in the desert;

column.name: text
column.value: all the kings of Zimri, Elam and Media;

column.name: text
column.value: and all the kings of the north, near and far, one after the other--all the kingdoms on the face of the earth. And after all of them, the king of Sheshach will drink it too.

column.name: text
column.value: "Then tell them, 'This is what the LORD Almighty, the God of Israel, says: Drink, get drunk and vomit, and fall to rise no more because of the sword I will send among you.'

column.name: text
column.value: But if they refuse to take the cup from your hand and drink, tell them, 'This is what the LORD Almighty says: You must drink it!

column.name: text
column.value: See, I am beginning to bring disaster on the city that bears my Name, and will you indeed go unpunished? You will not go unpunished, for I am calling down a sword upon all who live on the earth, declares the LORD Almighty.'

column.name: text
column.value: "Now prophesy all these words against them and say to them: "'The LORD will roar from on high; he will thunder from his holy dwelling and roar mightily against his land. He will shout like those who tread the grapes, shout against all who live on the earth.

column.name: text
column.value: The tumult will resound to the ends of the earth, for the LORD will bring charges against the nations; he will bring judgment on all mankind and put the wicked to the sword,'" declares the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: This is what the LORD Almighty says: "Look! Disaster is spreading from nation to nation; a mighty storm is rising from the ends of the earth."

column.name: text
column.value: At that time those slain by the LORD will be everywhere--from one end of the earth to the other. They will not be mourned or gathered up or buried, but will be like refuse lying on the ground.

column.name: text
column.value: Weep and wail, you shepherds; roll in the dust, you leaders of the flock. For your time to be slaughtered has come; you will fall and be shattered like fine pottery.

column.name: text
column.value: The shepherds will have nowhere to flee, the leaders of the flock no place to escape.

column.name: text
column.value: Hear the cry of the shepherds, the wailing of the leaders of the flock, for the LORD is destroying their pasture.

column.name: text
column.value: The peaceful meadows will be laid waste because of the fierce anger of the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: Like a lion he will leave his lair, and their land will become desolate because of the sword of the oppressor and because of the LORD'S fierce anger.

column.name: text
column.value: Early in the reign of Zedekiah son of Josiah king of Judah, this word came to Jeremiah from the LORD:

column.name: text
column.value: This is what the LORD said to me: "Make a yoke out of straps and crossbars and put it on your neck.

column.name: text
column.value: Then send word to the kings of Edom, Moab, Ammon, Tyre and Sidon through the envoys who have come to Jerusalem to Zedekiah king of Judah.

column.name: text
column.value: Give them a message for their masters and say, 'This is what the LORD Almighty, the God of Israel, says: "Tell this to your masters:

column.name: text
column.value: With my great power and outstretched arm I made the earth and its people and the animals that are on it, and I give it to anyone I please.

column.name: text
column.value: Now I will hand all your countries over to my servant Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon; I will make even the wild animals subject to him.

column.name: text
column.value: All nations will serve him and his son and his grandson until the time for his land comes; then many nations and great kings will subjugate him.

column.name: text
column.value: "' "If, however, any nation or kingdom will not serve Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon or bow its neck under his yoke, I will punish that nation with the sword, famine and plague, declares the LORD, until I destroy it by his hand.

column.name: text
column.value: So do not listen to your prophets, your diviners, your interpreters of dreams, your mediums or your sorcerers who tell you, 'You will not serve the king of Babylon.'

column.name: text
column.value: They prophesy lies to you that will only serve to remove you far from your lands; I will banish you and you will perish.

column.name: text
column.value: But if any nation will bow its neck under the yoke of the king of Babylon and serve him, I will let that nation remain in its own land to till it and to live there, declares the LORD." '"

column.name: text
column.value: I gave the same message to Zedekiah king of Judah. I said, "Bow your neck under the yoke of the king of Babylon; serve him and his people, and you will live.

column.name: text
column.value: Why will you and your people die by the sword, famine and plague with which the LORD has threatened any nation that will not serve the king of Babylon?

column.name: text
column.value: Do not listen to the words of the prophets who say to you, 'You will not serve the king of Babylon,' for they are prophesying lies to you.

column.name: text
column.value: 'I have not sent them,' declares the LORD. 'They are prophesying lies in my name. Therefore, I will banish you and you will perish, both you and the prophets who prophesy to you.'"

column.name: text
column.value: Then I said to the priests and all these people, "This is what the LORD says: Do not listen to the prophets who say, 'Very soon now the articles from the LORD'S house will be brought back from Babylon.' They are prophesying lies to you.

column.name: text
column.value: Do not listen to them. Serve the king of Babylon, and you will live. Why should this city become a ruin?

column.name: text
column.value: If they are prophets and have the word of the LORD, let them plead with the LORD Almighty that the furnishings remaining in the house of the LORD and in the palace of the king of Judah and in Jerusalem not be taken to Babylon.

column.name: text
column.value: For this is what the LORD Almighty says about the pillars, the Sea, the movable stands and the other furnishings that are left in this city,

column.name: text
column.value: which Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon did not take away when he carried Jehoiachin son of Jehoiakim king of Judah into exile from Jerusalem to Babylon, along with all the nobles of Judah and Jerusalem--

column.name: text
column.value: yes, this is what the LORD Almighty, the God of Israel, says about the things that are left in the house of the LORD and in the palace of the king of Judah and in Jerusalem:

column.name: text
column.value: 'They will be taken to Babylon and there they will remain until the day I come for them,' declares the LORD. 'Then I will bring them back and restore them to this place.'"

column.name: text
column.value: In the fifth month of that same year, the fourth year, early in the reign of Zedekiah king of Judah, the prophet Hananiah son of Azzur, who was from Gibeon, said to me in the house of the LORD in the presence of the priests and all the people:

column.name: text
column.value: "This is what the LORD Almighty, the God of Israel, says: 'I will break the yoke of the king of Babylon.

column.name: text
column.value: Within two years I will bring back to this place all the articles of the LORD'S house that Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon removed from here and took to Babylon.

column.name: text
column.value: I will also bring back to this place Jehoiachin son of Jehoiakim king of Judah and all the other exiles from Judah who went to Babylon,' declares the LORD, 'for I will break the yoke of the king of Babylon.'"

column.name: text
column.value: Then the prophet Jeremiah replied to the prophet Hananiah before the priests and all the people who were standing in the house of the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: He said, "Amen! May the LORD do so! May the LORD fulfill the words you have prophesied by bringing the articles of the LORD'S house and all the exiles back to this place from Babylon.

column.name: text
column.value: Nevertheless, listen to what I have to say in your hearing and in the hearing of all the people:

column.name: text
column.value: From early times the prophets who preceded you and me have prophesied war, disaster and plague against many countries and great kingdoms.

column.name: text
column.value: But the prophet who prophesies peace will be recognized as one truly sent by the LORD only if his prediction comes true."

column.name: text
column.value: Then the prophet Hananiah took the yoke off the neck of the prophet Jeremiah and broke it,

column.name: text
column.value: and he said before all the people, "This is what the LORD says: 'In the same way will I break the yoke of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon off the neck of all the nations within two years.'" At this, the prophet Jeremiah went on his way.

column.name: text
column.value: Shortly after the prophet Hananiah had broken the yoke off the neck of the prophet Jeremiah, the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah:

column.name: text
column.value: "Go and tell Hananiah, 'This is what the LORD says: You have broken a wooden yoke, but in its place you will get a yoke of iron.

column.name: text
column.value: This is what the LORD Almighty, the God of Israel, says: I will put an iron yoke on the necks of all these nations to make them serve Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and they will serve him. I will even give him control over the wild animals.'"

column.name: text
column.value: Then the prophet Jeremiah said to Hananiah the prophet, "Listen, Hananiah! The LORD has not sent you, yet you have persuaded this nation to trust in lies.

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore, this is what the LORD says: 'I am about to remove you from the face of the earth. This very year you are going to die, because you have preached rebellion against the LORD.'"

column.name: text
column.value: In the seventh month of that same year, Hananiah the prophet died.

column.name: text
column.value: Early in the reign of Jehoiakim son of Josiah king of Judah, this word came from the LORD:

column.name: text
column.value: "This is what the LORD says: Stand in the courtyard of the LORD'S house and speak to all the people of the towns of Judah who come to worship in the house of the LORD. Tell them everything I command you; do not omit a word.

column.name: text
column.value: Perhaps they will listen and each will turn from his evil way. Then I will relent and not bring on them the disaster I was planning because of the evil they have done.

column.name: text
column.value: Say to them, 'This is what the LORD says: If you do not listen to me and follow my law, which I have set before you,

column.name: text
column.value: and if you do not listen to the words of my servants the prophets, whom I have sent to you again and again (though you have not listened),

column.name: text
column.value: then I will make this house like Shiloh and this city an object of cursing among all the nations of the earth.'"

column.name: text
column.value: The priests, the prophets and all the people heard Jeremiah speak these words in the house of the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: But as soon as Jeremiah finished telling all the people everything the LORD had commanded him to say, the priests, the prophets and all the people seized him and said, "You must die!

column.name: text
column.value: Why do you prophesy in the LORD'S name that this house will be like Shiloh and this city will be desolate and deserted?" And all the people crowded around Jeremiah in the house of the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: When the officials of Judah heard about these things, they went up from the royal palace to the house of the LORD and took their places at the entrance of the New Gate of the LORD'S house.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the priests and the prophets said to the officials and all the people, "This man should be sentenced to death because he has prophesied against this city. You have heard it with your own ears!"

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jeremiah said to all the officials and all the people: "The LORD sent me to prophesy against this house and this city all the things you have heard.

column.name: text
column.value: Now reform your ways and your actions and obey the LORD your God. Then the LORD will relent and not bring the disaster he has pronounced against you.

column.name: text
column.value: As for me, I am in your hands; do with me whatever you think is good and right.

column.name: text
column.value: Be assured, however, that if you put me to death, you will bring the guilt of innocent blood on yourselves and on this city and on those who live in it, for in truth the LORD has sent me to you to speak all these words in your hearing."

column.name: text
column.value: Then the officials and all the people said to the priests and the prophets, "This man should not be sentenced to death! He has spoken to us in the name of the LORD our God."

column.name: text
column.value: Some of the elders of the land stepped forward and said to the entire assembly of people,

column.name: text
column.value: "Micah of Moresheth prophesied in the days of Hezekiah king of Judah. He told all the people of Judah, 'This is what the LORD Almighty says: "'Zion will be plowed like a field, Jerusalem will become a heap of rubble, the temple hill a mound overgrown with thickets.'

column.name: text
column.value: "Did Hezekiah king of Judah or anyone else in Judah put him to death? Did not Hezekiah fear the LORD and seek his favor? And did not the LORD relent, so that he did not bring the disaster he pronounced against them? We are about to bring a terrible disaster on ourselves!"

column.name: text
column.value: (Now Uriah son of Shemaiah from Kiriath Jearim was another man who prophesied in the name of the LORD; he prophesied the same things against this city and this land as Jeremiah did.

column.name: text
column.value: When King Jehoiakim and all his officers and officials heard his words, the king sought to put him to death. But Uriah heard of it and fled in fear to Egypt.

column.name: text
column.value: King Jehoiakim, however, sent Elnathan son of Acbor to Egypt, along with some other men.

column.name: text
column.value: They brought Uriah out of Egypt and took him to King Jehoiakim, who had him struck down with a sword and his body thrown into the burial place of the common people.)

column.name: text
column.value: Furthermore, Ahikam son of Shaphan supported Jeremiah, and so he was not handed over to the people to be put to death.

column.name: text
column.value: This is the text of the letter that the prophet Jeremiah sent from Jerusalem to the surviving elders among the exiles and to the priests, the prophets and all the other people Nebuchadnezzar had carried into exile from Jerusalem to Babylon.

column.name: text
column.value: (This was after King Jehoiachin and the queen mother, the court officials and the leaders of Judah and Jerusalem, the craftsmen and the artisans had gone into exile from Jerusalem.)

column.name: text
column.value: He entrusted the letter to Elasah son of Shaphan and to Gemariah son of Hilkiah, whom Zedekiah king of Judah sent to King Nebuchadnezzar in Babylon. It said:

column.name: text
column.value: This is what the LORD Almighty, the God of Israel, says to all those I carried into exile from Jerusalem to Babylon:

column.name: text
column.value: "Build houses and settle down; plant gardens and eat what they produce.

column.name: text
column.value: Marry and have sons and daughters; find wives for your sons and give your daughters in marriage, so that they too may have sons and daughters. Increase in number there; do not decrease.

column.name: text
column.value: Also, seek the peace and prosperity of the city to which I have carried you into exile. Pray to the LORD for it, because if it prospers, you too will prosper."

column.name: text
column.value: Yes, this is what the LORD Almighty, the God of Israel, says: "Do not let the prophets and diviners among you deceive you. Do not listen to the dreams you encourage them to have.

column.name: text
column.value: They are prophesying lies to you in my name. I have not sent them," declares the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: This is what the LORD says: "When seventy years are completed for Babylon, I will come to you and fulfill my gracious promise to bring you back to this place.

column.name: text
column.value: For I know the plans I have for you," declares the LORD, "plans to prosper you and not to harm you, plans to give you hope and a future.

column.name: text
column.value: Then you will call upon me and come and pray to me, and I will listen to you.

column.name: text
column.value: You will seek me and find me when you seek me with all your heart.

column.name: text
column.value: I will be found by you," declares the LORD, "and will bring you back from captivity. I will gather you from all the nations and places where I have banished you," declares the LORD, "and will bring you back to the place from which I carried you into exile."

column.name: text
column.value: You may say, "The LORD has raised up prophets for us in Babylon,"

column.name: text
column.value: but this is what the LORD says about the king who sits on David's throne and all the people who remain in this city, your countrymen who did not go with you into exile--

column.name: text
column.value: yes, this is what the LORD Almighty says: "I will send the sword, famine and plague against them and I will make them like poor figs that are so bad they cannot be eaten.

column.name: text
column.value: I will pursue them with the sword, famine and plague and will make them abhorrent to all the kingdoms of the earth and an object of cursing and horror, of scorn and reproach, among all the nations where I drive them.

column.name: text
column.value: For they have not listened to my words," declares the LORD, "words that I sent to them again and again by my servants the prophets. And you exiles have not listened either," declares the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore, hear the word of the LORD, all you exiles whom I have sent away from Jerusalem to Babylon.

column.name: text
column.value: This is what the LORD Almighty, the God of Israel, says about Ahab son of Kolaiah and Zedekiah son of Maaseiah, who are prophesying lies to you in my name: "I will hand them over to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and he will put them to death before your very eyes.

column.name: text
column.value: Because of them, all the exiles from Judah who are in Babylon will use this curse: 'The LORD treat you like Zedekiah and Ahab, whom the king of Babylon burned in the fire.'

column.name: text
column.value: For they have done outrageous things in Israel; they have committed adultery with their neighbors' wives and in my name have spoken lies, which I did not tell them to do. I know it and am a witness to it," declares the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: Tell Shemaiah the Nehelamite,

column.name: text
column.value: "This is what the LORD Almighty, the God of Israel, says: You sent letters in your own name to all the people in Jerusalem, to Zephaniah son of Maaseiah the priest, and to all the other priests. You said to Zephaniah,

column.name: text
column.value: 'The LORD has appointed you priest in place of Jehoiada to be in charge of the house of the LORD; you should put any madman who acts like a prophet into the stocks and neck-irons.

column.name: text
column.value: So why have you not reprimanded Jeremiah from Anathoth, who poses as a prophet among you?

column.name: text
column.value: He has sent this message to us in Babylon: It will be a long time. Therefore build houses and settle down; plant gardens and eat what they produce.'"

column.name: text
column.value: Zephaniah the priest, however, read the letter to Jeremiah the prophet.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah:

column.name: text
column.value: "Send this message to all the exiles: 'This is what the LORD says about Shemaiah the Nehelamite: Because Shemaiah has prophesied to you, even though I did not send him, and has led you to believe a lie,

column.name: text
column.value: this is what the LORD says: I will surely punish Shemaiah the Nehelamite and his descendants. He will have no one left among this people, nor will he see the good things I will do for my people, declares the LORD, because he has preached rebellion against me.'"

column.name: text
column.value: This is the word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD:

column.name: text
column.value: "This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: 'Write in a book all the words I have spoken to you.

column.name: text
column.value: The days are coming,' declares the LORD, 'when I will bring my people Israel and Judah back from captivity and restore them to the land I gave their forefathers to possess,' says the LORD."

column.name: text
column.value: These are the words the LORD spoke concerning Israel and Judah:

column.name: text
column.value: "This is what the LORD says: "'Cries of fear are heard--terror, not peace.

column.name: text
column.value: Ask and see: Can a man bear children? Then why do I see every strong man with his hands on his stomach like a woman in labor, every face turned deathly pale?

column.name: text
column.value: How awful that day will be! None will be like it. It will be a time of trouble for Jacob, but he will be saved out of it.

column.name: text
column.value: "' In that day,' declares the LORD Almighty, 'I will break the yoke off their necks and will tear off their bonds; no longer will foreigners enslave them.

column.name: text
column.value: Instead, they will serve the LORD their God and David their king, whom I will raise up for them.

column.name: text
column.value: "'So do not fear, O Jacob my servant; do not be dismayed, O Israel,' declares the LORD. 'I will surely save you out of a distant place, your descendants from the land of their exile. Jacob will again have peace and security, and no one will make him afraid.

column.name: text
column.value: I am with you and will save you,' declares the LORD. 'Though I completely destroy all the nations among which I scatter you, I will not completely destroy you. I will discipline you but only with justice; I will not let you go entirely unpunished.'

column.name: text
column.value: "This is what the LORD says: "'Your wound is incurable, your injury beyond healing.

column.name: text
column.value: There is no one to plead your cause, no remedy for your sore, no healing for you.

column.name: text
column.value: All your allies have forgotten you; they care nothing for you. I have struck you as an enemy would and punished you as would the cruel, because your guilt is so great and your sins so many.

column.name: text
column.value: Why do you cry out over your wound, your pain that has no cure? Because of your great guilt and many sins I have done these things to you.

column.name: text
column.value: "'But all who devour you will be devoured; all your enemies will go into exile. Those who plunder you will be plundered; all who make spoil of you I will despoil.

column.name: text
column.value: But I will restore you to health and heal your wounds,' declares the LORD, 'because you are called an outcast, Zion for whom no one cares.'

column.name: text
column.value: "This is what the LORD says: "'I will restore the fortunes of Jacob's tents and have compassion on his dwellings; the city will be rebuilt on her ruins, and the palace will stand in its proper place.

column.name: text
column.value: From them will come songs of thanksgiving and the sound of rejoicing. I will add to their numbers, and they will not be decreased; I will bring them honor, and they will not be disdained.

column.name: text
column.value: Their children will be as in days of old, and their community will be established before me; I will punish all who oppress them.

column.name: text
column.value: Their leader will be one of their own; their ruler will arise from among them. I will bring him near and he will come close to me, for who is he who will devote himself to be close to me?' declares the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: "'So you will be my people, and I will be your God.'"

column.name: text
column.value: See, the storm of the LORD will burst out in wrath, a driving wind swirling down on the heads of the wicked.

column.name: text
column.value: The fierce anger of the LORD will not turn back until he fully accomplishes the purposes of his heart. In days to come you will understand this.

column.name: text
column.value: "At that time," declares the LORD, "I will be the God of all the clans of Israel, and they will be my people."

column.name: text
column.value: This is what the LORD says: "The people who survive the sword will find favor in the desert; I will come to give rest to Israel."

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD appeared to us in the past, saying: "I have loved you with an everlasting love; I have drawn you with loving-kindness.

column.name: text
column.value: I will build you up again and you will be rebuilt, O Virgin Israel. Again you will take up your tambourines and go out to dance with the joyful.

column.name: text
column.value: Again you will plant vineyards on the hills of Samaria; the farmers will plant them and enjoy their fruit.

column.name: text
column.value: There will be a day when watchmen cry out on the hills of Ephraim, 'Come, let us go up to Zion, to the LORD our God.'"

column.name: text
column.value: This is what the LORD says: "Sing with joy for Jacob; shout for the foremost of the nations. Make your praises heard, and say, 'O LORD, save your people, the remnant of Israel.'

column.name: text
column.value: See, I will bring them from the land of the north and gather them from the ends of the earth. Among them will be the blind and the lame, expectant mothers and women in labor; a great throng will return.

column.name: text
column.value: They will come with weeping; they will pray as I bring them back. I will lead them beside streams of water on a level path where they will not stumble, because I am Israel's father, and Ephraim is my firstborn son.

column.name: text
column.value: "Hear the word of the LORD, O nations; proclaim it in distant coastlands: 'He who scattered Israel will gather them and will watch over his flock like a shepherd.'

column.name: text
column.value: For the LORD will ransom Jacob and redeem them from the hand of those stronger than they.

column.name: text
column.value: They will come and shout for joy on the heights of Zion; they will rejoice in the bounty of the LORD--the grain, the new wine and the oil, the young of the flocks and herds. They will be like a well-watered garden, and they will sorrow no more.

column.name: text
column.value: Then maidens will dance and be glad, young men and old as well. I will turn their mourning into gladness; I will give them comfort and joy instead of sorrow.

column.name: text
column.value: I will satisfy the priests with abundance, and my people will be filled with my bounty," declares the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: This is what the LORD says: "A voice is heard in Ramah, mourning and great weeping, Rachel weeping for her children and refusing to be comforted, because her children are no more."

column.name: text
column.value: This is what the LORD says: "Restrain your voice from weeping and your eyes from tears, for your work will be rewarded," declares the LORD. "They will return from the land of the enemy.

column.name: text
column.value: So there is hope for your future," declares the LORD. "Your children will return to their own land.

column.name: text
column.value: "I have surely heard Ephraim's moaning: 'You disciplined me like an unruly calf, and I have been disciplined. Restore me, and I will return, because you are the LORD my God.

column.name: text
column.value: After I strayed, I repented; after I came to understand, I beat my breast. I was ashamed and humiliated because I bore the disgrace of my youth.'

column.name: text
column.value: Is not Ephraim my dear son, the child in whom I delight? Though I often speak against him, I still remember him. Therefore my heart yearns for him; I have great compassion for him," declares the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: "Set up road signs; put up guideposts. Take note of the highway, the road that you take. Return, O Virgin Israel, return to your towns.

column.name: text
column.value: How long will you wander, O unfaithful daughter? The LORD will create a new thing on earth--a woman will surround a man."

column.name: text
column.value: This is what the LORD Almighty, the God of Israel, says: "When I bring them back from captivity, the people in the land of Judah and in its towns will once again use these words: 'The LORD bless you, O righteous dwelling, O sacred mountain.'

column.name: text
column.value: People will live together in Judah and all its towns--farmers and those who move about with their flocks.

column.name: text
column.value: I will refresh the weary and satisfy the faint."

column.name: text
column.value: At this I awoke and looked around. My sleep had been pleasant to me.

column.name: text
column.value: "The days are coming," declares the LORD, "when I will plant the house of Israel and the house of Judah with the offspring of men and of animals.

column.name: text
column.value: Just as I watched over them to uproot and tear down, and to overthrow, destroy and bring disaster, so I will watch over them to build and to plant," declares the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: "In those days people will no longer say, 'The fathers have eaten sour grapes, and the children's teeth are set on edge.'

column.name: text
column.value: Instead, everyone will die for his own sin; whoever eats sour grapes--his own teeth will be set on edge.

column.name: text
column.value: "The time is coming," declares the LORD, "when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah.

column.name: text
column.value: It will not be like the covenant I made with their forefathers when I took them by the hand to lead them out of Egypt, because they broke my covenant, though I was a husband to them," declares the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: "This is the covenant I will make with the house of Israel after that time," declares the LORD. "I will put my law in their minds and write it on their hearts. I will be their God, and they will be my people.

column.name: text
column.value: No longer will a man teach his neighbor, or a man his brother, saying, 'Know the LORD,' because they will all know me, from the least of them to the greatest," declares the LORD. "For I will forgive their wickedness and will remember their sins no more."

column.name: text
column.value: This is what the LORD says, he who appoints the sun to shine by day, who decrees the moon and stars to shine by night, who stirs up the sea so that its waves roar--the LORD Almighty is his name:

column.name: text
column.value: "Only if these decrees vanish from my sight," declares the LORD, "will the descendants of Israel ever cease to be a nation before me."

column.name: text
column.value: This is what the LORD says: "Only if the heavens above can be measured and the foundations of the earth below be searched out will I reject all the descendants of Israel because of all they have done," declares the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: "The days are coming," declares the LORD, "when this city will be rebuilt for me from the Tower of Hananel to the Corner Gate.

column.name: text
column.value: The measuring line will stretch from there straight to the hill of Gareb and then turn to Goah.

column.name: text
column.value: The whole valley where dead bodies and ashes are thrown, and all the terraces out to the Kidron Valley on the east as far as the corner of the Horse Gate, will be holy to the LORD. The city will never again be uprooted or demolished."

column.name: text
column.value: While Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and all his army and all the kingdoms and peoples in the empire he ruled were fighting against Jerusalem and all its surrounding towns, this word came to Jeremiah from the LORD:

column.name: text
column.value: "This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: Go to Zedekiah king of Judah and tell him, 'This is what the LORD says: I am about to hand this city over to the king of Babylon, and he will burn it down.

column.name: text
column.value: You will not escape from his grasp but will surely be captured and handed over to him. You will see the king of Babylon with your own eyes, and he will speak with you face to face. And you will go to Babylon.

column.name: text
column.value: "'Yet hear the promise of the LORD, O Zedekiah king of Judah. This is what the LORD says concerning you: You will not die by the sword;

column.name: text
column.value: you will die peacefully. As people made a funeral fire in honor of your fathers, the former kings who preceded you, so they will make a fire in your honor and lament, "Alas, O master!" I myself make this promise, declares the LORD.'"

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jeremiah the prophet told all this to Zedekiah king of Judah, in Jerusalem,

column.name: text
column.value: while the army of the king of Babylon was fighting against Jerusalem and the other cities of Judah that were still holding out--Lachish and Azekah. These were the only fortified cities left in Judah.

column.name: text
column.value: The word came to Jeremiah from the LORD after King Zedekiah had made a covenant with all the people in Jerusalem to proclaim freedom for the slaves.

column.name: text
column.value: Everyone was to free his Hebrew slaves, both male and female; no one was to hold a fellow Jew in bondage.

column.name: text
column.value: So all the officials and people who entered into this covenant agreed that they would free their male and female slaves and no longer hold them in bondage. They agreed, and set them free.

column.name: text
column.value: But afterward they changed their minds and took back the slaves they had freed and enslaved them again.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah:

column.name: text
column.value: "This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: I made a covenant with your forefathers when I brought them out of Egypt, out of the land of slavery. I said,

column.name: text
column.value: 'Every seventh year each of you must free any fellow Hebrew who has sold himself to you. After he has served you six years, you must let him go free.' Your fathers, however, did not listen to me or pay attention to me.

column.name: text
column.value: Recently you repented and did what is right in my sight: Each of you proclaimed freedom to his countrymen. You even made a covenant before me in the house that bears my Name.

column.name: text
column.value: But now you have turned around and profaned my name; each of you has taken back the male and female slaves you had set free to go where they wished. You have forced them to become your slaves again.

column.name: text
column.value: "Therefore, this is what the LORD says: You have not obeyed me; you have not proclaimed freedom for your fellow countrymen. So I now proclaim 'freedom' for you, declares the LORD--'freedom' to fall by the sword, plague and famine. I will make you abhorrent to all the kingdoms of the earth.

column.name: text
column.value: The men who have violated my covenant and have not fulfilled the terms of the covenant they made before me, I will treat like the calf they cut in two and then walked between its pieces.

column.name: text
column.value: The leaders of Judah and Jerusalem, the court officials, the priests and all the people of the land who walked between the pieces of the calf,

column.name: text
column.value: I will hand over to their enemies who seek their lives. Their dead bodies will become food for the birds of the air and the beasts of the earth.

column.name: text
column.value: "I will hand Zedekiah king of Judah and his officials over to their enemies who seek their lives, to the army of the king of Babylon, which has withdrawn from you.

column.name: text
column.value: I am going to give the order, declares the LORD, and I will bring them back to this city. They will fight against it, take it and burn it down. And I will lay waste the towns of Judah so no one can live there."

column.name: text
column.value: While Jeremiah was still confined in the courtyard of the guard, the word of the LORD came to him a second time:

column.name: text
column.value: "This is what the LORD says, he who made the earth, the LORD who formed it and established it--the LORD is his name:

column.name: text
column.value: 'Call to me and I will answer you and tell you great and unsearchable things you do not know.'

column.name: text
column.value: For this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says about the houses in this city and the royal palaces of Judah that have been torn down to be used against the siege ramps and the sword

column.name: text
column.value: in the fight with the Babylonians: 'They will be filled with the dead bodies of the men I will slay in my anger and wrath. I will hide my face from this city because of all its wickedness.

column.name: text
column.value: "'Nevertheless, I will bring health and healing to it; I will heal my people and will let them enjoy abundant peace and security.

column.name: text
column.value: I will bring Judah and Israel back from captivity and will rebuild them as they were before.

column.name: text
column.value: I will cleanse them from all the sin they have committed against me and will forgive all their sins of rebellion against me.

column.name: text
column.value: Then this city will bring me renown, joy, praise and honor before all nations on earth that hear of all the good things I do for it; and they will be in awe and will tremble at the abundant prosperity and peace I provide for it.'

column.name: text
column.value: "This is what the LORD says: 'You say about this place, "It is a desolate waste, without men or animals." Yet in the towns of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem that are deserted, inhabited by neither men nor animals, there will be heard once more

column.name: text
column.value: the sounds of joy and gladness, the voices of bride and bridegroom, and the voices of those who bring thank offerings to the house of the LORD, saying, "Give thanks to the LORD Almighty, for the LORD is good; his love endures forever." For I will restore the fortunes of the land as they were before,' says the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: "This is what the LORD Almighty says: 'In this place, desolate and without men or animals--in all its towns there will again be pastures for shepherds to rest their flocks.

column.name: text
column.value: In the towns of the hill country, of the western foothills and of the Negev, in the territory of Benjamin, in the villages around Jerusalem and in the towns of Judah, flocks will again pass under the hand of the one who counts them,' says the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: "'The days are coming,' declares the LORD, 'when I will fulfill the gracious promise I made to the house of Israel and to the house of Judah.

column.name: text
column.value: "'In those days and at that time I will make a righteous Branch sprout from David's line; he will do what is just and right in the land.

column.name: text
column.value: In those days Judah will be saved and Jerusalem will live in safety. This is the name by which it will be called: The LORD Our Righteousness.'

column.name: text
column.value: For this is what the LORD says: 'David will never fail to have a man to sit on the throne of the house of Israel,

column.name: text
column.value: nor will the priests, who are Levites, ever fail to have a man to stand before me continually to offer burnt offerings, to burn grain offerings and to present sacrifices.'"

column.name: text
column.value: The word of the LORD came to Jeremiah:

column.name: text
column.value: "This is what the LORD says: 'If you can break my covenant with the day and my covenant with the night, so that day and night no longer come at their appointed time,

column.name: text
column.value: then my covenant with David my servant--and my covenant with the Levites who are priests ministering before me--can be broken and David will no longer have a descendant to reign on his throne.

column.name: text
column.value: I will make the descendants of David my servant and the Levites who minister before me as countless as the stars of the sky and as measureless as the sand on the seashore.'"

column.name: text
column.value: The word of the LORD came to Jeremiah:

column.name: text
column.value: "Have you not noticed that these people are saying, 'The LORD has rejected the two kingdoms he chose'? So they despise my people and no longer regard them as a nation.

column.name: text
column.value: This is what the LORD says: 'If I have not established my covenant with day and night and the fixed laws of heaven and earth,

column.name: text
column.value: then I will reject the descendants of Jacob and David my servant and will not choose one of his sons to rule over the descendants of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. For I will restore their fortunes and have compassion on them.'"

column.name: text
column.value: This is the word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD in the tenth year of Zedekiah king of Judah, which was the eighteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar.

column.name: text
column.value: The army of the king of Babylon was then besieging Jerusalem, and Jeremiah the prophet was confined in the courtyard of the guard in the royal palace of Judah.

column.name: text
column.value: Now Zedekiah king of Judah had imprisoned him there, saying, "Why do you prophesy as you do? You say, 'This is what the LORD says: I am about to hand this city over to the king of Babylon, and he will capture it.

column.name: text
column.value: Zedekiah king of Judah will not escape out of the hands of the Babylonians but will certainly be handed over to the king of Babylon, and will speak with him face to face and see him with his own eyes.

column.name: text
column.value: He will take Zedekiah to Babylon, where he will remain until I deal with him, declares the LORD. If you fight against the Babylonians, you will not succeed.'"

column.name: text
column.value: Jeremiah said, "The word of the LORD came to me:

column.name: text
column.value: Hanamel son of Shallum your uncle is going to come to you and say, 'Buy my field at Anathoth, because as nearest relative it is your right and duty to buy it.'

column.name: text
column.value: "Then, just as the LORD had said, my cousin Hanamel came to me in the courtyard of the guard and said, 'Buy my field at Anathoth in the territory of Benjamin. Since it is your right to redeem it and possess it, buy it for yourself.' "I knew that this was the word of the LORD;

column.name: text
column.value: so I bought the field at Anathoth from my cousin Hanamel and weighed out for him seventeen shekels of silver.

column.name: text
column.value: I signed and sealed the deed, had it witnessed, and weighed out the silver on the scales.

column.name: text
column.value: I took the deed of purchase--the sealed copy containing the terms and conditions, as well as the unsealed copy--

column.name: text
column.value: and I gave this deed to Baruch son of Neriah, the son of Mahseiah, in the presence of my cousin Hanamel and of the witnesses who had signed the deed and of all the Jews sitting in the courtyard of the guard.

column.name: text
column.value: "In their presence I gave Baruch these instructions:

column.name: text
column.value: 'This is what the LORD Almighty, the God of Israel, says: Take these documents, both the sealed and unsealed copies of the deed of purchase, and put them in a clay jar so they will last a long time.

column.name: text
column.value: For this is what the LORD Almighty, the God of Israel, says: Houses, fields and vineyards will again be bought in this land.'

column.name: text
column.value: "After I had given the deed of purchase to Baruch son of Neriah, I prayed to the LORD:

column.name: text
column.value: "Ah, Sovereign LORD, you have made the heavens and the earth by your great power and outstretched arm. Nothing is too hard for you.

column.name: text
column.value: You show love to thousands but bring the punishment for the fathers' sins into the laps of their children after them. O great and powerful God, whose name is the LORD Almighty,

column.name: text
column.value: great are your purposes and mighty are your deeds. Your eyes are open to all the ways of men; you reward everyone according to his conduct and as his deeds deserve.

column.name: text
column.value: You performed miraculous signs and wonders in Egypt and have continued them to this day, both in Israel and among all mankind, and have gained the renown that is still yours.

column.name: text
column.value: You brought your people Israel out of Egypt with signs and wonders, by a mighty hand and an outstretched arm and with great terror.

column.name: text
column.value: You gave them this land you had sworn to give their forefathers, a land flowing with milk and honey.

column.name: text
column.value: They came in and took possession of it, but they did not obey you or follow your law; they did not do what you commanded them to do. So you brought all this disaster upon them.

column.name: text
column.value: "See how the siege ramps are built up to take the city. Because of the sword, famine and plague, the city will be handed over to the Babylonians who are attacking it. What you said has happened, as you now see.

column.name: text
column.value: And though the city will be handed over to the Babylonians, you, O Sovereign LORD, say to me, 'Buy the field with silver and have the transaction witnessed.'"

column.name: text
column.value: Then the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah:

column.name: text
column.value: "I am the LORD, the God of all mankind. Is anything too hard for me?

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore, this is what the LORD says: I am about to hand this city over to the Babylonians and to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, who will capture it.

column.name: text
column.value: The Babylonians who are attacking this city will come in and set it on fire; they will burn it down, along with the houses where the people provoked me to anger by burning incense on the roofs to Baal and by pouring out drink offerings to other gods.

column.name: text
column.value: "The people of Israel and Judah have done nothing but evil in my sight from their youth; indeed, the people of Israel have done nothing but provoke me with what their hands have made, declares the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: From the day it was built until now, this city has so aroused my anger and wrath that I must remove it from my sight.

column.name: text
column.value: The people of Israel and Judah have provoked me by all the evil they have done--they, their kings and officials, their priests and prophets, the men of Judah and the people of Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: They turned their backs to me and not their faces; though I taught them again and again, they would not listen or respond to discipline.

column.name: text
column.value: They set up their abominable idols in the house that bears my Name and defiled it.

column.name: text
column.value: They built high places for Baal in the Valley of Ben Hinnom to sacrifice their sons and daughters to Molech, though I never commanded, nor did it enter my mind, that they should do such a detestable thing and so make Judah sin.

column.name: text
column.value: "You are saying about this city, 'By the sword, famine and plague it will be handed over to the king of Babylon'; but this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says:

column.name: text
column.value: I will surely gather them from all the lands where I banish them in my furious anger and great wrath; I will bring them back to this place and let them live in safety.

column.name: text
column.value: They will be my people, and I will be their God.

column.name: text
column.value: I will give them singleness of heart and action, so that they will always fear me for their own good and the good of their children after them.

column.name: text
column.value: I will make an everlasting covenant with them: I will never stop doing good to them, and I will inspire them to fear me, so that they will never turn away from me.

column.name: text
column.value: I will rejoice in doing them good and will assuredly plant them in this land with all my heart and soul.

column.name: text
column.value: "This is what the LORD says: As I have brought all this great calamity on this people, so I will give them all the prosperity I have promised them.

column.name: text
column.value: Once more fields will be bought in this land of which you say, 'It is a desolate waste, without men or animals, for it has been handed over to the Babylonians.'

column.name: text
column.value: Fields will be bought for silver, and deeds will be signed, sealed and witnessed in the territory of Benjamin, in the villages around Jerusalem, in the towns of Judah and in the towns of the hill country, of the western foothills and of the Negev, because I will restore their fortunes, declares the LORD."

column.name: text
column.value: This is the word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD during the reign of Jehoiakim son of Josiah king of Judah:

column.name: text
column.value: "Go to the Recabite family and invite them to come to one of the side rooms of the house of the LORD and give them wine to drink."

column.name: text
column.value: So I went to get Jaazaniah son of Jeremiah, the son of Habazziniah, and his brothers and all his sons--the whole family of the Recabites.

column.name: text
column.value: I brought them into the house of the LORD, into the room of the sons of Hanan son of Igdaliah the man of God. It was next to the room of the officials, which was over that of Maaseiah son of Shallum the doorkeeper.

column.name: text
column.value: Then I set bowls full of wine and some cups before the men of the Recabite family and said to them, "Drink some wine."

column.name: text
column.value: But they replied, "We do not drink wine, because our forefather Jonadab son of Recab gave us this command: 'Neither you nor your descendants must ever drink wine.

column.name: text
column.value: Also you must never build houses, sow seed or plant vineyards; you must never have any of these things, but must always live in tents. Then you will live a long time in the land where you are nomads.'

column.name: text
column.value: We have obeyed everything our forefather Jonadab son of Recab commanded us. Neither we nor our wives nor our sons and daughters have ever drunk wine

column.name: text
column.value: or built houses to live in or had vineyards, fields or crops.

column.name: text
column.value: We have lived in tents and have fully obeyed everything our forefather Jonadab commanded us.

column.name: text
column.value: But when Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon invaded this land, we said, 'Come, we must go to Jerusalem to escape the Babylonian and Aramean armies.' So we have remained in Jerusalem."

column.name: text
column.value: Then the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah, saying:

column.name: text
column.value: "This is what the LORD Almighty, the God of Israel, says: Go and tell the men of Judah and the people of Jerusalem, 'Will you not learn a lesson and obey my words?' declares the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: 'Jonadab son of Recab ordered his sons not to drink wine and this command has been kept. To this day they do not drink wine, because they obey their forefather's command. But I have spoken to you again and again, yet you have not obeyed me.

column.name: text
column.value: Again and again I sent all my servants the prophets to you. They said, "Each of you must turn from your wicked ways and reform your actions; do not follow other gods to serve them. Then you will live in the land I have given to you and your fathers." But you have not paid attention or listened to me.

column.name: text
column.value: The descendants of Jonadab son of Recab have carried out the command their forefather gave them, but these people have not obeyed me.'

column.name: text
column.value: "Therefore, this is what the LORD God Almighty, the God of Israel, says: 'Listen! I am going to bring on Judah and on everyone living in Jerusalem every disaster I pronounced against them. I spoke to them, but they did not listen; I called to them, but they did not answer.'"

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jeremiah said to the family of the Recabites, "This is what the LORD Almighty, the God of Israel, says: 'You have obeyed the command of your forefather Jonadab and have followed all his instructions and have done everything he ordered.'

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore, this is what the LORD Almighty, the God of Israel, says: 'Jonadab son of Recab will never fail to have a man to serve me.'"

column.name: text
column.value: In the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah king of Judah, this word came to Jeremiah from the LORD:

column.name: text
column.value: "Take a scroll and write on it all the words I have spoken to you concerning Israel, Judah and all the other nations from the time I began speaking to you in the reign of Josiah till now.

column.name: text
column.value: Perhaps when the people of Judah hear about every disaster I plan to inflict on them, each of them will turn from his wicked way; then I will forgive their wickedness and their sin."

column.name: text
column.value: So Jeremiah called Baruch son of Neriah, and while Jeremiah dictated all the words the LORD had spoken to him, Baruch wrote them on the scroll.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jeremiah told Baruch, "I am restricted; I cannot go to the LORD'S temple.

column.name: text
column.value: So you go to the house of the LORD on a day of fasting and read to the people from the scroll the words of the LORD that you wrote as I dictated. Read them to all the people of Judah who come in from their towns.

column.name: text
column.value: Perhaps they will bring their petition before the LORD, and each will turn from his wicked ways, for the anger and wrath pronounced against this people by the LORD are great."

column.name: text
column.value: Baruch son of Neriah did everything Jeremiah the prophet told him to do; at the LORD'S temple he read the words of the LORD from the scroll.

column.name: text
column.value: In the ninth month of the fifth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah king of Judah, a time of fasting before the LORD was proclaimed for all the people in Jerusalem and those who had come from the towns of Judah.

column.name: text
column.value: From the room of Gemariah son of Shaphan the secretary, which was in the upper courtyard at the entrance of the New Gate of the temple, Baruch read to all the people at the LORD'S temple the words of Jeremiah from the scroll.

column.name: text
column.value: When Micaiah son of Gemariah, the son of Shaphan, heard all the words of the LORD from the scroll,

column.name: text
column.value: he went down to the secretary's room in the royal palace, where all the officials were sitting: Elishama the secretary, Delaiah son of Shemaiah, Elnathan son of Acbor, Gemariah son of Shaphan, Zedekiah son of Hananiah, and all the other officials.

column.name: text
column.value: After Micaiah told them everything he had heard Baruch read to the people from the scroll,

column.name: text
column.value: all the officials sent Jehudi son of Nethaniah, the son of Shelemiah, the son of Cushi, to say to Baruch, "Bring the scroll from which you have read to the people and come." So Baruch son of Neriah went to them with the scroll in his hand.

column.name: text
column.value: They said to him, "Sit down, please, and read it to us." So Baruch read it to them.

column.name: text
column.value: When they heard all these words, they looked at each other in fear and said to Baruch, "We must report all these words to the king."

column.name: text
column.value: Then they asked Baruch, "Tell us, how did you come to write all this? Did Jeremiah dictate it?"

column.name: text
column.value: "Yes," Baruch replied, "he dictated all these words to me, and I wrote them in ink on the scroll."

column.name: text
column.value: Then the officials said to Baruch, "You and Jeremiah, go and hide. Don't let anyone know where you are."

column.name: text
column.value: After they put the scroll in the room of Elishama the secretary, they went to the king in the courtyard and reported everything to him.

column.name: text
column.value: The king sent Jehudi to get the scroll, and Jehudi brought it from the room of Elishama the secretary and read it to the king and all the officials standing beside him.

column.name: text
column.value: It was the ninth month and the king was sitting in the winter apartment, with a fire burning in the firepot in front of him.

column.name: text
column.value: Whenever Jehudi had read three or four columns of the scroll, the king cut them off with a scribe's knife and threw them into the firepot, until the entire scroll was burned in the fire.

column.name: text
column.value: The king and all his attendants who heard all these words showed no fear, nor did they tear their clothes.

column.name: text
column.value: Even though Elnathan, Delaiah and Gemariah urged the king not to burn the scroll, he would not listen to them.

column.name: text
column.value: Instead, the king commanded Jerahmeel, a son of the king, Seraiah son of Azriel and Shelemiah son of Abdeel to arrest Baruch the scribe and Jeremiah the prophet. But the LORD had hidden them.

column.name: text
column.value: After the king burned the scroll containing the words that Baruch had written at Jeremiah's dictation, the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah:

column.name: text
column.value: "Take another scroll and write on it all the words that were on the first scroll, which Jehoiakim king of Judah burned up.

column.name: text
column.value: Also tell Jehoiakim king of Judah, 'This is what the LORD says: You burned that scroll and said, "Why did you write on it that the king of Babylon would certainly come and destroy this land and cut off both men and animals from it?"

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore, this is what the LORD says about Jehoiakim king of Judah: He will have no one to sit on the throne of David; his body will be thrown out and exposed to the heat by day and the frost by night.

column.name: text
column.value: I will punish him and his children and his attendants for their wickedness; I will bring on them and those living in Jerusalem and the people of Judah every disaster I pronounced against them, because they have not listened.'"

column.name: text
column.value: So Jeremiah took another scroll and gave it to the scribe Baruch son of Neriah, and as Jeremiah dictated, Baruch wrote on it all the words of the scroll that Jehoiakim king of Judah had burned in the fire. And many similar words were added to them.

column.name: text
column.value: Zedekiah son of Josiah was made king of Judah by Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon; he reigned in place of Jehoiachin son of Jehoiakim.

column.name: text
column.value: Neither he nor his attendants nor the people of the land paid any attention to the words the LORD had spoken through Jeremiah the prophet.

column.name: text
column.value: King Zedekiah, however, sent Jehucal son of Shelemiah with the priest Zephaniah son of Maaseiah to Jeremiah the prophet with this message: "Please pray to the LORD our God for us."

column.name: text
column.value: Now Jeremiah was free to come and go among the people, for he had not yet been put in prison.

column.name: text
column.value: Pharaoh's army had marched out of Egypt, and when the Babylonians who were besieging Jerusalem heard the report about them, they withdrew from Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah the prophet:

column.name: text
column.value: "This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: Tell the king of Judah, who sent you to inquire of me, 'Pharaoh's army, which has marched out to support you, will go back to its own land, to Egypt.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the Babylonians will return and attack this city; they will capture it and burn it down.'

column.name: text
column.value: "This is what the LORD says: Do not deceive yourselves, thinking, 'The Babylonians will surely leave us.' They will not!

column.name: text
column.value: Even if you were to defeat the entire Babylonian army that is attacking you and only wounded men were left in their tents, they would come out and burn this city down."

column.name: text
column.value: After the Babylonian army had withdrawn from Jerusalem because of Pharaoh's army,

column.name: text
column.value: Jeremiah started to leave the city to go to the territory of Benjamin to get his share of the property among the people there.

column.name: text
column.value: But when he reached the Benjamin Gate, the captain of the guard, whose name was Irijah son of Shelemiah, the son of Hananiah, arrested him and said, "You are deserting to the Babylonians!"

column.name: text
column.value: "That's not true!" Jeremiah said. "I am not deserting to the Babylonians." But Irijah would not listen to him; instead, he arrested Jeremiah and brought him to the officials.

column.name: text
column.value: They were angry with Jeremiah and had him beaten and imprisoned in the house of Jonathan the secretary, which they had made into a prison.

column.name: text
column.value: Jeremiah was put into a vaulted cell in a dungeon, where he remained a long time.

column.name: text
column.value: Then King Zedekiah sent for him and had him brought to the palace, where he asked him privately, "Is there any word from the LORD?" "Yes," Jeremiah replied, "you will be handed over to the king of Babylon."

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jeremiah said to King Zedekiah, "What crime have I committed against you or your officials or this people, that you have put me in prison?

column.name: text
column.value: Where are your prophets who prophesied to you, 'The king of Babylon will not attack you or this land'?

column.name: text
column.value: But now, my lord the king, please listen. Let me bring my petition before you: Do not send me back to the house of Jonathan the secretary, or I will die there."

column.name: text
column.value: King Zedekiah then gave orders for Jeremiah to be placed in the courtyard of the guard and given bread from the street of the bakers each day until all the bread in the city was gone. So Jeremiah remained in the courtyard of the guard.

column.name: text
column.value: This is how Jerusalem was taken: In the ninth year of Zedekiah king of Judah, in the tenth month, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon marched against Jerusalem with his whole army and laid siege to it.

column.name: text
column.value: And on the ninth day of the fourth month of Zedekiah's eleventh year, the city wall was broken through.

column.name: text
column.value: Then all the officials of the king of Babylon came and took seats in the Middle Gate: Nergal-Sharezer of Samgar, Nebo-Sarsekim a chief officer, Nergal-Sharezer a high official and all the other officials of the king of Babylon.

column.name: text
column.value: When Zedekiah king of Judah and all the soldiers saw them, they fled; they left the city at night by way of the king's garden, through the gate between the two walls, and headed toward the Arabah.

column.name: text
column.value: But the Babylonian army pursued them and overtook Zedekiah in the plains of Jericho. They captured him and took him to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon at Riblah in the land of Hamath, where he pronounced sentence on him.

column.name: text
column.value: There at Riblah the king of Babylon slaughtered the sons of Zedekiah before his eyes and also killed all the nobles of Judah.

column.name: text
column.value: Then he put out Zedekiah's eyes and bound him with bronze shackles to take him to Babylon.

column.name: text
column.value: The Babylonians set fire to the royal palace and the houses of the people and broke down the walls of Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: Nebuzaradan commander of the imperial guard carried into exile to Babylon the people who remained in the city, along with those who had gone over to him, and the rest of the people.

column.name: text
column.value: But Nebuzaradan the commander of the guard left behind in the land of Judah some of the poor people, who owned nothing; and at that time he gave them vineyards and fields.

column.name: text
column.value: Now Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had given these orders about Jeremiah through Nebuzaradan commander of the imperial guard:

column.name: text
column.value: "Take him and look after him; don't harm him but do for him whatever he asks."

column.name: text
column.value: So Nebuzaradan the commander of the guard, Nebushazban a chief officer, Nergal-Sharezer a high official and all the other officers of the king of Babylon

column.name: text
column.value: sent and had Jeremiah taken out of the courtyard of the guard. They turned him over to Gedaliah son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan, to take him back to his home. So he remained among his own people.

column.name: text
column.value: While Jeremiah had been confined in the courtyard of the guard, the word of the LORD came to him:

column.name: text
column.value: "Go and tell Ebed-Melech the Cushite, 'This is what the LORD Almighty, the God of Israel, says: I am about to fulfill my words against this city through disaster, not prosperity. At that time they will be fulfilled before your eyes.

column.name: text
column.value: But I will rescue you on that day, declares the LORD; you will not be handed over to those you fear.

column.name: text
column.value: I will save you; you will not fall by the sword but will escape with your life, because you trust in me, declares the LORD.'"

column.name: text
column.value: Shephatiah son of Mattan, Gedaliah son of Pashhur, Jehucal son of Shelemiah, and Pashhur son of Malkijah heard what Jeremiah was telling all the people when he said,

column.name: text
column.value: "This is what the LORD says: 'Whoever stays in this city will die by the sword, famine or plague, but whoever goes over to the Babylonians will live. He will escape with his life; he will live.'

column.name: text
column.value: And this is what the LORD says: 'This city will certainly be handed over to the army of the king of Babylon, who will capture it.'"

column.name: text
column.value: Then the officials said to the king, "This man should be put to death. He is discouraging the soldiers who are left in this city, as well as all the people, by the things he is saying to them. This man is not seeking the good of these people but their ruin."

column.name: text
column.value: "He is in your hands," King Zedekiah answered. "The king can do nothing to oppose you."

column.name: text
column.value: So they took Jeremiah and put him into the cistern of Malkijah, the king's son, which was in the courtyard of the guard. They lowered Jeremiah by ropes into the cistern; it had no water in it, only mud, and Jeremiah sank down into the mud.

column.name: text
column.value: But Ebed-Melech, a Cushite, an official in the royal palace, heard that they had put Jeremiah into the cistern. While the king was sitting in the Benjamin Gate,

column.name: text
column.value: Ebed-Melech went out of the palace and said to him,

column.name: text
column.value: "My lord the king, these men have acted wickedly in all they have done to Jeremiah the prophet. They have thrown him into a cistern, where he will starve to death when there is no longer any bread in the city."

column.name: text
column.value: Then the king commanded Ebed-Melech the Cushite, "Take thirty men from here with you and lift Jeremiah the prophet out of the cistern before he dies."

column.name: text
column.value: So Ebed-Melech took the men with him and went to a room under the treasury in the palace. He took some old rags and worn-out clothes from there and let them down with ropes to Jeremiah in the cistern.

column.name: text
column.value: Ebed-Melech the Cushite said to Jeremiah, "Put these old rags and worn-out clothes under your arms to pad the ropes." Jeremiah did so,

column.name: text
column.value: and they pulled him up with the ropes and lifted him out of the cistern. And Jeremiah remained in the courtyard of the guard.

column.name: text
column.value: Then King Zedekiah sent for Jeremiah the prophet and had him brought to the third entrance to the temple of the LORD. "I am going to ask you something," the king said to Jeremiah. "Do not hide anything from me."

column.name: text
column.value: Jeremiah said to Zedekiah, "If I give you an answer, will you not kill me? Even if I did give you counsel, you would not listen to me."
