column.name: text
column.value: But King Zedekiah swore this oath secretly to Jeremiah: "As surely as the LORD lives, who has given us breath, I will neither kill you nor hand you over to those who are seeking your life."

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jeremiah said to Zedekiah, "This is what the LORD God Almighty, the God of Israel, says: 'If you surrender to the officers of the king of Babylon, your life will be spared and this city will not be burned down; you and your family will live.

column.name: text
column.value: But if you will not surrender to the officers of the king of Babylon, this city will be handed over to the Babylonians and they will burn it down; you yourself will not escape from their hands.'"

column.name: text
column.value: King Zedekiah said to Jeremiah, "I am afraid of the Jews who have gone over to the Babylonians, for the Babylonians may hand me over to them and they will mistreat me."

column.name: text
column.value: "They will not hand you over," Jeremiah replied. "Obey the LORD by doing what I tell you. Then it will go well with you, and your life will be spared.

column.name: text
column.value: But if you refuse to surrender, this is what the LORD has revealed to me:

column.name: text
column.value: All the women left in the palace of the king of Judah will be brought out to the officials of the king of Babylon. Those women will say to you: "'They misled you and overcame you--those trusted friends of yours. Your feet are sunk in the mud; your friends have deserted you.'

column.name: text
column.value: "All your wives and children will be brought out to the Babylonians. You yourself will not escape from their hands but will be captured by the king of Babylon; and this city will be burned down."

column.name: text
column.value: Then Zedekiah said to Jeremiah, "Do not let anyone know about this conversation, or you may die.

column.name: text
column.value: If the officials hear that I talked with you, and they come to you and say, 'Tell us what you said to the king and what the king said to you; do not hide it from us or we will kill you,'

column.name: text
column.value: then tell them, 'I was pleading with the king not to send me back to Jonathan's house to die there.'"

column.name: text
column.value: All the officials did come to Jeremiah and question him, and he told them everything the king had ordered him to say. So they said no more to him, for no one had heard his conversation with the king.

column.name: text
column.value: And Jeremiah remained in the courtyard of the guard until the day Jerusalem was captured.

column.name: text
column.value: The word came to Jeremiah from the LORD after Nebuzaradan commander of the imperial guard had released him at Ramah. He had found Jeremiah bound in chains among all the captives from Jerusalem and Judah who were being carried into exile to Babylon.

column.name: text
column.value: When the commander of the guard found Jeremiah, he said to him, "The LORD your God decreed this disaster for this place.

column.name: text
column.value: And now the LORD has brought it about; he has done just as he said he would. All this happened because you people sinned against the LORD and did not obey him.

column.name: text
column.value: But today I am freeing you from the chains on your wrists. Come with me to Babylon, if you like, and I will look after you; but if you do not want to, then don't come. Look, the whole country lies before you; go wherever you please."

column.name: text
column.value: However, before Jeremiah turned to go, Nebuzaradan added, "Go back to Gedaliah son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan, whom the king of Babylon has appointed over the towns of Judah, and live with him among the people, or go anywhere else you please." Then the commander gave him provisions and a present and let him go.

column.name: text
column.value: So Jeremiah went to Gedaliah son of Ahikam at Mizpah and stayed with him among the people who were left behind in the land.

column.name: text
column.value: When all the army officers and their men who were still in the open country heard that the king of Babylon had appointed Gedaliah son of Ahikam as governor over the land and had put him in charge of the men, women and children who were the poorest in the land and who had not been carried into exile to Babylon,

column.name: text
column.value: they came to Gedaliah at Mizpah--Ishmael son of Nethaniah, Johanan and Jonathan the sons of Kareah, Seraiah son of Tanhumeth, the sons of Ephai the Netophathite, and Jaazaniah the son of the Maacathite, and their men.

column.name: text
column.value: Gedaliah son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan, took an oath to reassure them and their men. "Do not be afraid to serve the Babylonians," he said. "Settle down in the land and serve the king of Babylon, and it will go well with you.

column.name: text
column.value: I myself will stay at Mizpah to represent you before the Babylonians who come to us, but you are to harvest the wine, summer fruit and oil, and put them in your storage jars, and live in the towns you have taken over."

column.name: text
column.value: When all the Jews in Moab, Ammon, Edom and all the other countries heard that the king of Babylon had left a remnant in Judah and had appointed Gedaliah son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan, as governor over them,

column.name: text
column.value: they all came back to the land of Judah, to Gedaliah at Mizpah, from all the countries where they had been scattered. And they harvested an abundance of wine and summer fruit.

column.name: text
column.value: Johanan son of Kareah and all the army officers still in the open country came to Gedaliah at Mizpah

column.name: text
column.value: and said to him, "Don't you know that Baalis king of the Ammonites has sent Ishmael son of Nethaniah to take your life?" But Gedaliah son of Ahikam did not believe them.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Johanan son of Kareah said privately to Gedaliah in Mizpah, "Let me go and kill Ishmael son of Nethaniah, and no one will know it. Why should he take your life and cause all the Jews who are gathered around you to be scattered and the remnant of Judah to perish?"

column.name: text
column.value: But Gedaliah son of Ahikam said to Johanan son of Kareah, "Don't do such a thing! What you are saying about Ishmael is not true."

column.name: text
column.value: In the seventh month Ishmael son of Nethaniah, the son of Elishama, who was of royal blood and had been one of the king's officers, came with ten men to Gedaliah son of Ahikam at Mizpah. While they were eating together there,

column.name: text
column.value: Ishmael son of Nethaniah and the ten men who were with him got up and struck down Gedaliah son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan, with the sword, killing the one whom the king of Babylon had appointed as governor over the land.

column.name: text
column.value: Ishmael also killed all the Jews who were with Gedaliah at Mizpah, as well as the Babylonian soldiers who were there.

column.name: text
column.value: The day after Gedaliah's assassination, before anyone knew about it,

column.name: text
column.value: eighty men who had shaved off their beards, torn their clothes and cut themselves came from Shechem, Shiloh and Samaria, bringing grain offerings and incense with them to the house of the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: Ishmael son of Nethaniah went out from Mizpah to meet them, weeping as he went. When he met them, he said, "Come to Gedaliah son of Ahikam."

column.name: text
column.value: When they went into the city, Ishmael son of Nethaniah and the men who were with him slaughtered them and threw them into a cistern.

column.name: text
column.value: But ten of them said to Ishmael, "Don't kill us! We have wheat and barley, oil and honey, hidden in a field." So he let them alone and did not kill them with the others.

column.name: text
column.value: Now the cistern where he threw all the bodies of the men he had killed along with Gedaliah was the one King Asa had made as part of his defense against Baasha king of Israel. Ishmael son of Nethaniah filled it with the dead.

column.name: text
column.value: Ishmael made captives of all the rest of the people who were in Mizpah--the king's daughters along with all the others who were left there, over whom Nebuzaradan commander of the imperial guard had appointed Gedaliah son of Ahikam. Ishmael son of Nethaniah took them captive and set out to cross over to the Ammonites.

column.name: text
column.value: When Johanan son of Kareah and all the army officers who were with him heard about all the crimes Ishmael son of Nethaniah had committed,

column.name: text
column.value: they took all their men and went to fight Ishmael son of Nethaniah. They caught up with him near the great pool in Gibeon.

column.name: text
column.value: When all the people Ishmael had with him saw Johanan son of Kareah and the army officers who were with him, they were glad.

column.name: text
column.value: All the people Ishmael had taken captive at Mizpah turned and went over to Johanan son of Kareah.

column.name: text
column.value: But Ishmael son of Nethaniah and eight of his men escaped from Johanan and fled to the Ammonites.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Johanan son of Kareah and all the army officers who were with him led away all the survivors from Mizpah whom he had recovered from Ishmael son of Nethaniah after he had assassinated Gedaliah son of Ahikam: the soldiers, women, children and court officials he had brought from Gibeon.

column.name: text
column.value: And they went on, stopping at Geruth Kimham near Bethlehem on their way to Egypt

column.name: text
column.value: to escape the Babylonians. They were afraid of them because Ishmael son of Nethaniah had killed Gedaliah son of Ahikam, whom the king of Babylon had appointed as governor over the land.

column.name: text
column.value: Then all the army officers, including Johanan son of Kareah and Jezaniah son of Hoshaiah, and all the people from the least to the greatest approached

column.name: text
column.value: Jeremiah the prophet and said to him, "Please hear our petition and pray to the LORD your God for this entire remnant. For as you now see, though we were once many, now only a few are left.

column.name: text
column.value: Pray that the LORD your God will tell us where we should go and what we should do."

column.name: text
column.value: "I have heard you," replied Jeremiah the prophet. "I will certainly pray to the LORD your God as you have requested; I will tell you everything the LORD says and will keep nothing back from you."

column.name: text
column.value: Then they said to Jeremiah, "May the LORD be a true and faithful witness against us if we do not act in accordance with everything the LORD your God sends you to tell us.

column.name: text
column.value: Whether it is favorable or unfavorable, we will obey the LORD our God, to whom we are sending you, so that it will go well with us, for we will obey the LORD our God."

column.name: text
column.value: Ten days later the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah.

column.name: text
column.value: So he called together Johanan son of Kareah and all the army officers who were with him and all the people from the least to the greatest.

column.name: text
column.value: He said to them, "This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, to whom you sent me to present your petition, says:

column.name: text
column.value: 'If you stay in this land, I will build you up and not tear you down; I will plant you and not uproot you, for I am grieved over the disaster I have inflicted on you.

column.name: text
column.value: Do not be afraid of the king of Babylon, whom you now fear. Do not be afraid of him, declares the LORD, for I am with you and will save you and deliver you from his hands.

column.name: text
column.value: I will show you compassion so that he will have compassion on you and restore you to your land.'

column.name: text
column.value: "However, if you say, 'We will not stay in this land,' and so disobey the LORD your God,

column.name: text
column.value: and if you say, 'No, we will go and live in Egypt, where we will not see war or hear the trumpet or be hungry for bread,'

column.name: text
column.value: then hear the word of the LORD, O remnant of Judah. This is what the LORD Almighty, the God of Israel, says: 'If you are determined to go to Egypt and you do go to settle there,

column.name: text
column.value: then the sword you fear will overtake you there, and the famine you dread will follow you into Egypt, and there you will die.

column.name: text
column.value: Indeed, all who are determined to go to Egypt to settle there will die by the sword, famine and plague; not one of them will survive or escape the disaster I will bring on them.'

column.name: text
column.value: This is what the LORD Almighty, the God of Israel, says: 'As my anger and wrath have been poured out on those who lived in Jerusalem, so will my wrath be poured out on you when you go to Egypt. You will be an object of cursing and horror, of condemnation and reproach; you will never see this place again.'

column.name: text
column.value: "O remnant of Judah, the LORD has told you, 'Do not go to Egypt.' Be sure of this: I warn you today

column.name: text
column.value: that you made a fatal mistake when you sent me to the LORD your God and said, 'Pray to the LORD our God for us; tell us everything he says and we will do it.'

column.name: text
column.value: I have told you today, but you still have not obeyed the LORD your God in all he sent me to tell you.

column.name: text
column.value: So now, be sure of this: You will die by the sword, famine and plague in the place where you want to go to settle."

column.name: text
column.value: When Jeremiah finished telling the people all the words of the LORD their God--everything the LORD had sent him to tell them--

column.name: text
column.value: Azariah son of Hoshaiah and Johanan son of Kareah and all the arrogant men said to Jeremiah, "You are lying! The LORD our God has not sent you to say, 'You must not go to Egypt to settle there.'

column.name: text
column.value: But Baruch son of Neriah is inciting you against us to hand us over to the Babylonians, so they may kill us or carry us into exile to Babylon."

column.name: text
column.value: So Johanan son of Kareah and all the army officers and all the people disobeyed the LORD'S command to stay in the land of Judah.

column.name: text
column.value: Instead, Johanan son of Kareah and all the army officers led away all the remnant of Judah who had come back to live in the land of Judah from all the nations where they had been scattered.

column.name: text
column.value: They also led away all the men, women and children and the king's daughters whom Nebuzaradan commander of the imperial guard had left with Gedaliah son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan, and Jeremiah the prophet and Baruch son of Neriah.

column.name: text
column.value: So they entered Egypt in disobedience to the LORD and went as far as Tahpanhes.

column.name: text
column.value: In Tahpanhes the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah:

column.name: text
column.value: "While the Jews are watching, take some large stones with you and bury them in clay in the brick pavement at the entrance to Pharaoh's palace in Tahpanhes.

column.name: text
column.value: Then say to them, 'This is what the LORD Almighty, the God of Israel, says: I will send for my servant Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and I will set his throne over these stones I have buried here; he will spread his royal canopy above them.

column.name: text
column.value: He will come and attack Egypt, bringing death to those destined for death, captivity to those destined for captivity, and the sword to those destined for the sword.

column.name: text
column.value: He will set fire to the temples of the gods of Egypt; he will burn their temples and take their gods captive. As a shepherd wraps his garment around him, so will he wrap Egypt around himself and depart from there unscathed.

column.name: text
column.value: There in the temple of the sun in Egypt he will demolish the sacred pillars and will burn down the temples of the gods of Egypt.'"

column.name: text
column.value: This is the word of the LORD that came to Jeremiah the prophet concerning the Philistines before Pharaoh attacked Gaza:

column.name: text
column.value: This is what the LORD says: "See how the waters are rising in the north; they will become an overflowing torrent. They will overflow the land and everything in it, the towns and those who live in them. The people will cry out; all who dwell in the land will wail

column.name: text
column.value: at the sound of the hoofs of galloping steeds, at the noise of enemy chariots and the rumble of their wheels. Fathers will not turn to help their children; their hands will hang limp.

column.name: text
column.value: For the day has come to destroy all the Philistines and to cut off all survivors who could help Tyre and Sidon. The LORD is about to destroy the Philistines, the remnant from the coasts of Caphtor.

column.name: text
column.value: Gaza will shave her head in mourning; Ashkelon will be silenced. O remnant on the plain, how long will you cut yourselves?

column.name: text
column.value: "'Ah, sword of the LORD,' you cry,'how long till you rest? Return to your scabbard; cease and be still.'

column.name: text
column.value: But how can it rest when the LORD has commanded it, when he has ordered it to attack Ashkelon and the coast?"

column.name: text
column.value: This is the word of the LORD that came to Jeremiah the prophet concerning the nations:

column.name: text
column.value: Concerning Egypt: This is the message against the army of Pharaoh Neco king of Egypt, which was defeated at Carchemish on the Euphrates River by Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon in the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah king of Judah:

column.name: text
column.value: "Prepare your shields, both large and small, and march out for battle!

column.name: text
column.value: Harness the horses, mount the steeds! Take your positions with helmets on! Polish your spears, put on your armor!

column.name: text
column.value: What do I see? They are terrified, they are retreating, their warriors are defeated. They flee in haste without looking back, and there is terror on every side," declares the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: "The swift cannot flee nor the strong escape. In the north by the River Euphrates they stumble and fall.

column.name: text
column.value: "Who is this that rises like the Nile, like rivers of surging waters?

column.name: text
column.value: Egypt rises like the Nile, like rivers of surging waters. She says, 'I will rise and cover the earth; I will destroy cities and their people.'

column.name: text
column.value: Charge, O horses! Drive furiously, O charioteers! March on, O warriors--men of Cush and Put who carry shields, men of Lydia who draw the bow.

column.name: text
column.value: But that day belongs to the Lord, the LORD Almighty--a day of vengeance, for vengeance on his foes. The sword will devour till it is satisfied, till it has quenched its thirst with blood. For the Lord, the LORD Almighty, will offer sacrifice in the land of the north by the River Euphrates.

column.name: text
column.value: "Go up to Gilead and get balm, O Virgin Daughter of Egypt. But you multiply remedies in vain; there is no healing for you.

column.name: text
column.value: The nations will hear of your shame; your cries will fill the earth. One warrior will stumble over another; both will fall down together."

column.name: text
column.value: This is the message the LORD spoke to Jeremiah the prophet about the coming of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon to attack Egypt:

column.name: text
column.value: "Announce this in Egypt, and proclaim it in Migdol; proclaim it also in Memphis and Tahpanhes: 'Take your positions and get ready, for the sword devours those around you.'

column.name: text
column.value: Why will your warriors be laid low? They cannot stand, for the LORD will push them down.

column.name: text
column.value: They will stumble repeatedly; they will fall over each other. They will say, 'Get up, let us go back to our own people and our native lands, away from the sword of the oppressor.'

column.name: text
column.value: There they will exclaim, 'Pharaoh king of Egypt is only a loud noise; he has missed his opportunity.'

column.name: text
column.value: "As surely as I live," declares the King, whose name is the LORD Almighty, "one will come who is like Tabor among the mountains, like Carmel by the sea.

column.name: text
column.value: Pack your belongings for exile, you who live in Egypt, for Memphis will be laid waste and lie in ruins without inhabitant.

column.name: text
column.value: "Egypt is a beautiful heifer, but a gadfly is coming against her from the north.

column.name: text
column.value: The mercenaries in her ranks are like fattened calves. They too will turn and flee together, they will not stand their ground, for the day of disaster is coming upon them, the time for them to be punished.

column.name: text
column.value: Egypt will hiss like a fleeing serpent as the enemy advances in force; they will come against her with axes, like men who cut down trees.

column.name: text
column.value: They will chop down her forest," declares the LORD, "dense though it be. They are more numerous than locusts, they cannot be counted.

column.name: text
column.value: The Daughter of Egypt will be put to shame, handed over to the people of the north."

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD Almighty, the God of Israel, says: "I am about to bring punishment on Amon god of Thebes, on Pharaoh, on Egypt and her gods and her kings, and on those who rely on Pharaoh.

column.name: text
column.value: I will hand them over to those who seek their lives, to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and his officers. Later, however, Egypt will be inhabited as in times past," declares the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: "Do not fear, O Jacob my servant; do not be dismayed, O Israel. I will surely save you out of a distant place, your descendants from the land of their exile. Jacob will again have peace and security, and no one will make him afraid.

column.name: text
column.value: Do not fear, O Jacob my servant, for I am with you," declares the LORD. "Though I completely destroy all the nations among which I scatter you, I will not completely destroy you. I will discipline you but only with justice; I will not let you go entirely unpunished."

column.name: text
column.value: This is what Jeremiah the prophet told Baruch son of Neriah in the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah king of Judah, after Baruch had written on a scroll the words Jeremiah was then dictating:

column.name: text
column.value: "This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says to you, Baruch:

column.name: text
column.value: You said, 'Woe to me! The LORD has added sorrow to my pain; I am worn out with groaning and find no rest.'"

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD said,"Say this to him: 'This is what the LORD says: I will overthrow what I have built and uproot what I have planted, throughout the land.

column.name: text
column.value: Should you then seek great things for yourself? Seek them not. For I will bring disaster on all people, declares the LORD, but wherever you go I will let you escape with your life.'"

column.name: text
column.value: Concerning Moab: This is what the LORD Almighty, the God of Israel, says: "Woe to Nebo, for it will be ruined. Kiriathaim will be disgraced and captured; the stronghold will be disgraced and shattered.

column.name: text
column.value: Moab will be praised no more; in Heshbon men will plot her downfall: 'Come, let us put an end to that nation.' You too, O Madmen, will be silenced; the sword will pursue you.

column.name: text
column.value: Listen to the cries from Horonaim, cries of great havoc and destruction.

column.name: text
column.value: Moab will be broken; her little ones will cry out.

column.name: text
column.value: They go up the way to Luhith, weeping bitterly as they go; on the road down to Horonaim anguished cries over the destruction are heard.

column.name: text
column.value: Flee! Run for your lives; become like a bush in the desert.

column.name: text
column.value: Since you trust in your deeds and riches, you too will be taken captive, and Chemosh will go into exile, together with his priests and officials.

column.name: text
column.value: The destroyer will come against every town, and not a town will escape. The valley will be ruined and the plateau destroyed, because the LORD has spoken.

column.name: text
column.value: Put salt on Moab, for she will be laid waste; her towns will become desolate, with no one to live in them.

column.name: text
column.value: "A curse on him who is lax in doing the LORD'S work! A curse on him who keeps his sword from bloodshed!

column.name: text
column.value: "Moab has been at rest from youth, like wine left on its dregs, not poured from one jar to another--she has not gone into exile. So she tastes as she did, and her aroma is unchanged.

column.name: text
column.value: But days are coming," declares the LORD, "when I will send men who pour from jars, and they will pour her out; they will empty her jars and smash her jugs.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Moab will be ashamed of Chemosh, as the house of Israel was ashamed when they trusted in Bethel.

column.name: text
column.value: "How can you say, 'We are warriors, men valiant in battle'?

column.name: text
column.value: Moab will be destroyed and her towns invaded; her finest young men will go down in the slaughter," declares the King, whose name is the LORD Almighty.

column.name: text
column.value: "The fall of Moab is at hand; her calamity will come quickly.

column.name: text
column.value: Mourn for her, all who live around her, all who know her fame; say, 'How broken is the mighty scepter, how broken the glorious staff!'

column.name: text
column.value: "Come down from your glory and sit on the parched ground, O inhabitants of the Daughter of Dibon, for he who destroys Moab will come up against you and ruin your fortified cities.

column.name: text
column.value: Stand by the road and watch, you who live in Aroer. Ask the man fleeing and the woman escaping, ask them, 'What has happened?'

column.name: text
column.value: Moab is disgraced, for she is shattered. Wail and cry out! Announce by the Arnon that Moab is destroyed.

column.name: text
column.value: Judgment has come to the plateau--to Holon, Jahzah and Mephaath,

column.name: text
column.value: to Dibon, Nebo and Beth Diblathaim,

column.name: text
column.value: to Kiriathaim, Beth Gamul and Beth Meon,

column.name: text
column.value: to Kerioth and Bozrah--to all the towns of Moab, far and near.

column.name: text
column.value: Moab's horn is cut off; her arm is broken," declares the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: "Make her drunk, for she has defied the LORD. Let Moab wallow in her vomit; let her be an object of ridicule.

column.name: text
column.value: Was not Israel the object of your ridicule? Was she caught among thieves, that you shake your head in scorn whenever you speak of her?

column.name: text
column.value: Abandon your towns and dwell among the rocks, you who live in Moab. Be like a dove that makes its nest at the mouth of a cave.

column.name: text
column.value: "We have heard of Moab's pride--her overweening pride and conceit, her pride and arrogance and the haughtiness of her heart.

column.name: text
column.value: I know her insolence but it is futile," declares the LORD, "and her boasts accomplish nothing.

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore I wail over Moab, for all Moab I cry out, I moan for the men of Kir Hareseth.

column.name: text
column.value: I weep for you, as Jazer weeps, O vines of Sibmah. Your branches spread as far as the sea; they reached as far as the sea of Jazer. The destroyer has fallen on your ripened fruit and grapes.

column.name: text
column.value: Joy and gladness are gone from the orchards and fields of Moab. I have stopped the flow of wine from the presses; no one treads them with shouts of joy. Although there are shouts, they are not shouts of joy.

column.name: text
column.value: "The sound of their cry rises from Heshbon to Elealeh and Jahaz, from Zoar as far as Horonaim and Eglath Shelishiyah, for even the waters of Nimrim are dried up.

column.name: text
column.value: In Moab I will put an end to those who make offerings on the high places and burn incense to their gods," declares the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: "So my heart laments for Moab like a flute; it laments like a flute for the men of Kir Hareseth. The wealth they acquired is gone.

column.name: text
column.value: Every head is shaved and every beard cut off; every hand is slashed and every waist is covered with sackcloth.

column.name: text
column.value: On all the roofs in Moab and in the public squares there is nothing but mourning, for I have broken Moab like a jar that no one wants," declares the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: "How shattered she is! How they wail! How Moab turns her back in shame! Moab has become an object of ridicule, an object of horror to all those around her."

column.name: text
column.value: This is what the LORD says: "Look! An eagle is swooping down, spreading its wings over Moab.

column.name: text
column.value: Kerioth will be captured and the strongholds taken. In that day the hearts of Moab's warriors will be like the heart of a woman in labor.

column.name: text
column.value: Moab will be destroyed as a nation because she defied the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: Terror and pit and snare await you, O people of Moab," declares the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: "Whoever flees from the terror will fall into a pit, whoever climbs out of the pit will be caught in a snare; for I will bring upon Moab the year of her punishment," declares the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: "In the shadow of Heshbon the fugitives stand helpless, for a fire has gone out from Heshbon, a blaze from the midst of Sihon; it burns the foreheads of Moab, the skulls of the noisy boasters.

column.name: text
column.value: Woe to you, O Moab! The people of Chemosh are destroyed; your sons are taken into exile and your daughters into captivity.

column.name: text
column.value: "Yet I will restore the fortunes of Moab in days to come," declares the LORD. Here ends the judgment on Moab.

column.name: text
column.value: Concerning the Ammonites: This is what the LORD says: "Has Israel no sons? Has she no heirs? Why then has Molech taken possession of Gad? Why do his people live in its towns?

column.name: text
column.value: But the days are coming," declares the LORD, "when I will sound the battle cry against Rabbah of the Ammonites; it will become a mound of ruins, and its surrounding villages will be set on fire. Then Israel will drive out those who drove her out," says the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: "Wail, O Heshbon, for Ai is destroyed! Cry out, O inhabitants of Rabbah! Put on sackcloth and mourn; rush here and there inside the walls, for Molech will go into exile, together with his priests and officials.

column.name: text
column.value: Why do you boast of your valleys, boast of your valleys so fruitful? O unfaithful daughter, you trust in your riches and say, 'Who will attack me?'

column.name: text
column.value: I will bring terror on you from all those around you," declares the Lord, the LORD Almighty. "Every one of you will be driven away, and no one will gather the fugitives.

column.name: text
column.value: "Yet afterward, I will restore the fortunes of the Ammonites," declares the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: Concerning Edom: This is what the LORD Almighty says: "Is there no longer wisdom in Teman? Has counsel perished from the prudent? Has their wisdom decayed?

column.name: text
column.value: Turn and flee, hide in deep caves, you who live in Dedan, for I will bring disaster on Esau at the time I punish him.

column.name: text
column.value: If grape pickers came to you, would they not leave a few grapes? If thieves came during the night, would they not steal only as much as they wanted?

column.name: text
column.value: But I will strip Esau bare; I will uncover his hiding places, so that he cannot conceal himself. His children, relatives and neighbors will perish, and he will be no more.

column.name: text
column.value: Leave your orphans; I will protect their lives. Your widows too can trust in me."

column.name: text
column.value: This is what the LORD says: "If those who do not deserve to drink the cup must drink it, why should you go unpunished? You will not go unpunished, but must drink it.

column.name: text
column.value: I swear by myself," declares the LORD, "that Bozrah will become a ruin and an object of horror, of reproach and of cursing; and all its towns will be in ruins forever."

column.name: text
column.value: I have heard a message from the LORD: An envoy was sent to the nations to say, "Assemble yourselves to attack it! Rise up for battle!"

column.name: text
column.value: "Now I will make you small among the nations, despised among men.

column.name: text
column.value: The terror you inspire and the pride of your heart have deceived you, you who live in the clefts of the rocks, who occupy the heights of the hill. Though you build your nest as high as the eagle's, from there I will bring you down," declares the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: "Edom will become an object of horror; all who pass by will be appalled and will scoff because of all its wounds.

column.name: text
column.value: As Sodom and Gomorrah were overthrown, along with their neighboring towns," says the LORD, "so no one will live there; no man will dwell in it.

column.name: text
column.value: "Like a lion coming up from Jordan's thickets to a rich pastureland, I will chase Edom from its land in an instant. Who is the chosen one I will appoint for this? Who is like me and who can challenge me? And what shepherd can stand against me?"

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore, hear what the LORD has planned against Edom, what he has purposed against those who live in Teman: The young of the flock will be dragged away; he will completely destroy their pasture because of them.

column.name: text
column.value: At the sound of their fall the earth will tremble; their cry will resound to the Red Sea.

column.name: text
column.value: Look! An eagle will soar and swoop down, spreading its wings over Bozrah. In that day the hearts of Edom's warriors will be like the heart of a woman in labor.

column.name: text
column.value: Concerning Damascus: "Hamath and Arpad are dismayed, for they have heard bad news. They are disheartened, troubled like the restless sea.

column.name: text
column.value: Damascus has become feeble, she has turned to flee and panic has gripped her; anguish and pain have seized her, pain like that of a woman in labor.

column.name: text
column.value: Why has the city of renown not been abandoned, the town in which I delight?

column.name: text
column.value: Surely, her young men will fall in the streets; all her soldiers will be silenced in that day," declares the LORD Almighty.

column.name: text
column.value: "I will set fire to the walls of Damascus; it will consume the fortresses of Ben-Hadad."

column.name: text
column.value: Concerning Kedar and the kingdoms of Hazor, which Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon attacked: This is what the LORD says: "Arise, and attack Kedar and destroy the people of the East.

column.name: text
column.value: Their tents and their flocks will be taken; their shelters will be carried off with all their goods and camels. Men will shout to them, 'Terror on every side!'

column.name: text
column.value: "Flee quickly away! Stay in deep caves, you who live in Hazor," declares the LORD. "Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon has plotted against you; he has devised a plan against you.

column.name: text
column.value: "Arise and attack a nation at ease, which lives in confidence," declares the LORD, "a nation that has neither gates nor bars; its people live alone.

column.name: text
column.value: Their camels will become plunder, and their large herds will be booty. I will scatter to the winds those who are in distant places and will bring disaster on them from every side," declares the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: "Hazor will become a haunt of jackals, a desolate place forever. No one will live there; no man will dwell in it."

column.name: text
column.value: This is the word of the LORD that came to Jeremiah the prophet concerning Elam, early in the reign of Zedekiah king of Judah:

column.name: text
column.value: This is what the LORD Almighty says: "See, I will break the bow of Elam, the mainstay of their might.

column.name: text
column.value: I will bring against Elam the four winds from the four quarters of the heavens; I will scatter them to the four winds, and there will not be a nation where Elam's exiles do not go.

column.name: text
column.value: I will shatter Elam before their foes, before those who seek their lives; I will bring disaster upon them, even my fierce anger," declares the LORD. "I will pursue them with the sword until I have made an end of them.

column.name: text
column.value: I will set my throne in Elam and destroy her king and officials," declares the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: "Yet I will restore the fortunes of Elam in days to come," declares the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: This is what the LORD says: "See, I will stir up the spirit of a destroyer against Babylon and the people of Leb Kamai.

column.name: text
column.value: I will send foreigners to Babylon to winnow her and to devastate her land; they will oppose her on every side in the day of her disaster.

column.name: text
column.value: Let not the archer string his bow, nor let him put on his armor. Do not spare her young men; completely destroy her army.

column.name: text
column.value: They will fall down slain in Babylon, fatally wounded in her streets.

column.name: text
column.value: For Israel and Judah have not been forsaken by their God, the LORD Almighty, though their land is full of guilt before the Holy One of Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: "Flee from Babylon! Run for your lives! Do not be destroyed because of her sins. It is time for the LORD'S vengeance; he will pay her what she deserves.

column.name: text
column.value: Babylon was a gold cup in the LORD'S hand; she made the whole earth drunk. The nations drank her wine; therefore they have now gone mad.

column.name: text
column.value: Babylon will suddenly fall and be broken. Wail over her! Get balm for her pain; perhaps she can be healed.

column.name: text
column.value: "'We would have healed Babylon, but she cannot be healed; let us leave her and each go to his own land, for her judgment reaches to the skies, it rises as high as the clouds.'

column.name: text
column.value: "'The LORD has vindicated us; come, let us tell in Zion what the LORD our God has done.'

column.name: text
column.value: "Sharpen the arrows, take up the shields! The LORD has stirred up the kings of the Medes, because his purpose is to destroy Babylon. The LORD will take vengeance, vengeance for his temple.

column.name: text
column.value: Lift up a banner against the walls of Babylon! Reinforce the guard, station the watchmen, prepare an ambush! The LORD will carry out his purpose, his decree against the people of Babylon.

column.name: text
column.value: You who live by many waters and are rich in treasures, your end has come, the time for you to be cut off.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD Almighty has sworn by himself: I will surely fill you with men, as with a swarm of locusts, and they will shout in triumph over you.

column.name: text
column.value: "He made the earth by his power; he founded the world by his wisdom and stretched out the heavens by his understanding.

column.name: text
column.value: When he thunders, the waters in the heavens roar; he makes clouds rise from the ends of the earth. He sends lightning with the rain and brings out the wind from his storehouses.

column.name: text
column.value: "Every man is senseless and without knowledge; every goldsmith is shamed by his idols. His images are a fraud; they have no breath in them.

column.name: text
column.value: They are worthless, the objects of mockery; when their judgment comes, they will perish.

column.name: text
column.value: He who is the Portion of Jacob is not like these, for he is the Maker of all things, including the tribe of his inheritance--the LORD Almighty is his name.

column.name: text
column.value: "You are my war club, my weapon for battle--with you I shatter nations, with you I destroy kingdoms,

column.name: text
column.value: with you I shatter horse and rider, with you I shatter chariot and driver,

column.name: text
column.value: with you I shatter man and woman, with you I shatter old man and youth, with you I shatter young man and maiden,

column.name: text
column.value: with you I shatter shepherd and flock, with you I shatter farmer and oxen, with you I shatter governors and officials.

column.name: text
column.value: "Before your eyes I will repay Babylon and all who live in Babylonia for all the wrong they have done in Zion," declares the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: "I am against you, O destroying mountain, you who destroy the whole earth," declares the LORD. "I will stretch out my hand against you, roll you off the cliffs, and make you a burned-out mountain.

column.name: text
column.value: No rock will be taken from you for a cornerstone, nor any stone for a foundation, for you will be desolate forever," declares the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: "Lift up a banner in the land! Blow the trumpet among the nations! Prepare the nations for battle against her; summon against her these kingdoms: Ararat, Minni and Ashkenaz. Appoint a commander against her; send up horses like a swarm of locusts.

column.name: text
column.value: Prepare the nations for battle against her--the kings of the Medes, their governors and all their officials, and all the countries they rule.

column.name: text
column.value: The land trembles and writhes, for the LORD'S purposes against Babylon stand--to lay waste the land of Babylon so that no one will live there.

column.name: text
column.value: Babylon's warriors have stopped fighting; they remain in their strongholds. Their strength is exhausted; they have become like women. Her dwellings are set on fire; the bars of her gates are broken.

column.name: text
column.value: One courier follows another and messenger follows messenger to announce to the king of Babylon that his entire city is captured,

column.name: text
column.value: the river crossings seized, the marshes set on fire, and the soldiers terrified."

column.name: text
column.value: This is what the LORD Almighty, the God of Israel, says: "The Daughter of Babylon is like a threshing floor at the time it is trampled; the time to harvest her will soon come."

column.name: text
column.value: "Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon has devoured us, he has thrown us into confusion, he has made us an empty jar. Like a serpent he has swallowed us and filled his stomach with our delicacies, and then has spewed us out.

column.name: text
column.value: May the violence done to our flesh be upon Babylon," say the inhabitants of Zion. "May our blood be on those who live in Babylonia," says Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore, this is what the LORD says: "See, I will defend your cause and avenge you; I will dry up her sea and make her springs dry.

column.name: text
column.value: Babylon will be a heap of ruins, a haunt of jackals, an object of horror and scorn, a place where no one lives.

column.name: text
column.value: Her people all roar like young lions, they growl like lion cubs.

column.name: text
column.value: But while they are aroused, I will set out a feast for them and make them drunk, so that they shout with laughter--then sleep forever and not awake," declares the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: "I will bring them down like lambs to the slaughter, like rams and goats.

column.name: text
column.value: "How Sheshach will be captured, the boast of the whole earth seized! What a horror Babylon will be among the nations!

column.name: text
column.value: The sea will rise over Babylon; its roaring waves will cover her.

column.name: text
column.value: Her towns will be desolate, a dry and desert land, a land where no one lives, through which no man travels.

column.name: text
column.value: I will punish Bel in Babylon and make him spew out what he has swallowed. The nations will no longer stream to him. And the wall of Babylon will fall.

column.name: text
column.value: "Come out of her, my people! Run for your lives! Run from the fierce anger of the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: Do not lose heart or be afraid when rumors are heard in the land; one rumor comes this year, another the next, rumors of violence in the land and of ruler against ruler.

column.name: text
column.value: For the time will surely come when I will punish the idols of Babylon; her whole land will be disgraced and her slain will all lie fallen within her.

column.name: text
column.value: Then heaven and earth and all that is in them will shout for joy over Babylon, for out of the north destroyers will attack her," declares the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: "Babylon must fall because of Israel's slain, just as the slain in all the earth have fallen because of Babylon.

column.name: text
column.value: You who have escaped the sword, leave and do not linger! Remember the LORD in a distant land, and think on Jerusalem."

column.name: text
column.value: "We are disgraced, for we have been insulted and shame covers our faces, because foreigners have entered the holy places of the LORD'S house."

column.name: text
column.value: "But days are coming," declares the LORD, "when I will punish her idols, and throughout her land the wounded will groan.

column.name: text
column.value: Even if Babylon reaches the sky and fortifies her lofty stronghold, I will send destroyers against her," declares the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: "The sound of a cry comes from Babylon, the sound of great destruction from the land of the Babylonians.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD will destroy Babylon; he will silence her noisy din. Waves of enemies will rage like great waters; the roar of their voices will resound.

column.name: text
column.value: A destroyer will come against Babylon; her warriors will be captured, and their bows will be broken. For the LORD is a God of retribution; he will repay in full.

column.name: text
column.value: I will make her officials and wise men drunk, her governors, officers and warriors as well; they will sleep forever and not awake," declares the King, whose name is the LORD Almighty.

column.name: text
column.value: This is what the LORD Almighty says: "Babylon's thick wall will be leveled and her high gates set on fire; the peoples exhaust themselves for nothing, the nations' labor is only fuel for the flames."

column.name: text
column.value: This is the message Jeremiah gave to the staff officer Seraiah son of Neriah, the son of Mahseiah, when he went to Babylon with Zedekiah king of Judah in the fourth year of his reign.

column.name: text
column.value: Jeremiah had written on a scroll about all the disasters that would come upon Babylon--all that had been recorded concerning Babylon.

column.name: text
column.value: He said to Seraiah, "When you get to Babylon, see that you read all these words aloud.

column.name: text
column.value: Then say, 'O LORD, you have said you will destroy this place, so that neither man nor animal will live in it; it will be desolate forever.'

column.name: text
column.value: When you finish reading this scroll, tie a stone to it and throw it into the Euphrates.

column.name: text
column.value: Then say, 'So will Babylon sink to rise no more because of the disaster I will bring upon her. And her people will fall.'" The words of Jeremiah end here.

column.name: text
column.value: This is the word the LORD spoke through Jeremiah the prophet concerning Babylon and the land of the Babylonians:

column.name: text
column.value: "Announce and proclaim among the nations, lift up a banner and proclaim it; keep nothing back, but say, 'Babylon will be captured; Bel will be put to shame, Marduk filled with terror. Her images will be put to shame and her idols filled with terror.'

column.name: text
column.value: A nation from the north will attack her and lay waste her land. No one will live in it; both men and animals will flee away.

column.name: text
column.value: "In those days, at that time," declares the LORD, "the people of Israel and the people of Judah together will go in tears to seek the LORD their God.

column.name: text
column.value: They will ask the way to Zion and turn their faces toward it. They will come and bind themselves to the LORD in an everlasting covenant that will not be forgotten.

column.name: text
column.value: "My people have been lost sheep; their shepherds have led them astray and caused them to roam on the mountains. They wandered over mountain and hill and forgot their own resting place.

column.name: text
column.value: Whoever found them devoured them; their enemies said, 'We are not guilty, for they sinned against the LORD, their true pasture, the LORD, the hope of their fathers.'

column.name: text
column.value: "Flee out of Babylon; leave the land of the Babylonians, and be like the goats that lead the flock.

column.name: text
column.value: For I will stir up and bring against Babylon an alliance of great nations from the land of the north. They will take up their positions against her, and from the north she will be captured. Their arrows will be like skilled warriors who do not return empty-handed.

column.name: text
column.value: So Babylonia will be plundered; all who plunder her will have their fill," declares the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: "Because you rejoice and are glad, you who pillage my inheritance, because you frolic like a heifer threshing grain and neigh like stallions,

column.name: text
column.value: your mother will be greatly ashamed; she who gave you birth will be disgraced. She will be the least of the nations--a wilderness, a dry land, a desert.

column.name: text
column.value: Because of the LORD'S anger she will not be inhabited but will be completely desolate. All who pass Babylon will be horrified and scoff because of all her wounds.

column.name: text
column.value: "Take up your positions around Babylon, all you who draw the bow. Shoot at her! Spare no arrows, for she has sinned against the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: Shout against her on every side! She surrenders, her towers fall, her walls are torn down. Since this is the vengeance of the LORD, take vengeance on her; do to her as she has done to others.

column.name: text
column.value: Cut off from Babylon the sower, and the reaper with his sickle at harvest. Because of the sword of the oppressor let everyone return to his own people, let everyone flee to his own land.

column.name: text
column.value: "Israel is a scattered flock that lions have chased away. The first to devour him was the king of Assyria; the last to crush his bones was Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon."

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore this is what the LORD Almighty, the God of Israel, says: "I will punish the king of Babylon and his land as I punished the king of Assyria.

column.name: text
column.value: But I will bring Israel back to his own pasture and he will graze on Carmel and Bashan; his appetite will be satisfied on the hills of Ephraim and Gilead.

column.name: text
column.value: In those days, at that time," declares the LORD, "search will be made for Israel's guilt, but there will be none, and for the sins of Judah, but none will be found, for I will forgive the remnant I spare.

column.name: text
column.value: "Attack the land of Merathaim and those who live in Pekod. Pursue, kill and completely destroy them," declares the LORD. "Do everything I have commanded you.

column.name: text
column.value: The noise of battle is in the land, the noise of great destruction!

column.name: text
column.value: How broken and shattered is the hammer of the whole earth! How desolate is Babylon among the nations!

column.name: text
column.value: I set a trap for you, O Babylon, and you were caught before you knew it; you were found and captured because you opposed the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD has opened his arsenal and brought out the weapons of his wrath, for the Sovereign LORD Almighty has work to do in the land of the Babylonians.

column.name: text
column.value: Come against her from afar. Break open her granaries; pile her up like heaps of grain. Completely destroy her and leave her no remnant.

column.name: text
column.value: Kill all her young bulls; let them go down to the slaughter! Woe to them! For their day has come, the time for them to be punished.

column.name: text
column.value: Listen to the fugitives and refugees from Babylon declaring in Zion how the LORD our God has taken vengeance, vengeance for his temple.

column.name: text
column.value: "Summon archers against Babylon, all those who draw the bow. Encamp all around her; let no one escape. Repay her for her deeds; do to her as she has done. For she has defied the LORD, the Holy One of Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore, her young men will fall in the streets; all her soldiers will be silenced in that day," declares the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: "See, I am against you, O arrogant one," declares the Lord, the LORD Almighty, "for your day has come, the time for you to be punished.

column.name: text
column.value: The arrogant one will stumble and fall and no one will help her up; I will kindle a fire in her towns that will consume all who are around her."

column.name: text
column.value: This is what the LORD Almighty says: "The people of Israel are oppressed, and the people of Judah as well. All their captors hold them fast, refusing to let them go.

column.name: text
column.value: Yet their Redeemer is strong; the LORD Almighty is his name. He will vigorously defend their cause so that he may bring rest to their land, but unrest to those who live in Babylon.

column.name: text
column.value: "A sword against the Babylonians!" declares the LORD--"against those who live in Babylon and against her officials and wise men!

column.name: text
column.value: A sword against her false prophets! They will become fools. A sword against her warriors! They will be filled with terror.

column.name: text
column.value: A sword against her horses and chariots and all the foreigners in her ranks! They will become women. A sword against her treasures! They will be plundered.

column.name: text
column.value: A drought on her waters! They will dry up. For it is a land of idols, idols that will go mad with terror.

column.name: text
column.value: "So desert creatures and hyenas will live there, and there the owl will dwell. It will never again be inhabited or lived in from generation to generation.

column.name: text
column.value: As God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah along with their neighboring towns," declares the LORD, "so no one will live there; no man will dwell in it.

column.name: text
column.value: "Look! An army is coming from the north; a great nation and many kings are being stirred up from the ends of the earth.

column.name: text
column.value: They are armed with bows and spears; they are cruel and without mercy. They sound like the roaring sea as they ride on their horses; they come like men in battle formation to attack you, O Daughter of Babylon.

column.name: text
column.value: The king of Babylon has heard reports about them, and his hands hang limp. Anguish has gripped him, pain like that of a woman in labor.

column.name: text
column.value: Like a lion coming up from Jordan's thickets to a rich pastureland, I will chase Babylon from its land in an instant. Who is the chosen one I will appoint for this? Who is like me and who can challenge me? And what shepherd can stand against me?"

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore, hear what the LORD has planned against Babylon, what he has purposed against the land of the Babylonians: The young of the flock will be dragged away; he will completely destroy their pasture because of them.

column.name: text
column.value: At the sound of Babylon's capture the earth will tremble; its cry will resound among the nations.

column.name: text
column.value: Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem eleven years. His mother's name was Hamutal daughter of Jeremiah; she was from Libnah.

column.name: text
column.value: He did evil in the eyes of the LORD, just as Jehoiakim had done.

column.name: text
column.value: It was because of the LORD'S anger that all this happened to Jerusalem and Judah, and in the end he thrust them from his presence. Now Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon.

column.name: text
column.value: So in the ninth year of Zedekiah's reign, on the tenth day of the tenth month, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon marched against Jerusalem with his whole army. They camped outside the city and built siege works all around it.

column.name: text
column.value: The city was kept under siege until the eleventh year of King Zedekiah.

column.name: text
column.value: By the ninth day of the fourth month the famine in the city had become so severe that there was no food for the people to eat.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the city wall was broken through, and the whole army fled. They left the city at night through the gate between the two walls near the king's garden, though the Babylonians were surrounding the city. They fled toward the Arabah,

column.name: text
column.value: but the Babylonian army pursued King Zedekiah and overtook him in the plains of Jericho. All his soldiers were separated from him and scattered,

column.name: text
column.value: and he was captured. He was taken to the king of Babylon at Riblah in the land of Hamath, where he pronounced sentence on him.

column.name: text
column.value: There at Riblah the king of Babylon slaughtered the sons of Zedekiah before his eyes; he also killed all the officials of Judah.

column.name: text
column.value: Then he put out Zedekiah's eyes, bound him with bronze shackles and took him to Babylon, where he put him in prison till the day of his death.

column.name: text
column.value: On the tenth day of the fifth month, in the nineteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, Nebuzaradan commander of the imperial guard, who served the king of Babylon, came to Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: He set fire to the temple of the LORD, the royal palace and all the houses of Jerusalem. Every important building he burned down.

column.name: text
column.value: The whole Babylonian army under the commander of the imperial guard broke down all the walls around Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: Nebuzaradan the commander of the guard carried into exile some of the poorest people and those who remained in the city, along with the rest of the craftsmen and those who had gone over to the king of Babylon.

column.name: text
column.value: But Nebuzaradan left behind the rest of the poorest people of the land to work the vineyards and fields.

column.name: text
column.value: The Babylonians broke up the bronze pillars, the movable stands and the bronze Sea that were at the temple of the LORD and they carried all the bronze to Babylon.

column.name: text
column.value: They also took away the pots, shovels, wick trimmers, sprinkling bowls, dishes and all the bronze articles used in the temple service.

column.name: text
column.value: The commander of the imperial guard took away the basins, censers, sprinkling bowls, pots, lampstands, dishes and bowls used for drink offerings--all that were made of pure gold or silver.

column.name: text
column.value: The bronze from the two pillars, the Sea and the twelve bronze bulls under it, and the movable stands, which King Solomon had made for the temple of the LORD, was more than could be weighed.

column.name: text
column.value: Each of the pillars was eighteen cubits high and twelve cubits in circumference; each was four fingers thick, and hollow.

column.name: text
column.value: The bronze capital on top of the one pillar was five cubits high and was decorated with a network and pomegranates of bronze all around. The other pillar, with its pomegranates, was similar.

column.name: text
column.value: There were ninety-six pomegranates on the sides; the total number of pomegranates above the surrounding network was a hundred.

column.name: text
column.value: The commander of the guard took as prisoners Seraiah the chief priest, Zephaniah the priest next in rank and the three doorkeepers.

column.name: text
column.value: Of those still in the city, he took the officer in charge of the fighting men, and seven royal advisers. He also took the secretary who was chief officer in charge of conscripting the people of the land and sixty of his men who were found in the city.

column.name: text
column.value: Nebuzaradan the commander took them all and brought them to the king of Babylon at Riblah.

column.name: text
column.value: There at Riblah, in the land of Hamath, the king had them executed. So Judah went into captivity, away from her land.

column.name: text
column.value: This is the number of the people Nebuchadnezzar carried into exile: in the seventh year, 3,023 Jews;

column.name: text
column.value: in Nebuchadnezzar's eighteenth year, 832 people from Jerusalem;

column.name: text
column.value: in his twenty-third year, 745 Jews taken into exile by Nebuzaradan the commander of the imperial guard. There were 4,600 people in all.

column.name: text
column.value: In the thirty-seventh year of the exile of Jehoiachin king of Judah, in the year Evil-Merodach became king of Babylon, he released Jehoiachin king of Judah and freed him from prison on the twenty-fifth day of the twelfth month.

column.name: text
column.value: He spoke kindly to him and gave him a seat of honor higher than those of the other kings who were with him in Babylon.

column.name: text
column.value: So Jehoiachin put aside his prison clothes and for the rest of his life ate regularly at the king's table.

column.name: text
column.value: Day by day the king of Babylon gave Jehoiachin a regular allowance as long as he lived, till the day of his death.

column.name: text
column.value: How deserted lies the city, once so full of people! How like a widow is she, who once was great among the nations! She who was queen among the provinces has now become a slave.

column.name: text
column.value: Bitterly she weeps at night, tears are upon her cheeks. Among all her lovers there is none to comfort her. All her friends have betrayed her; they have become her enemies.

column.name: text
column.value: After affliction and harsh labor, Judah has gone into exile. She dwells among the nations; she finds no resting place. All who pursue her have overtaken her in the midst of her distress.

column.name: text
column.value: The roads to Zion mourn, for no one comes to her appointed feasts. All her gateways are desolate, her priests groan, her maidens grieve, and she is in bitter anguish.

column.name: text
column.value: Her foes have become her masters; her enemies are at ease. The LORD has brought her grief because of her many sins. Her children have gone into exile, captive before the foe.

column.name: text
column.value: All the splendor has departed from the Daughter of Zion. Her princes are like deer that find no pasture; in weakness they have fled before the pursuer.

column.name: text
column.value: In the days of her affliction and wandering Jerusalem remembers all the treasures that were hers in days of old. When her people fell into enemy hands, there was no one to help her. Her enemies looked at her and laughed at her destruction.

column.name: text
column.value: Jerusalem has sinned greatly and so has become unclean. All who honored her despise her, for they have seen her nakedness; she herself groans and turns away.

column.name: text
column.value: Her filthiness clung to her skirts; she did not consider her future. Her fall was astounding; there was none to comfort her. "Look, O LORD, on my affliction, for the enemy has triumphed."

column.name: text
column.value: The enemy laid hands on all her treasures; she saw pagan nations enter her sanctuary--those you had forbidden to enter your assembly.

column.name: text
column.value: All her people groan as they search for bread; they barter their treasures for food to keep themselves alive. "Look, O LORD, and consider, for I am despised."

column.name: text
column.value: "Is it nothing to you, all you who pass by? Look around and see. Is any suffering like my suffering that was inflicted on me, that the LORD brought on me in the day of his fierce anger?

column.name: text
column.value: "From on high he sent fire, sent it down into my bones. He spread a net for my feet and turned me back. He made me desolate, faint all the day long.

column.name: text
column.value: "My sins have been bound into a yoke; by his hands they were woven together. They have come upon my neck and the Lord has sapped my strength. He has handed me over to those I cannot withstand.

column.name: text
column.value: "The Lord has rejected all the warriors in my midst; he has summoned an army against me to crush my young men. In his winepress the Lord has trampled the Virgin Daughter of Judah.

column.name: text
column.value: "This is why I weep and my eyes overflow with tears. No one is near to comfort me, no one to restore my spirit. My children are destitute because the enemy has prevailed."

column.name: text
column.value: Zion stretches out her hands, but there is no one to comfort her. The LORD has decreed for Jacob that his neighbors become his foes; Jerusalem has become an unclean thing among them.

column.name: text
column.value: "The LORD is righteous, yet I rebelled against his command. Listen, all you peoples; look upon my suffering. My young men and maidens have gone into exile.

column.name: text
column.value: "I called to my allies but they betrayed me. My priests and my elders perished in the city while they searched for food to keep themselves alive.

column.name: text
column.value: "See, O LORD, how distressed I am! I am in torment within, and in my heart I am disturbed, for I have been most rebellious. Outside, the sword bereaves; inside, there is only death.

column.name: text
column.value: "People have heard my groaning, but there is no one to comfort me. All my enemies have heard of my distress; they rejoice at what you have done. May you bring the day you have announced so they may become like me.

column.name: text
column.value: "Let all their wickedness come before you; deal with them as you have dealt with me because of all my sins. My groans are many and my heart is faint."

column.name: text
column.value: How the Lord has covered the Daughter of Zion with the cloud of his anger! He has hurled down the splendor of Israel from heaven to earth; he has not remembered his footstool in the day of his anger.

column.name: text
column.value: Without pity the Lord has swallowed up all the dwellings of Jacob; in his wrath he has torn down the strongholds of the Daughter of Judah. He has brought her kingdom and its princes down to the ground in dishonor.

column.name: text
column.value: In fierce anger he has cut off every horn of Israel. He has withdrawn his right hand at the approach of the enemy. He has burned in Jacob like a flaming fire that consumes everything around it.

column.name: text
column.value: Like an enemy he has strung his bow; his right hand is ready. Like a foe he has slain all who were pleasing to the eye; he has poured out his wrath like fire on the tent of the Daughter of Zion.

column.name: text
column.value: The Lord is like an enemy; he has swallowed up Israel. He has swallowed up all her palaces and destroyed her strongholds. He has multiplied mourning and lamentation for the Daughter of Judah.

column.name: text
column.value: He has laid waste his dwelling like a garden; he has destroyed his place of meeting. The LORD has made Zion forget her appointed feasts and her Sabbaths; in his fierce anger he has spurned both king and priest.

column.name: text
column.value: The Lord has rejected his altar and abandoned his sanctuary. He has handed over to the enemy the walls of her palaces; they have raised a shout in the house of the LORD as on the day of an appointed feast.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD determined to tear down the wall around the Daughter of Zion. He stretched out a measuring line and did not withhold his hand from destroying. He made ramparts and walls lament; together they wasted away.

column.name: text
column.value: Her gates have sunk into the ground; their bars he has broken and destroyed. Her king and her princes are exiled among the nations, the law is no more, and her prophets no longer find visions from the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: The elders of the Daughter of Zion sit on the ground in silence; they have sprinkled dust on their heads and put on sackcloth. The young women of Jerusalem have bowed their heads to the ground.

column.name: text
column.value: My eyes fail from weeping, I am in torment within, my heart is poured out on the ground because my people are destroyed, because children and infants faint in the streets of the city.

column.name: text
column.value: They say to their mothers, "Where is bread and wine?" as they faint like wounded men in the streets of the city, as their lives ebb away in their mothers' arms.

column.name: text
column.value: What can I say for you? With what can I compare you, O Daughter of Jerusalem? To what can I liken you, that I may comfort you, O Virgin Daughter of Zion? Your wound is as deep as the sea. Who can heal you?

column.name: text
column.value: The visions of your prophets were false and worthless; they did not expose your sin to ward off your captivity. The oracles they gave you were false and misleading.

column.name: text
column.value: All who pass your way clap their hands at you; they scoff and shake their heads at the Daughter of Jerusalem: "Is this the city that was called the perfection of beauty, the joy of the whole earth?"

column.name: text
column.value: All your enemies open their mouths wide against you; they scoff and gnash their teeth and say, "We have swallowed her up. This is the day we have waited for; we have lived to see it."

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD has done what he planned; he has fulfilled his word, which he decreed long ago. He has overthrown you without pity, he has let the enemy gloat over you, he has exalted the horn of your foes.

column.name: text
column.value: The hearts of the people cry out to the Lord. O wall of the Daughter of Zion, let your tears flow like a river day and night; give yourself no relief, your eyes no rest.

column.name: text
column.value: Arise, cry out in the night, as the watches of the night begin; pour out your heart like water in the presence of the Lord. Lift up your hands to him for the lives of your children, who faint from hunger at the head of every street.

column.name: text
column.value: "Look, O LORD, and consider: Whom have you ever treated like this? Should women eat their offspring, the children they have cared for? Should priest and prophet be killed in the sanctuary of the Lord?

column.name: text
column.value: "Young and old lie together in the dust of the streets; my young men and maidens have fallen by the sword. You have slain them in the day of your anger; you have slaughtered them without pity.

column.name: text
column.value: "As you summon to a feast day, so you summoned against me terrors on every side. In the day of the LORD'S anger no one escaped or survived; those I cared for and reared, my enemy has destroyed."

column.name: text
column.value: I am the man who has seen affliction by the rod of his wrath.

column.name: text
column.value: He has driven me away and made me walk in darkness rather than light;

column.name: text
column.value: indeed, he has turned his hand against me again and again, all day long.

column.name: text
column.value: He has made my skin and my flesh grow old and has broken my bones.

column.name: text
column.value: He has besieged me and surrounded me with bitterness and hardship.

column.name: text
column.value: He has made me dwell in darkness like those long dead.

column.name: text
column.value: He has walled me in so I cannot escape; he has weighed me down with chains.

column.name: text
column.value: Even when I call out or cry for help, he shuts out my prayer.

column.name: text
column.value: He has barred my way with blocks of stone; he has made my paths crooked.

column.name: text
column.value: Like a bear lying in wait, like a lion in hiding,

column.name: text
column.value: he dragged me from the path and mangled me and left me without help.

column.name: text
column.value: He drew his bow and made me the target for his arrows.

column.name: text
column.value: He pierced my heart with arrows from his quiver.

column.name: text
column.value: I became the laughingstock of all my people; they mock me in song all day long.

column.name: text
column.value: He has filled me with bitter herbs and sated me with gall.

column.name: text
column.value: He has broken my teeth with gravel; he has trampled me in the dust.

column.name: text
column.value: I have been deprived of peace; I have forgotten what prosperity is.

column.name: text
column.value: So I say, "My splendor is gone and all that I had hoped from the LORD."

column.name: text
column.value: I remember my affliction and my wandering, the bitterness and the gall.

column.name: text
column.value: I well remember them, and my soul is downcast within me.

column.name: text
column.value: Yet this I call to mind and therefore I have hope:

column.name: text
column.value: Because of the LORD'S great love we are not consumed, for his compassions never fail.

column.name: text
column.value: They are new every morning; great is your faithfulness.

column.name: text
column.value: I say to myself, "The LORD is my portion; therefore I will wait for him."

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD is good to those whose hope is in him, to the one who seeks him;

column.name: text
column.value: it is good to wait quietly for the salvation of the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: It is good for a man to bear the yoke while he is young.

column.name: text
column.value: Let him sit alone in silence, for the LORD has laid it on him.

column.name: text
column.value: Let him bury his face in the dust--there may yet be hope.

column.name: text
column.value: Let him offer his cheek to one who would strike him, and let him be filled with disgrace.

column.name: text
column.value: For men are not cast off by the Lord forever.

column.name: text
column.value: Though he brings grief, he will show compassion, so great is his unfailing love.

column.name: text
column.value: For he does not willingly bring affliction or grief to the children of men.

column.name: text
column.value: To crush underfoot all prisoners in the land,

column.name: text
column.value: to deny a man his rights before the Most High,

column.name: text
column.value: to deprive a man of justice--would not the Lord see such things?

column.name: text
column.value: Who can speak and have it happen if the Lord has not decreed it?

column.name: text
column.value: Is it not from the mouth of the Most High that both calamities and good things come?

column.name: text
column.value: Why should any living man complain when punished for his sins?

column.name: text
column.value: Let us examine our ways and test them, and let us return to the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: Let us lift up our hearts and our hands to God in heaven, and say:

column.name: text
column.value: "We have sinned and rebelled and you have not forgiven.

column.name: text
column.value: "You have covered yourself with anger and pursued us; you have slain without pity.

column.name: text
column.value: You have covered yourself with a cloud so that no prayer can get through.

column.name: text
column.value: You have made us scum and refuse among the nations.

column.name: text
column.value: "All our enemies have opened their mouths wide against us.

column.name: text
column.value: We have suffered terror and pitfalls, ruin and destruction."

column.name: text
column.value: Streams of tears flow from my eyes because my people are destroyed.

column.name: text
column.value: My eyes will flow unceasingly, without relief,

column.name: text
column.value: until the LORD looks down from heaven and sees.

column.name: text
column.value: What I see brings grief to my soul because of all the women of my city.

column.name: text
column.value: Those who were my enemies without cause hunted me like a bird.

column.name: text
column.value: They tried to end my life in a pit and threw stones at me;

column.name: text
column.value: the waters closed over my head, and I thought I was about to be cut off.

column.name: text
column.value: I called on your name, O LORD, from the depths of the pit.

column.name: text
column.value: You heard my plea: "Do not close your ears to my cry for relief."

column.name: text
column.value: You came near when I called you, and you said, "Do not fear."

column.name: text
column.value: O Lord, you took up my case; you redeemed my life.

column.name: text
column.value: You have seen, O LORD, the wrong done to me. Uphold my cause!

column.name: text
column.value: You have seen the depth of their vengeance, all their plots against me.

column.name: text
column.value: O LORD, you have heard their insults, all their plots against me--

column.name: text
column.value: what my enemies whisper and mutter against me all day long.

column.name: text
column.value: Look at them! Sitting or standing, they mock me in their songs.

column.name: text
column.value: Pay them back what they deserve, O LORD, for what their hands have done.

column.name: text
column.value: Put a veil over their hearts, and may your curse be on them!

column.name: text
column.value: Pursue them in anger and destroy them from under the heavens of the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: This word came to Jeremiah concerning all the Jews living in Lower Egypt--in Migdol, Tahpanhes and Memphis--and in Upper Egypt:

column.name: text
column.value: "This is what the LORD Almighty, the God of Israel, says: You saw the great disaster I brought on Jerusalem and on all the towns of Judah. Today they lie deserted and in ruins

column.name: text
column.value: because of the evil they have done. They provoked me to anger by burning incense and by worshiping other gods that neither they nor you nor your fathers ever knew.

column.name: text
