column.value: "As for the rest of the tribes: Benjamin will have one portion; it will extend from the east side to the west side.

column.name: text
column.value: "Simeon will have one portion; it will border the territory of Benjamin from east to west.

column.name: text
column.value: "Issachar will have one portion; it will border the territory of Simeon from east to west.

column.name: text
column.value: "Zebulun will have one portion; it will border the territory of Issachar from east to west.

column.name: text
column.value: "Gad will have one portion; it will border the territory of Zebulun from east to west.

column.name: text
column.value: "The southern boundary of Gad will run south from Tamar to the waters of Meribah Kadesh, then along the Wadi of Egypt to the Great Sea.

column.name: text
column.value: "This is the land you are to allot as an inheritance to the tribes of Israel, and these will be their portions," declares the Sovereign LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: "These will be the exits of the city: Beginning on the north side, which is 4,500 cubits long,

column.name: text
column.value: the gates of the city will be named after the tribes of Israel. The three gates on the north side will be the gate of Reuben, the gate of Judah and the gate of Levi.

column.name: text
column.value: "On the east side, which is 4,500 cubits long, will be three gates: the gate of Joseph, the gate of Benjamin and the gate of Dan.

column.name: text
column.value: "On the south side, which measures 4,500 cubits, will be three gates: the gate of Simeon, the gate of Issachar and the gate of Zebulun.

column.name: text
column.value: "On the west side, which is 4,500 cubits long, will be three gates: the gate of Gad, the gate of Asher and the gate of Naphtali.

column.name: text
column.value: "The distance all around will be 18,000 cubits. "And the name of the city from that time on will be: THE LORD IS THERE."

column.name: text
column.value: In the third year of the reign of Jehoiakim king of Judah, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came to Jerusalem and besieged it.

column.name: text
column.value: And the Lord delivered Jehoiakim king of Judah into his hand, along with some of the articles from the temple of God. These he carried off to the temple of his god in Babylonia and put in the treasure house of his god.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the king ordered Ashpenaz, chief of his court officials, to bring in some of the Israelites from the royal family and the nobility--

column.name: text
column.value: young men without any physical defect, handsome, showing aptitude for every kind of learning, well informed, quick to understand, and qualified to serve in the king's palace. He was to teach them the language and literature of the Babylonians.

column.name: text
column.value: The king assigned them a daily amount of food and wine from the king's table. They were to be trained for three years, and after that they were to enter the king's service.

column.name: text
column.value: Among these were some from Judah: Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael and Azariah.

column.name: text
column.value: The chief official gave them new names: to Daniel, the name Belteshazzar; to Hananiah, Shadrach; to Mishael, Meshach; and to Azariah, Abednego.

column.name: text
column.value: But Daniel resolved not to defile himself with the royal food and wine, and he asked the chief official for permission not to defile himself this way.

column.name: text
column.value: Now God had caused the official to show favor and sympathy to Daniel,

column.name: text
column.value: but the official told Daniel, "I am afraid of my lord the king, who has assigned your food and drink. Why should he see you looking worse than the other young men your age? The king would then have my head because of you."

column.name: text
column.value: Daniel then said to the guard whom the chief official had appointed over Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael and Azariah,

column.name: text
column.value: "Please test your servants for ten days: Give us nothing but vegetables to eat and water to drink.

column.name: text
column.value: Then compare our appearance with that of the young men who eat the royal food, and treat your servants in accordance with what you see."

column.name: text
column.value: So he agreed to this and tested them for ten days.

column.name: text
column.value: At the end of the ten days they looked healthier and better nourished than any of the young men who ate the royal food.

column.name: text
column.value: So the guard took away their choice food and the wine they were to drink and gave them vegetables instead.

column.name: text
column.value: To these four young men God gave knowledge and understanding of all kinds of literature and learning. And Daniel could understand visions and dreams of all kinds.

column.name: text
column.value: At the end of the time set by the king to bring them in, the chief official presented them to Nebuchadnezzar.

column.name: text
column.value: The king talked with them, and he found none equal to Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael and Azariah; so they entered the king's service.

column.name: text
column.value: In every matter of wisdom and understanding about which the king questioned them, he found them ten times better than all the magicians and enchanters in his whole kingdom.

column.name: text
column.value: And Daniel remained there until the first year of King Cyrus.

column.name: text
column.value: In the second year of his reign, Nebuchadnezzar had dreams; his mind was troubled and he could not sleep.

column.name: text
column.value: So the king summoned the magicians, enchanters, sorcerers and astrologers to tell him what he had dreamed. When they came in and stood before the king,

column.name: text
column.value: he said to them, "I have had a dream that troubles me and I want to know what it means."

column.name: text
column.value: Then the astrologers answered the king in Aramaic, "O king, live forever! Tell your servants the dream, and we will interpret it."

column.name: text
column.value: The king replied to the astrologers, "This is what I have firmly decided: If you do not tell me what my dream was and interpret it, I will have you cut into pieces and your houses turned into piles of rubble.

column.name: text
column.value: But if you tell me the dream and explain it, you will receive from me gifts and rewards and great honor. So tell me the dream and interpret it for me."

column.name: text
column.value: Once more they replied, "Let the king tell his servants the dream, and we will interpret it."

column.name: text
column.value: Then the king answered, "I am certain that you are trying to gain time, because you realize that this is what I have firmly decided:

column.name: text
column.value: If you do not tell me the dream, there is just one penalty for you. You have conspired to tell me misleading and wicked things, hoping the situation will change. So then, tell me the dream, and I will know that you can interpret it for me."

column.name: text
column.value: The astrologers answered the king, "There is not a man on earth who can do what the king asks! No king, however great and mighty, has ever asked such a thing of any magician or enchanter or astrologer.

column.name: text
column.value: What the king asks is too difficult. No one can reveal it to the king except the gods, and they do not live among men."

column.name: text
column.value: This made the king so angry and furious that he ordered the execution of all the wise men of Babylon.

column.name: text
column.value: So the decree was issued to put the wise men to death, and men were sent to look for Daniel and his friends to put them to death.

column.name: text
column.value: When Arioch, the commander of the king's guard, had gone out to put to death the wise men of Babylon, Daniel spoke to him with wisdom and tact.

column.name: text
column.value: He asked the king's officer, "Why did the king issue such a harsh decree?" Arioch then explained the matter to Daniel.

column.name: text
column.value: At this, Daniel went in to the king and asked for time, so that he might interpret the dream for him.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Daniel returned to his house and explained the matter to his friends Hananiah, Mishael and Azariah.

column.name: text
column.value: He urged them to plead for mercy from the God of heaven concerning this mystery, so that he and his friends might not be executed with the rest of the wise men of Babylon.

column.name: text
column.value: During the night the mystery was revealed to Daniel in a vision. Then Daniel praised the God of heaven

column.name: text
column.value: and said: "Praise be to the name of God for ever and ever; wisdom and power are his.

column.name: text
column.value: He changes times and seasons; he sets up kings and deposes them. He gives wisdom to the wise and knowledge to the discerning.

column.name: text
column.value: He reveals deep and hidden things; he knows what lies in darkness, and light dwells with him.

column.name: text
column.value: I thank and praise you, O God of my fathers: You have given me wisdom and power, you have made known to me what we asked of you, you have made known to us the dream of the king."

column.name: text
column.value: Then Daniel went to Arioch, whom the king had appointed to execute the wise men of Babylon, and said to him, "Do not execute the wise men of Babylon. Take me to the king, and I will interpret his dream for him."

column.name: text
column.value: Arioch took Daniel to the king at once and said, "I have found a man among the exiles from Judah who can tell the king what his dream means."

column.name: text
column.value: The king asked Daniel (also called Belteshazzar), "Are you able to tell me what I saw in my dream and interpret it?"

column.name: text
column.value: Daniel replied, "No wise man, enchanter, magician or diviner can explain to the king the mystery he has asked about,

column.name: text
column.value: but there is a God in heaven who reveals mysteries. He has shown King Nebuchadnezzar what will happen in days to come. Your dream and the visions that passed through your mind as you lay on your bed are these:

column.name: text
column.value: "As you were lying there, O king, your mind turned to things to come, and the revealer of mysteries showed you what is going to happen.

column.name: text
column.value: As for me, this mystery has been revealed to me, not because I have greater wisdom than other living men, but so that you, O king, may know the interpretation and that you may understand what went through your mind.

column.name: text
column.value: "You looked, O king, and there before you stood a large statue--an enormous, dazzling statue, awesome in appearance.

column.name: text
column.value: The head of the statue was made of pure gold, its chest and arms of silver, its belly and thighs of bronze,

column.name: text
column.value: its legs of iron, its feet partly of iron and partly of baked clay.

column.name: text
column.value: While you were watching, a rock was cut out, but not by human hands. It struck the statue on its feet of iron and clay and smashed them.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the iron, the clay, the bronze, the silver and the gold were broken to pieces at the same time and became like chaff on a threshing floor in the summer. The wind swept them away without leaving a trace. But the rock that struck the statue became a huge mountain and filled the whole earth.

column.name: text
column.value: "This was the dream, and now we will interpret it to the king.

column.name: text
column.value: You, O king, are the king of kings. The God of heaven has given you dominion and power and might and glory;

column.name: text
column.value: in your hands he has placed mankind and the beasts of the field and the birds of the air. Wherever they live, he has made you ruler over them all. You are that head of gold.

column.name: text
column.value: "After you, another kingdom will rise, inferior to yours. Next, a third kingdom, one of bronze, will rule over the whole earth.

column.name: text
column.value: Finally, there will be a fourth kingdom, strong as iron--for iron breaks and smashes everything--and as iron breaks things to pieces, so it will crush and break all the others.

column.name: text
column.value: Just as you saw that the feet and toes were partly of baked clay and partly of iron, so this will be a divided kingdom; yet it will have some of the strength of iron in it, even as you saw iron mixed with clay.

column.name: text
column.value: As the toes were partly iron and partly clay, so this kingdom will be partly strong and partly brittle.

column.name: text
column.value: And just as you saw the iron mixed with baked clay, so the people will be a mixture and will not remain united, any more than iron mixes with clay.

column.name: text
column.value: "In the time of those kings, the God of heaven will set up a kingdom that will never be destroyed, nor will it be left to another people. It will crush all those kingdoms and bring them to an end, but it will itself endure forever.

column.name: text
column.value: This is the meaning of the vision of the rock cut out of a mountain, but not by human hands--a rock that broke the iron, the bronze, the clay, the silver and the gold to pieces. "The great God has shown the king what will take place in the future. The dream is true and the interpretation is trustworthy."

column.name: text
column.value: Then King Nebuchadnezzar fell prostrate before Daniel and paid him honor and ordered that an offering and incense be presented to him.

column.name: text
column.value: The king said to Daniel, "Surely your God is the God of gods and the Lord of kings and a revealer of mysteries, for you were able to reveal this mystery."

column.name: text
column.value: Then the king placed Daniel in a high position and lavished many gifts on him. He made him ruler over the entire province of Babylon and placed him in charge of all its wise men.

column.name: text
column.value: Moreover, at Daniel's request the king appointed Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego administrators over the province of Babylon, while Daniel himself remained at the royal court.

column.name: text
column.value: King Nebuchadnezzar made an image of gold, ninety feet high and nine feet wide, and set it up on the plain of Dura in the province of Babylon.

column.name: text
column.value: He then summoned the satraps, prefects, governors, advisers, treasurers, judges, magistrates and all the other provincial officials to come to the dedication of the image he had set up.

column.name: text
column.value: So the satraps, prefects, governors, advisers, treasurers, judges, magistrates and all the other provincial officials assembled for the dedication of the image that King Nebuchadnezzar had set up, and they stood before it.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the herald loudly proclaimed, "This is what you are commanded to do, O peoples, nations and men of every language:

column.name: text
column.value: As soon as you hear the sound of the horn, flute, zither, lyre, harp, pipes and all kinds of music, you must fall down and worship the image of gold that King Nebuchadnezzar has set up.

column.name: text
column.value: Whoever does not fall down and worship will immediately be thrown into a blazing furnace."

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore, as soon as they heard the sound of the horn, flute, zither, lyre, harp and all kinds of music, all the peoples, nations and men of every language fell down and worshiped the image of gold that King Nebuchadnezzar had set up.

column.name: text
column.value: At this time some astrologers came forward and denounced the Jews.

column.name: text
column.value: They said to King Nebuchadnezzar, "O king, live forever!

column.name: text
column.value: You have issued a decree, O king, that everyone who hears the sound of the horn, flute, zither, lyre, harp, pipes and all kinds of music must fall down and worship the image of gold,

column.name: text
column.value: and that whoever does not fall down and worship will be thrown into a blazing furnace.

column.name: text
column.value: But there are some Jews whom you have set over the affairs of the province of Babylon--Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego--who pay no attention to you, O king. They neither serve your gods nor worship the image of gold you have set up."

column.name: text
column.value: Furious with rage, Nebuchadnezzar summoned Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego. So these men were brought before the king,

column.name: text
column.value: and Nebuchadnezzar said to them, "Is it true, Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego, that you do not serve my gods or worship the image of gold I have set up?

column.name: text
column.value: Now when you hear the sound of the horn, flute, zither, lyre, harp, pipes and all kinds of music, if you are ready to fall down and worship the image I made, very good. But if you do not worship it, you will be thrown immediately into a blazing furnace. Then what god will be able to rescue you from my hand?"

column.name: text
column.value: Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego replied to the king, "O Nebuchadnezzar, we do not need to defend ourselves before you in this matter.

column.name: text
column.value: If we are thrown into the blazing furnace, the God we serve is able to save us from it, and he will rescue us from your hand, O king.

column.name: text
column.value: But even if he does not, we want you to know, O king, that we will not serve your gods or worship the image of gold you have set up."

column.name: text
column.value: Then Nebuchadnezzar was furious with Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego, and his attitude toward them changed. He ordered the furnace heated seven times hotter than usual

column.name: text
column.value: and commanded some of the strongest soldiers in his army to tie up Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego and throw them into the blazing furnace.

column.name: text
column.value: So these men, wearing their robes, trousers, turbans and other clothes, were bound and thrown into the blazing furnace.

column.name: text
column.value: The king's command was so urgent and the furnace so hot that the flames of the fire killed the soldiers who took up Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego,

column.name: text
column.value: and these three men, firmly tied, fell into the blazing furnace.

column.name: text
column.value: Then King Nebuchadnezzar leaped to his feet in amazement and asked his advisers, "Weren't there three men that we tied up and threw into the fire?" They replied, "Certainly, O king."

column.name: text
column.value: He said, "Look! I see four men walking around in the fire, unbound and unharmed, and the fourth looks like a son of the gods."

column.name: text
column.value: Nebuchadnezzar then approached the opening of the blazing furnace and shouted, "Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego, servants of the Most High God, come out! Come here!" So Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego came out of the fire,

column.name: text
column.value: and the satraps, prefects, governors and royal advisers crowded around them. They saw that the fire had not harmed their bodies, nor was a hair of their heads singed; their robes were not scorched, and there was no smell of fire on them.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Nebuchadnezzar said, "Praise be to the God of Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego, who has sent his angel and rescued his servants! They trusted in him and defied the king's command and were willing to give up their lives rather than serve or worship any god except their own God.

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore I decree that the people of any nation or language who say anything against the God of Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego be cut into pieces and their houses be turned into piles of rubble, for no other god can save in this way."

column.name: text
column.value: Then the king promoted Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego in the province of Babylon.

column.name: text
column.value: King Nebuchadnezzar, To the peoples, nations and men of every language, who live in all the world: May you prosper greatly!

column.name: text
column.value: It is my pleasure to tell you about the miraculous signs and wonders that the Most High God has performed for me.

column.name: text
column.value: How great are his signs, how mighty his wonders! His kingdom is an eternal kingdom; his dominion endures from generation to generation.

column.name: text
column.value: I, Nebuchadnezzar, was at home in my palace, contented and prosperous.

column.name: text
column.value: I had a dream that made me afraid. As I was lying in my bed, the images and visions that passed through my mind terrified me.

column.name: text
column.value: So I commanded that all the wise men of Babylon be brought before me to interpret the dream for me.

column.name: text
column.value: When the magicians, enchanters, astrologers and diviners came, I told them the dream, but they could not interpret it for me.

column.name: text
column.value: Finally, Daniel came into my presence and I told him the dream. (He is called Belteshazzar, after the name of my god, and the spirit of the holy gods is in him.)

column.name: text
column.value: I said, "Belteshazzar, chief of the magicians, I know that the spirit of the holy gods is in you, and no mystery is too difficult for you. Here is my dream; interpret it for me.

column.name: text
column.value: These are the visions I saw while lying in my bed: I looked, and there before me stood a tree in the middle of the land. Its height was enormous.

column.name: text
column.value: The tree grew large and strong and its top touched the sky; it was visible to the ends of the earth.

column.name: text
column.value: Its leaves were beautiful, its fruit abundant, and on it was food for all. Under it the beasts of the field found shelter, and the birds of the air lived in its branches; from it every creature was fed.

column.name: text
column.value: "In the visions I saw while lying in my bed, I looked, and there before me was a messenger, a holy one, coming down from heaven.

column.name: text
column.value: He called in a loud voice: 'Cut down the tree and trim off its branches; strip off its leaves and scatter its fruit. Let the animals flee from under it and the birds from its branches.

column.name: text
column.value: But let the stump and its roots, bound with iron and bronze, remain in the ground, in the grass of the field. "'Let him be drenched with the dew of heaven, and let him live with the animals among the plants of the earth.

column.name: text
column.value: Let his mind be changed from that of a man and let him be given the mind of an animal, till seven times pass by for him.

column.name: text
column.value: "'The decision is announced by messengers, the holy ones declare the verdict, so that the living may know that the Most High is sovereign over the kingdoms of men and gives them to anyone he wishes and sets over them the lowliest of men.'

column.name: text
column.value: "This is the dream that I, King Nebuchadnezzar, had. Now, Belteshazzar, tell me what it means, for none of the wise men in my kingdom can interpret it for me. But you can, because the spirit of the holy gods is in you."

column.name: text
column.value: Then Daniel (also called Belteshazzar) was greatly perplexed for a time, and his thoughts terrified him. So the king said, "Belteshazzar, do not let the dream or its meaning alarm you." Belteshazzar answered, "My lord, if only the dream applied to your enemies and its meaning to your adversaries!

column.name: text
column.value: The tree you saw, which grew large and strong, with its top touching the sky, visible to the whole earth,

column.name: text
column.value: with beautiful leaves and abundant fruit, providing food for all, giving shelter to the beasts of the field, and having nesting places in its branches for the birds of the air--

column.name: text
column.value: you, O king, are that tree! You have become great and strong; your greatness has grown until it reaches the sky, and your dominion extends to distant parts of the earth.

column.name: text
column.value: "You, O king, saw a messenger, a holy one, coming down from heaven and saying, 'Cut down the tree and destroy it, but leave the stump, bound with iron and bronze, in the grass of the field, while its roots remain in the ground. Let him be drenched with the dew of heaven; let him live like the wild animals, until seven times pass by for him.'

column.name: text
column.value: "This is the interpretation, O king, and this is the decree the Most High has issued against my lord the king:

column.name: text
column.value: You will be driven away from people and will live with the wild animals; you will eat grass like cattle and be drenched with the dew of heaven. Seven times will pass by for you until you acknowledge that the Most High is sovereign over the kingdoms of men and gives them to anyone he wishes.

column.name: text
column.value: The command to leave the stump of the tree with its roots means that your kingdom will be restored to you when you acknowledge that Heaven rules.

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore, O king, be pleased to accept my advice: Renounce your sins by doing what is right, and your wickedness by being kind to the oppressed. It may be that then your prosperity will continue."

column.name: text
column.value: All this happened to King Nebuchadnezzar.

column.name: text
column.value: Twelve months later, as the king was walking on the roof of the royal palace of Babylon,

column.name: text
column.value: he said, "Is not this the great Babylon I have built as the royal residence, by my mighty power and for the glory of my majesty?"

column.name: text
column.value: The words were still on his lips when a voice came from heaven, "This is what is decreed for you, King Nebuchadnezzar: Your royal authority has been taken from you.

column.name: text
column.value: You will be driven away from people and will live with the wild animals; you will eat grass like cattle. Seven times will pass by for you until you acknowledge that the Most High is sovereign over the kingdoms of men and gives them to anyone he wishes."

column.name: text
column.value: Immediately what had been said about Nebuchadnezzar was fulfilled. He was driven away from people and ate grass like cattle. His body was drenched with the dew of heaven until his hair grew like the feathers of an eagle and his nails like the claws of a bird.

column.name: text
column.value: At the end of that time, I, Nebuchadnezzar, raised my eyes toward heaven, and my sanity was restored. Then I praised the Most High; I honored and glorified him who lives forever. His dominion is an eternal dominion; his kingdom endures from generation to generation.

column.name: text
column.value: All the peoples of the earth are regarded as nothing. He does as he pleases with the powers of heaven and the peoples of the earth. No one can hold back his hand or say to him: "What have you done?"

column.name: text
column.value: At the same time that my sanity was restored, my honor and splendor were returned to me for the glory of my kingdom. My advisers and nobles sought me out, and I was restored to my throne and became even greater than before.

column.name: text
column.value: Now I, Nebuchadnezzar, praise and exalt and glorify the King of heaven, because everything he does is right and all his ways are just. And those who walk in pride he is able to humble.

column.name: text
column.value: King Belshazzar gave a great banquet for a thousand of his nobles and drank wine with them.

column.name: text
column.value: While Belshazzar was drinking his wine, he gave orders to bring in the gold and silver goblets that Nebuchadnezzar his father had taken from the temple in Jerusalem, so that the king and his nobles, his wives and his concubines might drink from them.

column.name: text
column.value: So they brought in the gold goblets that had been taken from the temple of God in Jerusalem, and the king and his nobles, his wives and his concubines drank from them.

column.name: text
column.value: As they drank the wine, they praised the gods of gold and silver, of bronze, iron, wood and stone.

column.name: text
column.value: Suddenly the fingers of a human hand appeared and wrote on the plaster of the wall, near the lampstand in the royal palace. The king watched the hand as it wrote.

column.name: text
column.value: His face turned pale and he was so frightened that his knees knocked together and his legs gave way.

column.name: text
column.value: The king called out for the enchanters, astrologers and diviners to be brought and said to these wise men of Babylon, "Whoever reads this writing and tells me what it means will be clothed in purple and have a gold chain placed around his neck, and he will be made the third highest ruler in the kingdom."

column.name: text
column.value: Then all the king's wise men came in, but they could not read the writing or tell the king what it meant.

column.name: text
column.value: So King Belshazzar became even more terrified and his face grew more pale. His nobles were baffled.

column.name: text
column.value: The queen, hearing the voices of the king and his nobles, came into the banquet hall. "O king, live forever!" she said. "Don't be alarmed! Don't look so pale!

column.name: text
column.value: There is a man in your kingdom who has the spirit of the holy gods in him. In the time of your father he was found to have insight and intelligence and wisdom like that of the gods. King Nebuchadnezzar your father--your father the king, I say--appointed him chief of the magicians, enchanters, astrologers and diviners.

column.name: text
column.value: This man Daniel, whom the king called Belteshazzar, was found to have a keen mind and knowledge and understanding, and also the ability to interpret dreams, explain riddles and solve difficult problems. Call for Daniel, and he will tell you what the writing means."

column.name: text
column.value: So Daniel was brought before the king, and the king said to him, "Are you Daniel, one of the exiles my father the king brought from Judah?

column.name: text
column.value: I have heard that the spirit of the gods is in you and that you have insight, intelligence and outstanding wisdom.

column.name: text
column.value: The wise men and enchanters were brought before me to read this writing and tell me what it means, but they could not explain it.

column.name: text
column.value: Now I have heard that you are able to give interpretations and to solve difficult problems. If you can read this writing and tell me what it means, you will be clothed in purple and have a gold chain placed around your neck, and you will be made the third highest ruler in the kingdom."

column.name: text
column.value: Then Daniel answered the king, "You may keep your gifts for yourself and give your rewards to someone else. Nevertheless, I will read the writing for the king and tell him what it means.

column.name: text
column.value: "O king, the Most High God gave your father Nebuchadnezzar sovereignty and greatness and glory and splendor.

column.name: text
column.value: Because of the high position he gave him, all the peoples and nations and men of every language dreaded and feared him. Those the king wanted to put to death, he put to death; those he wanted to spare, he spared; those he wanted to promote, he promoted; and those he wanted to humble, he humbled.

column.name: text
column.value: But when his heart became arrogant and hardened with pride, he was deposed from his royal throne and stripped of his glory.

column.name: text
column.value: He was driven away from people and given the mind of an animal; he lived with the wild donkeys and ate grass like cattle; and his body was drenched with the dew of heaven, until he acknowledged that the Most High God is sovereign over the kingdoms of men and sets over them anyone he wishes.

column.name: text
column.value: "But you his son, O Belshazzar, have not humbled yourself, though you knew all this.

column.name: text
column.value: Instead, you have set yourself up against the Lord of heaven. You had the goblets from his temple brought to you, and you and your nobles, your wives and your concubines drank wine from them. You praised the gods of silver and gold, of bronze, iron, wood and stone, which cannot see or hear or understand. But you did not honor the God who holds in his hand your life and all your ways.

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore he sent the hand that wrote the inscription.

column.name: text
column.value: "This is the inscription that was written: MENE, MENE, TEKEL, PARSIN

column.name: text
column.value: "This is what these words mean: Mene : God has numbered the days of your reign and brought it to an end.

column.name: text
column.value: Tekel : You have been weighed on the scales and found wanting.

column.name: text
column.value: Peres : Your kingdom is divided and given to the Medes and Persians."

column.name: text
column.value: Then at Belshazzar's command, Daniel was clothed in purple, a gold chain was placed around his neck, and he was proclaimed the third highest ruler in the kingdom.

column.name: text
column.value: That very night Belshazzar, king of the Babylonians, was slain,

column.name: text
column.value: and Darius the Mede took over the kingdom, at the age of sixty-two.

column.name: text
column.value: It pleased Darius to appoint 120 satraps to rule throughout the kingdom,

column.name: text
column.value: with three administrators over them, one of whom was Daniel. The satraps were made accountable to them so that the king might not suffer loss.

column.name: text
column.value: Now Daniel so distinguished himself among the administrators and the satraps by his exceptional qualities that the king planned to set him over the whole kingdom.

column.name: text
column.value: At this, the administrators and the satraps tried to find grounds for charges against Daniel in his conduct of government affairs, but they were unable to do so. They could find no corruption in him, because he was trustworthy and neither corrupt nor negligent.

column.name: text
column.value: Finally these men said, "We will never find any basis for charges against this man Daniel unless it has something to do with the law of his God."

column.name: text
column.value: So the administrators and the satraps went as a group to the king and said: "O King Darius, live forever!

column.name: text
column.value: The royal administrators, prefects, satraps, advisers and governors have all agreed that the king should issue an edict and enforce the decree that anyone who prays to any god or man during the next thirty days, except to you, O king, shall be thrown into the lions' den.

column.name: text
column.value: Now, O king, issue the decree and put it in writing so that it cannot be altered--in accordance with the laws of the Medes and Persians, which cannot be repealed."

column.name: text
column.value: So King Darius put the decree in writing.

column.name: text
column.value: Now when Daniel learned that the decree had been published, he went home to his upstairs room where the windows opened toward Jerusalem. Three times a day he got down on his knees and prayed, giving thanks to his God, just as he had done before.

column.name: text
column.value: Then these men went as a group and found Daniel praying and asking God for help.

column.name: text
column.value: So they went to the king and spoke to him about his royal decree: "Did you not publish a decree that during the next thirty days anyone who prays to any god or man except to you, O king, would be thrown into the lions' den?" The king answered, "The decree stands--in accordance with the laws of the Medes and Persians, which cannot be repealed."

column.name: text
column.value: Then they said to the king, "Daniel, who is one of the exiles from Judah, pays no attention to you, O king, or to the decree you put in writing. He still prays three times a day."

column.name: text
column.value: When the king heard this, he was greatly distressed; he was determined to rescue Daniel and made every effort until sundown to save him.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the men went as a group to the king and said to him, "Remember, O king, that according to the law of the Medes and Persians no decree or edict that the king issues can be changed."

column.name: text
column.value: So the king gave the order, and they brought Daniel and threw him into the lions' den. The king said to Daniel, "May your God, whom you serve continually, rescue you!"

column.name: text
column.value: A stone was brought and placed over the mouth of the den, and the king sealed it with his own signet ring and with the rings of his nobles, so that Daniel's situation might not be changed.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the king returned to his palace and spent the night without eating and without any entertainment being brought to him. And he could not sleep.

column.name: text
column.value: At the first light of dawn, the king got up and hurried to the lions' den.

column.name: text
column.value: When he came near the den, he called to Daniel in an anguished voice, "Daniel, servant of the living God, has your God, whom you serve continually, been able to rescue you from the lions?"

column.name: text
column.value: Daniel answered, "O king, live forever!

column.name: text
column.value: My God sent his angel, and he shut the mouths of the lions. They have not hurt me, because I was found innocent in his sight. Nor have I ever done any wrong before you, O king."

column.name: text
column.value: The king was overjoyed and gave orders to lift Daniel out of the den. And when Daniel was lifted from the den, no wound was found on him, because he had trusted in his God.

column.name: text
column.value: At the king's command, the men who had falsely accused Daniel were brought in and thrown into the lions' den, along with their wives and children. And before they reached the floor of the den, the lions overpowered them and crushed all their bones.

column.name: text
column.value: Then King Darius wrote to all the peoples, nations and men of every language throughout the land: "May you prosper greatly!

column.name: text
column.value: "I issue a decree that in every part of my kingdom people must fear and reverence the God of Daniel. "For he is the living God and he endures forever; his kingdom will not be destroyed, his dominion will never end.

column.name: text
column.value: He rescues and he saves; he performs signs and wonders in the heavens and on the earth. He has rescued Daniel from the power of the lions."

column.name: text
column.value: So Daniel prospered during the reign of Darius and the reign of Cyrus the Persian.

column.name: text
column.value: In the first year of Belshazzar king of Babylon, Daniel had a dream, and visions passed through his mind as he was lying on his bed. He wrote down the substance of his dream.

column.name: text
column.value: Daniel said: "In my vision at night I looked, and there before me were the four winds of heaven churning up the great sea.

column.name: text
column.value: Four great beasts, each different from the others, came up out of the sea.

column.name: text
column.value: "The first was like a lion, and it had the wings of an eagle. I watched until its wings were torn off and it was lifted from the ground so that it stood on two feet like a man, and the heart of a man was given to it.

column.name: text
column.value: "And there before me was a second beast, which looked like a bear. It was raised up on one of its sides, and it had three ribs in its mouth between its teeth. It was told, 'Get up and eat your fill of flesh!'

column.name: text
column.value: "After that, I looked, and there before me was another beast, one that looked like a leopard. And on its back it had four wings like those of a bird. This beast had four heads, and it was given authority to rule.

column.name: text
column.value: "After that, in my vision at night I looked, and there before me was a fourth beast--terrifying and frightening and very powerful. It had large iron teeth; it crushed and devoured its victims and trampled underfoot whatever was left. It was different from all the former beasts, and it had ten horns.

column.name: text
column.value: "While I was thinking about the horns, there before me was another horn, a little one, which came up among them; and three of the first horns were uprooted before it. This horn had eyes like the eyes of a man and a mouth that spoke boastfully.

column.name: text
column.value: "As I looked, "thrones were set in place, and the Ancient of Days took his seat. His clothing was as white as snow; the hair of his head was white like wool. His throne was flaming with fire, and its wheels were all ablaze.

column.name: text
column.value: A river of fire was flowing, coming out from before him. Thousands upon thousands attended him; ten thousand times ten thousand stood before him. The court was seated, and the books were opened.

column.name: text
column.value: "Then I continued to watch because of the boastful words the horn was speaking. I kept looking until the beast was slain and its body destroyed and thrown into the blazing fire.

column.name: text
column.value: (The other beasts had been stripped of their authority, but were allowed to live for a period of time.)

column.name: text
column.value: "In my vision at night I looked, and there before me was one like a son of man, coming with the clouds of heaven. He approached the Ancient of Days and was led into his presence.

column.name: text
column.value: He was given authority, glory and sovereign power; all peoples, nations and men of every language worshiped him. His dominion is an everlasting dominion that will not pass away, and his kingdom is one that will never be destroyed.

column.name: text
column.value: "I, Daniel, was troubled in spirit, and the visions that passed through my mind disturbed me.

column.name: text
column.value: I approached one of those standing there and asked him the true meaning of all this. "So he told me and gave me the interpretation of these things:

column.name: text
column.value: 'The four great beasts are four kingdoms that will rise from the earth.

column.name: text
column.value: But the saints of the Most High will receive the kingdom and will possess it forever--yes, for ever and ever.'

column.name: text
column.value: "Then I wanted to know the true meaning of the fourth beast, which was different from all the others and most terrifying, with its iron teeth and bronze claws--the beast that crushed and devoured its victims and trampled underfoot whatever was left.

column.name: text
column.value: I also wanted to know about the ten horns on its head and about the other horn that came up, before which three of them fell--the horn that looked more imposing than the others and that had eyes and a mouth that spoke boastfully.

column.name: text
column.value: As I watched, this horn was waging war against the saints and defeating them,

column.name: text
column.value: until the Ancient of Days came and pronounced judgment in favor of the saints of the Most High, and the time came when they possessed the kingdom.

column.name: text
column.value: "He gave me this explanation: 'The fourth beast is a fourth kingdom that will appear on earth. It will be different from all the other kingdoms and will devour the whole earth, trampling it down and crushing it.

column.name: text
column.value: The ten horns are ten kings who will come from this kingdom. After them another king will arise, different from the earlier ones; he will subdue three kings.

column.name: text
column.value: He will speak against the Most High and oppress his saints and try to change the set times and the laws. The saints will be handed over to him for a time, times and half a time.

column.name: text
column.value: "'But the court will sit, and his power will be taken away and completely destroyed forever.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the sovereignty, power and greatness of the kingdoms under the whole heaven will be handed over to the saints, the people of the Most High. His kingdom will be an everlasting kingdom, and all rulers will worship and obey him.'

column.name: text
column.value: "This is the end of the matter. I, Daniel, was deeply troubled by my thoughts, and my face turned pale, but I kept the matter to myself."

column.name: text
column.value: In the third year of King Belshazzar's reign, I, Daniel, had a vision, after the one that had already appeared to me.

column.name: text
column.value: In my vision I saw myself in the citadel of Susa in the province of Elam; in the vision I was beside the Ulai Canal.

column.name: text
column.value: I looked up, and there before me was a ram with two horns, standing beside the canal, and the horns were long. One of the horns was longer than the other but grew up later.

column.name: text
column.value: I watched the ram as he charged toward the west and the north and the south. No animal could stand against him, and none could rescue from his power. He did as he pleased and became great.

column.name: text
column.value: As I was thinking about this, suddenly a goat with a prominent horn between his eyes came from the west, crossing the whole earth without touching the ground.

column.name: text
column.value: He came toward the two-horned ram I had seen standing beside the canal and charged at him in great rage.

column.name: text
column.value: I saw him attack the ram furiously, striking the ram and shattering his two horns. The ram was powerless to stand against him; the goat knocked him to the ground and trampled on him, and none could rescue the ram from his power.

column.name: text
column.value: The goat became very great, but at the height of his power his large horn was broken off, and in its place four prominent horns grew up toward the four winds of heaven.

column.name: text
column.value: Out of one of them came another horn, which started small but grew in power to the south and to the east and toward the Beautiful Land.

column.name: text
column.value: It grew until it reached the host of the heavens, and it threw some of the starry host down to the earth and trampled on them.

column.name: text
column.value: It set itself up to be as great as the Prince of the host; it took away the daily sacrifice from him, and the place of his sanctuary was brought low.

column.name: text
column.value: Because of rebellion, the host of the saints and the daily sacrifice were given over to it. It prospered in everything it did, and truth was thrown to the ground.

column.name: text
column.value: Then I heard a holy one speaking, and another holy one said to him, "How long will it take for the vision to be fulfilled--the vision concerning the daily sacrifice, the rebellion that causes desolation, and the surrender of the sanctuary and of the host that will be trampled underfoot?"

column.name: text
column.value: He said to me, "It will take 2,300 evenings and mornings; then the sanctuary will be reconsecrated."

column.name: text
column.value: While I, Daniel, was watching the vision and trying to understand it, there before me stood one who looked like a man.

column.name: text
column.value: And I heard a man's voice from the Ulai calling, "Gabriel, tell this man the meaning of the vision."

column.name: text
column.value: As he came near the place where I was standing, I was terrified and fell prostrate. "Son of man," he said to me, "understand that the vision concerns the time of the end."

column.name: text
column.value: While he was speaking to me, I was in a deep sleep, with my face to the ground. Then he touched me and raised me to my feet.

column.name: text
column.value: He said: "I am going to tell you what will happen later in the time of wrath, because the vision concerns the appointed time of the end.

column.name: text
column.value: The two-horned ram that you saw represents the kings of Media and Persia.

column.name: text
column.value: The shaggy goat is the king of Greece, and the large horn between his eyes is the first king.

column.name: text
column.value: The four horns that replaced the one that was broken off represent four kingdoms that will emerge from his nation but will not have the same power.

column.name: text
column.value: "In the latter part of their reign, when rebels have become completely wicked, a stern-faced king, a master of intrigue, will arise.

column.name: text
column.value: He will become very strong, but not by his own power. He will cause astounding devastation and will succeed in whatever he does. He will destroy the mighty men and the holy people.

column.name: text
column.value: He will cause deceit to prosper, and he will consider himself superior. When they feel secure, he will destroy many and take his stand against the Prince of princes. Yet he will be destroyed, but not by human power.

column.name: text
column.value: "The vision of the evenings and mornings that has been given you is true, but seal up the vision, for it concerns the distant future."

column.name: text
column.value: I, Daniel, was exhausted and lay ill for several days. Then I got up and went about the king's business. I was appalled by the vision; it was beyond understanding.

column.name: text
column.value: In the first year of Darius son of Xerxes (a Mede by descent), who was made ruler over the Babylonian kingdom--

column.name: text
column.value: in the first year of his reign, I, Daniel, understood from the Scriptures, according to the word of the LORD given to Jeremiah the prophet, that the desolation of Jerusalem would last seventy years.

column.name: text
column.value: So I turned to the Lord God and pleaded with him in prayer and petition, in fasting, and in sackcloth and ashes.

column.name: text
column.value: I prayed to the LORD my God and confessed: "O Lord, the great and awesome God, who keeps his covenant of love with all who love him and obey his commands,

column.name: text
column.value: we have sinned and done wrong. We have been wicked and have rebelled; we have turned away from your commands and laws.

column.name: text
column.value: We have not listened to your servants the prophets, who spoke in your name to our kings, our princes and our fathers, and to all the people of the land.

column.name: text
column.value: "Lord, you are righteous, but this day we are covered with shame--the men of Judah and people of Jerusalem and all Israel, both near and far, in all the countries where you have scattered us because of our unfaithfulness to you.

column.name: text
column.value: O LORD, we and our kings, our princes and our fathers are covered with shame because we have sinned against you.

column.name: text
column.value: The Lord our God is merciful and forgiving, even though we have rebelled against him;

column.name: text
column.value: we have not obeyed the LORD our God or kept the laws he gave us through his servants the prophets.

column.name: text
column.value: All Israel has transgressed your law and turned away, refusing to obey you. "Therefore the curses and sworn judgments written in the Law of Moses, the servant of God, have been poured out on us, because we have sinned against you.

column.name: text
column.value: You have fulfilled the words spoken against us and against our rulers by bringing upon us great disaster. Under the whole heaven nothing has ever been done like what has been done to Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: Just as it is written in the Law of Moses, all this disaster has come upon us, yet we have not sought the favor of the LORD our God by turning from our sins and giving attention to your truth.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD did not hesitate to bring the disaster upon us, for the LORD our God is righteous in everything he does; yet we have not obeyed him.

column.name: text
column.value: "Now, O Lord our God, who brought your people out of Egypt with a mighty hand and who made for yourself a name that endures to this day, we have sinned, we have done wrong.

column.name: text
column.value: O Lord, in keeping with all your righteous acts, turn away your anger and your wrath from Jerusalem, your city, your holy hill. Our sins and the iniquities of our fathers have made Jerusalem and your people an object of scorn to all those around us.

column.name: text
column.value: "Now, our God, hear the prayers and petitions of your servant. For your sake, O Lord, look with favor on your desolate sanctuary.

column.name: text
column.value: Give ear, O God, and hear; open your eyes and see the desolation of the city that bears your Name. We do not make requests of you because we are righteous, but because of your great mercy.

column.name: text
column.value: O Lord, listen! O Lord, forgive! O Lord, hear and act! For your sake, O my God, do not delay, because your city and your people bear your Name."

column.name: text
column.value: While I was speaking and praying, confessing my sin and the sin of my people Israel and making my request to the LORD my God for his holy hill--

column.name: text
column.value: while I was still in prayer, Gabriel, the man I had seen in the earlier vision, came to me in swift flight about the time of the evening sacrifice.

column.name: text
column.value: He instructed me and said to me, "Daniel, I have now come to give you insight and understanding.

column.name: text
column.value: As soon as you began to pray, an answer was given, which I have come to tell you, for you are highly esteemed. Therefore, consider the message and understand the vision:

column.name: text
column.value: "Seventy 'sevens' are decreed for your people and your holy city to finish transgression, to put an end to sin, to atone for wickedness, to bring in everlasting righteousness, to seal up vision and prophecy and to anoint the most holy.

column.name: text
column.value: "Know and understand this: From the issuing of the decree to restore and rebuild Jerusalem until the Anointed One, the ruler, comes, there will be seven 'sevens,' and sixty-two 'sevens.' It will be rebuilt with streets and a trench, but in times of trouble.

column.name: text
column.value: After the sixty-two 'sevens,' the Anointed One will be cut off and will have nothing. The people of the ruler who will come will destroy the city and the sanctuary. The end will come like a flood: War will continue until the end, and desolations have been decreed.

column.name: text
column.value: He will confirm a covenant with many for one 'seven.' In the middle of the 'seven' he will put an end to sacrifice and offering. And on a wing of the temple he will set up an abomination that causes desolation, until the end that is decreed is poured out on him."

column.name: text
column.value: In the third year of Cyrus king of Persia, a revelation was given to Daniel (who was called Belteshazzar). Its message was true and it concerned a great war. The understanding of the message came to him in a vision.

column.name: text
column.value: At that time I, Daniel, mourned for three weeks.

column.name: text
column.value: I ate no choice food; no meat or wine touched my lips; and I used no lotions at all until the three weeks were over.

column.name: text
column.value: On the twenty-fourth day of the first month, as I was standing on the bank of the great river, the Tigris,

column.name: text
column.value: I looked up and there before me was a man dressed in linen, with a belt of the finest gold around his waist.

column.name: text
column.value: His body was like chrysolite, his face like lightning, his eyes like flaming torches, his arms and legs like the gleam of burnished bronze, and his voice like the sound of a multitude.

column.name: text
column.value: I, Daniel, was the only one who saw the vision; the men with me did not see it, but such terror overwhelmed them that they fled and hid themselves.

column.name: text
column.value: So I was left alone, gazing at this great vision; I had no strength left, my face turned deathly pale and I was helpless.

column.name: text
column.value: Then I heard him speaking, and as I listened to him, I fell into a deep sleep, my face to the ground.

column.name: text
column.value: A hand touched me and set me trembling on my hands and knees.

column.name: text
column.value: He said, "Daniel, you who are highly esteemed, consider carefully the words I am about to speak to you, and stand up, for I have now been sent to you." And when he said this to me, I stood up trembling.

column.name: text
column.value: Then he continued, "Do not be afraid, Daniel. Since the first day that you set your mind to gain understanding and to humble yourself before your God, your words were heard, and I have come in response to them.

column.name: text
column.value: But the prince of the Persian kingdom resisted me twenty-one days. Then Michael, one of the chief princes, came to help me, because I was detained there with the king of Persia.

column.name: text
column.value: Now I have come to explain to you what will happen to your people in the future, for the vision concerns a time yet to come."

column.name: text
column.value: While he was saying this to me, I bowed with my face toward the ground and was speechless.

column.name: text
column.value: Then one who looked like a man touched my lips, and I opened my mouth and began to speak. I said to the one standing before me, "I am overcome with anguish because of the vision, my lord, and I am helpless.

column.name: text
column.value: How can I, your servant, talk with you, my lord? My strength is gone and I can hardly breathe."

column.name: text
column.value: Again the one who looked like a man touched me and gave me strength.

column.name: text
column.value: "Do not be afraid, O man highly esteemed," he said. "Peace! Be strong now; be strong." When he spoke to me, I was strengthened and said, "Speak, my lord, since you have given me strength."

column.name: text
column.value: So he said, "Do you know why I have come to you? Soon I will return to fight against the prince of Persia, and when I go, the prince of Greece will come;

column.name: text
column.value: but first I will tell you what is written in the Book of Truth. (No one supports me against them except Michael, your prince.

column.name: text
column.value: And in the first year of Darius the Mede, I took my stand to support and protect him.)

column.name: text
column.value: "Now then, I tell you the truth: Three more kings will appear in Persia, and then a fourth, who will be far richer than all the others. When he has gained power by his wealth, he will stir up everyone against the kingdom of Greece.

column.name: text
column.value: Then a mighty king will appear, who will rule with great power and do as he pleases.

column.name: text
column.value: After he has appeared, his empire will be broken up and parceled out toward the four winds of heaven. It will not go to his descendants, nor will it have the power he exercised, because his empire will be uprooted and given to others.

column.name: text
column.value: "The king of the South will become strong, but one of his commanders will become even stronger than he and will rule his own kingdom with great power.

column.name: text
column.value: After some years, they will become allies. The daughter of the king of the South will go to the king of the North to make an alliance, but she will not retain her power, and he and his power will not last. In those days she will be handed over, together with her royal escort and her father and the one who supported her.

column.name: text
column.value: "One from her family line will arise to take her place. He will attack the forces of the king of the North and enter his fortress; he will fight against them and be victorious.

column.name: text
column.value: He will also seize their gods, their metal images and their valuable articles of silver and gold and carry them off to Egypt. For some years he will leave the king of the North alone.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the king of the North will invade the realm of the king of the South but will retreat to his own country.

column.name: text
column.value: His sons will prepare for war and assemble a great army, which will sweep on like an irresistible flood and carry the battle as far as his fortress.

column.name: text
column.value: "Then the king of the South will march out in a rage and fight against the king of the North, who will raise a large army, but it will be defeated.

column.name: text
column.value: When the army is carried off, the king of the South will be filled with pride and will slaughter many thousands, yet he will not remain triumphant.

column.name: text
column.value: For the king of the North will muster another army, larger than the first; and after several years, he will advance with a huge army fully equipped.

column.name: text
column.value: "In those times many will rise against the king of the South. The violent men among your own people will rebel in fulfillment of the vision, but without success.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the king of the North will come and build up siege ramps and will capture a fortified city. The forces of the South will be powerless to resist; even their best troops will not have the strength to stand.

column.name: text
column.value: The invader will do as he pleases; no one will be able to stand against him. He will establish himself in the Beautiful Land and will have the power to destroy it.

column.name: text
column.value: He will determine to come with the might of his entire kingdom and will make an alliance with the king of the South. And he will give him a daughter in marriage in order to overthrow the kingdom, but his plans will not succeed or help him.

column.name: text
column.value: Then he will turn his attention to the coastlands and will take many of them, but a commander will put an end to his insolence and will turn his insolence back upon him.

column.name: text
column.value: After this, he will turn back toward the fortresses of his own country but will stumble and fall, to be seen no more.

column.name: text
column.value: "His successor will send out a tax collector to maintain the royal splendor. In a few years, however, he will be destroyed, yet not in anger or in battle.

column.name: text
column.value: "He will be succeeded by a contemptible person who has not been given the honor of royalty. He will invade the kingdom when its people feel secure, and he will seize it through intrigue.

column.name: text
column.value: Then an overwhelming army will be swept away before him; both it and a prince of the covenant will be destroyed.

column.name: text
column.value: After coming to an agreement with him, he will act deceitfully, and with only a few people he will rise to power.

column.name: text
column.value: When the richest provinces feel secure, he will invade them and will achieve what neither his fathers nor his forefathers did. He will distribute plunder, loot and wealth among his followers. He will plot the overthrow of fortresses--but only for a time.

column.name: text
column.value: "With a large army he will stir up his strength and courage against the king of the South. The king of the South will wage war with a large and very powerful army, but he will not be able to stand because of the plots devised against him.

column.name: text
column.value: Those who eat from the king's provisions will try to destroy him; his army will be swept away, and many will fall in battle.

column.name: text
column.value: The two kings, with their hearts bent on evil, will sit at the same table and lie to each other, but to no avail, because an end will still come at the appointed time.

column.name: text
column.value: The king of the North will return to his own country with great wealth, but his heart will be set against the holy covenant. He will take action against it and then return to his own country.

column.name: text
column.value: "At the appointed time he will invade the South again, but this time the outcome will be different from what it was before.

column.name: text
column.value: Ships of the western coastlands will oppose him, and he will lose heart. Then he will turn back and vent his fury against the holy covenant. He will return and show favor to those who forsake the holy covenant.

column.name: text
column.value: "His armed forces will rise up to desecrate the temple fortress and will abolish the daily sacrifice. Then they will set up the abomination that causes desolation.

column.name: text
column.value: With flattery he will corrupt those who have violated the covenant, but the people who know their God will firmly resist him.

column.name: text
column.value: "Those who are wise will instruct many, though for a time they will fall by the sword or be burned or captured or plundered.

column.name: text
column.value: When they fall, they will receive a little help, and many who are not sincere will join them.

column.name: text
column.value: Some of the wise will stumble, so that they may be refined, purified and made spotless until the time of the end, for it will still come at the appointed time.

column.name: text
column.value: "The king will do as he pleases. He will exalt and magnify himself above every god and will say unheard-of things against the God of gods. He will be successful until the time of wrath is completed, for what has been determined must take place.

column.name: text
column.value: He will show no regard for the gods of his fathers or for the one desired by women, nor will he regard any god, but will exalt himself above them all.

column.name: text
column.value: Instead of them, he will honor a god of fortresses; a god unknown to his fathers he will honor with gold and silver, with precious stones and costly gifts.

column.name: text
column.value: He will attack the mightiest fortresses with the help of a foreign god and will greatly honor those who acknowledge him. He will make them rulers over many people and will distribute the land at a price.

column.name: text
column.value: "At the time of the end the king of the South will engage him in battle, and the king of the North will storm out against him with chariots and cavalry and a great fleet of ships. He will invade many countries and sweep through them like a flood.

column.name: text
column.value: He will also invade the Beautiful Land. Many countries will fall, but Edom, Moab and the leaders of Ammon will be delivered from his hand.

column.name: text
column.value: He will extend his power over many countries; Egypt will not escape.

column.name: text
column.value: He will gain control of the treasures of gold and silver and all the riches of Egypt, with the Libyans and Nubians in submission.

column.name: text
column.value: But reports from the east and the north will alarm him, and he will set out in a great rage to destroy and annihilate many.

column.name: text
column.value: He will pitch his royal tents between the seas at the beautiful holy mountain. Yet he will come to his end, and no one will help him.

column.name: text
column.value: "At that time Michael, the great prince who protects your people, will arise. There will be a time of distress such as has not happened from the beginning of nations until then. But at that time your people--everyone whose name is found written in the book--will be delivered.

column.name: text
column.value: Multitudes who sleep in the dust of the earth will awake: some to everlasting life, others to shame and everlasting contempt.

column.name: text
column.value: Those who are wise will shine like the brightness of the heavens, and those who lead many to righteousness, like the stars for ever and ever.

column.name: text
column.value: But you, Daniel, close up and seal the words of the scroll until the time of the end. Many will go here and there to increase knowledge."

column.name: text
column.value: Then I, Daniel, looked, and there before me stood two others, one on this bank of the river and one on the opposite bank.

column.name: text
column.value: One of them said to the man clothed in linen, who was above the waters of the river, "How long will it be before these astonishing things are fulfilled?"

column.name: text
column.value: The man clothed in linen, who was above the waters of the river, lifted his right hand and his left hand toward heaven, and I heard him swear by him who lives forever, saying, "It will be for a time, times and half a time. When the power of the holy people has been finally broken, all these things will be completed."

column.name: text
column.value: I heard, but I did not understand. So I asked, "My lord, what will the outcome of all this be?"

column.name: text
column.value: He replied, "Go your way, Daniel, because the words are closed up and sealed until the time of the end.

column.name: text
column.value: Many will be purified, made spotless and refined, but the wicked will continue to be wicked. None of the wicked will understand, but those who are wise will understand.

column.name: text
column.value: "From the time that the daily sacrifice is abolished and the abomination that causes desolation is set up, there will be 1,290 days.

column.name: text
column.value: Blessed is the one who waits for and reaches the end of the 1,335 days.

column.name: text
column.value: "As for you, go your way till the end. You will rest, and then at the end of the days you will rise to receive your allotted inheritance."

column.name: text
column.value: "Say of your brothers, 'My people,' and of your sisters, 'My loved one.'

column.name: text
column.value: "Rebuke your mother, rebuke her, for she is not my wife, and I am not her husband. Let her remove the adulterous look from her face and the unfaithfulness from between her breasts.

column.name: text
column.value: Otherwise I will strip her naked and make her as bare as on the day she was born; I will make her like a desert, turn her into a parched land, and slay her with thirst.

column.name: text
column.value: I will not show my love to her children, because they are the children of adultery.

column.name: text
column.value: Their mother has been unfaithful and has conceived them in disgrace. She said, 'I will go after my lovers, who give me my food and my water, my wool and my linen, my oil and my drink.'

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore I will block her path with thornbushes; I will wall her in so that she cannot find her way.

column.name: text
column.value: She will chase after her lovers but not catch them; she will look for them but not find them. Then she will say, 'I will go back to my husband as at first, for then I was better off than now.'

column.name: text
column.value: She has not acknowledged that I was the one who gave her the grain, the new wine and oil, who lavished on her the silver and gold--which they used for Baal.

column.name: text
column.value: "Therefore I will take away my grain when it ripens, and my new wine when it is ready. I will take back my wool and my linen, intended to cover her nakedness.

column.name: text
column.value: So now I will expose her lewdness before the eyes of her lovers; no one will take her out of my hands.

column.name: text
column.value: I will stop all her celebrations: her yearly festivals, her New Moons, her Sabbath days--all her appointed feasts.

column.name: text
column.value: I will ruin her vines and her fig trees, which she said were her pay from her lovers; I will make them a thicket, and wild animals will devour them.

column.name: text
column.value: I will punish her for the days she burned incense to the Baals; she decked herself with rings and jewelry, and went after her lovers, but me she forgot," declares the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: "Therefore I am now going to allure her; I will lead her into the desert and speak tenderly to her.

column.name: text
column.value: There I will give her back her vineyards, and will make the Valley of Achor a door of hope. There she will sing as in the days of her youth, as in the day she came up out of Egypt.

column.name: text
column.value: "In that day," declares the LORD, "you will call me 'my husband'; you will no longer call me 'my master.'

column.name: text
column.value: I will remove the names of the Baals from her lips; no longer will their names be invoked.

column.name: text
column.value: In that day I will make a covenant for them with the beasts of the field and the birds of the air and the creatures that move along the ground. Bow and sword and battle I will abolish from the land, so that all may lie down in safety.

column.name: text
column.value: I will betroth you to me forever; I will betroth you in righteousness and justice, in love and compassion.

column.name: text
column.value: I will betroth you in faithfulness, and you will acknowledge the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: "In that day I will respond," declares the LORD--"I will respond to the skies, and they will respond to the earth;

column.name: text
column.value: and the earth will respond to the grain, the new wine and oil, and they will respond to Jezreel.

column.name: text
column.value: I will plant her for myself in the land; I will show my love to the one I called 'Not my loved one.' I will say to those called 'Not my people,' 'You are my people'; and they will say, 'You are my God.'"

column.name: text
column.value: The word of the LORD that came to Hosea son of Beeri during the reigns of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz and Hezekiah, kings of Judah, and during the reign of Jeroboam son of Jehoash king of Israel:

column.name: text
column.value: When the LORD began to speak through Hosea, the LORD said to him, "Go, take to yourself an adulterous wife and children of unfaithfulness, because the land is guilty of the vilest adultery in departing from the LORD."

column.name: text
column.value: So he married Gomer daughter of Diblaim, and she conceived and bore him a son.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD said to Hosea, "Call him Jezreel, because I will soon punish the house of Jehu for the massacre at Jezreel, and I will put an end to the kingdom of Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: In that day I will break Israel's bow in the Valley of Jezreel."

column.name: text
column.value: Gomer conceived again and gave birth to a daughter. Then the LORD said to Hosea, "Call her Lo-Ruhamah, for I will no longer show love to the house of Israel, that I should at all forgive them.

column.name: text
column.value: Yet I will show love to the house of Judah; and I will save them--not by bow, sword or battle, or by horses and horsemen, but by the LORD their God."

column.name: text
column.value: After she had weaned Lo-Ruhamah, Gomer had another son.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD said, "Call him Lo-Ammi, for you are not my people, and I am not your God.

column.name: text
column.value: "Yet the Israelites will be like the sand on the seashore, which cannot be measured or counted. In the place where it was said to them, 'You are not my people,' they will be called 'sons of the living God.'

column.name: text
column.value: The people of Judah and the people of Israel will be reunited, and they will appoint one leader and will come up out of the land, for great will be the day of Jezreel.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD said to me, "Go, show your love to your wife again, though she is loved by another and is an adulteress. Love her as the LORD loves the Israelites, though they turn to other gods and love the sacred raisin cakes."

column.name: text
column.value: So I bought her for fifteen shekels of silver and about a homer and a lethek of barley.

column.name: text
column.value: Then I told her, "You are to live with me many days; you must not be a prostitute or be intimate with any man, and I will live with you."

column.name: text
column.value: For the Israelites will live many days without king or prince, without sacrifice or sacred stones, without ephod or idol.

column.name: text
column.value: Afterward the Israelites will return and seek the LORD their God and David their king. They will come trembling to the LORD and to his blessings in the last days.

column.name: text
column.value: Hear the word of the LORD, you Israelites, because the LORD has a charge to bring against you who live in the land: "There is no faithfulness, no love, no acknowledgment of God in the land.

column.name: text
column.value: There is only cursing, lying and murder, stealing and adultery; they break all bounds, and bloodshed follows bloodshed.

column.name: text
column.value: Because of this the land mourns, and all who live in it waste away; the beasts of the field and the birds of the air and the fish of the sea are dying.

column.name: text
column.value: "But let no man bring a charge, let no man accuse another, for your people are like those who bring charges against a priest.

column.name: text
column.value: You stumble day and night, and the prophets stumble with you. So I will destroy your mother--

column.name: text
column.value: my people are destroyed from lack of knowledge. "Because you have rejected knowledge, I also reject you as my priests; because you have ignored the law of your God, I also will ignore your children.

column.name: text
column.value: The more the priests increased, the more they sinned against me; they exchanged their Glory for something disgraceful.

column.name: text
column.value: They feed on the sins of my people and relish their wickedness.

column.name: text
column.value: And it will be: Like people, like priests. I will punish both of them for their ways and repay them for their deeds.

column.name: text
column.value: "They will eat but not have enough; they will engage in prostitution but not increase, because they have deserted the LORD to give themselves

column.name: text
column.value: to prostitution, to old wine and new, which take away the understanding

column.name: text
column.value: of my people. They consult a wooden idol and are answered by a stick of wood. A spirit of prostitution leads them astray; they are unfaithful to their God.

column.name: text
column.value: They sacrifice on the mountaintops and burn offerings on the hills, under oak, poplar and terebinth, where the shade is pleasant. Therefore your daughters turn to prostitution and your daughters-in-law to adultery.

column.name: text
column.value: "I will not punish your daughters when they turn to prostitution, nor your daughters-in-law when they commit adultery, because the men themselves consort with harlots and sacrifice with shrine prostitutes--a people without understanding will come to ruin!

column.name: text
column.value: "Though you commit adultery, O Israel, let not Judah become guilty. "Do not go to Gilgal; do not go up to Beth Aven. And do not swear, 'As surely as the LORD lives!'

column.name: text
column.value: The Israelites are stubborn, like a stubborn heifer. How then can the LORD pasture them like lambs in a meadow?

column.name: text
column.value: Ephraim is joined to idols; leave him alone!

column.name: text
column.value: Even when their drinks are gone, they continue their prostitution; their rulers dearly love shameful ways.

column.name: text
