column.value: The whole Judean countryside and all the people of Jerusalem went out to him. Confessing their sins, they were baptized by him in the Jordan River.

column.name: text
column.value: John wore clothing made of camel's hair, with a leather belt around his waist, and he ate locusts and wild honey.

column.name: text
column.value: And this was his message: "After me will come one more powerful than I, the thongs of whose sandals I am not worthy to stoop down and untie.

column.name: text
column.value: I baptize you with water, but he will baptize you with the Holy Spirit."

column.name: text
column.value: At that time Jesus came from Nazareth in Galilee and was baptized by John in the Jordan.

column.name: text
column.value: As Jesus was coming up out of the water, he saw heaven being torn open and the Spirit descending on him like a dove.

column.name: text
column.value: And a voice came from heaven: "You are my Son, whom I love; with you I am well pleased."

column.name: text
column.value: At once the Spirit sent him out into the desert,

column.name: text
column.value: and he was in the desert forty days, being tempted by Satan. He was with the wild animals, and angels attended him.

column.name: text
column.value: After John was put in prison, Jesus went into Galilee, proclaiming the good news of God.

column.name: text
column.value: "The time has come," he said. "The kingdom of God is near. Repent and believe the good news!"

column.name: text
column.value: As Jesus walked beside the Sea of Galilee, he saw Simon and his brother Andrew casting a net into the lake, for they were fishermen.

column.name: text
column.value: "Come, follow me," Jesus said, "and I will make you fishers of men."

column.name: text
column.value: At once they left their nets and followed him.

column.name: text
column.value: When he had gone a little farther, he saw James son of Zebedee and his brother John in a boat, preparing their nets.

column.name: text
column.value: Without delay he called them, and they left their father Zebedee in the boat with the hired men and followed him.

column.name: text
column.value: They went to Capernaum, and when the Sabbath came, Jesus went into the synagogue and began to teach.

column.name: text
column.value: The people were amazed at his teaching, because he taught them as one who had authority, not as the teachers of the law.

column.name: text
column.value: Just then a man in their synagogue who was possessed by an evil spirit cried out,

column.name: text
column.value: "What do you want with us, Jesus of Nazareth? Have you come to destroy us? I know who you are--the Holy One of God!"

column.name: text
column.value: "Be quiet!" said Jesus sternly. "Come out of him!"

column.name: text
column.value: The evil spirit shook the man violently and came out of him with a shriek.

column.name: text
column.value: The people were all so amazed that they asked each other, "What is this? A new teaching--and with authority! He even gives orders to evil spirits and they obey him."

column.name: text
column.value: News about him spread quickly over the whole region of Galilee.

column.name: text
column.value: As soon as they left the synagogue, they went with James and John to the home of Simon and Andrew.

column.name: text
column.value: Simon's mother-in-law was in bed with a fever, and they told Jesus about her.

column.name: text
column.value: So he went to her, took her hand and helped her up. The fever left her and she began to wait on them.

column.name: text
column.value: That evening after sunset the people brought to Jesus all the sick and demon-possessed.

column.name: text
column.value: The whole town gathered at the door,

column.name: text
column.value: and Jesus healed many who had various diseases. He also drove out many demons, but he would not let the demons speak because they knew who he was.

column.name: text
column.value: Very early in the morning, while it was still dark, Jesus got up, left the house and went off to a solitary place, where he prayed.

column.name: text
column.value: Simon and his companions went to look for him,

column.name: text
column.value: and when they found him, they exclaimed: "Everyone is looking for you!"

column.name: text
column.value: Jesus replied, "Let us go somewhere else--to the nearby villages--so I can preach there also. That is why I have come."

column.name: text
column.value: So he traveled throughout Galilee, preaching in their synagogues and driving out demons.

column.name: text
column.value: A man with leprosy came to him and begged him on his knees, "If you are willing, you can make me clean."

column.name: text
column.value: Filled with compassion, Jesus reached out his hand and touched the man. "I am willing," he said. "Be clean!"

column.name: text
column.value: Immediately the leprosy left him and he was cured.

column.name: text
column.value: Jesus sent him away at once with a strong warning:

column.name: text
column.value: "See that you don't tell this to anyone. But go, show yourself to the priest and offer the sacrifices that Moses commanded for your cleansing, as a testimony to them."

column.name: text
column.value: Instead he went out and began to talk freely, spreading the news. As a result, Jesus could no longer enter a town openly but stayed outside in lonely places. Yet the people still came to him from everywhere.

column.name: text
column.value: Another time he went into the synagogue, and a man with a shriveled hand was there.

column.name: text
column.value: Some of them were looking for a reason to accuse Jesus, so they watched him closely to see if he would heal him on the Sabbath.

column.name: text
column.value: Jesus said to the man with the shriveled hand, "Stand up in front of everyone."

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jesus asked them, "Which is lawful on the Sabbath: to do good or to do evil, to save life or to kill?" But they remained silent.

column.name: text
column.value: He looked around at them in anger and, deeply distressed at their stubborn hearts, said to the man, "Stretch out your hand." He stretched it out, and his hand was completely restored.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the Pharisees went out and began to plot with the Herodians how they might kill Jesus.

column.name: text
column.value: Jesus withdrew with his disciples to the lake, and a large crowd from Galilee followed.

column.name: text
column.value: When they heard all he was doing, many people came to him from Judea, Jerusalem, Idumea, and the regions across the Jordan and around Tyre and Sidon.

column.name: text
column.value: Because of the crowd he told his disciples to have a small boat ready for him, to keep the people from crowding him.

column.name: text
column.value: For he had healed many, so that those with diseases were pushing forward to touch him.

column.name: text
column.value: Whenever the evil spirits saw him, they fell down before him and cried out, "You are the Son of God."

column.name: text
column.value: But he gave them strict orders not to tell who he was.

column.name: text
column.value: Jesus went up on a mountainside and called to him those he wanted, and they came to him.

column.name: text
column.value: He appointed twelve--designating them apostles--that they might be with him and that he might send them out to preach

column.name: text
column.value: and to have authority to drive out demons.

column.name: text
column.value: These are the twelve he appointed: Simon (to whom he gave the name Peter);

column.name: text
column.value: James son of Zebedee and his brother John (to them he gave the name Boanerges, which means Sons of Thunder);

column.name: text
column.value: Andrew, Philip, Bartholomew, Matthew, Thomas, James son of Alphaeus, Thaddaeus, Simon the Zealot

column.name: text
column.value: and Judas Iscariot, who betrayed him.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jesus entered a house, and again a crowd gathered, so that he and his disciples were not even able to eat.

column.name: text
column.value: When his family heard about this, they went to take charge of him, for they said, "He is out of his mind."

column.name: text
column.value: And the teachers of the law who came down from Jerusalem said, "He is possessed by Beelzebub! By the prince of demons he is driving out demons."

column.name: text
column.value: So Jesus called them and spoke to them in parables: "How can Satan drive out Satan?

column.name: text
column.value: If a kingdom is divided against itself, that kingdom cannot stand.

column.name: text
column.value: If a house is divided against itself, that house cannot stand.

column.name: text
column.value: And if Satan opposes himself and is divided, he cannot stand; his end has come.

column.name: text
column.value: In fact, no one can enter a strong man's house and carry off his possessions unless he first ties up the strong man. Then he can rob his house.

column.name: text
column.value: I tell you the truth, all the sins and blasphemies of men will be forgiven them.

column.name: text
column.value: But whoever blasphemes against the Holy Spirit will never be forgiven; he is guilty of an eternal sin."

column.name: text
column.value: He said this because they were saying, "He has an evil spirit."

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jesus' mother and brothers arrived. Standing outside, they sent someone in to call him.

column.name: text
column.value: A crowd was sitting around him, and they told him, "Your mother and brothers are outside looking for you."

column.name: text
column.value: "Who are my mother and my brothers?" he asked.

column.name: text
column.value: Then he looked at those seated in a circle around him and said, "Here are my mother and my brothers!

column.name: text
column.value: Whoever does God's will is my brother and sister and mother."

column.name: text
column.value: Again Jesus began to teach by the lake. The crowd that gathered around him was so large that he got into a boat and sat in it out on the lake, while all the people were along the shore at the water's edge.

column.name: text
column.value: He taught them many things by parables, and in his teaching said:

column.name: text
column.value: "Listen! A farmer went out to sow his seed.

column.name: text
column.value: As he was scattering the seed, some fell along the path, and the birds came and ate it up.

column.name: text
column.value: Some fell on rocky places, where it did not have much soil. It sprang up quickly, because the soil was shallow.

column.name: text
column.value: But when the sun came up, the plants were scorched, and they withered because they had no root.

column.name: text
column.value: Other seed fell among thorns, which grew up and choked the plants, so that they did not bear grain.

column.name: text
column.value: Still other seed fell on good soil. It came up, grew and produced a crop, multiplying thirty, sixty, or even a hundred times."

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jesus said, "He who has ears to hear, let him hear."

column.name: text
column.value: When he was alone, the Twelve and the others around him asked him about the parables.

column.name: text
column.value: He told them, "The secret of the kingdom of God has been given to you. But to those on the outside everything is said in parables

column.name: text
column.value: so that, "'they may be ever seeing but never perceiving, and ever hearing but never understanding; otherwise they might turn and be forgiven!'"

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jesus said to them, "Don't you understand this parable? How then will you understand any parable?

column.name: text
column.value: The farmer sows the word.

column.name: text
column.value: Some people are like seed along the path, where the word is sown. As soon as they hear it, Satan comes and takes away the word that was sown in them.

column.name: text
column.value: Others, like seed sown on rocky places, hear the word and at once receive it with joy.

column.name: text
column.value: But since they have no root, they last only a short time. When trouble or persecution comes because of the word, they quickly fall away.

column.name: text
column.value: Still others, like seed sown among thorns, hear the word;

column.name: text
column.value: but the worries of this life, the deceitfulness of wealth and the desires for other things come in and choke the word, making it unfruitful.

column.name: text
column.value: Others, like seed sown on good soil, hear the word, accept it, and produce a crop--thirty, sixty or even a hundred times what was sown."

column.name: text
column.value: He said to them, "Do you bring in a lamp to put it under a bowl or a bed? Instead, don't you put it on its stand?

column.name: text
column.value: For whatever is hidden is meant to be disclosed, and whatever is concealed is meant to be brought out into the open.

column.name: text
column.value: If anyone has ears to hear, let him hear."

column.name: text
column.value: "Consider carefully what you hear," he continued. "With the measure you use, it will be measured to you--and even more.

column.name: text
column.value: Whoever has will be given more; whoever does not have, even what he has will be taken from him."

column.name: text
column.value: He also said, "This is what the kingdom of God is like. A man scatters seed on the ground.

column.name: text
column.value: Night and day, whether he sleeps or gets up, the seed sprouts and grows, though he does not know how.

column.name: text
column.value: All by itself the soil produces grain--first the stalk, then the head, then the full kernel in the head.

column.name: text
column.value: As soon as the grain is ripe, he puts the sickle to it, because the harvest has come."

column.name: text
column.value: Again he said, "What shall we say the kingdom of God is like, or what parable shall we use to describe it?

column.name: text
column.value: It is like a mustard seed, which is the smallest seed you plant in the ground.

column.name: text
column.value: Yet when planted, it grows and becomes the largest of all garden plants, with such big branches that the birds of the air can perch in its shade."

column.name: text
column.value: With many similar parables Jesus spoke the word to them, as much as they could understand.

column.name: text
column.value: He did not say anything to them without using a parable. But when he was alone with his own disciples, he explained everything.

column.name: text
column.value: That day when evening came, he said to his disciples, "Let us go over to the other side."

column.name: text
column.value: Leaving the crowd behind, they took him along, just as he was, in the boat. There were also other boats with him.

column.name: text
column.value: A furious squall came up, and the waves broke over the boat, so that it was nearly swamped.

column.name: text
column.value: Jesus was in the stern, sleeping on a cushion. The disciples woke him and said to him, "Teacher, don't you care if we drown?"

column.name: text
column.value: He got up, rebuked the wind and said to the waves, "Quiet! Be still!" Then the wind died down and it was completely calm.

column.name: text
column.value: He said to his disciples, "Why are you so afraid? Do you still have no faith?"

column.name: text
column.value: They were terrified and asked each other, "Who is this? Even the wind and the waves obey him!"

column.name: text
column.value: They went across the lake to the region of the Gerasenes.

column.name: text
column.value: When Jesus got out of the boat, a man with an evil spirit came from the tombs to meet him.

column.name: text
column.value: This man lived in the tombs, and no one could bind him any more, not even with a chain.

column.name: text
column.value: For he had often been chained hand and foot, but he tore the chains apart and broke the irons on his feet. No one was strong enough to subdue him.

column.name: text
column.value: Night and day among the tombs and in the hills he would cry out and cut himself with stones.

column.name: text
column.value: When he saw Jesus from a distance, he ran and fell on his knees in front of him.

column.name: text
column.value: He shouted at the top of his voice, "What do you want with me, Jesus, Son of the Most High God? Swear to God that you won't torture me!"

column.name: text
column.value: For Jesus had said to him, "Come out of this man, you evil spirit!"

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jesus asked him, "What is your name?" "My name is Legion," he replied, "for we are many."

column.name: text
column.value: And he begged Jesus again and again not to send them out of the area.

column.name: text
column.value: A large herd of pigs was feeding on the nearby hillside.

column.name: text
column.value: The demons begged Jesus, "Send us among the pigs; allow us to go into them."

column.name: text
column.value: He gave them permission, and the evil spirits came out and went into the pigs. The herd, about two thousand in number, rushed down the steep bank into the lake and were drowned.

column.name: text
column.value: Those tending the pigs ran off and reported this in the town and countryside, and the people went out to see what had happened.

column.name: text
column.value: When they came to Jesus, they saw the man who had been possessed by the legion of demons, sitting there, dressed and in his right mind; and they were afraid.

column.name: text
column.value: Those who had seen it told the people what had happened to the demon-possessed man--and told about the pigs as well.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the people began to plead with Jesus to leave their region.

column.name: text
column.value: As Jesus was getting into the boat, the man who had been demon-possessed begged to go with him.

column.name: text
column.value: Jesus did not let him, but said, "Go home to your family and tell them how much the Lord has done for you, and how he has had mercy on you."

column.name: text
column.value: So the man went away and began to tell in the Decapolis how much Jesus had done for him. And all the people were amazed.

column.name: text
column.value: When Jesus had again crossed over by boat to the other side of the lake, a large crowd gathered around him while he was by the lake.

column.name: text
column.value: Then one of the synagogue rulers, named Jairus, came there. Seeing Jesus, he fell at his feet

column.name: text
column.value: and pleaded earnestly with him, "My little daughter is dying. Please come and put your hands on her so that she will be healed and live."

column.name: text
column.value: So Jesus went with him. A large crowd followed and pressed around him.

column.name: text
column.value: And a woman was there who had been subject to bleeding for twelve years.

column.name: text
column.value: She had suffered a great deal under the care of many doctors and had spent all she had, yet instead of getting better she grew worse.

column.name: text
column.value: When she heard about Jesus, she came up behind him in the crowd and touched his cloak,

column.name: text
column.value: because she thought, "If I just touch his clothes, I will be healed."

column.name: text
column.value: Immediately her bleeding stopped and she felt in her body that she was freed from her suffering.

column.name: text
column.value: At once Jesus realized that power had gone out from him. He turned around in the crowd and asked, "Who touched my clothes?"

column.name: text
column.value: "You see the people crowding against you," his disciples answered, "and yet you can ask, 'Who touched me?'"

column.name: text
column.value: But Jesus kept looking around to see who had done it.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the woman, knowing what had happened to her, came and fell at his feet and, trembling with fear, told him the whole truth.

column.name: text
column.value: He said to her, "Daughter, your faith has healed you. Go in peace and be freed from your suffering."

column.name: text
column.value: While Jesus was still speaking, some men came from the house of Jairus, the synagogue ruler. "Your daughter is dead," they said. "Why bother the teacher any more?"

column.name: text
column.value: Ignoring what they said, Jesus told the synagogue ruler, "Don't be afraid; just believe."

column.name: text
column.value: He did not let anyone follow him except Peter, James and John the brother of James.

column.name: text
column.value: When they came to the home of the synagogue ruler, Jesus saw a commotion, with people crying and wailing loudly.

column.name: text
column.value: He went in and said to them, "Why all this commotion and wailing? The child is not dead but asleep."

column.name: text
column.value: But they laughed at him. After he put them all out, he took the child's father and mother and the disciples who were with him, and went in where the child was.

column.name: text
column.value: He took her by the hand and said to her, "Talitha koum!" (which means, "Little girl, I say to you, get up!").

column.name: text
column.value: Immediately the girl stood up and walked around (she was twelve years old). At this they were completely astonished.

column.name: text
column.value: He gave strict orders not to let anyone know about this, and told them to give her something to eat.

column.name: text
column.value: Jesus left there and went to his hometown, accompanied by his disciples.

column.name: text
column.value: When the Sabbath came, he began to teach in the synagogue, and many who heard him were amazed. "Where did this man get these things?" they asked. "What's this wisdom that has been given him, that he even does miracles!

column.name: text
column.value: Isn't this the carpenter? Isn't this Mary's son and the brother of James, Joseph, Judas and Simon? Aren't his sisters here with us?" And they took offense at him.

column.name: text
column.value: Jesus said to them, "Only in his hometown, among his relatives and in his own house is a prophet without honor."

column.name: text
column.value: He could not do any miracles there, except lay his hands on a few sick people and heal them.

column.name: text
column.value: And he was amazed at their lack of faith. Then Jesus went around teaching from village to village.

column.name: text
column.value: Calling the Twelve to him, he sent them out two by two and gave them authority over evil spirits.

column.name: text
column.value: These were his instructions: "Take nothing for the journey except a staff--no bread, no bag, no money in your belts.

column.name: text
column.value: Wear sandals but not an extra tunic.

column.name: text
column.value: Whenever you enter a house, stay there until you leave that town.

column.name: text
column.value: And if any place will not welcome you or listen to you, shake the dust off your feet when you leave, as a testimony against them."

column.name: text
column.value: They went out and preached that people should repent.

column.name: text
column.value: They drove out many demons and anointed many sick people with oil and healed them.

column.name: text
column.value: King Herod heard about this, for Jesus' name had become well known. Some were saying, "John the Baptist has been raised from the dead, and that is why miraculous powers are at work in him."

column.name: text
column.value: Others said, "He is Elijah." And still others claimed, "He is a prophet, like one of the prophets of long ago."

column.name: text
column.value: But when Herod heard this, he said, "John, the man I beheaded, has been raised from the dead!"

column.name: text
column.value: For Herod himself had given orders to have John arrested, and he had him bound and put in prison. He did this because of Herodias, his brother Philip's wife, whom he had married.

column.name: text
column.value: For John had been saying to Herod, "It is not lawful for you to have your brother's wife."

column.name: text
column.value: So Herodias nursed a grudge against John and wanted to kill him. But she was not able to,

column.name: text
column.value: because Herod feared John and protected him, knowing him to be a righteous and holy man. When Herod heard John, he was greatly puzzled; yet he liked to listen to him.

column.name: text
column.value: Finally the opportune time came. On his birthday Herod gave a banquet for his high officials and military commanders and the leading men of Galilee.

column.name: text
column.value: When the daughter of Herodias came in and danced, she pleased Herod and his dinner guests. The king said to the girl, "Ask me for anything you want, and I'll give it to you."

column.name: text
column.value: And he promised her with an oath, "Whatever you ask I will give you, up to half my kingdom."

column.name: text
column.value: She went out and said to her mother, "What shall I ask for?" "The head of John the Baptist," she answered.

column.name: text
column.value: At once the girl hurried in to the king with the request: "I want you to give me right now the head of John the Baptist on a platter."

column.name: text
column.value: The king was greatly distressed, but because of his oaths and his dinner guests, he did not want to refuse her.

column.name: text
column.value: So he immediately sent an executioner with orders to bring John's head. The man went, beheaded John in the prison,

column.name: text
column.value: and brought back his head on a platter. He presented it to the girl, and she gave it to her mother.

column.name: text
column.value: On hearing of this, John's disciples came and took his body and laid it in a tomb.

column.name: text
column.value: The apostles gathered around Jesus and reported to him all they had done and taught.

column.name: text
column.value: Then, because so many people were coming and going that they did not even have a chance to eat, he said to them, "Come with me by yourselves to a quiet place and get some rest."

column.name: text
column.value: So they went away by themselves in a boat to a solitary place.

column.name: text
column.value: But many who saw them leaving recognized them and ran on foot from all the towns and got there ahead of them.

column.name: text
column.value: When Jesus landed and saw a large crowd, he had compassion on them, because they were like sheep without a shepherd. So he began teaching them many things.

column.name: text
column.value: By this time it was late in the day, so his disciples came to him. "This is a remote place," they said, "and it's already very late.

column.name: text
column.value: Send the people away so they can go to the surrounding countryside and villages and buy themselves something to eat."

column.name: text
column.value: But he answered, "You give them something to eat." They said to him, "That would take eight months of a man's wages! Are we to go and spend that much on bread and give it to them to eat?"

column.name: text
column.value: "How many loaves do you have?" he asked. "Go and see." When they found out, they said, "Five--and two fish."

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jesus directed them to have all the people sit down in groups on the green grass.

column.name: text
column.value: So they sat down in groups of hundreds and fifties.

column.name: text
column.value: Taking the five loaves and the two fish and looking up to heaven, he gave thanks and broke the loaves. Then he gave them to his disciples to set before the people. He also divided the two fish among them all.

column.name: text
column.value: They all ate and were satisfied,

column.name: text
column.value: and the disciples picked up twelve basketfuls of broken pieces of bread and fish.

column.name: text
column.value: The number of the men who had eaten was five thousand.

column.name: text
column.value: Immediately Jesus made his disciples get into the boat and go on ahead of him to Bethsaida, while he dismissed the crowd.

column.name: text
column.value: After leaving them, he went up on a mountainside to pray.

column.name: text
column.value: When evening came, the boat was in the middle of the lake, and he was alone on land.

column.name: text
column.value: He saw the disciples straining at the oars, because the wind was against them. About the fourth watch of the night he went out to them, walking on the lake. He was about to pass by them,

column.name: text
column.value: but when they saw him walking on the lake, they thought he was a ghost. They cried out,

column.name: text
column.value: because they all saw him and were terrified. Immediately he spoke to them and said, "Take courage! It is I. Don't be afraid."

column.name: text
column.value: Then he climbed into the boat with them, and the wind died down. They were completely amazed,

column.name: text
column.value: for they had not understood about the loaves; their hearts were hardened.

column.name: text
column.value: When they had crossed over, they landed at Gennesaret and anchored there.

column.name: text
column.value: As soon as they got out of the boat, people recognized Jesus.

column.name: text
column.value: They ran throughout that whole region and carried the sick on mats to wherever they heard he was.

column.name: text
column.value: And wherever he went--into villages, towns or countryside--they placed the sick in the marketplaces. They begged him to let them touch even the edge of his cloak, and all who touched him were healed.

column.name: text
column.value: The Pharisees and some of the teachers of the law who had come from Jerusalem gathered around Jesus and

column.name: text
column.value: saw some of his disciples eating food with hands that were "unclean," that is, unwashed.

column.name: text
column.value: (The Pharisees and all the Jews do not eat unless they give their hands a ceremonial washing, holding to the tradition of the elders.

column.name: text
column.value: When they come from the marketplace they do not eat unless they wash. And they observe many other traditions, such as the washing of cups, pitchers and kettles.)

column.name: text
column.value: So the Pharisees and teachers of the law asked Jesus, "Why don't your disciples live according to the tradition of the elders instead of eating their food with 'unclean' hands?"

column.name: text
column.value: He replied, "Isaiah was right when he prophesied about you hypocrites; as it is written: "'These people honor me with their lips, but their hearts are far from me.

column.name: text
column.value: They worship me in vain; their teachings are but rules taught by men.'

column.name: text
column.value: You have let go of the commands of God and are holding on to the traditions of men."

column.name: text
column.value: And he said to them: "You have a fine way of setting aside the commands of God in order to observe your own traditions!

column.name: text
column.value: For Moses said, 'Honor your father and your mother,' and, 'Anyone who curses his father or mother must be put to death.'

column.name: text
column.value: But you say that if a man says to his father or mother: 'Whatever help you might otherwise have received from me is Corban' (that is, a gift devoted to God),

column.name: text
column.value: then you no longer let him do anything for his father or mother.

column.name: text
column.value: Thus you nullify the word of God by your tradition that you have handed down. And you do many things like that."

column.name: text
column.value: Again Jesus called the crowd to him and said, "Listen to me, everyone, and understand this.

column.name: text
column.value: Nothing outside a man can make him 'unclean' by going into him. Rather, it is what comes out of a man that makes him 'unclean.'"

column.name: text
column.value: After he had left the crowd and entered the house, his disciples asked him about this parable.

column.name: text
column.value: "Are you so dull?" he asked. "Don't you see that nothing that enters a man from the outside can make him 'unclean'?

column.name: text
column.value: For it doesn't go into his heart but into his stomach, and then out of his body." (In saying this, Jesus declared all foods "clean.")

column.name: text
column.value: He went on: "What comes out of a man is what makes him 'unclean.'

column.name: text
column.value: For from within, out of men's hearts, come evil thoughts, sexual immorality, theft, murder, adultery,

column.name: text
column.value: greed, malice, deceit, lewdness, envy, slander, arrogance and folly.

column.name: text
column.value: All these evils come from inside and make a man 'unclean.'"

column.name: text
column.value: Jesus left that place and went to the vicinity of Tyre. He entered a house and did not want anyone to know it; yet he could not keep his presence secret.

column.name: text
column.value: In fact, as soon as she heard about him, a woman whose little daughter was possessed by an evil spirit came and fell at his feet.

column.name: text
column.value: The woman was a Greek, born in Syrian Phoenicia. She begged Jesus to drive the demon out of her daughter.

column.name: text
column.value: "First let the children eat all they want," he told her, "for it is not right to take the children's bread and toss it to their dogs."

column.name: text
column.value: "Yes, Lord," she replied, "but even the dogs under the table eat the children's crumbs."

column.name: text
column.value: Then he told her, "For such a reply, you may go; the demon has left your daughter."

column.name: text
column.value: She went home and found her child lying on the bed, and the demon gone.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jesus left the vicinity of Tyre and went through Sidon, down to the Sea of Galilee and into the region of the Decapolis.

column.name: text
column.value: There some people brought to him a man who was deaf and could hardly talk, and they begged him to place his hand on the man.

column.name: text
column.value: After he took him aside, away from the crowd, Jesus put his fingers into the man's ears. Then he spit and touched the man's tongue.

column.name: text
column.value: He looked up to heaven and with a deep sigh said to him, "Ephphatha!" (which means, "Be opened!").

column.name: text
column.value: At this, the man's ears were opened, his tongue was loosened and he began to speak plainly.

column.name: text
column.value: Jesus commanded them not to tell anyone. But the more he did so, the more they kept talking about it.

column.name: text
column.value: People were overwhelmed with amazement. "He has done everything well," they said. "He even makes the deaf hear and the mute speak."

column.name: text
column.value: During those days another large crowd gathered. Since they had nothing to eat, Jesus called his disciples to him and said,

column.name: text
column.value: "I have compassion for these people; they have already been with me three days and have nothing to eat.

column.name: text
column.value: If I send them home hungry, they will collapse on the way, because some of them have come a long distance."

column.name: text
column.value: His disciples answered, "But where in this remote place can anyone get enough bread to feed them?"

column.name: text
column.value: "How many loaves do you have?" Jesus asked. "Seven," they replied.

column.name: text
column.value: He told the crowd to sit down on the ground. When he had taken the seven loaves and given thanks, he broke them and gave them to his disciples to set before the people, and they did so.

column.name: text
column.value: They had a few small fish as well; he gave thanks for them also and told the disciples to distribute them.

column.name: text
column.value: The people ate and were satisfied. Afterward the disciples picked up seven basketfuls of broken pieces that were left over.

column.name: text
column.value: About four thousand men were present. And having sent them away,

column.name: text
column.value: he got into the boat with his disciples and went to the region of Dalmanutha.

column.name: text
column.value: The Pharisees came and began to question Jesus. To test him, they asked him for a sign from heaven.

column.name: text
column.value: He sighed deeply and said, "Why does this generation ask for a miraculous sign? I tell you the truth, no sign will be given to it."

column.name: text
column.value: Then he left them, got back into the boat and crossed to the other side.

column.name: text
column.value: The disciples had forgotten to bring bread, except for one loaf they had with them in the boat.

column.name: text
column.value: "Be careful," Jesus warned them. "Watch out for the yeast of the Pharisees and that of Herod."

column.name: text
column.value: They discussed this with one another and said, "It is because we have no bread."

column.name: text
column.value: Aware of their discussion, Jesus asked them: "Why are you talking about having no bread? Do you still not see or understand? Are your hearts hardened?

column.name: text
column.value: Do you have eyes but fail to see, and ears but fail to hear? And don't you remember?

column.name: text
column.value: When I broke the five loaves for the five thousand, how many basketfuls of pieces did you pick up?" "Twelve," they replied.

column.name: text
column.value: "And when I broke the seven loaves for the four thousand, how many basketfuls of pieces did you pick up?" They answered, "Seven."

column.name: text
column.value: He said to them, "Do you still not understand?"

column.name: text
column.value: They came to Bethsaida, and some people brought a blind man and begged Jesus to touch him.

column.name: text
column.value: He took the blind man by the hand and led him outside the village. When he had spit on the man's eyes and put his hands on him, Jesus asked, "Do you see anything?"

column.name: text
column.value: He looked up and said, "I see people; they look like trees walking around."

column.name: text
column.value: Once more Jesus put his hands on the man's eyes. Then his eyes were opened, his sight was restored, and he saw everything clearly.

column.name: text
column.value: Jesus sent him home, saying, "Don't go into the village."

column.name: text
column.value: Jesus and his disciples went on to the villages around Caesarea Philippi. On the way he asked them, "Who do people say I am?"

column.name: text
column.value: They replied, "Some say John the Baptist; others say Elijah; and still others, one of the prophets."

column.name: text
column.value: "But what about you?" he asked. "Who do you say I am?" Peter answered, "You are the Christ."

column.name: text
column.value: Jesus warned them not to tell anyone about him.

column.name: text
column.value: He then began to teach them that the Son of Man must suffer many things and be rejected by the elders, chief priests and teachers of the law, and that he must be killed and after three days rise again.

column.name: text
column.value: He spoke plainly about this, and Peter took him aside and began to rebuke him.

column.name: text
column.value: But when Jesus turned and looked at his disciples, he rebuked Peter. "Get behind me, Satan!" he said. "You do not have in mind the things of God, but the things of men."

column.name: text
column.value: Then he called the crowd to him along with his disciples and said: "If anyone would come after me, he must deny himself and take up his cross and follow me.

column.name: text
column.value: For whoever wants to save his life will lose it, but whoever loses his life for me and for the gospel will save it.

column.name: text
column.value: What good is it for a man to gain the whole world, yet forfeit his soul?

column.name: text
column.value: Or what can a man give in exchange for his soul?

column.name: text
column.value: If anyone is ashamed of me and my words in this adulterous and sinful generation, the Son of Man will be ashamed of him when he comes in his Father's glory with the holy angels."

column.name: text
column.value: And he said to them, "I tell you the truth, some who are standing here will not taste death before they see the kingdom of God come with power."

column.name: text
column.value: After six days Jesus took Peter, James and John with him and led them up a high mountain, where they were all alone. There he was transfigured before them.

column.name: text
column.value: His clothes became dazzling white, whiter than anyone in the world could bleach them.

column.name: text
column.value: And there appeared before them Elijah and Moses, who were talking with Jesus.

column.name: text
column.value: Peter said to Jesus, "Rabbi, it is good for us to be here. Let us put up three shelters--one for you, one for Moses and one for Elijah."

column.name: text
column.value: (He did not know what to say, they were so frightened.)

column.name: text
column.value: Then a cloud appeared and enveloped them, and a voice came from the cloud: "This is my Son, whom I love. Listen to him!"

column.name: text
column.value: Suddenly, when they looked around, they no longer saw anyone with them except Jesus.

column.name: text
column.value: As they were coming down the mountain, Jesus gave them orders not to tell anyone what they had seen until the Son of Man had risen from the dead.

column.name: text
column.value: They kept the matter to themselves, discussing what "rising from the dead" meant.

column.name: text
column.value: And they asked him, "Why do the teachers of the law say that Elijah must come first?"

column.name: text
column.value: Jesus replied, "To be sure, Elijah does come first, and restores all things. Why then is it written that the Son of Man must suffer much and be rejected?

column.name: text
column.value: But I tell you, Elijah has come, and they have done to him everything they wished, just as it is written about him."

column.name: text
column.value: When they came to the other disciples, they saw a large crowd around them and the teachers of the law arguing with them.

column.name: text
column.value: As soon as all the people saw Jesus, they were overwhelmed with wonder and ran to greet him.

column.name: text
column.value: "What are you arguing with them about?" he asked.

column.name: text
column.value: A man in the crowd answered, "Teacher, I brought you my son, who is possessed by a spirit that has robbed him of speech.

column.name: text
column.value: Whenever it seizes him, it throws him to the ground. He foams at the mouth, gnashes his teeth and becomes rigid. I asked your disciples to drive out the spirit, but they could not."

column.name: text
column.value: "O unbelieving generation," Jesus replied, "how long shall I stay with you? How long shall I put up with you? Bring the boy to me."

column.name: text
column.value: So they brought him. When the spirit saw Jesus, it immediately threw the boy into a convulsion. He fell to the ground and rolled around, foaming at the mouth.

column.name: text
column.value: Jesus asked the boy's father, "How long has he been like this?" "From childhood," he answered.

column.name: text
column.value: "It has often thrown him into fire or water to kill him. But if you can do anything, take pity on us and help us."

column.name: text
column.value: "'If you can'?" said Jesus. "Everything is possible for him who believes."

column.name: text
column.value: Immediately the boy's father exclaimed, "I do believe; help me overcome my unbelief!"

column.name: text
column.value: When Jesus saw that a crowd was running to the scene, he rebuked the evil spirit. "You deaf and mute spirit," he said, "I command you, come out of him and never enter him again."

column.name: text
column.value: The spirit shrieked, convulsed him violently and came out. The boy looked so much like a corpse that many said, "He's dead."

column.name: text
column.value: But Jesus took him by the hand and lifted him to his feet, and he stood up.

column.name: text
column.value: After Jesus had gone indoors, his disciples asked him privately, "Why couldn't we drive it out?"

column.name: text
column.value: He replied, "This kind can come out only by prayer."

column.name: text
column.value: They left that place and passed through Galilee. Jesus did not want anyone to know where they were,

column.name: text
column.value: because he was teaching his disciples. He said to them, "The Son of Man is going to be betrayed into the hands of men. They will kill him, and after three days he will rise."

column.name: text
column.value: But they did not understand what he meant and were afraid to ask him about it.

column.name: text
column.value: They came to Capernaum. When he was in the house, he asked them, "What were you arguing about on the road?"

column.name: text
column.value: But they kept quiet because on the way they had argued about who was the greatest.

column.name: text
column.value: Sitting down, Jesus called the Twelve and said, "If anyone wants to be first, he must be the very last, and the servant of all."

column.name: text
column.value: He took a little child and had him stand among them. Taking him in his arms, he said to them,

column.name: text
column.value: "Whoever welcomes one of these little children in my name welcomes me; and whoever welcomes me does not welcome me but the one who sent me."

column.name: text
column.value: "Teacher," said John, "we saw a man driving out demons in your name and we told him to stop, because he was not one of us."

column.name: text
column.value: "Do not stop him," Jesus said. "No one who does a miracle in my name can in the next moment say anything bad about me,

column.name: text
column.value: for whoever is not against us is for us.

column.name: text
column.value: I tell you the truth, anyone who gives you a cup of water in my name because you belong to Christ will certainly not lose his reward.

column.name: text
column.value: "And if anyone causes one of these little ones who believe in me to sin, it would be better for him to be thrown into the sea with a large millstone tied around his neck.

column.name: text
column.value: If your hand causes you to sin, cut it off. It is better for you to enter life maimed than with two hands to go into hell, where the fire never goes out.

column.name: text
column.value: And if your foot causes you to sin, cut it off. It is better for you to enter life crippled than to have two feet and be thrown into hell.

column.name: text
column.value: And if your eye causes you to sin, pluck it out. It is better for you to enter the kingdom of God with one eye than to have two eyes and be thrown into hell,

column.name: text
column.value: where "'their worm does not die, and the fire is not quenched.'

column.name: text
column.value: Everyone will be salted with fire.

column.name: text
column.value: "Salt is good, but if it loses its saltiness, how can you make it salty again? Have salt in yourselves, and be at peace with each other."

column.name: text
column.value: Jesus then left that place and went into the region of Judea and across the Jordan. Again crowds of people came to him, and as was his custom, he taught them.

column.name: text
column.value: Some Pharisees came and tested him by asking, "Is it lawful for a man to divorce his wife?"

column.name: text
column.value: "What did Moses command you?" he replied.

column.name: text
column.value: They said, "Moses permitted a man to write a certificate of divorce and send her away."

column.name: text
column.value: "It was because your hearts were hard that Moses wrote you this law," Jesus replied.

column.name: text
column.value: "But at the beginning of creation God 'made them male and female.'

column.name: text
column.value: 'For this reason a man will leave his father and mother and be united to his wife,

column.name: text
column.value: and the two will become one flesh.' So they are no longer two, but one.

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore what God has joined together, let man not separate."

column.name: text
column.value: When they were in the house again, the disciples asked Jesus about this.

column.name: text
column.value: He answered, "Anyone who divorces his wife and marries another woman commits adultery against her.

column.name: text
column.value: And if she divorces her husband and marries another man, she commits adultery."

column.name: text
column.value: People were bringing little children to Jesus to have him touch them, but the disciples rebuked them.

column.name: text
column.value: When Jesus saw this, he was indignant. He said to them, "Let the little children come to me, and do not hinder them, for the kingdom of God belongs to such as these.

column.name: text
column.value: I tell you the truth, anyone who will not receive the kingdom of God like a little child will never enter it."

column.name: text
column.value: And he took the children in his arms, put his hands on them and blessed them.

column.name: text
column.value: As Jesus started on his way, a man ran up to him and fell on his knees before him. "Good teacher," he asked, "what must I do to inherit eternal life?"

column.name: text
column.value: "Why do you call me good?" Jesus answered. "No one is good--except God alone.

column.name: text
column.value: You know the commandments: 'Do not murder, do not commit adultery, do not steal, do not give false testimony, do not defraud, honor your father and mother.'"

column.name: text
column.value: "Teacher," he declared, "all these I have kept since I was a boy."

column.name: text
column.value: Jesus looked at him and loved him. "One thing you lack," he said. "Go, sell everything you have and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven. Then come, follow me."

column.name: text
column.value: At this the man's face fell. He went away sad, because he had great wealth.

column.name: text
column.value: Jesus looked around and said to his disciples, "How hard it is for the rich to enter the kingdom of God!"

column.name: text
column.value: The disciples were amazed at his words. But Jesus said again, "Children, how hard it is to enter the kingdom of God!

column.name: text
column.value: It is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter the kingdom of God."

column.name: text
column.value: The disciples were even more amazed, and said to each other, "Who then can be saved?"

column.name: text
column.value: Jesus looked at them and said, "With man this is impossible, but not with God; all things are possible with God."

column.name: text
column.value: Peter said to him, "We have left everything to follow you!"

column.name: text
column.value: "I tell you the truth," Jesus replied, "no one who has left home or brothers or sisters or mother or father or children or fields for me and the gospel

column.name: text
column.value: will fail to receive a hundred times as much in this present age (homes, brothers, sisters, mothers, children and fields--and with them, persecutions) and in the age to come, eternal life.

column.name: text
column.value: But many who are first will be last, and the last first."

column.name: text
column.value: They were on their way up to Jerusalem, with Jesus leading the way, and the disciples were astonished, while those who followed were afraid. Again he took the Twelve aside and told them what was going to happen to him.

column.name: text
column.value: "We are going up to Jerusalem," he said, "and the Son of Man will be betrayed to the chief priests and teachers of the law. They will condemn him to death and will hand him over to the Gentiles,

column.name: text
column.value: who will mock him and spit on him, flog him and kill him. Three days later he will rise."

column.name: text
column.value: Then James and John, the sons of Zebedee, came to him. "Teacher," they said, "we want you to do for us whatever we ask."

column.name: text
column.value: "What do you want me to do for you?" he asked.

column.name: text
column.value: They replied, "Let one of us sit at your right and the other at your left in your glory."

column.name: text
column.value: "You don't know what you are asking," Jesus said. "Can you drink the cup I drink or be baptized with the baptism I am baptized with?"

column.name: text
column.value: "We can," they answered. Jesus said to them, "You will drink the cup I drink and be baptized with the baptism I am baptized with,

column.name: text
column.value: but to sit at my right or left is not for me to grant. These places belong to those for whom they have been prepared."

column.name: text
column.value: When the ten heard about this, they became indignant with James and John.

column.name: text
column.value: Jesus called them together and said, "You know that those who are regarded as rulers of the Gentiles lord it over them, and their high officials exercise authority over them.

column.name: text
column.value: Not so with you. Instead, whoever wants to become great among you must be your servant,

column.name: text
column.value: and whoever wants to be first must be slave of all.

column.name: text
column.value: For even the Son of Man did not come to be served, but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many."

column.name: text
column.value: Then they came to Jericho. As Jesus and his disciples, together with a large crowd, were leaving the city, a blind man, Bartimaeus (that is, the Son of Timaeus), was sitting by the roadside begging.

column.name: text
column.value: When he heard that it was Jesus of Nazareth, he began to shout, "Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!"

column.name: text
column.value: Many rebuked him and told him to be quiet, but he shouted all the more, "Son of David, have mercy on me!"

column.name: text
column.value: Jesus stopped and said, "Call him." So they called to the blind man, "Cheer up! On your feet! He's calling you."

column.name: text
column.value: Throwing his cloak aside, he jumped to his feet and came to Jesus.

column.name: text
column.value: "What do you want me to do for you?" Jesus asked him. The blind man said, "Rabbi, I want to see."

column.name: text
column.value: "Go," said Jesus, "your faith has healed you." Immediately he received his sight and followed Jesus along the road.

column.name: text
column.value: As they approached Jerusalem and came to Bethphage and Bethany at the Mount of Olives, Jesus sent two of his disciples,

column.name: text
column.value: saying to them, "Go to the village ahead of you, and just as you enter it, you will find a colt tied there, which no one has ever ridden. Untie it and bring it here.

column.name: text
column.value: If anyone asks you, 'Why are you doing this?' tell him, 'The Lord needs it and will send it back here shortly.'"

column.name: text
column.value: They went and found a colt outside in the street, tied at a doorway. As they untied it,

column.name: text
column.value: some people standing there asked, "What are you doing, untying that colt?"

column.name: text
column.value: They answered as Jesus had told them to, and the people let them go.

column.name: text
column.value: When they brought the colt to Jesus and threw their cloaks over it, he sat on it.

column.name: text
column.value: Many people spread their cloaks on the road, while others spread branches they had cut in the fields.

column.name: text
column.value: Those who went ahead and those who followed shouted, "Hosanna!" "Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord!"

column.name: text
column.value: "Blessed is the coming kingdom of our father David!" "Hosanna in the highest!"

column.name: text
column.value: Jesus entered Jerusalem and went to the temple. He looked around at everything, but since it was already late, he went out to Bethany with the Twelve.

column.name: text
column.value: The next day as they were leaving Bethany, Jesus was hungry.

column.name: text
column.value: Seeing in the distance a fig tree in leaf, he went to find out if it had any fruit. When he reached it, he found nothing but leaves, because it was not the season for figs.

column.name: text
column.value: Then he said to the tree, "May no one ever eat fruit from you again." And his disciples heard him say it.

column.name: text
column.value: On reaching Jerusalem, Jesus entered the temple area and began driving out those who were buying and selling there. He overturned the tables of the money changers and the benches of those selling doves,

column.name: text
column.value: and would not allow anyone to carry merchandise through the temple courts.

column.name: text
column.value: And as he taught them, he said, "Is it not written: "'My house will be called a house of prayer for all nations'? But you have made it 'a den of robbers.'"

column.name: text
column.value: The chief priests and the teachers of the law heard this and began looking for a way to kill him, for they feared him, because the whole crowd was amazed at his teaching.

column.name: text
column.value: When evening came, they went out of the city.

column.name: text
column.value: In the morning, as they went along, they saw the fig tree withered from the roots.

column.name: text
column.value: Peter remembered and said to Jesus, "Rabbi, look! The fig tree you cursed has withered!"

column.name: text
column.value: "Have faith in God," Jesus answered.

column.name: text
column.value: "I tell you the truth, if anyone says to this mountain, 'Go, throw yourself into the sea,' and does not doubt in his heart but believes that what he says will happen, it will be done for him.

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore I tell you, whatever you ask for in prayer, believe that you have received it, and it will be yours.

column.name: text
column.value: And when you stand praying, if you hold anything against anyone, forgive him, so that your Father in heaven may forgive you your sins."

column.name: text
column.value: They arrived again in Jerusalem, and while Jesus was walking in the temple courts, the chief priests, the teachers of the law and the elders came to him.

column.name: text
column.value: "By what authority are you doing these things?" they asked. "And who gave you authority to do this?"

column.name: text
column.value: Jesus replied, "I will ask you one question. Answer me, and I will tell you by what authority I am doing these things.

column.name: text
column.value: John's baptism--was it from heaven, or from men? Tell me!"

column.name: text
column.value: They discussed it among themselves and said, "If we say, 'From heaven,' he will ask, 'Then why didn't you believe him?'

column.name: text
column.value: But if we say, 'From men' . . . ." (They feared the people, for everyone held that John really was a prophet.)

column.name: text
column.value: So they answered Jesus, "We don't know." Jesus said, "Neither will I tell you by what authority I am doing these things."

column.name: text
column.value: He then began to speak to them in parables: "A man planted a vineyard. He put a wall around it, dug a pit for the winepress and built a watchtower. Then he rented the vineyard to some farmers and went away on a journey.

column.name: text
column.value: At harvest time he sent a servant to the tenants to collect from them some of the fruit of the vineyard.

column.name: text
column.value: But they seized him, beat him and sent him away empty-handed.

column.name: text
column.value: Then he sent another servant to them; they struck this man on the head and treated him shamefully.

column.name: text
column.value: He sent still another, and that one they killed. He sent many others; some of them they beat, others they killed.

column.name: text
column.value: "He had one left to send, a son, whom he loved. He sent him last of all, saying, 'They will respect my son.'

column.name: text
column.value: "But the tenants said to one another, 'This is the heir. Come, let's kill him, and the inheritance will be ours.'

column.name: text
column.value: So they took him and killed him, and threw him out of the vineyard.

column.name: text
column.value: "What then will the owner of the vineyard do? He will come and kill those tenants and give the vineyard to others.

column.name: text
column.value: Haven't you read this scripture: "'The stone the builders rejected has become the capstone;

column.name: text
column.value: the Lord has done this, and it is marvelous in our eyes'?"

column.name: text
column.value: Then they looked for a way to arrest him because they knew he had spoken the parable against them. But they were afraid of the crowd; so they left him and went away.

column.name: text
column.value: Later they sent some of the Pharisees and Herodians to Jesus to catch him in his words.

column.name: text
column.value: They came to him and said, "Teacher, we know you are a man of integrity. You aren't swayed by men, because you pay no attention to who they are; but you teach the way of God in accordance with the truth. Is it right to pay taxes to Caesar or not?

column.name: text
column.value: Should we pay or shouldn't we?" But Jesus knew their hypocrisy. "Why are you trying to trap me?" he asked. "Bring me a denarius and let me look at it."

column.name: text
column.value: They brought the coin, and he asked them, "Whose portrait is this? And whose inscription?" "Caesar's," they replied.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jesus said to them, "Give to Caesar what is Caesar's and to God what is God's." And they were amazed at him.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the Sadducees, who say there is no resurrection, came to him with a question.

column.name: text
column.value: "Teacher," they said, "Moses wrote for us that if a man's brother dies and leaves a wife but no children, the man must marry the widow and have children for his brother.

column.name: text
column.value: Now there were seven brothers. The first one married and died without leaving any children.

column.name: text
column.value: The second one married the widow, but he also died, leaving no child. It was the same with the third.

column.name: text
column.value: In fact, none of the seven left any children. Last of all, the woman died too.

column.name: text
column.value: At the resurrection whose wife will she be, since the seven were married to her?"

column.name: text
column.value: Jesus replied, "Are you not in error because you do not know the Scriptures or the power of God?

column.name: text
column.value: When the dead rise, they will neither marry nor be given in marriage; they will be like the angels in heaven.

column.name: text
column.value: Now about the dead rising--have you not read in the book of Moses, in the account of the bush, how God said to him, 'I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob'?

column.name: text
column.value: He is not the God of the dead, but of the living. You are badly mistaken!"

column.name: text
column.value: One of the teachers of the law came and heard them debating. Noticing that Jesus had given them a good answer, he asked him, "Of all the commandments, which is the most important?"

column.name: text
column.value: "The most important one," answered Jesus, "is this: 'Hear, O Israel, the Lord our God, the Lord is one.

column.name: text
column.value: Love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your mind and with all your strength.'

column.name: text
column.value: The second is this: 'Love your neighbor as yourself.' There is no commandment greater than these."

column.name: text
column.value: "Well said, teacher," the man replied. "You are right in saying that God is one and there is no other but him.

column.name: text
column.value: To love him with all your heart, with all your understanding and with all your strength, and to love your neighbor as yourself is more important than all burnt offerings and sacrifices."

column.name: text
column.value: When Jesus saw that he had answered wisely, he said to him, "You are not far from the kingdom of God." And from then on no one dared ask him any more questions.

column.name: text
column.value: While Jesus was teaching in the temple courts, he asked, "How is it that the teachers of the law say that the Christ is the son of David?

column.name: text
column.value: David himself, speaking by the Holy Spirit, declared: "'The Lord said to my Lord: "Sit at my right hand until I put your enemies under your feet." '

column.name: text
column.value: David himself calls him 'Lord.' How then can he be his son?" The large crowd listened to him with delight.

column.name: text
column.value: As he taught, Jesus said, "Watch out for the teachers of the law. They like to walk around in flowing robes and be greeted in the marketplaces,

column.name: text
column.value: and have the most important seats in the synagogues and the places of honor at banquets.

column.name: text
column.value: They devour widows' houses and for a show make lengthy prayers. Such men will be punished most severely."

column.name: text
column.value: Jesus sat down opposite the place where the offerings were put and watched the crowd putting their money into the temple treasury. Many rich people threw in large amounts.

column.name: text
column.value: But a poor widow came and put in two very small copper coins, worth only a fraction of a penny.

column.name: text
column.value: Calling his disciples to him, Jesus said, "I tell you the truth, this poor widow has put more into the treasury than all the others.

column.name: text
column.value: They all gave out of their wealth; but she, out of her poverty, put in everything--all she had to live on."

column.name: text
column.value: Very early in the morning, the chief priests, with the elders, the teachers of the law and the whole Sanhedrin, reached a decision. They bound Jesus, led him away and handed him over to Pilate.

column.name: text
column.value: "Are you the king of the Jews?" asked Pilate. "Yes, it is as you say," Jesus replied.

column.name: text
column.value: The chief priests accused him of many things.

column.name: text
column.value: So again Pilate asked him, "Aren't you going to answer? See how many things they are accusing you of."

column.name: text
column.value: But Jesus still made no reply, and Pilate was amazed.

column.name: text
column.value: Now it was the custom at the Feast to release a prisoner whom the people requested.

column.name: text
column.value: A man called Barabbas was in prison with the insurrectionists who had committed murder in the uprising.

column.name: text
column.value: The crowd came up and asked Pilate to do for them what he usually did.

column.name: text
column.value: "Do you want me to release to you the king of the Jews?" asked Pilate,

column.name: text
column.value: knowing it was out of envy that the chief priests had handed Jesus over to him.

column.name: text
column.value: But the chief priests stirred up the crowd to have Pilate release Barabbas instead.

column.name: text
column.value: "What shall I do, then, with the one you call the king of the Jews?" Pilate asked them.

column.name: text
column.value: "Crucify him!" they shouted.

column.name: text
column.value: "Why? What crime has he committed?" asked Pilate. But they shouted all the louder, "Crucify him!"

column.name: text
column.value: Wanting to satisfy the crowd, Pilate released Barabbas to them. He had Jesus flogged, and handed him over to be crucified.

column.name: text
column.value: The soldiers led Jesus away into the palace (that is, the Praetorium) and called together the whole company of soldiers.

column.name: text
column.value: They put a purple robe on him, then twisted together a crown of thorns and set it on him.

column.name: text
column.value: And they began to call out to him, "Hail, king of the Jews!"

column.name: text
column.value: Again and again they struck him on the head with a staff and spit on him. Falling on their knees, they paid homage to him.

column.name: text
column.value: And when they had mocked him, they took off the purple robe and put his own clothes on him. Then they led him out to crucify him.

column.name: text
column.value: A certain man from Cyrene, Simon, the father of Alexander and Rufus, was passing by on his way in from the country, and they forced him to carry the cross.

column.name: text
column.value: They brought Jesus to the place called Golgotha (which means The Place of the Skull).

column.name: text
column.value: Then they offered him wine mixed with myrrh, but he did not take it.

column.name: text
column.value: And they crucified him. Dividing up his clothes, they cast lots to see what each would get.

column.name: text
column.value: It was the third hour when they crucified him.

column.name: text
column.value: The written notice of the charge against him read: THE KING OF THE JEWS.

column.name: text
column.value: They crucified two robbers with him, one on his right and one on his left.

column.name: text
column.value: Those who passed by hurled insults at him, shaking their heads and saying, "So! You who are going to destroy the temple and build it in three days,

column.name: text
column.value: come down from the cross and save yourself!"

column.name: text
column.value: In the same way the chief priests and the teachers of the law mocked him among themselves. "He saved others," they said, "but he can't save himself!

column.name: text
column.value: Let this Christ, this King of Israel, come down now from the cross, that we may see and believe." Those crucified with him also heaped insults on him.

column.name: text
column.value: At the sixth hour darkness came over the whole land until the ninth hour.

column.name: text
column.value: And at the ninth hour Jesus cried out in a loud voice, "Eloi, Eloi, lama sabachthani?"--which means, "My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?"

column.name: text
column.value: When some of those standing near heard this, they said, "Listen, he's calling Elijah."

column.name: text
column.value: One man ran, filled a sponge with wine vinegar, put it on a stick, and offered it to Jesus to drink. "Now leave him alone. Let's see if Elijah comes to take him down," he said.

column.name: text
column.value: With a loud cry, Jesus breathed his last.

column.name: text
column.value: The curtain of the temple was torn in two from top to bottom.

column.name: text
column.value: And when the centurion, who stood there in front of Jesus, heard his cry and saw how he died, he said, "Surely this man was the Son of God!"

column.name: text
column.value: Some women were watching from a distance. Among them were Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James the younger and of Joses, and Salome.

column.name: text
column.value: In Galilee these women had followed him and cared for his needs. Many other women who had come up with him to Jerusalem were also there.

column.name: text
column.value: It was Preparation Day (that is, the day before the Sabbath). So as evening approached,

column.name: text
column.value: Joseph of Arimathea, a prominent member of the Council, who was himself waiting for the kingdom of God, went boldly to Pilate and asked for Jesus' body.

column.name: text
column.value: Pilate was surprised to hear that he was already dead. Summoning the centurion, he asked him if Jesus had already died.

column.name: text
column.value: When he learned from the centurion that it was so, he gave the body to Joseph.

column.name: text
column.value: So Joseph bought some linen cloth, took down the body, wrapped it in the linen, and placed it in a tomb cut out of rock. Then he rolled a stone against the entrance of the tomb.

column.name: text
column.value: Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of Joses saw where he was laid.

column.name: text
column.value: Now the Passover and the Feast of Unleavened Bread were only two days away, and the chief priests and the teachers of the law were looking for some sly way to arrest Jesus and kill him.

column.name: text
column.value: "But not during the Feast," they said, "or the people may riot."

column.name: text
column.value: While he was in Bethany, reclining at the table in the home of a man known as Simon the Leper, a woman came with an alabaster jar of very expensive perfume, made of pure nard. She broke the jar and poured the perfume on his head.

column.name: text
column.value: Some of those present were saying indignantly to one another, "Why this waste of perfume?

column.name: text
column.value: It could have been sold for more than a year's wages and the money given to the poor." And they rebuked her harshly.

column.name: text
column.value: "Leave her alone," said Jesus. "Why are you bothering her? She has done a beautiful thing to me.

column.name: text
column.value: The poor you will always have with you, and you can help them any time you want. But you will not always have me.

column.name: text
column.value: She did what she could. She poured perfume on my body beforehand to prepare for my burial.

column.name: text
column.value: I tell you the truth, wherever the gospel is preached throughout the world, what she has done will also be told, in memory of her."

column.name: text
column.value: Then Judas Iscariot, one of the Twelve, went to the chief priests to betray Jesus to them.

column.name: text
column.value: They were delighted to hear this and promised to give him money. So he watched for an opportunity to hand him over.

column.name: text
column.value: On the first day of the Feast of Unleavened Bread, when it was customary to sacrifice the Passover lamb, Jesus' disciples asked him, "Where do you want us to go and make preparations for you to eat the Passover?"

column.name: text
column.value: So he sent two of his disciples, telling them, "Go into the city, and a man carrying a jar of water will meet you. Follow him.

column.name: text
column.value: Say to the owner of the house he enters, 'The Teacher asks: Where is my guest room, where I may eat the Passover with my disciples?'

column.name: text
column.value: He will show you a large upper room, furnished and ready. Make preparations for us there."

column.name: text
column.value: The disciples left, went into the city and found things just as Jesus had told them. So they prepared the Passover.

column.name: text
column.value: When evening came, Jesus arrived with the Twelve.

column.name: text
column.value: While they were reclining at the table eating, he said, "I tell you the truth, one of you will betray me--one who is eating with me."

column.name: text
column.value: They were saddened, and one by one they said to him, "Surely not I?"

column.name: text
column.value: "It is one of the Twelve," he replied, "one who dips bread into the bowl with me.

column.name: text
column.value: The Son of Man will go just as it is written about him. But woe to that man who betrays the Son of Man! It would be better for him if he had not been born."

column.name: text
column.value: While they were eating, Jesus took bread, gave thanks and broke it, and gave it to his disciples, saying, "Take it; this is my body."

column.name: text
column.value: Then he took the cup, gave thanks and offered it to them, and they all drank from it.

column.name: text
column.value: "This is my blood of the covenant, which is poured out for many," he said to them.

column.name: text
column.value: "I tell you the truth, I will not drink again of the fruit of the vine until that day when I drink it anew in the kingdom of God."

column.name: text
column.value: When they had sung a hymn, they went out to the Mount of Olives.

column.name: text
column.value: "You will all fall away," Jesus told them, "for it is written: "'I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered.'

column.name: text
column.value: But after I have risen, I will go ahead of you into Galilee."

column.name: text
column.value: Peter declared, "Even if all fall away, I will not."

column.name: text
column.value: "I tell you the truth," Jesus answered, "today--yes, tonight--before the rooster crows twice you yourself will disown me three times."

column.name: text
column.value: But Peter insisted emphatically, "Even if I have to die with you, I will never disown you." And all the others said the same.

column.name: text
column.value: They went to a place called Gethsemane, and Jesus said to his disciples, "Sit here while I pray."

column.name: text
column.value: He took Peter, James and John along with him, and he began to be deeply distressed and troubled.

column.name: text
column.value: "My soul is overwhelmed with sorrow to the point of death," he said to them. "Stay here and keep watch."

column.name: text
column.value: Going a little farther, he fell to the ground and prayed that if possible the hour might pass from him.

column.name: text
column.value: "Abba, Father," he said, "everything is possible for you. Take this cup from me. Yet not what I will, but what you will."

column.name: text
column.value: Then he returned to his disciples and found them sleeping. "Simon," he said to Peter, "are you asleep? Could you not keep watch for one hour?

column.name: text
column.value: Watch and pray so that you will not fall into temptation. The spirit is willing, but the body is weak."

column.name: text
column.value: Once more he went away and prayed the same thing.

column.name: text
column.value: When he came back, he again found them sleeping, because their eyes were heavy. They did not know what to say to him.

column.name: text
column.value: Returning the third time, he said to them, "Are you still sleeping and resting? Enough! The hour has come. Look, the Son of Man is betrayed into the hands of sinners.

column.name: text
column.value: Rise! Let us go! Here comes my betrayer!"

column.name: text
column.value: Just as he was speaking, Judas, one of the Twelve, appeared. With him was a crowd armed with swords and clubs, sent from the chief priests, the teachers of the law, and the elders.

column.name: text
column.value: Now the betrayer had arranged a signal with them: "The one I kiss is the man; arrest him and lead him away under guard."

column.name: text
column.value: Going at once to Jesus, Judas said, "Rabbi!" and kissed him.

column.name: text
column.value: The men seized Jesus and arrested him.

column.name: text
column.value: Then one of those standing near drew his sword and struck the servant of the high priest, cutting off his ear.

column.name: text
column.value: "Am I leading a rebellion," said Jesus, "that you have come out with swords and clubs to capture me?

column.name: text
column.value: Every day I was with you, teaching in the temple courts, and you did not arrest me. But the Scriptures must be fulfilled."

column.name: text
column.value: Then everyone deserted him and fled.

column.name: text
column.value: A young man, wearing nothing but a linen garment, was following Jesus. When they seized him,

column.name: text
column.value: he fled naked, leaving his garment behind.

column.name: text
column.value: They took Jesus to the high priest, and all the chief priests, elders and teachers of the law came together.

column.name: text
column.value: Peter followed him at a distance, right into the courtyard of the high priest. There he sat with the guards and warmed himself at the fire.

column.name: text
column.value: The chief priests and the whole Sanhedrin were looking for evidence against Jesus so that they could put him to death, but they did not find any.

column.name: text
column.value: Many testified falsely against him, but their statements did not agree.

column.name: text
column.value: Then some stood up and gave this false testimony against him:

column.name: text
