column.value: No one else dared join them, even though they were highly regarded by the people.

column.name: text
column.value: Nevertheless, more and more men and women believed in the Lord and were added to their number.

column.name: text
column.value: As a result, people brought the sick into the streets and laid them on beds and mats so that at least Peter's shadow might fall on some of them as he passed by.

column.name: text
column.value: Crowds gathered also from the towns around Jerusalem, bringing their sick and those tormented by evil spirits, and all of them were healed.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the high priest and all his associates, who were members of the party of the Sadducees, were filled with jealousy.

column.name: text
column.value: They arrested the apostles and put them in the public jail.

column.name: text
column.value: But during the night an angel of the Lord opened the doors of the jail and brought them out.

column.name: text
column.value: "Go, stand in the temple courts," he said, "and tell the people the full message of this new life."

column.name: text
column.value: At daybreak they entered the temple courts, as they had been told, and began to teach the people. When the high priest and his associates arrived, they called together the Sanhedrin--the full assembly of the elders of Israel--and sent to the jail for the apostles.

column.name: text
column.value: But on arriving at the jail, the officers did not find them there. So they went back and reported,

column.name: text
column.value: "We found the jail securely locked, with the guards standing at the doors; but when we opened them, we found no one inside."

column.name: text
column.value: On hearing this report, the captain of the temple guard and the chief priests were puzzled, wondering what would come of this.

column.name: text
column.value: Then someone came and said, "Look! The men you put in jail are standing in the temple courts teaching the people."

column.name: text
column.value: At that, the captain went with his officers and brought the apostles. They did not use force, because they feared that the people would stone them.

column.name: text
column.value: Having brought the apostles, they made them appear before the Sanhedrin to be questioned by the high priest.

column.name: text
column.value: "We gave you strict orders not to teach in this name," he said. "Yet you have filled Jerusalem with your teaching and are determined to make us guilty of this man's blood."

column.name: text
column.value: Peter and the other apostles replied: "We must obey God rather than men!

column.name: text
column.value: The God of our fathers raised Jesus from the dead--whom you had killed by hanging him on a tree.

column.name: text
column.value: God exalted him to his own right hand as Prince and Savior that he might give repentance and forgiveness of sins to Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: We are witnesses of these things, and so is the Holy Spirit, whom God has given to those who obey him."

column.name: text
column.value: When they heard this, they were furious and wanted to put them to death.

column.name: text
column.value: But a Pharisee named Gamaliel, a teacher of the law, who was honored by all the people, stood up in the Sanhedrin and ordered that the men be put outside for a little while.

column.name: text
column.value: Then he addressed them: "Men of Israel, consider carefully what you intend to do to these men.

column.name: text
column.value: Some time ago Theudas appeared, claiming to be somebody, and about four hundred men rallied to him. He was killed, all his followers were dispersed, and it all came to nothing.

column.name: text
column.value: After him, Judas the Galilean appeared in the days of the census and led a band of people in revolt. He too was killed, and all his followers were scattered.

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore, in the present case I advise you: Leave these men alone! Let them go! For if their purpose or activity is of human origin, it will fail.

column.name: text
column.value: But if it is from God, you will not be able to stop these men; you will only find yourselves fighting against God."

column.name: text
column.value: His speech persuaded them. They called the apostles in and had them flogged. Then they ordered them not to speak in the name of Jesus, and let them go.

column.name: text
column.value: The apostles left the Sanhedrin, rejoicing because they had been counted worthy of suffering disgrace for the Name.

column.name: text
column.value: Day after day, in the temple courts and from house to house, they never stopped teaching and proclaiming the good news that Jesus is the Christ.

column.name: text
column.value: In those days when the number of disciples was increasing, the Grecian Jews among them complained against the Hebraic Jews because their widows were being overlooked in the daily distribution of food.

column.name: text
column.value: So the Twelve gathered all the disciples together and said, "It would not be right for us to neglect the ministry of the word of God in order to wait on tables.

column.name: text
column.value: Brothers, choose seven men from among you who are known to be full of the Spirit and wisdom. We will turn this responsibility over to them

column.name: text
column.value: and will give our attention to prayer and the ministry of the word."

column.name: text
column.value: This proposal pleased the whole group. They chose Stephen, a man full of faith and of the Holy Spirit; also Philip, Procorus, Nicanor, Timon, Parmenas, and Nicolas from Antioch, a convert to Judaism.

column.name: text
column.value: They presented these men to the apostles, who prayed and laid their hands on them.

column.name: text
column.value: So the word of God spread. The number of disciples in Jerusalem increased rapidly, and a large number of priests became obedient to the faith.

column.name: text
column.value: Now Stephen, a man full of God's grace and power, did great wonders and miraculous signs among the people.

column.name: text
column.value: Opposition arose, however, from members of the Synagogue of the Freedmen (as it was called)--Jews of Cyrene and Alexandria as well as the provinces of Cilicia and Asia. These men began to argue with Stephen,

column.name: text
column.value: but they could not stand up against his wisdom or the Spirit by whom he spoke.

column.name: text
column.value: Then they secretly persuaded some men to say, "We have heard Stephen speak words of blasphemy against Moses and against God."

column.name: text
column.value: So they stirred up the people and the elders and the teachers of the law. They seized Stephen and brought him before the Sanhedrin.

column.name: text
column.value: They produced false witnesses, who testified, "This fellow never stops speaking against this holy place and against the law.

column.name: text
column.value: For we have heard him say that this Jesus of Nazareth will destroy this place and change the customs Moses handed down to us."

column.name: text
column.value: All who were sitting in the Sanhedrin looked intently at Stephen, and they saw that his face was like the face of an angel.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the high priest asked him, "Are these charges true?"

column.name: text
column.value: To this he replied: "Brothers and fathers, listen to me! The God of glory appeared to our father Abraham while he was still in Mesopotamia, before he lived in Haran.

column.name: text
column.value: 'Leave your country and your people,' God said, 'and go to the land I will show you.'

column.name: text
column.value: "So he left the land of the Chaldeans and settled in Haran. After the death of his father, God sent him to this land where you are now living.

column.name: text
column.value: He gave him no inheritance here, not even a foot of ground. But God promised him that he and his descendants after him would possess the land, even though at that time Abraham had no child.

column.name: text
column.value: God spoke to him in this way: 'Your descendants will be strangers in a country not their own, and they will be enslaved and mistreated four hundred years.

column.name: text
column.value: But I will punish the nation they serve as slaves,' God said, 'and afterward they will come out of that country and worship me in this place.'

column.name: text
column.value: Then he gave Abraham the covenant of circumcision. And Abraham became the father of Isaac and circumcised him eight days after his birth. Later Isaac became the father of Jacob, and Jacob became the father of the twelve patriarchs.

column.name: text
column.value: "Because the patriarchs were jealous of Joseph, they sold him as a slave into Egypt. But God was with him

column.name: text
column.value: and rescued him from all his troubles. He gave Joseph wisdom and enabled him to gain the goodwill of Pharaoh king of Egypt; so he made him ruler over Egypt and all his palace.

column.name: text
column.value: "Then a famine struck all Egypt and Canaan, bringing great suffering, and our fathers could not find food.

column.name: text
column.value: When Jacob heard that there was grain in Egypt, he sent our fathers on their first visit.

column.name: text
column.value: On their second visit, Joseph told his brothers who he was, and Pharaoh learned about Joseph's family.

column.name: text
column.value: After this, Joseph sent for his father Jacob and his whole family, seventy-five in all.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jacob went down to Egypt, where he and our fathers died.

column.name: text
column.value: Their bodies were brought back to Shechem and placed in the tomb that Abraham had bought from the sons of Hamor at Shechem for a certain sum of money.

column.name: text
column.value: "As the time drew near for God to fulfill his promise to Abraham, the number of our people in Egypt greatly increased.

column.name: text
column.value: Then another king, who knew nothing about Joseph, became ruler of Egypt.

column.name: text
column.value: He dealt treacherously with our people and oppressed our forefathers by forcing them to throw out their newborn babies so that they would die.

column.name: text
column.value: "At that time Moses was born, and he was no ordinary child. For three months he was cared for in his father's house.

column.name: text
column.value: When he was placed outside, Pharaoh's daughter took him and brought him up as her own son.

column.name: text
column.value: Moses was educated in all the wisdom of the Egyptians and was powerful in speech and action.

column.name: text
column.value: "When Moses was forty years old, he decided to visit his fellow Israelites.

column.name: text
column.value: He saw one of them being mistreated by an Egyptian, so he went to his defense and avenged him by killing the Egyptian.

column.name: text
column.value: Moses thought that his own people would realize that God was using him to rescue them, but they did not.

column.name: text
column.value: The next day Moses came upon two Israelites who were fighting. He tried to reconcile them by saying, 'Men, you are brothers; why do you want to hurt each other?'

column.name: text
column.value: "But the man who was mistreating the other pushed Moses aside and said, 'Who made you ruler and judge over us?

column.name: text
column.value: Do you want to kill me as you killed the Egyptian yesterday?'

column.name: text
column.value: When Moses heard this, he fled to Midian, where he settled as a foreigner and had two sons.

column.name: text
column.value: "After forty years had passed, an angel appeared to Moses in the flames of a burning bush in the desert near Mount Sinai.

column.name: text
column.value: When he saw this, he was amazed at the sight. As he went over to look more closely, he heard the Lord's voice:

column.name: text
column.value: 'I am the God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob.' Moses trembled with fear and did not dare to look.

column.name: text
column.value: "Then the Lord said to him, 'Take off your sandals; the place where you are standing is holy ground.

column.name: text
column.value: I have indeed seen the oppression of my people in Egypt. I have heard their groaning and have come down to set them free. Now come, I will send you back to Egypt.'

column.name: text
column.value: "This is the same Moses whom they had rejected with the words, 'Who made you ruler and judge?' He was sent to be their ruler and deliverer by God himself, through the angel who appeared to him in the bush.

column.name: text
column.value: He led them out of Egypt and did wonders and miraculous signs in Egypt, at the Red Sea and for forty years in the desert.

column.name: text
column.value: "This is that Moses who told the Israelites, 'God will send you a prophet like me from your own people.'

column.name: text
column.value: He was in the assembly in the desert, with the angel who spoke to him on Mount Sinai, and with our fathers; and he received living words to pass on to us.

column.name: text
column.value: "But our fathers refused to obey him. Instead, they rejected him and in their hearts turned back to Egypt.

column.name: text
column.value: They told Aaron, 'Make us gods who will go before us. As for this fellow Moses who led us out of Egypt--we don't know what has happened to him!'

column.name: text
column.value: That was the time they made an idol in the form of a calf. They brought sacrifices to it and held a celebration in honor of what their hands had made.

column.name: text
column.value: But God turned away and gave them over to the worship of the heavenly bodies. This agrees with what is written in the book of the prophets: "'Did you bring me sacrifices and offerings forty years in the desert, O house of Israel?

column.name: text
column.value: You have lifted up the shrine of Molech and the star of your god Rephan, the idols you made to worship. Therefore I will send you into exile' beyond Babylon.

column.name: text
column.value: "Our forefathers had the tabernacle of the Testimony with them in the desert. It had been made as God directed Moses, according to the pattern he had seen.

column.name: text
column.value: Having received the tabernacle, our fathers under Joshua brought it with them when they took the land from the nations God drove out before them. It remained in the land until the time of David,

column.name: text
column.value: who enjoyed God's favor and asked that he might provide a dwelling place for the God of Jacob.

column.name: text
column.value: But it was Solomon who built the house for him.

column.name: text
column.value: "However, the Most High does not live in houses made by men. As the prophet says:

column.name: text
column.value: "'Heaven is my throne, and the earth is my footstool. What kind of house will you build for me? says the Lord. Or where will my resting place be?

column.name: text
column.value: Has not my hand made all these things?'

column.name: text
column.value: "You stiff-necked people, with uncircumcised hearts and ears! You are just like your fathers: You always resist the Holy Spirit!

column.name: text
column.value: Was there ever a prophet your fathers did not persecute? They even killed those who predicted the coming of the Righteous One. And now you have betrayed and murdered him--

column.name: text
column.value: you who have received the law that was put into effect through angels but have not obeyed it."

column.name: text
column.value: When they heard this, they were furious and gnashed their teeth at him.

column.name: text
column.value: But Stephen, full of the Holy Spirit, looked up to heaven and saw the glory of God, and Jesus standing at the right hand of God.

column.name: text
column.value: "Look," he said, "I see heaven open and the Son of Man standing at the right hand of God."

column.name: text
column.value: At this they covered their ears and, yelling at the top of their voices, they all rushed at him,

column.name: text
column.value: dragged him out of the city and began to stone him. Meanwhile, the witnesses laid their clothes at the feet of a young man named Saul.

column.name: text
column.value: While they were stoning him, Stephen prayed, "Lord Jesus, receive my spirit."

column.name: text
column.value: Then he fell on his knees and cried out, "Lord, do not hold this sin against them." When he had said this, he fell asleep.

column.name: text
column.value: And Saul was there, giving approval to his death. On that day a great persecution broke out against the church at Jerusalem, and all except the apostles were scattered throughout Judea and Samaria.

column.name: text
column.value: Godly men buried Stephen and mourned deeply for him.

column.name: text
column.value: But Saul began to destroy the church. Going from house to house, he dragged off men and women and put them in prison.

column.name: text
column.value: Those who had been scattered preached the word wherever they went.

column.name: text
column.value: Philip went down to a city in Samaria and proclaimed the Christ there.

column.name: text
column.value: When the crowds heard Philip and saw the miraculous signs he did, they all paid close attention to what he said.

column.name: text
column.value: With shrieks, evil spirits came out of many, and many paralytics and cripples were healed.

column.name: text
column.value: So there was great joy in that city.

column.name: text
column.value: Now for some time a man named Simon had practiced sorcery in the city and amazed all the people of Samaria. He boasted that he was someone great,

column.name: text
column.value: and all the people, both high and low, gave him their attention and exclaimed, "This man is the divine power known as the Great Power."

column.name: text
column.value: They followed him because he had amazed them for a long time with his magic.

column.name: text
column.value: But when they believed Philip as he preached the good news of the kingdom of God and the name of Jesus Christ, they were baptized, both men and women.

column.name: text
column.value: Simon himself believed and was baptized. And he followed Philip everywhere, astonished by the great signs and miracles he saw.

column.name: text
column.value: When the apostles in Jerusalem heard that Samaria had accepted the word of God, they sent Peter and John to them.

column.name: text
column.value: When they arrived, they prayed for them that they might receive the Holy Spirit,

column.name: text
column.value: because the Holy Spirit had not yet come upon any of them; they had simply been baptized into the name of the Lord Jesus.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Peter and John placed their hands on them, and they received the Holy Spirit.

column.name: text
column.value: When Simon saw that the Spirit was given at the laying on of the apostles' hands, he offered them money

column.name: text
column.value: and said, "Give me also this ability so that everyone on whom I lay my hands may receive the Holy Spirit."

column.name: text
column.value: Peter answered: "May your money perish with you, because you thought you could buy the gift of God with money!

column.name: text
column.value: You have no part or share in this ministry, because your heart is not right before God.

column.name: text
column.value: Repent of this wickedness and pray to the Lord. Perhaps he will forgive you for having such a thought in your heart.

column.name: text
column.value: For I see that you are full of bitterness and captive to sin."

column.name: text
column.value: Then Simon answered, "Pray to the Lord for me so that nothing you have said may happen to me."

column.name: text
column.value: When they had testified and proclaimed the word of the Lord, Peter and John returned to Jerusalem, preaching the gospel in many Samaritan villages.

column.name: text
column.value: Now an angel of the Lord said to Philip, "Go south to the road--the desert road--that goes down from Jerusalem to Gaza."

column.name: text
column.value: So he started out, and on his way he met an Ethiopian eunuch, an important official in charge of all the treasury of Candace, queen of the Ethiopians. This man had gone to Jerusalem to worship,

column.name: text
column.value: and on his way home was sitting in his chariot reading the book of Isaiah the prophet.

column.name: text
column.value: The Spirit told Philip, "Go to that chariot and stay near it."

column.name: text
column.value: Then Philip ran up to the chariot and heard the man reading Isaiah the prophet. "Do you understand what you are reading?" Philip asked.

column.name: text
column.value: "How can I," he said, "unless someone explains it to me?" So he invited Philip to come up and sit with him.

column.name: text
column.value: The eunuch was reading this passage of Scripture: "He was led like a sheep to the slaughter, and as a lamb before the shearer is silent, so he did not open his mouth.

column.name: text
column.value: In his humiliation he was deprived of justice. Who can speak of his descendants? For his life was taken from the earth."

column.name: text
column.value: The eunuch asked Philip, "Tell me, please, who is the prophet talking about, himself or someone else?"

column.name: text
column.value: Then Philip began with that very passage of Scripture and told him the good news about Jesus.

column.name: text
column.value: As they traveled along the road, they came to some water and the eunuch said, "Look, here is water. Why shouldn't I be baptized?"

column.name: text
column.value: And he gave orders to stop the chariot. Then both Philip and the eunuch went down into the water and Philip baptized him.

column.name: text
column.value: When they came up out of the water, the Spirit of the Lord suddenly took Philip away, and the eunuch did not see him again, but went on his way rejoicing.

column.name: text
column.value: Philip, however, appeared at Azotus and traveled about, preaching the gospel in all the towns until he reached Caesarea.

column.name: text
column.value: The apostles and the brothers throughout Judea heard that the Gentiles also had received the word of God.

column.name: text
column.value: So when Peter went up to Jerusalem, the circumcised believers criticized him

column.name: text
column.value: and said, "You went into the house of uncircumcised men and ate with them."

column.name: text
column.value: Peter began and explained everything to them precisely as it had happened:

column.name: text
column.value: "I was in the city of Joppa praying, and in a trance I saw a vision. I saw something like a large sheet being let down from heaven by its four corners, and it came down to where I was.

column.name: text
column.value: I looked into it and saw four-footed animals of the earth, wild beasts, reptiles, and birds of the air.

column.name: text
column.value: Then I heard a voice telling me, 'Get up, Peter. Kill and eat.'

column.name: text
column.value: "I replied, 'Surely not, Lord! Nothing impure or unclean has ever entered my mouth.'

column.name: text
column.value: "The voice spoke from heaven a second time, 'Do not call anything impure that God has made clean.'

column.name: text
column.value: This happened three times, and then it was all pulled up to heaven again.

column.name: text
column.value: "Right then three men who had been sent to me from Caesarea stopped at the house where I was staying.

column.name: text
column.value: The Spirit told me to have no hesitation about going with them. These six brothers also went with me, and we entered the man's house.

column.name: text
column.value: He told us how he had seen an angel appear in his house and say, 'Send to Joppa for Simon who is called Peter.

column.name: text
column.value: He will bring you a message through which you and all your household will be saved.'

column.name: text
column.value: "As I began to speak, the Holy Spirit came on them as he had come on us at the beginning.

column.name: text
column.value: Then I remembered what the Lord had said: 'John baptized with water, but you will be baptized with the Holy Spirit.'

column.name: text
column.value: So if God gave them the same gift as he gave us, who believed in the Lord Jesus Christ, who was I to think that I could oppose God?"

column.name: text
column.value: When they heard this, they had no further objections and praised God, saying, "So then, God has granted even the Gentiles repentance unto life."

column.name: text
column.value: Now those who had been scattered by the persecution in connection with Stephen traveled as far as Phoenicia, Cyprus and Antioch, telling the message only to Jews.

column.name: text
column.value: Some of them, however, men from Cyprus and Cyrene, went to Antioch and began to speak to Greeks also, telling them the good news about the Lord Jesus.

column.name: text
column.value: The Lord's hand was with them, and a great number of people believed and turned to the Lord.

column.name: text
column.value: News of this reached the ears of the church at Jerusalem, and they sent Barnabas to Antioch.

column.name: text
column.value: When he arrived and saw the evidence of the grace of God, he was glad and encouraged them all to remain true to the Lord with all their hearts.

column.name: text
column.value: He was a good man, full of the Holy Spirit and faith, and a great number of people were brought to the Lord.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Barnabas went to Tarsus to look for Saul,

column.name: text
column.value: and when he found him, he brought him to Antioch. So for a whole year Barnabas and Saul met with the church and taught great numbers of people. The disciples were called Christians first at Antioch.

column.name: text
column.value: During this time some prophets came down from Jerusalem to Antioch.

column.name: text
column.value: One of them, named Agabus, stood up and through the Spirit predicted that a severe famine would spread over the entire Roman world. (This happened during the reign of Claudius.)

column.name: text
column.value: The disciples, each according to his ability, decided to provide help for the brothers living in Judea.

column.name: text
column.value: This they did, sending their gift to the elders by Barnabas and Saul.

column.name: text
column.value: Meanwhile, Saul was still breathing out murderous threats against the Lord's disciples. He went to the high priest

column.name: text
column.value: and asked him for letters to the synagogues in Damascus, so that if he found any there who belonged to the Way, whether men or women, he might take them as prisoners to Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: As he neared Damascus on his journey, suddenly a light from heaven flashed around him.

column.name: text
column.value: He fell to the ground and heard a voice say to him, "Saul, Saul, why do you persecute me?"

column.name: text
column.value: "Who are you, Lord?" Saul asked. "I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting," he replied.

column.name: text
column.value: "Now get up and go into the city, and you will be told what you must do."

column.name: text
column.value: The men traveling with Saul stood there speechless; they heard the sound but did not see anyone.

column.name: text
column.value: Saul got up from the ground, but when he opened his eyes he could see nothing. So they led him by the hand into Damascus.

column.name: text
column.value: For three days he was blind, and did not eat or drink anything.

column.name: text
column.value: In Damascus there was a disciple named Ananias. The Lord called to him in a vision, "Ananias!" "Yes, Lord," he answered.

column.name: text
column.value: The Lord told him, "Go to the house of Judas on Straight Street and ask for a man from Tarsus named Saul, for he is praying.

column.name: text
column.value: In a vision he has seen a man named Ananias come and place his hands on him to restore his sight."

column.name: text
column.value: "Lord," Ananias answered, "I have heard many reports about this man and all the harm he has done to your saints in Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: And he has come here with authority from the chief priests to arrest all who call on your name."

column.name: text
column.value: But the Lord said to Ananias, "Go! This man is my chosen instrument to carry my name before the Gentiles and their kings and before the people of Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: I will show him how much he must suffer for my name."

column.name: text
column.value: Then Ananias went to the house and entered it. Placing his hands on Saul, he said, "Brother Saul, the Lord--Jesus, who appeared to you on the road as you were coming here--has sent me so that you may see again and be filled with the Holy Spirit."

column.name: text
column.value: Immediately, something like scales fell from Saul's eyes, and he could see again. He got up and was baptized,

column.name: text
column.value: and after taking some food, he regained his strength. Saul spent several days with the disciples in Damascus.

column.name: text
column.value: At once he began to preach in the synagogues that Jesus is the Son of God.

column.name: text
column.value: All those who heard him were astonished and asked, "Isn't he the man who raised havoc in Jerusalem among those who call on this name? And hasn't he come here to take them as prisoners to the chief priests?"

column.name: text
column.value: Yet Saul grew more and more powerful and baffled the Jews living in Damascus by proving that Jesus is the Christ.

column.name: text
column.value: After many days had gone by, the Jews conspired to kill him,

column.name: text
column.value: but Saul learned of their plan. Day and night they kept close watch on the city gates in order to kill him.

column.name: text
column.value: But his followers took him by night and lowered him in a basket through an opening in the wall.

column.name: text
column.value: When he came to Jerusalem, he tried to join the disciples, but they were all afraid of him, not believing that he really was a disciple.

column.name: text
column.value: But Barnabas took him and brought him to the apostles. He told them how Saul on his journey had seen the Lord and that the Lord had spoken to him, and how in Damascus he had preached fearlessly in the name of Jesus.

column.name: text
column.value: So Saul stayed with them and moved about freely in Jerusalem, speaking boldly in the name of the Lord.

column.name: text
column.value: He talked and debated with the Grecian Jews, but they tried to kill him.

column.name: text
column.value: When the brothers learned of this, they took him down to Caesarea and sent him off to Tarsus.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the church throughout Judea, Galilee and Samaria enjoyed a time of peace. It was strengthened; and encouraged by the Holy Spirit, it grew in numbers, living in the fear of the Lord.

column.name: text
column.value: As Peter traveled about the country, he went to visit the saints in Lydda.

column.name: text
column.value: There he found a man named Aeneas, a paralytic who had been bedridden for eight years.

column.name: text
column.value: "Aeneas," Peter said to him, "Jesus Christ heals you. Get up and take care of your mat." Immediately Aeneas got up.

column.name: text
column.value: All those who lived in Lydda and Sharon saw him and turned to the Lord.

column.name: text
column.value: In Joppa there was a disciple named Tabitha (which, when translated, is Dorcas), who was always doing good and helping the poor.

column.name: text
column.value: About that time she became sick and died, and her body was washed and placed in an upstairs room.

column.name: text
column.value: Lydda was near Joppa; so when the disciples heard that Peter was in Lydda, they sent two men to him and urged him, "Please come at once!"

column.name: text
column.value: Peter went with them, and when he arrived he was taken upstairs to the room. All the widows stood around him, crying and showing him the robes and other clothing that Dorcas had made while she was still with them.

column.name: text
column.value: Peter sent them all out of the room; then he got down on his knees and prayed. Turning toward the dead woman, he said, "Tabitha, get up." She opened her eyes, and seeing Peter she sat up.

column.name: text
column.value: He took her by the hand and helped her to her feet. Then he called the believers and the widows and presented her to them alive.

column.name: text
column.value: This became known all over Joppa, and many people believed in the Lord.

column.name: text
column.value: Peter stayed in Joppa for some time with a tanner named Simon.

column.name: text
column.value: At Caesarea there was a man named Cornelius, a centurion in what was known as the Italian Regiment.

column.name: text
column.value: He and all his family were devout and God-fearing; he gave generously to those in need and prayed to God regularly.

column.name: text
column.value: One day at about three in the afternoon he had a vision. He distinctly saw an angel of God, who came to him and said, "Cornelius!"

column.name: text
column.value: Cornelius stared at him in fear. "What is it, Lord?" he asked. The angel answered, "Your prayers and gifts to the poor have come up as a memorial offering before God.

column.name: text
column.value: Now send men to Joppa to bring back a man named Simon who is called Peter.

column.name: text
column.value: He is staying with Simon the tanner, whose house is by the sea."

column.name: text
column.value: When the angel who spoke to him had gone, Cornelius called two of his servants and a devout soldier who was one of his attendants.

column.name: text
column.value: He told them everything that had happened and sent them to Joppa.

column.name: text
column.value: About noon the following day as they were on their journey and approaching the city, Peter went up on the roof to pray.

column.name: text
column.value: He became hungry and wanted something to eat, and while the meal was being prepared, he fell into a trance.

column.name: text
column.value: He saw heaven opened and something like a large sheet being let down to earth by its four corners.

column.name: text
column.value: It contained all kinds of four-footed animals, as well as reptiles of the earth and birds of the air.

column.name: text
column.value: Then a voice told him, "Get up, Peter. Kill and eat."

column.name: text
column.value: "Surely not, Lord!" Peter replied. "I have never eaten anything impure or unclean."

column.name: text
column.value: The voice spoke to him a second time, "Do not call anything impure that God has made clean."

column.name: text
column.value: This happened three times, and immediately the sheet was taken back to heaven.

column.name: text
column.value: While Peter was wondering about the meaning of the vision, the men sent by Cornelius found out where Simon's house was and stopped at the gate.

column.name: text
column.value: They called out, asking if Simon who was known as Peter was staying there.

column.name: text
column.value: While Peter was still thinking about the vision, the Spirit said to him, "Simon, three men are looking for you.

column.name: text
column.value: So get up and go downstairs. Do not hesitate to go with them, for I have sent them."

column.name: text
column.value: Peter went down and said to the men, "I'm the one you're looking for. Why have you come?"

column.name: text
column.value: The men replied, "We have come from Cornelius the centurion. He is a righteous and God-fearing man, who is respected by all the Jewish people. A holy angel told him to have you come to his house so that he could hear what you have to say."

column.name: text
column.value: Then Peter invited the men into the house to be his guests. The next day Peter started out with them, and some of the brothers from Joppa went along.

column.name: text
column.value: The following day he arrived in Caesarea. Cornelius was expecting them and had called together his relatives and close friends.

column.name: text
column.value: As Peter entered the house, Cornelius met him and fell at his feet in reverence.

column.name: text
column.value: But Peter made him get up. "Stand up," he said, "I am only a man myself."

column.name: text
column.value: Talking with him, Peter went inside and found a large gathering of people.

column.name: text
column.value: He said to them: "You are well aware that it is against our law for a Jew to associate with a Gentile or visit him. But God has shown me that I should not call any man impure or unclean.

column.name: text
column.value: So when I was sent for, I came without raising any objection. May I ask why you sent for me?"

column.name: text
column.value: Cornelius answered: "Four days ago I was in my house praying at this hour, at three in the afternoon. Suddenly a man in shining clothes stood before me

column.name: text
column.value: and said, 'Cornelius, God has heard your prayer and remembered your gifts to the poor.

column.name: text
column.value: Send to Joppa for Simon who is called Peter. He is a guest in the home of Simon the tanner, who lives by the sea.'

column.name: text
column.value: So I sent for you immediately, and it was good of you to come. Now we are all here in the presence of God to listen to everything the Lord has commanded you to tell us."

column.name: text
column.value: Then Peter began to speak: "I now realize how true it is that God does not show favoritism

column.name: text
column.value: but accepts men from every nation who fear him and do what is right.

column.name: text
column.value: You know the message God sent to the people of Israel, telling the good news of peace through Jesus Christ, who is Lord of all.

column.name: text
column.value: You know what has happened throughout Judea, beginning in Galilee after the baptism that John preached--

column.name: text
column.value: how God anointed Jesus of Nazareth with the Holy Spirit and power, and how he went around doing good and healing all who were under the power of the devil, because God was with him.

column.name: text
column.value: "We are witnesses of everything he did in the country of the Jews and in Jerusalem. They killed him by hanging him on a tree,

column.name: text
column.value: but God raised him from the dead on the third day and caused him to be seen.

column.name: text
column.value: He was not seen by all the people, but by witnesses whom God had already chosen--by us who ate and drank with him after he rose from the dead.

column.name: text
column.value: He commanded us to preach to the people and to testify that he is the one whom God appointed as judge of the living and the dead.

column.name: text
column.value: All the prophets testify about him that everyone who believes in him receives forgiveness of sins through his name."

column.name: text
column.value: While Peter was still speaking these words, the Holy Spirit came on all who heard the message.

column.name: text
column.value: The circumcised believers who had come with Peter were astonished that the gift of the Holy Spirit had been poured out even on the Gentiles.

column.name: text
column.value: For they heard them speaking in tongues and praising God. Then Peter said,

column.name: text
column.value: "Can anyone keep these people from being baptized with water? They have received the Holy Spirit just as we have."

column.name: text
column.value: So he ordered that they be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ. Then they asked Peter to stay with them for a few days.

column.name: text
column.value: It was about this time that King Herod arrested some who belonged to the church, intending to persecute them.

column.name: text
column.value: He had James, the brother of John, put to death with the sword.

column.name: text
column.value: When he saw that this pleased the Jews, he proceeded to seize Peter also. This happened during the Feast of Unleavened Bread.

column.name: text
column.value: After arresting him, he put him in prison, handing him over to be guarded by four squads of four soldiers each. Herod intended to bring him out for public trial after the Passover.

column.name: text
column.value: So Peter was kept in prison, but the church was earnestly praying to God for him.

column.name: text
column.value: The night before Herod was to bring him to trial, Peter was sleeping between two soldiers, bound with two chains, and sentries stood guard at the entrance.

column.name: text
column.value: Suddenly an angel of the Lord appeared and a light shone in the cell. He struck Peter on the side and woke him up. "Quick, get up!" he said, and the chains fell off Peter's wrists.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the angel said to him, "Put on your clothes and sandals." And Peter did so. "Wrap your cloak around you and follow me," the angel told him.

column.name: text
column.value: Peter followed him out of the prison, but he had no idea that what the angel was doing was really happening; he thought he was seeing a vision.

column.name: text
column.value: They passed the first and second guards and came to the iron gate leading to the city. It opened for them by itself, and they went through it. When they had walked the length of one street, suddenly the angel left him.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Peter came to himself and said, "Now I know without a doubt that the Lord sent his angel and rescued me from Herod's clutches and from everything the Jewish people were anticipating."

column.name: text
column.value: When this had dawned on him, he went to the house of Mary the mother of John, also called Mark, where many people had gathered and were praying.

column.name: text
column.value: Peter knocked at the outer entrance, and a servant girl named Rhoda came to answer the door.

column.name: text
column.value: When she recognized Peter's voice, she was so overjoyed she ran back without opening it and exclaimed, "Peter is at the door!"

column.name: text
column.value: "You're out of your mind," they told her. When she kept insisting that it was so, they said, "It must be his angel."

column.name: text
column.value: But Peter kept on knocking, and when they opened the door and saw him, they were astonished.

column.name: text
column.value: Peter motioned with his hand for them to be quiet and described how the Lord had brought him out of prison. "Tell James and the brothers about this," he said, and then he left for another place.

column.name: text
column.value: In the morning, there was no small commotion among the soldiers as to what had become of Peter.

column.name: text
column.value: After Herod had a thorough search made for him and did not find him, he cross-examined the guards and ordered that they be executed. Then Herod went from Judea to Caesarea and stayed there a while.

column.name: text
column.value: He had been quarreling with the people of Tyre and Sidon; they now joined together and sought an audience with him. Having secured the support of Blastus, a trusted personal servant of the king, they asked for peace, because they depended on the king's country for their food supply.

column.name: text
column.value: On the appointed day Herod, wearing his royal robes, sat on his throne and delivered a public address to the people.

column.name: text
column.value: They shouted, "This is the voice of a god, not of a man."

column.name: text
column.value: Immediately, because Herod did not give praise to God, an angel of the Lord struck him down, and he was eaten by worms and died.

column.name: text
column.value: But the word of God continued to increase and spread.

column.name: text
column.value: When Barnabas and Saul had finished their mission, they returned from Jerusalem, taking with them John, also called Mark.

column.name: text
column.value: In the church at Antioch there were prophets and teachers: Barnabas, Simeon called Niger, Lucius of Cyrene, Manaen (who had been brought up with Herod the tetrarch) and Saul.

column.name: text
column.value: While they were worshiping the Lord and fasting, the Holy Spirit said, "Set apart for me Barnabas and Saul for the work to which I have called them."

column.name: text
column.value: So after they had fasted and prayed, they placed their hands on them and sent them off.

column.name: text
column.value: The two of them, sent on their way by the Holy Spirit, went down to Seleucia and sailed from there to Cyprus.

column.name: text
column.value: When they arrived at Salamis, they proclaimed the word of God in the Jewish synagogues. John was with them as their helper.

column.name: text
column.value: They traveled through the whole island until they came to Paphos. There they met a Jewish sorcerer and false prophet named Bar-Jesus,

column.name: text
column.value: who was an attendant of the proconsul, Sergius Paulus. The proconsul, an intelligent man, sent for Barnabas and Saul because he wanted to hear the word of God.

column.name: text
column.value: But Elymas the sorcerer (for that is what his name means) opposed them and tried to turn the proconsul from the faith.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Saul, who was also called Paul, filled with the Holy Spirit, looked straight at Elymas and said,

column.name: text
column.value: "You are a child of the devil and an enemy of everything that is right! You are full of all kinds of deceit and trickery. Will you never stop perverting the right ways of the Lord?

column.name: text
column.value: Now the hand of the Lord is against you. You are going to be blind, and for a time you will be unable to see the light of the sun." Immediately mist and darkness came over him, and he groped about, seeking someone to lead him by the hand.

column.name: text
column.value: When the proconsul saw what had happened, he believed, for he was amazed at the teaching about the Lord.

column.name: text
column.value: From Paphos, Paul and his companions sailed to Perga in Pamphylia, where John left them to return to Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: From Perga they went on to Pisidian Antioch. On the Sabbath they entered the synagogue and sat down.

column.name: text
column.value: After the reading from the Law and the Prophets, the synagogue rulers sent word to them, saying, "Brothers, if you have a message of encouragement for the people, please speak."

column.name: text
column.value: Standing up, Paul motioned with his hand and said: "Men of Israel and you Gentiles who worship God, listen to me!

column.name: text
column.value: The God of the people of Israel chose our fathers; he made the people prosper during their stay in Egypt, with mighty power he led them out of that country,

column.name: text
column.value: he endured their conduct for about forty years in the desert,

column.name: text
column.value: he overthrew seven nations in Canaan and gave their land to his people as their inheritance.

column.name: text
column.value: All this took about 450 years. "After this, God gave them judges until the time of Samuel the prophet.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the people asked for a king, and he gave them Saul son of Kish, of the tribe of Benjamin, who ruled forty years.

column.name: text
column.value: After removing Saul, he made David their king. He testified concerning him: 'I have found David son of Jesse a man after my own heart; he will do everything I want him to do.'

column.name: text
column.value: "From this man's descendants God has brought to Israel the Savior Jesus, as he promised.

column.name: text
column.value: Before the coming of Jesus, John preached repentance and baptism to all the people of Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: As John was completing his work, he said: 'Who do you think I am? I am not that one. No, but he is coming after me, whose sandals I am not worthy to untie.'

column.name: text
column.value: "Brothers, children of Abraham, and you God-fearing Gentiles, it is to us that this message of salvation has been sent.

column.name: text
column.value: The people of Jerusalem and their rulers did not recognize Jesus, yet in condemning him they fulfilled the words of the prophets that are read every Sabbath.

column.name: text
column.value: Though they found no proper ground for a death sentence, they asked Pilate to have him executed.

column.name: text
column.value: When they had carried out all that was written about him, they took him down from the tree and laid him in a tomb.

column.name: text
column.value: But God raised him from the dead,

column.name: text
column.value: and for many days he was seen by those who had traveled with him from Galilee to Jerusalem. They are now his witnesses to our people.

column.name: text
column.value: "We tell you the good news: What God promised our fathers

column.name: text
column.value: he has fulfilled for us, their children, by raising up Jesus. As it is written in the second Psalm: "'You are my Son; today I have become your Father.'

column.name: text
column.value: The fact that God raised him from the dead, never to decay, is stated in these words: "'I will give you the holy and sure blessings promised to David.'

column.name: text
column.value: So it is stated elsewhere: "'You will not let your Holy One see decay.'

column.name: text
column.value: "For when David had served God's purpose in his own generation, he fell asleep; he was buried with his fathers and his body decayed.

column.name: text
column.value: But the one whom God raised from the dead did not see decay.

column.name: text
column.value: "Therefore, my brothers, I want you to know that through Jesus the forgiveness of sins is proclaimed to you.

column.name: text
column.value: Through him everyone who believes is justified from everything you could not be justified from by the law of Moses.

column.name: text
column.value: Take care that what the prophets have said does not happen to you:

column.name: text
column.value: "'Look, you scoffers, wonder and perish, for I am going to do something in your days that you would never believe, even if someone told you.'"

column.name: text
column.value: As Paul and Barnabas were leaving the synagogue, the people invited them to speak further about these things on the next Sabbath.

column.name: text
column.value: When the congregation was dismissed, many of the Jews and devout converts to Judaism followed Paul and Barnabas, who talked with them and urged them to continue in the grace of God.

column.name: text
column.value: On the next Sabbath almost the whole city gathered to hear the word of the Lord.

column.name: text
column.value: When the Jews saw the crowds, they were filled with jealousy and talked abusively against what Paul was saying.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Paul and Barnabas answered them boldly: "We had to speak the word of God to you first. Since you reject it and do not consider yourselves worthy of eternal life, we now turn to the Gentiles.

column.name: text
column.value: For this is what the Lord has commanded us: "'I have made you a light for the Gentiles, that you may bring salvation to the ends of the earth.'"

column.name: text
column.value: When the Gentiles heard this, they were glad and honored the word of the Lord; and all who were appointed for eternal life believed.

column.name: text
column.value: The word of the Lord spread through the whole region.

column.name: text
column.value: But the Jews incited the God-fearing women of high standing and the leading men of the city. They stirred up persecution against Paul and Barnabas, and expelled them from their region.

column.name: text
column.value: So they shook the dust from their feet in protest against them and went to Iconium.

column.name: text
column.value: And the disciples were filled with joy and with the Holy Spirit.

column.name: text
column.value: Some men came down from Judea to Antioch and were teaching the brothers: "Unless you are circumcised, according to the custom taught by Moses, you cannot be saved."

column.name: text
column.value: This brought Paul and Barnabas into sharp dispute and debate with them. So Paul and Barnabas were appointed, along with some other believers, to go up to Jerusalem to see the apostles and elders about this question.

column.name: text
column.value: The church sent them on their way, and as they traveled through Phoenicia and Samaria, they told how the Gentiles had been converted. This news made all the brothers very glad.

column.name: text
column.value: When they came to Jerusalem, they were welcomed by the church and the apostles and elders, to whom they reported everything God had done through them.

column.name: text
column.value: Then some of the believers who belonged to the party of the Pharisees stood up and said, "The Gentiles must be circumcised and required to obey the law of Moses."

column.name: text
column.value: The apostles and elders met to consider this question.

column.name: text
column.value: After much discussion, Peter got up and addressed them: "Brothers, you know that some time ago God made a choice among you that the Gentiles might hear from my lips the message of the gospel and believe.

column.name: text
column.value: God, who knows the heart, showed that he accepted them by giving the Holy Spirit to them, just as he did to us.

column.name: text
column.value: He made no distinction between us and them, for he purified their hearts by faith.

column.name: text
column.value: Now then, why do you try to test God by putting on the necks of the disciples a yoke that neither we nor our fathers have been able to bear?

column.name: text
column.value: No! We believe it is through the grace of our Lord Jesus that we are saved, just as they are."

column.name: text
column.value: The whole assembly became silent as they listened to Barnabas and Paul telling about the miraculous signs and wonders God had done among the Gentiles through them.

column.name: text
column.value: When they finished, James spoke up: "Brothers, listen to me.

column.name: text
column.value: Simon has described to us how God at first showed his concern by taking from the Gentiles a people for himself.

column.name: text
column.value: The words of the prophets are in agreement with this, as it is written:

column.name: text
column.value: "'After this I will return and rebuild David's fallen tent. Its ruins I will rebuild, and I will restore it,

column.name: text
column.value: that the remnant of men may seek the Lord, and all the Gentiles who bear my name, says the Lord, who does these things'

column.name: text
column.value: that have been known for ages.

column.name: text
column.value: "It is my judgment, therefore, that we should not make it difficult for the Gentiles who are turning to God.

column.name: text
column.value: Instead we should write to them, telling them to abstain from food polluted by idols, from sexual immorality, from the meat of strangled animals and from blood.

column.name: text
column.value: For Moses has been preached in every city from the earliest times and is read in the synagogues on every Sabbath."

column.name: text
column.value: Then the apostles and elders, with the whole church, decided to choose some of their own men and send them to Antioch with Paul and Barnabas. They chose Judas (called Barsabbas) and Silas, two men who were leaders among the brothers.

column.name: text
column.value: With them they sent the following letter: The apostles and elders, your brothers, To the Gentile believers in Antioch, Syria and Cilicia: Greetings.

column.name: text
column.value: We have heard that some went out from us without our authorization and disturbed you, troubling your minds by what they said.

column.name: text
column.value: So we all agreed to choose some men and send them to you with our dear friends Barnabas and Paul--

column.name: text
column.value: men who have risked their lives for the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore we are sending Judas and Silas to confirm by word of mouth what we are writing.

column.name: text
column.value: It seemed good to the Holy Spirit and to us not to burden you with anything beyond the following requirements:

column.name: text
column.value: You are to abstain from food sacrificed to idols, from blood, from the meat of strangled animals and from sexual immorality. You will do well to avoid these things. Farewell.

column.name: text
column.value: The men were sent off and went down to Antioch, where they gathered the church together and delivered the letter.

column.name: text
column.value: The people read it and were glad for its encouraging message.

column.name: text
column.value: Judas and Silas, who themselves were prophets, said much to encourage and strengthen the brothers.

column.name: text
column.value: After spending some time there, they were sent off by the brothers with the blessing of peace to return to those who had sent them.

column.name: text
column.value: But Paul and Barnabas remained in Antioch, where they and many others taught and preached the word of the Lord.

column.name: text
column.value: Some time later Paul said to Barnabas, "Let us go back and visit the brothers in all the towns where we preached the word of the Lord and see how they are doing."

column.name: text
column.value: Barnabas wanted to take John, also called Mark, with them,

column.name: text
column.value: but Paul did not think it wise to take him, because he had deserted them in Pamphylia and had not continued with them in the work.

column.name: text
column.value: They had such a sharp disagreement that they parted company. Barnabas took Mark and sailed for Cyprus,

column.name: text
column.value: but Paul chose Silas and left, commended by the brothers to the grace of the Lord.

column.name: text
column.value: He went through Syria and Cilicia, strengthening the churches.

column.name: text
column.value: He came to Derbe and then to Lystra, where a disciple named Timothy lived, whose mother was a Jewess and a believer, but whose father was a Greek.

column.name: text
column.value: The brothers at Lystra and Iconium spoke well of him.

column.name: text
column.value: Paul wanted to take him along on the journey, so he circumcised him because of the Jews who lived in that area, for they all knew that his father was a Greek.

column.name: text
column.value: As they traveled from town to town, they delivered the decisions reached by the apostles and elders in Jerusalem for the people to obey.

column.name: text
column.value: So the churches were strengthened in the faith and grew daily in numbers.

column.name: text
column.value: Paul and his companions traveled throughout the region of Phrygia and Galatia, having been kept by the Holy Spirit from preaching the word in the province of Asia.

column.name: text
column.value: When they came to the border of Mysia, they tried to enter Bithynia, but the Spirit of Jesus would not allow them to.

column.name: text
column.value: So they passed by Mysia and went down to Troas.

column.name: text
column.value: During the night Paul had a vision of a man of Macedonia standing and begging him, "Come over to Macedonia and help us."

column.name: text
column.value: After Paul had seen the vision, we got ready at once to leave for Macedonia, concluding that God had called us to preach the gospel to them.

column.name: text
column.value: From Troas we put out to sea and sailed straight for Samothrace, and the next day on to Neapolis.

column.name: text
column.value: From there we traveled to Philippi, a Roman colony and the leading city of that district of Macedonia. And we stayed there several days.

column.name: text
column.value: On the Sabbath we went outside the city gate to the river, where we expected to find a place of prayer. We sat down and began to speak to the women who had gathered there.

column.name: text
column.value: One of those listening was a woman named Lydia, a dealer in purple cloth from the city of Thyatira, who was a worshiper of God. The Lord opened her heart to respond to Paul's message.

column.name: text
column.value: When she and the members of her household were baptized, she invited us to her home. "If you consider me a believer in the Lord," she said, "come and stay at my house." And she persuaded us.

column.name: text
column.value: Once when we were going to the place of prayer, we were met by a slave girl who had a spirit by which she predicted the future. She earned a great deal of money for her owners by fortune-telling.

column.name: text
column.value: This girl followed Paul and the rest of us, shouting, "These men are servants of the Most High God, who are telling you the way to be saved."

column.name: text
column.value: She kept this up for many days. Finally Paul became so troubled that he turned around and said to the spirit, "In the name of Jesus Christ I command you to come out of her!" At that moment the spirit left her.

column.name: text
column.value: When the owners of the slave girl realized that their hope of making money was gone, they seized Paul and Silas and dragged them into the marketplace to face the authorities.

column.name: text
column.value: They brought them before the magistrates and said, "These men are Jews, and are throwing our city into an uproar

column.name: text
column.value: by advocating customs unlawful for us Romans to accept or practice."

column.name: text
column.value: The crowd joined in the attack against Paul and Silas, and the magistrates ordered them to be stripped and beaten.

column.name: text
column.value: After they had been severely flogged, they were thrown into prison, and the jailer was commanded to guard them carefully.

column.name: text
column.value: Upon receiving such orders, he put them in the inner cell and fastened their feet in the stocks.

column.name: text
column.value: About midnight Paul and Silas were praying and singing hymns to God, and the other prisoners were listening to them.

column.name: text
column.value: Suddenly there was such a violent earthquake that the foundations of the prison were shaken. At once all the prison doors flew open, and everybody's chains came loose.

column.name: text
column.value: The jailer woke up, and when he saw the prison doors open, he drew his sword and was about to kill himself because he thought the prisoners had escaped.

column.name: text
column.value: But Paul shouted, "Don't harm yourself! We are all here!"

column.name: text
column.value: The jailer called for lights, rushed in and fell trembling before Paul and Silas.

column.name: text
column.value: He then brought them out and asked, "Sirs, what must I do to be saved?"

column.name: text
column.value: They replied, "Believe in the Lord Jesus, and you will be saved--you and your household."

column.name: text
column.value: Then they spoke the word of the Lord to him and to all the others in his house.

column.name: text
column.value: At that hour of the night the jailer took them and washed their wounds; then immediately he and all his family were baptized.

column.name: text
column.value: The jailer brought them into his house and set a meal before them; he was filled with joy because he had come to believe in God--he and his whole family.

column.name: text
column.value: When it was daylight, the magistrates sent their officers to the jailer with the order: "Release those men."

column.name: text
column.value: The jailer told Paul, "The magistrates have ordered that you and Silas be released. Now you can leave. Go in peace."

column.name: text
column.value: But Paul said to the officers: "They beat us publicly without a trial, even though we are Roman citizens, and threw us into prison. And now do they want to get rid of us quietly? No! Let them come themselves and escort us out."

column.name: text
column.value: The officers reported this to the magistrates, and when they heard that Paul and Silas were Roman citizens, they were alarmed.

column.name: text
column.value: They came to appease them and escorted them from the prison, requesting them to leave the city.

column.name: text
column.value: After Paul and Silas came out of the prison, they went to Lydia's house, where they met with the brothers and encouraged them. Then they left.

column.name: text
column.value: At Iconium Paul and Barnabas went as usual into the Jewish synagogue. There they spoke so effectively that a great number of Jews and Gentiles believed.

column.name: text
column.value: But the Jews who refused to believe stirred up the Gentiles and poisoned their minds against the brothers.

column.name: text
column.value: So Paul and Barnabas spent considerable time there, speaking boldly for the Lord, who confirmed the message of his grace by enabling them to do miraculous signs and wonders.

column.name: text
column.value: The people of the city were divided; some sided with the Jews, others with the apostles.

column.name: text
column.value: There was a plot afoot among the Gentiles and Jews, together with their leaders, to mistreat them and stone them.

column.name: text
column.value: But they found out about it and fled to the Lycaonian cities of Lystra and Derbe and to the surrounding country,

column.name: text
column.value: where they continued to preach the good news.

column.name: text
column.value: In Lystra there sat a man crippled in his feet, who was lame from birth and had never walked.

column.name: text
column.value: He listened to Paul as he was speaking. Paul looked directly at him, saw that he had faith to be healed

column.name: text
column.value: and called out, "Stand up on your feet!" At that, the man jumped up and began to walk.

column.name: text
column.value: When the crowd saw what Paul had done, they shouted in the Lycaonian language, "The gods have come down to us in human form!"

column.name: text
column.value: Barnabas they called Zeus, and Paul they called Hermes because he was the chief speaker.

column.name: text
column.value: The priest of Zeus, whose temple was just outside the city, brought bulls and wreaths to the city gates because he and the crowd wanted to offer sacrifices to them.

column.name: text
column.value: But when the apostles Barnabas and Paul heard of this, they tore their clothes and rushed out into the crowd, shouting:

column.name: text
column.value: "Men, why are you doing this? We too are only men, human like you. We are bringing you good news, telling you to turn from these worthless things to the living God, who made heaven and earth and sea and everything in them.

column.name: text
column.value: In the past, he let all nations go their own way.

column.name: text
column.value: Yet he has not left himself without testimony: He has shown kindness by giving you rain from heaven and crops in their seasons; he provides you with plenty of food and fills your hearts with joy."

column.name: text
column.value: Even with these words, they had difficulty keeping the crowd from sacrificing to them.

column.name: text
column.value: Then some Jews came from Antioch and Iconium and won the crowd over. They stoned Paul and dragged him outside the city, thinking he was dead.

column.name: text
column.value: But after the disciples had gathered around him, he got up and went back into the city. The next day he and Barnabas left for Derbe.

column.name: text
column.value: They preached the good news in that city and won a large number of disciples. Then they returned to Lystra, Iconium and Antioch,

column.name: text
column.value: strengthening the disciples and encouraging them to remain true to the faith. "We must go through many hardships to enter the kingdom of God," they said.

column.name: text
column.value: Paul and Barnabas appointed elders for them in each church and, with prayer and fasting, committed them to the Lord, in whom they had put their trust.

column.name: text
column.value: After going through Pisidia, they came into Pamphylia,

column.name: text
column.value: and when they had preached the word in Perga, they went down to Attalia.

column.name: text
column.value: From Attalia they sailed back to Antioch, where they had been committed to the grace of God for the work they had now completed.

column.name: text
column.value: On arriving there, they gathered the church together and reported all that God had done through them and how he had opened the door of faith to the Gentiles.

column.name: text
column.value: And they stayed there a long time with the disciples.

column.name: text
column.value: When they had passed through Amphipolis and Apollonia, they came to Thessalonica, where there was a Jewish synagogue.

column.name: text
column.value: As his custom was, Paul went into the synagogue, and on three Sabbath days he reasoned with them from the Scriptures,

column.name: text
column.value: explaining and proving that the Christ had to suffer and rise from the dead. "This Jesus I am proclaiming to you is the Christ," he said.

column.name: text
column.value: Some of the Jews were persuaded and joined Paul and Silas, as did a large number of God-fearing Greeks and not a few prominent women.

column.name: text
column.value: But the Jews were jealous; so they rounded up some bad characters from the marketplace, formed a mob and started a riot in the city. They rushed to Jason's house in search of Paul and Silas in order to bring them out to the crowd.

column.name: text
column.value: But when they did not find them, they dragged Jason and some other brothers before the city officials, shouting: "These men who have caused trouble all over the world have now come here,

column.name: text
column.value: and Jason has welcomed them into his house. They are all defying Caesar's decrees, saying that there is another king, one called Jesus."

column.name: text
column.value: When they heard this, the crowd and the city officials were thrown into turmoil.

column.name: text
column.value: Then they made Jason and the others post bond and let them go.

column.name: text
column.value: As soon as it was night, the brothers sent Paul and Silas away to Berea. On arriving there, they went to the Jewish synagogue.

column.name: text
column.value: Now the Bereans were of more noble character than the Thessalonians, for they received the message with great eagerness and examined the Scriptures every day to see if what Paul said was true.

column.name: text
column.value: Many of the Jews believed, as did also a number of prominent Greek women and many Greek men.

column.name: text
column.value: When the Jews in Thessalonica learned that Paul was preaching the word of God at Berea, they went there too, agitating the crowds and stirring them up.

column.name: text
column.value: The brothers immediately sent Paul to the coast, but Silas and Timothy stayed at Berea.

column.name: text
column.value: The men who escorted Paul brought him to Athens and then left with instructions for Silas and Timothy to join him as soon as possible.

column.name: text
column.value: While Paul was waiting for them in Athens, he was greatly distressed to see that the city was full of idols.

column.name: text
column.value: So he reasoned in the synagogue with the Jews and the God-fearing Greeks, as well as in the marketplace day by day with those who happened to be there.

column.name: text
column.value: A group of Epicurean and Stoic philosophers began to dispute with him. Some of them asked, "What is this babbler trying to say?" Others remarked, "He seems to be advocating foreign gods." They said this because Paul was preaching the good news about Jesus and the resurrection.

column.name: text
column.value: Then they took him and brought him to a meeting of the Areopagus, where they said to him, "May we know what this new teaching is that you are presenting?

column.name: text
column.value: You are bringing some strange ideas to our ears, and we want to know what they mean."

column.name: text
column.value: (All the Athenians and the foreigners who lived there spent their time doing nothing but talking about and listening to the latest ideas.)

column.name: text
column.value: Paul then stood up in the meeting of the Areopagus and said: "Men of Athens! I see that in every way you are very religious.

column.name: text
column.value: For as I walked around and looked carefully at your objects of worship, I even found an altar with this inscription: TO AN UNKNOWN GOD. Now what you worship as something unknown I am going to proclaim to you.

column.name: text
column.value: "The God who made the world and everything in it is the Lord of heaven and earth and does not live in temples built by hands.

column.name: text
column.value: And he is not served by human hands, as if he needed anything, because he himself gives all men life and breath and everything else.

column.name: text
column.value: From one man he made every nation of men, that they should inhabit the whole earth; and he determined the times set for them and the exact places where they should live.

column.name: text
column.value: God did this so that men would seek him and perhaps reach out for him and find him, though he is not far from each one of us.

column.name: text
column.value: 'For in him we live and move and have our being.' As some of your own poets have said, 'We are his offspring.'

column.name: text
column.value: "Therefore since we are God's offspring, we should not think that the divine being is like gold or silver or stone--an image made by man's design and skill.

column.name: text
column.value: In the past God overlooked such ignorance, but now he commands all people everywhere to repent.

column.name: text
column.value: For he has set a day when he will judge the world with justice by the man he has appointed. He has given proof of this to all men by raising him from the dead."

column.name: text
column.value: When they heard about the resurrection of the dead, some of them sneered, but others said, "We want to hear you again on this subject."

column.name: text
column.value: At that, Paul left the Council.

column.name: text
column.value: A few men became followers of Paul and believed. Among them was Dionysius, a member of the Areopagus, also a woman named Damaris, and a number of others.

column.name: text
column.value: After this, Paul left Athens and went to Corinth.

column.name: text
column.value: There he met a Jew named Aquila, a native of Pontus, who had recently come from Italy with his wife Priscilla, because Claudius had ordered all the Jews to leave Rome. Paul went to see them,

column.name: text
column.value: and because he was a tentmaker as they were, he stayed and worked with them.

column.name: text
column.value: Every Sabbath he reasoned in the synagogue, trying to persuade Jews and Greeks.

column.name: text
column.value: When Silas and Timothy came from Macedonia, Paul devoted himself exclusively to preaching, testifying to the Jews that Jesus was the Christ.

column.name: text
column.value: But when the Jews opposed Paul and became abusive, he shook out his clothes in protest and said to them, "Your blood be on your own heads! I am clear of my responsibility. From now on I will go to the Gentiles."

column.name: text
column.value: Then Paul left the synagogue and went next door to the house of Titius Justus, a worshiper of God.

column.name: text
column.value: Crispus, the synagogue ruler, and his entire household believed in the Lord; and many of the Corinthians who heard him believed and were baptized.

column.name: text
column.value: One night the Lord spoke to Paul in a vision: "Do not be afraid; keep on speaking, do not be silent.

column.name: text
column.value: For I am with you, and no one is going to attack and harm you, because I have many people in this city."

column.name: text
column.value: So Paul stayed for a year and a half, teaching them the word of God.

column.name: text
column.value: While Gallio was proconsul of Achaia, the Jews made a united attack on Paul and brought him into court.

column.name: text
column.value: "This man," they charged, "is persuading the people to worship God in ways contrary to the law."

column.name: text
column.value: Just as Paul was about to speak, Gallio said to the Jews, "If you Jews were making a complaint about some misdemeanor or serious crime, it would be reasonable for me to listen to you.

column.name: text
column.value: But since it involves questions about words and names and your own law--settle the matter yourselves. I will not be a judge of such things."

column.name: text
column.value: So he had them ejected from the court.

column.name: text
column.value: Then they all turned on Sosthenes the synagogue ruler and beat him in front of the court. But Gallio showed no concern whatever.

column.name: text
column.value: Paul stayed on in Corinth for some time. Then he left the brothers and sailed for Syria, accompanied by Priscilla and Aquila. Before he sailed, he had his hair cut off at Cenchrea because of a vow he had taken.

column.name: text
column.value: They arrived at Ephesus, where Paul left Priscilla and Aquila. He himself went into the synagogue and reasoned with the Jews.

column.name: text
column.value: When they asked him to spend more time with them, he declined.

column.name: text
column.value: But as he left, he promised, "I will come back if it is God's will." Then he set sail from Ephesus.

column.name: text
column.value: When he landed at Caesarea, he went up and greeted the church and then went down to Antioch.

column.name: text
column.value: After spending some time in Antioch, Paul set out from there and traveled from place to place throughout the region of Galatia and Phrygia, strengthening all the disciples.

column.name: text
column.value: Meanwhile a Jew named Apollos, a native of Alexandria, came to Ephesus. He was a learned man, with a thorough knowledge of the Scriptures.

column.name: text
column.value: He had been instructed in the way of the Lord, and he spoke with great fervor and taught about Jesus accurately, though he knew only the baptism of John.

column.name: text
column.value: He began to speak boldly in the synagogue. When Priscilla and Aquila heard him, they invited him to their home and explained to him the way of God more adequately.

column.name: text
column.value: When Apollos wanted to go to Achaia, the brothers encouraged him and wrote to the disciples there to welcome him. On arriving, he was a great help to those who by grace had believed.

column.name: text
column.value: For he vigorously refuted the Jews in public debate, proving from the Scriptures that Jesus was the Christ.

column.name: text
column.value: While Apollos was at Corinth, Paul took the road through the interior and arrived at Ephesus. There he found some disciples

column.name: text
column.value: and asked them, "Did you receive the Holy Spirit when you believed?" They answered, "No, we have not even heard that there is a Holy Spirit."

column.name: text
column.value: So Paul asked, "Then what baptism did you receive?" "John's baptism," they replied.

column.name: text
column.value: Paul said, "John's baptism was a baptism of repentance. He told the people to believe in the one coming after him, that is, in Jesus."

column.name: text
column.value: On hearing this, they were baptized into the name of the Lord Jesus.

column.name: text
column.value: When Paul placed his hands on them, the Holy Spirit came on them, and they spoke in tongues and prophesied.

column.name: text
column.value: There were about twelve men in all.
