column.name: text
column.value: Paul entered the synagogue and spoke boldly there for three months, arguing persuasively about the kingdom of God.

column.name: text
column.value: But some of them became obstinate; they refused to believe and publicly maligned the Way. So Paul left them. He took the disciples with him and had discussions daily in the lecture hall of Tyrannus.

column.name: text
column.value: This went on for two years, so that all the Jews and Greeks who lived in the province of Asia heard the word of the Lord.

column.name: text
column.value: God did extraordinary miracles through Paul,

column.name: text
column.value: so that even handkerchiefs and aprons that had touched him were taken to the sick, and their illnesses were cured and the evil spirits left them.

column.name: text
column.value: Some Jews who went around driving out evil spirits tried to invoke the name of the Lord Jesus over those who were demon-possessed. They would say, "In the name of Jesus, whom Paul preaches, I command you to come out."

column.name: text
column.value: Seven sons of Sceva, a Jewish chief priest, were doing this.

column.name: text
column.value: One day the evil spirit answered them, "Jesus I know, and I know about Paul, but who are you?"

column.name: text
column.value: Then the man who had the evil spirit jumped on them and overpowered them all. He gave them such a beating that they ran out of the house naked and bleeding.

column.name: text
column.value: When this became known to the Jews and Greeks living in Ephesus, they were all seized with fear, and the name of the Lord Jesus was held in high honor.

column.name: text
column.value: Many of those who believed now came and openly confessed their evil deeds.

column.name: text
column.value: A number who had practiced sorcery brought their scrolls together and burned them publicly. When they calculated the value of the scrolls, the total came to fifty thousand drachmas.

column.name: text
column.value: In this way the word of the Lord spread widely and grew in power.

column.name: text
column.value: After all this had happened, Paul decided to go to Jerusalem, passing through Macedonia and Achaia. "After I have been there," he said, "I must visit Rome also."

column.name: text
column.value: He sent two of his helpers, Timothy and Erastus, to Macedonia, while he stayed in the province of Asia a little longer.

column.name: text
column.value: About that time there arose a great disturbance about the Way.

column.name: text
column.value: A silversmith named Demetrius, who made silver shrines of Artemis, brought in no little business for the craftsmen.

column.name: text
column.value: He called them together, along with the workmen in related trades, and said: "Men, you know we receive a good income from this business.

column.name: text
column.value: And you see and hear how this fellow Paul has convinced and led astray large numbers of people here in Ephesus and in practically the whole province of Asia. He says that man-made gods are no gods at all.

column.name: text
column.value: There is danger not only that our trade will lose its good name, but also that the temple of the great goddess Artemis will be discredited, and the goddess herself, who is worshiped throughout the province of Asia and the world, will be robbed of her divine majesty."

column.name: text
column.value: When they heard this, they were furious and began shouting: "Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!"

column.name: text
column.value: Soon the whole city was in an uproar. The people seized Gaius and Aristarchus, Paul's traveling companions from Macedonia, and rushed as one man into the theater.

column.name: text
column.value: Paul wanted to appear before the crowd, but the disciples would not let him.

column.name: text
column.value: Even some of the officials of the province, friends of Paul, sent him a message begging him not to venture into the theater.

column.name: text
column.value: The assembly was in confusion: Some were shouting one thing, some another. Most of the people did not even know why they were there.

column.name: text
column.value: The Jews pushed Alexander to the front, and some of the crowd shouted instructions to him. He motioned for silence in order to make a defense before the people.

column.name: text
column.value: But when they realized he was a Jew, they all shouted in unison for about two hours: "Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!"

column.name: text
column.value: The city clerk quieted the crowd and said: "Men of Ephesus, doesn't all the world know that the city of Ephesus is the guardian of the temple of the great Artemis and of her image, which fell from heaven?

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore, since these facts are undeniable, you ought to be quiet and not do anything rash.

column.name: text
column.value: You have brought these men here, though they have neither robbed temples nor blasphemed our goddess.

column.name: text
column.value: If, then, Demetrius and his fellow craftsmen have a grievance against anybody, the courts are open and there are proconsuls. They can press charges.

column.name: text
column.value: If there is anything further you want to bring up, it must be settled in a legal assembly.

column.name: text
column.value: As it is, we are in danger of being charged with rioting because of today's events. In that case we would not be able to account for this commotion, since there is no reason for it."

column.name: text
column.value: After he had said this, he dismissed the assembly.

column.name: text
column.value: After we had torn ourselves away from them, we put out to sea and sailed straight to Cos. The next day we went to Rhodes and from there to Patara.

column.name: text
column.value: We found a ship crossing over to Phoenicia, went on board and set sail.

column.name: text
column.value: After sighting Cyprus and passing to the south of it, we sailed on to Syria. We landed at Tyre, where our ship was to unload its cargo.

column.name: text
column.value: Finding the disciples there, we stayed with them seven days. Through the Spirit they urged Paul not to go on to Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: But when our time was up, we left and continued on our way. All the disciples and their wives and children accompanied us out of the city, and there on the beach we knelt to pray.

column.name: text
column.value: After saying good-by to each other, we went aboard the ship, and they returned home.

column.name: text
column.value: We continued our voyage from Tyre and landed at Ptolemais, where we greeted the brothers and stayed with them for a day.

column.name: text
column.value: Leaving the next day, we reached Caesarea and stayed at the house of Philip the evangelist, one of the Seven.

column.name: text
column.value: He had four unmarried daughters who prophesied.

column.name: text
column.value: After we had been there a number of days, a prophet named Agabus came down from Judea.

column.name: text
column.value: Coming over to us, he took Paul's belt, tied his own hands and feet with it and said, "The Holy Spirit says, 'In this way the Jews of Jerusalem will bind the owner of this belt and will hand him over to the Gentiles.'"

column.name: text
column.value: When we heard this, we and the people there pleaded with Paul not to go up to Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Paul answered, "Why are you weeping and breaking my heart? I am ready not only to be bound, but also to die in Jerusalem for the name of the Lord Jesus."

column.name: text
column.value: When he would not be dissuaded, we gave up and said, "The Lord's will be done."

column.name: text
column.value: After this, we got ready and went up to Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: Some of the disciples from Caesarea accompanied us and brought us to the home of Mnason, where we were to stay. He was a man from Cyprus and one of the early disciples.

column.name: text
column.value: When we arrived at Jerusalem, the brothers received us warmly.

column.name: text
column.value: The next day Paul and the rest of us went to see James, and all the elders were present.

column.name: text
column.value: Paul greeted them and reported in detail what God had done among the Gentiles through his ministry.

column.name: text
column.value: When they heard this, they praised God. Then they said to Paul: "You see, brother, how many thousands of Jews have believed, and all of them are zealous for the law.

column.name: text
column.value: They have been informed that you teach all the Jews who live among the Gentiles to turn away from Moses, telling them not to circumcise their children or live according to our customs.

column.name: text
column.value: What shall we do? They will certainly hear that you have come,

column.name: text
column.value: so do what we tell you. There are four men with us who have made a vow.

column.name: text
column.value: Take these men, join in their purification rites and pay their expenses, so that they can have their heads shaved. Then everybody will know there is no truth in these reports about you, but that you yourself are living in obedience to the law.

column.name: text
column.value: As for the Gentile believers, we have written to them our decision that they should abstain from food sacrificed to idols, from blood, from the meat of strangled animals and from sexual immorality."

column.name: text
column.value: The next day Paul took the men and purified himself along with them. Then he went to the temple to give notice of the date when the days of purification would end and the offering would be made for each of them.

column.name: text
column.value: When the seven days were nearly over, some Jews from the province of Asia saw Paul at the temple. They stirred up the whole crowd and seized him,

column.name: text
column.value: shouting, "Men of Israel, help us! This is the man who teaches all men everywhere against our people and our law and this place. And besides, he has brought Greeks into the temple area and defiled this holy place."

column.name: text
column.value: (They had previously seen Trophimus the Ephesian in the city with Paul and assumed that Paul had brought him into the temple area.)

column.name: text
column.value: The whole city was aroused, and the people came running from all directions. Seizing Paul, they dragged him from the temple, and immediately the gates were shut.

column.name: text
column.value: While they were trying to kill him, news reached the commander of the Roman troops that the whole city of Jerusalem was in an uproar.

column.name: text
column.value: He at once took some officers and soldiers and ran down to the crowd. When the rioters saw the commander and his soldiers, they stopped beating Paul.

column.name: text
column.value: The commander came up and arrested him and ordered him to be bound with two chains. Then he asked who he was and what he had done.

column.name: text
column.value: Some in the crowd shouted one thing and some another, and since the commander could not get at the truth because of the uproar, he ordered that Paul be taken into the barracks.

column.name: text
column.value: When Paul reached the steps, the violence of the mob was so great he had to be carried by the soldiers.

column.name: text
column.value: The crowd that followed kept shouting, "Away with him!"

column.name: text
column.value: As the soldiers were about to take Paul into the barracks, he asked the commander, "May I say something to you?" "Do you speak Greek?" he replied.

column.name: text
column.value: "Aren't you the Egyptian who started a revolt and led four thousand terrorists out into the desert some time ago?"

column.name: text
column.value: Paul answered, "I am a Jew, from Tarsus in Cilicia, a citizen of no ordinary city. Please let me speak to the people."

column.name: text
column.value: Having received the commander's permission, Paul stood on the steps and motioned to the crowd. When they were all silent, he said to them in Aramaic:

column.name: text
column.value: "Brothers and fathers, listen now to my defense."

column.name: text
column.value: When they heard him speak to them in Aramaic, they became very quiet. Then Paul said:

column.name: text
column.value: "I am a Jew, born in Tarsus of Cilicia, but brought up in this city. Under Gamaliel I was thoroughly trained in the law of our fathers and was just as zealous for God as any of you are today.

column.name: text
column.value: I persecuted the followers of this Way to their death, arresting both men and women and throwing them into prison,

column.name: text
column.value: as also the high priest and all the Council can testify. I even obtained letters from them to their brothers in Damascus, and went there to bring these people as prisoners to Jerusalem to be punished.

column.name: text
column.value: "About noon as I came near Damascus, suddenly a bright light from heaven flashed around me.

column.name: text
column.value: I fell to the ground and heard a voice say to me, 'Saul! Saul! Why do you persecute me?'

column.name: text
column.value: "'Who are you, Lord?' I asked. "'I am Jesus of Nazareth, whom you are persecuting,' he replied.

column.name: text
column.value: My companions saw the light, but they did not understand the voice of him who was speaking to me.

column.name: text
column.value: "'What shall I do, Lord?' I asked. "'Get up,' the Lord said, 'and go into Damascus. There you will be told all that you have been assigned to do.'

column.name: text
column.value: My companions led me by the hand into Damascus, because the brilliance of the light had blinded me.

column.name: text
column.value: "A man named Ananias came to see me. He was a devout observer of the law and highly respected by all the Jews living there.

column.name: text
column.value: He stood beside me and said, 'Brother Saul, receive your sight!' And at that very moment I was able to see him.

column.name: text
column.value: "Then he said: 'The God of our fathers has chosen you to know his will and to see the Righteous One and to hear words from his mouth.

column.name: text
column.value: You will be his witness to all men of what you have seen and heard.

column.name: text
column.value: And now what are you waiting for? Get up, be baptized and wash your sins away, calling on his name.'

column.name: text
column.value: "When I returned to Jerusalem and was praying at the temple, I fell into a trance

column.name: text
column.value: and saw the Lord speaking. 'Quick!' he said to me. 'Leave Jerusalem immediately, because they will not accept your testimony about me.'

column.name: text
column.value: "'Lord,' I replied, 'these men know that I went from one synagogue to another to imprison and beat those who believe in you.

column.name: text
column.value: And when the blood of your martyr Stephen was shed, I stood there giving my approval and guarding the clothes of those who were killing him.'

column.name: text
column.value: "Then the Lord said to me, 'Go; I will send you far away to the Gentiles.'"

column.name: text
column.value: The crowd listened to Paul until he said this. Then they raised their voices and shouted, "Rid the earth of him! He's not fit to live!"

column.name: text
column.value: As they were shouting and throwing off their cloaks and flinging dust into the air,

column.name: text
column.value: the commander ordered Paul to be taken into the barracks. He directed that he be flogged and questioned in order to find out why the people were shouting at him like this.

column.name: text
column.value: As they stretched him out to flog him, Paul said to the centurion standing there, "Is it legal for you to flog a Roman citizen who hasn't even been found guilty?"

column.name: text
column.value: When the centurion heard this, he went to the commander and reported it. "What are you going to do?" he asked. "This man is a Roman citizen."

column.name: text
column.value: The commander went to Paul and asked, "Tell me, are you a Roman citizen?" "Yes, I am," he answered.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the commander said, "I had to pay a big price for my citizenship." "But I was born a citizen," Paul replied.

column.name: text
column.value: Those who were about to question him withdrew immediately. The commander himself was alarmed when he realized that he had put Paul, a Roman citizen, in chains.

column.name: text
column.value: The next day, since the commander wanted to find out exactly why Paul was being accused by the Jews, he released him and ordered the chief priests and all the Sanhedrin to assemble. Then he brought Paul and had him stand before them.

column.name: text
column.value: Paul looked straight at the Sanhedrin and said, "My brothers, I have fulfilled my duty to God in all good conscience to this day."

column.name: text
column.value: At this the high priest Ananias ordered those standing near Paul to strike him on the mouth.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Paul said to him, "God will strike you, you whitewashed wall! You sit there to judge me according to the law, yet you yourself violate the law by commanding that I be struck!"

column.name: text
column.value: Those who were standing near Paul said, "You dare to insult God's high priest?"

column.name: text
column.value: Paul replied, "Brothers, I did not realize that he was the high priest; for it is written: 'Do not speak evil about the ruler of your people.'"

column.name: text
column.value: Then Paul, knowing that some of them were Sadducees and the others Pharisees, called out in the Sanhedrin, "My brothers, I am a Pharisee, the son of a Pharisee. I stand on trial because of my hope in the resurrection of the dead."

column.name: text
column.value: When he said this, a dispute broke out between the Pharisees and the Sadducees, and the assembly was divided.

column.name: text
column.value: (The Sadducees say that there is no resurrection, and that there are neither angels nor spirits, but the Pharisees acknowledge them all.)

column.name: text
column.value: There was a great uproar, and some of the teachers of the law who were Pharisees stood up and argued vigorously. "We find nothing wrong with this man," they said. "What if a spirit or an angel has spoken to him?"

column.name: text
column.value: The dispute became so violent that the commander was afraid Paul would be torn to pieces by them. He ordered the troops to go down and take him away from them by force and bring him into the barracks.

column.name: text
column.value: The following night the Lord stood near Paul and said, "Take courage! As you have testified about me in Jerusalem, so you must also testify in Rome."

column.name: text
column.value: The next morning the Jews formed a conspiracy and bound themselves with an oath not to eat or drink until they had killed Paul.

column.name: text
column.value: More than forty men were involved in this plot.

column.name: text
column.value: They went to the chief priests and elders and said, "We have taken a solemn oath not to eat anything until we have killed Paul.

column.name: text
column.value: Now then, you and the Sanhedrin petition the commander to bring him before you on the pretext of wanting more accurate information about his case. We are ready to kill him before he gets here."

column.name: text
column.value: But when the son of Paul's sister heard of this plot, he went into the barracks and told Paul.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Paul called one of the centurions and said, "Take this young man to the commander; he has something to tell him."

column.name: text
column.value: So he took him to the commander. The centurion said, "Paul, the prisoner, sent for me and asked me to bring this young man to you because he has something to tell you."

column.name: text
column.value: The commander took the young man by the hand, drew him aside and asked, "What is it you want to tell me?"

column.name: text
column.value: He said: "The Jews have agreed to ask you to bring Paul before the Sanhedrin tomorrow on the pretext of wanting more accurate information about him.

column.name: text
column.value: Don't give in to them, because more than forty of them are waiting in ambush for him. They have taken an oath not to eat or drink until they have killed him. They are ready now, waiting for your consent to their request."

column.name: text
column.value: The commander dismissed the young man and cautioned him, "Don't tell anyone that you have reported this to me."

column.name: text
column.value: Then he called two of his centurions and ordered them, "Get ready a detachment of two hundred soldiers, seventy horsemen and two hundred spearmen to go to Caesarea at nine tonight.

column.name: text
column.value: Provide mounts for Paul so that he may be taken safely to Governor Felix."

column.name: text
column.value: He wrote a letter as follows:

column.name: text
column.value: Claudius Lysias, To His Excellency, Governor Felix: Greetings.

column.name: text
column.value: This man was seized by the Jews and they were about to kill him, but I came with my troops and rescued him, for I had learned that he is a Roman citizen.

column.name: text
column.value: I wanted to know why they were accusing him, so I brought him to their Sanhedrin.

column.name: text
column.value: I found that the accusation had to do with questions about their law, but there was no charge against him that deserved death or imprisonment.

column.name: text
column.value: When I was informed of a plot to be carried out against the man, I sent him to you at once. I also ordered his accusers to present to you their case against him.

column.name: text
column.value: So the soldiers, carrying out their orders, took Paul with them during the night and brought him as far as Antipatris.

column.name: text
column.value: The next day they let the cavalry go on with him, while they returned to the barracks.

column.name: text
column.value: When the cavalry arrived in Caesarea, they delivered the letter to the governor and handed Paul over to him.

column.name: text
column.value: The governor read the letter and asked what province he was from. Learning that he was from Cilicia,

column.name: text
column.value: he said, "I will hear your case when your accusers get here." Then he ordered that Paul be kept under guard in Herod's palace.

column.name: text
column.value: When the uproar had ended, Paul sent for the disciples and, after encouraging them, said good-by and set out for Macedonia.

column.name: text
column.value: He traveled through that area, speaking many words of encouragement to the people, and finally arrived in Greece,

column.name: text
column.value: where he stayed three months. Because the Jews made a plot against him just as he was about to sail for Syria, he decided to go back through Macedonia.

column.name: text
column.value: He was accompanied by Sopater son of Pyrrhus from Berea, Aristarchus and Secundus from Thessalonica, Gaius from Derbe, Timothy also, and Tychicus and Trophimus from the province of Asia.

column.name: text
column.value: These men went on ahead and waited for us at Troas.

column.name: text
column.value: But we sailed from Philippi after the Feast of Unleavened Bread, and five days later joined the others at Troas, where we stayed seven days.

column.name: text
column.value: On the first day of the week we came together to break bread. Paul spoke to the people and, because he intended to leave the next day, kept on talking until midnight.

column.name: text
column.value: There were many lamps in the upstairs room where we were meeting.

column.name: text
column.value: Seated in a window was a young man named Eutychus, who was sinking into a deep sleep as Paul talked on and on. When he was sound asleep, he fell to the ground from the third story and was picked up dead.

column.name: text
column.value: Paul went down, threw himself on the young man and put his arms around him. "Don't be alarmed," he said. "He's alive!"

column.name: text
column.value: Then he went upstairs again and broke bread and ate. After talking until daylight, he left.

column.name: text
column.value: The people took the young man home alive and were greatly comforted.

column.name: text
column.value: We went on ahead to the ship and sailed for Assos, where we were going to take Paul aboard. He had made this arrangement because he was going there on foot.

column.name: text
column.value: When he met us at Assos, we took him aboard and went on to Mitylene.

column.name: text
column.value: The next day we set sail from there and arrived off Kios. The day after that we crossed over to Samos, and on the following day arrived at Miletus.

column.name: text
column.value: Paul had decided to sail past Ephesus to avoid spending time in the province of Asia, for he was in a hurry to reach Jerusalem, if possible, by the day of Pentecost.

column.name: text
column.value: From Miletus, Paul sent to Ephesus for the elders of the church.

column.name: text
column.value: When they arrived, he said to them: "You know how I lived the whole time I was with you, from the first day I came into the province of Asia.

column.name: text
column.value: I served the Lord with great humility and with tears, although I was severely tested by the plots of the Jews.

column.name: text
column.value: You know that I have not hesitated to preach anything that would be helpful to you but have taught you publicly and from house to house.

column.name: text
column.value: I have declared to both Jews and Greeks that they must turn to God in repentance and have faith in our Lord Jesus.

column.name: text
column.value: "And now, compelled by the Spirit, I am going to Jerusalem, not knowing what will happen to me there.

column.name: text
column.value: I only know that in every city the Holy Spirit warns me that prison and hardships are facing me.

column.name: text
column.value: However, I consider my life worth nothing to me, if only I may finish the race and complete the task the Lord Jesus has given me--the task of testifying to the gospel of God's grace.

column.name: text
column.value: "Now I know that none of you among whom I have gone about preaching the kingdom will ever see me again.

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore, I declare to you today that I am innocent of the blood of all men.

column.name: text
column.value: For I have not hesitated to proclaim to you the whole will of God.

column.name: text
column.value: Keep watch over yourselves and all the flock of which the Holy Spirit has made you overseers. Be shepherds of the church of God, which he bought with his own blood.

column.name: text
column.value: I know that after I leave, savage wolves will come in among you and will not spare the flock.

column.name: text
column.value: Even from your own number men will arise and distort the truth in order to draw away disciples after them.

column.name: text
column.value: So be on your guard! Remember that for three years I never stopped warning each of you night and day with tears.

column.name: text
column.value: "Now I commit you to God and to the word of his grace, which can build you up and give you an inheritance among all those who are sanctified.

column.name: text
column.value: I have not coveted anyone's silver or gold or clothing.

column.name: text
column.value: You yourselves know that these hands of mine have supplied my own needs and the needs of my companions.

column.name: text
column.value: In everything I did, I showed you that by this kind of hard work we must help the weak, remembering the words the Lord Jesus himself said: 'It is more blessed to give than to receive.'"

column.name: text
column.value: When he had said this, he knelt down with all of them and prayed.

column.name: text
column.value: They all wept as they embraced him and kissed him.

column.name: text
column.value: What grieved them most was his statement that they would never see his face again. Then they accompanied him to the ship.

column.name: text
column.value: Three days after arriving in the province, Festus went up from Caesarea to Jerusalem,

column.name: text
column.value: where the chief priests and Jewish leaders appeared before him and presented the charges against Paul.

column.name: text
column.value: They urgently requested Festus, as a favor to them, to have Paul transferred to Jerusalem, for they were preparing an ambush to kill him along the way.

column.name: text
column.value: Festus answered, "Paul is being held at Caesarea, and I myself am going there soon.

column.name: text
column.value: Let some of your leaders come with me and press charges against the man there, if he has done anything wrong."

column.name: text
column.value: After spending eight or ten days with them, he went down to Caesarea, and the next day he convened the court and ordered that Paul be brought before him.

column.name: text
column.value: When Paul appeared, the Jews who had come down from Jerusalem stood around him, bringing many serious charges against him, which they could not prove.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Paul made his defense: "I have done nothing wrong against the law of the Jews or against the temple or against Caesar."

column.name: text
column.value: Festus, wishing to do the Jews a favor, said to Paul, "Are you willing to go up to Jerusalem and stand trial before me there on these charges?"

column.name: text
column.value: Paul answered: "I am now standing before Caesar's court, where I ought to be tried. I have not done any wrong to the Jews, as you yourself know very well.

column.name: text
column.value: If, however, I am guilty of doing anything deserving death, I do not refuse to die. But if the charges brought against me by these Jews are not true, no one has the right to hand me over to them. I appeal to Caesar!"

column.name: text
column.value: After Festus had conferred with his council, he declared: "You have appealed to Caesar. To Caesar you will go!"

column.name: text
column.value: A few days later King Agrippa and Bernice arrived at Caesarea to pay their respects to Festus.

column.name: text
column.value: Since they were spending many days there, Festus discussed Paul's case with the king. He said: "There is a man here whom Felix left as a prisoner.

column.name: text
column.value: When I went to Jerusalem, the chief priests and elders of the Jews brought charges against him and asked that he be condemned.

column.name: text
column.value: "I told them that it is not the Roman custom to hand over any man before he has faced his accusers and has had an opportunity to defend himself against their charges.

column.name: text
column.value: When they came here with me, I did not delay the case, but convened the court the next day and ordered the man to be brought in.

column.name: text
column.value: When his accusers got up to speak, they did not charge him with any of the crimes I had expected.

column.name: text
column.value: Instead, they had some points of dispute with him about their own religion and about a dead man named Jesus who Paul claimed was alive.

column.name: text
column.value: I was at a loss how to investigate such matters; so I asked if he would be willing to go to Jerusalem and stand trial there on these charges.

column.name: text
column.value: When Paul made his appeal to be held over for the Emperor's decision, I ordered him held until I could send him to Caesar."

column.name: text
column.value: Then Agrippa said to Festus, "I would like to hear this man myself." He replied, "Tomorrow you will hear him."

column.name: text
column.value: The next day Agrippa and Bernice came with great pomp and entered the audience room with the high ranking officers and the leading men of the city. At the command of Festus, Paul was brought in.

column.name: text
column.value: Festus said: "King Agrippa, and all who are present with us, you see this man! The whole Jewish community has petitioned me about him in Jerusalem and here in Caesarea, shouting that he ought not to live any longer.

column.name: text
column.value: I found he had done nothing deserving of death, but because he made his appeal to the Emperor I decided to send him to Rome.

column.name: text
column.value: But I have nothing definite to write to His Majesty about him. Therefore I have brought him before all of you, and especially before you, King Agrippa, so that as a result of this investigation I may have something to write.

column.name: text
column.value: For I think it is unreasonable to send on a prisoner without specifying the charges against him."

column.name: text
column.value: Five days later the high priest Ananias went down to Caesarea with some of the elders and a lawyer named Tertullus, and they brought their charges against Paul before the governor.

column.name: text
column.value: When Paul was called in, Tertullus presented his case before Felix: "We have enjoyed a long period of peace under you, and your foresight has brought about reforms in this nation.

column.name: text
column.value: Everywhere and in every way, most excellent Felix, we acknowledge this with profound gratitude.

column.name: text
column.value: But in order not to weary you further, I would request that you be kind enough to hear us briefly.

column.name: text
column.value: "We have found this man to be a troublemaker, stirring up riots among the Jews all over the world. He is a ringleader of the Nazarene sect

column.name: text
column.value: and even tried to desecrate the temple; so we seized him.

column.name: text
column.value: By examining him yourself you will be able to learn the truth about all these charges we are bringing against him."

column.name: text
column.value: The Jews joined in the accusation, asserting that these things were true.

column.name: text
column.value: When the governor motioned for him to speak, Paul replied: "I know that for a number of years you have been a judge over this nation; so I gladly make my defense.

column.name: text
column.value: You can easily verify that no more than twelve days ago I went up to Jerusalem to worship.

column.name: text
column.value: My accusers did not find me arguing with anyone at the temple, or stirring up a crowd in the synagogues or anywhere else in the city.

column.name: text
column.value: And they cannot prove to you the charges they are now making against me.

column.name: text
column.value: However, I admit that I worship the God of our fathers as a follower of the Way, which they call a sect. I believe everything that agrees with the Law and that is written in the Prophets,

column.name: text
column.value: and I have the same hope in God as these men, that there will be a resurrection of both the righteous and the wicked.

column.name: text
column.value: So I strive always to keep my conscience clear before God and man.

column.name: text
column.value: "After an absence of several years, I came to Jerusalem to bring my people gifts for the poor and to present offerings.

column.name: text
column.value: I was ceremonially clean when they found me in the temple courts doing this. There was no crowd with me, nor was I involved in any disturbance.

column.name: text
column.value: But there are some Jews from the province of Asia, who ought to be here before you and bring charges if they have anything against me.

column.name: text
column.value: Or these who are here should state what crime they found in me when I stood before the Sanhedrin--

column.name: text
column.value: unless it was this one thing I shouted as I stood in their presence: 'It is concerning the resurrection of the dead that I am on trial before you today.'"

column.name: text
column.value: Then Felix, who was well acquainted with the Way, adjourned the proceedings. "When Lysias the commander comes," he said, "I will decide your case."

column.name: text
column.value: He ordered the centurion to keep Paul under guard but to give him some freedom and permit his friends to take care of his needs.

column.name: text
column.value: Several days later Felix came with his wife Drusilla, who was a Jewess. He sent for Paul and listened to him as he spoke about faith in Christ Jesus.

column.name: text
column.value: As Paul discoursed on righteousness, self-control and the judgment to come, Felix was afraid and said, "That's enough for now! You may leave. When I find it convenient, I will send for you."

column.name: text
column.value: At the same time he was hoping that Paul would offer him a bribe, so he sent for him frequently and talked with him.

column.name: text
column.value: When two years had passed, Felix was succeeded by Porcius Festus, but because Felix wanted to grant a favor to the Jews, he left Paul in prison.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Agrippa said to Paul, "You have permission to speak for yourself." So Paul motioned with his hand and began his defense:

column.name: text
column.value: "King Agrippa, I consider myself fortunate to stand before you today as I make my defense against all the accusations of the Jews,

column.name: text
column.value: and especially so because you are well acquainted with all the Jewish customs and controversies. Therefore, I beg you to listen to me patiently.

column.name: text
column.value: "The Jews all know the way I have lived ever since I was a child, from the beginning of my life in my own country, and also in Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: They have known me for a long time and can testify, if they are willing, that according to the strictest sect of our religion, I lived as a Pharisee.

column.name: text
column.value: And now it is because of my hope in what God has promised our fathers that I am on trial today.

column.name: text
column.value: This is the promise our twelve tribes are hoping to see fulfilled as they earnestly serve God day and night. O king, it is because of this hope that the Jews are accusing me.

column.name: text
column.value: Why should any of you consider it incredible that God raises the dead?

column.name: text
column.value: "I too was convinced that I ought to do all that was possible to oppose the name of Jesus of Nazareth.

column.name: text
column.value: And that is just what I did in Jerusalem. On the authority of the chief priests I put many of the saints in prison, and when they were put to death, I cast my vote against them.

column.name: text
column.value: Many a time I went from one synagogue to another to have them punished, and I tried to force them to blaspheme. In my obsession against them, I even went to foreign cities to persecute them.

column.name: text
column.value: "On one of these journeys I was going to Damascus with the authority and commission of the chief priests.

column.name: text
column.value: About noon, O king, as I was on the road, I saw a light from heaven, brighter than the sun, blazing around me and my companions.

column.name: text
column.value: We all fell to the ground, and I heard a voice saying to me in Aramaic, 'Saul, Saul, why do you persecute me? It is hard for you to kick against the goads.'

column.name: text
column.value: "Then I asked, 'Who are you, Lord?' "'I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting,' the Lord replied.

column.name: text
column.value: 'Now get up and stand on your feet. I have appeared to you to appoint you as a servant and as a witness of what you have seen of me and what I will show you.

column.name: text
column.value: I will rescue you from your own people and from the Gentiles. I am sending you to them

column.name: text
column.value: to open their eyes and turn them from darkness to light, and from the power of Satan to God, so that they may receive forgiveness of sins and a place among those who are sanctified by faith in me.'

column.name: text
column.value: "So then, King Agrippa, I was not disobedient to the vision from heaven.

column.name: text
column.value: First to those in Damascus, then to those in Jerusalem and in all Judea, and to the Gentiles also, I preached that they should repent and turn to God and prove their repentance by their deeds.

column.name: text
column.value: That is why the Jews seized me in the temple courts and tried to kill me.

column.name: text
column.value: But I have had God's help to this very day, and so I stand here and testify to small and great alike. I am saying nothing beyond what the prophets and Moses said would happen--

column.name: text
column.value: that the Christ would suffer and, as the first to rise from the dead, would proclaim light to his own people and to the Gentiles."

column.name: text
column.value: At this point Festus interrupted Paul's defense. "You are out of your mind, Paul!" he shouted. "Your great learning is driving you insane."

column.name: text
column.value: "I am not insane, most excellent Festus," Paul replied. "What I am saying is true and reasonable.

column.name: text
column.value: The king is familiar with these things, and I can speak freely to him. I am convinced that none of this has escaped his notice, because it was not done in a corner.

column.name: text
column.value: King Agrippa, do you believe the prophets? I know you do."

column.name: text
column.value: Then Agrippa said to Paul, "Do you think that in such a short time you can persuade me to be a Christian?"

column.name: text
column.value: Paul replied, "Short time or long--I pray God that not only you but all who are listening to me today may become what I am, except for these chains."

column.name: text
column.value: The king rose, and with him the governor and Bernice and those sitting with them.

column.name: text
column.value: They left the room, and while talking with one another, they said, "This man is not doing anything that deserves death or imprisonment."

column.name: text
column.value: Agrippa said to Festus, "This man could have been set free if he had not appealed to Caesar."

column.name: text
column.value: When it was decided that we would sail for Italy, Paul and some other prisoners were handed over to a centurion named Julius, who belonged to the Imperial Regiment.

column.name: text
column.value: We boarded a ship from Adramyttium about to sail for ports along the coast of the province of Asia, and we put out to sea. Aristarchus, a Macedonian from Thessalonica, was with us.

column.name: text
column.value: The next day we landed at Sidon; and Julius, in kindness to Paul, allowed him to go to his friends so they might provide for his needs.

column.name: text
column.value: From there we put out to sea again and passed to the lee of Cyprus because the winds were against us.

column.name: text
column.value: When we had sailed across the open sea off the coast of Cilicia and Pamphylia, we landed at Myra in Lycia.

column.name: text
column.value: There the centurion found an Alexandrian ship sailing for Italy and put us on board.

column.name: text
column.value: We made slow headway for many days and had difficulty arriving off Cnidus. When the wind did not allow us to hold our course, we sailed to the lee of Crete, opposite Salmone.

column.name: text
column.value: We moved along the coast with difficulty and came to a place called Fair Havens, near the town of Lasea.

column.name: text
column.value: Much time had been lost, and sailing had already become dangerous because by now it was after the Fast. So Paul warned them,

column.name: text
column.value: "Men, I can see that our voyage is going to be disastrous and bring great loss to ship and cargo, and to our own lives also."

column.name: text
column.value: But the centurion, instead of listening to what Paul said, followed the advice of the pilot and of the owner of the ship.

column.name: text
column.value: Since the harbor was unsuitable to winter in, the majority decided that we should sail on, hoping to reach Phoenix and winter there. This was a harbor in Crete, facing both southwest and northwest.

column.name: text
column.value: When a gentle south wind began to blow, they thought they had obtained what they wanted; so they weighed anchor and sailed along the shore of Crete.

column.name: text
column.value: Before very long, a wind of hurricane force, called the "northeaster," swept down from the island.

column.name: text
column.value: The ship was caught by the storm and could not head into the wind; so we gave way to it and were driven along.

column.name: text
column.value: As we passed to the lee of a small island called Cauda, we were hardly able to make the lifeboat secure.

column.name: text
column.value: When the men had hoisted it aboard, they passed ropes under the ship itself to hold it together. Fearing that they would run aground on the sandbars of Syrtis, they lowered the sea anchor and let the ship be driven along.

column.name: text
column.value: We took such a violent battering from the storm that the next day they began to throw the cargo overboard.

column.name: text
column.value: On the third day, they threw the ship's tackle overboard with their own hands.

column.name: text
column.value: When neither sun nor stars appeared for many days and the storm continued raging, we finally gave up all hope of being saved.

column.name: text
column.value: After the men had gone a long time without food, Paul stood up before them and said: "Men, you should have taken my advice not to sail from Crete; then you would have spared yourselves this damage and loss.

column.name: text
column.value: But now I urge you to keep up your courage, because not one of you will be lost; only the ship will be destroyed.

column.name: text
column.value: Last night an angel of the God whose I am and whom I serve stood beside me

column.name: text
column.value: and said, 'Do not be afraid, Paul. You must stand trial before Caesar; and God has graciously given you the lives of all who sail with you.'

column.name: text
column.value: So keep up your courage, men, for I have faith in God that it will happen just as he told me.

column.name: text
column.value: Nevertheless, we must run aground on some island."

column.name: text
column.value: On the fourteenth night we were still being driven across the Adriatic Sea, when about midnight the sailors sensed they were approaching land.

column.name: text
column.value: They took soundings and found that the water was a hundred and twenty feet deep. A short time later they took soundings again and found it was ninety feet deep.

column.name: text
column.value: Fearing that we would be dashed against the rocks, they dropped four anchors from the stern and prayed for daylight.

column.name: text
column.value: In an attempt to escape from the ship, the sailors let the lifeboat down into the sea, pretending they were going to lower some anchors from the bow.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Paul said to the centurion and the soldiers, "Unless these men stay with the ship, you cannot be saved."

column.name: text
column.value: So the soldiers cut the ropes that held the lifeboat and let it fall away.

column.name: text
column.value: Just before dawn Paul urged them all to eat. "For the last fourteen days," he said, "you have been in constant suspense and have gone without food--you haven't eaten anything.

column.name: text
column.value: Now I urge you to take some food. You need it to survive. Not one of you will lose a single hair from his head."

column.name: text
column.value: After he said this, he took some bread and gave thanks to God in front of them all. Then he broke it and began to eat.

column.name: text
column.value: They were all encouraged and ate some food themselves.

column.name: text
column.value: Altogether there were 276 of us on board.

column.name: text
column.value: When they had eaten as much as they wanted, they lightened the ship by throwing the grain into the sea.

column.name: text
column.value: When daylight came, they did not recognize the land, but they saw a bay with a sandy beach, where they decided to run the ship aground if they could.

column.name: text
column.value: Cutting loose the anchors, they left them in the sea and at the same time untied the ropes that held the rudders. Then they hoisted the foresail to the wind and made for the beach.

column.name: text
column.value: But the ship struck a sandbar and ran aground. The bow stuck fast and would not move, and the stern was broken to pieces by the pounding of the surf.

column.name: text
column.value: The soldiers planned to kill the prisoners to prevent any of them from swimming away and escaping.

column.name: text
column.value: But the centurion wanted to spare Paul's life and kept them from carrying out their plan. He ordered those who could swim to jump overboard first and get to land.

column.name: text
column.value: The rest were to get there on planks or on pieces of the ship. In this way everyone reached land in safety.

column.name: text
column.value: Once safely on shore, we found out that the island was called Malta.

column.name: text
column.value: The islanders showed us unusual kindness. They built a fire and welcomed us all because it was raining and cold.

column.name: text
column.value: Paul gathered a pile of brushwood and, as he put it on the fire, a viper, driven out by the heat, fastened itself on his hand.

column.name: text
column.value: When the islanders saw the snake hanging from his hand, they said to each other, "This man must be a murderer; for though he escaped from the sea, Justice has not allowed him to live."

column.name: text
column.value: But Paul shook the snake off into the fire and suffered no ill effects.

column.name: text
column.value: The people expected him to swell up or suddenly fall dead, but after waiting a long time and seeing nothing unusual happen to him, they changed their minds and said he was a god.

column.name: text
column.value: There was an estate nearby that belonged to Publius, the chief official of the island. He welcomed us to his home and for three days entertained us hospitably.

column.name: text
column.value: His father was sick in bed, suffering from fever and dysentery. Paul went in to see him and, after prayer, placed his hands on him and healed him.

column.name: text
column.value: When this had happened, the rest of the sick on the island came and were cured.

column.name: text
column.value: They honored us in many ways and when we were ready to sail, they furnished us with the supplies we needed.

column.name: text
column.value: After three months we put out to sea in a ship that had wintered in the island. It was an Alexandrian ship with the figurehead of the twin gods Castor and Pollux.

column.name: text
column.value: We put in at Syracuse and stayed there three days.

column.name: text
column.value: From there we set sail and arrived at Rhegium. The next day the south wind came up, and on the following day we reached Puteoli.

column.name: text
column.value: There we found some brothers who invited us to spend a week with them. And so we came to Rome.

column.name: text
column.value: The brothers there had heard that we were coming, and they traveled as far as the Forum of Appius and the Three Taverns to meet us. At the sight of these men Paul thanked God and was encouraged.

column.name: text
column.value: When we got to Rome, Paul was allowed to live by himself, with a soldier to guard him.

column.name: text
column.value: Three days later he called together the leaders of the Jews. When they had assembled, Paul said to them: "My brothers, although I have done nothing against our people or against the customs of our ancestors, I was arrested in Jerusalem and handed over to the Romans.

column.name: text
column.value: They examined me and wanted to release me, because I was not guilty of any crime deserving death.

column.name: text
column.value: But when the Jews objected, I was compelled to appeal to Caesar--not that I had any charge to bring against my own people.

column.name: text
column.value: For this reason I have asked to see you and talk with you. It is because of the hope of Israel that I am bound with this chain."

column.name: text
column.value: They replied, "We have not received any letters from Judea concerning you, and none of the brothers who have come from there has reported or said anything bad about you.

column.name: text
column.value: But we want to hear what your views are, for we know that people everywhere are talking against this sect."

column.name: text
column.value: They arranged to meet Paul on a certain day, and came in even larger numbers to the place where he was staying. From morning till evening he explained and declared to them the kingdom of God and tried to convince them about Jesus from the Law of Moses and from the Prophets.

column.name: text
column.value: Some were convinced by what he said, but others would not believe.

column.name: text
column.value: They disagreed among themselves and began to leave after Paul had made this final statement: "The Holy Spirit spoke the truth to your forefathers when he said through Isaiah the prophet:

column.name: text
column.value: "'Go to this people and say, "You will be ever hearing but never understanding; you will be ever seeing but never perceiving."

column.name: text
column.value: For this people's heart has become calloused; they hardly hear with their ears, and they have closed their eyes. Otherwise they might see with their eyes, hear with their ears, understand with their hearts and turn, and I would heal them.'

column.name: text
column.value: "Therefore I want you to know that God's salvation has been sent to the Gentiles, and they will listen!"

column.name: text
column.value: For two whole years Paul stayed there in his own rented house and welcomed all who came to see him.

column.name: text
column.value: Boldly and without hindrance he preached the kingdom of God and taught about the Lord Jesus Christ.

column.name: text
column.value: You, therefore, have no excuse, you who pass judgment on someone else, for at whatever point you judge the other, you are condemning yourself, because you who pass judgment do the same things.

column.name: text
column.value: Now we know that God's judgment against those who do such things is based on truth.

column.name: text
column.value: So when you, a mere man, pass judgment on them and yet do the same things, do you think you will escape God's judgment?

column.name: text
column.value: Or do you show contempt for the riches of his kindness, tolerance and patience, not realizing that God's kindness leads you toward repentance?

column.name: text
column.value: But because of your stubbornness and your unrepentant heart, you are storing up wrath against yourself for the day of God's wrath, when his righteous judgment will be revealed.

column.name: text
column.value: God "will give to each person according to what he has done."

column.name: text
column.value: To those who by persistence in doing good seek glory, honor and immortality, he will give eternal life.

column.name: text
column.value: But for those who are self-seeking and who reject the truth and follow evil, there will be wrath and anger.

column.name: text
column.value: There will be trouble and distress for every human being who does evil: first for the Jew, then for the Gentile;

column.name: text
column.value: but glory, honor and peace for everyone who does good: first for the Jew, then for the Gentile.

column.name: text
column.value: For God does not show favoritism.

column.name: text
column.value: All who sin apart from the law will also perish apart from the law, and all who sin under the law will be judged by the law.

column.name: text
column.value: For it is not those who hear the law who are righteous in God's sight, but it is those who obey the law who will be declared righteous.

column.name: text
column.value: (Indeed, when Gentiles, who do not have the law, do by nature things required by the law, they are a law for themselves, even though they do not have the law,

column.name: text
column.value: since they show that the requirements of the law are written on their hearts, their consciences also bearing witness, and their thoughts now accusing, now even defending them.)

column.name: text
column.value: This will take place on the day when God will judge men's secrets through Jesus Christ, as my gospel declares.

column.name: text
column.value: Now you, if you call yourself a Jew; if you rely on the law and brag about your relationship to God;

column.name: text
column.value: if you know his will and approve of what is superior because you are instructed by the law;

column.name: text
column.value: if you are convinced that you are a guide for the blind, a light for those who are in the dark,

column.name: text
column.value: an instructor of the foolish, a teacher of infants, because you have in the law the embodiment of knowledge and truth--

column.name: text
column.value: you, then, who teach others, do you not teach yourself? You who preach against stealing, do you steal?

column.name: text
column.value: You who say that people should not commit adultery, do you commit adultery? You who abhor idols, do you rob temples?

column.name: text
column.value: You who brag about the law, do you dishonor God by breaking the law?

column.name: text
column.value: As it is written: "God's name is blasphemed among the Gentiles because of you."

column.name: text
column.value: Circumcision has value if you observe the law, but if you break the law, you have become as though you had not been circumcised.

column.name: text
column.value: If those who are not circumcised keep the law's requirements, will they not be regarded as though they were circumcised?

column.name: text
column.value: The one who is not circumcised physically and yet obeys the law will condemn you who, even though you have the written code and circumcision, are a lawbreaker.

column.name: text
column.value: A man is not a Jew if he is only one outwardly, nor is circumcision merely outward and physical.

column.name: text
column.value: No, a man is a Jew if he is one inwardly; and circumcision is circumcision of the heart, by the Spirit, not by the written code. Such a man's praise is not from men, but from God.

column.name: text
column.value: Paul, a servant of Christ Jesus, called to be an apostle and set apart for the gospel of God--

column.name: text
column.value: the gospel he promised beforehand through his prophets in the Holy Scriptures

column.name: text
column.value: regarding his Son, who as to his human nature was a descendant of David,

column.name: text
column.value: and who through the Spirit of holiness was declared with power to be the Son of God by his resurrection from the dead: Jesus Christ our Lord.

column.name: text
column.value: Through him and for his name's sake, we received grace and apostleship to call people from among all the Gentiles to the obedience that comes from faith.

column.name: text
column.value: And you also are among those who are called to belong to Jesus Christ.

column.name: text
column.value: To all in Rome who are loved by God and called to be saints: Grace and peace to you from God our Father and from the Lord Jesus Christ.

column.name: text
column.value: First, I thank my God through Jesus Christ for all of you, because your faith is being reported all over the world.

column.name: text
column.value: God, whom I serve with my whole heart in preaching the gospel of his Son, is my witness how constantly I remember you

column.name: text
column.value: in my prayers at all times; and I pray that now at last by God's will the way may be opened for me to come to you.

column.name: text
column.value: I long to see you so that I may impart to you some spiritual gift to make you strong--

column.name: text
column.value: that is, that you and I may be mutually encouraged by each other's faith.

column.name: text
column.value: I do not want you to be unaware, brothers, that I planned many times to come to you (but have been prevented from doing so until now) in order that I might have a harvest among you, just as I have had among the other Gentiles.

column.name: text
column.value: I am obligated both to Greeks and non-Greeks, both to the wise and the foolish.

column.name: text
column.value: That is why I am so eager to preach the gospel also to you who are at Rome.

column.name: text
column.value: I am not ashamed of the gospel, because it is the power of God for the salvation of everyone who believes: first for the Jew, then for the Gentile.

column.name: text
column.value: For in the gospel a righteousness from God is revealed, a righteousness that is by faith from first to last, just as it is written: "The righteous will live by faith."

column.name: text
column.value: The wrath of God is being revealed from heaven against all the godlessness and wickedness of men who suppress the truth by their wickedness,

column.name: text
column.value: since what may be known about God is plain to them, because God has made it plain to them.

column.name: text
column.value: For since the creation of the world God's invisible qualities--his eternal power and divine nature--have been clearly seen, being understood from what has been made, so that men are without excuse.

column.name: text
column.value: For although they knew God, they neither glorified him as God nor gave thanks to him, but their thinking became futile and their foolish hearts were darkened.

column.name: text
column.value: Although they claimed to be wise, they became fools

column.name: text
column.value: and exchanged the glory of the immortal God for images made to look like mortal man and birds and animals and reptiles.

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore God gave them over in the sinful desires of their hearts to sexual impurity for the degrading of their bodies with one another.

column.name: text
column.value: They exchanged the truth of God for a lie, and worshiped and served created things rather than the Creator--who is forever praised. Amen.

column.name: text
column.value: Because of this, God gave them over to shameful lusts. Even their women exchanged natural relations for unnatural ones.

column.name: text
column.value: In the same way the men also abandoned natural relations with women and were inflamed with lust for one another. Men committed indecent acts with other men, and received in themselves the due penalty for their perversion.

column.name: text
column.value: Furthermore, since they did not think it worthwhile to retain the knowledge of God, he gave them over to a depraved mind, to do what ought not to be done.

column.name: text
column.value: They have become filled with every kind of wickedness, evil, greed and depravity. They are full of envy, murder, strife, deceit and malice. They are gossips,

column.name: text
column.value: slanderers, God-haters, insolent, arrogant and boastful; they invent ways of doing evil; they disobey their parents;

column.name: text
column.value: they are senseless, faithless, heartless, ruthless.

column.name: text
column.value: Although they know God's righteous decree that those who do such things deserve death, they not only continue to do these very things but also approve of those who practice them.

column.name: text
column.value: What then shall we say that Abraham, our forefather, discovered in this matter?

column.name: text
column.value: If, in fact, Abraham was justified by works, he had something to boast about--but not before God.

column.name: text
column.value: What does the Scripture say? "Abraham believed God, and it was credited to him as righteousness."

column.name: text
column.value: Now when a man works, his wages are not credited to him as a gift, but as an obligation.

column.name: text
column.value: However, to the man who does not work but trusts God who justifies the wicked, his faith is credited as righteousness.

column.name: text
column.value: David says the same thing when he speaks of the blessedness of the man to whom God credits righteousness apart from works:

column.name: text
column.value: "Blessed are they whose transgressions are forgiven, whose sins are covered.

column.name: text
column.value: Blessed is the man whose sin the Lord will never count against him."

column.name: text
column.value: Is this blessedness only for the circumcised, or also for the uncircumcised? We have been saying that Abraham's faith was credited to him as righteousness.

column.name: text
column.value: Under what circumstances was it credited? Was it after he was circumcised, or before? It was not after, but before!

column.name: text
column.value: And he received the sign of circumcision, a seal of the righteousness that he had by faith while he was still uncircumcised. So then, he is the father of all who believe but have not been circumcised, in order that righteousness might be credited to them.

column.name: text
column.value: And he is also the father of the circumcised who not only are circumcised but who also walk in the footsteps of the faith that our father Abraham had before he was circumcised.

column.name: text
column.value: It was not through law that Abraham and his offspring received the promise that he would be heir of the world, but through the righteousness that comes by faith.

column.name: text
column.value: For if those who live by law are heirs, faith has no value and the promise is worthless,

column.name: text
column.value: because law brings wrath. And where there is no law there is no transgression.

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore, the promise comes by faith, so that it may be by grace and may be guaranteed to all Abraham's offspring--not only to those who are of the law but also to those who are of the faith of Abraham. He is the father of us all.

column.name: text
column.value: As it is written: "I have made you a father of many nations." He is our father in the sight of God, in whom he believed--the God who gives life to the dead and calls things that are not as though they were.

column.name: text
column.value: Against all hope, Abraham in hope believed and so became the father of many nations, just as it had been said to him, "So shall your offspring be."

column.name: text
column.value: Without weakening in his faith, he faced the fact that his body was as good as dead--since he was about a hundred years old--and that Sarah's womb was also dead.

column.name: text
column.value: Yet he did not waver through unbelief regarding the promise of God, but was strengthened in his faith and gave glory to God,

column.name: text
column.value: being fully persuaded that God had power to do what he had promised.

column.name: text
column.value: This is why "it was credited to him as righteousness."

column.name: text
column.value: The words "it was credited to him" were written not for him alone,

column.name: text
column.value: but also for us, to whom God will credit righteousness--for us who believe in him who raised Jesus our Lord from the dead.

column.name: text
column.value: He was delivered over to death for our sins and was raised to life for our justification.

column.name: text
column.value: Do you not know, brothers--for I am speaking to men who know the law--that the law has authority over a man only as long as he lives?

column.name: text
column.value: For example, by law a married woman is bound to her husband as long as he is alive, but if her husband dies, she is released from the law of marriage.

column.name: text
column.value: So then, if she marries another man while her husband is still alive, she is called an adulteress. But if her husband dies, she is released from that law and is not an adulteress, even though she marries another man.

column.name: text
column.value: So, my brothers, you also died to the law through the body of Christ, that you might belong to another, to him who was raised from the dead, in order that we might bear fruit to God.

column.name: text
column.value: For when we were controlled by the sinful nature, the sinful passions aroused by the law were at work in our bodies, so that we bore fruit for death.

column.name: text
column.value: But now, by dying to what once bound us, we have been released from the law so that we serve in the new way of the Spirit, and not in the old way of the written code.

column.name: text
column.value: What shall we say, then? Is the law sin? Certainly not! Indeed I would not have known what sin was except through the law. For I would not have known what coveting really was if the law had not said, "Do not covet."

column.name: text
column.value: But sin, seizing the opportunity afforded by the commandment, produced in me every kind of covetous desire. For apart from law, sin is dead.

column.name: text
column.value: Once I was alive apart from law; but when the commandment came, sin sprang to life and I died.

column.name: text
column.value: I found that the very commandment that was intended to bring life actually brought death.

column.name: text
column.value: For sin, seizing the opportunity afforded by the commandment, deceived me, and through the commandment put me to death.

column.name: text
column.value: So then, the law is holy, and the commandment is holy, righteous and good.

column.name: text
column.value: Did that which is good, then, become death to me? By no means! But in order that sin might be recognized as sin, it produced death in me through what was good, so that through the commandment sin might become utterly sinful.

column.name: text
column.value: We know that the law is spiritual; but I am unspiritual, sold as a slave to sin.

column.name: text
column.value: I do not understand what I do. For what I want to do I do not do, but what I hate I do.

column.name: text
column.value: And if I do what I do not want to do, I agree that the law is good.

column.name: text
column.value: As it is, it is no longer I myself who do it, but it is sin living in me.

column.name: text
column.value: I know that nothing good lives in me, that is, in my sinful nature. For I have the desire to do what is good, but I cannot carry it out.

column.name: text
column.value: For what I do is not the good I want to do; no, the evil I do not want to do--this I keep on doing.

column.name: text
column.value: Now if I do what I do not want to do, it is no longer I who do it, but it is sin living in me that does it.

column.name: text
column.value: So I find this law at work: When I want to do good, evil is right there with me.

column.name: text
column.value: For in my inner being I delight in God's law;

column.name: text
column.value: but I see another law at work in the members of my body, waging war against the law of my mind and making me a prisoner of the law of sin at work within my members.

column.name: text
column.value: What a wretched man I am! Who will rescue me from this body of death?

column.name: text
column.value: Thanks be to God--through Jesus Christ our Lord! So then, I myself in my mind am a slave to God's law, but in the sinful nature a slave to the law of sin.

column.name: text
column.value: What shall we say, then? Shall we go on sinning so that grace may increase?

column.name: text
column.value: By no means! We died to sin; how can we live in it any longer?

column.name: text
column.value: Or don't you know that all of us who were baptized into Christ Jesus were baptized into his death?

column.name: text
column.value: We were therefore buried with him through baptism into death in order that, just as Christ was raised from the dead through the glory of the Father, we too may live a new life.

column.name: text
column.value: If we have been united with him like this in his death, we will certainly also be united with him in his resurrection.

column.name: text
column.value: For we know that our old self was crucified with him so that the body of sin might be done away with, that we should no longer be slaves to sin--

column.name: text
column.value: because anyone who has died has been freed from sin.

column.name: text
column.value: Now if we died with Christ, we believe that we will also live with him.

column.name: text
column.value: For we know that since Christ was raised from the dead, he cannot die again; death no longer has mastery over him.

column.name: text
column.value: The death he died, he died to sin once for all; but the life he lives, he lives to God.

column.name: text
column.value: In the same way, count yourselves dead to sin but alive to God in Christ Jesus.

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore do not let sin reign in your mortal body so that you obey its evil desires.

column.name: text
column.value: Do not offer the parts of your body to sin, as instruments of wickedness, but rather offer yourselves to God, as those who have been brought from death to life; and offer the parts of your body to him as instruments of righteousness.

column.name: text
column.value: For sin shall not be your master, because you are not under law, but under grace.

column.name: text
column.value: What then? Shall we sin because we are not under law but under grace? By no means!

column.name: text
column.value: Don't you know that when you offer yourselves to someone to obey him as slaves, you are slaves to the one whom you obey--whether you are slaves to sin, which leads to death, or to obedience, which leads to righteousness?

column.name: text
column.value: But thanks be to God that, though you used to be slaves to sin, you wholeheartedly obeyed the form of teaching to which you were entrusted.

column.name: text
column.value: You have been set free from sin and have become slaves to righteousness.

column.name: text
column.value: I put this in human terms because you are weak in your natural selves. Just as you used to offer the parts of your body in slavery to impurity and to ever-increasing wickedness, so now offer them in slavery to righteousness leading to holiness.

column.name: text
column.value: When you were slaves to sin, you were free from the control of righteousness.

column.name: text
column.value: What benefit did you reap at that time from the things you are now ashamed of? Those things result in death!

column.name: text
column.value: But now that you have been set free from sin and have become slaves to God, the benefit you reap leads to holiness, and the result is eternal life.

column.name: text
column.value: For the wages of sin is death, but the gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord.

column.name: text
column.value: What advantage, then, is there in being a Jew, or what value is there in circumcision?

column.name: text
column.value: Much in every way! First of all, they have been entrusted with the very words of God.

column.name: text
column.value: What if some did not have faith? Will their lack of faith nullify God's faithfulness?

column.name: text
column.value: Not at all! Let God be true, and every man a liar. As it is written: "So that you may be proved right when you speak and prevail when you judge."

column.name: text
column.value: But if our unrighteousness brings out God's righteousness more clearly, what shall we say? That God is unjust in bringing his wrath on us? (I am using a human argument.)

column.name: text
column.value: Certainly not! If that were so, how could God judge the world?

column.name: text
column.value: Someone might argue, "If my falsehood enhances God's truthfulness and so increases his glory, why am I still condemned as a sinner?"

column.name: text
column.value: Why not say--as we are being slanderously reported as saying and as some claim that we say--"Let us do evil that good may result"? Their condemnation is deserved.

column.name: text
column.value: What shall we conclude then? Are we any better? Not at all! We have already made the charge that Jews and Gentiles alike are all under sin.

column.name: text
column.value: As it is written: "There is no one righteous, not even one;

column.name: text
column.value: there is no one who understands, no one who seeks God.

column.name: text
column.value: All have turned away, they have together become worthless; there is no one who does good, not even one."

column.name: text
column.value: "Their throats are open graves; their tongues practice deceit." "The poison of vipers is on their lips."

column.name: text
column.value: "Their mouths are full of cursing and bitterness."

column.name: text
column.value: "Their feet are swift to shed blood;

column.name: text
column.value: ruin and misery mark their ways,

column.name: text
column.value: and the way of peace they do not know."

column.name: text
column.value: "There is no fear of God before their eyes."

column.name: text
column.value: Now we know that whatever the law says, it says to those who are under the law, so that every mouth may be silenced and the whole world held accountable to God.

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore no one will be declared righteous in his sight by observing the law; rather, through the law we become conscious of sin.

column.name: text
column.value: But now a righteousness from God, apart from law, has been made known, to which the Law and the Prophets testify.

column.name: text
column.value: This righteousness from God comes through faith in Jesus Christ to all who believe. There is no difference,

column.name: text
column.value: for all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God,

column.name: text
column.value: and are justified freely by his grace through the redemption that came by Christ Jesus.

column.name: text
column.value: God presented him as a sacrifice of atonement, through faith in his blood. He did this to demonstrate his justice, because in his forbearance he had left the sins committed beforehand unpunished--

column.name: text
column.value: he did it to demonstrate his justice at the present time, so as to be just and the one who justifies those who have faith in Jesus.

column.name: text
column.value: Where, then, is boasting? It is excluded. On what principle? On that of observing the law? No, but on that of faith.

column.name: text
column.value: For we maintain that a man is justified by faith apart from observing the law.

column.name: text
column.value: Is God the God of Jews only? Is he not the God of Gentiles too? Yes, of Gentiles too,

column.name: text
column.value: since there is only one God, who will justify the circumcised by faith and the uncircumcised through that same faith.

column.name: text
column.value: Do we, then, nullify the law by this faith? Not at all! Rather, we uphold the law.

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore, since we have been justified through faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ,

column.name: text
column.value: through whom we have gained access by faith into this grace in which we now stand. And we rejoice in the hope of the glory of God.

column.name: text
column.value: Not only so, but we also rejoice in our sufferings, because we know that suffering produces perseverance;

column.name: text
column.value: perseverance, character; and character, hope.

column.name: text
column.value: And hope does not disappoint us, because God has poured out his love into our hearts by the Holy Spirit, whom he has given us.

column.name: text
column.value: You see, at just the right time, when we were still powerless, Christ died for the ungodly.

column.name: text
column.value: Very rarely will anyone die for a righteous man, though for a good man someone might possibly dare to die.

column.name: text
